q: What is the mineral deposited in the sands of valley floors and the base of hills?
qs.e: Placer deposits are mineral deposits formed by the accumulation of weathered materials transported by water, typically found in valley floors and the base of hills. They contain heavy minerals such as gold, diamond, tin, platinum, and iron ore. These deposits are created when water flow carries away lighter particles and deposits heavier minerals. Placer deposits are known as surface deposits and are formed through the process of sedimentation. They are mainly found in riverbeds and beaches. Other options: Load deposits are vein deposits, Wayne deposits are formed in fissures, and Layered deposits occur in sedimentary rocks.
qs.kf:
☛ What process forms placer deposits? → Sedimentation
☛ Which minerals are mainly found in placer deposits? → Gold, diamond, tin, platinum
☛ Where are placer deposits found? → River valleys, beaches, and hill bases
☛ What is another name for placer deposits? → Accumulated deposits
☛ What factor leads to the formation of placer deposits? → Water flow

q: Which of these is not a major tea growing area of India?
qs.e: The major tea-producing regions of India are Assam, Darjeeling, and Nilgiri. Assam Hills is the largest tea-producing area in the world, contributing about 52% of India's total tea production. Darjeeling Hills is famous for its high-quality tea, which has received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Nilgiri Hills is a major tea cultivation center in South India. Meanwhile, Kashmir Valley is known for saffron and apples, but it has no significant commercial tea production. Although 'Kahwa' (a traditional tea beverage) is popular in Kashmir, it is not produced on a large scale. Hence, Kashmir Valley is not a major tea-growing area of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest tea-producing state in India → Assam
☛ Darjeeling tea got GI tag in → 2004
☛ Second largest tea-producing state → West Bengal
☛ Nilgiri tea is produced in → Tamil Nadu
☛ India's rank in world tea production → Second (after China)

q: Kaziranga National Park is situated in ________.
qs.e: Kaziranga National Park is situated in the state of Assam, India. It is located along the banks of the Brahmaputra River and is world-famous for its population of the one-horned rhinoceros. The park was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. It covers an area of approximately 430 square kilometers and is home to elephants, tigers, deer, and various bird species. Kaziranga was established as a national park in 1974.
qs.kf:
☛ Kaziranga National Park is located in which state? → Assam
☛ Which river flows through Kaziranga? → Brahmaputra
☛ Kaziranga is famous for which animal? → One-horned rhinoceros
☛ When was Kaziranga declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1985
☛ What is the approximate area of Kaziranga National Park? → 430 sq km

q: Tungabhadra Dam is situated in ________.
qs.e: Tungabhadra Dam is located in the state of Karnataka. This dam is built on the Tungabhadra River, which is a major tributary of the Godavari River. The dam primarily serves purposes of irrigation and hydroelectric power generation. Its construction began in 1953 and was completed in 1957. The height of the dam is approximately 49.5 metres and its length is 783 metres. It is a crucial water source for both Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. The reservoir of the Tungabhadra Dam is situated at a place called Mallapuram.
qs.kf:
☛ Tungabhadra River is a tributary of which river? → Godavari
☛ Which two states dispute over Tungabhadra Dam water? → Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
☛ What is the height of Tungabhadra Dam? → 49.5 metres
☛ When was Tungabhadra Dam completed? → 1957
☛ On which river is Tungabhadra Dam built? → Tungabhadra River

q: Which among the following states has a maximum area in the forest in India? (India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2019)
qs.e: The state with the maximum forest area in India is Madhya Pradesh. According to ISFR 2019, the forest cover of Madhya Pradesh is 77,482 sq km, which is 25.14% of its total geographical area. It is followed by Arunachal Pradesh (67,248 sq km) and Chhattisgarh (55,586 sq km). Andhra Pradesh recorded the highest increase in forest cover. The extensive forests in Madhya Pradesh are due to the presence of the Vindhya and Satpura mountain ranges, which provide a favorable environment. The state also hosts several national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
qs.kf:
☛ State with largest forest area → Madhya Pradesh
☛ State with second largest forest area → Arunachal Pradesh
☛ State with third largest forest area → Chhattisgarh
☛ State with highest increase in forest cover (ISFR 2019) → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Forest cover percentage in Madhya Pradesh → 25.14%

q: Ukai Dam is located in ________
qs.e: Ukai Dam is located in the state of Gujarat on the Tapti River. It is a major multipurpose dam constructed in 1972, providing irrigation and hydroelectric power to the region. The dam's reservoir has a capacity of about 7,400 million cubic meters, and its hydroelectric plant has an installed capacity of 300 MW. Ukai Dam is situated in the Tapi district of Gujarat and is a key water resource for the state.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Ukai Dam located? → Tapti River
☛ In which year was Ukai Dam completed? → 1972
☛ What is the hydroelectric capacity of Ukai Dam? → 300 MW
☛ In which state is Ukai Dam located? → Gujarat
☛ What is the main purpose of Ukai Dam? → Irrigation and hydroelectricity

q: Sundarban National Park is located in ______
qs.e: Sundarban National Park is located in the state of West Bengal, India. It is situated in the delta region of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers. The park is renowned for the Bengal Tiger and was declared a national park in 1984. The name 'Sundarban' translates to 'beautiful forest'. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Sundarban National Park located? → West Bengal
☛ Which river delta is Sundarban in? → Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna
☛ What is Sundarban famous for? → Bengal Tiger
☛ When was Sundarban declared a national park? → 1984
☛ Which UNESCO list is Sundarban included in? → World Heritage Site

q: Which of the following regions have the highest percentage of the forest?
qs.e: Among the Indian states, Mizoram has the highest percentage of forest cover. According to the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021, Mizoram's total geographical area is 21,081 sq km, out of which 17,820 sq km (approximately 84.53%) is under forest cover. This makes Mizoram the greenest state in terms of forest percentage. After Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh (79.63%) and Meghalaya (76.33%) hold the next positions. The high forest cover in Mizoram is due to its hilly topography, low population density, and awareness among local communities about forest conservation. The forests here are mainly tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen types.
qs.kf:
☛ State with highest forest percentage → Mizoram (84.53%)
☛ State with second highest forest percentage → Arunachal Pradesh (79.63%)
☛ State with third highest forest percentage → Meghalaya (76.33%)
☛ State with lowest forest percentage → Haryana (3.63%)
☛ Agency publishing forest survey → Forest Survey of India (FSI)

q: Which of the following states is found in the Jemu Glacier state?
qs.e: The Jemu Glacier is a prominent glacier located in the state of Sikkim. Part of the eastern Himalayan ranges, it lies near the Kanchenjunga mountain range. The glacier is considered one of the sources of the Teesta River, which is a lifeline for Sikkim. Situated at an altitude of about 4,500 meters above sea level, Jemu Glacier is a popular destination for tourists and trekkers. Covering an area of approximately 26 square kilometers, it is significant for studying climate change due to melting ice. The glacier contributes to the region's freshwater supply and ecosystems.
qs.kf:
☛ Jemu Glacier is located in which state? → Sikkim
☛ Which river originates from Jemu Glacier? → Teesta River
☛ Near which mountain range is Jemu Glacier situated? → Kanchenjunga
☛ What is the largest glacier in Sikkim? → Jemu Glacier
☛ Approximate altitude of Jemu Glacier? → 4,500 meters

q: National Highway 1 goes from Delhi to ___________.
qs.e: National Highway 1 (NH-1) is a major highway in India that runs from Delhi to Amritsar. It forms a part of the historic Grand Trunk Road. NH-1 passes through Delhi, Haryana, and Punjab. Its total length is approximately 456 km. The highway terminates near Attari, close to the India-Pakistan border, which is near Amritsar. NH-1 was later merged into NH-44, but the old name is still commonly used. It is an important route for transportation and trade.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the old number of NH-1? → NH-1
☛ NH-1 is part of which historic road? → Grand Trunk Road
☛ What is the total length of NH-1? → Approximately 456 km
☛ Which state does NH-1 NOT pass through? → Uttarakhand
☛ Into which new highway was NH-1 merged? → NH-44

q: Which of the following is located in Iron and Steel Factory in Karnataka?
qs.e: The only iron and steel plant located in Karnataka is at Bhadravati. It is known as Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant (VISL). It was established in 1923 under the efforts of Sir M. Visvesvaraya. Initially, it was called Mysore Iron and Steel Works. This plant is situated on the banks of the Bhadra River. Currently, it is a unit of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL). The plant is known for producing special steel and alloy steel. It is one of the oldest steel plants in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest steel plant in India → TISCO (Jamshedpur)
☛ Headquarters of SAIL → New Delhi
☛ First public sector steel plant in India → Rourkela (1959)
☛ Location of Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant → Bhadravati (Karnataka)
☛ Bhilai Steel Plant → Chhattisgarh

q: Which states are included in Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal?
qs.e: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted to resolve the dispute over the sharing of waters of the Vansadhara River. This river flows through the states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh and meets the Bay of Bengal. There has been a long-standing conflict between the two states regarding water allocation, dam construction, and irrigation projects. The central government formed this tribunal under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956. The tribunal aims to determine a fair and equitable distribution of the river's water, taking into account the interests of both states.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Vansadhara River → Hills of Kalahandi district, Odisha
☛ Total length of Vansadhara River → Approximately 254 km
☛ Chairman of Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal → Justice R. K. Patnaik
☛ Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 → Empowers central government to constitute tribunals for resolving river water disputes
☛ Drainage system of Vansadhara River → Falls into the Bay of Bengal

q: Sardar Sarovar dam is located in
qs.e: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is located in the state of Gujarat on the Narmada River. It is the second largest concrete gravity dam in the world. The dam was built in memory of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The Sardar Sarovar Project includes the dam, a canal system, and hydroelectric power generation. This dam provides water and electricity to Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Its height is 163 meters and it controls the flow of the Narmada River.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Sardar Sarovar Dam built? → Narmada River
☛ What type of dam is it? → Concrete gravity dam
☛ What is its height? → 163 meters
☛ In which state is it located? → Gujarat
☛ How many states benefit from this project? → Four states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra)

q: Pench National Park is situated in ________________
qs.e: Pench National Park is located on the border of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. Its core area lies in Seoni and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh. The park is named after the Pench River that flows through it. It was declared a national park in 1975 and is a part of Project Tiger. The park is home to tigers, leopards, wolves, and chital. It is famous for its biodiversity and tourism.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river flows through Pench National Park? → Pench River
☛ In which year was Pench National Park established? → 1975
☛ Which states share the Pench National Park? → Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
☛ Which project is Pench National Park associated with? → Project Tiger
☛ What is the primary state of Pench National Park? → Madhya Pradesh

q: Two main methods of cultivating Indigo were ______ and _____.
qs.e: The two main methods of cultivating Indigo were Ryoti and Nij. In the Ryoti system, peasants were forced to grow indigo under contract, while in the Nij system, landlords cultivated indigo on their own land. Both systems were prevalent in Bengal and Bihar during British rule for indigo production. The Ryoti system was more exploitative, leading to peasant discontent and the Indigo Revolt (1859-60). The Nij system gave landlords more direct control.
qs.kf:
☛ Two main methods of cultivating Indigo → Ryoti and Nij
☛ Ryoti system meaning → Peasants forced to grow indigo under contract
☛ Nij system → Landlords grew indigo on their own land
☛ Year of Indigo Revolt → 1859-60
☛ Main area of Indigo Revolt → Bengal (Nadia district)

q: Where is Vansda National Park located?
qs.e: Vansda National Park is located in the state of Gujarat, specifically in Navsari district. It was declared a national park in 1979 and covers an area of about 24 sq km. The park is known for its rich biodiversity and hosts wildlife like leopard, sloth bear, and spotted deer. It lies within the Western Ghats region.
qs.kf:
☛ Vansda National Park is in which state? → Gujarat
☛ When was Vansda National Park established? → 1979
☛ What is the area of Vansda National Park? → 24 sq km
☛ How many national parks are in Gujarat? → 4
☛ Which is the largest national park in Gujarat? → Gir National Park

q: India’s first National Centre for Marine Bio-diversity (NCMB) is located in-
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (D) Jamnagar

q: In which of the following Indian states/Union Territories is Dal Lake situated?
qs.e: Dal Lake is located in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is situated in Srinagar city and is renowned for its natural beauty, shikaras, and houseboats. The lake was formed by the melting of Himalayan glaciers. It covers an area of approximately 18 square kilometers. Dal Lake is often referred to as the "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir" or the "Soul of Srinagar." It also supports an important irrigation system. Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Gujarat do not have Dal Lake.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Dal Lake located? → Jammu and Kashmir
☛ In which city is Dal Lake situated? → Srinagar
☛ What is the nickname of Dal Lake? → Jewel in the crown of Kashmir
☛ What is the area of Dal Lake? → Approximately 18 sq km
☛ What is found in Dal Lake? → Shikaras and houseboats

q: In which district of Jharkhand is Tagore Hill located?
qs.e: Tagore Hill is located in the Ranchi district of Jharkhand. This hill is associated with the famous poet Rabindranath Tagore, who spent some time here. It is situated about 5 km from the main city area of Ranchi and is also known as 'Morhabadi'. The height of Tagore Hill is approximately 300 meters, and it offers a panoramic view of Ranchi city. It is a popular picnic spot among tourists and locals. Ranchi district is one of the major districts of Jharkhand and was established in 1899. The hill holds historical and cultural significance, attracting visitors interested in literature and nature.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Tagore Hill located? → Ranchi, Jharkhand
☛ What is the other name of Tagore Hill? → Morhabadi
☛ Which river flows through Ranchi? → Swarnarekha River
☛ What is the capital of Jharkhand? → Ranchi
☛ When was Ranchi district established? → 1899

q: Which is India's eastern most state?
qs.e: India's easternmost state is Arunachal Pradesh. It is located in Northeast India and is known for its natural beauty and cultural diversity. Its capital is Itanagar. Arunachal Pradesh shares international borders with China to the north, Myanmar to the east, and Bhutan to the west. It also borders the Indian states of Assam and Nagaland to the south. The state is home to numerous indigenous tribes, including Adi, Nyishi, and Monpa. It is famous for Buddhist monasteries, trekking trails, and wildlife sanctuaries. The easternmost point of India is located in Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ India's easternmost state → Arunachal Pradesh
☛ Capital of Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar
☛ Neighbouring countries of Arunachal Pradesh → China, Myanmar, Bhutan
☛ Major tribes of Arunachal Pradesh → Adi, Nyishi, Monpa
☛ Easternmost point of India → Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh

q: Amindivi and Minicoy are parts of which Indian Union Territory?
qs.e: The Amindivi and Minicoy islands are part of the Lakshadweep Union Territory. Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory of India, comprising 36 islands. It is located in the Arabian Sea and is known for its coral reefs. The Amindivi group lies in the northern part, while Minicoy is in the southern part. The administrative headquarters of Lakshadweep is Kavaratti. This Union Territory is famous for its natural beauty and marine life. In 1956, under the States Reorganization Act, Lakshadweep was made a separate Union Territory.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest island of Lakshadweep → Andrott
☛ Administrative headquarters of Lakshadweep → Kavaratti
☛ Official language of Lakshadweep → Malayalam
☛ Total number of islands in Lakshadweep → 36
☛ Southernmost island of Lakshadweep → Minicoy

q: Which of these is a hill station in Rajasthan?
qs.e: Mount Abu is the only hill station in Rajasthan, located in the Sirohi district. It is part of the Aravalli Range and situated at an altitude of about 1220 meters above sea level. Mount Abu is known for its natural beauty and historical significance. It houses the famous Dilwara Temples, an important pilgrimage site for Jainism. Other major attractions include Nakki Lake and Sunset Point. Among other options, Kasauli is in Himachal Pradesh, Panchgani in Maharashtra, and Nainital in Uttarakhand. Hence, Mount Abu is the correct answer as the only hill station in Rajasthan.
qs.kf:
☛ Only hill station of Rajasthan → Mount Abu
☛ Mount Abu is located in which district → Sirohi
☛ Height of Mount Abu → 1220 meters
☛ Famous temple in Mount Abu → Dilwara Temples
☛ Famous lake in Mount Abu → Nakki Lake

q: What is the name of the border line between India and China?
qs.e: The border line between India and China is called the McMahon Line. It was established under the Simla Convention of 1914 between British India and Tibet, and was drawn by British officer Henry McMahon. This line demarcates the boundary between Arunachal Pradesh (India) and China's Tibet Autonomous Region. China does not recognize the McMahon Line and considers it illegal, leading to an ongoing border dispute between the two countries. The line is about 890 km long and remains a contentious issue in bilateral relations.
qs.kf:
☛ India-China border line → McMahon Line
☛ Treaty establishing McMahon Line → Simla Convention (1914)
☛ Who drew the McMahon Line → Henry McMahon
☛ India-Pakistan border line → Radcliffe Line
☛ India-Afghanistan border line → Durand Line

q: In which of the following cities is the longest beach in India located?
qs.e: The longest beach in India is Marina Beach located in Chennai. It is approximately 13 kilometers long and is the second longest urban beach in the world. It lies along the Bay of Bengal. Marina Beach is a major tourist attraction in Chennai. Among the options, Mangalore, Mumbai, and Cochin also have beaches, but they are shorter than Marina Beach. The sunrise and sunset views at Marina Beach are very beautiful.
qs.kf:
☛ Longest beach in India → Marina Beach, Chennai
☛ Second longest urban beach in the world → Marina Beach
☛ Marina Beach is located on which bay → Bay of Bengal
☛ Length of Marina Beach → Approximately 13 km
☛ Major beach in Chennai → Marina Beach

q: The Sabarmati River originates from which Indian State?
qs.e: The Sabarmati River originates from Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary in the Aravalli mountain range, located in the Udaipur district of Rajasthan. It flows in a southwesterly direction, enters Gujarat, passes through Ahmedabad city, and ultimately falls into the Gulf of Khambhat. The total length of the Sabarmati is approximately 371 kilometers. On the banks of this river lies the historic Sabarmati Ashram, associated with Mahatma Gandhi. This river is important for both Rajasthan and Gujarat states.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Sabarmati River → Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary, Rajasthan
☛ Mountain range of Sabarmati → Aravalli
☛ Mouth of Sabarmati → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ Length of Sabarmati → 371 km
☛ Ashram on Sabarmati banks → Sabarmati Ashram (associated with Gandhi)

q: In which of the following states is the Gir National Park located?
qs.e: Gir National Park is located in the state of Gujarat, in the districts of Junagadh and Gir Somnath. It is famous for the Asiatic lion, an endangered species of lion. The park was declared a national park in 1965 and covers an area of about 1412 square kilometers. Apart from lions, it is home to leopards, sambar, chital, nilgai, and various birds. Gir National Park is the last natural habitat of the Asiatic lion, and significant conservation efforts have been made to protect them. Currently, there are around 674 lions in the park.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Gir National Park in? → Gujarat
☛ What is Gir National Park famous for? → Asiatic lion
☛ When was Gir National Park established? → 1965
☛ What is the area of Gir National Park? → 1412 sq km
☛ Which is the last natural habitat of the Asiatic lion? → Gir National Park

q: In which Indian state is the greater part of the Desert located?
qs.e: The greater part of the Indian desert is located in the state of Rajasthan, known as the Thar Desert or the Great Indian Desert. This desert extends into parts of Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana but its largest portion lies in Rajasthan. The Thar Desert covers an area of approximately 2,00,000 sq km and is the 17th largest desert in the world. In Rajasthan, it spreads across districts like Jaisalmer, Barmer, Jodhpur, and Bikaner. The annual rainfall here is less than 25 cm, and summer temperatures can reach up to 50°C. The desert is known for its sand dunes and wildlife.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state contains the largest part of the Thar Desert? → Rajasthan
☛ What is the area of the Thar Desert? → Approximately 2,00,000 sq km
☛ What is the rank of the Thar Desert in the world? → 17th largest desert
☛ Which districts in Rajasthan have the Thar Desert? → Jaisalmer, Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner
☛ What is the annual rainfall in the Thar Desert? → Less than 25 cm

q: In which of the following places is Malampuzha dam located?
qs.e: Malampuzha dam is located in the Palakkad district of Kerala. It is built on the Malampuzha River and is the second largest dam in Kerala. The dam was completed in 1955 and is important for irrigation and drinking water supply. It features a scenic garden and a boating facility, making it a popular tourist destination. The dam is situated at the foothills of the Western Ghats, and the Kannan Devan Hills Produce Company assisted in its construction.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Malampuzha dam located? → Kerala
☛ On which river is Malampuzha dam built? → Malampuzha River
☛ In which district is Malampuzha dam situated? → Palakkad
☛ When was Malampuzha dam completed? → 1955
☛ What is the purpose of Malampuzha dam? → Irrigation and drinking water

q: In which Indian state is the white Desert located? A. Gujarat
B. Tamil Nadu
C. Jammu and Kashmir
D. Sikkim
qs.e: The white desert of India, also known as the Rann of Kutch, is located in the state of Gujarat. It is a vast salt marsh that gets submerged during the monsoon and covered with a white layer of salt in winter. This region is famous for its unique geographical structure and biodiversity. The Rann of Kutch is divided into two parts: the Great Rann of Kutch and the Little Rann of Kutch. It is a major tourist attraction, especially during winter when the Rann Utsav is celebrated. People from all over the world visit to witness the white desert. The area is also home to various migratory birds.
qs.kf:
☛ Scientific name of white desert → Rann of Kutch
☛ State where white desert is located → Gujarat
☛ Largest part of Rann of Kutch → Great Rann of Kutch
☛ When Rann Utsav is celebrated → Winter
☛ Animal found in Rann of Kutch → Wild ass

q: Mica is available abundantly in which state?
A. West Bengal
B. Madhya Pradesh
C. Bihar
D. Rajasthan
qs.e: Mica is an important mineral used in electrical insulators, paints, and cosmetics. India is the world's leading producer of mica. Rajasthan has the largest deposits of mica, especially in Ajmer, Bhilwara, and Tonk districts. The mica here is of high quality. Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand also have mica reserves, but Rajasthan is the top producer. Mica is formed in igneous and metamorphic rocks. Rajasthan's mineral wealth makes it industrially significant.
qs.kf:
☛ India's rank in mica production → First
☛ Major mica producing district of Rajasthan → Ajmer
☛ Use of mica → Electrical insulator
☛ Mica is found in which type of rock → Igneous and metamorphic
☛ Chemical name of mica → Muscovite

q: Where is the Masai Mara National Reserve?
A. Mali
B. Kenya
C. Gabon
D. Zambia
qs.e: The Masai Mara National Reserve is located in southwestern Kenya. It borders Tanzania's Serengeti National Park and is one of Africa's most famous wildlife conservation areas. The reserve is named after the Maasai people who inhabit the region. It is renowned for the annual Great Migration of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles. The reserve hosts a high density of wildlife including lions, leopards, cheetahs, and elephants. Though not a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is a major tourist destination. The landscape consists of open grasslands, rivers, and acacia woodlands.
qs.kf:
☛ Masai Mara is located in which country? → Kenya
☛ Which national park shares a border with Masai Mara? → Serengeti
☛ Masai Mara is named after which tribe? → Maasai
☛ What is Masai Mara famous for? → Wildlife migration
☛ What is the capital of Kenya? → Nairobi

q: The Dibru-Saikhowa, Nameri and Orang National Park are all found in which state?
A. Andhra Pradesh
B. Assam
C. Arunachal Pradesh
D. Uttarakhand
qs.e: Dibru-Saikhowa, Nameri and Orang National Parks are all located in the state of Assam. Dibru-Saikhowa National Park is situated in Tinsukia district along the Brahmaputra and Dibru rivers. Nameri National Park lies in Sonitpur district and is part of the Eastern Himalayas biodiversity hotspot. Orang National Park, also known as Rajiv Gandhi Orang National Park, spans Darrang and Sonitpur districts of Assam. These three parks are known for their rich biodiversity and wildlife, including rare species like white-winged wood duck and tiger.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state has Dibru-Saikhowa National Park? → Assam
☛ Nameri National Park is known for? → Bird diversity and tiger
☛ Alternative name for Orang National Park? → Rajiv Gandhi Orang National Park
☛ Which river is common near these parks? → Brahmaputra and its tributaries
☛ How many national parks are there in Assam? → 7 (as of 2025)

q: India covers _______ of earth's land area. (approximate)
qs.e: India's total geographical area is approximately 3.287 million square kilometers. The total land area of the earth is about 13.7 crore sq km. India's area accounts for about 2.4% of the world's total land area. This makes India the seventh largest country in the world by area. Countries larger than India in terms of area include Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil, and Australia. Notably, India covers only 2.4% of the world's land area but is home to more than 17% of the global population, highlighting its high population density. This fact is frequently tested in competitive exams.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total area of India? → Approx. 3.287 million sq km
☛ Which is the seventh largest country by area? → India
☛ What percentage of world's land area does India cover? → 2.4%
☛ Which country is larger than India in area after the top six? → Australia (eighth largest)
☛ What percentage of world population lives in India? → Over 17%

q: Bangladesh has a land border with
A. Only India
B. India and Myanmar
C. India and Bhutan
D. India and China
qs.e: Bangladesh shares its land borders with only two countries: India and Myanmar. The Bangladesh-India border is approximately 4,096 km long, making it the fifth-longest land border in the world. The Bangladesh-Myanmar border is about 271 km long, located in the southeastern part of the country. Bhutan and China do not share a land border with Bangladesh. The total land area of Bangladesh is about 1,47,570 sq km.
qs.kf:
☛ Total land border length of Bangladesh → 4,367 km
☛ Longest land border of Bangladesh is with → India
☛ Second land border of Bangladesh is with → Myanmar
☛ Area of Bangladesh → about 1,47,570 sq km
☛ Length of Bangladesh-India border → about 4,096 km

q: Ajanta caves in Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, in which about 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves were built, how ancient was that? A. 8th century BC B. 2nd century BC C. 6th century BC
D. 4th century BC
qs.e: The Ajanta Caves are located in Aurangabad district of Maharashtra. These are about 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves that were built from the 2nd century BC to the 6th century AD. The earliest caves (Cave 9, 10, 12, 13) were constructed during the Hinayana phase in the 2nd century BC, while later caves (Cave 1, 2, 16, 17, 19, 26) were built in the 5th-6th centuries AD during the Mahayana phase. These caves are renowned for their paintings and sculptures and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.kf:
☛ Period of Ajanta cave construction → 2nd century BC to 6th century AD
☛ Early Ajanta cave numbers → Cave 9, 10, 12, 13 (Hinayana)
☛ Total number of Ajanta caves → 30 (29 caves + 1 unfinished)
☛ Location of Ajanta → Aurangabad, Maharashtra
☛ Ajanta caves are famous for → Buddhist paintings and sculptures

q: Kanha National Park is in which state?
A. Uttar Pradesh
B. Madhya Pradesh
C. Rajasthan
D. Uttarakhand
qs.e: Kanha National Park is located in the state of Madhya Pradesh, specifically in the districts of Mandla and Balaghat. It is one of the oldest national parks in India, established in 1955. The park is famous for its tiger conservation efforts and the barasingha (swamp deer). It is a key area under Project Tiger and is known for its rich biodiversity. Kanha covers an area of approximately 940 sq km and is home to tigers, leopards, bears, and numerous bird species. The park's landscape consists of sal and bamboo forests, grasslands, and streams.
qs.kf:
☛ Kanha National Park is in which state? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Kanha is famous for which species? → Tiger and barasingha
☛ When was Kanha established? → 1955
☛ Kanha is located in which districts? → Mandla and Balaghat
☛ Kanha is part of which project? → Project Tiger

q: Which state in India is the highest producer of raw silk?
A. Kerala B. Andhra Pradesh C. Karnataka D. Maharashtra
qs.e: Karnataka is the highest producer of raw silk in India, contributing approximately 40% of the country's total silk production. The major silk-producing districts in Karnataka are Mysuru and Ramanagara. The state's climate and soil are suitable for mulberry cultivation, which is the primary food source for silkworms. India is the second largest silk producer in the world after China, and Karnataka leads the domestic production. Other significant silk-producing states include Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest silk-producing state in India → Karnataka
☛ Second largest silk-producing state in India → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Largest silk-producing country in the world → China
☛ Major types of silk in India → Mulberry, Tasar, Eri, Muga
☛ Central organization for silk in India → Central Silk Board

q: The largest state (in terms of area) in India is:
qs.e: The largest state in India by area is Rajasthan, with an area of approximately 3,42,239 sq km, which constitutes about 10.4% of India's total geographical area. The capital of Rajasthan is Jaipur, and it is often referred to as the 'Land of Kings'. The state is famous for the Thar Desert, historic forts, and rich cultural heritage. Rajasthan shares its border with Pakistan and the states of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat. In terms of area, Madhya Pradesh is the second largest and Maharashtra is the third largest state in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest state in India (by area) → Rajasthan
☛ Area of Rajasthan → 3,42,239 sq km
☛ Capital of Rajasthan → Jaipur
☛ States bordering Rajasthan → Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat
☛ Second largest state (by area) → Madhya Pradesh

q: Goecha La is a pass in which of the following Indian State?
A. Sikkim B. Assam C. Meghalaya D. Uttarakhand
qs.e: Goecha La is a high mountain pass located in the Indian state of Sikkim. It remains covered with snow and is situated at an elevation of approximately 4940 meters above sea level. Goecha La is near the Kanchenjunga National Park and is a popular destination for trekkers. The pass is famous for offering stunning views of the Kanchenjunga mountain. Other notable passes in Sikkim include Nathu La and Jelep La. The trek to Goecha La starts from Yuksom. This pass is an important part of Sikkim's natural beauty and biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Goecha La in? → Sikkim
☛ What is the elevation of Goecha La? → 4940 meters
☛ Which national park is near Goecha La? → Kanchenjunga National Park
☛ Which mountain is visible from Goecha La? → Kanchenjunga
☛ What are other major passes in Sikkim? → Nathu La and Jelep La

q: Which of the following states does not share a border with Myanmar?
A. Assam
B. Mizoram
C. Nagaland
D. Manipur
qs.e: Four Indian states share an international border with Myanmar: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram. Assam does not share a border with Myanmar. The total length of the India-Myanmar border is approximately 1,643 kilometers. This border is strategically important for Northeast India. Assam shares its borders with Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, West Bengal, and Tripura, but not with Myanmar.
qs.kf:
☛ How many Indian states share a border with Myanmar? → 4 (Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram)
☛ What is the length of the India-Myanmar border? → Approximately 1,643 km
☛ Which state does not share a border with Myanmar? → Assam
☛ Which northeastern state does not share a border with Myanmar? → Assam
☛ Which town is located on the India-Myanmar border? → Moreh (Manipur)

q: South West Monsoon generates in _______ A. Arabian Sea
B. Pacific Ocean C. Bay of Bengal D. Himalayas
qs.e: The South West Monsoon originates in the Arabian Sea. This monsoon is the primary source of rainfall in India. During summer, intense heating of the Indian subcontinent creates a low-pressure area, drawing moisture-laden winds from the Indian Ocean. These winds are known as the South West Monsoon. The branch from the Arabian Sea brings rainfall to the Western Ghats and northwestern India. Another branch comes from the Bay of Bengal and moves northeastwards. Thus, the South West Monsoon originates in the Arabian Sea, not in the Pacific Ocean or Himalayas. The monsoon is crucial for Indian agriculture and economy.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does South West Monsoon originate? → Arabian Sea
☛ What causes monsoon in India? → Differential heating of land and sea
☛ Which region gets rain from Arabian Sea branch? → Western Ghats and Northwestern India
☛ Where does the Bay of Bengal branch go? → Northeastwards
☛ From which language is the word monsoon derived? → Arabic

q: Which state of India produces the highest quantity of Jute?
A. Bihar
B. Odisha
C. West Bengal
D. Jharkhand
qs.e: In India, the highest production of jute occurs in the state of West Bengal. It accounts for over 70% of the country's jute output, mainly in the Hooghly River basin. Jute cultivation requires a warm and humid climate, high rainfall, and alluvial soil, all of which are abundant in West Bengal. According to 2018-19 data, West Bengal produced about 1.2 crore bales of jute, which is roughly 50% of India's total production. Other major producers include Bihar, Assam, and Odisha. Jute is used for making sacks, ropes, carpets, and paper.
qs.kf:
☛ Scientific name of jute fibre → Corchorus capsularis (white jute) and Corchorus olitorius (tossa jute)
☛ Largest producer of jute in the world → India
☛ Second largest jute producing state in India → Bihar
☛ Ideal temperature for jute cultivation → 24-35 °C
☛ Annual rainfall required for jute → 150-250 cm

q: The river Godavari does NOT pass through which of the following states?
A. Maharashtra
B. Gujarat
C. Chhattisgarh
D. Andhra Pradesh
qs.e: The Godavari river flows through the states of Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh, but does not pass through Gujarat. It originates in the Trimbakeshwar hills of the Western Ghats in Maharashtra and empties into the Bay of Bengal. Godavari is the second longest river in India, with a length of about 1465 km. It is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Ganga of the South'. The river flows through Nasik, Aurangabad (Maharashtra), Bastar (Chhattisgarh), Warangal, Khammam (Telangana), and Rajahmundry (Andhra Pradesh). The Godavari basin is the largest in India by area.
qs.kf:
☛ Source of Godavari river → Trimbakeshwar, Nasik (Maharashtra)
☛ Tributary of Godavari → Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira
☛ Famous dam on Godavari → Sriram Sagar Project (Telangana)
☛ Godavari is called → Dakshin Ganga (Vriddha Ganga)
☛ Total length of Godavari → About 1465 km

q: The largest border of India with which country?
A. Pakistan
B. Bangladesh
C. China
D. Nepal
qs.e: India's longest international border is with Bangladesh, stretching approximately 4,096.7 km. This border touches five Indian states: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. The India-Bangladesh border includes several enclaves and exclaves, such as Dahagram-Angarpota. In comparison, India's border with China is about 3,488 km, with Pakistan about 3,323 km, and with Nepal about 1,751 km. A significant portion of the Bangladesh border is defined by rivers and forests, making management challenging. The border agreement between India and Bangladesh was signed in 1974 and finalized under the Land Boundary Agreement in 2015.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country shares the longest border with India? → Bangladesh (4,096.7 km)
☛ How many Indian states touch the India-Bangladesh border? → Five (West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram)
☛ Length of India-China border? → Approximately 3,488 km
☛ What is the India-Pakistan border called? → Radcliffe Line (about 3,323 km)
☛ Length of India-Nepal border? → Approximately 1,751 km

q: Which of the following does not belong to the group?
A. Lakshadweep
B. Puducherry
C. Nicobar
D. Andaman
qs.e: Lakshadweep, Nicobar, and Andaman are Union Territories of India that are island groups. Lakshadweep is an archipelago in the Arabian Sea, while Andaman and Nicobar are two separate island groups in the Bay of Bengal. Puducherry is also a Union Territory, but it is not an island group; it is located on the mainland and consists of four scattered districts. Therefore, Puducherry does not belong to the group as the other three are island groups.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Union Territory is not an island group? → Puducherry
☛ Which Union Territories are island groups in India? → Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands
☛ Where is Lakshadweep located? → Arabian Sea
☛ Where are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands located? → Bay of Bengal
☛ Which Union Territory has four districts? → Puducherry

q: Eastern boundary of Kashmir is A. LOC B. Jammu C. POK
D. Ladakh region
qs.e: The eastern boundary of Kashmir is the Ladakh region. Ladakh is a union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, sharing borders with the Karakoram mountain range and Tibet. It is known for its high-altitude desert and places like Leh-Ladakh. The LOC (Line of Control) lies on the western boundary and is the de facto border between India and Pakistan. Jammu is in the southern region, while POK (Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir) lies west across the LOC. Hence, the eastern boundary is Ladakh, extending to the Siachen Glacier and the China border.
qs.kf:
☛ Newly formed Union Territory from J&K → Ladakh
☛ LOC is the boundary between → India and Pakistan
☛ Region to the east of Kashmir → Ladakh
☛ Capital of Ladakh → Leh and Kargil
☛ Siachen Glacier is located in → Ladakh

q: Which of the following state have highest number of Lignite coal reserve?
qs.e: India's largest lignite coal reserves are located in Tamilnadu. The Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC) is the major producer here. After Tamilnadu, lignite reserves are found in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir. Lignite is also called brown coal, a low-grade form of coal with lower calorific value and higher moisture content. It is used for electricity generation. Odisha and Jharkhand have more bituminous coal reserves, not lignite. Assam has minor lignite deposits. Thus, among the given options, Tamilnadu has the highest lignite reserves.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest lignite producing state in India → Tamilnadu
☛ Location of Neyveli Lignite Corporation → Tamilnadu
☛ Lignite is also known as → Brown coal
☛ Quality of lignite → Low grade, high moisture
☛ Major bituminous coal states → Jharkhand, Odisha

q: In which state is the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary located?
qs.e: Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Chikkamagaluru district of Karnataka state. It is part of the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot and was established in 1974. Spanning approximately 492 sq km, it lies in the catchment area of the Bhadra River. The sanctuary is known for wildlife such as tiger, leopard, elephant, sambar, and spotted deer. It was declared a tiger reserve in 1998 under Project Tiger. The area is surrounded by the Mullayanagiri and Baba Budangiri hills.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary located? → Karnataka
☛ When was it declared a tiger reserve? → 1998
☛ Which river's catchment does it lie in? → Bhadra River
☛ Which district is it in? → Chikkamagaluru
☛ Under which project is it a tiger reserve? → Project Tiger

q: In which state did India's White Revolution have its origin?
qs.e: India's White Revolution, also known as the Dairy Revolution, originated in Anand, Gujarat. It was spearheaded by Dr. Verghese Kurien, known as the 'Milkman of India'. In 1970, he established 'Amul' in Anand and promoted dairy cooperatives to enhance milk production. The revolution was implemented through a program called 'Operation Flood', which transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest milk producer. The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), headquartered in Anand, played a pivotal role in replicating the Anand model across the country. The White Revolution not only boosted rural economy but also empowered millions of small farmers.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of White Revolution in India? → Dr. Verghese Kurien
☛ Which scheme is related to White Revolution? → Operation Flood
☛ Where is the main center of White Revolution? → Anand, Gujarat
☛ Headquarters of National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)? → Anand, Gujarat
☛ Which state is associated with the Amul brand? → Gujarat

q: Name the major river that flows through the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
qs.e: The Damanganga river flows through the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. It originates in the Dang district of Gujarat and is approximately 80 km long. After passing through Dadra and Nagar Haveli, it empties into the Arabian Sea. The river is named after the town of Daman located at its mouth. It is a vital source for agriculture and water supply in the region. Other options: Pinjal flows in Maharashtra, Narmada flows through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, and Par is a minor river in Gujarat.
qs.kf:
☛ Major river of Dadra and Nagar Haveli → Damanganga
☛ Origin of Damanganga → Dang district, Gujarat
☛ Mouth of Damanganga → Arabian Sea
☛ Capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli → Silvassa
☛ Length of Damanganga → Approx. 80 km

q: Girnar Hills of Junagadh, Gujarat is famous for ________ Mangoes.
qs.e: The Girnar Hills are located in the Junagadh district of Gujarat, and this region is famous for Kesar mangoes. Kesar mangoes are known for their bright yellow color, distinct aroma, and sweet taste. They have received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Among the other options, Totapuri is popular in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, Alphonso (also known as Hapus) is from the Ratnagiri region of Maharashtra, and Dasheri is from the Lucknow region of Uttar Pradesh. In Gujarat, the Kesar mango is a major export variety, often called the "Queen of Mangoes."
qs.kf:
☛ Which mango is famous from Girnar Hills? → Kesar
☛ What is the GI-tagged mango of Gujarat? → Kesar
☛ Where is Alphonso mango primarily grown? → Maharashtra (Ratnagiri)
☛ Dasheri mango is associated with which state? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ Totapuri mango is mainly grown in which states? → Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu

q: Which of the following cities is NOT in Madhya Pradesh?
qs.e: Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh, which was formed in 2000 after being carved out of Madhya Pradesh. Major cities of Madhya Pradesh include Bhopal (capital), Jabalpur (located on Narmada river), and Gwalior (historical city). Thus, Raipur is not in Madhya Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Madhya Pradesh → Bhopal
☛ City on Narmada river in MP → Jabalpur
☛ Famous historical city in MP → Gwalior
☛ Area of Madhya Pradesh → 3,08,252 sq km
☛ Neighbouring states of MP → Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra

q: Sariska National Park is located in :
qs.e: Sariska National Park is located in the Alwar district of Rajasthan. It was established as a wildlife sanctuary in 1955 and later declared a national park in 1978. The park is known for its population of Bengal tigers, leopards, sambar deer, and various bird species. It is part of the Aravalli Hills and features dry deciduous forests. Sariska is an important tiger reserve under Project Tiger. In 2004, tigers became extinct from the park due to poaching, but they were reintroduced through a relocation program. The park also contains historical ruins, including the Kankwari Fort.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Sariska National Park located? → Rajasthan
☛ When was Sariska declared a National Park? → 1978
☛ Which major wildlife species is found in Sariska? → Bengal Tiger
☛ Under which project does Sariska come? → Project Tiger
☛ In which district is Sariska National Park located? → Alwar

q: The Challenger Deep in the _______ is considered to be the deepest point known on Earth.
qs.e: The Challenger Deep is located in the Mariana Trench and is considered the deepest known point on Earth. It is situated in the Pacific Ocean near the Mariana Islands. The depth of Challenger Deep is approximately 11,034 meters. It was discovered in 1951 by the British survey ship HMS Challenger. The Mariana Trench is a subduction zone where the Pacific Plate is subducted under the Philippine Plate. The trench is about 2,550 kilometers long and 69 kilometers wide. The first manned descent to Challenger Deep was made in 1960 by Don Walsh and Jacques Piccard in the bathyscaphe Trieste.
qs.kf:
☛ Deepest point on Earth → Mariana Trench
☛ Depth of Challenger Deep → Approximately 11,034 meters
☛ Year of discovery of Challenger Deep → 1951
☛ First manned descent to Challenger Deep → 1960, by Don Walsh and Jacques Piccard
☛ Ocean where Mariana Trench is located → Pacific Ocean

q: The Ajanta caves are located in ___________.
qs.e: The Ajanta caves are located in Maharashtra state, in Aurangabad district. These caves belong to Buddhist tradition and are famous for their exquisite paintings and sculptures. The caves were built in two phases: first phase around 2nd century BCE and second phase during 5th-6th century CE (Vakataka period). Ajanta caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and consist of 30 caves. The murals depict Jataka tales and events from Buddha's life.
qs.kf:
☛ Where are the Ajanta caves located? → Maharashtra
☛ Which religion are the Ajanta caves associated with? → Buddhism
☛ During which period were the Ajanta caves built? → 2nd century BCE and Vakataka period
☛ How many Ajanta caves are there? → 30
☛ Which organization declared Ajanta caves as a World Heritage site? → UNESCO

q: Which of the following is the largest bauxite producing states of India?
qs.e: The largest bauxite producing state in India is Odisha. Odisha accounts for more than 50% of the total bauxite reserves of the country. The major bauxite mines are located in the districts of Koraput, Kalahandi, and Bolangir. Bauxite is the primary ore for the production of aluminium. India ranks fifth in the world in bauxite production. Apart from Odisha, other leading bauxite producing states include Gujarat, Jharkhand, and Maharashtra. The Panchpatmali and Gandhamardan hills are major sources of bauxite in Odisha.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest bauxite producing state → Odisha
☛ Second largest bauxite producing state → Gujarat
☛ Main use of bauxite → Aluminium production
☛ Bauxite is an ore of → Aluminium
☛ India's rank in world bauxite production → Fifth

q: The Keoladeo Ghana National Park is situated in_____.
qs.e: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is located in the Bharatpur district of Rajasthan, India. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. The park is famous as a bird sanctuary and hosts many migratory birds, including the Siberian Crane. Originally, it was a private duck hunting reserve for the maharajas, later declared a national park in 1982. The name derives from the Keoladeo temple and the word 'ghana' meaning dense area.
qs.kf:
☛ Keoladeo Ghana National Park is in which district? → Bharatpur
☛ When was Keoladeo Ghana declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1985
☛ Keoladeo Ghana is famous for? → Bird diversity
☛ What was Keoladeo Ghana earlier? → Hunting reserve
☛ How many national parks are in Rajasthan? → 4

q: Which of the following cities is known as “The Queen of the Arabian Sea'?
qs.e: Kochi (formerly known as Cochin) is called the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea'. It is a major port city in the state of Kerala, located on the coast of the Arabian Sea. Historically, Kochi was a significant trading center for spices, silk, and other goods. In the 15th century, Portuguese, Dutch, and British colonizers established settlements here. Its natural harbor and backwaters also make it a prominent tourist destination. Kochi earned this title due to its strategic geographical location and commercial importance. Among the other options, Mumbai is known as the 'City of Dreams', Visakhapatnam as the 'Goa of the East', and Port Blair as the capital of the Andaman Islands.
qs.kf:
☛ Major port city in Kerala → Kochi
☛ Former name of Kochi → Cochin
☛ Sea on which Kochi is located → Arabian Sea
☛ First European colonial center in India → Kochi (Portuguese)
☛ Popular tourist attractions in Kochi → Backwaters and Marine Drive

q: Where is Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport located?
qs.e: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport is located in Amritsar, Punjab. It is named after Guru Ram Das, the fourth Sikh Guru. The airport connects Amritsar to domestic and international destinations and is significant for pilgrims visiting the nearby Golden Temple. It is the largest and busiest airport in Punjab.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport located? → Amritsar, Punjab
☛ After whom is this airport named? → Guru Ram Das (fourth Sikh Guru)
☛ What is the famous religious site in Amritsar? → Golden Temple
☛ Which is the largest airport in Punjab? → Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar
☛ Which river is Amritsar situated on? → Beas River

q: What is contour ploughing?
o: Ploughing on sloping land along the contour lines.
Ploughing on plains along the contour lines
Ploughing on barren land along the contour lines.
Ploughing in a zig-zag manner along the contour lines.
qs.e: Contour ploughing is an agricultural practice where ploughing is done on sloping land along the contour lines. Its main objective is to prevent soil erosion and conserve water. When ploughing is done up and down the slope, water flows quickly and carries away the topsoil. By ploughing along contour lines, water runoff is slowed down, allowing more water to infiltrate into the soil. This helps in maintaining soil moisture and fertility, especially in hilly or mountainous regions. Contour ploughing is an effective method for sustainable farming on slopes.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main purpose of contour ploughing? → To prevent soil erosion and conserve water.
☛ On which type of land is it practiced? → Sloping land.
☛ In which direction is ploughing done? → Along contour lines.
☛ What is the opposite practice called? → Up and down ploughing.
☛ Which natural disaster is reduced by this technique? → Soil erosion.

q: Which Indian state has the largest mica reserves?
qs.e: The largest mica reserves in India are found in Andhra Pradesh, especially in the Nellore district. This mica is of high quality and is used in the electrical industry, electronics, and cosmetics. India is the world's leading producer of mica, and Andhra Pradesh contributes about 40% of the total production. Apart from this, mica deposits are also found in Rajasthan and Jharkhand, but Andhra Pradesh holds the prime position. Mica is a natural mineral with a layered structure, used in sheet or powder form. It is valued for its electrical insulation properties and heat resistance.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest mica producing state → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Major mica mining areas → Nellore (Andhra Pradesh), Ajmer (Rajasthan)
☛ Uses of mica → Electrical insulators, electronics, paints
☛ World's largest mica producer → India
☛ India's share in mica production → About 60%

q: Slash and burn agriculture is known as Bewar in which state of India?
qs.e: Slash and burn agriculture is known by different names in different states of India. In Madhya Pradesh, it is called Bewar or Bever. This traditional farming method involves cutting and burning forest vegetation to clear land for cultivation. Other states have distinct names: in Andhra Pradesh it is called Podu, in Jharkhand it is known as Pahadi Kheti, and in Rajasthan it is called Walra or Barah. Thus, Bewar is specifically used in Madhya Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Slash and burn agriculture in Andhra Pradesh → Podu
☛ Slash and burn agriculture in Jharkhand → Pahadi Kheti
☛ Slash and burn agriculture in Madhya Pradesh → Bewar
☛ Slash and burn agriculture in Rajasthan → Walra
☛ Slash and burn agriculture in Northeast India → Jhum

q: In which of the following states in India the 'rat hole mining' is still practised?
qs.e: Rat-hole mining is a hazardous and illegal mining method primarily practised in the state of Meghalaya. In this method, narrow tunnels are dug to extract coal, often leading to accidents and fatalities. This method is common in Meghalaya because coal seams here are thin and uneven. The National Green Tribunal (NGT) and the Supreme Court have banned it, yet it continues illegally in some areas. It is harmful to the environment and workers' health.
qs.kf:
☛ Main area of rat-hole mining → Meghalaya
☛ Mineral extracted by this mining → Coal
☛ Body that banned rat-hole mining → NGT and Supreme Court
☛ Characteristic of coal seams in Meghalaya → Thin and uneven
☛ Impact of rat-hole mining → Dangerous for environment and workers

q: Which among the following Indian states does NOT share its boundaries with Nepal?
qs.e: Five Indian states share a border with Nepal: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Sikkim. Jharkhand, formed in 2000, does not have any international border. It is surrounded by Bihar, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh but does not touch Nepal. The total length of the India-Nepal border is approximately 1,751 km.
qs.kf:
☛ States sharing border with Nepal → Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim
☛ Total length of India-Nepal border → Approximately 1,751 km
☛ State with longest border with Nepal → Uttar Pradesh
☛ State not sharing border with Nepal → Jharkhand
☛ Length of Sikkim-Nepal border → Approximately 97 km

q: Where is the Kolleru Lake situated?
qs.e: Kolleru Lake is a freshwater lake located in southern India. It lies between the deltas of the Godavari and Krishna rivers in the state of Andhra Pradesh. The lake spans an area of about 245 sq km and is one of the Ramsar sites, recognized for its importance as a habitat for migratory birds. The lake supports a rich ecosystem, benefiting local fisheries and agriculture. Over time, the lake's size has reduced due to human activities like encroachment and aquaculture.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Kolleru Lake situated? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What type of lake is Kolleru Lake? → Freshwater lake
☛ Between which river deltas is Kolleru Lake located? → Godavari and Krishna
☛ What is the significance of Kolleru Lake as a Ramsar site? → Habitat for migratory birds
☛ What is the approximate area of Kolleru Lake? → 245 sq km

q: Which among the following states has the longest mainland coastline in India?
qs.e: The longest mainland coastline in India belongs to the state of Gujarat. Gujarat's coastline is approximately 1600 km long, which accounts for about 24% of India's total mainland coastline. It lies along the Arabian Sea and includes the Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Khambhat, and the Saurashtra coast. In comparison, Tamil Nadu has a coastline of about 1076 km, Maharashtra 720 km, and Odisha 480 km. Gujarat houses major ports like Kandla, Mundra, and Bhavnagar.

☛ Length of Gujarat coastline → Approx 1600 km
☛ Total mainland coastline of India → Approx 6100 km

q: The world's largest reef system the 'Great Barrier Reef' is situated in which sea?
qs.e: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, located in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, Australia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stretching over 2,300 kilometers and comprising more than 2,900 individual reef systems and 900 islands. The Coral Sea is a part of the Pacific Ocean, known for its rich marine biodiversity. The reef is home to many endangered species like sea turtles and dugongs. Climate change, pollution, and coral bleaching pose significant threats to this ecosystem. It is one of the seven natural wonders of the world and attracts millions of tourists annually.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Great Barrier Reef located? → Coral Sea, off the east coast of Australia
☛ What is the length of the Great Barrier Reef? → Approximately 2,300 kilometers
☛ How many individual reefs are in the Great Barrier Reef? → More than 2,900
☛ What UNESCO status does the Great Barrier Reef hold? → World Heritage Site
☛ The Great Barrier Reef is part of which ocean? → Pacific Ocean

q: Where is the Valmiki National Park is located?
qs.e: Valmiki National Park is located in the West Champaran district of Bihar, India. It is the 18th Tiger Reserve of India and the only tiger reserve in Bihar. The park is adjacent to Chitwan National Park in Nepal and the Valmiki Wildlife Sanctuary. It was established as a wildlife sanctuary in 1978 and as a national park in 1990. Situated along the Gandak River, it covers an area of about 900 sq km. The park hosts a variety of wildlife including Bengal tiger, leopard, wild boar, and numerous bird species. It forms a part of the Terai-Duar savanna and grasslands ecoregion.
qs.kf:
☛ Valmiki National Park is located in which state? → Bihar
☛ Which is the only tiger reserve in Bihar? → Valmiki Tiger Reserve

☛ When was Valmiki National Park established? → 1990
☛ Which Nepalese national park is adjacent to Valmiki National Park? → Chitwan National Park

q: Most of the chromite deposits in India are found in:
qs.e: Most of the chromite deposits in India are found in the state of Odisha. The major mining areas are the Sukinda Valley and Baula-Nausahi regions. Chromite is a crucial metallic mineral used in the production of stainless steel and other alloys. India's chromite production is approximately 98% from Odisha. Other states like Jharkhand and Karnataka have small deposits, but Odisha is the largest producer. This mineral is essential for making ferrochromium, which is vital for the steel industry.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest chromite producing state → Odisha
☛ Major chromite areas in Odisha → Sukinda Valley and Baula-Nausahi
☛ Use of chromite → Stainless steel and alloys production
☛ India's chromite production share → About 98%
☛ Other chromite producing states → Jharkhand and Karnataka

q: Which of the following states does NOT share its border with Bangladesh?
qs.e: The Indian states that share a border with Bangladesh are West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Manipur shares its international border only with Myanmar, not with Bangladesh. This northeastern state is geographically isolated from Bangladesh. Among the options, Tripura, Meghalaya, and Mizoram all share borders with Bangladesh. The India-Bangladesh border is one of the longest land borders in the world, stretching about 4,096 km.

q: The pre-monsoon showers which are a common phenomenon in Kerala and the coastal areas of Karnataka are locally known as _______.
qs.e: The pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka are called mango showers. They occur in April-May and help in the ripening of mangoes. These showers are caused by moist winds from the Bay of Bengal. They are also beneficial for coffee and cardamom cultivation in Kerala.

q: Where is Raisina Hill?
o: It is the place where the Dogra rulers of Jammu and Kashmir built their fort in Jammu
It is situated in the same location as Rashtrapati Bhavan.
It is the rock feature at Kanyakumari where Swami Vivekananda's statue was erected.
qs.e: Raisina Hill is a hill in Delhi where Rashtrapati Bhavan is located. It is part of the central administrative area of the Government of India, which also includes the North and South Blocks. Rashtrapati Bhavan was built in 1929 and serves as the official residence of the President of India. The name Raisina Hill is derived from the village of Raisina that previously existed there. This location symbolizes India's political and historical significance.

☛ In which year was Rashtrapati Bhavan built? → 1929
☛ In which city is Rashtrapati Bhavan located? → Delhi

☛ What is the official residence of the President of India? → Rashtrapati Bhavan

q: Cyclone Amphan hit West Bengal in May, 2020. Where did the cyclone originate from?
qs.e: Cyclone Amphan occurred in May 2020 and originated from the Bay of Bengal. It was a tropical cyclone that caused massive destruction in eastern India and Bangladesh. The Bay of Bengal is a major source of tropical cyclones, especially in the pre-monsoon and post-monsoon periods. Amphan affected coastal areas of West Bengal, Odisha, and Bangladesh. It developed into a Super Cyclonic Storm with wind speeds reaching up to 260 km/h. The cyclone led to widespread flooding, power outages, and damage to infrastructure. The storm surge inundated low-lying areas, affecting millions of people.

☛ Intensity of Cyclone Amphan → Super Cyclonic Storm
☛ Maximum wind speed → 260 km/h

q: Where is the Kanha Tiger Reserve?
qs.e: Kanha Tiger Reserve is located in the Mandla and Balaghat districts of Madhya Pradesh. It is one of India's premier tiger reserves and was established in 1973 under Project Tiger. The reserve covers an area of approximately 940 sq km. It is home to species like barasingha, gaur, and leopard. The reserve is known for its rich biodiversity and successful tiger conservation efforts.

q: Where is the world's largest coral reef found?
qs.e: The world's largest coral reef is the Great Barrier Reef, located off the eastern coast of Australia. It stretches over 2,300 km and covers an area of approximately 3,44,400 sq km. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981. The reef is home to a vast diversity of marine life, including many species of fish, corals, and other organisms. Currently, it faces threats from climate change, pollution, and rising ocean temperatures leading to coral bleaching.

q: _______ is the only State of India where the Sangai deer is found.
qs.e: The Sangai deer (Cervus eldi eldi) is found only in Manipur state in India, specifically in the Keibul Lamjao National Park. This deer is known for its long antlers and agile body. It was discovered in the 19th century and is the state animal of Manipur. It inhabits the floating islands (phumdis) of Loktak Lake. The species is listed as Endangered by the IUCN and is included in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act 1972.

☛ National park associated with Sangai deer → Keibul Lamjao National Park, Manipur

q: Which of the following states holds India's highest graphite reserves according to the Geological Survey of India?
qs.e: According to the Geological Survey of India (GSI), Arunachal Pradesh holds the largest graphite reserves in India, accounting for about 40% of the country's total reserves. Graphite is a critical mineral used in batteries, lubricants, and nuclear reactors. After Arunachal Pradesh, Odisha has significant graphite deposits. Graphite is considered a strategic mineral due to its use in energy storage and high-tech industries. India is working towards self-sufficiency in graphite. Besides Arunachal Pradesh, graphite reserves are also found in Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu, and West Bengal.

☛ Main use of graphite → Batteries and lubricants

q: Which of the following is the border between India and Pakistan?
qs.e: The border between India and Pakistan is known as the Radcliffe Line. It was named after Sir Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer who was tasked with drawing the boundaries during the Partition of India in 1947. This line defines the international border between India and Pakistan. Other options: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan; the Mannerheim Line was between Finland and Russia; and the Hindenburg Line was a defensive line in World War I between Germany and Poland.
qs.kf:

☛ Who drew the Radcliffe Line → Sir Cyril Radcliffe
☛ Pakistan-Afghanistan border → Durand Line
☛ India-China border → McMahon Line
☛ India-Bangladesh border → Eastern part of Radcliffe Line

q: How many Indian states share their boundaries with Nepal?
qs.e: India shares its international border with Nepal across 5 states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Sikkim. The total length of the India-Nepal border is approximately 1,751 km. This border is an open border under the 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, allowing citizens of both nations to travel without passports or visas. Sikkim is the smallest state sharing a border with Nepal, while Uttar Pradesh has the longest border segment. Key border points include Banbasa, Raxaul, and Panitanki, facilitating trade and cultural exchange. The border region is also known for its strategic significance and shared heritage.

☛ Year of India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship → 1950

q: Where are one-horned rhinoceros is found in India?
qs.e: In India, the one-horned rhinoceros (Indian rhinoceros) is primarily found in the state of Assam. Its main habitat is Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This rhino, scientifically known as Rhinoceros unicornis, has a single horn and thick skin with natural armor-like folds. Its diet mainly consists of grass and aquatic plants. The majority of India's rhino population resides in Assam's protected areas including Kaziranga, Manas, Pobitora, and Orang National Parks. It is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List and is protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

☛ Kaziranga National Park is located in which state → Assam

☛ Schedule under which rhino is protected → Schedule I of Wildlife Protection Act

q: How does most of India's foreign trade take place?
o: Equally through land, air and sea routes each
qs.e: Most of India's foreign trade takes place through sea and air routes. Sea routes are the most economical for transporting heavy and bulk cargo, while air routes are used for quick transport of valuable and perishable goods. Land routes are limited to neighboring countries and account for a very small share. Major Indian ports like Mumbai, Nhava Sheva, Chennai, and Kolkata handle sea trade, while international airports such as Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru lead air trade. Overall, sea and air routes play the most significant role in India's foreign trade.
qs.kf:
☛ Which route accounts for the largest share of India's total foreign trade? → Sea route
☛ Which route is best for exporting perishable goods? → Air route
☛ Which is India's busiest port? → Nhava Sheva (Jawaharlal Nehru Port)
☛ Which is India's largest international airport? → Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi
☛ India's land trade is mainly with which countries? → Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan

q: In which state is the Mudumalai National Park located?
qs.e: Mudumalai National Park is located in the state of Tamil Nadu. It is situated in the Nilgiri Hills and is a part of the Tiger Reserve. The park covers an area of approximately 321 sq km. It was established in 1978. The park is home to animals like elephants, tigers, leopards, sambar, and spotted deer. It shares its boundaries with Bandipur National Park (Karnataka) and Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary (Kerala). The name 'Mudumalai' means ancient hill in the Tamil language. It is a part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: In which of the following states of India is Lord Mahavir National Park situated?
qs.e: Lord Mahavir National Park is situated in the state of Goa. It is the only national park in Goa, established in 1978. The park covers an area of approximately 107 sq km. It is part of the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot and hosts many rare flora and fauna. One can find Indian tigers, leopards, sloth bears, and various reptiles here. The park is named after Lord Mahavir, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. It is also known as Mollem National Park and is located in the northeastern part of Goa.

q: Lodha Waterfall is situated in _____________ state.
qs.e: Lodha Waterfall is located in Jharkhand state, in the Latehar district. This waterfall is formed on the Burha River and has a height of about 143 meters, making it the highest waterfall in Jharkhand. Lodha Waterfall is also known as 'Lodh Falls' or 'Burha Ghagh'. It is situated near Betla National Park and is a major tourist attraction. Other waterfalls in Jharkhand include Hundru Falls (on Swarnarekha River), Dasham Falls (on Kanhar River), and Hirani Falls.

q: Which state has the highest number of national parks in India?
qs.e: The state with the highest number of national parks in India is Madhya Pradesh. It has a total of 11 national parks, which is the highest in the country. Prominent among them are Kanha National Park, Bandhavgarh National Park, Pench National Park, Satpura National Park, and Madhav National Park. These parks are renowned for their biodiversity and wildlife. Madhya Pradesh is also known as the 'Tiger State' as it has the highest tiger population in India. Among the other options, Punjab has only one national park, Tripura has two, and Tamil Nadu has five. Thus, Madhya Pradesh tops the list with the maximum number of national parks.

q: Which of the following area is most likely area to experience landslides?
qs.e: The Himalayas are the most landslide-prone region due to being a young fold mountain with active geological processes. Steep slopes, heavy rainfall, earthquakes, and river erosion trigger landslides here. Human activities like road construction, deforestation, and mining further destabilize the terrain. In contrast, Kutch (desert), Eastern Coastal Plains (flat terrain), and Rajasthan (arid region) have minimal landslide risk due to gentle slopes and stable geology.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest landslide-prone area in India → Himalayas
☛ Major cause of large landslides in Himalayas → Earthquakes and heavy rainfall
☛ Landslide risk zones in India (as per NDMA) → Himalayas, Western Ghats
☛ Anthropogenic factor for landslides → Deforestation, mining
☛ Natural cause of landslides → Heavy rainfall, earthquake

q: Which of the following states of India is experiencing mango shower?
qs.e: Mango shower is a seasonal phenomenon that occurs in the state of Kerala during the pre-monsoon period. This event typically takes place in April-May when mango trees begin to bear fruit. This rainfall is caused by moist winds from the Bay of Bengal that strike the Western Ghats and cause precipitation in Kerala. Also known as Cherry Blossom or Coffee Shower, this rain is important for coffee plantations in Karnataka as well.

q: Dr. Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary is located in ______ state.
qs.e: Dr. Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary is located in the state of Goa. This sanctuary is named after the renowned ornithologist Dr. Salim Ali. It is situated on Chorão Island and is known for its mangrove forests. Various migratory birds can be seen here, such as kingfishers, egrets, and herons. q: Where is the Forest Research Institute located?
qs.e: The Forest Research Institute (FRI) was established in 1906 and is located in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It is the largest forest research center in India, and the headquarters of the Indian Forest Survey is also in Dehradun. FRI was merged with the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy in 2006 for training Indian Forest Service officers. The institute is renowned for forestry research, education, and extension. qs.e: All three sites are important Natural World Heritage Sites in India. Manas Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Assam and was inscribed in 1985. q: Kichiopolari Lake is located in which of the following states?
qs.e: Kichiopolari Lake is located in the state of Sikkim. Situated in the East Sikkim district at an altitude of about 4,500 meters above sea level, it is also known as the Queen of Himalayas. The lake is considered sacred by Buddhists and attracts pilgrims every year. Surrounded by snow-capped mountains and lush green meadows, it is a popular tourist destination. The water of Kichiopolari Lake is blue and clear, adding to its beauty. The lake is also a source of several streams that flow into the Teesta River.

q: Which of the following states is under zone 1-highly dry prone area?
qs.e: In India, drought-prone areas are classified into different zones based on climate and rainfall. Zone 1 is the highly dry prone area, where average annual rainfall is less than 750 mm and the probability of drought is highest. Most parts of Rajasthan fall under this category, especially the Thar Desert region. Rajasthan receives very low and erratic rainfall, leading to frequent droughts. In contrast, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, and Assam receive relatively higher rainfall and are not in Zone 1. Thus, Rajasthan is the correct example of Zone 1-highly dry prone area.

q: Panna district of Madhya Pradesh is famous for what?
qs.e: Panna district in Madhya Pradesh is renowned for its diamond mines, being the only place in India where commercial diamond mining occurs. The Majhgawan diamond mine in Panna is the largest diamond mine in the country, yielding high-quality diamonds. The diamond deposits here are primarily from kimberlite pipes, a volcanic rock type known for hosting diamonds. Panna also houses the Panna National Park, a significant tiger reserve. Besides diamonds, the region is known for agriculture, including bajra and gram cultivation. The district's unique geology and mining history make it a key area for gemstone production in India.

q: Which state is the major producer of mulberry silk in India (Currently)?
qs.e: India is the second largest producer of silk in the world. Mulberry silk accounts for about 70% of the total silk produced in India. Karnataka is the largest producer of mulberry silk, contributing around 46% of the country's total mulberry silk production. Major production centers in Karnataka include Mysore, Ramanagara, and Tumkur districts. Other prominent mulberry silk producing states are Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Jammu & Kashmir. Karnataka's favorable climate and advanced sericulture techniques keep it as the leading state in mulberry silk production.

q: Which one of the following states is also known as "Molasses basin"?
qs.e: Mizoram is also known as the 'Molasses Basin' because its rocks are mainly of molasses type, formed during the Tertiary period. q: Forest Research Institute is located in _________
qs.e: The Forest Research Institute (FRI) is India's premier forestry research institute, located in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It was established in 1906 as the Imperial Forest Research Institute. q: Kathiawar Peninsula is found in which of the following states?

It extends into the Arabian Sea and is bordered by the Gulf of Khambhat and the Gulf of Kutch. This peninsula is known for its historical and cultural significance. q: The Sonapani glacier is situated in which of the following states of India?
