The state has a well-developed network of roads connecting rural and urban areas. Among the other options, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh have lower road densities compared to Kerala. This data is based on reports from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
qs.kf:
☛ State with highest road density → Kerala
☛ Road density of Kerala (per 100 sq km) → ~517 km
☛ National average road density (per 100 sq km) → ~192 km
☛ State with second highest road density → West Bengal
☛ State with lowest road density → Arunachal Pradesh

q: Which one of the following Indian state is the leading producer of soybean in year 2019-20?
qs.e: In the year 2019-20, the leading producer of soybean in India was Madhya Pradesh. Soybean cultivation in Madhya Pradesh is primarily concentrated in the Malwa region, often called the 'Soybean Bowl' of India. Soybean is a major kharif crop in India. Other significant producers include Maharashtra and Rajasthan, but Madhya Pradesh leads in production. Soybean is an important oilseed and protein-rich crop, used for edible oil, animal feed, and industrial products. India is the fifth largest producer of soybean in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest producer of soybean in the world → Brazil
☛ Leading soybean producer state in India → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Soybean cultivation season → Kharif
☛ Soybean is also known as → 'Malwa ka Sona'
☛ Main nutrient in soybean → Protein

q: Which of the following hills is situated on India's north-eastern border with Myanmar?
qs.e: The Patkai hills are situated on India's north-eastern border with Myanmar, running through the states of Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram. They are part of the southern extension of the Himalayas and are also known as the 'Patkai Bum' or 'Patkai Range'. This region is known for its dense forests and rich biodiversity. In contrast, the Sahyadhri (Western Ghats) are located in western India, while the Vindhyachal and Satpura ranges are in central India, and none of these share a border with Myanmar.
qs.kf:
☛ Patkai hills → Located on India-Myanmar border
☛ Sahyadhri → Another name for Western Ghats
☛ Vindhyachal → Mountain range in central India
☛ Satpura → Spread across Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
☛ India-Myanmar border → Extends from Arunachal to Mizoram

q: Saffron is produced in a large scale in
qs.e: In India, saffron is produced on a large scale mainly in Jammu and Kashmir. The Pampore region in the Pulwama district is famous for saffron cultivation. Saffron comes from the plant Crocus sativus and is also known as red gold. It requires a cold climate and well-drained soil for cultivation. Apart from Jammu and Kashmir, saffron is also grown in Himachal Pradesh on a small scale, but the major producing state is Jammu and Kashmir. Saffron is used as a spice, medicine, and dye.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the scientific name of saffron? → Crocus sativus
☛ What is saffron commonly known as? → Red gold
☛ Which region in Jammu and Kashmir is famous for saffron? → Pampore (Pulwama)
☛ What climate is required for saffron cultivation? → Cold climate
☛ Which Indian state leads in saffron production? → Jammu and Kashmir

q: Where is the 'Zojila Tunnel Project' located?
qs.e: The Zojila Tunnel Project is located in the union territory of Jammu & Kashmir, India. It involves the construction of a 14.15 km long tunnel on the National Highway 1 at the Zojila pass, connecting Srinagar and Ladakh. This will be Asia's longest bi-lane tunnel, providing all-weather connectivity. The tunnel will ensure year-round access to Ladakh, which is strategically important. The project is being executed by the National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL).
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Zojila Tunnel → 14.15 km
☛ National Highway for Zojila Tunnel → NH 1
☛ Executing agency of Zojila Tunnel → NHIDCL
☛ Regions connected by Zojila Tunnel → Srinagar and Ladakh
☛ State/UT of Zojila Tunnel → Jammu & Kashmir

q: Which of the following nuclear power plants has been INCORRECTLY matched with the state within which it is located?
qs.e: The Kalpakkam nuclear power plant is located in Tamil Nadu, not Karnataka. It consists of two Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) and was constructed in the 1970s. The Kakrapar plant is in Gujarat, Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu, and Kaiga is in Karnataka. These three are correctly matched. Kalpakkam is also known as the Madras Atomic Power Station.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Kalpakkam nuclear power plant located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ In which state is Kaiga nuclear power plant located? → Karnataka
☛ In which state is Kakrapar nuclear power plant located? → Gujarat
☛ In which state is Kudankulam nuclear power plant located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which is India's first nuclear power plant? → Tarapur (Maharashtra)

q: Khardung La Pass is located in which Indian state?
qs.e: Khardung La Pass is located in the Indian union territory of Ladakh, which was formerly part of the state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is one of the highest motorable passes in the world, at an elevation of approximately 5,359 meters (17,582 feet). The pass connects the city of Leh with the Nubra Valley and the Siachen Glacier. Historically, Khardung La was part of the ancient Silk Route and remains strategically important for military and tourism. Due to its challenging terrain and altitude, it is a popular destination for adventure travelers. Among the options, Jammu and Kashmir is the most appropriate because Ladakh was carved out as a separate union territory in 2019.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state/UT is Khardung La Pass in? → Ladakh
☛ What is the altitude of Khardung La Pass? → Approximately 5,359 meters
☛ Which places does Khardung La Pass connect? → Leh and Nubra Valley
☛ Which is the highest motorable pass in the world? → Umling La (though Khardung La is also high)
☛ When did Ladakh become a union territory? → 31 October 2019

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The Eastern Peripheral Expressway is built to decongest traffic in _____.
qs.e: The Eastern Peripheral Expressway (EPE) is built to decongest traffic in the national capital region of Delhi. This 135 km long six-lane expressway starts from Kundli in Uttar Pradesh and ends at Palwal in Haryana. It was inaugurated in May 2018 by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari. The expressway is designed to divert heavy vehicles around Delhi, reducing traffic congestion and pollution inside the city. Along with the Western Peripheral Expressway, it forms a ring road around Delhi. The project cost about ₹11,000 crore and was built under the public-private partnership model. It is considered a landmark infrastructure project for the National Capital Region.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Eastern Peripheral Expressway → 135 km
☛ Inauguration year of Eastern Peripheral Expressway → 2018
☛ States through which Eastern Peripheral Expressway passes → Uttar Pradesh and Haryana
☛ Purpose of Eastern Peripheral Expressway → Decongest Delhi traffic
☛ Lane width of Eastern Peripheral Expressway → Six-lane

q: The 'Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant' is located in which state?
qs.e: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is located in the Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu. It is India's largest nuclear power plant with a total capacity of 2,000 MW (2x1,000 MW). It was built in collaboration with Russia. The first unit was commissioned in 2013 and the second in 2016. The plant uses VVER-1000 reactors, which are pressurized water reactors. It is operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What is its total capacity? → 2,000 MW
☛ Which country collaborated in its construction? → Russia
☛ Type of reactor used? → VVER-1000
☛ Operating agency? → NPCIL

q: The Salem Steel Plant is located in which state?
qs.e: The Salem Steel Plant is located in the state of Tamil Nadu, specifically in the Salem district. It is a major plant of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and specializes in the production of stainless steel and special steels. Established in 1982, it is one of the key steel production centers in the country. Its location in Tamil Nadu contributes significantly to the industrial development of South India. The plant mainly produces stainless steel sheets, plates, and coils.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of SAIL → New Delhi
☛ Largest steel plant in India → Bhilai Steel Plant (Chhattisgarh)
☛ Establishment year of Salem Steel Plant → 1982
☛ Organization under which Salem Steel Plant operates → Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)
☛ Special product of Salem Steel Plant → Stainless steel

q: Which of the following States/Union Territories shares a border with Afghanistan?
qs.e: India's union territory Ladakh shares a border with Afghanistan through the Wakhan Corridor, connecting to Badakhshan province. Although this area is currently controlled by Pakistan, the Line of Control does not affect the historical boundary. The India-Afghanistan border is approximately 106 kilometers long. Among the options, Rajasthan and Punjab only share borders with Pakistan, while Jammu and Kashmir borders Pakistan and China, not Afghanistan. Thus, Ladakh is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of India-Afghanistan border? → 106 km
☛ Which countries border Ladakh? → Pakistan, China, Afghanistan
☛ Which union territory contains the Wakhan Corridor? → Ladakh
☛ Which Indian territory touches Afghanistan? → Ladakh
☛ What was Afghanistan earlier known as? → Aryavarta

q: Administrators of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Puducherry are designated as _________.
qs.e: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a Union Territory and Puducherry is also a Union Territory. According to the Indian Constitution, Union Territories are administered by the President through an Administrator. However, for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Administrator is designated as Lieutenant Governor, and similarly for Puducherry, the designation is Lieutenant Governor. This designation reflects the special status of these regions, as Puducherry has its own Legislative Assembly while Andaman and Nicobar Islands does not. Thus, the administrators of both are named as Lieutenant Governor.
qs.kf:
☛ Administrator of Andaman and Nicobar Islands → Lieutenant Governor
☛ Administrator of Puducherry → Lieutenant Governor
☛ Administrator of Delhi → Lieutenant Governor
☛ Administrator of Chandigarh → Administrator (Chief Administrator of UT)
☛ Administrator of UT without legislature → Administrator

q: The McMahon Line separates India from which country?
qs.e: The McMahon Line is a disputed boundary between India and China. It was defined in 1914 during the Shimla Convention between British India and Tibet, which China does not recognize. The line runs through Arunachal Pradesh, which China claims as part of South Tibet. India considers the McMahon Line as its international border, while China deems it illegal. The line is named after British diplomat Sir Henry McMahon. It stretches for about 890 km along the peaks of the Himalayas. The dispute over this line led to the Sino-Indian War in 1962.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the McMahon Line defined? → 1914
☛ Under which convention was the McMahon Line defined? → Shimla Convention
☛ Which Indian state does the McMahon Line pass through? → Arunachal Pradesh
☛ After whom is the McMahon Line named? → Sir Henry McMahon
☛ What is the length of the McMahon Line? → Approximately 890 km

q: The Nagarhole National Park is located in the state of:
qs.e: Nagarhole National Park is located in southern India and spans the Kodagu and Mysore districts of Karnataka. It was established as a sanctuary in 1955 and declared a national park in 1988. It is part of the Western Ghats and is also known as Rajiv Gandhi National Park. The park is home to tigers, elephants, leopards, and barking deer. It forms a crucial part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve and is drained by the Kabini River.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Nagarhole National Park established? → 1988
☛ Which river flows through the park? → Kabini
☛ Which biosphere reserve is it part of? → Nilgiri
☛ What is the other name of the park? → Rajiv Gandhi National Park
☛ In which state is it located? → Karnataka

q: Which of the following states is also known as the ‘Molassis basin’, which is made up of soft unconsolidated deposits?
qs.e: Mizoram is known as the 'Molassis basin' because the region is primarily composed of soft, unconsolidated sedimentary deposits. These deposits originated from debris eroding from the Himalayan mountain-building process during the Tertiary period. Molasse is a type of sedimentary rock group consisting of coarse-grained sandstone, shale, and conglomerate. The hills of Mizoram are made of these soft rocks, which are susceptible to erosion. This geological structure distinguishes it from other northeastern states.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is known as Molassis basin? → Mizoram
☛ Molasse deposits belong to which period? → Tertiary period
☛ What type of rocks are Molasse? → Soft, unconsolidated sedimentary
☛ Soil type in Mizoram? → Alluvial and lateritic
☛ Average rainfall in Mizoram? → 2,000-3,000 mm

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 1
q: The Sabarmati river originates from which of the following places?
qs.e: The Sabarmati river originates from the Aravalli Hills in the Udaipur district of Rajasthan. It flows in a south-westerly direction, enters Gujarat, and finally discharges into the Gulf of Khambhat. The total length of the river is about 371 km. Major cities like Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar are situated on its banks. Mahatma Gandhi established the Sabarmati Ashram in 1917, which became a focal point for India's freedom struggle. The river is largely rain-fed and dries up during summer months.
qs.kf:
☛ Sabarmati river originates from → Aravalli Hills, Rajasthan
☛ Length of Sabarmati river → approximately 371 km
☛ Sabarmati river falls into → Gulf of Khambhat
☛ Major city on banks of Sabarmati → Ahmedabad
☛ Sabarmati Ashram was established by → Mahatma Gandhi

q: Which of the following was NOT an excavated site of the Banas culture?
qs.e: The Banas culture, also known as the Ahar culture, was a Chalcolithic culture that flourished in the Banas river region of Rajasthan. Its major excavated sites include Ahar, Gilund, and Bagor. In contrast, Nagda is an archaeological site in Madhya Pradesh associated with the Malwa culture. The Banas culture is characterized by red and black pottery, copper objects, and an agricultural lifestyle. Excavations at Nagda were conducted in 1955-56, revealing a significant center of the Malwa culture. Therefore, Nagda was not an excavated site of the Banas culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Major site of Banas culture → Ahar
☛ Other name of Banas culture → Ahar culture
☛ Gilund is located in → Rajasthan
☛ Bagor is associated with → Mesolithic and Banas culture
☛ Nagda is a site of → Malwa culture

q: In which of the following states is the slash and burn agriculture known as ‘Kuruwa’?
qs.e: Slash and burn agriculture, also known as shifting cultivation, is practiced in various parts of India under different local names. In Jharkhand, it is known as Kuruwa or Kuruwa method. This practice is mainly adopted by tribal communities, where a patch of forest is cut and burned to clear land for cultivation. In other states, it is called by different names: in Madhya Pradesh it is known as Bewar or Dahiya, in Arunachal Pradesh as Jhum, and in Rajasthan as Walra or Kuril. Thus, the term Kuruwa is specifically associated with Jharkhand.
qs.kf:
☛ Local name of shifting cultivation in Jharkhand → Kuruwa
☛ Local name in Madhya Pradesh → Bewar or Dahiya
☛ Local name in Arunachal Pradesh → Jhum
☛ Local name in Rajasthan → Walra
☛ Local name in Andhra Pradesh → Podu

q: Mango showers occur in which of the following groups of states?
qs.e: Mango showers are pre-monsoon rainfall that occur before the arrival of the southwest monsoon. These showers are mainly experienced in Kerala, Karnataka, and parts of Tamil Nadu. The name comes from the fact that they help in the flowering and growth of mango trees. In Bihar and West Bengal, similar pre-monsoon thunderstorms are called 'Kal Baisakhi' or 'Nor'westers'. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana generally remain dry during this period. Therefore, among the given options, Karnataka and Kerala receive mango showers. These showers are crucial for mango cultivation in the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where do mango showers occur? → Kerala and Karnataka
☛ What are pre-monsoon showers called in eastern India? → Kal Baisakhi
☛ In which season do mango showers occur? → Summer (pre-monsoon)
☛ Significance of mango showers in agriculture? → Beneficial for mango flowering and fruit
☛ When does the southwest monsoon arrive in Kerala? → First week of June

q: Which of the following factors causes Ooty to have cooler summers than Coimbatore, even though both are located at nearly the same latitude?
o: Ooty is influenced by cold desert winds from the north
Coimbatore receives less solar radiation during the year
Ooty is located closer to the sea, while Coimbatore is inland
Ooty is situated at a higher altitude, leading to lower temperatures
qs.e: Ooty and Coimbatore are located at nearly the same latitude, yet Ooty experiences cooler summers due to difference in altitude. Ooty is situated at an elevation of about 2240 meters above sea level, while Coimbatore is at about 432 meters. As altitude increases, temperature decreases (approximately 6.5°C per 1000 meters), known as the lapse rate. This makes Ooty's average temperature significantly lower than Coimbatore's. Other options are incorrect: Ooty is not influenced by cold desert winds from the north; Coimbatore does not receive less solar radiation; and Ooty is not closer to the sea but is an inland hill station.
qs.kf:
☛ Height of Ooty above sea level → 2240 m
☛ Height of Coimbatore above sea level → 432 m
☛ Temperature lapse rate → 6.5°C per 1000 m
☛ Ooty is located in which state → Tamil Nadu
☛ Highest peak in Nilgiri Hills → Doddabetta (2637 m)

q: What is the primary material used in the 8th-century CE Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram?
qs.e: The Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram was built in the 8th century CE by Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) of the Pallava dynasty. The primary material used in its construction is sandstone. This temple is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture and features numerous mandapas, a pyramidal vimana, and 58 small shrines. The walls contain inscriptions in Sanskrit. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, the temple's name refers to Mount Kailash, Shiva's abode. It is one of the earliest structural temples in South India and exemplifies the transition from rock-cut to structural architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Kailasanatha Temple? → Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)
☛ Which dynasty built the temple? → Pallava dynasty
☛ What is the architectural style? → Dravidian style
☛ The temple is dedicated to which deity? → Shiva
☛ Where is Kanchipuram located? → Tamil Nadu

q: Which two districts of Uttarakhand share the inter-state border with Himachal Pradesh in the north-west?
qs.e: The two districts of Uttarakhand that share the inter-state border with Himachal Pradesh in the north-west are Uttarkashi and Dehradun. Uttarkashi district is located in the north-western part of Uttarakhand and borders Kinnaur and Shimla districts of Himachal Pradesh. Dehradun district also shares its north-western boundary with Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh. The other options are incorrect: Chamoli and Pithoragarh border Tibet (China) in the north-east, while Pauri and Rudraprayag, and Champawat and Bageshwar do not share a border with Himachal Pradesh. Hence, the correct answer is Uttarkashi and Dehradun.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country touches the north-eastern border of Uttarakhand? → Tibet (China)
☛ Which districts of Uttarakhand border Himachal Pradesh? → Uttarkashi and Dehradun
☛ Which districts of Uttarakhand border Nepal? → Pithoragarh, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar
☛ Which is the largest district of Uttarakhand by area? → Chamoli
☛ Which is the smallest district of Uttarakhand by area? → Champawat

q: India shares a maritime boundary (sea boundary) with which one of the following countries across the Arabian Sea or the Indian Ocean?
qs.e: India's maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean is shared with several countries. Maldives is an island nation located in the Indian Ocean, southwest of India, and shares a maritime border with India. Mongolia, Russia, and Afghanistan are landlocked countries with no coastline. Therefore, among the given options, India shares a maritime boundary across the Arabian Sea or Indian Ocean only with Maldives.
qs.kf:
☛ Which are India's maritime neighbors? → Maldives, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia
☛ Where does the maritime boundary between India and Maldives pass? → Eight Degree Channel
☛ Which is the southernmost maritime neighbor of India? → Sri Lanka
☛ Which Indian union territory shares a maritime boundary with Maldives? → Lakshadweep
☛ In which year was the India-Maldives maritime boundary established? → 1976

q: Which of the following Indian states shares an international boundary with both Bangladesh and Myanmar?
qs.e: Among the northeastern states of India, only Mizoram shares an international boundary with both Bangladesh and Myanmar. Mizoram borders the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh and the Chin State of Myanmar. Other states like Tripura and Assam share borders only with Bangladesh, while Manipur shares a border only with Myanmar. Mizoram is a strategically important border state with a total boundary length of about 722 km, of which 318 km is with Bangladesh and 404 km with Myanmar. It is one of the 'Seven Sisters' of Northeast India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Indian state shares a border with both Bangladesh and Myanmar? → Mizoram
☛ What is the length of Mizoram's border with Bangladesh? → 318 km
☛ What is the length of Mizoram's border with Myanmar? → 404 km
☛ Which Indian state shares a border only with Bangladesh? → Tripura
☛ Which Indian state shares a border only with Myanmar? → Manipur

q: The India–Nepal international border passes through all of the following Indian states except which one?
qs.e: The India-Nepal border is approximately 1,751 km long and passes through five Indian states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Sikkim. This border connects northern and eastern parts of India with Nepal. Assam does not share a border with Nepal; its international borders are primarily with Bhutan and Bangladesh. Sikkim, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar are all part of this international boundary. The border is crucial for India-Nepal relations, facilitating trade and movement through several open points. Understanding which states are included is important for geography.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of India-Nepal border → 1,751 km
☛ State not touching India-Nepal border → Assam
☛ Number of Indian states on India-Nepal border → 5
☛ Easternmost state on India-Nepal border → Sikkim
☛ Major pass on India-Nepal border → Lipulekh Pass

q: In which Indian state is the Tehri Dam located?
qs.e: The Tehri Dam is located in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is built on the Bhagirathi River and is the second highest dam in India after the Srisailam Dam in Andhra Pradesh, with a height of approximately 260.5 meters. The dam is situated in Tehri district and was constructed by the Tehri Hydro Development Corporation. It is a multipurpose dam used for electricity generation, irrigation, and drinking water supply.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is the Tehri Dam built? → Bhagirathi
☛ What is the height of Tehri Dam? → 260.5 meters
☛ In which state is Tehri Dam located? → Uttarakhand
☛ Which is the tallest dam in India? → Srisailam Dam (Andhra Pradesh)
☛ Who constructed the Tehri Dam? → Tehri Hydro Development Corporation

q: Moplah Rebellion against British occupation and the atrocities of the landlords mainly took place in which of the following regions of India?
qs.e: The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 took place in the Malabar region of Kerala. It was primarily a revolt by the Moplah (Muslim tenant farmers) against the tyranny of British landlords and the colonial government. The farmers were oppressed by high land revenue and the exploitation of landlords. The rebellion also supported the Khilafat Movement. The British suppressed it with military force, killing or exiling many Moplahs. This rebellion is a significant peasant uprising in India's freedom struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Main cause of Moplah Rebellion → British revenue policy and landlord exploitation
☛ Leadership of Moplah Rebellion → Ali Musliyar and Variakunnath Kunhamed Haji
☛ Moplah Rebellion linked to → Khilafat Movement
☛ Region of Moplah Rebellion → Malabar (Kerala)
☛ Year of Moplah Rebellion → 1921

q: At approximately what depth inside the Earth is the boundary between the mantle and the core located?
qs.e: The boundary between the mantle and the core inside the Earth is called the Gutenberg discontinuity. It lies at a depth of approximately 2,900 km. At this boundary, the velocity of seismic waves changes abruptly: P-waves slow down, and S-waves are completely stopped because the outer core is in a liquid state. The mantle has a density range of about 3.3 to 5.7 g/cm³, while the core density ranges from 9.9 to 13 g/cm³. This discontinuity is crucial for understanding Earth's internal structure and separating the silicate mantle from the iron-nickel core.
qs.kf:
☛ Depth of Earth's center → 6,371 km
☛ Temperature of the core → 5,000–6,000°C
☛ Depth of Gutenberg discontinuity → 2,900 km
☛ Depth of Mohorovičić discontinuity → 35 km (continental)
☛ State of outer core → liquid

q: Which two neighbors combined have a land border with India longer than China’s border?
qs.e: India's land border is about 15,200 km, shared with neighboring countries. The India-China border is approximately 3,488 km long. India shares a 4,096 km border with Bangladesh and a 3,323 km border with Pakistan, totaling about 7,419 km, which exceeds the China border length. Bangladesh has the longest border with India, followed by China and Pakistan. Other options: Nepal (1,751 km), Myanmar (1,643 km), Bhutan (699 km), and Afghanistan (106 km) have combined lengths less than that of China. Thus, the correct pair is Bangladesh and Pakistan.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country shares the longest land border with India? → Bangladesh (4,096 km)
☛ What is the length of the India-China border? → 3,488 km
☛ What is the India-Pakistan border called? → Radcliffe Line
☛ What is the India-Bangladesh border called? → Radcliffe Line (Eastern part)
☛ Which Indian state touches the most international borders? → West Bengal (Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan)

q: Which statement best distinguishes primitive subsistence farming from commercial farming in India?
o: Commercial farming relies mainly on monsoon rainfall
Primitive farming emphasises family consumption needs
Primitive farming focuses on market-oriented surplus production
Commercial farming avoids the use of modern technology
qs.e: The primary distinction between primitive subsistence farming and commercial farming lies in the purpose of production. In primitive subsistence farming, farmers grow crops mainly to meet the consumption needs of their family, with little or no surplus for sale. This type of farming relies on traditional tools, family labor, and monsoon rainfall. In contrast, commercial farming is market-oriented, producing large quantities of crops for sale, using modern technology, high-yielding seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation. Option 2 is the most accurate because it captures the subsistence nature of primitive farming. Option 1 is incorrect because commercial farming does not depend on monsoon; option 3 wrongly attributes market orientation to primitive farming; option 4 is false as commercial farming heavily uses modern technology.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main objective of primitive subsistence farming in India? → To meet family consumption needs
☛ What is the primary focus of commercial farming? → Market-oriented surplus production
☛ What type of technology is used in primitive farming? → Traditional tools and reliance on monsoon
☛ What inputs are commonly used in commercial farming? → Modern machinery, fertilizers, and pesticides
☛ In which regions is primitive farming prevalent in India? → Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, and northeastern states

q: Which island country, along with Sri Lanka, is identified as India’s southern neighbour across the Indian Ocean?
qs.e: The Maldives, along with Sri Lanka, is identified as India's southern neighbour in the Indian Ocean. It is an island nation located southwest of India, consisting of 26 atolls. Its capital is Malé. The Maldives holds strategic importance for India, and both nations share close diplomatic and economic ties. It is the smallest country in Asia by land area and population. The Maldivian economy relies heavily on tourism and fishing. India has provided aid during crises like the water shortage in 2014, highlighting bilateral cooperation. The country's highest point is only about 2 meters above sea level, making it vulnerable to climate change.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Maldives → Malé
☛ Currency of Maldives → Maldivian Rufiyaa
☛ Highest point in Maldives → Villingili Island (approx. 2 m)
☛ Population of Maldives (2024 estimate) → About 520,000
☛ Maritime boundary between India and Maldives → Eight Degree Channel

q: Which of the following countries is India’s nearest neighbour in the northwest?
qs.e: India's nearest neighbour in the northwest is Pakistan. The India-Pakistan border is approximately 3,323 km long, mainly defined by the Radcliffe Line. This border touches the states of Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir. Among the other options, Nepal lies to India's north, Bhutan to the northeast, and China to the north. Geographically, Pakistan is located at India's northwestern corner.
qs.kf:
☛ India-Pakistan border line → Radcliffe Line
☛ Longest international border → Bangladesh (4,096 km)
☛ Country in northwest of India → Pakistan
☛ Capital of Pakistan → Islamabad
☛ States on India-Pak border → Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir

q: The total area covered by the Andaman & Nicobar Islands is approximately:
qs.e: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a union territory of India located in the Bay of Bengal. Its total geographical area is approximately 8,249 square kilometers. It comprises around 572 islands, of which only 38 are permanently inhabited. The islands are known for their rich biodiversity, beautiful beaches, and historical significance. Port Blair is the capital city. This region lies to the southeast of the Indian mainland and is close to Myanmar and Indonesia.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Andaman and Nicobar → Port Blair
☛ Highest peak → Saddle Peak (732 m)
☛ Largest island group in India → Andaman and Nicobar
☛ Famous national park → Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
☛ Where is Cellular Jail located → Port Blair

q: Which of the following countries serves as India’s gateway to the ASEAN region by being the only ASEAN nation sharing a land boundary with India?
qs.e: Myanmar is the only ASEAN nation that shares a land border with India, serving as India's gateway to the Southeast Asian region. The India-Myanmar boundary extends approximately 1,643 km and touches four Indian states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram. As a member of ASEAN, Myanmar also participates in regional forums like BIMSTEC and the Mekong-Ganga Cooperation. Under India's Act East Policy, Myanmar plays a strategic role in enhancing trade, connectivity, and energy security. Other options— Bhutan, Nepal, and Bangladesh—are not ASEAN members. Myanmar's location makes it a crucial link for India's engagement with the ASEAN region.
qs.kf:
☛ Only ASEAN country sharing land border with India → Myanmar
☛ Length of India-Myanmar border → 1,643 km
☛ Indian states bordering Myanmar → Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram
☛ India's policy emphasizing Myanmar → Act East Policy
☛ Year of ASEAN establishment → 1967

q: Which tree is found in tropical deciduous forests?
qs.e: Tropical deciduous forests are characterized by trees that shed their leaves during the dry season. Sandalwood (Santalum album) is a significant tree found in these forests, especially in regions with monsoon climate and rainfall between 100-200 cm. Mango is also common, but sandalwood is specifically listed. Rhododendron grows in temperate forests, and cedar is found in coniferous forests. Sandalwood is valued for its fragrant heartwood used in perfumes, incense, and medicines. Thus, sandalwood is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for tropical deciduous forests → Monsoon forests
☛ Scientific name of sandalwood → Santalum album
☛ State tree of which state is sandalwood → Karnataka
☛ Rainfall range in tropical deciduous forests → 100-200 cm
☛ Use of sandalwood → Perfumes, incense, medicine

q: Which wildlife sanctuary was set up in West India for preserving Indian lions?
qs.e: Gir Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Gujarat and is the last natural habitat of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica). It was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1965 and later a Gir National Park was also established. The lion population has increased due to conservation efforts, now estimated at around 674. It is the only place in West India where Asiatic lions are found. Other options: Ranthambore (Rajasthan, tigers), Keoladeo Ghana (Rajasthan, birds), Kaziranga (Assam, rhinos).
qs.kf:
☛ Natural habitat of Asiatic lion → Gir Forest, Gujarat
☛ Year of establishment of Gir Wildlife Sanctuary → 1965
☛ Year of declaration of Gir National Park → 1975
☛ Scientific name of Asiatic lion → Panthera leo persica
☛ Estimated lion population in Gir (2023) → 674

q: Which was India's first National Park?
qs.e: India's first National Park is Jim Corbett National Park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park. Located in Nainital district of Uttarakhand, it covers an area of about 520 sq km. It was renamed after Jim Corbett, a renowned hunter and conservationist. The park is known for its rich biodiversity, including the Bengal Tiger and Asian Elephant. In 1973, it became the first reserve under Project Tiger. It is a major hub for eco-tourism and wildlife conservation.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first National Park → Jim Corbett National Park
☛ Year of establishment of Jim Corbett → 1936
☛ Original name of Jim Corbett National Park → Hailey National Park
☛ Year Project Tiger was launched → 1973
☛ State where Jim Corbett is located → Uttarakhand

q: Which of the following statements is false?
o: Mangroves are being destroyed due to urbanization.
qs.e: This statement is false because mangroves are trees or shrubs that grow in coastal saline water. They do not provide fruits like mangoes. Mangroves actually maintain biodiversity, prevent flooding, and protect coastlines from erosion. Mangrove ecosystems are threatened worldwide due to urbanization and development. Mangroves provide habitat for various marine life, sequester carbon, and act as storm buffers.
qs.kf:
☛ Main function of mangrove ecosystem → Coastal protection and biodiversity conservation
☛ Largest mangrove area in India → Sundarbans
☛ One species found in mangroves → Rhizophora mangle
☛ Major cause of mangrove destruction → Urbanization and aquaculture
☛ International day for mangrove conservation → July 26

q: Which of the following is NOT a National Park in India?
qs.e: Shandur National Park is NOT a National Park in India; it is a high-altitude plateau located in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Balphakram National Park is in Meghalaya, known for its rich biodiversity. Anshi National Park is located in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka and is a habitat for tigers and elephants. Dachigam National Park is situated in Jammu and Kashmir and is famous for the Hangul (Kashmir stag). Hence, Shandur is the correct answer as it is not a national park in India.
qs.kf:
☛ First National Park of India → Jim Corbett (1936)
☛ State of Balphakram National Park → Meghalaya
☛ Anshi National Park is in which state → Karnataka
☛ Dachigam National Park is famous for → Hangul (Kashmir stag)
☛ Where is Shandur located → Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan

q: Reforestation means
o: Taking care of animals in the forests
Planting new trees in the destroyed forests
qs.e: Reforestation means planting new trees in forests that have been destroyed due to cutting, fire, or other reasons. This process helps maintain environmental balance, prevent soil erosion, and increase carbon absorption. Visiting forests is just tourism, taking care of animals is animal husbandry, and reinforcing forests is part of forest management, not reforestation. Reforestation also plays a crucial role in mitigating climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide.
qs.kf:
☛ Main objective of reforestation → Restore forests
☛ Difference between afforestation and reforestation → Afforestation is planting in new areas, reforestation is restoring destroyed forests
☛ Environmental benefit of reforestation → Carbon dioxide absorption
☛ Reforestation scheme in India → National Afforestation Programme (NAP)
☛ Forest Conservation Act → Enacted in 1980

q: Which Indian wildlife sanctuary is the home for Asiatic Lions?
qs.e: Gir Wildlife Sanctuary, also known as Gir National Park, is located in the state of Gujarat, India. It is the last natural habitat of the Asiatic lion, a critically endangered species. In the early 1900s, the lion population had dwindled to around 20, but due to conservation efforts, it has now increased to over 600. Gir was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1965. Sariska (Rajasthan) is known for tigers, Kanha (Madhya Pradesh) is famous for tigers and barasingha, and Bandhavgarh (Madhya Pradesh) is also known for tigers. Apart from lions, Gir is home to leopards, spotted deer, and crocodiles.
qs.kf:
☛ Natural habitat of Asiatic lions → Gir National Park
☛ State where Gir Wildlife Sanctuary is located → Gujarat
☛ Main tree species found in Gir → Teak
☛ Other animals found in Gir → Leopard, spotted deer, crocodile
☛ Year of establishment of Gir Sanctuary → 1965

q: In which type of forests Tendu, Amaltas, Bael (Bengal Quince) are found in India?
qs.e: Tendu, Amaltas, and Bael (Bengal Quince) are characteristic trees of dry deciduous forests. These forests are found in regions with moderate rainfall (75-100 cm) and shed their leaves during the dry season. Tendu leaves are used for making beedis, Amaltas has bright yellow flowers, and Bael fruit is known for its medicinal properties. Dry deciduous forests are predominantly found in states like Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Gujarat. They are less dense than moist deciduous forests and also include trees like Sal, Teak, and Mahua.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the rainfall range for dry deciduous forests? → 75-100 cm
☛ What is the use of Tendu leaves? → Making beedis
☛ What color are Amaltas flowers? → Yellow
☛ What is Bael (Bengal Quince) known for? → Medicinal properties
☛ Which states have dry deciduous forests? → Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat

q: Travelling from the Arctic Circle to the Equator what sequence of biomes would one pass through?
o: Tundra, Taiga, Temperate Forests, Tropical Rain Forests
Tropical Rain Forests, Temperate Forests, Taiga, Tundra
Tundra, Temperate Forests, Taiga, Tropical Rain Forests
Taiga, Tundra, Temperate Forests, Tropical Rain Forests
qs.e: Traveling from the Arctic Circle to the Equator, the sequence of biomes follows latitudinal temperature and precipitation patterns. Nearest the Arctic Circle is the Tundra biome, characterized by extreme cold and low precipitation. Next is Taiga (boreal forest), dominated by coniferous trees. Following that are Temperate Forests, with seasonal changes and deciduous trees. Finally, near the Equator, Tropical Rain Forests occur, with warm, humid climates and high biodiversity. This sequence is based on the principle of latitudinal vegetation zones.
qs.kf:
☛ Tundra biome → Found in Arctic and alpine regions
☛ Taiga biome → Boreal forest, dominated by conifers
☛ Temperate Forests → Deciduous and mixed forests, mid-latitudes
☛ Tropical Rain Forests → Near Equator, high biodiversity
☛ Latitudinal vegetation sequence → Pole to Equator: Tundra, Taiga, Temperate Forests, Tropical Forests

q: Sal and teak are the most important _______ trees.
qs.e: Sal and teak are deciduous trees found in monsoon climates. They shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve moisture. They are major components of tropical deciduous forests. Sal is found in eastern and central India, while teak grows in central and southern India. Their wood is strong and used for furniture and construction. Coniferous trees like pine grow in cold regions, while pioneer trees colonize barren lands. Medicinal trees include neem and harad.
qs.kf:
☛ In which type of forest are sal and teak found? → Tropical deciduous forest
☛ What is the main feature of deciduous trees? → Shedding leaves in dry season
☛ Which trees are called coniferous? → Those bearing cone-shaped fruits (e.g., pine)
☛ Where do pioneer trees grow? → First on barren or degraded land
☛ Where is sal tree mainly found? → Eastern and central India

q: Bamboo, birch, sal, spruce and sheesham can be found in the ______ forest.
qs.e: Temperate deciduous forests are found in regions with moderate climates, where winters are cold and summers are warm. Trees in these forests shed their leaves in autumn. Bamboo, birch, sal, spruce, and sheesham are species that can be found in temperate deciduous forests. Spruce is a conifer, but it can also be found in mixed temperate deciduous forests. Coniferous forests have trees like pine and cedar. Alpine forests occur at high altitudes. Temperate forests include broadleaf evergreens, but the given trees are of deciduous nature.
qs.kf:
☛ Where are temperate deciduous forests found? → Eastern North America, Western Europe, East Asia
☛ What is the main characteristic of temperate deciduous forests? → Trees shed leaves in autumn
☛ Oak, maple, beech are found in which forest? → Temperate deciduous forest
☛ What type of tree is spruce? → Coniferous
☛ Sal is found in which forest? → Temperate deciduous forest

q: Which national park in India has the maximum number of rhinos?
qs.e: Kaziranga National Park, located in Assam, is the national park in India with the highest number of rhinos. It is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros (Indian rhinoceros). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and hosts about two-thirds of the world's population of one-horned rhinos. Kaziranga is spread across the floodplains of the Brahmaputra River and features grasslands, swamps, and dense forests. The park is renowned for rhino conservation under Project Rhino.
qs.kf:
☛ India's largest rhino sanctuary → Kaziranga National Park
☛ Scientific name of one-horned rhino → Rhinoceros unicornis
☛ Kaziranga National Park is in which state → Assam
☛ River along which Kaziranga lies → Brahmaputra River
☛ Major campaign for rhino conservation → Project Rhino

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about mangrove forests?
o: Mangrove forests stabilise the coastline, reducing erosion.
Mangrove trees grow in areas with oxygen-rich soil.
qs.e: Mangrove forests are unique coastal ecosystems found in tropical and subtropical regions. They play a crucial role in stabilising coastlines and reducing erosion. Mangrove trees are salt-tolerant and grow in anaerobic (oxygen-poor) soil because tidal areas experience waterlogging, leading to oxygen deficiency. Thus, the statement that mangroves grow in oxygen-rich soil is incorrect. Mangroves cannot withstand freezing temperatures, which limits their distribution. They are trees, not herbs, so the statement that mangroves are salt-tolerant herbs is also incorrect. Mangrove roots have specialised structures like pneumatophores to obtain oxygen from the air.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of soil do mangroves grow in? → Anaerobic (oxygen-poor) soil
☛ What is the ecological benefit of mangroves? → Coastline stabilisation and erosion reduction
☛ What temperature can mangroves not tolerate? → Freezing temperatures
☛ What is the nature of mangroves? → Salt-tolerant trees
☛ Where are mangroves found? → Tropical and subtropical coastal areas

q: What type of forests are found in the Sunderbans Delta in India?
qs.e: The Sunderbans Delta, formed at the confluence of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, contains Mangrove forests. It is the largest mangrove forest region in the world, spanning India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh. Mangrove plants grow in saline water and are the characteristic vegetation of this area. The famous Royal Bengal Tiger is found in these forests. Mangrove forests protect coastal areas from tsunamis and cyclones.
qs.kf:
☛ Most famous animal of Sunderbans → Royal Bengal Tiger
☛ Main characteristic of mangrove forests → Growing in saline water
☛ In which Indian state is Sunderbans located → West Bengal
☛ World's largest mangrove forest → Sunderbans
☛ Ecological benefit of mangrove forests → Coastal protection

q: As per NASA, how much of Earth's land surface is covered by forests?
qs.e: According to NASA, approximately 30% of Earth's total land surface is covered by forests. This figure is derived from satellite data and global forest mapping. Forests are vital for the planet's ecosystem as they contribute to carbon absorption, oxygen production, biodiversity conservation, and climate regulation. The distribution of forests is uneven, with most forests found in tropical, temperate, and boreal regions. Deforestation and climate change are causing a decline in forest area. NASA and other space agencies regularly conduct satellite-based assessments to monitor global forest cover.
qs.kf:
☛ What percentage of Earth's land area is covered by forests? → 30%
☛ Which country has the largest forest cover? → Russia
☛ What is the forest cover percentage in India? → Approximately 21.7%
☛ What is a primary function of forests? → Carbon absorption and oxygen production
☛ Which agency is responsible for global forest cover monitoring? → NASA and FAO

q: Which of the following National Highway passes through the Kaziranga National Park is imposing key threat for the wildlife?
qs.e: Kaziranga National Park is located in Assam and is a wildlife sanctuary. It is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros. The NH-37 national highway passes through this park, posing a major threat to wildlife. This road divides the park into two parts, disrupting animal movement and causing vehicle collisions. The government has built underpasses and overpasses to protect wildlife, yet NH-37 remains a key threat.
qs.kf:
☛ Kaziranga National Park is located in which state? → Assam
☛ Kaziranga is famous for which animal? → One-horned rhinoceros
☛ Which National Highway passes through Kaziranga? → NH-37
☛ How does NH-37 threaten wildlife? → By dividing the park and causing vehicle collisions
☛ What was built in Kaziranga for wildlife safety? → Underpasses and overpasses

q: Which among the following is the tallest tree species in the world?
qs.e: The tallest tree species in the world is the Redwood (Sequoia sempervirens). It is primarily found in the coastal regions of California, USA. Redwoods can reach heights of up to 115 meters. One redwood tree, named Hyperion, is recorded at 116 meters tall. These trees are evergreen, coniferous, and can live for over 2000 years. Deodar, Oak, and Eucalyptus are also tall, but Redwood is the tallest.
qs.kf:
☛ World's tallest tree species → Redwood (Sequoia sempervirens)
☛ Tallest redwood tree → Hyperion (116 meters)
☛ Main location of redwood → California, USA
☛ Botanical name of redwood → Sequoia sempervirens
☛ Tallest tree in India → Deodar (Cedrus deodara)

q: Kaziranga National Park is famous for:
qs.e: Kaziranga National Park is located in Assam and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is famous for hosting the largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros. Established in 1905, it spans the floodplains of the Brahmaputra River. Besides rhinos, it is home to elephants, tigers, leopards, wild buffaloes, and numerous bird species. It is also important for the conservation of the Royal Bengal Tiger and Asian elephant. Kaziranga was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. It is one of the oldest national parks in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Kaziranga National Park located? → Assam
☛ Which river flows near Kaziranga? → Brahmaputra
☛ Which species of rhino is found in Kaziranga? → Indian one-horned rhino
☛ When did Kaziranga become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1985
☛ Which are the major mammals found in Kaziranga? → Rhino, elephant, tiger, buffalo

q: _____ is NOT a notified Biosphere Reserve in India.
qs.e: India has 18 notified Biosphere Reserves. Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (2000), Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve (2001), and Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve (1999) are notified. However, Nallamalai is not a Biosphere Reserve; it is a forest area located in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Nallamalai is part of the Eastern Ghats and is a component of the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve. It is not included in the list of Biosphere Reserves.
qs.kf:
☛ First Biosphere Reserve of India → Nilgiri (2000)
☛ State with most Biosphere Reserves → West Bengal (3)
☛ Largest Biosphere Reserve → Great Nicobar
☛ Indian Biosphere Reserves recognized by UNESCO → 12
☛ Nallamalai is part of which Tiger Reserve → Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam

q: Which of the following tiger reserve is located in the protected place at Sabarimala?
qs.e: The Sabarimala pilgrimage site falls within the Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala. Located in the Western Ghats, Periyar was established as a wildlife sanctuary in 1950 and later declared a tiger reserve in 1978. It is renowned for its biodiversity and the Periyar Lake, where elephants, tigers, and other wildlife can be spotted. The area also holds religious significance due to the Sabarimala temple, which attracts millions of devotees annually. Among the options, Parambikulam, Bandipur, and Mudumalai are located in Tamil Nadu and Kerala but are not directly associated with Sabarimala.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Periyar Tiger Reserve located? → Kerala
☛ When was Periyar Tiger Reserve established? → 1978
☛ Which river flows through Periyar sanctuary? → Periyar River
☛ Which tiger reserve contains the Sabarimala temple? → Periyar
☛ What was Periyar Tiger Reserve originally called? → Nilgiri Tahr Sanctuary

q: Oak and chestnut trees are ________________.
qs.e: Oak and chestnut trees are evergreen wide leafy trees. This vegetation is mainly found in Mediterranean regions and temperate forests. Their leaves remain green throughout the year and are broad. They are hardwood trees, used in furniture and construction. They do not belong to tundra or mangrove vegetation, but are key components of mixed forests. Although some species may be deciduous, the common classification places them under evergreen broadleaf. This vegetation is more common in Northern Hemisphere temperate zones.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of trees are oak trees? → Evergreen wide leafy
☛ What is the botanical name of chestnut? → Castanea sativa
☛ What is the main vegetation of Mediterranean region? → Evergreen broadleaf trees
☛ Which trees provide hardwood? → Oak, chestnut, teak
☛ When do evergreen trees shed leaves? → Old leaves fall as new leaves emerge, not all at once

q: What type of Forests are found in trees, such as teak, sal, and shisham?
qs.e: Trees like teak, sal, and shisham are found in Tropical Deciduous Forests. These forests are the most widespread in India and are also known as Monsoon Forests. They are divided into moist and dry deciduous types based on rainfall. Key tree species include teak, sal, shisham, mahua, amla, and bamboo. In moist deciduous forests, sal and teak dominate, while dry deciduous forests feature shisham and others. These forests are spread across Assam, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, and southern India. Teak wood is valuable for furniture and construction. Sal wood is used for railway sleepers and timber. The trees shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the botanical name of teak? → Tectona grandis
☛ Which family does sal tree belong to? → Dipterocarpaceae
☛ What is the botanical name of shisham? → Dalbergia sissoo
☛ Which state in India is famous for sal forests? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ What is the other name of tropical deciduous forests? → Monsoon forests

q: What was the specific target for forest area as a percentage of the total land area set in the Forest Policy of India?
qs.e: The National Forest Policy of India, 1952 first set the target of having 33% of the total geographical area under forest cover. This target was reaffirmed by the National Forest Policy, 1988. The policy recommends 33% forest cover for plains and 67% for hilly regions. The main objectives are maintaining ecological balance, conserving biodiversity, and ensuring climate stability. Currently, India's forest cover is about 21.71% (2021 report), which is significantly below the target.
qs.kf:
☛ Forest target set by National Forest Policy, 1952 → 33%
☛ Forest target set by National Forest Policy, 1988 → 33%
☛ Forest target for hilly regions → 67%
☛ Current forest cover of India (2021) → 21.71%
☛ Main objective of forest policy → Ecological balance

q: What types of forest are found in areas with rainfall over 200 cm?
qs.e: Areas receiving rainfall over 200 cm are home to Tropical Evergreen Forests. These forests thrive in regions with high rainfall (over 200 cm) and high temperatures. They are dense, multi-layered, and remain green throughout the year as trees do not shed their leaves all at once. Key species include mahogany, ebony, rosewood, bamboo, and rubber. In India, these forests are found in the Western Ghats, Assam, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and parts of the northeastern states. Globally, they are found in the Amazon Basin, Congo Basin, and Southeast Asia. These forests have rich biodiversity and are also known as rainforests.
qs.kf:
☛ Which forest receives the highest rainfall? → Tropical Evergreen Forest
☛ What is the average annual rainfall for evergreen forests? → Over 200 cm (often up to 400 cm)
☛ What is a key characteristic of evergreen forests? → Trees remain leafy throughout the year and do not shed leaves at a specific time
☛ Where are evergreen forests mainly found in India? → Western Ghats, Assam, Andaman & Nicobar Islands
☛ What are common species in evergreen forests? → Mahogany, ebony, rosewood, bamboo, rubber

q: Which of the following important diversity is found in Himalayan wet forest?
qs.e: Himalayan wet forests are mainly found in the Eastern Himalayas and the Western Ghats. These forests develop in high rainfall areas. In these forests, Oak (Quercus spp.) trees are predominant. Oak is an important tree species found at high altitudes. It thrives in humid environments. Teak and Mahogany are mainly found in tropical dry or moist forests, while Oak is a characteristic tree of Himalayan wet forests. It is a significant component of biodiversity and provides habitat for wildlife.
qs.kf:
☛ Dominant tree species in Himalayan wet forest → Oak (Quercus)
☛ Altitude range of Himalayan wet forest → 1500-3300 meters
☛ Scientific name of Oak tree → Quercus
☛ Fruit of Oak tree → Acorn
☛ Other trees found in Himalayan wet forest → Rhododendron, Deodar

q: Which forest trees do not have any definite time to drop their leaves?
qs.e: Tropical Evergreen Forests do not have a definite time for leaf shedding because they are found in regions with high temperature and rainfall. The climate remains favorable throughout the year, so trees retain their leaves permanently. The leaves are broad and dark green. These forests are found in the Amazon Basin, Congo Basin, and Southeast Asia. In India, they occur in the Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and Assam. They are also called rainforests.
qs.kf:
☛ Time of leaf fall in Tropical Evergreen Forests → No definite time
☛ Annual rainfall in Tropical Evergreen Forests → More than 200 cm
☛ Forest with highest biodiversity → Tropical Evergreen Forests
☛ Areas of Tropical Evergreen Forests in India → Western Ghats, Northeast India, Andaman & Nicobar
☛ Other name for Tropical Evergreen Forests → Rainforests

q: Which of the following is a protected biosphere situated in Assam?
qs.e: Manas is a protected biosphere situated in Assam, India. It was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1989. Located on the banks of the Manas River, it was initially established as a sanctuary in 1928. The region is famous for rare species like the Bengal tiger, Asian elephant, and golden langur. Other wildlife includes the hispid hare and pygmy hog. Manas was also declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985, though later listed as endangered. It remains a crucial conservation area. Among the other options, Sunderban is in West Bengal, Nørrek is in Meghalaya (though not a biosphere reserve), and Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand. Thus, Manas is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the first national park of Assam? → Kaziranga National Park
☛ Which river flows through Manas? → Manas River
☛ When was Manas declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve? → 1989
☛ Which rare primate is found in Manas? → Golden langur
☛ Which smallest pig species is found in Manas? → Pygmy hog

q: Which of the following biosphere is not included in the World Network of Biosphere Reserve?
qs.e: A total of 18 biosphere reserves from India are included in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves. Gulf of Mannar (2001), Nanda Devi (2004), and Great Nicobar (2018) are part of this network. Dibru-Sakhova is a biosphere reserve located in Assam, but it has not yet been included in the UNESCO network. It is a protected area known for its rare flora and fauna.
qs.kf:
☛ First biosphere reserve of India → Nilgiri (1986)
☛ Number of Indian biosphere reserves in UNESCO network → 18
☛ Largest biosphere reserve → Great Nicobar
☛ Dibru-Sakhova is in which state → Assam
☛ Gulf of Mannar is associated with which state → Tamil Nadu

q: Which of the following Wildlife Sanctuaries is located in Madhya Pradesh?
qs.e: Bori Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Hoshangabad district of Madhya Pradesh and forms part of the Satpura Tiger Reserve. It was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1977 and covers an area of approximately 518 sq km. The sanctuary is rich in biodiversity and is home to tigers, leopards, sloth bears, sambar, and chital. Manas Wildlife Sanctuary is in Assam, Bandipur National Park is in Karnataka, and Indravati Tiger Reserve is in Chhattisgarh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state has Bori Wildlife Sanctuary? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Bori Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which district? → Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram)
☛ Bori Wildlife Sanctuary is part of which Tiger Reserve? → Satpura Tiger Reserve
☛ When was Bori Wildlife Sanctuary established? → 1977
☛ Bandipur National Park is in which state? → Karnataka

q: Which of the following tiger sanctuaries is located in Madhya Pradesh?
qs.e: Panna National Park is a prominent tiger sanctuary located in Madhya Pradesh. It is situated in the Panna district of north Madhya Pradesh and was declared a tiger reserve in 1994. It is the third largest tiger reserve in the state by area. The park is also home to the Panna diamond mining area, famous for diamond extraction. Bandipur and Nagarhole are in Karnataka, while Manas is in Assam.
qs.kf:
☛ How many tiger reserves are in Madhya Pradesh? → 7
☛ Which is the largest tiger reserve in Madhya Pradesh? → Kanha National Park
☛ When was Panna Tiger Reserve established? → 1994
☛ In which state is Manas National Park? → Assam
☛ In which state is Bandipur National Park? → Karnataka

q: Which of the following protected areas is also a Tiger Reserve?
o: Gahirmatha Seaboard Wildlife Sanctuary (Marine Wildlife Sanctuary)
qs.e: Jim Corbett National Park is India's first national park, established in 1936. Located in Uttarakhand, it is also a Tiger Reserve, declared under Project Tiger in 1973. Veedathangal Wildlife Sanctuary is in Tamil Nadu, Gahirmatha Seaboard Wildlife Sanctuary is in Odisha, and Saddle Peak Biosphere Reserve is in the Andaman Islands. None of these three are Tiger Reserves. Therefore, Jim Corbett National Park is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first national park → Jim Corbett National Park
☛ Former name of Jim Corbett → Hailey National Park
☛ Project Tiger started in → 1973
☛ Jim Corbett located in → Uttarakhand
☛ Year of establishment of Jim Corbett → 1936

q: Forest land, which is further protected from deprivation, is known as ____________.
qs.e: In India, forests are classified based on the degree of government protection. Protected Forest is forest land that is further safeguarded from deprivation. This category is defined under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, where activities are regulated by forest officials with certain restrictions, though less stringent than Reserve Forests. Holy Grooves are areas protected due to cultural reasons, while Unincorporated Forests fall outside government control. Thus, the correct answer is Protected Forest.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indian Forest Act enacted? → 1927
☛ Which is the most protected forest category? → Reserve Forest
☛ Who must permit activities in Protected Forests? → Forest officers
☛ Why are Holy Grooves protected? → Religious/cultural reasons
☛ Unincorporated Forests are under which ownership? → Private

q: The vegetation grown in the British climate is characterized by-
qs.e: The British climate is a temperate maritime climate, characterized by adequate rainfall and moderate temperatures throughout the year. The natural vegetation here is deciduous forests, which shed their leaves in autumn. Hence, this vegetation is characterized by 'decline', referring to the process of leaf fall. Lead grasslands and mixed forests belong to other regions, while desert vegetation is not found in Britain.
qs.kf:
☛ Climate type of Britain → Temperate maritime (Cfb)
☛ Natural vegetation of Britain → Deciduous forests
☛ Average annual temperature of Britain → About 10°C
☛ Rainfall distribution in Britain → Uniform throughout the year
☛ Effect of Gulf Stream → Makes British climate temperate

q: Which of the following Mangrove forest is found in West Bengal?
qs.e: Sunderbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, located in West Bengal and Bangladesh. It lies in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Pichavaram is in Tamil Nadu, Mahanadi in Odisha, and Ratnagiri in Maharashtra. This forest is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger and diverse species.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest mangrove forest in India → Sunderbans
☛ Delta where Sunderbans is located → Ganges-Brahmaputra delta
☛ Countries where Sunderbans is spread → India and Bangladesh
☛ Year Sunderbans became UNESCO site → 1987
☛ Famous animal found in Sunderbans → Royal Bengal Tiger

q: Which of the following national parks is in Assam?
qs.e: Manas National Park is located in the state of Assam. It lies in the foothills of the Himalayas and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is famous for tiger conservation and biodiversity. The park is home to the Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros, tiger, elephant, and Pygmy Hog. Other options: Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand), Namdafa (Arunachal Pradesh), and Silent Valley (Kerala).
qs.kf:
☛ National parks in Assam → Manas and Kaziranga
☛ UNESCO World Heritage Sites → Manas, Kaziranga (Assam), Sundarbans (WB), Nokrek (Meghalaya)
☛ Habitat of Pygmy Hog → Manas National Park
☛ Manas River → Tributary of Brahmaputra
☛ Biosphere Reserve → Manas Biosphere Reserve

q: Which type of vegetation is mostly found in the Thar Desert?
qs.e: The Thar Desert is a hot and arid region with annual rainfall less than 25 cm. Due to extreme temperatures and low water availability, thorny bushes and shrubs thrive here. These plants are adapted to survive with minimal water through features like leaves reduced to spines, thick bark, and deep root systems. Common species include Acacia, Khejri (Prosopis cineraria), and various grasses. Deciduous forests, alpine vegetation, and tropical rainforests cannot exist in desert conditions as they require high moisture and suitable climate. Thus, the Thar Desert predominantly supports thorny bushes and shrubs.
qs.kf:
☛ Main vegetation of Thar Desert → Thorny bushes and shrubs
☛ Common tree found in Thar Desert → Khejri (Prosopis cineraria)
☛ Climate of Thar Desert → Extremely hot and dry
☛ Average annual rainfall in Thar Desert → Less than 25 cm
☛ Adaptation of thorny plants in Thar Desert → Leaves reduced to spines to conserve water

q: Which of the following states has the Sundarbans mangrove forest?
qs.e: The Sundarbans mangrove forest is located in West Bengal. It is the largest mangrove forest in the world, spread across the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta. A part of it is also in Bangladesh. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger. The name 'Sundarbans' is derived from the 'Sundari' tree found there. This area is rich in biodiversity and home to many endangered species. The Sundarbans National Park was established in 1984.
qs.kf:
☛ Which delta is the Sundarbans located in? → Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta
☛ In which Indian state is the Sundarbans? → West Bengal
☛ What is the Sundarbans famous for? → Royal Bengal Tiger
☛ From which tree is the name Sundarbans derived? → Sundari
☛ When was the Sundarbans National Park established? → 1984

q: Which type of forests are found in areas with annual rainfall above 200 cm?
qs.e: Areas with annual rainfall above 200 cm have Tropical Evergreen Forests. These forests are dense, multi-layered, and rich in biodiversity. They are also called Rain Forests. Trees remain green throughout the year and do not shed leaves simultaneously. Major species include Rosewood, Ebony, Mahogany, Rubber etc. In India, these forests are mainly found in the Western Ghats, Northeast India, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
qs.kf:
☛ Other names of Tropical Evergreen Forests → Rain Forests, Equatorial Forests
☛ Major tree species in Tropical Evergreen Forests → Rosewood, Ebony, Mahogany, Rubber
☛ Extent of Tropical Evergreen Forests in India → Western Ghats, Northeast India, Andaman & Nicobar
☛ Characteristic of Tropical Evergreen Forests → Dense, multi-layered, rich biodiversity
☛ Average annual rainfall in Tropical Evergreen Forests → Above 200 cm

q: In India, the Sundari tree is a prominent species found in which type of forests?
qs.e: The Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes) is a prominent species found in mangrove forests in India. It is predominantly found in the Sundarbans region, located in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta in West Bengal and Bangladesh. The Sundari tree is tolerant to saline water and plays a vital role in the mangrove ecosystem. Its wood is hard and durable, used for construction and boat building. Mangrove forests are found in coastal areas of India and provide protection against storms and tsunamis. Besides Sundari, other major mangrove species include Goran and Gewa.
qs.kf:
☛ On which delta is the Sundarbans located? → Ganges-Brahmaputra delta
☛ What is the scientific name of the Sundari tree? → Heritiera fomes
☛ Which is the largest mangrove forest in India? → Sundarbans
☛ In what type of water are mangrove forests found? → Saline water
☛ What is the wood of the Sundari tree used for? → Construction and boat building

q: In which type of forest is scrub vegetation typically found in India?
qs.e: In India, scrub vegetation is typically found in Tropical Thorn forests. These forests develop in dry and semi-arid regions where annual rainfall is less than 50 cm. The trees are sparse and widely scattered, with thorny shrubs and bushes like Acacia, Cactus, and Euphorbia being dominant. These forests are mainly located in parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, and some dry areas of the Deccan Plateau. The leaves are small and waxy to conserve water, adapting to the arid climate.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the geographical extent of Tropical Thorn forests? → Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana
☛ What is the annual rainfall range in these forests? → Less than 50 cm
☛ What is the dominant vegetation in Thorn forests? → Acacia, Cactus, Khair
☛ What other name are these forests known by? → Dry forests
☛ What is the leaf characteristic in Thorn forests? → Small and waxy leaves

q: Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option regarding their correctness.
Statement I: ‘Project Tiger’ is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) of the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change.

Statement II: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has been fulfilling its mandate of strengthening tiger conservation in the country within the ambit of the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972.
o: Statement I is incorrect, while Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
qs.e: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) under the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change. Its goal is to protect tigers and their habitats. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) was established under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. It works to strengthen tiger conservation in India by managing tiger reserves, preventing poaching, and conserving habitats. Thus, both statements are accurate.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Project Tiger launched? → 1 April 1973
☛ Which ministry administers Project Tiger? → Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change
☛ What does NTCA stand for? → National Tiger Conservation Authority
☛ Under which act was NTCA constituted? → Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
☛ Which scheme is a CSS for tiger conservation? → Project Tiger

q: In which regions of India are the Mangrove Forests found?
qs.e: Mangrove forests are primarily found in the delta regions of India, where rivers meet the sea. These forests grow in saline water environments and have roots that are exposed above water. Major mangrove forests in India include the Sundarbans (Ganga-Brahmaputra delta), Godavari-Krishna delta, Kutch, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. They are ecologically vital for preventing coastal erosion, providing storm protection, and serving as breeding grounds for fish. Cold deserts, hot deserts, and plateaus are not suitable for mangrove growth.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the largest mangrove forest in India? → Sundarbans (West Bengal)
☛ What type of water is required for mangrove forests? → Saline water
☛ In which state is the Godavari-Krishna delta located? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Name a prominent tree species in mangroves. → Sundari (Heritiera fomes)
☛ India ranks which in terms of mangrove area globally? → Fourth largest

q: Which of the following is the first biosphere reserve established in India?
qs.e: India's first biosphere reserve is the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, established in the year 1986. It is located at the confluence of the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats and spans the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is renowned for its rich biodiversity and includes several national parks and wildlife sanctuaries such as Mudumalai, Wayanad, Bandipur, Nagarhole, and Silent Valley. It is also part of UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Program.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first biosphere reserve → Nilgiri (1986)
☛ Total biosphere reserves in India → 18
☛ UNESCO-recognized biosphere reserves in India → 12
☛ States included in Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve → Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka
☛ Largest biosphere reserve in India → Rann of Kutch

q: Which of the following options best describes the purpose of the Red Data Book?
o: A list of protected forest areas
A compilation of forest conservation laws
A record of endangered plant and animal species
qs.e: The Red Data Book is a document published by the IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) that records endangered and threatened species of plants and animals. Its purpose is to raise awareness for biodiversity conservation and prioritize conservation efforts. It categorizes species based on their threat status (e.g., extinct, endangered, vulnerable). The Red Data Book is not a list of forest areas, laws, or tree species; it specifically focuses on biodiversity under threat. It serves as a crucial tool for policymakers, researchers, and conservationists to identify species needing urgent protection.
qs.kf:
☛ Who publishes the Red Data Book? → IUCN
☛ Which species are included in the Red Data Book? → Endangered and threatened species
☛ What is the main purpose of the Red Data Book? → Awareness and priority for conservation
☛ What is the difference between Red List and Red Data Book? → Red List is IUCN's global list; Red Data Book can be at national level
☛ Which Indian institutions prepare the Red Data Book? → Wildlife Institute of India (WII) and Forest Survey of India (FSI)

q: Which of the following natural regions is known for evergreen dense forests and high biodiversity?
qs.e: The equatorial region is located around the equator on Earth, experiencing high temperatures and heavy rainfall throughout the year. This climate is ideal for the growth of evergreen rainforests, which are characterized by dense trees, multi-layered canopies, and extremely high biodiversity. Countless species of plants and animals inhabit these forests. The tundra region is very cold and treeless, the steppe region consists of dry grasslands, and the Mediterranean region has forests with hard-leaved vegetation. Therefore, only the equatorial region is known for these features.
qs.kf:
☛ Evergreen rainforests are found in which climate? → Equatorial climate (hot and humid)
☛ Which natural region has the highest biodiversity? → Equatorial rainforest
☛ Average annual rainfall in equatorial region? → More than 200 cm
☛ Temperature of equatorial region is? → High throughout the year (about 25°C-28°C)
☛ What is the vegetation of tundra region? → Treeless, mosses and lichens are found

q: The Western Ghats and the northeastern hills of India are primarily covered with which type of natural vegetation?
qs.e: The Western Ghats and northeastern hills of India are primarily covered with Tropical Evergreen Forests. These regions receive high rainfall(over 200 cm) and have high temperatures, which allow trees to remain green throughout the year without shedding leaves. Important trees include rosewood, mahogany, and ebony. The Western Ghats get heavy rain from the western winds, while northeastern states receive abundant rainfall from the southwest monsoon. These forests are biodiversity hotspots and contain many endemic species. They are also found in the Andaman Islands and parts of Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ Forests mainly found in Western Ghats → Tropical Evergreen Forests
☛ Rainfall required for evergreen forests → Over 200 cm
☛ Biodiversity hotspot in India → Western Ghats and Northeast
☛ Major trees in evergreen forests → Mahogany, Ebony, Rosewood
☛ Regions with tropical evergreen forests → Andaman Islands, Kerala, Assam

q: In which of the following Indian states is the Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve located?
qs.e: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve is located in West Bengal, India. It is part of the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta and is one of the largest mangrove forest areas in the world. This region is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The biosphere reserve includes three zones: core, buffer, and transition. It is renowned for its rich biodiversity and unique ecosystem.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve established? → 1989
☛ In which year did Sundarbans National Park become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1987
☛ What is the total area of the Sundarbans? → Approximately 10,000 sq km
☛ Which rivers form the Sundarbans delta? → Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna
☛ Which famous tiger subspecies is found in Sundarbans? → Royal Bengal Tiger

q: Which of the following Biosphere Reserves is located in Tamil Nadu?
qs.e: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is located in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is India's first marine biosphere reserve, established in 1989. This reserve encompasses the coastal areas and 21 islands of the Gulf of Mannar. It is renowned for its rich biodiversity, including species like sea turtles, dugongs, and various types of fish. The reserve conserves ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrasses, and coral reefs. UNESCO has included it in the World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which is India's first marine biosphere reserve? → Gulf of Mannar
☛ When was the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve established? → 1989
☛ How many islands are included in the Gulf of Mannar reserve? → 21
☛ Which marine mammal is found in the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve? → Dugong

q: Wildlife sanctuaries in India are primarily established for:
qs.e: Wildlife sanctuaries in India are primarily established for protecting endangered species and their natural habitats. These protected areas safeguard wildlife from poaching, encroachment, and human interference. They are notified under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. Human activities are restricted in sanctuaries, but tourism is allowed. Their aim is to maintain ecological balance and conserve biodiversity. India has over 500 wildlife sanctuaries.
qs.kf:
☛ Primary purpose of wildlife sanctuary → Conservation of endangered species
☛ First wildlife sanctuary in India → Mudumalai (1940)
☛ Largest wildlife sanctuary → Kaziranga (Assam)
☛ Wildlife Protection Act → 1972
☛ Difference between sanctuary and national park → Partial human activity allowed in sanctuary

q: What type of vegetation is the Mediterranean region most known for?
qs.e: The Mediterranean region is characterized by hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. The native vegetation is primarily composed of shrubs and drought-resistant trees such as olive, cedar, oak, and pine. This vegetation is adapted to survive the long dry season, featuring thick bark, small leaves, and deep root systems. The region includes countries around the Mediterranean Sea like Spain, Italy, Greece, Turkey, and North Africa, as well as other parts of the world with similar climates such as California, central Chile, and southwestern Australia. This vegetation type is known as sclerophyll or chaparral.
qs.kf:
☛ Mediterranean climate → Hot dry summers, mild wet winters
☛ Main vegetation type → Shrubs and drought-resistant trees
☛ Characteristic tree species → Olive, cedar, oak, pine
☛ Example regions → California, Chile, South Africa
☛ Adaptations → Thick bark, small leaves, deep roots

q: Tussocky grass grows mainly in which type of forests?
qs.e: Tussocky grass grows mainly in tropical thorn forests. These forests are found in dry and semi-arid climates with annual rainfall between 50-75 cm. They are characterized by thorny shrubs, acacia, and euphorbia plants. Tussocky grass is the dominant ground cover in these forests and is used as fodder for livestock. This grass is drought-resistant and thrives in open, sunny areas. In India, such forests are mainly found in parts of southern Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Karnataka.
qs.kf:
☛ Grass found in Tropical Thorn forests → Tussocky grass
☛ Annual rainfall in Tropical Thorn forests → 50-75 cm
☛ Geographical extent in India → Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka
☛ Major tree species → Acacia, Euphorbia
☛ Use of Tussocky grass → Animal fodder

q: Littoral forests are most associated with which kind of ecosystem?
