q: Which satellite was launched by PSLV-C51 on 28 February 2021?
qs.e: On 28 February 2021, India's PSLV-C51 rocket successfully launched Brazil's Amazonia-1 satellite. It was the 53rd mission of PSLV and ISRO's first commercial mission with a foreign satellite as the main payload. Amazonia-1 is an Earth observation satellite that monitors vegetation and environmental changes in the Amazon region. The mission also carried 18 other small satellites. This launch strengthened India's space capabilities and promoted international cooperation.
qs.kf:
☛ Main payload of PSLV-C51 → Amazonia-1
☛ Amazonia-1 belongs to which country → Brazil
☛ When was PSLV-C51 launched → 28 February 2021
☛ Which was the 53rd mission of PSLV → PSLV-C51
☛ How many satellites were there in PSLV-C51 besides Amazonia-1 → 18

q: Thumba was chosen as the ideal site for rocket launch due to the presence of _______
qs.e: Thumba was chosen as the ideal site for rocket launch because it is located near the equator and has the presence of equatorial electrojets. These are strong electric currents in the ionosphere that interact with Earth's magnetic field and help in studying the upper atmosphere. The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) was established in 1963. Its proximity to the magnetic equator allows rockets to effectively study the Earth's magnetic field and ionospheric phenomena, making it a unique and valuable location for space research.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Thumba rocket launch station located? → Near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala
☛ What is the full form of TERLS? → Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station
☛ When was Thumba chosen as a launch site? → 1963
☛ In which layer are equatorial electrojets found? → Ionosphere
☛ Near which line is Thumba located? → Equator

q: When was India's first satellite, the Aryabhata spacecraft launched?
qs.e: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched on April 19, 1975 from Kapustin Yar, Soviet Union. It was named after the renowned Indian mathematician and astronomer Aryabhata. The satellite was built by ISRO and launched using a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket. Aryabhata's primary objectives included scientific experiments and telecommunications. It was placed in low Earth orbit and weighed approximately 360 kilograms. The launch of Aryabhata marked India's entry into space research and gave the country a new identity in the field.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first satellite → Aryabhata
☛ Launch site of Aryabhata → Kapustin Yar, Soviet Union
☛ Launch vehicle of Aryabhata → Kosmos-3M
☛ Weight of Aryabhata → 360 kilograms
☛ Launch year of Aryabhata → 1975

q: Which of the following is the indigenously developed Beyond-Visual-Range Air- to-Air Missile (BVRAAM), successfully test-fired by the Indian Air Force in September 2018?
qs.e: Astra is an indigenously developed Beyond-Visual-Range Air-to-Air Missile (BVRAAM), developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). It has a range of 110 km and is capable of supersonic speed. In September 2018, the Indian Air Force successfully test-fired it from a Su-30 MKI fighter aircraft, hitting the target with precision. Astra is part of India's Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) and marks a significant step towards self-reliance in air-to-air missile technology.
qs.kf:
☛ Range of Astra missile → 110 km
☛ Developer of Astra missile → DRDO
☛ Test year of Astra missile → 2018
☛ Type of Astra missile → BVRAAM
☛ Aircraft used for Astra test → Su-30 MKI

q: Sriharikota, from where Chandrayaan-2 was launched, is located in which district?
qs.e: Sriharikota is located in the Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh. It houses the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), which is the primary launch center of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Chandrayaan-2 was launched from here on July 22, 2019. This center is situated on the Sriharikota island, between the Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal. The city of Nellore is the district headquarters and lies about 80 km north of Chennai.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Satish Dhawan Space Centre located? → Sriharikota, Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh
☛ What is the launch site of Chandrayaan-2? → Satish Dhawan Space Centre
☛ Which is ISRO's primary launch center? → Satish Dhawan Space Centre
☛ Which state is Nellore district in? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Between which districts is Pulicat Lake located? → Nellore and Tiruvallur

q: _______ orbit did not have a space station. A. Mir B. Salyut 7
C. Skylab D. Voyager 1
qs.e: Voyager 1 is a space probe launched by NASA in 1977, not a space station. It was designed to study the outer planets of the solar system and is now traveling in interstellar space. In contrast, Mir, Salyut 7, and Skylab are all space stations. Mir was a Soviet space station active from 1986 to 2001. Salyut 7 operated from 1982 to 1991. Skylab was an American space station that operated from 1973 to 1979. Therefore, Voyager 1 is the correct answer as it never operated as an orbital space station.
qs.kf:
☛ Which was the first space station? → Salyut 1
☛ First American space station? → Skylab
☛ Longest operating space station before ISS? → Mir (15 years)
☛ Launch year of ISS? → 1998
☛ Voyager 1 launch year? → 1977

q: How many times does a GPS satellite circle the earth?
qs.e: GPS (Global Positioning System) satellites orbit the Earth in medium Earth orbit at an altitude of approximately 20,200 km. They complete one full orbit around the Earth in about 12 hours, meaning they circle the Earth twice a day. This orbital period ensures that at least four satellites are visible from any point on Earth at any given time, which is necessary for accurate positioning. The system was developed by the U.S. Department of Defense and currently consists of 31 active satellites.
qs.kf:
☛ Orbital period of GPS satellites → 12 hours
☛ Altitude of GPS satellites → Approximately 20,200 km
☛ Minimum visible satellites required → 4
☛ Developer of GPS system → U.S. Department of Defense
☛ Number of active GPS satellites → 31

q: The first sounding rocket, Nike -Apache was launched by India in ________.
qs.e: India launched its first sounding rocket, Nike-Apache, on November 21, 1963, from the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS). This marked the beginning of the Indian space program. The rocket was used to study the upper atmosphere. Under the leadership of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, this launch paved the way for the establishment of ISRO. The Nike-Apache was a two-stage rocket obtained from the United States. This launch was a crucial first step towards India's self-reliance in space research.
qs.kf:
☛ What was India's first sounding rocket? → Nike-Apache
☛ Launch site of Nike-Apache? → Thumba (TERLS), Kerala
☛ Year of launch of India's first sounding rocket? → 1963
☛ Who was the head of the Indian space program at that time? → Dr. Vikram Sarabhai
☛ From which country was the Nike-Apache rocket obtained? → United States

q: Which is the heaviest and most powerful communication satellite of India?
qs.e: GSAT-11 is India's heaviest (5854 kg) and most powerful communication satellite. It was launched on December 5, 2018, aboard an Ariane-5 rocket. The satellite generates over 7 kilowatts of power in orbit and provides high-speed data and broadband services across the country. GSAT-11 is part of ISRO's communication satellite series and carries 40 transponders (Ku and Ka bands). It covers India and surrounding regions. Its designed life is 15 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of GSAT-11 → 2018
☛ Weight of GSAT-11 → 5854 kg
☛ Power of GSAT-11 → 7 kilowatts
☛ Transponders in GSAT-11 → 40 (Ku and Ka band)
☛ Launch vehicle of GSAT-11 → Ariane-5

q: What is the range of the supersonic Akash missile?
qs.e: The Akash missile is a medium-range surface-to-air missile developed by India. Its strike range is approximately 25 km, and it can engage targets at altitudes up to 20 km. The missile is supersonic, traveling at speeds greater than Mach 2.5, and is guided by radar. It was developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and is produced by Bharat Dynamics Limited. The Akash missile can destroy various aerial targets, including fighter jets, drones, and missiles. It has been inducted into the Indian Air Force and the Indian Army.
qs.kf:
☛ Type of Akash missile → Medium-range surface-to-air missile
☛ Speed of Akash missile → Supersonic (greater than Mach 2.5)
☛ Developer of Akash missile → DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation)
☛ Manufacturer of Akash missile → Bharat Dynamics Limited
☛ Warhead of Akash missile → 55 kg high explosive

q: Who has produced the indigenous LCA fighter jets Tejas?
qs.e: The indigenous LCA Tejas fighter jets are produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). It is a lightweight, multirole combat aircraft designed and developed indigenously by India and inducted into the Indian Air Force. HAL is a state-owned aerospace and defense company headquartered in Bengaluru. The Tejas made its maiden flight in 2001 and entered service in 2016. The aircraft was developed under the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) of DRDO. HAL is also responsible for manufacturing other military aircraft like MiG-21, Sukhoi-30, and various helicopters. The Tejas Mk 1A is the fully operational variant currently being produced for the IAF.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first flight of Tejas? → 2001
☛ When was Tejas inducted into service? → 2016
☛ Who manufactures Tejas? → Hindustan Aeronautics Limited
☛ Which is the fully operational variant of Tejas? → Mk 1A
☛ Where is HAL headquartered? → Bengaluru

q: The new version of the Akash surface-to-air defence missile 'Akash 1S' is fitted with:
o: a new indigenously - developed command guidance programme
qs.e: The Akash 1S is an upgraded version of the Akash surface-to-air missile system, fitted with an indigenously developed seeker. This seeker enables the missile to independently track and engage targets, significantly enhancing its kill capability. Unlike the earlier Akash 1, which used a command guidance system, the Akash 1S employs an active radio frequency seeker, providing a fire-and-forget capability. This means the missile does not require additional guidance after launch. Developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), this upgrade strengthens the air defence capabilities of the Indian Air Force. The new seeker improves accuracy and reduces dependency on ground-based guidance systems.
qs.kf:
☛ What new indigenous component is fitted in Akash 1S missile? → indigenous seeker
☛ What type of guidance system does Akash 1S use? → active radio frequency seeker
☛ What capability does Akash 1S missile provide? → fire-and-forget
☛ Which organization developed the Akash 1S missile? → DRDO
☛ What is the purpose of Akash 1S missile? → strengthen air defence capability

q: India's first artificial satellite, ___________, was launched in space by Indian Space Research Organisation.
qs.e: India's first artificial satellite was Aryabhatta, launched on 19 April 1975 by ISRO using a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket. It was named after the ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer Aryabhatta. The satellite's objectives included studying astrophysics, solar physics, and atmospheric science. It was placed in a sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 360 km. This mission laid the foundation for India's space program. Later satellites like Bhaskara, ScatSat, and Resourcesat were developed.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is India's first satellite? → Aryabhatta
☛ When was Aryabhatta launched? → 19 April 1975
☛ Which rocket launched Aryabhatta? → Kosmos-3M (Soviet Union)
☛ What was the orbital altitude of Aryabhatta? → 360 km
☛ After whom was Aryabhatta named? → Ancient Indian mathematician Aryabhatta

q: _________ is a standard for wireless broadband communication for high speed data.
qs.e: LTE (Long Term Evolution) is a wireless broadband communication standard designed for high-speed data transmission. It was developed by 3GPP and forms the foundation of 4G networks. LTE provides download speeds up to 100 Mbps and upload speeds up to 50 Mbps. It uses technologies like OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access) and MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output). LTE is widely used in mobile phones, data cards, and IoT devices. Other options like Dolby Digital (audio), GPS One (navigation), and 8VSB (digital TV) are not related to wireless broadband.
qs.kf:
☛ LTE full form → Long Term Evolution
☛ Which organization developed LTE → 3GPP
☛ LTE downlink speed → Up to 100 Mbps
☛ LTE uplink speed → Up to 50 Mbps
☛ Technologies used in LTE → OFDMA and MIMO

q: What does Net neutrality mean?
A. Stop people from using the Internet.
B. Pricing of subsidized internet services.
C. Internet companies provide free data.
D. Differential pricing of Internet services.
qs.e: Net neutrality is the principle that internet service providers (ISPs) must treat all online content equally, without discrimination. This means they cannot block, throttle, or charge extra fees for specific websites or services. Option D is correct because net neutrality prohibits differential pricing, where ISPs charge different rates for different types of data or services. This principle ensures the internet remains an open and fair platform, fostering innovation and competition. Without net neutrality, large corporations could pay for faster access, putting smaller competitors at a disadvantage. The debate around net neutrality involves regulators, ISPs, and consumers, as it impacts free speech, innovation, and digital rights. Key regulations like India's TRAI have upheld net neutrality, banning discriminatory practices. Understanding this concept is crucial for grasping how internet governance affects everyday users and businesses.
qs.kf:
☛ Main goal of Net Neutrality → Equal treatment of all data by ISPs
☛ Who opposes Net Neutrality → ISPs and telecom companies
☛ Indian regulator supporting Net Neutrality → TRAI
☛ First country to enact Net Neutrality law → Chile (2010)
☛ Anti-Net Neutrality practice → Zero-rating plans (e.g., Facebook Free Basics)

q: Who is considered the world's first programmer?
A. Alan Turing
B. Ada Lovelace
C. Tim Berners - Lee
D. Steve Wozniak
qs.e: Ada Lovelace is considered the world's first programmer. In the 19th century, she wrote an algorithm for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, which is regarded as the first computer program. She was a mathematician and writer, and she understood the potential of computing. Alan Turing proposed the concept of the Turing machine, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web, and Steve Wozniak co-founded Apple Computer.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is considered the first programmer? → Ada Lovelace
☛ For which machine was the first computer program written? → Analytical Engine
☛ Who invented the Analytical Engine? → Charles Babbage
☛ Ada Lovelace is famous in which field? → Mathematics and Computer Science
☛ In which century did computer programming begin? → 19th century

q: The major objective of INSAT series of satellites is to facilitate.
A. TV relay to remote areas
B. Mobile network in remote areas
C. Internet services
D. Mapping locations through GPS
qs.e: The primary objective of the INSAT (Indian National Satellite System) series is to provide telecommunication, broadcasting, meteorology, and disaster management services. Its most significant application is enabling TV and radio broadcasting in remote and rural areas, allowing educational and informational programs to reach the masses. INSAT satellites carry C-band and Ku-band transponders that transmit TV signals. While mobile networks and internet services are also supported by INSAT, its main goal is TV relay. GPS mapping is done by dedicated navigation satellites like IRNSS/NavIC, not INSAT.
qs.kf:
☛ Primary use of INSAT series → Telecommunications and broadcasting
☛ First INSAT satellite → INSAT-1B (1983)
☛ Organization operating INSAT → ISRO
☛ Bands used in INSAT → C-band and Ku-band
☛ Not a function of INSAT → GPS mapping

q: Which company developed the Android OS, a mobile operating system Software in 2007?
qs.e: The Android OS was developed by Google Corp., a mobile operating system. It was initially created by Android Inc. in 2003, which was acquired by Google in 2005. The first Android device was launched in 2007. Android is based on the Linux kernel and is open-source. It is the most widely used mobile operating system globally, powering smartphones, tablets, and other devices.
qs.kf:
☛ Who developed the Android OS? → Google Corp.
☛ What kernel is Android based on? → Linux kernel
☛ When did Google acquire Android Inc.? → 2005
☛ When was the first Android device launched? → 2007
☛ What was the initial version of Android called? → Android 1.0 Apple Pie

q: Who is the co-founder of Apple Computers?
qs.e: The co-founder of Apple Computers is Steve Jobs. He founded Apple in 1976 along with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. Steve Jobs was a visionary entrepreneur who led the personal computer revolution. He played a key role in the development of products like the Macintosh, iPod, iPhone, and iPad. Jobs was born on February 24, 1955 in San Francisco and passed away on October 5, 2011. Apple is currently one of the most valuable companies in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Apple founded? → 1976
☛ Who are the three co-founders of Apple? → Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne
☛ When is Steve Jobs' birthday? → February 24, 1955
☛ When did Steve Jobs die? → October 5, 2011
☛ What was Apple's first computer? → Apple I

q: _______ in Hyderabad is responsible for remote sensing satellite data acquisition and processing, data dissemination, aerial remote sensing and decision support for disaster management.
o: Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research (IISER)
qs.e: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), located in Hyderabad, is a primary center under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). It is responsible for remote sensing satellite data acquisition, processing, dissemination, aerial remote sensing, and decision support for disaster management. NRSC operates the Data Processing and Archive System (DPAS) and provides data through geoportals like Bhuvan. For disaster management, it runs the Disaster Management Support (DMS) programme. Other options: NIC provides IT services, ISRO is the parent organization, and IISER is an educational institute.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is NRSC headquartered? → Hyderabad
☛ Under which organization does NRSC work? → ISRO
☛ Which geoportal is launched by NRSC? → Bhuvan
☛ What is the disaster management programme of NRSC? → Disaster Management Support (DMS)
☛ What is the full name of NRSC? → National Remote Sensing Centre

q: What is the name of the web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunications that will allow tracking of radiation emitted from mobile towers within their locality and check for their compliance with the Electro-Magnetic Field (EMF) emission norms defined by the government?
qs.e: The web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is called Tarang Sancharwith. This portal allows citizens to track the electromagnetic radiation emitted from mobile towers in their locality and check their compliance with the government-defined EMF emission norms. It is part of the DoT's efforts to ensure EMF compliance and transparency. Users can view the locations of mobile towers and their radiation levels on the portal, which helps address public concerns about tower radiation. The portal enhances trust and provides a simple way for people to verify safety standards.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched Tarang Sancharwith? → Department of Telecommunications (DoT)
☛ What is the main purpose of Tarang Sancharwith? → Tracking EMF radiation from mobile towers and checking compliance with norms
☛ Who benefits from Tarang Sancharwith? → Citizens
☛ What can be checked on Tarang Sancharwith? → Location and radiation levels of mobile towers
☛ Full form of EMF? → Electro-Magnetic Field

q: Which ministry launched the website e-Sahaj that allows organizations/firms/companies/individuals to apply for security clearance from anywhere over the internet?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
qs.e: The Ministry of Home Affairs launched the e-Sahaj website, which allows organizations, firms, companies, and individuals to apply for security clearance from anywhere over the internet. This portal is a completely digital process, eliminating the need for physical visits to offices. It enhances transparency and brings efficiency to the application process. e-Sahaj aims to simplify and speed up the security clearance process, thereby promoting ease of doing business.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched the e-Sahaj portal? → Ministry of Home Affairs
☛ What is the purpose of e-Sahaj? → Online application for security clearance
☛ What benefit does e-Sahaj provide? → Increased transparency and efficiency
☛ Who can apply on e-Sahaj? → Organizations, firms, companies, individuals
☛ From where can security clearance be obtained under e-Sahaj? → Anywhere over the internet

q: Which among the following unit is used to count the speed of modern printers?
qs.e: The speed of modern printers is measured in PPM (Pages Per Minute). This unit indicates how many pages a printer can print in one minute. PPM is primarily used for measuring the speed of modern printers such as laser printers and inkjet printers. LPM (Lines Per Minute) and CPM (Characters Per Minute) were used for older dot matrix printers, while BIT is a unit for measuring data. Therefore, PPM is the correct unit for counting the speed of modern printers.
qs.kf:
☛ Standard unit for measuring printer speed → PPM
☛ LPM measures speed of which printer → Dot matrix printer
☛ Full form of CPM → Characters Per Minute
☛ Fastest printer category → Laser printer
☛ Full form of PPM → Pages Per Minute

q: With reference to GPS, which of the following is correct?
o: Mountains and building blocks can act as obstacles to GPS signals.
Its full form is Global Placing System.
It has been developed by Russia
Its full form is Galileo Positioning System.
qs.e: GPS stands for Global Positioning System, developed by the United States. It uses satellites to provide precise location data on Earth. GPS signals are based on radio waves that travel in a straight line. Therefore, obstacles like mountains, tall buildings, and dense forests can block or weaken these signals, causing inaccuracies in positioning. This is why GPS may be less reliable in urban areas or mountainous regions. Other options are incorrect: 'Global Placing System' is a misnomer, Russia developed GLONASS, and Galileo is the European Union's system.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of GPS? → Global Positioning System
☛ Which country developed GPS? → USA
☛ Factors that can obstruct GPS signals? → Mountains, buildings, atmospheric conditions
☛ Russia's satellite navigation system? → GLONASS
☛ European Union's navigation system? → Galileo

q: Financial inclusion helps reduce income inequality in rural areas. Which platform provides a unified digital database for unorganised workers?
qs.e: E-Shram portal is a digital database launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in 2021 to create a unified national record of unorganised workers. Its aim is to link these workers with social security schemes. In rural areas, financial inclusion helps reduce income inequality, and E-Shram plays a key role by providing identity and benefits to informal workers. Jan Dhan Yojana facilitates bank accounts, BHIM app enables digital payments, and UPI dashboard tracks transactions, but only E-Shram portal provides an integrated digital database for unorganised workers. The platform registers workers and issues a 12-digit E-Shram card, enabling them to access various welfare schemes.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched the E-Shram portal? → Ministry of Labour and Employment
☛ When was E-Shram portal launched? → August 26, 2021
☛ What do registered workers on E-Shram get? → 12-digit E-Shram card
☛ What is the objective of E-Shram portal? → Unified database and social security for unorganised workers
☛ Who can register on E-Shram portal? → Unorganised workers aged 16-59 years

q: What is 'Google Beam' introduced under Project Starline?
o: A language translation tool for real-time communication
An AI-powered video communication platform aiming to redefine virtual interactions
A new satellite launched by Google for global internet coverage
A hardware device for enhancing internet speed in rural areas
qs.e: Google Beam is a component of Project Starline, an advanced video conferencing system that uses AI and 3D imaging technology to create a lifelike experience where participants feel like they are in the same room. It employs multiple cameras and sensors to generate a real-time 3D model of the user, enabling natural eye contact and depth perception. The platform is designed to make remote interactions more immersive and realistic, bridging the gap between physical and virtual presence. Unlike traditional video calls, Google Beam provides a volumetric display that enhances communication for business meetings and personal connections. It represents Google's effort to redefine virtual communication using cutting-edge technology.
qs.kf:
☛ Project Starline aims to → make virtual communication realistic
☛ Technology used in Google Beam → AI and 3D imaging
☛ Use of Google Beam → remote meetings and personal interactions
☛ Difference from traditional video calls → 3D image and eye contact
☛ Other Google communication tools → Google Meet, Duo

q: In 2025, the Central government selected which of the following start-ups to build India’s first indigenous artificial intelligence (AI) large language model (LLM)?
qs.e: In 2025, the Central government selected Sarvam startup to build India's first indigenous artificial intelligence (AI) large language model (LLM). This model will be developed considering Indian languages and contexts. Sarvam is a domestic AI startup focused on providing AI solutions in Indian languages. This initiative is a significant step towards increasing self-reliance in the AI sector under the Atmanirbhar Bharat and Digital India campaigns. The government provided financial assistance and technical guidance for this project. Sarvam was chosen due to its technical expertise and focus on Indian languages. This LLM will be used in various sectors such as education, health, and government services.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first indigenous AI LLM building startup → Sarvam
☛ Startup selected by Central government in 2025 → Sarvam
☛ Focus area of Sarvam → Indian languages AI solutions
☛ Initiative under which this project falls → Atmanirbhar Bharat and Digital India
☛ Potential sectors for LLM usage → Education, Health, Government services

q: The first Indian Communication satellite is
qs.e: India's first communication satellite was APPLE (Ariane Passenger Payload Experiment), launched on June 19, 1981, aboard the Ariane-1 rocket. It was an experimental communication satellite that demonstrated communication capabilities in India. Subsequently, India launched communication satellites using indigenous GSLV and PSLV rockets. Aryabhatta (1975) was India's first satellite, but it was a scientific satellite, not a communication one. Rohini were experimental satellites, and MOM (Mars Orbiter Mission) was a Mars mission. Hence, the first Indian communication satellite was APPLE.

☛ India's first communication satellite → APPLE (1981)
☛ Launch vehicle for APPLE → Ariane-1 (France)

☛ India's first Mars mission → MOM (2013)

q: Which among the following is NOT an open source software?
qs.e: Open source software is software whose source code is publicly available, allowing users to modify, share, and distribute it. Microsoft Office is proprietary software with a closed source code, requiring a paid license for use. In contrast, Linux is a popular open source operating system. Mozilla Firefox is an open source web browser developed by the Mozilla Foundation. Android is also open source, based on the Linux kernel and developed by Google. Therefore, among the given options, only Microsoft Office is not open source.

☛ Who developed Mozilla Firefox? → Mozilla Foundation
☛ Which kernel is Android based on? → Linux kernel
☛ Example of an open source license? → GNU General Public License (GPL)
☛ Open source alternative to Microsoft Office? → LibreOffice

q: Which of the following companies owns KUKA Robotics (Industrial Robots)?
qs.e: KUKA Robotics is a leading German industrial robot manufacturer. In 2017, it was acquired by the Chinese company Midea Group, a major consumer electronics and home appliances firm. This acquisition was part of China's 'Made in China 2025' initiative to boost robotics and automation. KUKA produces robots used in heavy industries, automotive, and electronics. q: Which computer application is mainly used for booking railway tickets and flight reservations?
qs.e: The Reservation System is the primary computer application used for booking railway tickets and flight reservations. It digitally handles the booking, cancellation, and management of seats and tickets for travelers. For Indian Railways, the IRCTC reservation system is a key example, while airlines use Global Distribution Systems (GDS) like Amadeus and Sabre. This system allows multiple users to book tickets simultaneously, check availability, and process payments efficiently. It is specifically designed for reservation purposes and is not related to education, communication, or banking. The reservation system streamlines the entire booking process, making it convenient for passengers to secure their travel arrangements online or at ticketing counters.
qs.kf:
☛ System used for railway ticket booking → IRCTC
☛ Common system for flight booking → Global Distribution System (GDS)
☛ Examples of GDS → Amadeus, Sabre, Galileo
☛ Main function of reservation system → Managing seat availability and bookings
☛ Purpose of this application → To provide easy reservation facilities to travelers

q: Which of these devices controls the heart rate of patients?
qs.e: A pacemaker is a medical device that helps control the heart rate. It sends electrical signals to the heart muscles to make them beat at a normal rate. It is used in patients with abnormally slow heartbeats (bradycardia) or irregular rhythms. The pacemaker is implanted in the body and powered by a battery. Other options: CAT scanner creates internal images of the body, Respirator assists breathing, and ECG machine records the heart's electrical activity but does not control it.
qs.kf:
☛ Device that controls heart rate → Pacemaker
☛ Primary function of pacemaker → Regulate heartbeat via electrical signals
☛ Condition where pacemaker is used → Bradycardia (slow heart rate)
☛ Function of ECG machine → Records heart's electrical activity
☛ Use of respirator → Assists breathing

q: What is the full name of SONAR?
A. Sound Neutralization and Ranging
B. Sound Navigating and Reaching
C. Sound Navigation and Ranging
D. Sound Neuralization and Reaching
qs.e: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation and Ranging, a technology that uses sound waves to detect, locate, and measure the distance of objects underwater. It is widely used in marine research, submarines, fishing, and naval operations. SONAR is of two types: Active SONAR (which emits sound pulses and listens for echoes) and Passive SONAR (which only listens to sounds made by other objects). This technology is also crucial for waterway navigation and studying marine life. It works on the principle of echo or sound reflection.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of SONAR → Sound Navigation and Ranging
☛ Use of SONAR → Detecting underwater objects
☛ Active SONAR → Emits own sound and measures echo
☛ Passive SONAR → Only listens to sounds from others
☛ Principle of SONAR → Echo (sound reflection)

q: In 1998, nuclear explosive devices were tested at ______ in India.
qs.e: In 1998, India conducted five nuclear explosive tests at Pokharan in Rajasthan under Operation Shakti. The tests were carried out on May 11 and 13, 1998. Pokharan is the primary nuclear test site of India, controlled by the Indian Army. The first nuclear test at Pokharan was conducted in 1974, code-named Smiling Buddha. After these tests, India declared itself a nuclear weapons state. Pokharan is located in the Thar Desert and is heavily guarded.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Pokharan nuclear test site located? → Rajasthan
☛ When was Operation Shakti conducted? → 1998
☛ Code name of 1974 nuclear test? → Smiling Buddha
☛ India's only nuclear test site? → Pokharan
☛ Pokharan is located in which desert? → Thar Desert

q: A lie detector apparatus is also known as a:
qs.e: A lie detector apparatus is known as a polygraph. It is a device that measures physiological responses such as heart rate, blood pressure, respiration rate, and skin conductivity. These measurements record changes in a person's bodily reactions when questions are asked during the test. Polygraphs are often used in law enforcement and security screening, although their reliability is debated. It is also commonly referred to as a 'lie detector machine'.
qs.kf:
☛ Who invented the polygraph? → John Augustus Larson
☛ On what principle does a polygraph work? → Measurement of physiological responses
☛ How many parameters are measured in a polygraph? → Four main (heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, skin conductivity)
☛ What is the synonym of polygraph? → Lie detector machine
☛ What does a seismograph measure? → Intensity of earthquakes

q: The telephone was invented in:
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (D) 1876

q: Which device is used to measure the relative density of the fluid?
qs.e: A hydrometer is used to measure the relative density (specific gravity) of a liquid. It works on Archimedes' principle, which states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced. The hydrometer is a graduated glass tube with a weighted bulb at the bottom. When placed in a liquid, it floats and sinks to a depth depending on the liquid's density. Lower density causes it to sink deeper; higher density makes it float higher. Hydrometers are commonly used to measure the density of battery acid, milk, and alcohol. Other options: Hydrometeor refers to atmospheric phenomena, Venturimeter measures flow rate, and Anonymous is unrelated.
qs.kf:
☛ Which principle does a hydrometer work on? → Archimedes' principle
☛ Which device measures relative density of liquids? → Hydrometer
☛ Where is a hydrometer commonly used? → Battery acid, milk, alcohol density measurement
☛ What is the structure of a hydrometer? → Graduated glass tube with weighted bulb
☛ On what does the sinking depth of a hydrometer depend? → Density of the liquid

q: Which of these scientists is NOT linked with the invention of television?
qs.e: The invention of television is linked to scientists such as John Logie Baird, Vladimir Zworykin, and Philo Farnsworth. Baird demonstrated the first mechanical television system in 1925. Zworykin invented the iconoscope camera tube in 1923, which became the basis for electronic television. Farnsworth demonstrated the first fully electronic television system in 1927. Christiaan Huygens (1629–1695) was a Dutch mathematician, astronomer, and physicist. He made significant contributions such as the pendulum clock, Saturn's rings, and the wave theory of light, but he had no involvement in the invention of television. Therefore, Huygens is the scientist not linked with television.
qs.kf:
☛ First mechanical television system inventor → John Logie Baird
☛ Iconoscope camera tube inventor → Vladimir Zworykin
☛ Father of fully electronic television → Philo Farnsworth
☛ Christiaan Huygens' major contribution → Pendulum clock and wave theory of light
☛ Discoverer of Saturn's rings → Christiaan Huygens

q: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organisation under which of the following ministries of the Government of India?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
qs.e: The Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Established in 1991, its primary objective is to promote software exports and IT services from India. STPI has played a pivotal role in providing infrastructure, incubation facilities, and export-oriented services to the IT/ITES industry across the country. Its centers have helped empower startups and MSMEs by offering high-speed data communication, ready-to-use office space, and other support. The organization contributes to the development of the electronics hardware and software sectors. It works in synergy with other government initiatives to boost India's digital economy and innovation ecosystem.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of STPI located?→ New Delhi
☛ When was STPI established?→ 1991
☛ Under which ministry does STPI operate?→ MeitY
☛ What is the full form of STPI?→ Software Technology Parks of India
☛ What is the main objective of STPI?→ To promote software exports and IT services

q: In Information Technology, what does DASD stand for?
o: Device for Access and Storage of Domain
qs.e: DASD stands for Direct Access Storage Device. It is a type of secondary storage device that allows data to be accessed directly without sequential scanning. Examples include Hard Disk Drives (HDD) and Solid State Drives (SSD). The term originated from IBM mainframe computers. It is called 'direct access' because any data block can be read or written directly. This contrasts with sequential access devices like tape drives. DASD is typically used for online storage requiring fast random access.
qs.kf:
☛ What does DASD stand for? → Direct Access Storage Device
☛ Example of a DASD? → Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
☛ What type of access does DASD provide? → Direct (Random) Access
☛ Which storage device is opposite to DASD? → Sequential Access Device (e.g., Magnetic Tape)
☛ DASD is primarily used in which type of computers? → Mainframe Computers

q: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research was set up under the vision of:
qs.e: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) was established in 1945 in Mumbai under the vision of Dr. Homi J Bhabha. His goal was to promote research in nuclear energy and fundamental sciences in India. The institute was set up with support from the Tata Group and later came under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). Dr. Bhabha is known as the 'father of the Indian nuclear program'. TIFR has played a key role in India's nuclear technology and space science advancements.
qs.kf:
☛ When was TIFR established? → 1945
☛ Where is TIFR located? → Mumbai
☛ Dr. Homi Bhabha is known as? → Father of Indian Nuclear Program
☛ TIFR comes under which department? → Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)
☛ Which institutes did Dr. Homi Bhabha help establish? → TIFR and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)

q: Who formulated India's three-stage nuclear power program?
qs.e: India's three-stage nuclear power program was formulated by Homi Jehangir Bhabha in the 1950s. The program aims to maximize energy production using thorium while considering the limited availability of uranium in the country. The first stage uses Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) fueled by natural uranium. The second stage involves Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs) that use plutonium and uranium-233. The third stage will use thorium-based reactors to produce uranium-233. Bhabha is regarded as the father of the Indian nuclear program.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of India's three-stage nuclear program? → Homi Jehangir Bhabha
☛ Which reactors are used in the first stage? → PHWR (Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors)
☛ What are the reactors in the second stage? → Fast Breeder Reactors (FBR)
☛ Which fuel is used in the third stage? → Thorium
☛ Where was India's first nuclear power plant located? → Tarapur

q: The Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia-Pacific (CSSTEAP) is at:
qs.e: The Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia-Pacific (CSSTEAP) was established in collaboration with the United Nations and the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Its headquarters is located in Dehradun. This centre provides high-level education in space science and technology to countries in the Asia-Pacific region. The objective of CSSTEAP is to promote regional cooperation in the development of space technology. The centre primarily offers training in subjects such as remote sensing, satellite communication, and space science.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of CSSTEAP → Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia-Pacific
☛ Headquarters of CSSTEAP → Dehradun, Uttarakhand
☛ CSSTEAP established by → Collaboration of UN and ISRO
☛ Objective of CSSTEAP → Regional cooperation and education in space science
☛ Main areas of CSSTEAP → Remote sensing, satellite communication, space science

q: The first large scale electrical air conditioning was invented and used in1902 by
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (A) Willis Carrier

q: _______ is an electrically powered and Remotely Operated Vehicle by DRDO.
qs.e: DAKSH is an electrically powered, remotely operated robot developed by DRDO. It is primarily used for bomb disposal and handling of hazardous materials. The robot is equipped with a CCTV camera, gripper, and X-ray system. DAKSH is deployed at railway stations, airports, and other security-sensitive locations. It runs on battery power and is controlled via remote control.
qs.kf:
☛ Who developed DAKSH? → DRDO
☛ What is DAKSH used for? → Bomb disposal and hazardous material handling
☛ What type of robot is DAKSH? → Electrically powered and remotely operated
☛ What equipment does DAKSH have? → CCTV camera, gripper, and X-ray system
☛ Where is DAKSH deployed? → Railway stations, airports, and security-sensitive locations

q: Who among the following inaugurated an advanced electronic surveillance system along the 61-km India-Bangladesh border in Dhubri district of Assam in 2019?
qs.e: In 2019, the then Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated an advanced electronic surveillance system along the 61-km India-Bangladesh border in Dhubri district of Assam. This system is known as the Border Electronic Monitoring System (BEMS). It enables the Border Security Force (BSF) to carry out real-time surveillance. The advanced technology helps in preventing activities like human trafficking, infiltration, and illegal trade. The project was executed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL).
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of India-Bangladesh border → 4,096 km
☛ Longest international border of India → with Bangladesh
☛ Force deployed on China border → ITBP
☛ Year of BSF establishment → 1965
☛ Name of surveillance system on India-Pakistan border → Border Electronic Surveillance System

q: Verification of log-in name and password is for
A. Authenticating the user
B. Re-confirming the user
C. Providing formal access to the user
D. Completing the formality of login-in
qs.e: Verification of login name and password is performed to confirm the identity of a user in a system. This process is known as Authentication. It ensures that the user is who they claim to be. Only after authentication is the user granted access to resources. It is a fundamental principle of cybersecurity. Other options like re-confirming or providing formal access are subsequent steps after authentication.
qs.kf:
☛ Main purpose of authentication → Verify identity
☛ Authorization means → Granting access to resources
☛ Multi-factor authentication includes → Password, OTP, biometrics
☛ Used in session management → Tokens and cookies
☛ Three factors of authentication → Knowledge, possession, inherence

q: An example of Full Duplex communication channel.
A. Radio Broadcasting
B. Television Broadcasting
C. Walkie-Talkie
D. Telephone conversation
qs.e: A full-duplex communication system allows both parties to transmit simultaneously. A telephone conversation is an example where both persons can speak and listen at the same time. Radio and TV broadcasting are simplex (one-way). Walkie-talkie is half-duplex, where only one transmits at a time. Full-duplex requires two separate channels or efficient bandwidth management.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of full-duplex → Telephone conversation
☛ Example of half-duplex → Walkie-talkie
☛ Example of simplex → Radio broadcasting
☛ Full-duplex requires → Two frequency bands or channels
☛ Half-duplex data flow → One direction at a time

q: Which of the following statements is true with respect to ASCII?
A. A programming language
B. ASCII chart is not for decimals
C. American Security Code for Information Interchange
D. A character encoding scheme
qs.e: ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) is a character encoding standard used to represent text in computers as numeric codes. It defines codes for English letters, digits, and special characters using values from 0 to 127. ASCII is not a programming language; it is a data representation standard. Option A is incorrect because ASCII is not a programming language. Option B is incorrect because the ASCII chart does include decimal values. Option C is incorrect because the full form is American Standard Code for Information Interchange, not Security. Thus, option D is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of ASCII? → American Standard Code for Information Interchange
☛ How many bits does ASCII use? → 7 bits
☛ How many characters are in ASCII? → 128
☛ What is the ASCII range? → 0 to 127
☛ Is ASCII only for English? → Yes, it encodes the English alphabet

q: An E-Way Bill is related with which of the following?
o: Supply of goods from one place to another
Making toll payments on national highways
qs.e: An E-Way Bill is an electronic document for goods transport in India implemented under the GST system. It is not related to the supply of goods from one place to another, but rather tracks the payment process after goods are received, known as post-payment. Its main purpose is to prevent tax evasion.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which tax system is the E-Way Bill implemented? → GST
☛ What is the main purpose of the E-Way Bill? → To prevent tax evasion
☛ What type of payment does the E-Way Bill ensure? → Post-payment
☛ Which system does the E-Way Bill belong to? → GST e-way bill system
☛ What information is recorded in an E-Way Bill? → Goods details, transporter info

q: Who was the first Indian poet who was invited to record his poems at the Library of Congress in Washington DC?
qs.e: Abhay K is a renowned Indian poet and diplomat. He became the first Indian poet invited to record his poems at the Library of Congress in Washington DC. This invitation was part of the Library of Congress's Archive of World Poetry, which preserves the voices of poets worldwide. Abhay K's poetry often revolves around nature, travel, and culture. This achievement gave Indian poetry new recognition on an international platform. It highlights India's growing role in cultural diplomacy and literary exchange. His work has been widely appreciated for its lyrical quality and diverse themes.
qs.kf:
☛ First Indian poet to record at Library of Congress → Abhay K
☛ Full name of Abhay K → Abhay Kumar Singh
☛ Birthplace of Abhay K → Bihar, India
☛ Collection at Library of Congress is called → Archive of World Poetry
☛ A famous poem by Abhay K → "The Magic of Mangroves"

q: Which of the following two organisations teamed up to develop India’s first indigenous CAR-T cell therapy?
o: IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre
qs.e: India's first indigenous CAR-T cell therapy was developed jointly by IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre. This therapy is named NexCAR19. It is a major breakthrough in cancer treatment. CAR-T therapy involves genetically modifying a patient's own T-cells to recognize and destroy cancer cells. This technology is particularly effective in treating blood cancers such as B-cell lymphoma and leukemia. This development makes India self-reliant in the field of CAR-T therapy and will reduce treatment costs.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of India's first indigenous CAR-T cell therapy → NexCAR19
☛ Full form of CAR-T therapy → Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell therapy
☛ Organizations that developed NexCAR19 → IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre
☛ Which cell is used in CAR-T therapy → T-cell
☛ CAR-T therapy is mainly used to treat which disease → Blood cancers (B-cell lymphoma/leukemia)

q: The physical place where a computer stores information is called __________.
qs.e: The physical place where a computer stores information permanently is called a hard disk. It is a non-volatile storage device that retains data even when power is off. Hard disks contain magnetic platters where data is written and read. A modem is a networking device, Wi-Fi is a wireless technology, and POP is an email protocol; these are not storage devices.
qs.kf:
☛ Permanent storage device in a computer → Hard disk
☛ How is data stored on a hard disk? → Magnetically
☛ Hard disk capacity is measured in → Gigabytes or Terabytes
☛ Types of hard disk → Internal (HDD/SSD) and External
☛ Example of non-volatile memory → Hard disk

q: A/An ______ is a special high-speed storage mechanism.
qs.e: A cache is a high-speed storage mechanism that sits between the processor and main memory, used to speed up data access. It temporarily stores frequently used data and instructions, reducing the time the processor takes to retrieve data. Cache memory is typically made of SRAM (Static Random Access Memory), which is faster than DRAM. There are three main levels of cache: L1, L2, and L3. L1 cache is the fastest and smallest, while L3 cache is slower but larger. Cache memory plays a crucial role in improving processor performance by minimizing the latency of memory access.
qs.kf:
☛ Which type of memory is the fastest? → Cache memory
☛ What type of memory is cache memory? → SRAM
☛ Where is L2 cache located? → Inside the processor or on the motherboard
☛ What is the function of cache? → To speed up data access
☛ Which is the smallest cache level? → L1 cache

q: What is full form of SMPS?
qs.e: The full form of SMPS is Switch Mode Power Supply. It is an electronic device that efficiently converts electrical power using switching transistors to regulate voltage. SMPS operates by rapidly switching the input power on and off, reducing energy loss compared to linear power supplies. This results in higher efficiency (typically 80-90%) and a smaller form factor. SMPS is widely used in devices like computers, mobile chargers, TVs, and other electronics due to its compact size and heat efficiency. It plays a crucial role in modern electronics by providing stable and efficient power conversion.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of SMPS → Switch Mode Power Supply
☛ Switching device used in SMPS → Transistor or MOSFET
☛ Efficiency of SMPS → 80-90%
☛ Applications of SMPS → Computers, chargers, TVs
☛ Less efficient than SMPS → Linear power supply

q: RAM is a _____
qs.e: RAM (Random Access Memory) is a temporary memory device, also known as volatile memory. This means that when the computer is turned off, the data stored in it is lost. RAM is used to store data and instructions that the processor needs to access quickly. It acts as a buffer between the CPU and storage devices, improving system speed. There are two main types of RAM: DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM). DRAM is used as main memory, while SRAM is used for cache memory.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of RAM → Random Access Memory
☛ Which memory is temporary? → RAM
☛ Which memory loses data when computer is turned off? → RAM
☛ Types of RAM → DRAM and SRAM
☛ Which RAM is used in cache memory? → SRAM

q: What is the device that converts digital signals into analog signals?
A. WiFi
B. Modem
C. Port
D. USB
qs.e: A modem (modulator-demodulator) is a device that converts digital signals into analog signals and vice versa. It is used to connect computers to the internet via telephone lines or cables. Modulation is the process of converting digital to analog, while demodulation converts analog to digital. WiFi is a wireless networking technology, a port is a connector, and USB is an interface. None of these perform digital-to-analog conversion.
qs.kf:
☛ Process of converting digital to analog signal → Modulation
☛ Process of converting analog to digital signal → Demodulation
☛ Full form of modem → Modulator-Demodulator
☛ Full form of WiFi → Wireless Fidelity
☛ Full form of USB → Universal Serial Bus

q: What is the full form of ISI? A. Inter-Services Intelligence
B. International Services Intelligence C. International Space Intelligence D. International Scientific Infrastructure
qs.e: The full form of ISI is Inter-Services Intelligence. It is the premier intelligence agency of Pakistan, established in 1948 with its headquarters in Islamabad. Its primary functions include gathering military and political intelligence, detecting national security threats, and coordinating cross-border military operations. The agency operates under the command of the Pakistan Army and plays a key role in counter-terrorism, espionage, and counter-intelligence activities. The other options—'International Services Intelligence', 'International Space Intelligence', and 'International Scientific Infrastructure'—are not related to ISI.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of ISI? → Inter-Services Intelligence
☛ Which country's intelligence agency is ISI? → Pakistan
☛ When was ISI established? → 1948
☛ Where is the headquarters of ISI? → Islamabad
☛ Under which command does ISI operate? → Pakistan Army

q: Which one is considered as India's first supercomputer?
A. Aditya
B. Vikram - 100
C. Param 8000
D. Shastra T
qs.e: India's first supercomputer is Param 8000, developed in 1991 by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing). It was built under the initiative of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Param 8000 was created using indigenous technology, making India self-reliant in supercomputing. Its processing speed was about 1 GFlops (Giga Floating Point Operations Per Second). After Param 8000, the Param series included Param 10000, Param Padma, and others. Among the options, Aditya is a weather forecasting supercomputer, Vikram-100 is a space applications supercomputer, and Shastra T is another supercomputer, but Param 8000 was the first.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first supercomputer name → Param 8000
☛ Organization that developed Param 8000 → C-DAC
☛ Launch year of Param 8000 → 1991
☛ Processing speed of Param 8000 → 1 GFlops
☛ Current fastest supercomputer in India → Aryabhatta (AI Supercomputer)

q: Who invented the mouse of a computer? A. John Backus
B. Charlas Babbage C. Douglas Engelbart D. Simon Colton
qs.e: The computer mouse was invented by Douglas Engelbart. He developed the prototype at the Stanford Research Institute in the 1960s. It was a wooden block with two wheels and a button. Engelbart called it the "X-Y Position Indicator." Later, in the 1970s, Xerox PARC popularized the mouse. The mouse is an input device that controls the cursor on the screen.
qs.kf:
☛ Inventor of computer mouse → Douglas Engelbart
☛ Initial name of mouse → X-Y Position Indicator
☛ Company that popularized mouse → Xerox PARC
☛ Type of input device → Pointing device
☛ Other invention by Engelbart → Hypertext and Graphical User Interface

q: Which among the following is the brain of the computer?
A. Software B. Hardware C. CPU D. Monitor
qs.e: The brain of the computer is the CPU (Central Processing Unit). It controls all operations and performs calculations. The CPU is also called a microprocessor. It consists of two main parts: the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and the Control Unit. The ALU handles arithmetic and logical operations, while the Control Unit decodes and executes instructions. Software is a set of programs, hardware refers to physical components, and the monitor is an output device. Hence, the CPU is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of CPU → Central Processing Unit
☛ CPU is known as → Brain of the computer
☛ Main parts of CPU → ALU and Control Unit
☛ Function of ALU → Arithmetic and logical operations
☛ Function of Control Unit → Decode and control instructions

q: The computer system which does not require any storage device?
A. Analog
B. Digital
C. Hybrid
D. Third generation computer
qs.e: Analog computers do not require any storage device because they work by measuring continuous physical quantities like voltage, pressure, or temperature. They process data directly through physical measurements and do not need to store data digitally. Digital computers store data in binary form and require storage devices. Hybrid computers combine both analog and digital components. Third generation computers use integrated circuits and require storage devices. Analog computers are mainly used in scientific and engineering applications where real-time measurement is needed.
qs.kf:
☛ Analog computers are based on? → Measurement of physical quantities
☛ Digital computers use which type of data? → Binary data
☛ Hybrid computers contain? → Both analog and digital features
☛ Main feature of third generation computers? → Integrated Circuits (ICs)
☛ Example of an analog computer? → Speedometer

q: On the basis of Memory size & performance, which type of computer is known as "Big iron"?
A. Micro Computer
B. Mini Computer
C. Main Frame
D. Super Computer
qs.e: Mainframe computers are called 'Big Iron' due to their large memory size and high performance. These powerful computers are used by large organizations for massive data processing, transactions, and critical applications. They can serve thousands of users simultaneously and provide high reliability and availability. Mainframes are characterized by their robust I/O capability, security, and scalability. Supercomputers are built for scientific computations, whereas mainframes excel in business data processing. Key manufacturers include IBM and Unisys. Mainframes remain vital in banking, insurance, and government sectors.
qs.kf:
☛ What is 'Big Iron'? → Mainframe computer
☛ Mainframe primary use? → Banking, insurance, government
☛ Difference between supercomputer and mainframe? → Supercomputer for calculations, mainframe for data processing
☛ Mainframe manufacturers? → IBM, Unisys
☛ Mainframe feature? → High reliability, large I/O capacity

q: Full form of BIOS is
A. Binary Interchange Operation System
B. Basic Input Output System
C. Beginner’s Input Operation Symbol
D. Basic Interface Oriented service
qs.e: BIOS stands for Basic Input Output System. It is a firmware chip stored in the ROM on the computer's motherboard. When the computer starts, the BIOS first performs the Power-On Self-Test (POST), which checks the hardware's functionality. After that, it locates the boot device (like hard disk or SSD) to load the operating system. BIOS provides a low-level interface between the hardware and the OS. Modern computers have replaced it with UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface), which offers more advanced features.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is BIOS stored? → ROM (on motherboard)
☛ What is the initial test performed by BIOS called? → POST (Power-On Self-Test)
☛ What is the main function of BIOS? → To boot the operating system
☛ What is the full form of UEFI? → Unified Extensible Firmware Interface
☛ Which system activates first when a computer is turned on? → BIOS

q: Which of the following does computing in a personal computer?
A. CPU
B. Motherboard
C. RAM
D. BIOS
qs.e: In a personal computer, all computations are performed by the CPU (Central Processing Unit), which is often referred to as the brain of the computer. It is responsible for arithmetic and logical operations, data processing, and executing instructions. The Motherboard is the main circuit board that connects all components but does not perform computations itself. RAM stores temporary data for quick access by the CPU, while BIOS is the basic input/output system that helps boot the computer. Thus, only the CPU carries out actual computing tasks.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of CPU → Central Processing Unit
☛ Main components of CPU → ALU, Control Unit, and Registers
☛ Which part is called the brain of computer → CPU
☛ Functions performed by CPU → Data processing, calculations, and instruction execution
☛ Unit to measure CPU speed → Hertz (GHz)

q: Which one of the following does not belong to the group?
A. Monitor B. Keyboard C. Webcam D. Mouse
qs.e: A Monitor is an output device that displays processed information from the computer. Keyboard, Webcam, and Mouse are all input devices used to provide data or commands to the computer. The Keyboard is used for typing, the Mouse for pointing, and the Webcam for capturing video. Since the Monitor outputs data while the other three input data, it does not belong to the same group. Hence, Monitor is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of device is a Keyboard? → Input device
☛ What type of device is a Mouse? → Input device
☛ What type of device is a Webcam? → Input device
☛ What type of device is a Monitor? → Output device
☛ What type of device is a Printer? → Output device

q: In computer terminology, what is a nibble?
qs.e: In computer terminology, the smallest unit of data is a bit. A group of 4 bits is called a nibble. Since one byte consists of 8 bits, a nibble represents half a byte. Nibbles are commonly used in hexadecimal numbering systems because 4 bits can represent values from 0 to 15, which correspond to a single hexadecimal digit. The other options, such as terabyte, gigabyte, and kilobyte, are much larger units and are not related to the concept of a nibble.
qs.kf:
☛ How many bits are in a nibble? → 4 bits
☛ How many nibbles are in a byte? → 2 nibbles
☛ In which number system is a nibble used? → Hexadecimal
☛ Full form of bit? → Binary digit
☛ How many bytes are in a kilobyte? → 1024 bytes

q: A/An ________ is an interface between the user and hardware.
qs.e: An operating system (OS) is essential software that acts as an interface between the user and the computer hardware. It manages hardware resources like CPU, memory, and storage, and allows users to run application programs. Without an OS, a computer cannot function because it controls every task, from executing commands to managing files. The OS also handles input/output operations, making it possible for peripherals like keyboard, mouse, and printer to work. Examples include Windows, Linux, and macOS. The other options—screen, memory, and command—are either hardware components or inputs, not interfaces. The screen is an output device, memory stores data, and a command is an instruction. Therefore, the correct answer is operating system.
qs.kf:
☛ What is an operating system? → Interface between user and hardware
☛ Which OS is open-source? → Linux
☛ First GUI OS? → Macintosh
☛ Windows OS developed by? → Microsoft
☛ Main function of OS? → Manage hardware and software resources

q: Which of the following is a volatile memory?
qs.e: Volatile memory is a type of computer memory that loses its data when the power is turned off. RAM (Random Access Memory) is a volatile memory because it retains data only while the computer is powered on. In contrast, ROM (Read-Only Memory), PROM (Programmable ROM), and EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM) are non-volatile memories, which retain data even after power is off. RAM is used for temporary storage of data and programs currently in use by the processor. It is crucial for fast performance and high-speed data access. However, due to its volatility, data must be saved to non-volatile storage like hard drives before shutting down.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of volatile memory → RAM (DRAM and SRAM)
☛ Example of non-volatile memory → ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM
☛ Types of RAM → DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM)
☛ Types of ROM → PROM, EPROM, EEPROM
☛ Characteristic of volatile memory → Data lost when power is off

q: Non-volatile memory is a type of computer memory that can retain stored information even when the computer is:
qs.e: Non-volatile memory is a type of computer memory that retains stored data even when the power supply is turned off. Examples include ROM, flash memory, and hard drives. In contrast, volatile memory like RAM requires continuous power to maintain data. Non-volatile memory is used in firmware, boot programs, and USB drives. This technology ensures data persistence, allowing information to remain available after a system restart. It is essential for BIOS and SSD storage.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of non-volatile memory → ROM, Flash memory, SSD
☛ Which is volatile memory → RAM (DRAM, SRAM)
☛ Memory that retains data without power → Non-volatile memory
☛ Firmware is stored in → ROM
☛ Fastest non-volatile memory → NVMe SSD

q: How many different values can be stored by a 32 bit register?
qs.e: A 32-bit register consists of 32 binary digits (bits), each capable of storing either 0 or 1. Therefore, the total number of distinct combinations is 232, which equals 4,294,967,296 different values. Registers are fast storage components of the CPU used for temporary data. An n-bit register can store 2n distinct values. This fundamental concept is crucial for understanding computer architecture and data representation.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum value stored in an 8-bit register → 255 (28 - 1)
☛ Total values stored by a 16-bit register → 65,536 (216)
☛ Number of bits in an n-bit register → n
☛ Relation of 32-bit register to UNICODE → UNICODE uses 32-bit encoding
☛ Addressable memory of a 32-bit processor → 4 GB (232 bytes)

q: Who is considered to be the Father of Modern Computers?
qs.e: Alan Turing is widely regarded as the Father of Modern Computers. He proposed the concept of the Turing Machine, which laid the theoretical foundation for modern computers. During World War II, he played a crucial role in breaking the Enigma code. Turing also contributed to the field of artificial intelligence and proposed the Turing Test. His work laid the groundwork for modern computer science, while Charles Babbage is known as the 'Father of Computers', Turing is recognized as the father of modern computing.
qs.kf:
☛ Who proposed the Turing Machine? → Alan Turing
☛ Who is considered the father of Artificial Intelligence? → Alan Turing
☛ What is the Turing Test related to? → Machine intelligence
☛ Who cracked the Enigma code? → Alan Turing
☛ Who is the father of modern computer science? → Alan Turing

q: Which of the following is NOT an output device?
qs.e: Output devices are hardware components that receive data from a computer and present it in a human-readable form. Printer produces hard copies of digital documents, Speaker outputs audio, and Monitor displays visual information. These are all output devices. A Scanner is an input device that converts physical documents or images into digital form and sends them to the computer. It inputs data into the computer, not outputs. Therefore, Scanner is not an output device.
qs.kf:
☛ What is an output device? → A device that receives data from a computer and presents it to the user.
☛ What is the function of a printer? → To print digital data on paper.
☛ What type of device is a scanner? → Input device.
☛ What is a monitor used for? → To display visual output.
☛ What does a speaker output? → Audio output.

q: A computer monitor is also known by the name:
qs.e: A computer monitor is also known as a VDU, which stands for Visual Display Unit. It is an output device that displays processed data from the computer in visual form. CPU is a processing unit, LED is a display technology, and CCTV is a security camera system. The term VDU is primarily used for monitors, especially in the context of older CRT monitors. In modern times, LCD, LED, and OLED monitors are common, but the term VDU is still in use. The monitor is an essential part of a computer that allows users to view the graphical interface, text, and images.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of VDU → Visual Display Unit
☛ Monitor is which type of device → Output device
☛ Full form of CPU → Central Processing Unit
☛ Full form of LED → Light Emitting Diode
☛ Full form of CCTV → Closed Circuit Television

q: Which among the following is the largest unit of memory of a computer system?
qs.e: Computer memory units start from byte and increase in size. Among them, Yottabyte (YB) is the largest unit. It equals 1,024 zettabytes or 10^24 bytes. Zettabyte (ZB) is smaller, exabyte (EB) is even smaller, and petabyte (PB) is the smallest among the given options. Yottabyte is used to measure global data storage.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest unit of data measurement → Yottabyte
☛ Number of bytes in 1 yottabyte → 10^24 bytes
☛ Unit after yottabyte → Brontobyte (unofficial)
☛ Smallest data unit → Bit
☛ Number of terabytes in 1 petabyte → 1,024 terabytes

q: Which of the following acts as an interface between the CPU and the main memory?
qs.e: Cache memory is a small, fast memory located between the CPU and the main memory (RAM). It stores frequently accessed data and instructions, reducing access time and improving processing speed. It acts as a buffer to bridge the speed gap between the CPU and main memory. Magnetic tape, hard disk, and compact disk are secondary storage devices and do not directly interface with the CPU. Cache memory is organized into levels L1, L2, and L3, with L1 being the fastest and smallest. It uses SRAM technology, which is faster but more expensive than DRAM used in main memory.
qs.kf:
☛ Fastest memory between CPU and RAM → Cache memory
☛ Cache level built inside the CPU chip → L1 cache
☛ Primary purpose of cache memory → Increase data access speed
☛ Not an example of secondary storage → Cache memory
☛ Technology used by cache memory → SRAM (Static RAM)

q: Which option is correct regarding the abbreviation, full form and its primary function?
o: LAN - Local Area Network connects computers within a limited area.
CD - Central Disk Operating System permanently stores
ASCII - American Standard Communication for Input and Interface used for graphic design -
ASCII - Advanced System for Communication Interface - used in LAN setup
qs.e: LAN stands for Local Area Network and its primary function is to connect computers and devices within a limited geographical area, such as an office, building, or campus, enabling them to share resources and data. The other options are incorrect: CD stands for Compact Disc, not Central Disk Operating System; ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange, used for text encoding, not for graphic design or LAN setup.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of LAN → Local Area Network
☛ Area covered by LAN → Limited geographical area
☛ Primary function of LAN → Connects computers and shares resources
☛ Full form of CD → Compact Disc
☛ Full form of ASCII → American Standard Code for Information Interchange

q: Which of the following devices performs optical character recognition (OCR)?
qs.e: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a technology that converts printed or handwritten text into digital form. The device specifically designed for this task is an OCR Scanner. It scans the text and converts it into editable electronic data. Other options: OMR Scanner detects marks (e.g., answer sheets), Flatbed Scanner scans general images, and Barcode Reader only reads barcodes. Thus, only an OCR scanner performs OCR.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of OCR → Optical Character Recognition
☛ Use of OCR technology → To digitize text
☛ Use of OMR → To recognize marks on answer sheets
☛ Function of barcode reader → To decode barcodes
☛ Example of OCR scanner → Samsung Clearer Scanner

q: Which of the following is NOT a series of the supercomputer PARAM that was developed by Indian scientists?
qs.e: The PARAM series is a line of supercomputers developed by India's Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC). This series includes models like PARAM 8000, PARAM 8600, PARAM 10000, and PARAM BRAHMA. PARAM 8000, launched in 1991, was India's first supercomputer. PARAM BRAHMA is a high-performance computing system used for climate modeling and genomics. However, 'PARAM MITRA' is not part of this series; no such model exists in the PARAM lineup. Therefore, it is the incorrect option among the given choices.
qs.kf:
☛ First supercomputer of PARAM series → PARAM 8000
☛ Organization that developed PARAM series → C-DAC
☛ PARAM 8600 was based on which processor → Intel i860
☛ PARAM BRAHMA is used in which field → Climate modeling and genomics
☛ Latest supercomputer in PARAM series → PARAM Siddhi-AI

q: Which of the following is a First Generation Computer?
qs.e: First generation computers used vacuum tubes. SEAC (Standards Eastern Automatic Computer) was built in 1950 and is a first generation computer. ATLAS is a second generation computer (transistor-based, 1962). STAR 1000 and ABACUS are not computers; ABACUS is an ancient calculating device. First generation (1940-1956) includes ENIAC, UNIVAC, IBM 701, etc. SEAC used vacuum tubes and was used for weather prediction and scientific calculations.
qs.kf:
☛ Main technology used in first generation → Vacuum tubes
☛ Main technology used in second generation → Transistors
☛ Programming language of first generation → Machine language
☛ Full form of ENIAC → Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer
☛ Time period of first generation → 1940-1956

q: Desktop computers, laptop computers, tablets and smartphones are different types of:
qs.e: Desktop computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones all fall under the category of microcomputers. Microcomputers are computers that use a microprocessor as their central processing unit and are designed for individual use. Mainframe computers are used by large organizations for bulk data processing. Supercomputers are extremely fast and used for scientific calculations. Minicomputers are mid-sized systems between microcomputers and mainframes. In the modern era, microcomputers are the most widely used type of computer due to their affordability and versatility.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for personal computer → Microcomputer
☛ Chip used in microcomputers → Microprocessor
☛ Most powerful computer → Supercomputer
☛ Computer used in banking → Mainframe computer
☛ Alternative to minicomputer → Microcomputer

q: SAGA-220 was developed by Indian Space Research Organization. What is SAGA-220?
qs.e: SAGA-220 is a state-of-the-art super computer developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). It was built at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC). 'SAGA' stands for Scatter Available GPU Accelerated, and 220 denotes its peak performance of 220 teraflops. This super computer assists in complex tasks like weather forecasting, climate modeling, and space mission data processing. It operates on GPU-based architecture, making it energy efficient. ISRO developed it using indigenous technology, showcasing India's capability in high-performance computing.
qs.kf:
☛ ISRO's fastest supercomputer → Pratyush
☛ Speed of SAGA-220 → 220 teraflops
☛ Location of VSSC → Thiruvananthapuram
☛ ISRO's first supercomputer → SAGA-220
☛ Full form of GPU → Graphics Processing Unit

q: Which of the storage device of computers has now become obsolete?
qs.e: Floppy disk is an outdated magnetic storage medium that was popular from the 1970s to the 2000s. It had very low storage capacity (1.44 MB) and was easily damaged. Compared to USB pen drives, CD-ROMs and hard disks, floppy disks are now completely obsolete. Modern computers do not include a floppy drive. USB flash drives have replaced floppy disks due to higher storage, faster speed and reliability. CD-ROM and hard disk are still in use, while pen drives are the most popular portable storage.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest portable storage device → Floppy disk
☛ Capacity of floppy disk → 1.44 MB
☛ Type of floppy disk → Magnetic storage
☛ Technology that replaced floppy → USB flash drive
☛ Storage devices still in use → Hard disk, CD-ROM, pen drive

q: From the given options, select the developer of 'PARAM 10000', a supercomputer of Indian origin.
qs.e: PARAM 10000 is a supercomputer of Indian origin, developed by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune. It is part of the PARAM series, which was initiated in the 1990s. C-DAC was established in 1988 by the Government of India to develop supercomputing capabilities in the country. PARAM 10000 was launched in 1998 and was a powerful supercomputer at that time. It played a key role in making India self-reliant in supercomputing.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of C-DAC → Centre for Development of Advanced Computing
☛ PARAM 10000 launch year → 1998
☛ First supercomputer of PARAM series → PARAM 8000 (1991)
☛ Headquarters of C-DAC → Pune, Maharashtra
☛ Establishment year of C-DAC → 1988

q: In the context of computing, which among the following is the correct order?
qs.e: In computing, the basic unit of data measurement is the byte. After that come kilobyte (KB), megabyte (MB), gigabyte (GB), and terabyte (TB). Each unit is 1024 times larger than the previous one. 1 TB = 1024 GB, 1 GB = 1024 MB, 1 MB = 1024 KB. Therefore, the largest unit is terabyte, followed by gigabyte, then megabyte, and the smallest is kilobyte. Thus, the correct descending order is TB > GB > MB > KB.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the smallest data unit? → Bit
☛ How many MB in 1 GB? → 1024 MB
☛ How many GB in 1 TB? → 1024 GB
☛ How many KB in 1 MB? → 1024 KB
☛ What is the largest data unit? → Yottabyte (YB)

q: Who among the following is known as the 'father of Indian Supercomputers'?
qs.e: Dr. Vijay Bhatkar is known as the 'father of Indian Supercomputers'. He developed India's first supercomputer, PARAM 8000, which was launched in 1991. This achievement made India self-reliant in the field of supercomputing. Dr. Bhatkar also served as the founder director of C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing). For his contributions, he was honored with prestigious awards like Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first supercomputer → PARAM 8000
☛ Developer of PARAM 8000 → Dr. Vijay Bhatkar
☛ Full form of C-DAC → Centre for Development of Advanced Computing
☛ Award received by Vijay Bhatkar → Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan
☛ Nandan Nilkeni associated with → Infosys and Aadhaar

q: Write the name of the supercomputer developed by Tata Group in 2007.
qs.e: In 2007, the Tata Group under its research arm Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) developed a supercomputer named EKA. It became the fourth fastest supercomputer in the world at that time, with a computing speed of 117.9 teraflops. It was installed at the Computational Research Laboratories (CRL) in Pune. EKA put India on the global supercomputing map, entering the TOP500 list at rank 4. Built on HP Cluster Platform, its cost was around Rs. 50 crore. Later, it was used by the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) for weather forecasting.
qs.kf:
☛ Meaning of EKA → Sanskrit word for 'oneness' or 'unity'
☛ Developer of EKA → Tata Group (TCS)
☛ Speed of EKA → 117.9 teraflops
☛ World rank in 2007 → Fourth
☛ Use of EKA → Weather forecasting (IMD)

q: Who among the following pioneered binary logic and arithmetic in computer programming?
qs.e: Claude Shannon is considered the pioneer of binary logic and arithmetic in computer programming. In his 1937 master's thesis "A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits," he demonstrated how Boolean algebra could be implemented using electrical switches and relays, laying the foundation for digital computers. His work introduced the binary system through logic gates, which is the basis of all modern computers. Shannon is also known as the "Father of Information Theory." Without his contributions, modern computing and digital communication would not exist.
qs.kf:
☛ Father of binary logic → Claude Shannon
☛ Father of Information Theory → Claude Shannon
☛ Applied Boolean algebra to switching circuits → Claude Shannon
