qs.e: Preparing report cards, maintaining student records, and creating question papers are actions related to Education administration in computer applications. This area focuses on managing academic data, automating administrative tasks, and making the teaching process efficient in educational institutions. Education administration involves storing, processing, and updating student data, grades, attendance, and other academic records. It is widely used in schools, colleges, and universities. Other options like space research, business marketing, and automobile control serve different purposes. Education administration helps streamline operations, reduce manual work, and improve accuracy in handling student information. It is a key application of computers in the education sector.
qs.kf:
☛ Which area of computer application deals with academic data management? → Education administration.
☛ Preparing report cards is part of which computer application? → Education administration.
☛ Maintaining student records falls under which field? → Education administration.
☛ Creating question papers is a function of which computer application? → Education administration.
☛ What is the main use of education administration? → Data management and administrative tasks in institutions.

q: What is the function of the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Tab?
qs.e: The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Tab is used to switch between open tabs in a browser or other software. This shortcut moves the focus from the current tab to the next tab. It is especially useful for quick navigation without using a mouse when multiple tabs are open. Ctrl + Shift + Tab is used to switch tabs in the opposite direction. This shortcut works in most modern browsers and tab-based applications.
qs.kf:
☛ Function of Ctrl + Tab → Switch between open tabs
☛ Function of Ctrl + Shift + Tab → Go to previous tab
☛ Function of Ctrl + W → Close current tab
☛ Function of Ctrl + T → Open a new tab
☛ Function of Alt + Tab → Switch between open applications

q: Which pair of keyboard shortcuts is used to quickly copy and paste text?
qs.e: To quickly copy and paste text, the keyboard shortcuts Ctrl + C (copy) and Ctrl + V (paste) are used. Ctrl + C copies the selected text or object to the clipboard, while Ctrl + V pastes the clipboard content at the current location. These shortcuts are standard in most operating systems and software, such as Windows, Mac, and Linux. Other options like Ctrl + F is used for find, Ctrl + S for save, and Ctrl + Tab for switching tabs.
qs.kf:
☛ Shortcut for cut → Ctrl + X
☛ Shortcut for undo → Ctrl + Z
☛ Shortcut for redo → Ctrl + Y
☛ Shortcut for save → Ctrl + S
☛ Shortcut for print → Ctrl + P

q: ________ is the most common way of connecting computers on a network with wired connection.
qs.e: Ethernet is the most common way of connecting computers on a network with wired connection. It is a wired networking technology used in LAN (Local Area Network). Ethernet uses RJ45 connectors and twisted pair cables. It is based on the IEEE 802.3 standard and uses the CSMA/CD protocol for data transfer. LAN is a network type, while Ethernet is a technology. Wi-Fi is wireless and the Internet is a global network, so they are not correct.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the standard for Ethernet? → IEEE 802.3
☛ Which protocol is used in Ethernet? → CSMA/CD
☛ Types of Ethernet cables? → Twisted Pair, Coaxial, Fiber Optic
☛ In which network is Ethernet used? → LAN
☛ Which connector is used in Ethernet? → RJ45

q: A/An ______ is software used to maintain the security of a private network.
qs.e: A firewall is a security software or hardware that protects a private network from unauthorized access. It controls incoming and outgoing traffic and blocks malicious data. The network security firewall acts as a barrier between internal and external threats. It uses techniques like packet filtering, stateful inspection, and application-layer gateways based on rules. Malware, encryption, and clickbait, unlike firewall, serve different purposes for network security. Firewalls are essential in today's cyber threat landscape.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main function of a firewall? → To filter and control network traffic
☛ At which layer does packet filtering work? → Network layer (OSI model)
☛ What does a stateful firewall track? → The state of active connections
☛ At which layer does an application-layer firewall operate? → Application layer of OSI model
☛ Which software performs the opposite function of a firewall? → VPN (for encryption and tunneling)

q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
qs.e: The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 while he was working at CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research). He developed HTML (Hypertext Markup Language), HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), and the first web browser. This invention revolutionized information sharing on the internet. Robert E. Kahn and Vint Cerf are the fathers of the Internet Protocol (TCP/IP), while Antonio Meucci is credited with inventing the telephone. The WWW was opened to the public in 1991, becoming the primary medium for global information exchange.
qs.kf:
☛ Inventor of WWW → Tim Berners-Lee
☛ First web browser → WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus)
☛ First website → info.cern.ch
☛ Father of HTTP protocol → Tim Berners-Lee
☛ Founder of HTML language → Tim Berners-Lee

q: ________ is an interactive computer-generated experience taking place within a simulated environment.
qs.e: The definition describes Virtual Reality (VR), which is an interactive, computer-generated experience within a simulated environment. VR immerses the user completely in a synthetic world where they can interact with objects and surroundings. In contrast, Augmented Reality (AR) overlays digital information onto the real world. Artificial Intelligence (AI) involves machines mimicking human intelligence, while the Internet of Things (IoT) connects physical devices via the internet. VR is widely used in gaming, training simulations, education, and therapy, providing a sense of presence in a virtual space.
qs.kf:
☛ Headset used in Virtual Reality → HMD (Head-Mounted Display)
☛ Technology that overlays digital info on real world → Augmented Reality
☛ Branch of AI that understands human language → Natural Language Processing (NLP)
☛ Medium of communication between IoT devices → Internet
☛ Device tracking user movement in VR → Motion controller

q: Which among them is the largest network in terms of area?
A. MAN
B. WAN
C. Intranet
D. Internet
qs.e: Networks are classified based on their geographical area. LAN (Local Area Network) is the smallest, covering a room or building. MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a city or metropolis. WAN (Wide Area Network) connects countries or continents, forming the backbone of the Internet. Intranet is a private network limited to an organization. Internet is the largest network, connecting millions of networks worldwide. It is a global system enabling various types of data and communication. Therefore, in terms of area, the Internet is the largest network.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the smallest network? → LAN
☛ What does MAN stand for? → Metropolitan Area Network
☛ What does WAN stand for? → Wide Area Network
☛ What type of network is Intranet? → Private network
☛ What is Internet also known as? → Network of Networks

q: Name the device used to connect computers for communication via telephone lines.
A. HUB
B. Switch
C. Repeater
D. MODEM
qs.e: The device used to connect computers for communication via telephone lines is the MODEM (Modulator-Demodulator). It converts digital signals from a computer into analog signals for transmission over telephone lines and vice versa. HUB and Switch connect devices within a Local Area Network (LAN), while a Repeater regenerates weakened signals. Therefore, for telephone line communication, a MODEM is essential to enable data transfer over the analog telephone network.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of MODEM → Modulator-Demodulator
☛ Primary function of MODEM → Conversion between analog and digital signals
☛ Which device is used for communication via telephone lines → MODEM
☛ Early device for internet connectivity → Dial-up MODEM
☛ Device to connect devices in a LAN → HUB or Switch

q: Which among the following network topologies has the highest transmission speed? A) LAN B) WAN C) MAN D) Both LAN and WAN have equal transmission speeds.
qs.e: LAN (Local Area Network) spans a small geographical area such as an office or building. Due to its limited distance, data transmission experiences low latency and high speed, typically ranging from 100 Mbps to 10 Gbps. WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographical areas like countries or continents, and due to long distances, it has higher latency and lower speed (usually 1-100 Mbps). MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a city-sized area and has speed lower than LAN but higher than WAN. Thus, LAN has the highest transmission speed among these network topologies.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of LAN? → Local Area Network
☛ What is the maximum distance covered by WAN? → Unlimited (country or global)
☛ What area does MAN cover? → City or metropolitan area
☛ What type of cable is commonly used in LAN? → Ethernet cable (UTP)
☛ What is the typical speed of WAN? → 1-100 Mbps

q: Trojan Horse is a form of:
qs.e: A Trojan Horse is a type of malware that disguises itself as a legitimate program or file. It tricks users into installing it on their system, after which it performs malicious activities such as stealing data or damaging the system. Unlike worms, Trojans do not self-replicate; they rely on user interaction to spread. Therefore, Trojan Horse is considered a form of virus attack. It is different from Slammer worm and Melissa worm, which are self-propagating worms. Trojans often create a backdoor for unauthorized access to the system.
qs.kf:
☛ Main purpose of Trojan Horse → Gaining unauthorized access to a system
☛ How Trojan Horse spreads → Through deceptive downloads or email attachments
☛ Trojan vs Worm → Worms self-replicate; Trojans do not
☛ Origin of the name Trojan Horse → Derived from ancient Greek mythology
☛ Backdoor Trojan → Provides remote access to hackers

q: In Computer terminology, what is the full form of IDN?
qs.e: The full form of IDN in computer terminology is Internationalized Domain Name. It allows the use of non-ASCII characters (such as Devanagari, Arabic, Chinese, etc.) in website URLs, enabling domain names in local languages. IDN is standardized by ICANN and is based on Punycode encoding. This technology has made multilingual domain names possible, such as example.भारत. The goal of IDN is to make the internet more inclusive and multilingual, allowing users worldwide to access websites using their native scripts.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of IDN → Internationalized Domain Name
☛ Encoding used for IDN → Punycode
☛ Standardizing body for IDN → ICANN
☛ Characters used in IDN → Non-ASCII (local languages)
☛ Purpose of IDN → Promote multilingual internet

q: The system that converts an IP address into an easy to remember format is called:
qs.e: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a crucial internet system that converts IP addresses into human-readable names. IP addresses are numerical (e.g., 192.168.1.1) and difficult to remember. DNS translates them into domain names (e.g., www.google.com), which are easy to recall. It operates as a distributed database and is essential for internet functionality. Without DNS, users would have to memorize IP addresses to access websites. Options 1, 2, and 3 are either unrelated to the internet or incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of DNS? → Domain Name System
☛ Which port number does DNS use? → 53
☛ Which protocols does DNS work on? → UDP and TCP
☛ How many DNS root servers are there? → 13
☛ What type of database is DNS? → Distributed database

q: Which of the following servers convert IP addresses to domain names?
qs.e: DNS (Domain Name System) is a server that converts IP addresses to domain names. It uses the reverse lookup process to retrieve the domain name associated with a given IP address. Without DNS, users would have to memorize numerical IP addresses to access websites. It is a fundamental pillar of the internet. Email is a service, P2P is a network model, and Cloud Services provide resources, but only DNS performs domain name resolution.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of DNS? → Domain Name System
☛ Which port does DNS use? → 53
☛ Which DNS record maps IP to domain? → PTR record
☛ Reverse DNS lookup is used for? → Spam filtering
☛ What is the main function of DNS server? → Convert domain names to IP addresses

q: In HTTP, P stands for:
qs.e: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, which is the standard protocol for transferring data on the web. P stands for Protocol, which is a set of rules and standards that govern communication in a computer network. HTTP is used to send and receive data between a web server and a client (such as a browser). It is an application layer protocol based on TCP/IP and is the foundation of the World Wide Web. It was developed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. The three main versions of HTTP are HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/2.
qs.kf:
☛ What does S stand for in HTTPS? → Secure
☛ What is the full form of HTTP? → HyperText Transfer Protocol
☛ On which port does HTTP work? → 80
☛ On which port does HTTPS work? → 443
☛ Who invented HTTP? → Tim Berners-Lee

q: Which of the following refers to protection of data against accidental or intentional disclosure to unauthorised persons or unauthorised modification or destruction?
qs.e: Data security refers to the protection of data from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or destruction. It ensures that only authorized individuals can access data and maintains the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data. A database is merely a collection of data, privacy data is a type of data, and data redundancy refers to duplication of data.
qs.kf:
☛ Three main pillars of data security → Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
☛ Technologies related to data security → Encryption, Firewall, Access Control
☛ Meaning of data integrity → Protection from unauthorized modification
☛ Way to ensure confidentiality → Grant access only to authorized users
☛ Threats to data security → Hacking, Malware, Phishing

q: Who among the following is considered as the father of the world wide web?
qs.e: Sir Timothy John Berners-Lee is considered the father of the World Wide Web. He invented HTTP, HTML, and URL in 1989, which are the foundations of the web. He also created the first web browser and server in 1990 while working at CERN. Robert Cailliau was a co-inventor, Pei-Yuan Wei developed the ViolaWWW browser, and James H. Clark co-founded Netscape.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the World Wide Web invented? → 1989
☛ What was the name of Berners-Lee's first web browser? → WorldWideWeb
☛ Which organization develops web standards? → W3C
☛ What does HTTP stand for? → HyperText Transfer Protocol
☛ What does HTML stand for? → HyperText Markup Language

q: ______ is an improvement on WEP used in Wi-Fi networks.
qs.e: WPA (Wi-Fi Protected Access) is an improved version of WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy) for wireless network security. WEP had security vulnerabilities due to weak encryption, which were addressed in WPA. WPA uses TKIP (Temporal Key Integrity Protocol) to strengthen data encryption. Later, WPA2 and WPA3 were introduced as even more secure options. SSL is a protocol that secures online data transfer, not Wi-Fi networks. SAAS is a cloud service model and POP is an email protocol; both are unrelated to Wi-Fi security.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of WEP → Wired Equivalent Privacy
☛ Full form of WPA → Wi-Fi Protected Access
☛ Encryption protocol used in WPA → TKIP
☛ More secure successor of WPA → WPA2
☛ Latest encryption standard in WPA3 → SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals)

q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
o: Vint Cerf is recognised as one of the ‘Fathers of the Internet’.
In internet terminology, IP means Internet Practice.
The first computer in India was installed in the Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata.
Hotmail is the first free web-based email service introduced in 1995.
qs.e: This statement is incorrect because in internet terminology, IP stands for Internet Protocol, not Internet Practice. IP is a fundamental communication protocol that defines rules for sending and receiving data over the internet. Vint Cerf is indeed recognised as one of the 'Fathers of the Internet'. The first computer in India was installed at the Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata, which was a FACOM 128B. Hotmail was the first free web-based email service introduced in 1995. Therefore, the second statement is false.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of IP? → Internet Protocol
☛ Who is known as the Father of the Internet? → Vint Cerf and Robert Kahn
☛ Which was the first computer in India? → FACOM 128B
☛ Where was the first computer installed in India? → Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata
☛ Which was the first free web-based email service? → Hotmail (1995)

q: Which one is not a network protocol?
qs.e: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is a markup language used to define the structure and content of web pages. It is not a network protocol. Network protocols are rules and standards that govern data communication over computer networks. SSH (Secure Shell) is a secure remote login protocol. PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) establishes direct communication between two network nodes. POP (Post Office Protocol) is used to retrieve emails. Thus, HTML is not a network protocol.
qs.kf:
☛ Example of network protocol → TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP
☛ Full form of HTML → HyperText Markup Language
☛ Full form of SSH → Secure Shell
☛ Full form of PPP → Point-to-Point Protocol
☛ Full form of POP → Post Office Protocol

q: Find the odd statement out in relation to firewall.
o: Firewall can be a combination of software & hardware.
qs.e: A firewall is a security system that protects a computer network from unauthorized access, not from fire. It can be a software, hardware, or a combination of both. Firewalls filter incoming and outgoing traffic based on predefined rules, thereby defending against cyber attacks. Thus, the statement about protecting from fire is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Primary function of firewall → Protect network from unauthorized access
☛ Firewall software examples → Windows Defender Firewall, ZoneAlarm
☛ Firewall hardware examples → Cisco ASA, Palo Alto Networks
☛ Types of firewalls → Packet Filter, Stateful Inspection, Proxy Firewall
☛ Firewall is the → first line of defense in network security

q: What does TCP stand for with respect to computer networks?
qs.e: TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol. It is a core protocol of the Internet Protocol Suite, responsible for reliable data transmission between devices over a network. TCP breaks data into packets, ensures they are delivered in the correct order, and checks for errors. It is a connection-oriented protocol, meaning a reliable connection is established before data transfer. TCP operates at the transport layer and, together with IP, forms the backbone of internet communication.
qs.kf:
☛ What does TCP stand for? → Transmission Control Protocol
☛ Which layer does TCP operate in? → Transport Layer
☛ What type of protocol is TCP? → Connection-oriented
☛ Which protocol is TCP associated with? → IP (Internet Protocol)
☛ What does TCP ensure? → Reliable delivery of data

q: Who invented ‘www’ ?
qs.e: The World Wide Web (www) was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. He is a British computer scientist. He also developed the first web browser and web server. www is an information system that links documents via hypertext links on the internet. It was developed at CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research). Other options: Vint Cerf and Robert E. Kahn are the fathers of internet protocol (TCP/IP), while Charles Babbage is considered the father of the Analytical Engine.
qs.kf:
☛ Who invented the www? → Tim Berners-Lee
☛ Where was www developed? → CERN
☛ Who created the first web browser? → Tim Berners-Lee
☛ Who invented TCP/IP? → Vint Cerf and Robert E. Kahn
☛ Who invented the Analytical Engine? → Charles Babbage

q: Which of the following best describes a LAN?
o: A storage device used to read optical discs
A network covering a small geographical area like an office or school
A code used to represent characters in numbers
qs.e: A LAN (Local Area Network) is a network that covers a small geographical area, such as an office, school, or building. It connects computers and other devices to share data and resources like printers. The range of a LAN is typically limited to a few kilometers. It offers high speed and low latency. Other options: an optical disc reader is a storage device; a high-capacity CD format could be DVD or Blu-ray; a code for representing characters as numbers is ASCII or Unicode. All these are unrelated to LAN.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of LAN → Local Area Network
☛ LAN coverage → Small geographical area (up to a few km)
☛ Common LAN topologies → Star, Bus, Ring
☛ LAN vs WAN → Smaller than WAN, larger than PAN
☛ LAN speed → High (10 Mbps to 10 Gbps)

q: LAN is often used in schools and offices. This abbreviation expands to:
qs.e: LAN stands for Local Area Network, which connects computers within a limited geographical area such as a school, office, or building. It enables fast data transfer and sharing of resources like printers and files. Unlike WAN (Wide Area Network), which covers large areas, LAN is confined to a small region. It is typically implemented using Ethernet and Wi-Fi technologies. LANs are essential for local communication and collaboration.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of LAN? → Local Area Network
☛ What is the full form of WAN? → Wide Area Network
☛ What geographical area does LAN cover? → Small area (a building or office)
☛ Is data transfer rate higher in LAN or WAN? → LAN
☛ What are common technologies used in LAN? → Ethernet and Wi-Fi

q: In the field of e-commerce and financial trading, which application of computers is essential for analyzing massive volumes of rapidly changing market data and detecting complex patterns to inform investment decisions?
qs.e: In the field of e-commerce and financial trading, Real-time Predictive Analytics is essential for analyzing massive volumes of rapidly changing market data and detecting complex patterns to inform investment decisions. This technology uses machine learning and statistical models to analyze data in real-time and predict future trends, enabling timely and informed decisions. Other options like Inventory Management Systems, Data Encryption, and Word Processing do not serve this purpose as they focus on different aspects such as stock tracking or data security.
qs.kf:
☛ What is Real-time Predictive Analytics based on? → Machine learning and statistical models
☛ What is a major use of real-time data analysis in e-commerce? → Predicting customer behavior and pricing strategies
☛ Which technology is used in financial trading to analyze rapid market changes? → Real-time Predictive Analytics
☛ What does Data Encryption and Security Software provide? → Data confidentiality and integrity
☛ What is Inventory Management System useful for? → Monitoring stock levels and order management

q: JPEG stands for __________.
qs.e: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group. It is a popular image compression standard used to reduce the size of digital images. It was developed in 1992 by ISO and ITU-T. JPEG is widely used in photography, websites, and social media. It uses lossy compression, which slightly reduces image quality but results in much smaller file sizes. The other options are incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of JPEG? → Joint Photographic Experts Group
☛ What type of compression does JPEG use? → Lossy compression
☛ When was JPEG developed? → 1992
☛ Who developed JPEG? → ISO and ITU-T
☛ What is JPEG used for? → Compression of digital images

q: What is the expansion of IRNSS?
o: Indian Renal and Nephrological Scientific Studies
qs.e: The full form of IRNSS is Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System. It is India's indigenous regional satellite navigation system developed by ISRO. The aim is to provide accurate position and time services to India and surrounding regions. Its operational name is NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation). The constellation consists of 7 satellites and operates in the L5 and S bands. IRNSS is used for road, air, and maritime navigation, disaster management, and mobile phone applications.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the operational name of IRNSS? → NavIC
☛ Which agency developed IRNSS? → ISRO
☛ How many satellites are in IRNSS? → 7
☛ Which frequency bands does IRNSS use? → L5 and S band
☛ What does NavIC stand for? → Navigation with Indian Constellation

q: Where is the "title block" usually made?
o: on the upper right hand corner of the drawing sheet
lower right corner of the drawing sheet
on the upper left corner of the drawing sheet
qs.e: The title block is a crucial part of a technical drawing that includes the drawing title, scale, drafter's name, date, and other information. According to international standards (ISO 7200), the title block is placed at the lower right corner of the drawing sheet. This location ensures easy visibility when the drawing is read from left to right. The title block also contains data on projection methods, revision history, and drawing number. Standardization of this location, as per ISO and IS norms, ensures uniform understanding across engineering drawings.
qs.kf:
☛ Standard location of title block → lower right corner
☛ ISO standard number → ISO 7200
☛ Information included in title block → title, scale, date, drawing number
☛ Indian Standard number → IS 10714-1985
☛ Standard for drawing sheet sizes → IS 10711

q: Which is India's first super computer?
qs.e: India's first super computer is Param 8000, developed in 1991 by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing) under the leadership of Dr. Vijay Bhatkar. Param 8000 made India self-reliant in supercomputing, despite US restrictions. It had a processing speed of 1 gigaflop. This was the first supercomputer in the Param series, followed by advanced versions like Param 10000, Param Padma, and Param Yuva. Param 8000 played a crucial role in weather forecasting, scientific research, and defense sectors.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first super computer name → Param 8000
☛ Developer of Param 8000 → C-DAC
☛ Lead scientist of Param 8000 → Dr. Vijay Bhatkar
☛ Processing speed of Param 8000 → 1 Gigaflop
☛ Year of Param 8000 development → 1991

q: Which of the following characteristics represents the ability of a computer to work continuously without fatigue?
qs.e: The diligence characteristic of a computer enables it to work continuously without fatigue. While humans get tired and make mistakes, computers can work for long periods without losing efficiency. This feature makes computers indispensable in robotics, automation, and data processing. Speed refers to fast operation, Accuracy to correctness, and Versatility to performing multiple tasks. Diligence means tirelessness or hardworking, which is a key attribute of computers. It ensures consistent performance over time.
qs.kf:
☛ Computer's ability to work without fatigue → Diligence
☛ Speed represents → Fast processing
☛ Accuracy refers to → Correctness
☛ Versatility means → Ability to perform different tasks
☛ Diligence is NOT related to → Speed or accuracy

q: Which characteristic of computers enables them to perform various tasks such as calculations, graphics, and communication?
qs.e: The characteristic of versatility in computers allows them to perform a wide variety of tasks like calculations, graphics, communication, data processing, and more. This makes computers useful in different fields. Speed refers to how fast tasks are executed, accuracy means precision in calculations, and automation means the ability to work without human intervention. However, these are specific capabilities, while versatility enables the computer to handle multiple types of tasks simultaneously. Hence, the correct answer is Versatility.
qs.kf:
☛ Computer speed is measured in → MIPS (Million Instructions Per Second)
☛ Accuracy of computer means → error-free calculations
☛ Automation in computer → ability to work without human help
☛ Versatility means → ability to perform different types of work
☛ Memory of computer → stores data and programs

q: Unlike humans, a computer does not feel tired or bored while repeating the same task all day. This shows which characteristic?
qs.e: The characteristic of a computer that allows it to perform the same task repeatedly without getting tired or bored is called Diligence. Unlike humans, computers do not suffer from fatigue or lack of concentration, enabling them to work consistently for long hours. Intelligence refers to the ability to learn or make decisions, which computers lack. Versatility is the ability to perform multiple tasks simultaneously, while Speed refers to the rapid execution of tasks. Diligence is a key feature that makes computers ideal for repetitive jobs, ensuring accuracy and reliability over extended periods.
qs.kf:
☛ Which characteristic of computers enables them to work without getting tired? → Diligence
☛ Is intelligence a characteristic of computers? → No, it is not
☛ Difference between versatility and diligence? → Versatility means doing many tasks; diligence means doing one task repeatedly
☛ Speed is which characteristic of computers? → Ability to work fast
☛ Diligence in Hindi is called? → अध्यवसाय

name: Set 1 · Q1–49
sub: Arts & Culture - Classical Dances & Folk Dances

q: Ghoomar is folk dance belongs to ________
qs.e: Ghoomar is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, primarily performed by the Bhil tribe. It is performed by women who twirl in colorful ghaghra and chunari. Ghoomar has been included in the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list. This dance is performed on special occasions like weddings and festivals. Other folk dances of Rajasthan include Kalbelia, Bhavai, and Gair. Ghoomar originated from the Hadoti region. It symbolizes the cultural identity of Rajasthan.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the most famous folk dance of Rajasthan? → Ghoomar
☛ Ghoomar dance is associated with which tribe? → Bhil
☛ Which folk dance is included in UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list? → Ghoomar
☛ What do women wear in Ghoomar dance? → Ghaghra and Chunari
☛ Which Rajasthani folk dance is based on spinning motion? → Ghoomar

q: Which of the following dance styles is known as 'Saga of East'?
qs.e: Kathakali is a classical dance form from Kerala, known as 'Saga of the East' or 'Story of the East'. It is a dance-drama that depicts mythological stories with elaborate costumes, colorful makeup, and expressive eye movements. The term 'Kathakali' literally means 'story-play'. Unlike Mohiniyattam (feminine), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), or Kathak (North India), Kathakali is characterized by its vigorous movements and distinct facial expressions. It is traditionally performed by male dancers.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin of Kathakali → Kerala
☛ Theme of Kathakali → Mythological stories
☛ Instruments used in Kathakali → Chenda, Maddalam
☛ Distinct feature of Kathakali → Green makeup for hero
☛ Kathakali is also known as → Saga of the East

q: Which of these is NOT a classical dance?
qs.e: India recognizes eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya. Rasali is a folk dance primarily performed by tribal communities in Gujarat and Rajasthan. It is not included in the list of classical dances. Manipuri, Odissi, and Kuchipudi are all classical dances. The Sangeet Natak Akademi and the Ministry of Culture have officially recognized these eight forms.
qs.kf:
☛ How many classical dances are recognized in India? → 8
☛ Which classical dance originated in Odisha? → Odissi
☛ Kuchipudi dance is associated with which state? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Manipuri dance is the classical dance of which state? → Manipur
☛ Which category does Rasali dance belong to? → Folk dance

q: Lavani is a famous folk dance of __________.
qs.e: Lavani is a famous folk dance of Maharashtra, known for its fast tempo and powerful rhythm. It is primarily performed by women, with songs sung to the beat of the dholki. Lavani is traditionally used for entertainment and to convey social messages. It is an important part of Maharashtra's culture and is often performed at festivals and weddings. Lavani has also been widely incorporated into Maharashtra's theatre and popular cinema.

☛ Which state is the folk dance Kathakali from? → Kerala

q: Which of the following is a popular folk dance of Himachal Pradesh?
qs.e: Among the popular folk dances of Himachal Pradesh, Charba is a significant dance, mainly performed in the Kullu and Mandi regions. This dance is performed on special occasions and festivals, where men and women participate together. Dancers form a circular chain, holding hands and rotating while singing traditional songs. The rhythm is slow and melodious, reflecting Himachali culture. Among the other options, Jawara is a folk dance of Madhya Pradesh, Alkap belongs to West Bengal, and Matki is from Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

☛ What is the state dance of Himachal Pradesh? → Nati
☛ What is a famous folk dance of Himachal Pradesh? → Charba
☛ What is another folk dance of Himachal Pradesh? → Jhorra
☛ What is a festival dance of Himachal Pradesh? → Dangi
☛ What is a famous folk song of Himachal Pradesh? → Jhoori

q: Which of the following dance forms belongs to the state of Jammu and Kashmir?
qs.e: Rouf is a famous folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir, primarily performed by women during festivals like Eid and weddings. It is an integral part of the cultural identity of the Kashmir Valley. In Rouf, women stand in rows and perform graceful hand movements and rhythmic footwork. Other dances of Kashmir include Hafiza and Band Pather. Among the incorrect options, Bidesia is a dance from Bihar, Karma is from Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and Swang is from Haryana and Punjab. Hence, Rouf correctly belongs to Jammu and Kashmir.

☛ Swang dance belongs to which state? → Haryana and Punjab

q: Which of the following folk dances is from Punjab?
qs.e: Giddha is a famous folk dance of Punjab, primarily performed by women during festivals and special occasions. This dance is performed to the beat of the dhol and exhibits energy and joy. Bagurumba is from Assam, Lezim is from Maharashtra, and Nati is from Himachal Pradesh. Giddha is an integral part of Punjabi culture and is especially performed during festivals like Vaisakhi.

☛ Main instrument used in Giddha → Dhol
☛ Bagurumba dance is from which state → Assam

q: Which of the following is NOT a traditional dance of Rajasthan?
qs.e: Rajasthan is known for its rich cultural heritage and traditional dance forms. Ghoomar is the most famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed mainly by women. Kathputli is a renowned puppet dance of Rajasthan. Gair is a popular dance among the Bhil and other tribal communities of Rajasthan. Dumhal is not a dance of Rajasthan; it is a traditional dance of Jammu and Kashmir, performed primarily by the Wattal tribe. Therefore, Dumhal is NOT a traditional dance of Rajasthan.

q: Which of the following folk dances is from Assam?
qs.e: Bagurumba is a well-known folk dance from Assam, primarily performed by the Bodo community. It is performed during the arrival of spring and the Bishu festival. In this dance, women wear colorful costumes and perform gestures that depict the beauty of nature. Giddha is from Punjab, Lezim from Maharashtra, and Nati from Himachal Pradesh. Other major dances of Assam include Bihu and Jhumur.

q: Which of the following folk dances is from Himachal Pradesh?
qs.e: Nati is a famous folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, predominantly performed in Kullu, Mandi, Kangra, and Shimla regions. It is performed during weddings, festivals, and special occasions, where men and women hold hands and move in a circular formation. Among the other options, Lezim is from Maharashtra, Bagurumba is from Assam, and Giddha is from Punjab. Other folk dances of Himachal Pradesh include Dangi, Jhoola, and Chhappar.

☛ Folk dance of Maharashtra → Lezim
☛ Folk dance of Assam → Bagurumba

q: Kuchipudi has its roots in which Indian State?
qs.e: Kuchipudi is one of the eight major classical dances of India. It originated in the village of Kuchipudi in the state of Andhra Pradesh. This dance form was originally associated with the devotional tradition and was developed according to the rules of the Natya Shastra. Kuchipudi is known for its fast pace, fluid movements, and dramatic elements. It incorporates three aspects: nritta (pure dance), natya (drama), and nattaka (storytelling). Prominent exponents include Siddhendra Yogi and Vempati Chinna Satyam. It was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2011.
qs.kf:
☛ Kuchipudi is the classical dance of which state? → Andhra Pradesh

☛ When was Kuchipudi included in UNESCO list? → 2011
☛ Who are the famous Kuchipudi dancers? → Siddhendra Yogi, Vempati Chinna Satyam

q: Laho dance belongs to the state of _________ in India.
qs.e: Laho is a famous traditional dance of the state of Meghalaya in Northeast India. It is primarily performed by the Khasi and Jaintia tribes. This dance is usually presented during harvest season and festivals, where young men and women participate. Dancers wear colorful traditional attire and move rhythmically to the beats of drums. Laho dance reflects the rich cultural heritage of Meghalaya and is also popular among tourists.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the most popular folk dance of Meghalaya? → Laho
☛ Which communities perform Laho dance? → Khasi and Jaintia

☛ What is the capital of Meghalaya? → Shillong
☛ Which tribes are mainly found in Meghalaya? → Khasi, Garo, Jaintia

q: Find the ODD one out from the given options.
qs.e: Odissi, Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi are classical dances of India, while Lavani is a folk dance. India has eight recognized classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Mohiniyattam (Kerala) and Sattriya (Assam). Lavani is a popular folk dance from Maharashtra, known for its fast tempo and songs. Therefore, Lavani does not belong to the category of classical dances, making it the odd one out.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the eight classical dances of India? → Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya
☛ Lavani is from which state? → Maharashtra
☛ Bharatanatyam belongs to which state? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Kuchipudi is the classical dance of which state? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Odissi is from which state? → Odisha

q: Which of the following dances is NOT a classical dance of India?
qs.e: India recognizes eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Odissi, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya. Kuchipudi originates from Andhra Pradesh, Manipuri from Manipur, and Odissi from Odisha. Bugaku is a Japanese classical dance that developed in the Japanese imperial court. It is distinct from Noh and Kabuki and is performed with Gagaku music. Therefore, Bugaku is not an Indian classical dance.

☛ Sattriya dance belongs to which state? → Assam
☛ Bugaku dance is associated with which country? → Japan
☛ Which state is Kuchipudi from? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Mohiniyattam is a classical dance of which state? → Kerala

q: Which of the following states is associated with the classical dance, Odissi?
qs.e: Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha. This dance style is primarily associated with the Jagannath Temple in Puri, where it was performed by temple dancers (devadasis). It finds mention in the ancient treatise Natyashastra. Odissi is characterized by the Tribhangi posture (three bends) and Chowk stance. The dance expresses themes of love, devotion, and mythology. Renowned Odissi exponents include Sujata Mohapatra and Kelucharan Mohapatra.
qs.kf:
☛ State of origin of Odissi dance → Odisha
☛ Major temple associated with Odissi → Jagannath Temple, Puri
☛ Key posture in Odissi → Tribhangi
☛ Ancient text mentioning Odissi → Natyashastra
☛ Famous Odissi dancer → Kelucharan Mohapatra

q: Thillana is one of the presentation styles of which dance form?
qs.e: Thillana is a presentation style of Bharatanatyam dance form. It is a pure dance (nritta) segment focusing on rhythm and speed. Thillana is typically performed at the end of a recital and involves intricate footwork and poses. It is based on the talas (rhythmic cycles) of Carnatic music and features fast-paced dance sequences. The word 'Thillana' is derived from 'til' (sesame) and 'ana' (bring), signifying the celebratory and energetic nature of the dance. Other major presentation styles in Bharatanatyam include Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Varnam, and Padam.
qs.kf:
☛ In which dance is Thillana performed at the end? → Bharatanatyam
☛ What is the first presentation style of Bharatanatyam? → Alarippu
☛ Which music system is Bharatanatyam primarily based on? → Carnatic music
☛ What type of dance is Thillana? → Nritta (pure dance)
☛ What does the word Bharatanatyam mean? → Bharata (bhava+raga+tala) and Natyam (dance)

q: Which of the following is a folk dance popular during the harvest season in Punjab?
qs.e: Bhangra is the most famous folk dance of Punjab, performed during the harvest season, especially on the festival of Vaisakhi. This dance symbolizes the joy and fertility of farmers and is accompanied by traditional instruments like the dhol. Bhangra is an integral part of Punjabi culture. The other options - Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (North India), and Garba (Gujarat) - are not harvest dances of Punjab.

☛ Main instrument used in Bhangra → Dhol

☛ Odissi dance belongs to which state → Odisha

q: Which of the following is essentially a solo dance?
qs.e: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, primarily performed by women and is essentially a solo dance. It emphasizes graceful expressions and the lasya style. Among the other options, Kathak from North India can be performed both solo and in groups. Manipuri from Manipur is also performed both solo and in groups. Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh was originally a solo dance but is now also performed in groups. In Mohiniyattam, a single dancer performs, narrating the story of Vishnu's Mohini avatar. The dance is known for its gentle movements and expressive face.

☛ Which state is Mohiniyattam associated with? → Kerala
☛ Which style is predominantly used in Mohiniyattam? → Lasya style

☛ Which is considered the oldest classical dance after Bharatanatyam? → Mohiniyattam

q: Which of the following is a popular folk dance of Maharashtra?
qs.e: Tamasha is a popular folk dance of Maharashtra, predominantly performed in the rural areas of the state. It is a vibrant dance form combining music, dance, and drama, often accompanied by Lavani songs. The dance involves energetic movements, spins, and hand gestures. Both men and women participate in Tamasha, which is performed for religious and entertainment purposes. Option 1, Garba, is a folk dance of Gujarat; Option 2, Bhangra, is from Punjab; and Option 3, Dandiya, is also associated with Gujarat's Navratri festival. Other folk dances of Maharashtra include Powada and Koli.

q: The classical dance of Kathakali belongs to which Indian state?
A. Odisha
B. Kerala
C. Andhra Pradesh
D. Assam
qs.e: Kathakali is a major classical dance form of India that originates from the state of Kerala. It is known for its elaborate makeup, costumes, and facial expressions (mudras). The word Kathakali literally means 'story play' derived from Sanskrit 'katha' (story) and 'kali' (play). Traditionally, it depicts stories from epics like the Ramayana and the Mahabharata. This dance style is famous for its intricate eye movements and hand gestures (mudras). Kathakali is believed to have originated around the 16th century.

q: Krishnanattam is a famous dance of which of the following states?
A. Andhra Pradesh.
B. Karnataka.
C. Kerala.
D. Tamilnadu.
qs.e: Krishnanattam is a famous classical dance form of Kerala, depicting the life of Lord Krishna. It originated in the 17th century under the patronage of King Kalariyattil of Manjeri, based on the composition of Kalakkala. This dance is considered a precursor to Kathakali and is traditionally performed at the Guruvayur Temple in Kerala. The performance spans eight nights, narrating the complete story of Krishna from birth to ascension. Krishnanattam is known for its elaborate makeup, costumes, and expressive acting.

☛ How many days does a Krishnanattam performance last? → Eight days

q: Which of the following dance forms does NOT belong to Rajasthan?
qs.e: Lavani is a famous folk dance of Maharashtra, while Ghoomar, Kalbelia, and Gangaur are traditional dances of Rajasthan. Ghoomar is the most famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by women in a swirling motion. Kalbelia is performed by the Kalbelia tribe and has been declared an Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO. Gangaur is a dance performed by women during the Gangaur festival. Lavani is known for its energetic and sensual style, performed to the beat of the dhol.

☛ UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage dance of Rajasthan → Kalbelia

q: Name the Indian classical dance form which is believed to be revealed by Lord Brahma to Bharata, a famous sage, who then codified this sacred dance in a Sanskrit text called 'Natya Shastra'.
qs.e: Bharatanatyam is a major Indian classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu. It is believed that Lord Brahma revealed this dance to the sage Bharata, who later codified it in the Sanskrit text 'Natya Shastra'. 'Natya Shastra' is the oldest treatise on dance, music, and theatre. Bharatanatyam is known for its perfect blend of bhava (expression), raga (melody), and tala (rhythm). The dance uses intricate mudras (hand gestures) and facial expressions to narrate stories, mainly from Hindu mythology. It flourished in temples and royal courts, with major styles including Thanjavur, Kanchipuram, and Pandanallur. Bharatanatyam is considered a sacred art form and is a cultural treasure of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote the Natya Shastra? → Sage Bharata
☛ Which state is associated with Bharatanatyam? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which deity is primarily worshipped in Bharatanatyam? → Shiva (Nataraja)
☛ How many classical dances are recognized in India? → 8
☛ What is the traditional costume for Bharatanatyam? → Sari

q: Yakshagana is a folk performance of which Indian state?
qs.e: Yakshagana is a traditional folk theatre form of Karnataka, prevalent in coastal districts like Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada, Kasaragod, and Shivamogga. It is inspired by Natyashastra and depicts episodes from epics like Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas. The performance combines dance, music, dialogue, and elaborate costumes. The primary musical instruments are maddale (drum) and taala (cymbals). Yakshagana has been recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

☛ Main instruments in Yakshagana → Maddale and Taala
☛ Ancient text influencing Yakshagana → Natyashastra

☛ UNESCO recognition of Yakshagana → Intangible Cultural Heritage

q: Hurkiya Baul is a folk dance form associated with which Indian state?
qs.e: Hurkiya Baul is a famous folk dance form of Uttarakhand, primarily prevalent in the Kumaon region. It is performed during weddings, festivals, and other auspicious occasions. 'Hurkiya' refers to the player of 'Hurka' (a type of drum), and 'Baul' means song. Both men and women participate in this dance, wearing traditional attire. This dance symbolizes the rich cultural heritage of Uttarakhand.

q: Bardo Chham is folk dance of:
qs.e: Bardo Chham is a traditional folk dance performed in the Tawang district of Arunachal Pradesh. This dance is associated with Buddhism and is performed during the 'Bardo' period, which symbolizes the intermediate state between death and rebirth. It is performed by the Sherdukpen tribe, who wear colorful masks and traditional costumes. The dance is believed to ward off evil spirits and bring prosperity. Bardo Chham has also been recognized as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO. The dance is an important part of the cultural identity of Arunachal Pradesh and showcases the rich traditions of the Himalayan region.

☛ Bardo Chham dance is associated with which religion? → Buddhism

☛ What is used in Bardo Chham dance? → Colorful masks and traditional costumes
☛ In which district is Bardo Chham dance prevalent? → Tawang district (Arunachal Pradesh)

q: Ghoomar is a folk song and dance form that is popular in:
qs.e: Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance and song form of Rajasthan, primarily performed by the Bhil community. The dance involves women twirling in circles with their flowing veils, creating a mesmerizing visual effect. Ghoomar is considered a symbol of Rajasthani culture and is performed during weddings, festivals, and other auspicious occasions. It has been recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage. Other famous folk dances of Rajasthan include Kachhi Ghodi, Bhavai, and Kalbelia.

q: With which dance form is the noted dancer Pratibha Prahlad associated?
qs.e: Pratibha Prahlad is a renowned Bharata Natyam dancer. Born in Chennai, she trained under gurus like Rukmini Devi Arundale. Bharata Natyam is a classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, based on bhava, raga, and tala. Pratibha Prahlad has received honors such as the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contributions. This dance form originated in temples and is now performed on stage. It is based on the Natya Shastra.

☛ Which award did Pratibha Prahlad receive? → Padma Shri

q: Indian classical dance form Kuchipudi developed in the state of ________.
qs.e: Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from the state of Andhra Pradesh, India. It derives its name from the village of Kuchipudi in the Krishna district. This dance form evolved as a dance-drama dedicated to Lord Krishna. Its style incorporates Natya (dramatic expression), Nritta (pure dance), and Nritya (expressive dance). Initially, it was performed only by male dancers. Renowned Kuchipudi exponents include Siddhendra Yogi, Vempati Chinnasatyam, and Raja Reddy. It is recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

q: Potloi is the bridal dress worn by the brides belonging to which state?
qs.e: Potloi is the traditional bridal dress worn by the brides of the Meitei community in Manipur. It is a royal red colored garment embroidered with golden and silver threads. It is worn along with a traditional shawl called Inafi and over a petticoat known as Langin. Potloi is an integral part of Manipuri wedding ceremonies and reflects the rich cultural heritage of the state. The practice of wearing Potloi dates back centuries and is a symbol of the identity of the Meitei community.

☛ Which classical dance form is associated with Manipur? → Manipuri

q: World-famous Chhattisgarhi folk singer Teejan Bai is an exponent of what type of folk music?
qs.e: Teejan Bai is a renowned exponent of Pandavani, a traditional folk singing style from Chhattisgarh. Pandavani is based on the epic Mahabharata and involves narrative singing with dramatic gestures. Teejan Bai is considered the most prominent artist of this genre and has been honored with prestigious awards like Padma Shri (1988) and Padma Bhushan (2003). This folk form is primarily popular in Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh. The artist typically performs alone, using a musical instrument called tambura. Teejan Bai is especially known for her unique style of singing in the 'female character' role in Pandavani.

q: In which of the following states is the Gambhira - a popular dance, performed using various wooden masks?
qs.e: Gambhira is a popular folk dance from West Bengal, performed using various wooden masks. This dance is mainly prevalent in the districts of Malda and Murshidabad. It is also known as 'Gambhira Nach' and is based on stories of Hindu deities. Dancers wear colorful wooden masks representing different characters. The dance is usually performed during festivals and special occasions. Gambhira is an important part of West Bengal's rich cultural heritage.

q: Sonal Mansingh is famous for:
qs.e: Sonal Mansingh is a renowned classical dancer from India. She has mastered primarily Odissi and Bharatanatyam dance forms. She has been honored with Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan. In 2003, she received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. Apart from being an exceptional dancer, she is also a noted choreographer and teacher. She has played a significant role in popularizing Indian classical dance globally. q: Which of the following is popular folk dance of Gujarat?
qs.e: Garba is the most famous folk dance of Gujarat, primarily performed during the festival of Navratri. This dance is dedicated to the worship of Goddess Durga and celebrates shakti (power). In Garba, women wear colorful attire and dance in circular movements, clapping their hands in rhythmic beats. In contrast, Chhau (eastern India), Kalbelia (Rajasthan), and Muffler (not a folk dance) are not associated with Gujarat. q: In which of the following period is the idol of the famous Nataraja in the Tandav dance currency?
qs.e: The famous bronze idol of Nataraja in the Tandava dance posture belongs to the Chola period (approximately 9th-12th century). The Chola rulers were great patrons of art and architecture, especially known for their exquisite bronze sculptures, with the Nataraja being the most iconic. These idols depict Lord Shiva as the cosmic dancer performing the Tandava, symbolizing the cycle of creation and destruction. The Chola dynasty, based in southern India, reached its peak during this time, and their bronze casting technique is considered unparalleled. The Nataraja idol is not only a religious symbol but also a masterpiece of Indian art, reflecting the Cholas' cultural and artistic achievements. The Chola empire's capital was Thanjavur, which remains a center of art.
qs.kf:
☛ Dynasty associated with Nataraja idol → Chola
☛ Chola period art highlight → Bronze sculptures
☛ God associated with Tandava dance → Shiva
☛ Capital of Chola empire → Thanjavur
☛ Symbolism of Nataraja posture → Cosmic dance

q: Which of the following states is known for 'Cherawan' dance with bamboo?
qs.e: 'Cherawan' or 'Chero' is a famous folk dance of Mizoram performed using bamboo. It is also called the 'Bamboo Dance'. In this dance, men beat bamboo sticks on the ground rhythmically while women dance between them. This dance is an integral part of Mizoram's culture. The popular dance of Manipur is 'Lai Haraoba' or 'Ras Leela', Assam's is 'Bihu', and Nagaland's is 'Zeme' or 'Lim'. Hence, the correct answer is Mizoram.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is associated with Cherawan dance? → Mizoram
☛ What is the famous bamboo dance of Mizoram called? → Cherawan
☛ Which instrument is used in Cherawan dance? → Bamboo sticks
☛ What is the capital of Mizoram? → Aizawl
☛ Name the state known for bamboo dance? → Mizoram

q: Where is the relationship between Pala and Das Kathia folk music tradition?
qs.e: The Pala and Das Kathia folk music traditions belong to the state of Odisha. Pala is a traditional folk dance-drama that narrates mythological stories, while Das Kathia is a percussion-based style featuring the kathia drum. These art forms are an integral part of Odisha's rich cultural heritage and are performed in villages during festivals and special occasions. They reflect the devotional and narrative aspects of Odia folk culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is associated with Pala folk dance? → Odisha
☛ Which instrument is used in Das Kathia? → Kathia
☛ Pala folk dance of Odisha is based on which theme? → Mythological stories
☛ Kathia is what type of instrument? → Percussion
☛ Which state's folk traditions include Pala and Das Kathia? → Odisha

q: Where is the folk musician 'Manganiyar' related?
qs.e: Manganiyar are folk musicians from Rajasthan. They are mainly found in the Thar Desert region, especially in Jaisalmer and Barmer districts. The Manganiyar community is traditionally skilled in singing and playing instruments. They primarily use instruments like khadtaal, dholak, sarangi, and murli. Their music is based on Rajasthani folk tales and devotional compositions. Manganiyars are also known as the 'bardic community' of Rajasthan. Their music has been recognized by UNESCO.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state are the Manganiyar folk musicians from? → Rajasthan
☛ Which region are Manganiyars mainly found in? → Thar Desert
☛ What is the primary musical instrument of the Manganiyars? → Khadtaal
☛ What is the Manganiyar music based on? → Rajasthani folk tales and devotional compositions
☛ What is the Manganiyar community also known as? → Bardic community

q: Which is the folk dance of Andhra Pradesh?
qs.e: The main folk dance of Andhra Pradesh is Ottam Thedal. This dance is primarily performed in the Godavari region and is associated with worship and festivals. Dancers wear colorful costumes and perform to the beats of drums. Ottam Thedal symbolizes devotion and celebration. Other options like Pakhupila, Khantum, and Cherokan are not folk dances of Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Folk dance of Andhra Pradesh → Ottam Thedal
☛ Region of Ottam Thedal → Godavari region
☛ Other folk dance of Andhra Pradesh → Kolattam
☛ Instrument used in Ottam Thedal → Drum
☛ Occasion for Ottam Thedal → Worship and festivals

q: Which of the following is the oldest classical dance genre?
qs.e: Bharatanatyam is the oldest classical dance genre of India, originating over 2000 years ago in Tamil Nadu. It is mentioned in the ancient treatise Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni. This dance form evolved primarily in temples as a form of worship to deities. Bharatanatyam is known for its perfect blend of bhava (emotion), raga (music), and tala (rhythm). Other options: Bardo Chum is a Tibetan dance, Ghumura is a folk dance of Odisha, and Bihu is a folk dance of Assam. Among classical dances, Bharatanatyam is followed by Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, etc. It is recognized as a classical dance by the Government of India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the ancient name of Bharatanatyam? → Sadir or Dasi Attam
☛ Who authored Natya Shastra? → Bharata Muni
☛ What are the hand gestures in Bharatanatyam called? → Hasta Mudras
☛ Which instruments are mainly used in Bharatanatyam? → Mridangam, Veena, Violin
☛ Who are famous Bharatanatyam dancers? → Rukmini Devi Arundale, Padma Subrahmanyam

q: What is Goa's folk dance?
qs.e: The folk dance of Goa is Mando, a blend of Portuguese and Indian music. It is performed mainly at weddings and festivals. Gagor is a folk dance of Rajasthan, Chakwa of Bihar, and Lure of Gujarat. In Mando, couples dance in a slow, graceful manner accompanied by instruments like drums, violins, and guitars. It reflects Goa's rich cultural heritage and is an integral part of Goan identity.
qs.kf:
☛ Folk dance of Goa → Mando
☛ Folk music of Goa → Dashavadyam
☛ Traditional theatre of Goa → Tiatr
☛ Festival of Goa → Carnival
☛ Language of Goa → Konkani

q: Which of the following is famous for its martial arts 'Thang Ta' style?
qs.e: Thang Ta is a traditional martial art form from Manipur, known for the use of sword (thang) and spear (ta). This ancient art was developed by Manipuri warriors and incorporates dance, music, and spirituality. Thang Ta is preserved as a cultural heritage of Manipur and is performed during festivals and ceremonies. Other states like Nagaland have their own martial arts, while Mizoram and Assam have distinct traditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Thang Ta is the martial art of which state? → Manipur
☛ Which weapons are used in Thang Ta? → Sword and spear
☛ What is the name of Manipur's martial art? → Thang Ta
☛ Thang Ta is related to which field? → Martial arts
☛ What does Thang Ta include? → Dance, music, and spirituality

q: Dandiya is a traditional folk dance-
qs.e: Dandiya is a traditional folk dance primarily associated with the state of Gujarat. This dance is especially famous during the festival of Navratri, where men and women dressed in colorful costumes perform with sticks called dandiyas. Dandiya is considered a form of Raas or Garba and is inspired by Lord Krishna's Raas Leela. The dance is not only popular in Gujarat but also across India. Dandiya involves energetic movements, rhythmic clashing of sticks, and vibrant music.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Dandiya dance mainly associated with? → Gujarat
☛ Which festival is Dandiya especially performed during? → Navratri
☛ What is the main prop used in Dandiya dance? → Sticks (Dandiyas)
☛ The Dandiya dance is inspired by the Raas Leela of which deity? → Lord Krishna
☛ What is the difference between Garba and Dandiya? → Garba is performed in a circular motion while Dandiya uses sticks

q: Lavani is the most famous folk dance style of ___________.
qs.e: Lavani is the most famous folk dance style of Maharashtra. It is primarily performed by women, featuring fast-paced dance and songs accompanied by the beats of a dholak. The term 'Lavani' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Lavanya', meaning beauty. This dance form gained popularity during the Peshwa era in the 18th century. Lavani songs often revolve around themes of love, politics, or social issues. Its distinct feature is the rapid tempo and rhythmic footwork. It remains an integral part of Maharashtra's cultural identity.

☛ During which period did Lavani gain popularity? → Peshwa era (18th century)

q: Triangle mudra is associated with which dance form?
qs.e: The triangle mudra is a fundamental element of the Odissi dance form. Odissi is a classical dance from Odisha, characterized by the tribhanga (three-curve) posture involving the head, torso, and legs. This mudra enhances the grace and fluidity of the dance. Odissi originated from the temple dance tradition dedicated to Lord Jagannath. Among the other options, Kuchipudi belongs to Andhra Pradesh, Mohiniyattam to Kerala, and Kathak to North India, but the triangle mudra is specifically associated with Odissi.
qs.kf:

☛ How many classical dances are recognized in India? → 8
☛ Which state does Kuchipudi dance belong to? → Andhra Pradesh

q: Which of the following is popular folk dance of the state of Gujarat?
qs.e: The most popular folk dance of Gujarat is Garba. It is traditionally performed during the festival of Navratri, where women dressed in colorful attire dance in circles around an earthen lamp or an idol of the goddess. Garba is dedicated to Goddess Durga and symbolizes power and fertility. The word 'Garba' derives from the Sanskrit word 'Garbha', meaning womb. The dance reflects the rich culture and tradition of Gujarat. Other options: Ras Leela is from Uttar Pradesh, Bardo Chum is Tibetan, and Muffler is not a dance.
qs.kf:

☛ Festival associated with Garba → Navratri
☛ Deity worshipped during Garba → Goddess Durga
☛ Origin of the word Garba → Sanskrit
☛ Formation in Garba dance → Circular

q: Chakayar Kuthu is a famous dance style
qs.e: Chakayar Kuthu is an ancient and traditional dance style of Kerala, India. It is primarily performed in Hindu temples and is considered an excellent blend of dance and acting. This dance form is mentioned in ancient texts and symbolizes the rich cultural heritage of Kerala. Chakayar Kuthu is mainly performed by the Chakyar community, a traditional artist community in Kerala. This dance style is distinct from other Kerala dance forms like Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Chakayar Kuthu emphasizes storytelling and music. While not recognized by UNESCO, it holds a unique place among Indian classical dances. The dance involves elaborate costumes and expressions and is often accompanied by percussion instruments like mizhavu.

☛ Which state's dance style is Chakayar Kuthu? → Kerala

q: Which of the following states is the traditional folk dance of Dandiya Ras?
qs.e: Dandiya Ras is a traditional folk dance of Gujarat, primarily performed during the Navratri festival. Dancers use colorful sticks (dandiyas) and move in rhythmic steps. This dance is associated with Lord Krishna and his Rasleela. Although it is also popular in Rajasthan and Maharashtra, its origin is in Gujarat. Dandiya Ras is often coupled with Garba, where Garba involves circling an earthen lamp, while Dandiya is performed with sticks.

☛ Which festival is Dandiya Ras associated with? → Navratri

☛ Difference between Garba and Dandiya? → Garba is around a lamp, Dandiya uses sticks

name: Set 2 · Q50–98
sub: Arts & Culture - Classical Dances & Folk Dances

q: Which of the following classical dance is based on Hindustani music?
qs.e: Kathak is a major classical dance form of India that is based on the Hindustani music tradition of North India. This dance style developed in the Mughal courts and emphasizes rhythm and footwork. Kathak involves storytelling through expressions and gestures. Other options like Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, and Kathakali are classical dances of South India and are based on Carnatic music. Kathak is performed with Hindustani classical music, distinguishing it from other classical dances.
qs.kf:
☛ Classical dance based on Hindustani music → Kathak
☛ Kathak developed in which courts → Mughal courts
☛ Main instruments used in Kathak → Tabla and Pakhavaj
☛ Famous Kathak dancer → Birju Maharaj
☛ Region of origin of Kathak → North India

q: Which is the popular mask dance of Sikkim?
qs.e: The popular mask dance of Sikkim is Singhhi Chham, a traditional Buddhist dance also known as the Lion Dance. Performers wear lion masks and costumes, dancing to the rhythm of drums and cymbals. This dance is usually performed during festivals like Losar (Tibetan New Year) and other celebratory occasions along the banks of the Teesta River. Among the other options, Thang Ta is a Manipuri martial art dance, Kumami is a folk dance of Uttarakhand, and Zumar is a dance from Assam. Singhhi Chham reflects Sikkim's rich cultural heritage and Buddhist traditions.

q: Birju Maharaj is a renowned virtuoso in which dance form?
qs.e: Birju Maharaj is the most famous exponent of the Kathak dance form. He belongs to the Lucknow gharana and his father Acchan Maharaj was also a renowned Kathak dancer. Birju Maharaj brought global recognition to Kathak and was honored with the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. Kathak is a major classical dance form of North India that evolved in the Mughal courts. It emphasizes rhythm, footwork, expression, and storytelling. Birju Maharaj is noted for his mastery of abhinaya and rhythmic patterns.
qs.kf:
☛ Birju Maharaj belongs to → Lucknow gharana
☛ His father's name → Acchan Maharaj
☛ Highest civilian award received by him → Padma Vibhushan
☛ Key features of Kathak → Rhythm and expression
☛ Kathak developed during → Mughal period

q: Ghoomar is a traditional as well as an enthusiastic folk dance of-
qs.e: Ghoomar is a famous traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, mainly performed by the Bhil community and Rajput women. The dance is known for its swirling movements and colorful attire. It is specially performed during festivals and weddings. The origin of Ghoomar dance is believed to be from the Marwar region (Jodhpur). Women perform it in groups accompanied by songs. This dance is a symbol of Rajasthan's culture and tradition.
qs.kf:
☛ Ghoomar dance belongs to which state? → Rajasthan
☛ Which community is associated with Ghoomar dance? → Bhil community
☛ From which region did Ghoomar originate? → Marwar (Jodhpur)

q: Which of the following is a dance drama?
qs.e: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from Kerala, India. The word 'Kathakali' means 'story play', combining 'katha' (story) and 'kali' (play/drama). It is a synthesis of dance, music, and acting, where performers enact stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas using elaborate makeup, costumes, and facial expressions. Kathakali is considered a dance drama because it is narrative-driven, unlike pure dance forms. The other options—Kathak (a classical dance from North India), Odissi (dance from Odisha), and Manipuri (dance from Manipur)—are primarily dance forms, not dance-dramas.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Kathakali dance-drama associated with? → Kerala
☛ Main instruments used in Kathakali? → Chenda (drum) and Idakka
☛ Types of acting in Kathakali? → Facial and eye expressions
☛ Dominant rasas in Kathakali? → Raudra (fury) and Veera (valor)
☛ Famous exponent of Kathakali? → Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair

q: 'Ottan Thullal' is a dance form of -
qs.e: Ottan Thullal is a popular dance form of Kerala, developed in the 18th century by poet Kunchan Nambiar. It resembles Kathakali and Mohiniyattam but emphasizes humor and satire. The performer sings and dances simultaneously, while background music is provided. It is part of Kerala's rich cultural heritage and is often performed in temples and festivals.

☛ Which is the classical dance of Kerala? → Kathakali
☛ In which century was Ottan Thullal developed? → 18th century

q: Bhangara is a folk dance of-
qs.e: Bhangara is a famous folk dance of Punjab, primarily performed during the harvest festival of Baisakhi in the spring season. This dance is a symbol of Punjabi culture and is performed by men to the beat of the dhol. Bhangara enjoys immense popularity not only in India but across the world. The dance is associated with agriculture and the harvesting of crops. Other folk dances of Punjab include Gidda (performed by women) and Jhumar. Bhangara gained international recognition after being incorporated into pop music in the 1990s.

☛ Which festival is associated with Bhangara? → Baisakhi
☛ What is the main musical instrument used in Bhangara? → Dhol

☛ What is the main crop of Punjab? → Wheat

q: 'Kaikottikali', a famous dance form originated in -
qs.e: Kaikottikali is a famous folk dance form from Kerala, predominantly performed by women during festivals like Onam. The dance is performed in a circle, with dancers clapping their hands and singing songs. The name 'Kaikottikali' is derived from 'kai' (hand) and 'kottikali' (clapping). It is part of Kerala's rich cultural heritage and distinct from other South Indian states.
qs.kf:
☛ Kaikottikali belongs to which state? → Kerala
☛ What instrument is used in Kaikottikali? → Hands (clapping)

☛ Famous dances of Kerala? → Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Kaikottikali

q: With which of the following dances is Rajendra Gangani associated?
qs.e: Rajendra Gangani is a renowned Kathak dancer from India. He was born in the Jaipur Gharana and learned Kathak from Pandit Kundanlal Gangani. He is a leading exponent of the Jaipur Gharana of Kathak. Rajendra Gangani has been honored with the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award by the Government of India. He has contributed to global recognition of Kathak through innovative experiments within the classical dance form.

☛ Which Gharana does Rajendra Gangani belong to? → Jaipur Gharana
☛ Who was the guru of Rajendra Gangani? → Pandit Kundanlal Gangani
☛ Which awards have been given to Rajendra Gangani? → Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award
☛ What are the major Gharanas of Kathak dance? → Jaipur, Lucknow, Benares

q: Kalaripayattu is:
o: Martial arts and warfare of Kerala
qs.e: Kalaripayattu is one of the oldest martial arts in India, originating in Kerala. This warfare art focuses on physical fitness, flexibility, and self-defense. It includes the use of weapons such as swords, shields, spears, and maces. Kalaripayattu has two major styles: the Northern style (Vadakkan) emphasizing weapons, and the Southern style (Thekkan) focusing on hand-to-hand combat. It is not only a combat art but also recognized as an art form and exercise system. It is an integral part of Kerala's cultural heritage and is famous worldwide.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state's martial art is Kalaripayattu? → Kerala
☛ What is the Northern style of Kalaripayattu called? → Vadakkan
☛ What is the Southern style of Kalaripayattu called? → Thekkan
☛ What are the main weapons used in Kalaripayattu? → Sword, shield, spear, mace
☛ What is the primary purpose of Kalaripayattu? → Self-defense and physical development

q: 'Gatka' is a martial art. It is related to which state?
qs.e: Gatka is a traditional martial art primarily associated with the state of Punjab. It is an ancient fighting style of the Sikh warriors, involving the use of sticks, swords, and shields. The history of Gatka is linked to the Sikh Gurus, especially Guru Hargobind Sahib and Guru Gobind Singh Ji, who emphasized combat training. Today, Gatka is performed during Sikh festivals such as Hola Mohalla and other traditional events. It is not just a physical skill but also a means of teaching self-defense and discipline.
qs.kf:
☛ Gatka is associated with which state? → Punjab
☛ What weapons are used in Gatka? → Sticks, swords, shields
☛ Gatka is the martial art of which religion? → Sikhism
☛ Which Sikh Gurus are linked to Gatka? → Guru Hargobind Sahib and Guru Gobind Singh Ji
☛ Which festival is associated with Gatka? → Hola Mohalla

q: Which of the following statements is correct about Kati Bihu, one of the three Bihus celebrated especially in the state of Assam?
o: Kati Bihu is also known as Rangali Bihu.
Kati Bihu marks the beginning of sowing by farmers.
Kati Bihu marks the season of harvesting.
Kati Bihu is observed to pray for standing crops.
qs.e: Assam celebrates three Bihus: Bohag Bihu (Rangali Bihu), Kati Bihu (Kongali Bihu), and Magh Bihu (Bhogali Bihu). Kati Bihu is also called Kongali Bihu, meaning 'poor Bihu', as it falls during a period of food scarcity. This festival is observed in October-November when standing crops (like paddy) require care. Farmers light lamps near Tulsi plants and offer prayers for the protection and good yield of crops. Thus, Kati Bihu is a festival of prayer for standing crops, not for sowing or harvesting.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the three Bihus of Assam? → Bohag (Rangali), Kati (Kongali), Magh (Bhogali)
☛ What is another name for Kati Bihu? → Kongali Bihu
☛ What season does Rangali Bihu mark? → Spring and the start of the new year
☛ What is Bhogali Bihu associated with? → Harvest and feasting
☛ Which plant is lit with a lamp during Kati Bihu? → Tulsi plant

q: Rahul Acharya is a famous _____ dancer.
qs.e: Rahul Acharya is a famous Odissi dancer. Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha. This dance style is known for its distinctive Tribhangi posture and expressive gestures. Rahul Acharya has been awarded the Padma Shri for his contributions to Odissi dance. He has brought global recognition to this classical dance form.

☛ Where did Odissi dance originate? → Odisha
☛ What is the distinctive posture of Odissi dance? → Tribhangi
☛ Which award was given to Rahul Acharya? → Padma Shri
☛ How many classical dances are there in India? → Eight
☛ Which deity is primarily worshipped in Odissi dance? → Jagannath

q: Bimbava Devi is a famous _____ dancer.
qs.e: Bimbavati Devi is a famous Manipuri dancer. She was honored with India's prestigious Padma Shri award. Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dances of India, originating from the state of Manipur. This dance form is known for its soft and fluid movements, with Ras Leela and Lai Haraoba being prominent styles. Bimbavati Devi has made significant contributions to the preservation and promotion of this dance form.
qs.kf:
☛ Where did Manipuri dance originate? → Manipur
☛ Major festival associated with Manipuri dance? → Ras Purnima
☛ Main style of Manipuri dance? → Ras Leela
☛ Which award did Bimbavati Devi receive? → Padma Shri
☛ How many classical dances are there in India? → Eight

q: Which of the following dance forms evolved from Assam?
qs.e: Sattriya is a classical dance form that evolved in the state of Assam. It was introduced by the great Vaishnava saint Sankardev in the 15th century. The dance developed in the Sattras (Vaishnava monasteries) of Assam, hence the name Sattriya. It was officially recognized as a classical dance by the Government of India in 2000. The themes are primarily based on the Bhagavata Purana and Krishna Leela. Both male and female dancers perform it. A unique feature is the use of masks to depict characters. Other options: Kuchipudi is from Andhra Pradesh, Kathakali from Kerala, and Kathak from North India.

☛ Founder of Sattriya dance → Sankardev

☛ Folk dances of Assam → Bihu, Bagurumba

q: Jabro dance is a nomadic dance of ___________.
qs.e: Jabro dance is a famous nomadic dance of Ladakh. It is performed by the Changpa tribe, who are nomadic yak herders. This dance is especially performed during festivals and celebrations. Dancers wear traditional costumes and use masks made of yak skin. The dance symbolizes their culture and tradition. Ladakh is known for its rich cultural heritage and various folk dances.

☛ Jabro dance is associated with which tribe → Changpa tribe
