☛ What is the meaning of 'Singhchalam'? → Lion hill
☛ Which architectural style is the Singhchalam temple built in? → Kalinga style

q: Which of the following temples is famous for the erotic composition?
qs.e: Khajuraho Temple is located in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh. It is world-famous for its erotic sculptures. Built by the Chandela dynasty between 950 and 1050 CE, these temples are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The walls are adorned with carvings inspired by the Kama Sutra. The Martand Sun Temple in Kashmir is dedicated to the Sun God. The Kamakhya Temple in Assam is a Shakti Peeth. The Dilwara Temple in Rajasthan is a Jain temple known for its marble craftsmanship.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dynasty built the Khajuraho temples? → Chandela dynasty
☛ How many temples are there in Khajuraho? → About 25 temples
☛ Which is the largest temple in Khajuraho? → Kandariya Mahadeva Temple
☛ Khajuraho is located on the banks of which river? → Betwa River
☛ Which deities are the Khajuraho temples dedicated to? → Shiva, Vishnu, and Jain Tirthankaras

q: The entrances to South Indian temples are called ________.
qs.e: The entrances to South Indian temples are called Gopurams. These are large, ornate, pyramid-like structures located at the main gateway of the temple. Gopuram is a key element of Dravidian architecture, developed during the Chola, Pandya, and Vijayanagara dynasties. They are richly carved with images of gods, goddesses, mythological scenes, and demons. Famous examples include the gopurams of Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, Thanjavur Brihadeeswara Temple, and Srirangam Temple. The gopuram serves as the main entrance and is often the most prominent part of the temple complex, rising high above the surrounding structures.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the entrance of South Indian temples called? → Gopuram
☛ Which architectural style features gopurams? → Dravidian architecture
☛ Which dynasties promoted gopuram construction? → Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara
☛ What is carved on gopurams? → Deities and mythological stories
☛ Which temple in Madurai has famous gopurams? → Meenakshi Temple

q: In the architecture, the Panchayat style is related to the term ________.
qs.e: In Indian architecture, the Panchayat style is related to temples. This style is primarily found in Kerala, where a temple consists of five parts: garbhagriha, antarala, mandapa, nritya mandapa, and bali pitha. The term 'Panchayat' is derived from 'five' and 'ayat', meaning a group of five temples or five features. This style is an important concept in South Indian temple architecture, symbolizing the Panchabhuta (five elements). Temples built in Panchayat style follow the rules of Vastushastra and Agama Shastras. Hence, the Panchayat style is related to the term temple.
qs.kf:
☛ Panchayat style is associated with which architecture? → Temple architecture
☛ Panchayat style is mainly found in which state? → Kerala
☛ How many parts does the Panchayat style temple have? → Five
☛ What is the meaning of the term 'Panchayat'? → Five enclosures or group of five temples
☛ What does the Panchayat style symbolize? → Panchabhuta (five elements)

q: The Kendaria Mahadev Temple in Khajuraho is dedicated to Lord ________.
qs.e: The Kandariya Mahadev Temple in Khajuraho is dedicated to Lord Shiva (Shankar). Built by the Chandela dynasty in the 11th century, it is one of the largest and most ornate temples in Khajuraho. The temple is renowned for its Nagara style architecture and erotic sculptures. It was constructed by King Vidhyadhara. The name 'Kandariya' means 'cave' and 'Mahadev' refers to Shiva, symbolizing the lord dwelling in a cave. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Khajuraho temples. The temple stands on the banks of the Banaganga River.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Kandariya Mahadev Temple located? → Khajuraho
☛ Which dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadev Temple? → Chandela dynasty
☛ What is the architectural style of Kandariya Mahadev Temple? → Nagara style
☛ In which century was Kandariya Mahadev Temple built? → 11th century
☛ Which river flows near Kandariya Mahadev Temple? → Banaganga River

q: The famous 'Seven Hills' temple is situated in which state?
qs.e: The famous 'Seven Hills' temple is the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, located in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh. This temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is called the 'Seven Hills temple' because it is surrounded by seven hills. It is one of the richest temples in the world and is managed by the Titumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD). Thousands of devotees visit daily for darshan.

☛ Which river is Tirupati located on? → Swarnamukhi River
☛ Famous prasadam of Tirumala temple? → Laddu

q: In which state, the Virupaksha temple is located?
qs.e: The Virupaksha Temple is located in the Bellary district of Karnataka state, specifically in the historical site of Hampi. This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and was built during the Vijayanagara Empire. It is renowned for its Dravidian-style architecture. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and lies on the banks of the Tungabhadra River. The Virupaksha Temple is one of the most prominent temples of the Vijayanagara Empire and has been an important pilgrimage site for centuries.

q: World heritage site 'Ellora Caves' is situated in which state?
qs.e: The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the state of Maharashtra, India, specifically in the Aurangabad district. They were inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1983. The site comprises 34 caves, representing Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain traditions. The most notable is the Kailash Temple (Cave 16), which is a monolithic rock-cut structure. The Ellora Caves are renowned for their exquisite architecture and sculptures, showcasing the artistic excellence of ancient India.

☛ Which cave houses the Kailash Temple? → Cave 16

☛ Which religions are represented in Ellora? → Buddhism, Hinduism, Jainism

q: Amravati style of architecture is associated with which of these states?
qs.e: The Amravati style of architecture is associated with Andhra Pradesh. This style is famous for Buddhist stupas and sculptures. The Amaravati Stupa, located in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh, was a significant center of Buddhist art. This style developed during the Satavahana and Ikshvaku periods. It is characterized by intricate carvings and delicate designs on marble stones. The Amaravati school of art is preserved by the Archaeological Survey of India.
qs.kf:

q: Konark Sun Temple is located in ______.
qs.e: The Konark Sun Temple is located in the state of Odisha, India, built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. This temple is dedicated to the Sun God and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is architecturally designed as a giant chariot with 12 pairs of wheels and seven horses. The temple's name combines 'kona' (meaning angle) and 'arka' (meaning sun). It is oriented eastwards so that the first rays of the sun strike the main entrance. The temple is renowned for its exquisite stone carvings and sculptures, depicting various aspects of life and mythology.

☛ What is the shape of the temple? → Chariot shape

q: Kalbelia, the UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage from ______ state.
qs.e: Kalbelia is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan state in India, also known as the Snake Dance. It is primarily performed by the Kalbelia tribe, which is traditionally involved in catching snakes and trading their venom. In this dance, women wear black swirling skirts and move gracefully imitating the movements of snakes. It was inscribed in the year 2010 by UNESCO on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. This dance symbolizes the rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan and efforts have been made to preserve this unique tradition. The dance is accompanied by the been (a wind instrument) and is an integral part of the community's identity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is famous for Kalbelia dance → Rajasthan
☛ Kalbelia dance is performed by which tribe → Kalbelia tribe
☛ In which year was Kalbelia recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage → 2010
☛ What is the other name for Kalbelia dance → Snake Dance
☛ What instrument accompanies Kalbelia dance → Been (wind instrument)

q: 'Monument symbols in Hampi' In which state is the World Heritage Site located?
qs.e: The group of monuments at Hampi is located in the state of Karnataka, in the Vijayanagara district. It was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, which flourished from the 14th to the 16th century. The site was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986. Key monuments include the Vitthala Temple, Hazara Rama Temple, Lotus Mahal, and Krishna Temple. The Virupaksha Temple is an important active worship site. Hampi is situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River and is often called the 'City of Ruins'.

☛ In which district is Hampi located? → Vijayanagara district

q: In which state is the Bhormadeva Temple situated?
qs.e: The Bhormadeva Temple is located in the Kabirdham district of Chhattisgarh state. It is often called the 'Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh'. The temple is built in the Nagara style of architecture and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It was constructed by the Kalachuri kings in the 11th century. The temple walls are adorned with exquisite carvings and sculptures. It is protected as a monument of national importance.
qs.kf:

q: The wing style of architecture is related to which of the following states?
qs.e: Wing style of architecture is associated with West Bengal. Also known as Bangla roof or Do-chala, this style is prominently seen in temples and houses. Its characteristic curved roof resembles a bird's wing. This style developed in the Bengal region to protect against heavy rain and humidity. Notable examples include Dakshineswar Kali Temple and the temples of Bishnupur. The wing style is a defining feature of Bengali culture and architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is associated with wing style architecture? → West Bengal
☛ Which style includes Bangla roof? → Wing style
☛ Temples of Bishnupur are built in which style? → Wing style

q: Where is Angkor Wat Temple located?
qs.e: Angkor Wat Temple is located in Cambodia, within the Angkor region. It was built in the 12th century by King Suryavarman II and dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu. It is the largest religious monument in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The temple's architecture is an excellent example of Khmer Empire art. Initially a Hindu temple, it later transformed into a Buddhist temple.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country is Angkor Wat in? → Cambodia
☛ Who built Angkor Wat? → Suryavarman II
☛ Which god is it dedicated to? → Vishnu
☛ In which century was it built? → 12th
☛ Which empire's art does it represent? → Khmer Empire

q: In which of the following cities is the Palitana temple located?
qs.e: The Palitana temple is located in the Bhavnagar district of Gujarat, India. It is a major Jain pilgrimage site situated on the Shatrunjaya hill. The complex comprises over 900 marble temples, mostly built in white marble. This sacred place is associated with Rishabhdev, the first Tirthankara of Jainism. Palitana is considered a holy land for Jain Tirthankaras and attracts thousands of devotees annually. The temple cluster is a renowned heritage site known for its exquisite architecture and spiritual significance.
qs.kf:
☛ Palitana temple is located in which state? → Gujarat
☛ On which hill is Palitana situated? → Shatrunjaya hill
☛ How many temples are in Palitana? → Over 900
☛ Palitana temple belongs to which religion? → Jainism
☛ What material are Palitana temples made of? → White marble

q: The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur marks the greatest achievement of the architects of the ______ dynasty.
qs.e: The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur was built by Raja Raja Chola I of the Chola dynasty in the 11th century. It is considered the greatest achievement of Chola architecture. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Its massive gopuram and 66-meter tall vimana represent the excellence of the Chola style. The Chola kings promoted temple construction and played a significant role in preserving art and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is the Brihadeeswarar Temple located? → Kaveri River
☛ Who built the Brihadeeswarar Temple? → Raja Raja Chola I

☛ What was the capital of the Chola dynasty? → Thanjavur
☛ What is the name of the main deity of the Brihadeeswarar Temple? → Brihadeeswarar (Shiva)

q: Which of the following temples is located in Odisha ?
o: Both Konark Sun Temple and Puri Jagannath Temple
qs.e: Odisha is home to several famous temples, most notably the Puri Jagannath Temple and the Konark Sun Temple. Puri Jagannath Temple, dedicated to Lord Jagannath, is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites. Konark Sun Temple, also known as the 'Black Pagoda', is dedicated to the Sun God and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Brihadeeswarar Temple is located in Tamil Nadu, not Odisha. Hence, both temples in Odisha are correctly identified.

q: Where is the statue depicting Ravana shaking Mount Kailash found?
qs.e: The famous depiction of Ravana shaking Mount Kailash is found in the Ellora Caves, specifically in Cave 14, known as Ravana ki Khai. Located in Aurangabad district, Maharashtra, Ellora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The scene illustrates an episode from the Shiva Purana where Ravana attempts to lift Mount Kailash, and Lord Shiva subdues him by pressing the mountain with his toe. Ellora Caves are renowned for their Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist rock-cut architecture. This sculpture highlights both Ravana's might and Shiva's supremacy.
qs.kf:

q: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus is a prime example of which of the following types of architectural style?
qs.e: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus), located in Mumbai, is a prime example of the Indo-Saracenic architectural style. This style blends Indian, Islamic, and Gothic elements. The station was designed by British architect Frederick William Stevens. It features Gothic arches, Islamic domes, and Indian carved pillars. In 2004, it was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This style became popular in British India during the late 19th century. Other notable examples of Indo-Saracenic architecture include the Chennai High Court and the Mysore Palace.
qs.kf:
☛ Which architectural style is exemplified by Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus? → Indo-Saracenic
☛ What was the former name of this station? → Victoria Terminus
☛ Who was the architect of this building? → Frederick William Stevens
☛ In which year was it declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 2004
☛ Give another example of Indo-Saracenic architecture. → Chennai High Court or Mysore Palace

q: Which of the following is a common feature of Dravidian temples?
qs.e: The most distinctive feature of Dravidian temples is the Gopuram, a massive, ornate tower at the entrance. These towers are pyramidal in shape and heavily decorated with sculptures. In Dravidian architecture, the sanctum sanctorum is topped by a vimana, similar to a sikhara, but the gopuram is at the entrance. Other options: pillarless hall is not typical; Dravidian temples have pillared halls called mandapas; sikhara is characteristic of Nagara style; flat roof is not common. The Gopuram is a hallmark of Dravidian architecture and is common in South Indian temples.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the entrance tower of a Dravidian temple called? → Gopuram
☛ What is the structure above the sanctum called? → Vimana
☛ What is the topmost part of a Nagara temple called? → Sikhara
☛ What is the assembly hall in a Dravidian temple called? → Mandapa
☛ Brihadeeswara Temple is built in which style? → Dravidian

q: Which architectural style characterises the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) building in Mumbai, India, completed in 1887?
qs.e: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), formerly known as Victoria Terminus, was completed in 1887. The building is characterized by the Victorian Gothic architectural style, a prominent example of British architecture. This style features high spires, pointed arches, and ornate decorations. The designer of CSMT was the British architect Frederick William Stevens. This building is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It presents a unique blend of Victorian Gothic style with traditional Indian motifs. Mughal and Rajput styles are indigenous to India, while Indo-Saracenic style is not applied to this building.
qs.kf:
☛ Architectural style of CSMT building → Victorian Gothic
☛ Designer of CSMT → Frederick William Stevens
☛ Old name of CSMT → Victoria Terminus
☛ UNESCO status of CSMT → World Heritage Site
☛ Year of completion of CSMT → 1887

q: Which architectural style characterises the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) building in Mumbai, India, completed in 1887?
qs.e: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) in Mumbai is a historic railway station completed in 1887. Its architecture is characterized by the Victorian Gothic style, featuring pointed arches, spires, stained glass windows, and intricate carvings. The design was created by British architect Frederick William Stevens. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is a prime example of British colonial architecture in India. The Indo-Saracenic style blends Indian and Islamic elements, while Mughal and Rajput styles are distinct. CSMT's Victorian Gothic design reflects the 19th-century Gothic Revival movement adapted for a modern railway station.

q: What is the total number of cave structures at the Ajanta Caves location in Maharashtra, India, including the one that was never completed?
qs.e: The Ajanta Caves are located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, India, and are associated with Buddhist religion. There are a total of 30 caves, including one that was never completed. These caves were constructed between approximately 2nd century BCE and 6th century CE. Ajanta Caves are renowned for their paintings and sculptures and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The cave structures include both chaityas (prayer halls) and viharas (monasteries). The incomplete cave is also counted among these 30 structures.

☛ Total number of Ajanta Caves → 30
☛ Religion associated with Ajanta Caves → Buddhism
☛ State where Ajanta Caves are located → Maharashtra
☛ Period of construction of Ajanta Caves → approximately 2nd century BCE to 6th century CE
☛ UNESCO status of Ajanta Caves → World Heritage Site

q: Which architectural style, introduced by the British, combines Indian traditional elements with Gothic, Victorian and Neo-Classical forms?
qs.e: The Indo-Saracenic architectural style was developed during the British colonial period in India. It blends traditional Indian elements such as chhatris, jali windows, and domes with Gothic, Victorian, and Neo-Classical forms. This style aimed to symbolize the fusion of Indian culture and British colonial power. Notable examples include the Madras High Court in Chennai, the Victoria Memorial in Kolkata, and the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai. It gained prominence in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

☛ Which Indian elements are included in this style? → Chhatris and jali windows
☛ During which period was Indo-Saracenic popular? → Late 19th to early 20th century

q: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora is an example of which of the following types of architecture?
qs.e: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora is a prime example of rock-cut architecture. It is carved out of a single rock and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It was built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE. The temple is renowned for its massive size, intricate carvings, and unique architectural style. The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and include temples associated with Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism. The Kailasa Temple is considered one of the largest rock-cut temples in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Which king built the Kailasa Temple at Ellora? → Krishna I (Rashtrakuta)
☛ Which god is the Kailasa Temple dedicated to? → Shiva
☛ In which state are the Ellora Caves located? → Maharashtra
☛ Total number of caves at Ellora? → 34
☛ Which is the largest temple at Ellora? → Kailasa Temple

q: Which of the following styles of temple architecture is predominantly found in North India?
qs.e: The Nagara style of temple architecture is predominantly found in North India. Its main feature is the shikhara (a tall, curved or straight spire) over the sanctum. The sanctum is usually square-shaped with a circumambulatory path. Prominent examples include Khajuraho temples, Konark Sun Temple, and Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar. The Dravidian style is prevalent in South India, Vesara is a mix of Nagara and Dravidian found in Central India, and Baroque is a European style.
qs.kf:
☛ Key element of Nagara style → Shikhara
☛ Khajuraho temples belong to which style → Nagara style
☛ Where is Dravidian style found → South India
☛ Vesara style is a blend of → Nagara and Dravidian
☛ Location of Konark Sun Temple → Odisha

q: To which group of temples does Kandariya Mahadev Temple belong?
qs.e: The Kandariya Mahadev Temple belongs to the Khajuraho group of temples. It is the largest and most famous temple in the Khajuraho complex. Built by King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty around 1025-1050 CE, this temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is renowned for its magnificent architecture, intricate carvings, and the Nagara style of temple architecture. The Khajuraho group of temples is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, comprising about 20 temples. The Kandariya Mahadev Temple includes a grand shikhara (spire), beautifully carved pillars, and numerous sculptures depicting various deities and mythological scenes. It is located in the Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadev Temple? → Chandela dynasty
☛ Who built the Kandariya Mahadev Temple? → Dhangadeva
☛ Which god is the Kandariya Mahadev Temple dedicated to? → Lord Shiva
☛ What architectural style is the Kandariya Mahadev Temple? → Nagara style
☛ Where is the Khajuraho temple group located? → Madhya Pradesh

q: The style of temple architecture that became popular in Northern India is known as:
qs.e: In Northern India, the Nagara style of temple architecture became popular. This style is characterized by a curvilinear or conical shikhara (spire) directly above the sanctum. Nagara temples are generally open on all sides with the entrance facing east or west. This style evolved from the Gupta period and reached its peak during the medieval period. Prominent examples include the Khajuraho temples and the Sun Temple, Konark. Nagara style is further classified into three sub-styles: Lata, Shekhari, and Bhumija. In contrast, the Dravida style belongs to South India, Vesara is a mixed style, and Gupta style is an early phase. The Nagara style emphasizes verticality and intricate carvings, often featuring a mandapa (pillared hall) and a garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum).
qs.kf:
☛ Northern Indian temple architecture style → Nagara
☛ Characteristic of Nagara style → Curvilinear shikhara
☛ Example of Nagara style → Khajuraho temples
☛ Southern Indian style → Dravida
☛ Mixed style → Vesara

q: Which part of a Hindu temple incorporates space for large number of worshippers?
qs.e: In Hindu temple architecture, the Mandapa is the pillared hall or pavilion that accommodates a large number of worshippers. It is situated between the Garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum) and the entrance of the temple. The mandapa is used for religious rituals, prayers, and cultural gatherings. In contrast, the Garbhagriha is small and accessible only to priests. The Shikhar is the spire or tower over the sanctum, while Vimana refers to the tower above the sanctum in South Indian temples. Thus, the mandapa serves as the congregation hall for devotees.
qs.kf:
☛ Most sacred part of a Hindu temple → Garbhagriha
☛ Hall where devotees gather in a temple → Mandapa
☛ Spire or tower of a temple → Shikhar
☛ Tower above sanctum in South Indian temples → Vimana
☛ Meaning of Garbhagriha → Womb-chamber, housing the main deity

q: In which state of India can we find the preserved Buddhist caves called 'Karla'?
qs.e: The Karla Caves are ancient Buddhist caves located in the Pune district of Maharashtra, India. These caves are about 2000 years old and belong to the Hinayana sect of Buddhism. They feature a large chaitya griha (stupa worship hall), which is considered one of the oldest and largest chaitya caves in India. The architecture of the Karla Caves is unique, with intricate carvings and inscriptions. These caves were situated on ancient trade routes, serving as rest stops for merchants and monks. The main cave is known for its elaborately carved entrance and a large stupa inside.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state are the Karla Caves located? → Maharashtra
☛ Which religion are the Karla Caves associated with? → Buddhism
☛ What is the main architectural feature of the Karla Caves? → Chaitya griha
☛ Which sect of Buddhism is linked to the Karla Caves? → Hinayana
☛ In which district are the Karla Caves situated? → Pune

q: What is the balcony-shaped structure on stupa known as?
qs.e: The balcony-shaped structure on a stupa is called Harmika. It is a square or rectangular platform at the top of the stupa, surrounded by a railing. Above the Harmika, the Chhatri (umbrella) is placed, which is the highest part of the stupa. Other parts of the stupa include the Anda (hemispherical dome), Yashti (central pillar), and Medhi (circumambulatory path). The Harmika is an important component of Buddhist stupa architecture, designed to resemble a balcony. This structure marks the sacred site of the stupa and aids in meditation focus.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the lowest part of a stupa called? → Medhi
☛ What is the dome-shaped part of a stupa called? → Anda
☛ What is the umbrella on top of a stupa called? → Chhatri
☛ What shape is a Harmika? → Square or rectangular
☛ What is Yashti? → The central pillar of a stupa

q: What is the name of the pillared hall at the front of a Hindu temple where devotees gather?
qs.e: In Hindu temple architecture, a Mandapa is a pillared hall located at the front of the temple, between the entrance and the Garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum). It serves as a gathering place for devotees for rituals, prayers, and religious activities. Mandapas are often open or semi-open structures with intricately carved pillars. The Garbhagriha is the innermost sanctum housing the main deity. Amalaka is a circular stone disc placed on top of the temple's shikhara (spire). Antarala is a narrow passage connecting the Garbhagriha and the Mandapa. Thus, the pillared hall where devotees gather is called Mandapa.
qs.kf:
☛ Most sacred part of temple → Garbhagriha
☛ Circular stone on spire → Amalaka
☛ Passage between Garbhagriha and Mandapa → Antarala

☛ Mandapa in Dravida style → Mandapa

q: What kind of architectural style is seen in the shikharas of the Jageshwar temple complexes in Uttarakhand, India?
qs.e: The Jageshwar temple complexes in Uttarakhand feature curvilinear (curvilinear) style shikharas. These shikharas are built above the sanctum sanctorum of the temple and have a curved shape. This style is more prevalent in North Indian temples. The Jageshwar temples are believed to have been built between the 7th and 13th centuries and are dedicated to Lord Shiva. The architecture of these temples is influenced by the Katyuri and Chand dynasties. The curvilinear shikharas represent the height of the temple and are adorned with intricate carvings.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Jageshwar temple located? → Uttarakhand
☛ Which deity is the Jageshwar temple dedicated to? → Shiva
☛ The architectural style of Jageshwar temples is influenced by which styles? → Katyuri and Chand styles
☛ Which style of shikhara is common in North Indian temples? → Curvilinear
☛ On the banks of which river is the Jageshwar temple situated? → Jataganga

q: Which of the following cities is known for its world famous Meenakshi Temple?
qs.e: The Meenakshi Temple is a historic Hindu temple located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (Parvati) and Lord Sundareshwar (Shiva). It was built in the 17th century by King Thirumalai Nayak. The temple is renowned for its towering gopurams, vibrant sculptures, and the hall of 985 pillars. It is an outstanding example of Dravidian architecture and is considered one of the grandest temples in the world. In contrast, Chidambaram is known for the Nataraja Temple, Thanjavur for the Brihadeeswarar Temple, and Tirupati for the Venkateswara Temple.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Meenakshi Temple located? → Madurai (Tamil Nadu)
☛ Meenakshi Temple is dedicated to which deities? → Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareshwar
☛ Which river flows through Madurai? → Vaigai River
☛ Who built the Meenakshi Temple? → King Thirumalai Nayak
☛ Meenakshi Temple is an example of which architecture? → Dravidian architecture

q: Which temple in Thanjavur has chola architecture and was built by Emperor Rajaraja?
qs.e: The Brihadisvara Temple, also known as Rajarajeswaram Temple, is located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu. It was built by Chola Emperor Rajaraja I between 1003 and 1010 CE. This temple is a prime example of Dravidian architecture and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The temple's vimana (tower) is 66 meters high, making it one of the tallest temple towers in the world. The temple houses a massive Shiva lingam carved from a single granite block. The Chola bronzes and mural paintings here reflect the artistic excellence of the period.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is the Brihadisvara Temple located on? → Kaveri River
☛ Which Chola ruler built the Brihadisvara Temple? → Rajaraja I
☛ What is the height of the Brihadisvara Temple vimana? → 66 meters
☛ In which year was the Brihadisvara Temple inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1987
☛ Who is the principal deity of the Brihadisvara Temple? → Shiva

q: Which group of monuments consists of the Vitthala Temple?
qs.e: The Vitthala Temple is located in Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Dedicated to Lord Vitthala (an incarnation of Vishnu), this temple is famous for its musical pillars and the stone chariot. The Group of Monuments at Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and includes over 1,600 remnants. The temple represents the finest example of Vijayanagara architecture and was built during the reign of Krishnadevaraya. Hampi's monuments showcase the grandeur of the empire, with the Vitthala Temple being a highlight due to its intricate carvings and innovative acoustic features.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is Hampi located? → Tungabhadra River
☛ What are the musical pillars of Vitthala Temple called? → Sarang pillars
☛ Who founded the Vijayanagara Empire? → Harihara and Bukka
☛ In which text is Hampi referred to as Vijayanagara? → 'Abhijnanashakuntalam'
☛ Which ruler built the Vitthala Temple? → Krishnadevaraya

q: What architectural style is the Meenakshi Amman Temple known for?
qs.e: The Meenakshi Amman Temple is located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, and is a prime example of the Dravidian architectural style. It was built during the 17th century under the Vijayanagara Empire. Key features of Dravidian style include tall gopurams (gateway towers), elaborate mandapas, and colorful sculptures. The temple has 14 gopurams, the tallest being the southern gopuram at 51.9 meters. The temple complex also contains the famous Hall of Thousand Pillars. It is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (Parvati) and Lord Sundareswarar (Shiva).
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Meenakshi Amman Temple located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the height of the tallest gopuram of the Meenakshi Temple? → 51.9 meters
☛ Which deities are worshipped at the Meenakshi Temple? → Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar
☛ Under which empire was the Meenakshi Temple built? → Vijayanagara Empire
☛ What is the entrance tower of a Dravidian-style temple called? → Gopuram

q: What is the meaning of 'gopuram' in temple architecture?
qs.e: Gopuram is a prominent element of South Indian temple architecture. It refers to a large, ornate gateway or entrance tower that stands at the entrance of a temple complex. Gopurams are typically tall, multi-storied structures decorated with intricate carvings of deities, mythological scenes, and geometric patterns. They are located along the path leading to the main sanctum and mark the boundary of the temple. The primary function of a gopuram is to separate the sacred space inside the temple from the outside world and to signify the beginning of the spiritual journey for devotees.
qs.kf:
☛ Which architectural style features gopurams? → Dravidian architecture
☛ Gopurams are the entrance towers of which temples? → South Indian temples
☛ What is the main function of a gopuram? → To separate sacred space from the outside world
☛ What carvings are found on gopurams? → Carvings of deities and mythological scenes
☛ What is the literal meaning of the word gopuram? → Door

q: Which feature of the 10th-century CE Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar reflects the Nagara architectural style?
qs.e: The Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar, built in the 10th century CE, is a prominent Shiva temple. Its curvilinear shikhara is a key feature of the Nagara style of architecture. In Nagara style, the shikhara rises upward in a curved manner. The temple's vimana is about 180 feet high. It is an excellent example of Kalinga architecture. A stepped pyramid vimana is characteristic of the Dravidian style. Ornate gopuram entrances are also found in Dravidian style. Circular stupa domes are associated with Buddhist or Jain architecture.
qs.kf:
☛ Shape of shikhara in Nagara style → Curvilinear
☛ Shape of vimana in Dravidian style → Stepped pyramid
☛ Period of Lingaraja Temple construction → 10th century CE
☛ Location of Lingaraja Temple → Bhubaneswar, Odisha
☛ Deity of Lingaraja Temple → Lord Shiva

q: Which temple's garbhagriha houses a Chaturmukha (four-faced) Vishnu image?
qs.e: The Lakshmana Temple, located in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh, was built by the Chandela dynasty. Its garbhagriha houses a rare Chaturmukha (four-faced) image of Lord Vishnu, showcasing exquisite craftsmanship. The temple is dedicated to Vishnu and is built in the Nagara style of architecture. The other options: Meenakshi Temple in Madurai is a Dravidian-style temple, Brihadiswara Temple in Thanjavur is dedicated to Shiva, and the Dashavatara Temple in Deogarh dates back to the Gupta period and is also Vaishnavite but not with a Chaturmukha image.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Lakshmana Temple located? → Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Which temple houses the Chaturmukha Vishnu image? → Lakshmana Temple, Khajuraho
☛ Who built the Lakshmana Temple? → Chandela king Yashovarman
☛ What is the architectural style of Lakshmana Temple? → Nagara style
☛ What are Khajuraho temples famous for? → Erotic sculptures

q: The widespread use of which architectural features distinguishes Mughal architecture from earlier trabeate temple construction?
qs.e: Mughal architecture is distinguished by its extensive use of arches and domes, unlike earlier trabeate temple construction which relied on horizontal beams placed on columns. The Mughal style introduced true arches and bulbous domes, often made of brick and mortar, and later marble. This technique derived from Persian and Central Asian traditions. Iconic Mughal structures like the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Jama Masjid showcase these features.
qs.kf:
☛ Key feature of Mughal architecture → Arches and domes
☛ Technique used in trabeate style → Columns and beams
☛ Primary building materials in Mughal architecture → Red sandstone and marble
☛ Architectural style of Taj Mahal → Mughal architecture
☛ Greatest influence on Mughal architecture → Persian architecture

name: Set 1 · Q1–26
sub: Arts & Culture - Festivals, Fairs, Languages & Literature

q: Which of the following states celebrates Hornbill festival every year?
qs.e: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated annually in the Indian state of Nagaland. Named after the state bird, the Hornbill, this festival is held from 1st to 10th December. It aims to promote and preserve the rich cultural heritage of the various tribes of Nagaland. The festival features traditional dances, music, sports, handicrafts exhibition, and local cuisine. It symbolizes the unity and cultural diversity of the Naga people. The Hornbill Festival is often called the "Festival of Festivals" and attracts tourists from around the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state celebrates Hornbill Festival? → Nagaland
☛ When is Hornbill Festival held? → 1-10 December
☛ What is the state bird of Nagaland? → Hornbill
☛ What is the capital of Nagaland? → Kohima
☛ Hornbill Festival is also known as? → Festival of Festivals

q: South Indian languages are related to which of the following language group?
qs.e: South Indian languages belong to the Dravidian language family. This is a major language family in India, which includes languages such as Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam. Dravidian languages are primarily spoken in South India, Sri Lanka, and some other regions. There are about 26 languages in this family in India. Tibeto-Burman, Austric, and Anglo-Indian are other language families that are not related to South Indian languages.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest language of Dravidian family → Tamil
☛ Most spoken Dravidian language → Telugu
☛ Total languages in Dravidian family → 26
☛ Main states where Dravidian languages are spoken → Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala
☛ Region outside India where Dravidian languages are spoken → Sri Lanka

q: Which of the following festivals is called the festival of colours?
qs.e: Holi is called the festival of colours. It is a major Hindu festival celebrated on the full moon day of the month of Phalguna. On this day, people play with coloured powders and water, hence it is known as the festival of colours. Holi also has religious significance - it is associated with the story of Prahlada and Holika, symbolising the victory of good over evil. Other options: Janmashtami is associated with Lord Krishna's birth, Durga Pooja worships Goddess Durga, and Dussehra marks the victory of Rama over Ravana; none of these are called the festival of colours.
qs.kf:
☛ In which month is Holi celebrated? → Phalguna month
☛ Which mythological story is associated with Holi? → Prahlada and Holika
☛ What is burnt during Holi? → Holika (effigy)
☛ What is the day after Holi called? → Dhulendi or Rangwali Holi
☛ What is the Sanskrit name of Holi? → Holikotsav

q: Hornbill festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
qs.e: The Hornbill festival is celebrated in the state of Nagaland. It is a major cultural festival held annually in the first week of December, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the Naga tribes. The festival is named after the Hornbill bird, which holds great significance in Naga culture. The event features traditional dances, music, games, and cuisine, promoting unity among the various tribes. It is often referred to as the "Festival of Festivals" and plays a crucial role in boosting tourism in the state.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Hornbill festival celebrated? → Nagaland
☛ In which month is it held? → December
☛ After which bird is it named? → Hornbill
☛ What is it also known as? → Festival of Festivals
☛ What type of festival is it? → Cultural

q: Losar festival is celebrated by which of the following religions?
qs.e: The Losar festival is the primary festival of Tibetan Buddhism, celebrated on the occasion of the New Year. It is mainly observed in Tibet, Nepal, Bhutan, and parts of North India. The word 'Losar' means 'New Year' – 'Lo' means year and 'Sar' means new. This festival is celebrated according to the Tibetan lunar calendar and includes family gatherings, special dishes, and religious rituals. Followers of Tibetan Buddhism celebrate this festival with great enthusiasm.
qs.kf:
☛ Which religion celebrates Losar? → Buddhism
☛ Where is Losar primarily celebrated? → Tibet, Nepal, Bhutan
☛ What does Losar mean? → New Year
☛ Which calendar is used for Losar? → Tibetan lunar calendar
☛ Major Buddhist festivals? → Losar, Buddha Purnima, Dhammachakra Pravartan Day

q: In India's cultural history, who belongs to the North, just like the Dravidians belong to the South?
qs.e: In India's cultural history, Indo-Aryans are associated with the North, just as the Dravidians are associated with the South. The Indo-Aryan language family originated in Central Asia and entered India around 1500 BCE. They laid the foundation of Vedic culture and developed the Sanskrit language. Dravidians are the indigenous people of South India, with languages like Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam. This division is based on linguistic and cultural differences. After the Vedic period, Indo-Aryans spread across northern India. Today, most languages in northern India belong to the Indo-Aryan family.
qs.kf:
☛ Major language family of North India → Indo-Aryan
☛ Major language family of South India → Dravidian
☛ Founders of Vedic culture → Indo-Aryans
☛ Oldest Dravidian language → Tamil
☛ Indo-Aryans arrived in India around → 1500 BCE

q: In the Punjabi festival of Lohri, which element of the nature worshipped?
qs.e: The famous Punjabi festival of Lohri is primarily associated with the worship of Fire. This festival marks the end of winter and the harvest season of Rabi crops. On the night of Lohri, people light a bonfire and perform rituals around it, offering prayers. The fire ritual is performed to wish for a good harvest and prosperity. Lohri is celebrated a day before Makar Sankranti. Offerings such as peanuts, rewri, sesame seeds, and jaggery are thrown into the fire as part of the tradition. The festival symbolizes gratitude towards nature and highlights the importance of fire as a source of energy and life.
qs.kf:
☛ Which element is worshipped in Lohri? → Fire
☛ Lohri marks the harvest of which crop season? → Rabi crops
☛ Which festival comes one day after Lohri? → Makar Sankranti
☛ What offerings are made to the fire in Lohri? → Sesame, jaggery, rewri
☛ Lohri is primarily a festival of which state? → Punjab

q: Which one of these is a harvest festival?
qs.e: Onam is a major harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated to commemorate the return of King Mahabali according to Hindu mythology. It falls in the month of Chingam (August-September) and lasts for 10 days. The festival includes Pookkalam (flower rangoli), Onam Sadya (feast), Vallamkali (boat race) and Kathakali dance. Other options - Teej (women's festival in Sawan), Janmashtami (Krishna's birth) and Deepawali (festival of lights) are not harvest festivals.
qs.kf:
☛ Harvest festival of Kerala → Onam
☛ Month of Onam celebration → Chingam (August-September)
☛ Mythological figure associated with Onam → King Mahabali
☛ Flower rangoli made during Onam → Pookkalam
☛ Special feast of Onam → Onam Sadya

q: “Gudi Padwa” is an auspicious day that marks the beginning of the traditional New Year for Marathi Hindus. Which Hindu month is it celebrated in?
qs.e: Gudi Padwa is the traditional Marathi Hindu New Year, celebrated on the Shukla Pratipada (first day of the bright fortnight) of the month of Chaitra. This day marks the beginning of the Hindu calendar year and is observed with great enthusiasm in Maharashtra. People erect a Gudi (a decorated pole with a silk cloth, neem leaves, and a garland) outside their homes to symbolize victory and prosperity. The festival also heralds the arrival of spring season. The other options – Vaisakha, Shravana, and Bhadra – are incorrect as Gudi Padwa is specifically celebrated in Chaitra month.
qs.kf:
☛ In which month is Gudi Padwa celebrated? → Chaitra
☛ On which tithi is Gudi Padwa observed? → Chaitra Shukla Pratipada
☛ Which state celebrates Gudi Padwa as a major festival? → Maharashtra
☛ Which season does Gudi Padwa mark? → Spring
☛ What is erected on Gudi Padwa? → Gudi

q: The thanksgiving festival of Pongal is primarily celebrated in which state of India?
qs.e: Pongal is a major Hindu festival celebrated over four days. It is primarily observed in Tamilnadu and is one of the most important festivals for Tamil people. The festival marks the end of the harvest season and the beginning of the sun's northward journey (Uttarayana). The word 'Pongal' literally means 'to boil' or 'overflow', and it is associated with the tradition of cooking new rice. During this time, people give thanks to the Sun God. The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm across Tamilnadu, involving decorations, special meals, and traditional dances.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state's main festival is Pongal? → Tamilnadu
☛ Pongal is also known by what other name? → Tamil New Year
☛ Pongal is related to which crop? → Rice crop
☛ What is the first day of Pongal called? → Bhogi Pongal
☛ What is the literal meaning of Pongal? → To boil or overflow

q: In which state did Bharatanatyam originate?
qs.e: Bharatanatyam is one of the classical dances of India, originating in the state of Tamil Nadu. This dance form is deeply rooted in the tradition of ancient temples and was originally performed by temple dancers known as Devadasis. Bharatanatyam finds mention in the ancient treatise 'Natyashastra' written by Bharata Muni. It is distinct from other classical dances like Kathak, Odissi, and Kuchipudi in its unique postures and expressive style. The dance was revived in the 20th century and is now popular worldwide. Apart from Tamil Nadu, this dance is also practiced in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state did Bharatanatyam originate? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which ancient text is associated with Bharatanatyam? → Natyashastra
☛ What are the major styles of Bharatanatyam? → Pandanallur, Vazhuvoor, Thanjavur
☛ Which deity is primarily worshipped in Bharatanatyam? → Nataraja (Shiva)
☛ Who are famous Bharatanatyam dancers? → Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Mrinalini Sarabhai

q: 'Onam' is one of the most important festivals of-
qs.e: Onam is the most important festival of the state of Kerala, celebrated to mark the homecoming of the legendary King Mahabali. It falls in the month of Chingam (August-September) as per the Malayalam calendar and lasts for 10 days. The festival is also a harvest festival, characterized by flower decorations (Pookalam), grand feasts known as Sadhya, and traditional games including the famous boat race Vallam Kali. In contrast, Gujarat's major festivals include Navratri and Diwali, Karnataka celebrates Ugadi, and Maharashtra is known for Ganesh Chaturthi.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state celebrates Onam? → Kerala
☛ In whose memory is Onam celebrated? → King Mahabali
☛ When is Onam celebrated? → Chingam month (Aug-Sep)
☛ What is the traditional Onam feast called? → Sadhya
☛ What is the boat race associated with Onam? → Vallam Kali

q: Kumbh Mela takes place in which of these cities of Madhya Pradesh -
A. Gwalior
B. Bhopal
C. Ujjain
D. Indore
qs.e: Kumbh Mela is held at four sacred places: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik. Among these, Ujjain is located in Madhya Pradesh. This fair is also known as Simhastha or Sinhasth. In Ujjain, the Kumbh Mela is held on the banks of the Shipra River. It occurs every 12 years when Jupiter is in Leo. It is the largest religious gathering in Hinduism.
qs.kf:
☛ Four Kumbh Mela sites → Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik
☛ Name of Ujjain Kumbh → Simhastha
☛ River associated with Ujjain Kumbh → Shipra River
☛ Interval of Ujjain Kumbh → 12 years
☛ Planetary position for Ujjain Kumbh → Jupiter in Leo

q: The famous Hornbill Festival is unique to which Northeast state of India?
qs.e: The Hornbill Festival is the most significant festival of Nagaland, celebrated annually from 1st to 10th December in Kohima. It is named after the state bird, the hornbill. This festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of the 16 major tribes of Nagaland. It is also known as the 'Festival of Festivals' and was initiated in 2000 by the Nagaland government to promote tourism. The festival features traditional dances, songs, crafts, and cuisines, making it a vibrant display of Naga culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Hornbill Festival held? → Kohima, Nagaland
☛ When is the Hornbill Festival celebrated? → 1-10 December
☛ What is the state bird of Nagaland? → Hornbill
☛ When was the Hornbill Festival started? → 2000
☛ What is the Hornbill Festival also known as? → Festival of Festivals

q: In which part of India is the festival 'Moatsu' celebrated?
qs.e: The festival 'Moatsu' is celebrated in Nagaland, primarily by the Ao Naga tribe. It marks the end of the sowing season and is observed in the first week of May. The festival involves community feasting, singing, dancing, and various rituals. 'Moatsu' literally means 'to eat together' and symbolizes unity and cooperation among the people. During the festival, traditional songs and dances are performed, and young people engage in sports and games. The festival is a time for seeking blessings for a good harvest and prosperity. It is an integral part of the cultural heritage of the Ao tribe and reflects their agricultural traditions and social bonds.
qs.kf:
☛ Which tribe celebrates Moatsu festival? → Ao tribe
☛ In which state is Moatsu festival celebrated? → Nagaland
☛ Moatsu is celebrated after which season? → Sowing season
☛ What is the meaning of Moatsu? → To eat together
☛ In which month is Moatsu celebrated? → May

q: Which of the following union territories celebrates Tarpa festival?
qs.e: The Tarpa festival is celebrated in the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. It is a major tribal festival primarily observed by the Warli and Bhil communities. The festival is held after the harvest season and features traditional dances, music, and communal feasts. The Tarpa dance, performed in a circular formation by both men and women, is the main attraction. This festival is a way to express gratitude to nature and celebrate the bounty of the harvest.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Tarpa festival celebrated? → Dadra and Nagar Haveli
☛ Which tribes are associated with Tarpa? → Warli and Bhil
☛ When is Tarpa festival observed? → After harvest season
☛ What is the main dance of Tarpa festival? → Tarpa dance
☛ What is the capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli? → Silvassa

q: Which of the following cities hosted the 4-day India International Cherry Blossom festival in 2019?
qs.e: The India International Cherry Blossom Festival is held annually in Shillong, Meghalaya. Inspired by Japan's famous cherry blossom season, the festival showcases similar blooming flowers in Shillong. In 2019, the 4-day festival took place in November. The event aims to boost tourism and promote cultural exchange. Shillong is also known as the 'Scotland of the East'.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Cherry Blossom Festival held in India? → Shillong
☛ What is the scientific name of cherry blossom? → Prunus serrulata
☛ Cherry blossom is the national flower of which country? → Japan
☛ What is the capital of Meghalaya? → Shillong
☛ When did the India International Cherry Blossom Festival start? → 2016

q: What form of art is used to decorate the floor in front of the house?
qs.e: Kolam is a traditional South Indian folk art form where geometric patterns are drawn on the floor in front of houses using rice flour or colored powders. It is especially prevalent in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Andhra Pradesh. Kolam is created daily by women in the morning and symbolizes prosperity and auspiciousness. This art is used to decorate the entrance of homes and to ward off evil spirits. The use of rice paste in Kolam also provides food for ants and insects, conveying a message of compassion and coexistence.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Kolam associated with? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the main material used in Kolam? → Rice flour
☛ What is the primary purpose of making Kolam? → To beautify the home and bring auspiciousness
☛ What type of art is Kolam? → Floor Art
☛ During which month is Kolam especially created? → Margazhi (December-January)

q: The Hornbill festival is a famous tribal festival. It is celebrated in which of the following North-Eastern states of India?
qs.e: The Hornbill Festival is the largest tribal festival of Nagaland, often called the 'Festival of Festivals'. It is held annually from 1st to 10th December in Kohima. The festival is named after the hornbill bird, which is considered sacred in Naga culture. It showcases the rich cultural heritage, traditional dances, music, cuisine, and handicrafts of the Naga tribes. The festival promotes state tourism and brings all Naga tribes together on a common platform. It is one of the most popular festivals in the North-Eastern states of India.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Hornbill Festival celebrated? → Nagaland
☛ Where is Hornbill Festival held? → Kohima
☛ When is Hornbill Festival celebrated? → 1st to 10th December
☛ Which bird is the Hornbill Festival named after? → Hornbill bird
☛ What is Hornbill Festival also known as? → Festival of Festivals

q: Which of the following is the traditional theatre of Kerala where eight plays are performed in eight days?
qs.e: Krishnanattam is a traditional theatre form of Kerala where eight plays are performed over eight days. It is written in Manipravalam, a mixture of Sanskrit and Malayalam. Krishnanattam was composed by Zamorin Raja Manavedan, the ruler of Calicut. The eight plays depict the life of Lord Krishna and are performed sequentially over eight nights. This art form is distinct from other Kerala styles like Kathakali. Krishnanattam has been recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage. The performance involves elaborate costumes, makeup, and music, and is traditionally staged in temples. It is a devotional art form with deep religious significance.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed Krishnanattam? → Zamorin Raja Manavedan
☛ How many plays in Krishnanattam? → Eight
☛ Language of Krishnanattam? → Manipravalam
☛ State of Krishnanattam? → Kerala
☛ Theme of Krishnanattam? → Life of Lord Krishna

q: Pushkar Fair is the annual animal fair held in which the state of India?
qs.e: The Pushkar Fair is an annual animal fair held in the town of Pushkar in the Ajmer district of Rajasthan, India. It takes place during the Kartik Purnima (full moon) and is known for the trading of camels, horses, and cattle. It is one of the largest camel fairs in the world. The fair also features cultural events, dance, music, and competitions like camel races. Pushkar Fair is a major tourist attraction and draws visitors from across the globe.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Pushkar Fair held? → Rajasthan (Pushkar, Ajmer)
☛ When is Pushkar Fair held? → Kartik Purnima
☛ What is Pushkar Fair famous for? → Camel trading
☛ Duration of Pushkar Fair? → Approximately 7 days
☛ Famous temple in Pushkar? → Brahma Temple

q: Which of the following is a traditional martial art of Korea?
qs.e: Taekwondo is a traditional martial art of Korea, developed in the 1950s. It is famous for its high kicks, jumping kicks, and spinning kicks. Karate is a Japanese martial art, Krav Maga is an Israeli military self-defense system, and Kabaddi is an Indian sport. The term 'Taekwondo' means 'the way of the foot and fist'. It became an Olympic sport in the 2000 Sydney Olympics and is governed by the World Taekwondo Federation (WTF).
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for Taekwondo → WTF Taekwondo
☛ Taekwondo belt ranks → White to Black
☛ Taekwondo became Olympic sport → 2000 Sydney Olympics
☛ Taekwondo origin → Korea
☛ Meaning of Taekwondo → The way of the foot and fist

q: In which state did Toda begin the Art of embroidery?
qs.e: The Toda embroidery art is practiced by the Toda tribe in the state of Tamilnadu. This tribe resides in the Nilgiri hills and is known for its distinctive embroidery style. Toda embroidery primarily uses red and black threads to create geometric patterns. This art form has been granted the Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Traditionally, Toda women perform this embroidery, which is used to adorn their garments.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is associated with Toda embroidery? → Tamilnadu
☛ Where does the Toda tribe live? → Nilgiri hills
☛ Which colors are primarily used in Toda embroidery? → Red and black
☛ What tag has Toda embroidery received? → GI tag
☛ Who performs Toda embroidery? → Toda women

q: Dullu Kunitha is a famous folk music tradition in _______________.
qs.e: Dullu Kunitha is a famous folk music tradition in the state of Karnataka. It is primarily prevalent in the northern parts of the state and is performed on special occasions like weddings and festivals. This tradition is centuries old and has even been recognized by UNESCO. The performance involves the use of drums and cymbals, and it is sung in groups. The lyrics often depict historical and mythological stories, making it an integral part of Karnataka's cultural heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Dullu Kunitha associated with? → Karnataka
☛ What instruments are mainly used in Dullu Kunitha? → Drums and cymbals
☛ Which region of Karnataka is known for Dullu Kunitha? → Northern Karnataka
☛ On what occasions is Dullu Kunitha performed? → Weddings and festivals
☛ Which international body has recognized Dullu Kunitha? → UNESCO

q: The composition of creation of ornamental handwriting is called ________.
qs.e: The composition of creation of ornamental handwriting is called Calligraphy. It is the art of writing letters and words in a beautiful and decorative manner. The word calligraphy literally means 'beautiful writing'. It has been practiced in various cultures since ancient times, especially in Islamic, Chinese, and European traditions. Calligraphy involves different styles and tools such as pens, brushes, and ink. India also has a rich tradition of calligraphy, including scripts like Devanagari, Persian, and Urdu.
qs.kf:
☛ What is calligraphy? → The art of ornamental handwriting
☛ Literal meaning of calligraphy? → Beautiful writing
☛ In which culture is calligraphy especially prominent? → Islamic culture
☛ Which scripts are used in Indian calligraphy? → Devanagari, Persian, Urdu
☛ Main tools used in calligraphy? → Pen, brush, ink

q: Lai Haraoba festival is celebrated in which of these states?
qs.e: The Lai Haraoba festival is a significant religious and cultural event celebrated in the state of Manipur. It is primarily observed by the Meitei community and involves the worship of deities and the enactment of the mythological story of creation. The festival is also known as the 'Festival of Gods'. It is held in the month of May-June. During Lai Haraoba, traditional dances, music, and theatrical performances are showcased. The main purpose of this festival is to invoke divine forces and celebrate the creation of the universe. Thus, Lai Haraoba festival is a symbol of the rich cultural heritage of Manipur.
qs.kf:
☛ Lai Haraoba festival is related to which state? → Manipur
☛ Which community primarily celebrates Lai Haraoba? → Meitei community
☛ What is the literal meaning of Lai Haraoba? → Festival of Gods
☛ What is the capital of Manipur? → Imphal
☛ What are the major folk dances of Manipur? → Lai Haraoba dance, Thang-Ta, Nat Sankirtan

q: The world famous Majuli festival is celebrated in ________.
qs.e: The Majuli festival is celebrated in the state of Assam, India. Majuli is the world's largest river island, located in the Brahmaputra River. This festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of Assam, including traditional dance, music, and art. It is held annually in November-December and is a major attraction for tourists. The festival aims to promote Assamese culture and traditions. Majuli has been recognized as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. The festival features performances by local artists, craft fairs, and food stalls, making it a vibrant celebration of Assamese identity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is Majuli Island located in? → Brahmaputra River
☛ What status does Majuli have? → UNESCO World Heritage Site
☛ What is the state festival of Assam? → Bihu
☛ What is the capital of Assam? → Dispur
☛ When is the Majuli festival celebrated? → November-December

q: 'Bhakri' and 'Thalipeeth' traditionally belong to which cuisine?
qs.e: Bhakri and Thalipeeth are traditional foods of Maharashtra, India. Bhakri is a dry, unleavened flatbread made from flours like jowar (sorghum), bajra (pearl millet), or wheat, often eaten with chutney, yogurt, or vegetables. Thalipeeth is a spicy multigrain flatbread prepared with bhaji (green leafy vegetables) and spices, commonly paired with white butter or yogurt. Both dishes have been staple foods for farmers in Maharashtra. While variations of bhakri exist in Gujarati and Rajasthani cuisines, thalipeeth is uniquely Maharashtrian. Punjabi cuisine features naan, tandoori roti, and parathas. Hence, these dishes belong to Maharashtrian cuisine.
qs.kf:
☛ Traditional Maharashtrian dry flatbread → Bhakri
☛ Main grain mix used in Thalipeeth → Jowar, bajra, rice, lentils
☛ Spiced Maharashtrian flatbread with leafy greens → Thalipeeth
☛ Another state where Bhakri is popular → Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka
☛ Common accompaniment for Thalipeeth → White butter or yogurt

q: The Hornbill Festival, also known as 'the Festival of Festivals', is celebrated in which Indian state?
qs.e: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in the Indian state of Nagaland. It is famously called the 'Festival of Festivals' as it showcases the rich culture, dances, songs, and traditional attires of all the major tribes of Nagaland. The festival is held annually from 1 to 10 December at the Naga Heritage Village (Kisama) near Kohima. The event aims to preserve the indigenous Naga traditions and promote tourism in the region. It is named after the Hornbill bird, which is revered in Naga folklore.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Hornbill Festival celebrated? → Nagaland
☛ What are the dates of the Hornbill Festival? → 1-10 December
☛ Which venue hosts the Hornbill Festival? → Naga Heritage Village, Kohima
☛ What is the Hornbill Festival also known as? → 'Festival of Festivals'
☛ What is the purpose of the Hornbill Festival? → Preservation of Naga culture and tourism promotion

q: In Tamil Nadu, which day of Pongal is celebrated as Kaanum Pongal?
qs.e: Pongal is a four-day harvest festival in Tamil Nadu. The first day is Bogi Pongal (discarding old things), the second day is Surya Pongal (main day, worship of Sun God), the third day is Mattu Pongal (honoring cattle), and the fourth day is Kaanum Pongal (visiting family and friends). Kaanum means 'to see', and on this day people go out, have community feasts, and enjoy games. The festival celebrates the harvest season.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the main day of Pongal? → Surya Pongal (second day)
☛ Mattu Pongal is dedicated to whom? → Cattle
☛ What is done on Bogi Pongal? → Burning old items
☛ What does Kaanum Pongal mean? → 'To see'
☛ Which state's major festival is Pongal? → Tamil Nadu

q: Mundari is a ritualistic dance form of the Munda tribes prevalent in _______________.
qs.e: Mundari is a ritualistic dance form of the Munda tribe, predominantly prevalent in the state of Jharkhand. This dance is performed during harvest, marriage, and festivals, involving both men and women. It is dedicated to nature and deities, reflecting the community's unity and cultural heritage. While the Munda tribe also resides in parts of Odisha, West Bengal, and Bihar, the Mundari dance is uniquely associated with Jharkhand. The dance involves rhythmic movements and traditional musical instruments, showcasing the tribe's rich traditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which tribe performs the Mundari dance? → Munda
☛ What is the nature of Mundari dance? → Ritualistic
☛ Which is the main region of Munda tribe? → Jharkhand
☛ On which occasions is Mundari dance performed? → Harvest and marriage
☛ Which language family does the Munda language belong to? → Austroasiatic

q: The Simhastha Kumbh Mela festival at Ujjain is celebrated on the banks of river _____.
qs.e: The Simhastha Kumbh Mela held in Ujjain is celebrated on the banks of the holy Shipra River. The Shipra River flows in Madhya Pradesh and holds immense religious significance. Simhastha Kumbh Mela is organized every 12 years when a special planetary alignment occurs. This festival is one of the four Kumbh Mela sites in India, the others being Haridwar (Ganga), Prayagraj (confluence of Ganga-Yamuna-Saraswati), and Nashik (Godavari). The Shipra River is also venerated due to its connection with the Mahakal Temple. During the Kumbh Mela, devotees take a holy dip and seek spiritual benefits.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Simhastha Kumbh Mela held? → Ujjain
☛ Which river flows in Ujjain? → Shipra
☛ How often is Kumbh Mela held? → Every 12 years
☛ What are the four Kumbh sites? → Haridwar, Prayagraj, Ujjain, Nashik
☛ Which famous temple is in Ujjain? → Mahakaleshwar Temple

q: Which state’s Tourism and Art and Culture Department organises the Hornbill Festival?
qs.e: The Hornbill Festival is organised by the Tourism and Art and Culture Department of the state of Nagaland. It is an annual festival celebrated from 1st to 10th December in Kohima. The festival aims to preserve and promote the rich cultural heritage of Nagaland. It is also known as the 'Festival of Festivals' and brings together various Naga tribes. q: Kathputli is a traditional puppet show of which of the following Indian states?
qs.e: Kathputli is a famous traditional puppet show from Rajasthan. It is an ancient art form where wooden puppets dressed in colorful costumes are controlled by strings. Performed by the Bhatt community, it brings stories and folk songs to life. Kathputli is a symbol of Rajasthan's cultural identity.

q: Gyaneshwar (1275 A.D.) holds a unique position in Marathi literature, primarily because he was:
o: the first and foremost Bhakti poet
qs.e: Gyaneshwar (1275 A.D.) is regarded as the first and foremost Bhakti poet in Marathi literature. He composed the Gyaneshwari, a famous commentary on the Bhagavad Gita in Marathi, which is known for its philosophical depth and devotional fervor. He laid the foundation of the Warkari tradition, centered on the worship of Vithoba (Vishnu). His language was simple, accessible to the common people, which helped the Bhakti movement gain widespread support. His work enriched Marathi language and influenced later poets like Tukaram and Eknath.
qs.kf:
☛ What is Gyaneshwar's major work? → Gyaneshwari
☛ Which Bhakti tradition is Gyaneshwar associated with? → Warkari tradition
☛ On which scripture did Gyaneshwar write a commentary? → Bhagavad Gita
☛ Who is considered the first poet of Marathi Bhakti poetry? → Gyaneshwar
☛ What is the time period of Gyaneshwar? → 1275 A.D. (13th century)

q: The Acheulian cultural tradition is primarily identified with which types of advanced and symmetrical stone tools?
qs.e: The Acheulian cultural tradition belongs to the Lower Paleolithic period and is primarily identified with hand-axes and cleavers. These tools were bifacially flaked, symmetrical, and technologically advanced. This tradition began around 1.76 million years ago and spread across Africa, Europe, and Asia. Associated with Homo erectus, key Acheulian sites include Saint-Acheul in France, after which the tradition is named. In India, Acheulian tools have been found at sites like Attirampakkam, Hunsgi, and Didwana.
qs.kf:
☛ Which hominid is mainly associated with the Acheulian tradition? → Homo erectus
☛ After which site is the Acheulian culture named? → Saint-Acheul, France
☛ What are the three main cultures of the Lower Paleolithic period? → Oldowan, Acheulian, Clactonian
☛ Where are Acheulian tools found in India? → Attirampakkam, Hunsgi, Didwana
☛ Which stone was primarily used to make hand-axes? → Quartzite

q: When referring to the conventional rod puppet shows of West Bengal, what is the name used?
qs.e: The traditional rod puppet show of West Bengal is called Putul Nautch. This ancient folk art involves puppets made of wood or cloth controlled by rods. 'Putul Nautch' literally means 'dance of dolls'. These shows are typically performed in rural areas and include music and dialogues. Other options: Kathputli belongs to Rajasthan, Yakshagana is a shadow puppet form from Karnataka, and Gombeyatta is a rod puppet form from Karnataka. Hence, the correct name for West Bengal's rod puppet show is Putul Nautch.
qs.kf:
☛ What is a rod puppet? → Puppet controlled with the help of rods
☛ Name of Rajasthan's puppet style? → Kathputli
☛ Name of Karnataka's shadow puppet? → Yakshagana
☛ Name of Karnataka's rod puppet? → Gombeyatta
☛ Material used in Putul Nautch? → Wood and cloth

q: The earliest documented evidence of puppetry in India is in which of the following languages?
qs.e: The earliest documented evidence of puppetry in India is found in the Tamil language. This evidence is present in Sangam literature, which was composed between 500 BCE and 300 CE. The Tamil epic 'Silappadikaram' (2nd century CE) describes a puppet dance. Puppetry is one of the ancient folk arts of India, where stories are narrated using dolls. In Tamil Nadu, it is known as 'Bommalattam'. Thus, the earliest evidence in Tamil makes this the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language is the earliest written evidence of puppetry in India found? → Tamil
☛ What is the Tamil puppetry art called? → Bommalattam
☛ Which Tamil text mentions puppetry? → Silappadikaram
☛ What is the period of Sangam literature? → 500 BCE to 300 CE
☛ What are the main types of puppetry? → Glove puppet, String puppet, Rod puppet, Shadow puppet

q: Which of the following influential poets was renowned for employing ultabasi (also written as ulatbansi), a distinctive poetic style characterised by paradoxes and enigmas?
qs.e: Kabir, a 15th-century influential poet and saint, is renowned for using the ultabasi (ulatbansi) style, a distinctive poetic form characterized by paradoxes and enigmas. This style reverses conventional logic to convey deep spiritual and philosophical truths. For instance, his line 'Jal mein kumbh, kumbh mein jal hai' is a classic example of ultabasi. Among the other options: Agyeya was a modern experimental poet, Bal Krishna Sharma Naveen was a Chhayawadi poet, and Ramdhari Singh Dinkar was a nationalist poet. Kabir's ultabasi blends folk language and mysticism uniquely.
qs.kf:
☛ Which poet is associated with 'UltaBansi' style? → Kabir
☛ What is the poetic style using paradoxes and riddles called? → UltaBansi
☛ What language did Kabir use? → Sadhukkadi
☛ What is the major work of Kabir? → Bijak
☛ To which period does Kabir belong? → Bhakti period

q: What is the name of the ancient Indian text on dramaturgy and theatre?
qs.e: The ancient Indian text on dramaturgy and theatre is Natya Shastra, composed by the sage Bharata Muni. This foundational work of Sanskrit literature comprehensively covers drama, dance, music, acting, aesthetics (rasa), emotions (bhava), stage design, costumes, and theatrical principles. It consists of 36 chapters and is often referred to as the 'Fifth Veda'. Arthashastra is a treatise on statecraft and economics, Manusmriti is a legal and religious text, and Rigveda is a collection of Vedic hymns. Therefore, Natya Shastra is the authoritative ancient Indian text on dramaturgy and theatre.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the author of Natya Shastra? → Bharata Muni
☛ How many chapters does Natya Shastra have? → 36
☛ What is Natya Shastra also known as? → Fifth Veda
☛ How many rasas (emotions) are described in Natya Shastra? → 8 (later 9)
☛ What language is Natya Shastra written in? → Sanskrit

q: What is 'Jallikattu'?
o: A popular watersport enjoyed by the Marina beach, Chennai
A traditional bull-taming sport popular in Tamil Nadu
The traditional name for "People's Leader" in Tamil
A bull worship festival at Pashupatinath temple, Nepal
qs.e: Jallikattu is an ancient traditional sport of Tamil Nadu where participants tame a bull. It is also known as 'Eru Thazhuvuthal' and 'Manju Virattu'. This sport is played during the Pongal festival and is a vital part of Tamil culture. Men attempt to control the bull by jumping onto its hump. The sport has faced accusations of animal cruelty, but in 2023, the Supreme Court permitted it to preserve Tamil culture. Jallikattu symbolizes the bravery and tradition of the Tamil people.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state's traditional sport is Jallikattu? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which festival is Jallikattu associated with? → Pongal
☛ What are the other names of Jallikattu? → Eru Thazhuvuthal, Manju Virattu
☛ In which year was Jallikattu given legal validity? → 2023 (Supreme Court)
☛ What is the main action in Jallikattu? → Taming the bull

q: Which of the following tribes celebrates the Bhagoriya festival?
qs.e: The Bhagoriya festival is celebrated by the Bhil tribe. It is a significant festival primarily observed among the Bhil communities of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Also known as 'Bhagoria Haat' or 'Bhagoria Mela', it is celebrated around Holi. During this festival, young men and women gather to choose their life partners voluntarily. The festival symbolizes social freedom and communal celebration in Bhil culture. The Bhil tribe is one of the largest tribal groups in India, mainly found in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra.

☛ Which tribe celebrates the Bhagoriya festival? → Bhil
☛ Around which festival is Bhagoriya celebrated? → Holi

☛ What is Bhagoriya also known as? → Bhagoria Haat or Mela

q: Who is the author of the famous Kannada play ‘Tughlaq’ which is also staged in other Indian languages?
qs.e: Girish Karnad was a renowned Indian writer, playwright, actor, and film director. He made significant contributions to Kannada literature. His play 'Tughlaq', published in 1964, is based on the life of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, the 14th-century Sultan of Delhi. The play received widespread acclaim and has been translated and staged in many Indian languages. Karnad was awarded the Jnanpith Award in 1998. His other major plays include 'Yayati', 'Nagamandala', and 'Hayavadana'.

q: Which of the following states is known for Bihu music?
qs.e: Bihu music is a traditional folk music of Assam, primarily performed during the Bihu festival. It is an integral part of Assamese culture and involves traditional instruments like dhol, pepa (a horn made from buffalo horn), gagana, and bansuri. The music typically revolves around themes of agriculture and nature. Bihu is celebrated in mid-April, marking the Assamese New Year and the onset of the harvesting season. The other options—Punjab is known for Bhangra and Gidda, Rajasthan for its folk songs, and Tamil Nadu for Carnatic music—are incorrect.

q: A/An ______ is a pointing and drawing device shaped like a pen. It is used on a touch screen.
qs.e: A stylus is a pointed, pen-shaped input device used on touch screens for precise input such as writing, drawing, or navigating. It is especially useful on tablets, smartphones, and graphics tablets, offering greater accuracy than fingers. Common among artists, designers, and note-takers, modern styli often include features like pressure sensitivity and palm rejection. The other options—flag, cursor, and index—do not describe this device. Thus, the correct answer is stylus.

q: Which of the following describes a drainage pattern resembling a dome like structure?
qs.e: Radial drainage pattern describes rivers flowing outward in all directions from a central high point like a dome or hill, resembling spokes on a wheel. This pattern is common on volcanic cones or dome-shaped hills. Other patterns: Trellis (parallel main rivers with tributaries at right angles), Dendritic (tree-like branching, common in plains), Rectangular (right-angle bends due to faults). The radial pattern is distinct because it originates from a single elevated feature, unlike dendritic which spreads randomly.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is radial drainage found? → On volcanic cones and domed hills
☛ What is dendritic pattern like? → Tree-shaped branching rivers
☛ In trellis pattern, main rivers are? → Parallel, with tributaries meeting at right angles
☛ Rectangular pattern is caused by? → Geological faults and joints
☛ Example of radial pattern? → Some tributaries of the Amazon River

q: In which of the following states, the famous martial arts Kalarippayattu was born?
qs.e: Kalarippayattu is one of the oldest martial arts in India, originating from the state of Kerala. It is particularly prevalent in the Malabar region of Kerala and is considered one of the world's oldest martial arts. The history of Kalarippayattu is believed to be around 3000 years old, with references found in ancient texts. This martial art is based on various techniques like Attam (dance-like movements), Vayu prayog (breath control), and Vadi (weapon handling). Kalarippayattu has gained global recognition and is also acknowledged by UNESCO. It is an integral part of Kerala's cultural heritage.

☛ Major festival associated with Kalarippayattu → Onam

q: When did the Ministry of Human Resource Development launch Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan which the scheme focuses on improving the quality of education and using technology to empower children and teachers?
qs.e: The Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan was launched by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (now Ministry of Education) in May 2018. It is an integrated scheme for school education merging three previous schemes: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, and the Teacher Education Programme. The scheme focuses on improving the quality of education, promoting the use of digital technology, and empowering children and teachers. It covers all aspects of school education from pre-primary to Class 12.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan launched? → May 2018
☛ Which schemes were merged to form Samagra Shiksha? → Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, Teacher Education Programme
☛ What is the main objective of Samagra Shiksha? → Improve quality of education and use of technology
☛ Which classes does the scheme cover? → Pre-primary to Class 12
☛ Under which ministry does Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan fall? → Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development)

q: Name the scheme launched by the Government of India in April, 2005, that aims to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective and reliable primary health care especially to the poor and vulnerable sections of the population.
qs.e: The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM), launched by the Government of India in April 2005, aims to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective, and reliable primary health care, especially to the poor and vulnerable sections of the population. It is a component of the National Health Mission (NHM). NRHM includes initiatives such as ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) workers, Village Health Committees, and the Janani Suraksha Yojana. Its key focus areas are reducing maternal and infant mortality, promoting family planning, and controlling communicable diseases. The implementation of NRHM has improved the rural health infrastructure, including strengthening Primary Health Centers (PHCs) and Community Health Centers (CHCs).
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NRHM? → National Rural Health Mission
☛ Year of launch of NRHM? → 2005
☛ Rural health workers under NRHM are called? → ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)
☛ Objective of NRHM? → Provide accessible, affordable, accountable primary health care to poor and vulnerable sections
☛ NRHM is part of which mission? → National Health Mission (NHM)

q: The National TB programme (NTP) was launched by the Government of India in year ______ in the form of District TB Centre Model involved with BCG Vaccination and TB treatment.
qs.e: The National TB Programme (NTP) was launched by the Government of India in the year 1962 as the District TB Centre Model, which integrated BCG vaccination and TB treatment.
