This programme aimed to control the spread of tuberculosis and provide timely treatment to patients. In 1997, it was revised and renamed as the Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP), and later in 2020, it was restructured as the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). The year 1962 marks a significant milestone in India's fight against tuberculosis.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of NTP launch? → 1962
☛ Model of NTP? → District TB Centre Model
☛ BCG vaccine protects against? → Tuberculosis
☛ Year of RNTCP launch? → 1997
☛ Year of NTEP launch? → 2020

q: The Mid-Day Meal scheme comes under the purview of which ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
qs.e: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme is a flagship program of the Government of India that provides nutritious meals to school children. It currently comes under the purview of the Ministry of Education. Earlier, it was under the Ministry of Human Resource Development, but the ministry was renamed in 2020. The scheme aims to improve the nutritional status of children, increase enrollment and attendance in schools. It is one of the largest school feeding programs in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Mid-Day Meal Scheme launched? → 1995
☛ What is the main objective of this scheme? → Improving nutrition and education of children
☛ Which age group of children is covered? → 6-14 years
☛ What does the central government provide under this scheme? → Free grains and financial assistance
☛ Which act is this scheme linked to? → Right to Education Act 2009

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the growth area under the Digital India programme?
qs.e: The Digital India programme has nine growth areas, including Broadband Highways, Universal Access to Mobile Services, E-governance, Digital Literacy, etc. 'Public school education for all' is not a part of these growth areas; it pertains to the Right to Education (RTE) Act. Digital India aims to create digital infrastructure, deliver digital services, and enhance digital literacy. Other options like Broadband Highways, Universal Access to Mobile Services, and E-governance are key pillars of the initiative.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the nine growth areas of Digital India? → Broadband Highways, Universal Mobile Access, E-governance, etc.
☛ What is the objective of Digital India? → Digital infrastructure, services, and literacy
☛ E-governance relates to? → Digitalization of government services
☛ Broadband Highways refer to? → High-speed internet connectivity
☛ When was Digital India launched? → 1 July 2015

q: Which of the following statements is correct in the context of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan?
o: North-Eastern states are not involved in the campaign.
It was launched to achieve the goal of universal sanitation.
qs.e: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on October 2, 2014, not 2015. It covers all states including North-Eastern states. It is not limited to rural areas; it includes urban areas as well. The primary goal was to achieve universal sanitation and make India open defecation free by 2019. The campaign focused on building toilets, waste management, and promoting hygiene awareness. It was launched on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swachh Bharat Abhiyan launched? → October 2, 2014
☛ What was the main objective of the campaign? → Open defecation free India by 2019
☛ Which areas does the campaign cover? → Both rural and urban
☛ What was emphasized in the campaign? → Toilet construction and waste management
☛ What is the slogan of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → One step towards cleanliness

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about Ayushman Bharat Scheme (ABS)?
o: Senior Citizen Health Insurance Scheme (SCHIS) is not covered under the scheme.
The scheme will have a defined benefit cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year.
Ayushman Bharat is a National Health Protection Scheme.
Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) has been subsumed under Ayushman Bharat Scheme (ABS).
qs.e: Ayushman Bharat Scheme (ABS) is a National Health Protection Scheme that provides health insurance cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year. It has subsumed both Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) and Senior Citizen Health Insurance Scheme (SCHIS). Hence, the statement that SCHIS is not covered is incorrect. The scheme benefits over 10 crore poor and vulnerable families. It is also known as Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY).
qs.kf:
☛ Full name of Ayushman Bharat Scheme → Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
☛ Cover amount under the scheme → ₹5 lakh per family per year
☛ Number of beneficiary families → Over 10 crore
☛ Previous schemes subsumed → RSBY and SCHIS
☛ Type of scheme → National Health Protection Scheme

q: Which Abhiyan was launched in 2014 on the birth anniversary of the Father of the Nation?
qs.e: The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on 2 October 2014 on the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. Its objective was to make India open defecation free and improve solid waste management. The campaign was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It was implemented in two phases: rural and urban. This initiative promoted sanitation and public health, leading to increased toilet construction and hygiene awareness across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan launched? → 2 October 2014
☛ Who is the inspiration behind Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What mission is included under Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Open Defecation Free India
☛ What is the slogan of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Ek Kadam Swachhata Ki Ore
☛ How many toilets were built under Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Over 10 crore

q: In which of the following years did the Government of India initiate the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE)
qs.e: The Government of India initiated the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE) in the year 1995. This programme later came to be known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme. Its objective was to provide nutritional support to children studying in primary schools and to increase enrollment and attendance. The scheme was implemented in all government and government-aided primary schools across the country. NP-NSPE is administered by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (now Ministry of Education). This programme has been instrumental in reducing malnutrition among children and improving the level of primary education.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of launch of NP-NSPE → 1995
☛ Current name of NP-NSPE → Mid-Day Meal Scheme
☛ Objective of the scheme → Nutritional support to primary education
☛ Implementing ministry → Ministry of Human Resource Development
☛ Beneficiaries → Children in government primary schools

q: A financial assistance of_______ rupees will be given to the community health centres so that they can be strengthened to meet the standards of sanitation, hygiene and infection control under the 'Swachh Swasth Sarvatra’.
qs.e: Under the 'Swachh Swasth Sarvatra' scheme, financial assistance of 10 lakh rupees is provided to Community Health Centres (CHCs). This scheme is jointly implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Its objective is to strengthen sanitation, hygiene, and infection control standards in healthcare facilities. While Primary Health Centres (PHCs) receive 5 lakh rupees, CHCs are allocated 10 lakh rupees. The fund is used for infrastructure improvement, sanitation facilities, and infection control measures. The scheme was launched in 2018 to promote clean and healthy healthcare environments.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the financial assistance for Community Health Centres under Swachh Swasth Sarvatra? → 10 lakh rupees
☛ What is the financial assistance for Primary Health Centres under this scheme? → 5 lakh rupees
☛ Which ministries jointly implement Swachh Swasth Sarvatra? → Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ What is the main objective of the scheme? → To strengthen sanitation, hygiene, and infection control standards in health centres
☛ When was the Swachh Swasth Sarvatra scheme launched? → 2018

q: Which government initiative primarily focuses on improving human development by ensuring healthcare and nutrition for women and children?
qs.e: Poshan Abhiyaan, also known as the National Nutrition Mission, is a flagship initiative of the Government of India focused on improving the health and nutrition of women and children. It aims to reduce malnutrition, anemia, and low birth weight through a combination of healthcare services, nutrition education, and dietary improvement. Launched in 2018, it targets a reduction in stunting, undernutrition, and anemia by 2022. The program is implemented through Anganwadi centers and involves inter-ministerial coordination. Poshan Abhiyaan emphasizes a life-cycle approach, addressing nutrition needs from pregnancy to adolescence.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Poshan Abhiyaan launched? → 2018
☛ What is the main objective of Poshan Abhiyaan? → Reduce malnutrition among women and children
☛ Which ministry oversees Poshan Abhiyaan? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ What was the earlier name of Poshan Abhiyaan? → National Nutrition Mission
☛ What is the slogan of Poshan Abhiyaan? → Malnutrition Free India

q: When was the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) launched by the Government of India?
qs.e: The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) was launched by the Government of India on 12 April 2005. Its aim was to improve healthcare services in rural areas, especially for vulnerable sections. This mission is part of the National Health Mission (NHM), which also includes the Urban Health Mission. The primary goal of NRHM was to reduce maternal and child mortality rates and strengthen health infrastructure in rural areas. Under this mission, initiatives like recruitment of ASHA workers and the Janani Suraksha Yojana were introduced.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NRHM launched? → 12 April 2005
☛ What is the full form of NRHM? → National Rural Health Mission
☛ Under which mission does NRHM fall? → National Health Mission (NHM)
☛ Which scheme was launched under NRHM? → Janani Suraksha Yojana
☛ What is the role of ASHA workers in NRHM? → Assist in rural healthcare services

q: When was the Community Development Programme (CDP) launched in India?
qs.e: The Community Development Programme (CDP) in India was launched on 2 October 1952. It was the first comprehensive rural development programme aimed at improving the economic and social infrastructure of villages. The programme started with 55 projects covering 27,000 villages. Its objective was to provide farmers with modern agricultural techniques, education, sanitation, and health services. Later, it was integrated with the Panchayati Raj system. CDP is considered the foundation of India's rural development efforts.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Community Development Programme launched? → 2 October 1952
☛ Who is known as the father of CDP? → Dr. Surendranath Dubey
☛ Where was the first CDP project started? → Etah (U.P.) and Faridabad (Haryana)
☛ How many villages were covered under CDP? → 27,000 villages
☛ Which programme replaced CDP? → IRDP (1978)

q: Clean cooking fuel is essential for rural women’s health and environmental sustainability. Which scheme provides LPG connections to women in BPL households?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May 2016. It aims to provide free LPG connections to women from BPL households, reducing health risks from traditional cooking fuels like firewood and coal. This scheme contributes to rural women's health and environmental sustainability. Over 10 crore connections have been issued so far.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMUY launched? → May 2016
☛ Who gets LPG connections under this scheme? → Women from BPL families
☛ Main objective of PMUY? → Provide clean cooking fuel
☛ Benefit of LPG use? → Reduction in health hazards
☛ Target number of connections? → 10 crore

q: Which of the following does not represent the things that make a ‘Smart City’, under the smart city campaign?
o: Affordable housing, especially for the poor.
qs.e: The Smart City Mission aims to equip cities with infrastructure, technology, and services to improve the quality of life for citizens. Key elements of a smart city include affordable housing, adequate water supply, and a sustainable environment. However, free health and education are not core components of the smart city framework; they are part of welfare schemes. The focus of a smart city is on smart governance, smart mobility, and smart infrastructure. Therefore, providing free health and education does not represent the things that make a smart city under this campaign.
qs.kf:
☛ Main objective of Smart City → sustainable and technologically advanced urban development
☛ Not included in Smart City → free health and education
☛ Smart City Mission launched → by Government of India in 2015
☛ Components of Smart City → smart governance, smart energy, smart buildings
☛ Sustainable environment → integral part of smart city

q: Which of the following schemes of the government of India is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ujjwala Yojana – Distribution of LPG cylinders to woman of BPL family
Ayushman Bharat – Health for All and Universal Health Coverage
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana – To promote the welfare of the Girl child
qs.e: Mission Indradhanush is a vaccination campaign by the Government of India, aimed at reaching children and pregnant women who missed routine immunizations. It was launched by the Ministry of Health in 2014, not related to employment. Options 1, 3, and 4 are correctly matched: Ujjwala Yojana (LPG distribution), Ayushman Bharat (health coverage), and Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (girl child welfare). Therefore, associating Mission Indradhanush with employment is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Ujjwala Yojana aim → Provide LPG connections to women of BPL families
☛ Mission Indradhanush related to → Vaccination of children and pregnant women
☛ Ayushman Bharat scheme → Health insurance cover for over 10 crore families
☛ Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana → Financial security for girl child's education and marriage
☛ Mission Indradhanush launched → In 2014 by Ministry of Health

q: Which of the following options is NOT correct regarding Swachh Bharat Abhiyan?
o: The main goal of the campaign was to eradicate the practice of open defecation.
It was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the year 2014
It is the restructuring of Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan
It's main focus is achieving cleanliness only in urban areas of India
qs.e: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on October 2, 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its primary goals were to eradicate open defecation and improve solid waste management. The campaign is focused on both rural and urban areas, not just urban areas. The rural component is called Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) and the urban component is called Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban). It is a restructuring of the earlier Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, which was launched in 2012. Therefore, option 4 is incorrect to state it only focuses on urban areas.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swachh Bharat Abhiyan launched? → October 2, 2014
☛ What was the main aim of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Open defecation free India
☛ Who inspired the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What are the two components of Swachh Bharat Mission? → Rural and Urban
☛ When was Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan launched? → 2012

q: The first on-line NISHTHA programme has been launched by the Ministry of Human Resource Development in _______.
qs.e: The Ministry of Human Resource Development (now Ministry of Education) launched the first online NISHTHA programme in Andhra Pradesh. NISHTHA stands for 'National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement'. This programme was initiated for the holistic development of school heads and teachers. It is the largest teacher training programme in the country. Its objective is to build the capacity of teachers and improve the quality of education. The programme was launched in online mode during the COVID-19 pandemic.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NISHTHA? → National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement
☛ Which ministry launched NISHTHA? → Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development)
☛ What is the objective of NISHTHA? → Capacity building of teachers and improvement of education quality
☛ When was NISHTHA launched? → 2019
☛ Who is NISHTHA for? → School heads and teachers

q: What does the SWAYAM scheme launched by Government of India aim to achieve?
o: Access, equity and quality of education
qs.e: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) is a digital education initiative of the Government of India launched in 2017. Its primary objective is to ensure access, equity and quality in education. This platform offers courses from school to postgraduate level online. It is operated by institutions such as the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), University Grants Commission (UGC), and All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE). While it aligns with Digital India and Skill India missions, its core aim is making education accessible to all.
qs.kf:
☛ SWAYAM full form → Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
☛ Classes covered under SWAYAM → 9th to Postgraduate
☛ Course providers on SWAYAM platform → CBSE, NIOS, UGC, AICTE, NPTEL
☛ Objective of SWAYAM → Access, equity and quality in education
☛ Year of launch of SWAYAM → 2017

q: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana was launched on:
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) is a maternity benefit scheme of the Government of India, providing financial assistance to pregnant and lactating women. It was launched nationwide on 1st January 2017. Under this scheme, a total of 5,000 rupees is given in three installments for the first live birth. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. Earlier, it was known as 'Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana', which started in 2010. PMMVY aims to improve the health of women during pregnancy and childbirth and to reduce infant mortality.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of PMMVY → 2017
☛ Total amount under the scheme → 5,000 rupees
☛ Number of installments → Three
☛ Implementing ministry → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ Former name → Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana

q: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan was launched by _______.
qs.e: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is a flagship program of the Government of India launched in 2000-2001 under the leadership of then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Its objective is to provide elementary education to all children aged 6-14 years and to implement the Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009. The program focuses on universalization of education, gender equality, and quality education. SSA has significantly increased school enrollment and reduced dropout rates, becoming a cornerstone of India's educational policy.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan → 2000-2001
☛ Age group for elementary education → 6-14 years
☛ Year of Right to Education Act → 2009
☛ Main objective of SSA → Universal elementary education
☛ Right to Education under RTE Act → Fundamental right

q: What is the amount of annual health benefit cover to be provided per family under the 'Ayushman Bharat' scheme of the Government of India?
qs.e: The Ayushman Bharat scheme, also known as Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), is a flagship health insurance scheme of the Government of India. It provides an annual health cover of ₹5 lakh per family. This cover is for poor and vulnerable families and includes hospitalization expenses for secondary and tertiary care. The scheme offers cashless and paperless treatment at both government and private hospitals across the country. The coverage is per family, not per individual. It is the largest government-funded health insurance scheme in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the annual cover under Ayushman Bharat? → ₹5 lakh per family
☛ What is the other name of this scheme? → Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
☛ What type of care does it cover? → Secondary and tertiary care
☛ How is treatment provided under the scheme? → Cashless and paperless
☛ Who are the beneficiaries? → Poor and vulnerable families

q: Sarva Siksha Abhiyan is a significant step towards providing elementary education to all the children in the age group of ______ years.
qs.e: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is a flagship program of the Government of India aimed at providing elementary education to all children in the age group of 6 to 14 years. Launched in 2001, it gained legal backing through the Right to Education Act (RTE Act, 2009). The program focuses on improving school infrastructure, teacher recruitment, and promoting girls' education. Its primary goal is to achieve Universal Elementary Education (UEE) by ensuring that every child in this age group has access to free and compulsory education. SSA has significantly contributed to increasing literacy rates and reducing gender disparities in education across India.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan launched? → 2001
☛ What is the full form of SSA? → Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
☛ When was the RTE Act enacted? → 2009
☛ Which age group does SSA target? → 6-14 years
☛ What is the main objective of SSA? → Universal Elementary Education (UEE)

q: The 'Sustainable Action for Transforming Human capital (SATH)' programme plans to focus on which two sectors?
qs.e: The SATH programme stands for Sustainable Action for Transforming Human capital. It is an initiative launched by NITI Aayog focused on human capital development. Its primary objective is to improve the education and health sectors. The programme is implemented in partnership with states and provides technical assistance. SATH aims to enhance the quality of education and strengthen health services. It was launched in 2017 and has helped several states implement their human capital development strategies.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of SATH? → Sustainable Action for Transforming Human capital
☛ Which institution launched SATH? → NITI Aayog
☛ In which year was SATH launched? → 2017
☛ What are the two focus sectors of SATH? → Education and health
☛ What is the objective of SATH? → Improve human capital development

q: Which of the following aspects is covered by the Ayushman Sahakar Scheme?
qs.e: The Ayushman Sahakar Scheme is an initiative of the Government of India aimed at strengthening healthcare and education infrastructure through cooperative societies. It is implemented by the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) and provides financial assistance for setting up hospitals, medical colleges, nursing institutions, and educational institutes. The primary focus of this scheme is to improve access to healthcare and education services in rural and remote areas. Agriculture, housing, or physical infrastructure are not covered under this scheme.
qs.kf:
☛ Which agency implements the Ayushman Sahakar Scheme? → National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)
☛ Which sectors are covered under this scheme? → Healthcare and Education infrastructure
☛ What is the main objective of the scheme? → Promote healthcare and education services in rural areas
☛ Which ministry does this scheme fall under? → Ministry of Cooperation
☛ Is agriculture infrastructure included in this scheme? → No

q: Which state government launched the 'Yuva Nidhi Scheme' for providing financial aid to unemployed youth?
qs.e: The Karnataka state government launched the Yuva Nidhi Scheme to provide financial aid to unemployed youth. This scheme was introduced in 2024. Under this scheme, unemployed youth receive a monthly financial assistance of ₹3,000 for a period of 2 years. The scheme is for youth aged between 18 and 25 years who have passed at least PU (Pre-University) or equivalent examination with a passing score. The objective is to reduce unemployment and provide skill development opportunities to youth.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state launched the Yuva Nidhi Scheme? → Karnataka
☛ What is the monthly financial assistance under this scheme? → ₹3,000
☛ What is the age group eligible for this scheme? → 18 to 25 years
☛ What is the minimum educational qualification for this scheme? → Passed PU (Pre-University)
☛ When was this scheme launched? → 2024

q: What is the full form of the NAMASTE Scheme, to be implemented for a period of 3 years from FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26?
o: National Aid for Mechanised Sanitation Technology Enhancement
National Assistance for Manual Sanitation and Treatment Endeavors
National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem
National Approach for Manual Sanitation and Treatment Enhancement
qs.e: The full form of the NAMASTE Scheme is National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem. It is being implemented for a period of three years from FY 2023-24 to 2025-26. The scheme aims to improve the lives of manual scavengers engaged in cleaning sewers and septic tanks, and to transition them into mechanized sanitation work. Under this scheme, beneficiaries are provided skills training, equipment, and loans to enable self-employment. It is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NAMASTE Scheme → National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem
☛ Duration of scheme → FY 2023-24 to 2025-26 (three years)
☛ Beneficiaries → Manual scavengers and their families
☛ Objective → Promote mechanized sanitation and end manual scavenging
☛ Implementing Ministry → Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

q: The 'SATH-E' project is associated with which of the following fields?
qs.e: The SATH-E project is related to the field of Education. It is an initiative by NITI Aayog aimed at improving school education in India. SATH stands for Sustainable Action for Transforming Human Capital. Under this project, NITI Aayog collaborates with states to enhance education quality, improve student learning outcomes, and strengthen the education system. Initially, the project was launched in five states— Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan. It focuses on structural reforms in the education sector.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of SATH-E? → Sustainable Action for Transforming Human Capital-Education
☛ Which commission launched the SATH-E project? → NITI Aayog
☛ How many states were covered under SATH-E initially? → Five states
☛ SATH-E is associated with which field? → Education
☛ When was SATH-E launched? → 2017

q: In 2005, ASHA was instituted by the Government of India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare as a part of the National Rural Health Mission. What is the full form of 'ASHA'?
qs.e: The full form of ASHA is Accredited Social Health Activist. It was instituted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2005 as part of the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM). ASHA workers serve as a link between the community and the health system, especially in rural areas. They provide services such as immunization, antenatal care, family planning, and prevention of communicable diseases. ASHAs are trained and accredited community health activists who promote health awareness and facilitate access to healthcare services. They play a crucial role in improving maternal and child health outcomes by acting as a bridge between primary health centers and the community.
qs.kf:
☛ Which mission includes ASHA workers? → National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)
☛ When was ASHA established? → 2005
☛ What is the primary work area of ASHA? → Rural areas
☛ Which ministry oversees ASHA? → Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
☛ What is the main objective of ASHA? → Improve maternal and child health

q: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) aims to provide useful and relevant elementary education for all children in the age group of ____ years.
qs.e: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is a flagship program of the Government of India, launched in the year 2000-01. Its primary objective is to provide useful and relevant elementary education to all children in the 6 to 14 years age group. This program has been instrumental in implementing the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009. SSA aims at universal access, retention, and improvement in the quality of education. It focuses on school infrastructure, teacher training, and teaching-learning materials.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of SSA → Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
☛ Launch year of SSA → 2000-01
☛ Age group covered under SSA → 6-14 years
☛ Act associated with SSA → RTE Act, 2009
☛ Main aim of SSA → Universal elementary education

q: 'COVAXIN' is India's indigenous COVID-19 vaccine developed by:
o: ICMR and Indian Medicines Pharmaceutical Corporation Limited
Bharat Biotech and ICMR-National Institute of Virology
Indian Medicines Pharmaceutical Corporation Limited and Rajasthan Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Limited
Bharat Biotech and National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority
qs.e: COVAXIN is India's first indigenous COVID-19 vaccine, jointly developed by Bharat Biotech and the ICMR-National Institute of Virology (NIV). It is an inactivated virus-based vaccine, where the SARS-CoV-2 virus is chemically inactivated for use. Also known as BBV152, this vaccine was granted emergency use authorization by the Indian government in January 2021. Its clinical trials were conducted across multiple centers in India, showing an efficacy of around 78%. COVAXIN can be stored at 2-8°C, making its distribution easier. The collaboration between Bharat Biotech, a leading vaccine manufacturer, and ICMR-NIV, a premier virology research institute, ensured a scientific and rapid development process.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the commercial name of COVAXIN? → BBV152
☛ What type of vaccine is COVAXIN? → Inactivated Virus
☛ Who conducted the clinical trials of COVAXIN? → Bharat Biotech and ICMR-NIV
☛ When was COVAXIN approved for emergency use in India? → January 2021
☛ At what temperature is COVAXIN stable? → 2-8°C

q: How much is the amount received under the central scheme "MP Member Local Area Development Scheme" (MPLD) (in rupees)?
qs.e: Under the central scheme 'MP Member Local Area Development Scheme' (MPLADS), each Member of Parliament receives 5 crore rupees per year. This amount is recommended by the MP for development works in their constituency. The scheme was launched in 1993 with the objective of promoting local infrastructure and community facilities. MPs can use the funds for areas like education, health, roads, drinking water, and sanitation. The funds are allocated from the central budget and implemented by the district administration.
qs.kf:
☛ When was MPLADS launched? → 1993
☛ Annual amount per MP? → 5 crore rupees
☛ Main objective of the scheme? → Local area development
☛ Who implements the funds? → District administration
☛ Which ministry oversees MPLADS? → Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

q: What was the main objective of the Special Campaign 4.0 launched by the Department of Financial Services in October 2024?
o: To minimise pendency and institutionalise Swachhata
qs.e: In October 2024, the Department of Financial Services launched Special Campaign 4.0 with the main objective of minimising pendency and institutionalising Swachhata. This campaign aimed to enhance efficiency in government offices by focusing on the disposal of pending files, complaints, and records. It emphasized completing tasks within a stipulated timeframe. The department ensured that cleanliness and transparency were maintained across all offices.
qs.kf:
☛ Who launched Special Campaign 4.0? → Department of Financial Services
☛ When was this campaign launched? → October 2024
☛ What was the objective of the campaign? → To minimise pendency and institutionalise Swachhata
☛ Where was this campaign implemented? → Government offices
☛ What was the focus of the campaign? → Disposal of files, complaints, and records

q: When was Swachh Bharat Mission launched?
qs.e: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary. Its goal was to make India open defecation free (ODF) by 2 October 2019. The mission was implemented in two phases: rural (SBM-G) and urban (SBM-U). Under this mission, millions of toilets were constructed, improving sanitation and public health. It is the world's largest cleanliness drive.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of Swachh Bharat Mission? → Prime Minister Narendra Modi
☛ What is the slogan of Swachh Bharat Mission? → Ek Kadam Swachhta Ki Ore
☛ Which ministry funds Swachh Bharat Mission (Rural)? → Ministry of Jal Shakti
☛ Which ministry funds Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ How many toilets were targeted under Swachh Bharat Mission? → 10 crore

q: The Ayushman Bharat Scheme was started in _________ in the year 2018.
qs.e: The Ayushman Bharat Scheme, also known as the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), was launched in the year 2018 from Jharkhand. It is the world's largest health insurance scheme, providing coverage of up to 5 lakh rupees per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. The scheme was inaugurated on 23 September 2018 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand. Although implemented across India, its launch took place in Jharkhand. The scheme aims to benefit over 10 crore poor and vulnerable families.
qs.kf:
☛ Alternate name of Ayushman Bharat Scheme → PM-JAY (Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana)
☛ Launch date of the scheme → 23 September 2018
☛ Insurance cover under the scheme → 5 lakh rupees per family per year
☛ Beneficiary identification basis → Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data
☛ Implementing agency of the scheme → National Health Authority (NHA)

q: What is Vidyanjali project?
o: Volunteers in government schools to help scholastic work
Giving free uniform and clothes to government school children
qs.e: The Vidyanjali project is an initiative by the Government of India that encourages volunteers to assist in scholastic activities in government and aided schools. Its aim is to improve the quality of school education through enhanced community participation. Volunteers can help with teaching, skill development, sports, and co-curricular activities. The program is under the Ministry of Education and aligns with the National Education Policy 2020. Vidyanjali focuses on volunteering, not on tuition, computer instruction, or uniform distribution.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry is Vidyanjali project under? → Ministry of Education
☛ What is the main objective of Vidyanjali? → To increase community participation in schools
☛ Who can become a volunteer in Vidyanjali? → Any Indian citizen (above 18 years)
☛ What is the Vidyanjali portal for? → Volunteer registration and linking with schools
☛ Which policy does Vidyanjali align with? → National Education Policy 2020

q: On which date did the Department of Posts launch the philately scholarship scheme in 2024?
qs.e: The Department of Posts launched the Philately Scholarship Scheme on 24 August 2024. This scheme aims to promote stamp collection (philately) among the youth. Selected students will receive a scholarship of ₹12,000 per annum. The scheme is available for students from classes 6 to 12 in government and recognized private schools across India. The application process will be conducted through a digital platform. The objective of the scheme is to encourage philatelic activities and connect students with postal history.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Philately Scholarship launched? → 24 August 2024
☛ What is the scholarship amount under this scheme? → ₹12,000 per annum
☛ Which classes are eligible for the scheme? → Classes 6 to 12
☛ Who can benefit from the scheme? → Students of government and recognized private schools
☛ Through which medium is the application process conducted? → Digital platform

q: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched on:
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India, launched on 1 May 2016 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh. The scheme aims to provide free LPG connections to poor households, especially women in rural areas, to enable them to use clean cooking fuel and protect their health from smoke-related diseases. It is part of the central government's vision of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas'. Initially, the target was to provide 5 crore LPG connections, which was later increased to 8 crore. Beneficiaries are selected based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data and receive financial support for the first connection and subsidized cylinders.
qs.kf:
☛ PMUY comes under which ministry? → Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
☛ What is the objective of PMUY? → To provide clean fuel (LPG) to poor households
☛ What is the target of LPG connections under PMUY? → 8 crore
☛ How are beneficiaries selected under PMUY? → Based on SECC 2011 data for below poverty line families
☛ Which international award did PMUY receive? → United Nations Award in 2017

q: The 2024 philately scholarship scheme was launched by the Department of Posts under the ______.
qs.e: The 2024 philately scholarship scheme was launched by the Department of Posts under the Deen Dayal SPARSH Yojana. SPARSH stands for Stamp Philately Study and Research Centre. The aim of this scheme is to promote philately (stamp collection) among the youth. The scholarship is offered to students from classes 6 to 9 to encourage their interest in philately. Selected students receive an annual scholarship. This initiative is part of India Post's efforts to promote cultural and educational enrichment through philately.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of SPARSH → Stamp Philately Study and Research Centre
☛ Eligibility for the scheme → Students of classes 6 to 9
☛ Purpose of the scheme → Promote stamp collection
☛ Benefit → Annual scholarship
☛ Implementing department → Department of Posts

q: In which year was the Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB) scheme launched?
qs.e: The Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB) scheme was launched in 2014. It is a national-level initiative aimed at developing basic literacy and numeracy skills among children in early grades, specifically Classes 1 and 2. The scheme is implemented under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan and focuses on helping children acquire foundational reading, writing, and arithmetic skills. The primary goal is to ensure that all children achieve foundational literacy and numeracy by the time they reach Class 3. This centrally sponsored scheme is implemented across all states and union territories to ensure universal access to quality early education.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PBBB scheme launched? → 2014
☛ Full form of PBBB? → Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat
☛ PBBB is under which ministry? → Ministry of Education
☛ PBBB focuses on which classes? → Class 1 and 2
☛ PBBB is part of which mission? → Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan

name: Set 1 · Q1–43
sub: Govt Schemes and Policies - Agriculture, Rural Development & Employment

q: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana was launched in April, 2015 to support and promote-
qs.e: The Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) was launched in April 2015 to promote organic farming. This scheme encourages farmers to use natural and organic inputs instead of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. PKVY aims to improve soil fertility, maintain environmental sustainability, and provide market access for organic products. Under this scheme, farmers receive financial assistance of up to ₹50,000 per hectare. It is a part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA). The scheme focuses on cluster-based approach and certification of organic produce.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana launched? → April 2015
☛ What is the main objective of PKVY? → Promote organic farming
☛ How much assistance is given under PKVY? → ₹50,000 per hectare
☛ Under which mission does PKVY fall? → National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)
☛ What is avoided in organic farming? → Chemical fertilizers and pesticides

q: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swabhiman Yojana launched by Madhya Pradesh government is associated with ____________.
o: 200 days of employment every year to urban youth from economically weaker sections
Financial support to the girls from economically weaker sections
Free education to the children from economically weaker sections
100 days of employment every year to urban youth from economically weaker sections
qs.e: The Mukhyamantri Yuva Swabhiman Yojana launched by the Madhya Pradesh government aims to provide 100 days of employment every year to urban youth from economically weaker sections. Under this scheme, youth aged 18 to 29 years are given skill development and employment opportunities in urban areas. It is implemented to reduce unemployment and promote self-reliance. Payment is made at the minimum wage rate for 100 days of work. The scheme specifically targets youth from economically weaker urban families.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state launched Mukhyamantri Yuva Swabhiman Yojana? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ How many days of employment are provided under this scheme? → 100 days
☛ Who are the beneficiaries of this scheme? → Urban youth aged 18-29 from economically weaker sections
☛ What is the objective of the scheme? → To reduce urban unemployment and promote self-reliance
☛ At what rate is payment made? → Minimum wage rate

q: What is the strategic aim of IRDP?
o: To provide the required input for increasing agricultural productivity
To provide more opportunities for rural employment and credit facilities at concessional rate of interest
qs.e: IRDP stands for Integrated Rural Development Programme, launched in 1978-79. Its primary objective was poverty alleviation and employment generation in rural areas. The programme focused on providing self-employment opportunities to rural poor families by offering them subsidies and bank loans at concessional interest rates. Beneficiaries were assisted in acquiring income-generating assets (such as livestock, shops, or handicraft tools) to create sustainable livelihoods. IRDP was later merged into the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), which further evolved into the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM).
qs.kf:
☛ What does IRDP stand for? → Integrated Rural Development Programme
☛ When was IRDP launched? → 1978-79
☛ What was the main goal of IRDP? → To provide self-employment opportunities to rural poor
☛ At what interest rate were loans provided under IRDP? → Concessional rate
☛ Which scheme replaced IRDP? → Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)

q: E-shakti, a project on digitisation of self-help groups, was launched by ________.
qs.e: The e-Shakti project was launched by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) to digitize self-help groups (SHGs). NABARD is a development bank that focuses on rural financial inclusion and microfinance. Through e-Shakti, SHG transactions were brought onto a digital platform, enhancing transparency and improving credit delivery. This project was a significant step towards women empowerment and digitizing the rural economy. It helped in better monitoring of SHG activities and facilitated easier access to formal credit.
qs.kf:
☛ Who launched the e-Shakti project? → NABARD
☛ What is the objective of e-Shakti? → Digitisation of self-help groups
☛ Where is NABARD headquarters? → Mumbai
☛ When was NABARD established? → 1982
☛ Who benefits from e-Shakti? → Rural self-help groups

q: What is the purpose of the "Samanvay" portal launched by the Ministry of Rural Development?
A. Providing a nomination facility under a social security scheme.
B. Promoting bank finance to start a new business (an entrepreneurial venture).
C. Monitoring the progress and implementation of the Parliament Model Village Scheme.
D. Monitoring the progress and implementation of "Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana".
qs.e: The 'Samanvay' portal was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development with the primary objective of monitoring the progress and implementation of the Parliament Model Village Scheme (SAGY). This portal serves as an online platform that facilitates real-time tracking of the scheme's implementation, activities, and outcomes. It enhances coordination among gram panchayats, district administration, and Members of Parliament. The portal promotes transparency and ensures that the benefits of the scheme reach the targeted beneficiaries. Thus, option 'C' is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched the Samanvay portal? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the purpose of the Samanvay portal? → Monitoring the Parliament Model Village Scheme
☛ When was the Parliament Model Village Scheme launched? → 11 October 2014
☛ How many villages are adopted per MP under SAGY? → Five villages
☛ What type of platform is the Samanvay portal? → Online monitoring platform

q: To provide at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to every household in a financial year for unskilled manual work done by an adult is the objective of which flagship programme of the Government of India?
qs.e: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), enacted in 2005, is a flagship programme of the Government of India. Its objective is to provide at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. This legal guarantee aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by creating durable assets and reducing poverty. Other options: NRHM focuses on healthcare, PMKVY on skill development, and JNNURM on urban infrastructure.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of MGNREGA? → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ When was MGNREGA enacted? → 2005
☛ How many days of employment are guaranteed under MGNREGA? → 100 days
☛ Which sector does MGNREGA focus on? → Rural areas
☛ What is the main objective of MGNREGA? → To provide livelihood security to rural households

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the National Social Assistance Programme?
o: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme
Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme
qs.e: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a centrally sponsored scheme of the Government of India that provides financial assistance to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities living below the poverty line. It consists of five components: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme, Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme, Annapurna, and Maternity Benefit Scheme. AYUSH is a separate ministry and program dealing with Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy, and is not part of NSAP. Hence, the correct answer is 'AYUSH'.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NSAP launched? → 1995
☛ Which ministry administers NSAP? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Objective of Annapurna scheme → Free food grains for the elderly
☛ Beneficiary of IGNDPS → Persons aged 18-79 years with severe disability
☛ Latest NSAP component → Maternity Benefit Scheme (added in 2011)

q: Which flagship programme under the Ministry of Rural Development aims to organise the rural poor women into their own institutions like self-help groups and their federations, producers' collectives etc. and also ensure their financial inclusion and livelihood support?
o: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Programme (MGNREGA)
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
qs.e: DAY-NRLM is a flagship programme under the Ministry of Rural Development that aims to organise rural poor women into self-help groups (SHGs) and their federations, producers’ collectives, etc. Its objective is to ensure financial inclusion and livelihood support for these women by providing access to micro-credit, bank linkages, skill development, and market linkages. Launched in 2011, the mission focuses on empowering women through community institutions and collective action. It plays a crucial role in poverty alleviation and rural development by promoting sustainable livelihoods and financial independence among marginalized women. The programme also emphasizes convergence with other government schemes to enhance impact.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main objective of DAY-NRLM? → To organise rural poor women into self-help groups and provide livelihood support.
☛ When was DAY-NRLM launched? → In 2011.
☛ What types of groups are formed under DAY-NRLM? → Self-help groups (SHGs) and their federations.
☛ What does DAY-NRLM aim to improve? → Financial inclusion and livelihood support.
☛ Under which ministry does DAY-NRLM operate? → Ministry of Rural Development.

q: Name the scheme that the Government of India announced in Budget 2019, which will provide a guaranteed income of Rs. 6,000 per year to small and marginal farmers.
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was announced by Finance Minister Piyush Goyal in the Interim Budget 2019-20. Under this scheme, small and marginal farmers receive an income support of Rs. 6,000 per year, paid in three equal installments. Initially, the scheme was for farmers with up to 2 hectares of land, but later it was extended to all farmers. The objective is to supplement the financial needs of farmers and ensure their livelihood stability. Eligible farmers are identified by state governments, and the amount is directly transferred to their bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
qs.kf:
☛ How much assistance is provided under PM-KISAN per year? → Rs. 6,000
☛ In which budget was PM-KISAN announced? → Interim Budget 2019-20
☛ How many installments are paid under PM-KISAN? → 3 installments
☛ Who are the beneficiaries of PM-KISAN? → All farmers (initially small and marginal)
☛ How is the amount transferred under PM-KISAN? → Directly to bank accounts (DBT)

q: Which of the following is NOT a flagship programme of India?
qs.e: The flagship programmes of India include Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin, National Rural Health Mission, and Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan. These are major central government schemes launched with nationwide coverage. In contrast, the Desert Development Programme is a regional scheme focused on the development of desert areas and is not classified as a flagship programme. Therefore, the Desert Development Programme is NOT a flagship programme of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin → 2009
☛ Launch year of National Rural Health Mission → 2005
☛ Launch year of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan → 2001
☛ Objective of Desert Development Programme → Development of desert areas
☛ Characteristic of flagship programmes → Nationwide coverage

q: Under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana, rice is provided for rupees:
qs.e: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana is a flagship food security scheme of the Government of India, launched in the year 2000. It aims to provide highly subsidized food grains to the poorest of the poor families. Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries receive wheat at Rs. 2 per kg and rice at Rs. 3 per kg. These rates are fixed under the National Food Security Act, 2013. Each Antyodaya family is entitled to 35 kg of food grains per month. The scheme specifically targets the most deprived sections of society to ensure their food security and eliminate hunger.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Antyodaya Anna Yojana launched? → 2000
☛ How much food grain does an Antyodaya family get per month? → 35 kg
☛ What is the price of wheat under this scheme? → Rs. 2 per kg
☛ Under which act is this scheme governed? → National Food Security Act, 2013
☛ What is the main objective of Antyodaya Anna Yojana? → To provide subsidized food to the poorest families

q: The UN system is based on six principal organs. Which of the following organs does NOT come under it?
o: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
qs.e: The United Nations has six principal organs: the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Secretariat, International Court of Justice, and Trusteeship Council. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is a specialized agency, part of the UN system but not a principal organ. FAO was established in 1945 and is headquartered in Rome. It focuses on food security and agricultural development. The other options—Economic and Social Council, UN Secretariat, and International Court of Justice—are among the six principal organs. Therefore, FAO is not included.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of principal organs of UN → 6
☛ Principal judicial organ of UN → International Court of Justice
☛ Head of UN Secretariat → Secretary-General
☛ Members of Economic and Social Council → 54
☛ Headquarters of FAO → Rome

q: Rythu Bandhu scheme is the scheme of which of the following states?
qs.e: The Rythu Bandhu scheme is a farmer welfare initiative launched by the Telangana government in 2018. Under this scheme, farmers receive direct financial assistance per acre of land through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to their bank accounts. The aim is to provide initial investment support to farmers for crop cultivation. The scheme covers both Kharif and Rabi seasons, offering ₹5,000 per acre per season. This scheme is unique to Telangana and is not implemented in Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, or Tamil Nadu with the same name.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Rythu Bandhu scheme launched? → 2018
☛ What is the amount given per acre under Rythu Bandhu? → ₹5,000 per crop
☛ Rythu Bandhu scheme belongs to which state? → Telangana
☛ How many crop seasons are covered under Rythu Bandhu? → Two (Kharif and Rabi)
☛ What is the mode of payment in Rythu Bandhu? → Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)

q: The Department of Posts has launched a scheme called _______ to ensure universal coverage of flagship postal schemes in rural areas of the country in Sept, 2020.
qs.e: The Department of Posts launched the 'Five Star Villages' scheme in September 2020 to ensure universal coverage of flagship postal schemes in rural areas. Under this scheme, villages are given star ratings based on the availability of postal services. Five stars indicate that all major postal services, such as savings accounts, RD, PPF, postal life insurance, and basic postal services, are available. The scheme promotes financial inclusion in rural areas.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Five Star Villages scheme launched? → September 2020
☛ What is the aim of the scheme? → Universal coverage of postal schemes in rural areas
☛ What does five stars signify? → All major postal services are available
☛ Which services are included under the scheme? → Savings account, RD, PPF, postal life insurance
☛ Who benefits from the scheme? → Residents of rural areas

q: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana was launched in _________.
qs.e: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is a flagship skill development scheme of the Government of India, launched to provide employment opportunities to rural youth. It was launched on 25 September 2014 by the Ministry of Rural Development. The scheme aims to train poor youth aged 15-35 years from rural areas to prepare them for wage employment or self-employment. It is a part of the Livelihood Mission and is implemented under the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM). DDU-GKY guarantees placement to trained youth. The scheme is named after the renowned Indian politician Deen Dayal Upadhyaya.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of DDU-GKY? → Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
☛ Which ministry implements DDU-GKY? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the target age group for DDU-GKY? → 15-35 years
☛ DDU-GKY is a part of which mission? → National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)
☛ What is the mascot of DDU-GKY? → Kaushal Bharat

q: Which political party was in power in England when the Cabinet Mission came to India?
qs.e: When the Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946, the Labour Party was in power in England, with Clement Attlee as Prime Minister. The mission consisted of three members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander. Its purpose was to devise a plan for the formation of a Constituent Assembly and the transfer of power in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the British Prime Minister during the Cabinet Mission? → Clement Attlee
☛ Who were the three members of the Cabinet Mission? → Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander
☛ What was the objective of the Cabinet Mission? → To plan the formation of the Constituent Assembly in India
☛ What step did the Labour Party take regarding Indian independence? → Passed the Indian Independence Act 1947
☛ What was the proposal of provincial groups in the Cabinet Mission Plan? → Suggestion to create three groups (A, B, C)

q: Which of the following is NOT a UN Agenda for Sustainable Development 2030?
o: Reduce the total population of the world by \(\frac{1}{3}\)rd
End poverty in all its forms everywhere
Reduce inequality within and among nations
qs.e: The United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted in 2015 by all UN member states, sets out 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). These goals focus on ending poverty, achieving food security, reducing inequality, climate action, and peace. There is no goal related to reducing population. Option 1, 'Reduce the total population of the world by 1/3rd', is not part of any SDG. The other three options correspond to SDG 2 (ending hunger), SDG 1 (ending poverty), and SDG 10 (reducing inequality), respectively. Hence, this option is not part of the UN Agenda for Sustainable Development 2030.
qs.kf:
☛ Total number of UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) → 17
☛ Objective of SDG 2 → End hunger and achieve food security by 2030
☛ Objective of SDG 10 → Reduce inequality within and among countries
☛ Objective of SDG 1 → End poverty in all its forms everywhere
☛ When did the 2030 Agenda come into effect → 1 January 2016

q: Which of the following is INCORRECT about Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)?
o: It was launched to promote organic farming.
In three years 2,00,000 clusters will be formed.
Every farmer under this scheme will be provided Rs. 20,000 per acre in three years for seeds, to harvest the crops and to transport the produce.
qs.e: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) was launched in April 2015 to promote organic farming. The target was to form 10,000 clusters over three years, not 2,00,000. Each cluster covers 50 acres or 20 hectares of land. Under the scheme, farmers receive financial assistance of Rs. 20,000 per acre over three years for seeds, harvesting, and transportation. The scheme aims to reduce chemical fertilizers and pesticides, enhancing soil health and environmental sustainability.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the target number of clusters under PKVY? → 10,000 clusters
☛ What area does each cluster cover? → 50 acres or 20 hectares
☛ How much assistance is provided per acre? → Rs. 20,000 (over three years)
☛ Which ministry implements PKVY? → Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare
☛ What is the objective of PKVY? → To promote organic farming

q: National Skill Development Mission was launched by the Prime Minister of India in:
qs.e: The National Skill Development Mission (NSDM) was launched on 15 July 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The mission aims to accelerate skill development in India and create employment opportunities. It is a key part of the Skill India campaign, which targets training 400 million people by 2022. Under NSDM, several sub-missions and schemes operate, notably the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). A separate ministry, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), was formed in 2014, but the mission itself was launched in 2015. NSDM coordinates skill development efforts across various sectors and government departments, focusing on entrepreneurship, vocational training, and industry partnerships.
qs.kf:
☛ National Skill Development Mission launched → 2015
☛ Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana started → 2015
☛ Skill Development Ministry formed → 2014
☛ Skill India campaign target → 400 million trained by 2022
☛ NSDM objective → coordinate skill development efforts

q: Which of the following is CORRECT statement for Kishor category under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana?
o: Loan to small businessmen from 35 thousand up to 7.5 lakhs
Loan to small businessmen from 50 thousand up to 5 lakhs
Loan to small business from 75 thousand up to 15 lakhs
Loan to small businessmen from 25 thousand up to 5 lakhs
qs.e: Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), there are three categories: Shishu (0-50,000 rupees), Kishor (50,000-5 lakh rupees), and Tarun (5-10 lakh rupees). The Kishor category provides loans from 50 thousand to 5 lakh rupees to small businessmen. This scheme was launched in 2015 to provide financial support to non-corporate, non-farm small enterprises. Its objective is to promote self-employment and entrepreneurship. The Kishor category is for businesses that are slightly more established and require higher capital. The interest rate is market-based, and no subsidy is provided. The scheme is implemented through banks, NBFCs, and microfinance institutions.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the loan limit for Shishu category under PMMY? → 0 to 50,000 rupees
☛ What is the loan limit for Tarun category under PMMY? → 5 lakh to 10 lakh rupees
☛ When was PMMY launched? → In 2015
☛ Which type of enterprises are covered under PMMY? → Non-corporate, non-farm small enterprises
☛ What is the full form of PMMY? → Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana

q: What is the amount provided per year to the farmers holding up to 2 hectre under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Siddhi (PMKSS)?
qs.e: Under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Siddhi (PMKISAN) scheme, farmers with up to 2 hectares of land are provided financial assistance of 6000 Rupees per year. The amount is disbursed in three equal installments of 2000 Rupees each. The scheme aims to supplement the income of small and marginal farmers. It was launched in 2019 and is implemented by the central government. Eligible farmers must own up to 2 hectares of agricultural land.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of launch of PMKISAN scheme → 2019
☛ Annual assistance amount → 6000 Rupees
☛ Amount per installment → 2000 Rupees
☛ Land ceiling for eligibility → 2 hectares
☛ Implementing ministry → Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

q: _____ was started in 2002, for ensuring drinking water supply to all villages.
qs.e: Swajaldhara Yojana was started in 2002 to ensure drinking water supply in all villages. This scheme was launched by the central government to provide safe drinking water in rural areas. Under this scheme, village panchayats were given the responsibility of managing the water supply system. Later, it was merged into the National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP). The objective of Swajaldhara was to implement water supply projects with community participation.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swajaldhara Yojana launched? → 2002
☛ What was the main objective of Swajaldhara? → Ensuring drinking water supply in villages
☛ Who was responsible for managing water supply under Swajaldhara? → Gram Panchayat
☛ Which programme later included Swajaldhara? → National Rural Drinking Water Programme
☛ What was the key principle of Swajaldhara? → Community participation

q: Rural Employment Generation Program (REGP) was started in _____.
qs.e: The Rural Employment Generation Program (REGP) was launched in the year 1995. This program was initiated by the Government of India to create employment opportunities in rural areas and to alleviate poverty. REGP was implemented through the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). Its main objective was to promote the establishment of micro and small enterprises in rural regions. The program played a crucial role in employment generation and livelihood enhancement. Later, it was merged into the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Program (PMEGP).
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was REGP launched? → 1995
☛ REGP was implemented by which body? → KVIC
☛ What was the objective of REGP? → Rural employment generation and poverty alleviation
☛ REGP was later merged into which scheme? → PMEGP
☛ Full form of REGP? → Rural Employment Generation Program

q: Which of the following programs are aimed at building self-employment opportunities in rural areas and small towns?
qs.e: The Rural Employment Generation Program (REGP) was launched by the Government of India in 1995 with the primary objective of creating self-employment opportunities in rural areas and small towns. It is implemented through the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME). REGP provides loans and subsidies to unemployed youth to set up micro-enterprises, thereby strengthening the rural economy and reducing migration. Other options: PMGY focuses on rural infrastructure, PMJDY aims at financial inclusion, and SGSY (now NRLM) also promotes self-employment but REGP is specifically targeted at rural and small urban areas. This program has been instrumental in generating sustainable livelihoods and promoting entrepreneurship in non-farm sectors.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of REGP? → Rural Employment Generation Program
☛ In which year was REGP launched? → 1995
☛ Under which ministry does REGP come? → Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
☛ Through which agency is REGP implemented? → Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)
☛ What is the main objective of REGP? → To create self-employment opportunities in rural areas and small towns

q: Antyodaya Anna Yojana was started in which Year?
qs.e: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) is a major food security scheme of the Government of India, launched on 25 December 2000 by the then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The scheme aims to provide subsidized food grains to the poorest families among the Below Poverty Line (BPL) households. Eligible families receive 35 kg of wheat and rice per month. The scheme is operated under the Public Distribution System (PDS). Later, it was incorporated into the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013. AAY was initially launched to cover 1 crore families.
qs.kf:
☛ How much food grain is provided per month under Antyodaya Anna Yojana? → 35 kg
☛ Under which system is Antyodaya Anna Yojana operated? → Public Distribution System (PDS)
☛ Under which Act was Antyodaya Anna Yojana included? → National Food Security Act, 2013
☛ Who launched Antyodaya Anna Yojana? → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ On which date was Antyodaya Anna Yojana launched? → 25 December 2000

q: In which year did the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) begin?
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched on 25 December 2000 by the then Prime Minister of India, Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The primary objective of this scheme is to improve connectivity in rural areas and connect unconnected villages with all-weather roads. PMGSY aims to provide road connectivity to villages with a population of more than 1000, thereby boosting rural development and enhancing access to basic amenities.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMGSY launched? → 2000
☛ What is the objective of PMGSY? → To provide road connectivity to rural villages
☛ Who launched PMGSY? → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ Which population villages are prioritized under PMGSY? → More than 1000
☛ Date of launch of PMGSY? → 25 December 2000

q: Which of the following programs provides state-of-the-art central assistance to basic services such as primary health, primary education, rural shelter, rural drinking water and rural electrification?
qs.e: Prime Minister Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) was launched in 2000-01. Its objective is to provide central assistance for basic services in rural areas, including primary health, primary education, rural shelter, rural drinking water, and rural electrification. This scheme provides additional resources to states to improve these services. Among other options, SGSY is related to self-employment, PMJDY to financial inclusion, and AAY to food security. Hence, the correct answer is PMGY.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMGY → Prime Minister Gramodaya Yojana
☛ Objective of PMGY → Central assistance for rural basic services
☛ PMGY launched in → 2000-01
☛ Services under PMGY → Primary health, education, shelter, drinking water, electrification
☛ Ministry handling PMGY → Ministry of Rural Development

q: Which Ministry of Indian Government launched the "Startup India Scheme"?
qs.e: The 'Startup India' scheme was launched on 16 January 2016 by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. This initiative aims to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in India, create a favorable ecosystem for startups, and generate employment opportunities. Under this scheme, startups receive benefits such as tax exemptions, funding support, fast-track patent filing, and simplified regulations. The scheme has strengthened the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' campaign and positioned India as a global startup hub.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Startup India launched? → 16 January 2016
☛ Which fund provides loan guarantees under Startup India? → Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
☛ How many years of tax exemption are available under Startup India? → 3 years
☛ What is the main objective of Startup India? → To promote innovation and entrepreneurship
☛ Startup India is part of which national campaign? → Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan

q: Which year did the Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment (TRYSEM) take place?
qs.e: The TRYSEM (Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment) scheme was launched on 15 August 1979. Its objective was to provide skill training to rural youth (aged 18-35) to enable them for self-employment. Implemented under the Ministry of Rural Development, it was later merged with the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY). TRYSEM aimed to reduce unemployment in rural areas and promote self-reliance. After training, beneficiaries were provided bank loans and subsidies to create employment opportunities.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of TRYSEM → Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment
☛ Launch year of TRYSEM → 1979
☛ Objective of TRYSEM → To provide skill training to rural youth for self-employment
☛ TRYSEM merged with → Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
☛ Age limit under TRYSEM → 18 to 35 years

q: Which scheme is redesigned as Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana(SGSY)?
qs.e: The Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was redesigned and relaunched as the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) in 2011. The objective of this scheme is to provide self-employment opportunities to rural poor families and improve their livelihoods. NRLM primarily focuses on empowering women through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and promoting rural financial inclusion. The Prime Minister's Employment Plan (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Program (REGP) are separate schemes, while the Prime Minister Twenty Point Program is a broad economic program. Hence, the correct answer is the National Rural Livelihood Mission.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NRLM → National Rural Livelihood Mission
☛ Launch year of NRLM → 2011
☛ Objective of NRLM → Improve livelihoods of rural poor
☛ Key vehicle of NRLM → Self-Help Groups (SHGs)
☛ Focus of NRLM → Women empowerment and financial inclusion

q: Employment Assurance Scheme was started in which year?
qs.e: The Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) was a employment generation scheme launched by the Government of India. It was introduced in the year 1993. The scheme aimed to provide employment on demand to unemployed people in rural areas. Initially, it was implemented in selected backward blocks and later expanded to the entire country. Its objective was to reduce rural unemployment and provide livelihood security. Later, it was merged with MGNREGA in 2005.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Employment Assurance Scheme started? → 1993
☛ Which area did this scheme focus on? → Rural areas
☛ Into which scheme was it later merged? → MGNREGA (2005)
☛ Which ministry implemented it? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What type of employment did it provide? → Employment on demand

q: What is the minimum number of days of employment provided by Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme?
qs.e: Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA), every household is guaranteed at least 100 days of employment in a financial year. This scheme was launched in 2005 with the aim of ensuring employment in rural areas. If employment is not provided, the government pays an unemployment allowance. The scheme comes under the Ministry of Rural Development.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of MGNREGA → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Launch year of MGNREGA → 2005
☛ Guaranteed days of employment → 100 days
☛ Who provides unemployment allowance → State government
☛ Objective of scheme → To ensure employment in rural areas

q: The Prime Minister's Employment Plan began in __________.
qs.e: The Prime Minister's Employment Plan (PMRY) was launched in 1993 by the Government of India to provide self-employment opportunities to educated unemployed youth. It remained operational from 1993 to 2007, after which it was merged into the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP). Under PMRY, loans up to ₹10 lakh were provided, with 15% margin money subsidized by the government. The scheme targeted youth aged 18-35 years, with preference given to women, SC/ST, and backward classes. PMRY played a key role in promoting entrepreneurship among educated youth in both urban and rural areas.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the urban employment scheme launched? → 1990 (Jawahar Rozgar Yojana)
☛ When was the rural employment scheme launched? → 2006 (NREGA)
☛ What is the full form of PMRY? → Prime Minister's Employment Plan
☛ What was the maximum loan limit under PMRY? → ₹10 lakh
☛ Into which scheme was PMRY merged? → PMEGP (2008)

q: Which of the following schemes/programmes is/are mainly aimed to bring inclusive growth in India?
qs.e: Inclusive growth means that the benefits of economic development reach all sections of society, especially the weaker and disadvantaged groups. MGNREGA (2005) provides a legal guarantee of 100 days of employment to rural households, improving rural income and livelihoods. Swabhimaan Yojana (2015) promotes financial inclusion by providing banking facilities in rural areas through bank branches. Both schemes directly target the rural poor, while RTI enhances transparency and accountability but does not directly lead to economic inclusion. Therefore, 'Swabhimaan and MGNREGA' both serve the main objective of inclusive growth.
qs.kf:
☛ MGNREGA full form → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ MGNREGA employment guarantee → 100 days per financial year
☛ Swabhimaan objective → To provide banking facilities in rural areas
☛ Inclusive growth main goal → Reduce income inequality and reach benefits to poor
☛ RTI main objective → Enhance transparency by giving right to information

q: Which of the following is a government programme meant to reduce poverty in India?
qs.e: NRLM, or National Rural Livelihoods Mission, is a flagship government program launched in 2011 to reduce poverty in rural India. It aims to empower poor households by organizing them into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and providing them with livelihood opportunities. Other options are not primarily poverty alleviation schemes: Digital India focuses on digital infrastructure, Green Revolution on agricultural productivity, and Make in India on manufacturing. Thus, NRLM is the correct choice.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NRLM? → National Rural Livelihoods Mission
☛ When was NRLM launched? → 2011
☛ What is the main objective of NRLM? → Rural poverty reduction and livelihood promotion
☛ Which ministry implements NRLM? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the key organizational unit under NRLM? → Self-Help Group (SHG)

q: What is the goal of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: Ensure at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year.
qs.e: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) aims to provide at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households. Enacted in 2005, it seeks to enhance livelihood security in rural areas. The scheme includes works like water conservation, land development, afforestation, and rural roads. It is a legal right that guarantees employment within 15 days of demand. MGNREGA helps in poverty alleviation and rural infrastructure development. It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development and ensures women's participation of at least one-third. Wage payments are made directly into bank or post office accounts.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the mascot of MGNREGA? → Gaanv ki Garima
☛ What is the women's representation in MGNREGA? → At least one-third
☛ How are wages paid under MGNREGA? → Direct transfer to bank/post office accounts
☛ Which ministry implements MGNREGA? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the main focus of MGNREGA? → Sustainable livelihood and rural development

q: Which of these programmes aims to improve the physical infrastructure in rural areas?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India aimed at providing road connectivity and improving physical infrastructure in rural areas. Launched in 2000 under the leadership of then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, PMGSY focuses on connecting rural areas to markets, education, and health facilities, thereby promoting economic development. In contrast, Smart Cities Mission focuses on urban development, Digital India promotes digital services, and Make in India emphasizes manufacturing. Therefore, PMGSY is the correct choice for improving rural physical infrastructure.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMGSY launched? → 2000
☛ What is the full form of PMGSY? → Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
☛ What is the objective of PMGSY? → To provide road connectivity to unconnected villages
☛ Under which ministry does PMGSY come? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What type of infrastructure does PMGSY target? → Physical infrastructure

q: The National Rural Livelihood Mission was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, in the year ________.
qs.e: The National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, in the year 2011. Its objective is to provide livelihood opportunities to rural poor families and increase their income. NRLM organizes the poor through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations, enabling them to collectively access credit, markets, and skill development. This mission is a key poverty alleviation program and was later renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihood Mission (DAY-NRLM).
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of NRLM → 2011
☛ Full name of NRLM → Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihood Mission
☛ Nodal Ministry → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Main implementation unit → Self-Help Groups (SHGs)
☛ Objective → Improving livelihoods of rural poor

q: Which of the following was launched to support farmers and enhance agricultural productivity in 2000?
qs.e: The National Agriculture Policy was launched in 2000 by the Government of India to support farmers and enhance agricultural productivity. Its objectives included sustainable agricultural growth, doubling farmers' income, and strengthening food security. The policy emphasized agricultural credit, irrigation, seed distribution, and technical assistance.
