Other options: Operation Flood (1970) was for dairy development, Green Revolution (1960s) focused on food grain production, and Rural Employment Generation Programme was launched later. Thus, the National Agriculture Policy of 2000 is the correct choice.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the National Agriculture Policy implemented? → 2000
☛ Which policy aims to double farmers' income? → National Agriculture Policy
☛ When did the Green Revolution start in India? → 1960s
☛ What was the objective of Operation Flood? → Boost dairy production
☛ Which program relates to rural employment? → Rural Employment Generation Programme

q: The Government of India had launched Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) in the year _____ for the rural areas with the objectives of electrification of all un-electrified villages, as per Census 2011.
qs.e: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) was launched by the Government of India in 2014. Its primary objective was to electrify all un-electrified villages in rural areas as per the 2011 Census. This scheme succeeded the earlier Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY). DDUGJY focused on strengthening rural power supply, improving metering and billing, and promoting renewable energy sources. The implementation of this scheme enabled millions of villages to gain access to electricity, boosting rural development and quality of life.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of DDUGJY → 2014
☛ Objective of DDUGJY → Electrification of all un-electrified villages
☛ Predecessor scheme → Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY)
☛ Basis for village identification → 2011 Census
☛ Merger of DDUGJY → Merged with Saubhagya scheme in 2018

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Pradhan Mantri Grammen Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)?

1. PMGSY is a 100% centrally sponsored scheme. 2. This schemes connect the unconnected habitats of rural areas with a population 500 persons and above in plain areas. 3. This scheme is not applicable to hilly areas and North East states.
qs.e: PMGSY is a centrally sponsored scheme, but it is not 100% centrally sponsored; it involves both central and state funds. Hence statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 is correct: the scheme connects unconnected habitats in rural areas with a population of 500 persons and above in plain areas. Statement 3 is incorrect: the scheme is also applicable to hilly areas, North East states, and other difficult areas, where the population threshold may be 250 or less. PMGSY aims to enhance rural connectivity.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMGSY → Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
☛ Objective of PMGSY → To connect unconnected rural habitats with all-weather roads
☛ Population threshold in plain areas → 500 persons
☛ Population threshold in hilly/North East areas → 250 persons
☛ Year of launch of PMGSY → 2000

q: The Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana and Employment Assurance Scheme were merged into _________ in 2001.
qs.e: This is an employment generation scheme launched in 2001 by merging Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana and Employment Assurance Scheme. Its objective was to provide employment and create basic infrastructure in rural areas. It was implemented by the Government of India and later subsumed under MNREGA in 2006.
qs.kf:
☛ Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana → Launched in 1999.
☛ MNREGA → Launched in 2006.
☛ Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana → Launched in 1999.
☛ Employment Assurance Scheme → Launched in 1993.
☛ DWACRA → Women self-help group scheme.

q: Which of the following are the main objectives of the Community Development Programme?
1. Due recognition was given to the importance of planning
2. Recognition was also given to recruitment of trained personnel
3. It introduced modern technologies in agriculture
qs.e: The Community Development Programme (launched in 1952) aimed at holistic development of rural areas. It gave due recognition to planning for efficient resource utilization. Recruitment of trained personnel was recognized to ensure effective implementation. It also introduced modern technologies in agriculture such as improved seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation methods, boosting productivity. All three objectives were integral to the programme, which strengthened the rural economy.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of launch of Community Development Programme → 1952
☛ Main focus area → Rural development
☛ Example of modern technology in agriculture → High-yield variety seeds
☛ Role of trained personnel → Implementation and monitoring
☛ Initiated by → Planning Commission

name: Set 2 · Q44–86
sub: Govt Schemes and Policies - Agriculture, Rural Development & Employment

q: Which of the following schemes focuses on rural employment?
qs.e: MNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India focused on providing rural employment. Under this scheme, adult members of rural households are guaranteed 100 days of wage employment in a financial year. It aims to secure rural livelihoods and develop rural infrastructure. This scheme was launched in 2006 and provides a legal right to employment. Other options like Swachh Bharat Mission focus on sanitation, Digital India on digitization, and GST on tax reforms, not employment.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of MNREGA → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Year of launch of MNREGA → 2006
☛ Guaranteed employment days under MNREGA → 100 days per household per year
☛ Objective of MNREGA → Rural employment and livelihood security
☛ MNREGA is based on which right → Legal right (Right to Employment)

q: During which of the following periods will Phase IV of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana be implemented?
qs.e: Phase IV of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) will be implemented from FY 2024-25 to FY 2028-29. This phase aims to strengthen rural road connectivity by constructing over 25,000 km of roads. The scheme comes under the Ministry of Rural Development and focuses on connecting unconnected habitations. PMGSY was launched in 2000 and has been pivotal in improving rural infrastructure. Phase IV will prioritize tribal and backward areas to ensure inclusive development.
qs.kf:
☛ PMGSY launched → 2000
☛ PMGSY Phase IV duration → 2024-25 to 2028-29
☛ PMGSY Phase IV coverage → over 25,000 km roads
☛ PMGSY nodal ministry → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ PMGSY objective → provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations

q: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) were merged in April 1989 with the __________ scheme.
qs.e: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) were merged in April 1989 into the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). JRY aimed at creating employment and developing infrastructure in rural areas. It was implemented through Panchayati Raj institutions. Later, it was subsumed under the Rural Employment Programme (REP). NREP was launched in 1980 and RLEGP in 1983. The merger aimed to create a more effective employment programme. JRY was named after Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NREP launched? → 1980
☛ When was RLEGP launched? → 1983
☛ What is the full form of JRY? → Jawahar Rozgar Yojana
☛ After whom is JRY named? → Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ Which institutions implemented JRY? → Panchayati Raj institutions

q: The Pradhan Mantri Grammen Sadak Yojana was launched in the year _____________.
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Grammen Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India launched on December 25, 2000 by the then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The scheme aims to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations in rural areas. It is implemented under the Ministry of Rural Development. The primary target is to connect villages with a population of 500 or more. PMGSY was later extended as Pradhan Mantri Grammen Sadak Yojana- II to include higher standards and upgrades.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of PMGSY → 2000
☛ Prime Minister who launched PMGSY → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ Ministry responsible for PMGSY → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Main objective of PMGSY → Rural road connectivity
☛ Phase II of PMGSY launched in → 2013

q: Which of the following is a government scheme for rural employment in India?
o: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
qs.e: This scheme is designed to provide employment in rural areas. Under this act, every household is guaranteed 100 days of employment in a financial year. It is a demand-driven scheme, where work must be provided within 15 days of application. MGNREGA was enacted in 2005 and also aims to develop rural infrastructure. It provides social security to workers and reduces migration from rural areas. Other options include Skill India (skill development), Swachh Bharat (sanitation), and Ayushman Bharat (health insurance), which are not directly related to rural employment.
qs.kf:
☛ When was MGNREGA implemented? → 2005
☛ How many days of employment per household under MGNREGA? → 100 days
☛ What type of scheme is MGNREGA? → Demand-driven
☛ Full form of MGNREGA? → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Objective of MGNREGA? → Ensure rural employment

q: In which of the following years was the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) launched by the Government of India to provide connectivity to unconnected habitations as part of a poverty reduction strategy?
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched by the Government of India on 25 December 2000. Its main objective is to provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations in rural areas as part of a poverty reduction strategy. The scheme comes under the Ministry of Rural Development and is fully funded by the central government. PMGSY initially targeted connecting villages with a population of 500 or more (250 in hilly regions). Over the years, the scheme has been instrumental in enhancing access to education, healthcare, and markets for rural communities, thereby reducing poverty. PMGSY is a flagship program for rural infrastructure and inclusive growth.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMGSY launched? → 25 December 2000
☛ Which ministry implements PMGSY? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the funding pattern of PMGSY? → 100% central funding
☛ What is the main objective of PMGSY? > To provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations
☛ What is the population criterion for PMGSY in plain areas? → 500 persons

q: Rural infrastructure development is crucial to improve connectivity and access to markets and services. Which scheme focuses on providing all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations?
o: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched in the year 2000. Its objective is to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations. This scheme is crucial for rural infrastructure development, helping farmers access markets and essential services like education and healthcare. Currently, the third phase (PMGSY-III) is underway, aiming to construct 2 lakh km of roads by 2030.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana → 2000
☛ Target year for road construction under PMGSY-III → 2030
☛ Type of roads constructed under PMGSY → All-weather roads
☛ Full form of PMGSY → Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
☛ Main objective of PMGSY → Provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations

q: The 'Special Food Grain Production Programme (SFPP) on Pulses' was implemented during the year ______.
qs.e: The Special Food Grain Production Programme (SFPP) on Pulses was implemented during the year 1988-89. This programme was launched to boost the production of pulses, which are a key source of protein in the Indian diet. Under this scheme, farmers were provided with improved seeds, fertilizers, and technical support. The objective of SFPP was to achieve self-sufficiency in pulse production. It came after the Green Revolution era, when food grain production had increased significantly, but pulse production lagged behind. The programme helped in improving the area and productivity of pulses in India.
qs.kf:
☛ SFPP on pulses was launched in which year? → 1988-89
☛ Which crop group was targeted under SFPP? → Pulses
☛ What was the main goal of SFPP? → To increase pulse production and reduce imports
☛ Which ministry implemented SFPP? → Ministry of Agriculture
☛ What kind of assistance was given to farmers under SFPP? → Improved seeds, fertilizers, and technology

q: Who initiated the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)?
qs.e: The Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) was initiated by the Central Government on 25th September 2001. The aim of this scheme was to generate employment in rural areas and provide food security. It was formed by merging the earlier employment schemes like Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) and Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS). Under SGRY, the target was to provide at least 100 days of employment per year to the rural poor. The financial contribution between the central and state governments was in the ratio of 75:25. Later, in 2006, it was merged into the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA). SGRY focused on rural infrastructure development and employment generation.
qs.kf:
☛ Ministry implementing SGRY → Ministry of Rural Development (Central Government)
☛ Objective of SGRY → Additional employment generation and food security in rural areas
☛ Centre-State ratio for SGRY → 75:25
☛ Year SGRY merged → 2006, into NREGA
☛ Predecessor schemes of SGRY → Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) and Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS)

q: What was the main aim of TRYSEM (Training for Rural Youth for Self-Employment)?
o: Offering free education in rural areas
Upgrading skills of rural youth to tackle unemployment
qs.e: The main aim of TRYSEM was to train rural youth for self-employment, thereby reducing unemployment. Launched in 1979, it later merged with the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY). Under this scheme, rural youth were provided training in various trades to make them self-reliant. The scheme focused on poverty alleviation and employment generation by upgrading the skills of rural youth.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of TRYSEM → Training for Rural Youth for Self-Employment
☛ When was TRYSEM launched? → 1979
☛ Objective of TRYSEM → Training rural youth for self-employment
☛ Which scheme did TRYSEM merge into? → Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
☛ TRYSEM was under which ministry? → Ministry of Rural Development

q: What was the main aim of IRDP (Integrated Rural Development Programme) ?
o: To provide free food to rural families
To assist poor rural families in acquiring assets or skills for self-employment
qs.e: The Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) was launched in 1978-79. Its main aim was to provide self-employment opportunities to rural families living below the poverty line (BPL). The programme helped beneficiaries acquire income-generating assets like livestock, small shops, or skills training. The goal was to increase their income and lift them out of poverty. IRDP was later merged into the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), which is now part of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM).
qs.kf:
☛ When was IRDP launched? → 1978-79
☛ Who was the target group of IRDP? → Rural families below poverty line (BPL)
☛ What kind of assistance was given under IRDP? → Assets or skills for self-employment
☛ Which scheme succeeded IRDP? → Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
☛ Which ministry implemented IRDP? → Ministry of Rural Development

q: Which of the following is the primary objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM)?
o: Development of rural clusters with urban-like facilities
Ensuring 100 days of wage employment in rural areas
qs.e: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM) was launched in 2016. Its primary objective is to provide urban-like basic facilities in rural areas, thereby boosting the rural economy and reducing migration to cities. This mission identifies rural clusters and develops them with necessary physical, social, and economic infrastructure. It includes facilities like roads, water supply, electricity, education, and healthcare. The mission is under the Ministry of Rural Development and aims to ensure balanced development in rural areas. Other options like electrification or skill development are part of the mission but not its primary objective.
qs.kf:
☛ Main objective of SPMRM → Providing urban facilities in rural clusters
☛ When was SPMRM launched → 2016
☛ Which ministry oversees SPMRM → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Goal of SPMRM → Reducing the gap between rural and urban areas
☛ Basis for cluster selection in SPMRM → Population and lack of basic infrastructure

q: When was the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) launched?
qs.e: The Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was launched by the Government of India on 15 August 1983. Its aim was to provide employment to landless workers in rural areas. This programme was launched during the tenure of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. RLEGP focused on developing rural infrastructure such as roads, irrigation, and community buildings. Later in 1989, it was merged with Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). It was a significant step towards creating employment opportunities for the rural poor.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of RLEGP? → Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme
☛ In which year was RLEGP launched? → 1983
☛ What was the objective of RLEGP? → To provide employment to landless rural workers
☛ Into which scheme was RLEGP merged? → Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)
☛ Under which Prime Minister was RLEGP launched? → Indira Gandhi

q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provides legal assurance of wage employment in rural areas. Under MGNREGA, how many days of guaranteed wage employment per year is a rural household entitled to?
qs.e: According to the MGNREGA Act, 2005, every rural household is entitled to 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year. This Act provides a legal right to employment for adult members in rural areas. If employment is not provided within 15 days of application, the government is required to pay an unemployment allowance. The scheme is implemented through Gram Panchayats and primarily involves unskilled manual labor. The objective is to ensure livelihood security and reduce poverty in rural areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Guaranteed employment days under MGNREGA → 100 days
☛ Full name of MGNREGA → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Year MGNREGA was enacted → 2005
☛ Time limit for unemployment allowance → 15 days after application
☛ Implementing body of MGNREGA → Gram Panchayat

q: Who among the following are eligible for the training programs under Deen Dayal Upadhyay – Gramin Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)?
o: Individuals between the ages of 15 and 35 years
Individuals between the ages of 15 and 25 years
Individuals between the ages of 18 and 35 years
Individuals between the ages of 25 and 55 years
qs.e: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gramin Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is a flagship skill training scheme of the Government of India aimed at making rural youth employable. The eligibility age for training programs under this scheme is 15 to 35 years. This age range covers a majority of the rural youth population. Additionally, the beneficiary should not be availing benefits of any other skill development scheme run by the Government of India. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. Training programs include pre-placement training and placement assistance.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of DDU-GKY → Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gramin Kaushalya Yojana
☛ Implementing Ministry → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Eligibility age → 15 to 35 years
☛ Condition on other schemes → Not availing other skill schemes
☛ Objective → To make rural youth employable through skill training

q: Where is the primary focus of the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)?
qs.e: The primary focus of the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) is on rural areas to provide employment and food security. Launched in 2001, the scheme aimed to generate wage employment and create durable assets in rural India. It was implemented through Panchayati Raj Institutions. Later, SGRY was merged with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). Key activities included road construction, water conservation, and school building. The scheme focused on strengthening the rural economy and reducing poverty by providing 100 days of employment. SGRY targeted the most vulnerable sections, ensuring minimum wages and equal pay for men and women.
qs.kf:
☛ When was SGRY launched? → 2001
☛ What was the objective of SGRY? → Rural employment and food security
☛ Which scheme merged with SGRY? → MGNREGA
☛ Through which institutions was SGRY implemented? → Panchayati Raj Institutions
☛ What were priority works under SGRY? → Roads, water conservation, building construction

q: Which of the following schemes focuses on providing rural connectivity through allweather roads?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched in the year 2000 with the objective of providing all-weather road connectivity to rural areas. This scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development and its main focus is to connect unconnected villages with a population of more than 500 through all-weather roads. PMGSY has significantly boosted the rural economy by improving access to markets and social services like education and healthcare. The scheme emphasizes construction, maintenance, and upgradation of rural roads. Funding is shared between central and state governments. In contrast, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin deals with housing, RURBAN Mission focuses on urban-rural integration, and Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana aims at model village development.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMGSY → Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
☛ Launch year → 2000
☛ Ministry → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Target population → Unconnected villages with more than 500 people
☛ Main objective → Providing all-weather rural connectivity

q: What is the primary aim of the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM)?
o: Encouraging foreign investment in urban infrastructure
Reducing urban poverty through skill development and self-employment
Promoting smart cities in Tier-2 towns
Providing subsidised housing to rural workers
qs.e: The National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM) is a flagship program launched by the Government of India in 2013 to reduce urban poverty by providing skill development and self-employment opportunities to urban poor families. It focuses on empowering the urban poor through vocational training, credit support, and social security, enabling them to become self-reliant. NULM does not aim at foreign investment or smart cities; its core objective is poverty alleviation in urban areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NULM → National Urban Livelihoods Mission
☛ Launch year of NULM → 2013
☛ Goal of NULM → Urban poverty eradication
☛ Main focus of NULM → Skill development and self-employment
☛ Implementing bodies → Municipal corporations and urban local bodies

q: What is the full name of MNREGA in the Indian policy context?
o: Modern National Rural Employment Growth Act
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
Ministry for National Rural Employment Growth Agenda
Mainstream National Rural Education Guarantee Act
qs.e: The full form of MNREGA is Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act. It is a flagship scheme of the Indian government launched in 2005. The Act provides 100 days of employment per year to rural households. It aims to improve living standards and reduce migration in rural areas. It is also known as MGNREGA.
qs.kf:
☛ Full name of MNREGA → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ MNREGA was launched in → 2005
☛ Number of days of employment under MNREGA → 100 days
☛ Objective of MNREGA → Rural development and employment generation
☛ Type of work under MNREGA → Unskilled manual work

q: In which of the following years was the Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) launched with the aim to translate the comprehensive vision of Mahatma Gandhi about an ideal Indian village into reality, keeping in view the present context?
qs.e: The Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) was launched on 11th October 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The objective of this scheme is to realize Mahatma Gandhi's vision of an ideal village, focusing on rural development, sanitation, education, health, and self-reliance. Under this scheme, each Member of Parliament adopts a village in their constituency and develops it as an ideal model village. This initiative is a significant step towards holistic development of rural India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was SAGY launched? → 2014
☛ Full form of SAGY? → Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana
☛ What is the objective of SAGY? → Rural development and creation of ideal villages
☛ Which ministry does SAGY fall under? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Who adopts a village under SAGY? → Member of Parliament

q: Which programme was launched in 1953 to expand rural development more feasibly?
o: Training for Rural Youth for Self-Employment
qs.e: The National Extension Service (NES) was launched in 1953 to expand rural development more feasibly. It aimed to provide technical assistance and training to rural communities in areas like agriculture, animal husbandry, health, and education. NES helped expand the Community Development Programme (CDP), which was started in 1952. This program provided a framework for implementing government schemes in rural areas. Through NES, farmers and villagers gained access to modern farming techniques and resources, improving productivity and living standards. NES later became the precursor to the Rural Extension Service. It played a crucial role in transforming India's rural landscape by bridging the gap between policy and implementation.
qs.kf:
☛ When was National Extension Service (NES) launched? → 1953
☛ What was the main objective of NES? → Expand rural development
☛ When was Community Development Programme (CDP) started? → 1952
☛ NES was an extension of which programme? → Community Development Programme
☛ Which was the first rural development programme in India? → Community Development Programme (1952)

q: In which of the following years was the Aajeevika - Deendayal Antyodaya YojnaNational Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India?
qs.e: The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) was launched in 2011 by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. This scheme was initiated for poverty alleviation and livelihood enhancement in rural areas. Its objective is to organize rural poor families through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and provide them with sustainable livelihood opportunities. DAY-NRLM was earlier known as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) and was later renamed under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana. It is one of the flagship programs of the Ministry of Rural Development and is implemented with the cooperation of state governments.
qs.kf:
☛ When was DAY-NRLM launched? → 2011
☛ Which ministry administers DAY-NRLM? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Which group forms the base of DAY-NRLM? → Self-Help Groups (SHGs)
☛ Main objective of DAY-NRLM? → Rural poverty alleviation and livelihood enhancement
☛ Previous name of DAY-NRLM? → National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)

q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (MGNREGA) provides a legal guarantee for how many days of employment per year to every rural household in India?
qs.e: MGNREGA, 2005 is a landmark social security law in India that provides a legal guarantee of 100 days of employment per year to every rural household. It offers employment in the form of unskilled manual work to adult members. The scheme was launched to eradicate poverty and ensure livelihood security in rural areas. If employment is not provided, the government is liable to pay an unemployment allowance. It is implemented as the Prime Minister's Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of MGNREGA → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Year of enactment → 2005
☛ Type of work → Unskilled manual labor
☛ Unemployment allowance → Paid if work is not provided
☛ Target area → Rural areas

q: Employment generation became a focus in later Five-Year Plans. Which Five-Year Plan introduced the Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)?
qs.e: The Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) was launched during India's Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985). Its primary objectives were poverty alleviation and employment generation in rural areas. Under IRDP, rural families were provided assistance through income-generating assets, training, and credit. This programme reflected the growing focus on employment creation in later Five-Year Plans. The Sixth Plan prioritized rural development and employment, laying the foundation for initiatives like IRDP. The programme aimed to uplift below-poverty-line families by providing sustainable livelihood opportunities.
qs.kf:
☛ Which plan introduced IRDP? → Sixth Five-Year Plan
☛ What was the main objective of IRDP? → Rural poverty alleviation and employment generation
☛ What assistance did IRDP provide? → Income-generating assets, training, and credit
☛ Which plan emphasized employment generation? → Sixth Plan and subsequent plans
☛ What sector did IRDP focus on? → Rural development

q: In which year was the PM JI-VAN (Biofuel-Vatra Sukla Crop Residue Removal) scheme launched?
qs.e: The PM JI-VAN (Biofuel-Vatra Sukla Crop Residue Removal) scheme was launched in the year 2019. The scheme aims to promote the production of biofuels in India and reduce environmental pollution caused by crop residue burning. It provides financial support for second-generation (2G) ethanol projects. Under this scheme, the central government has approved 12 commercial projects and 10 demonstration projects. This helps farmers avoid burning crop residues and contributes to environmental protection.
qs.kf:
☛ Full name of PM JI-VAN scheme → Biofuel-Vatra Sukla Crop Residue Removal
☛ Main objective of the scheme → Promote second-generation ethanol production
☛ Year of launch → 2019
☛ Financial assistance under the scheme → For commercial and demonstration projects
☛ Beneficiaries of the scheme → Farmers and fuel producing companies

q: Which of the following schemes of the Govt. of India aims at enhancing the livelihood security of people in rural areas by guaranteeing hundred days of wage-employment?
qs.e: MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India, enacted in 2005. Its primary objective is to enhance the livelihood security of people in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. This act aims to create durable assets and reduce poverty in rural India. PMJDY focuses on financial inclusion, PMGSY on rural road development, and Skilled India Yojana on skill development. Therefore, MGNREGA is the correct answer as it directly guarantees wage employment for 100 days.
qs.kf:
☛ Guaranteed employment days under MGNREGA → 100 days
☛ Full form of MGNREGA → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Year of enactment of MGNREGA → 2005
☛ Payment under MGNREGA → at minimum wage rate
☛ Objective of MGNREGA → enhance rural livelihood security

q: When was 'Antyodaya Anna Yojana' launched?
qs.e: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) was launched by the Government of India in December 2000 as a food security scheme. Its objective is to provide highly subsidized food grains to the poorest families below the poverty line (BPL). Under the scheme, each eligible family receives 35 kg of rice or wheat per month through the Public Distribution System (PDS). Initially covering 1 crore families, the scheme was later expanded and now reaches approximately 2.5 crore families. AAY is now subsumed under the National Food Security Act, 2013, ensuring legal entitlement to food grains. This scheme plays a crucial role in reducing hunger and malnutrition among the most vulnerable sections of society.
qs.kf:
☛ Objective of Antyodaya Anna Yojana → Food security for the poorest families
☛ Food grains provided under the scheme → 35 kg rice/wheat per family per month
☛ Launch date of the scheme → December 2000
☛ Implementing system → Public Distribution System (PDS)
☛ Current beneficiaries → Approximately 2.5 crore families

q: The 'Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi' initiative was announced during the _______ Union Budget of India.
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was announced in the Interim Union Budget of 2019-20 by Finance Minister Piyush Goyal. It was launched on February 24, 2019. Under this scheme, small and marginal farmers receive an annual income support of Rs 6,000, paid in three equal installments. The scheme is fully funded by the central government. Its objective is to supplement farmers' income and reduce their cultivation costs.
qs.kf:
☛ Annual financial benefit under PM-KISAN → Rs 6,000
☛ Number of installments → 3
☛ Launch date of PM-KISAN → 24 February 2019
☛ Type of budget → Interim Budget
☛ Finance Minister in 2019 → Piyush Goyal

q: In which year did the National Social Assistance Plan come into effect?
qs.e: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) was launched by the Government of India on 15 August 1995. This scheme provides financial assistance to below poverty line (BPL) families in cases of old age, widowhood, and disability. Key components of NSAP include the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS). Its objective is to provide social security and improve the economic condition of vulnerable sections. NSAP is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented through state governments.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NSAP? → National Social Assistance Programme
☛ Which ministry administers NSAP? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the pension amount under IGNOAPS? → Rs 200 per month (60-79 years) and Rs 500 per month (80 years and above)
☛ What is the objective of NSAP? → To provide social security to BPL families
☛ Under whose prime ministership was NSAP launched? → P.V. Narasimha Rao

q: Which of the following scheme was launched in April 2020 to enable an integrated property validation solution for rural India?
qs.e: SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) scheme was launched in April 2020 to enable an integrated property validation solution for rural India. The scheme aims to update land records and provide property cards to rural residents. This gives them legal proof of property ownership, enabling access to financial services like bank loans. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and state governments through drone surveys. SVAMITVA helps strengthen the rural economy and reduce land disputes.
qs.kf:
☛ When was SVAMITVA scheme launched? → April 2020
☛ What is the objective of SVAMITVA? → Integrated property validation solution for rural India
☛ Which ministry implements SVAMITVA? → Ministry of Panchayati Raj
☛ What technology is used in SVAMITVA? → Drone survey
☛ Full form of SVAMITVA? → Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas

q: Prime Minister Rozgar Yojgar (PMRY), to create self-employment opportunities for educated unemployed youth, was implemented in which year?
qs.e: Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) was launched on 2nd October 1993 to create self-employment opportunities for educated unemployed youth. Under this scheme, youth aged 18-35 years are provided bank loans and subsidies to establish self-employment ventures in small industries, service, and business sectors. It was implemented across India and later merged into the Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP).
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMRY launched? → 2nd October 1993
☛ What is the full form of PMRY? → Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana
☛ What is the age limit for PMRY? → 18-35 years
☛ Which sectors does PMRY cover? → Small industries, service, and trade
☛ Under which scheme was PMRY merged? → PMEGP

q: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)?
o: To optimally utilise available natural resources for input production
To promote export of organic farm produce
To launch eco-friendly concept of cultivation reducing the dependency on agro-chemicals and fertilisers
To create employment opportunities in the rural as well as urban sector
qs.e: The Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) aims to promote organic farming. Its objectives include optimal use of natural resources, reducing dependency on agro-chemicals, and promoting export of organic produce. Employment generation is not a primary objective; the scheme focuses on environmental sustainability and organic agriculture. Launched in 2015, PKVY encourages farmers to adopt organic farming by providing financial support and training. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PKVY → Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
☛ Year of launch of PKVY → 2015
☛ Main objective of PKVY → To promote organic farming
☛ Financial assistance under PKVY → 50,000 per hectare
☛ Ministry under PKVY → Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare

q: Which of the following indemnity levels has been provided under the 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana'?
qs.e: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), three indemnity levels are provided: 70%, 80%, and 90%. These levels are based on the risk profile of the crops. The 70% level applies to low-risk crops, 80% to medium-risk crops, and 90% to high-risk crops like horticultural crops. The scheme aims to protect farmers from crop losses. Premium rates are also determined according to these indemnity levels. PMFBY was launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Agriculture.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMFBY launched? → 2016
☛ Farmer's premium in PMFBY? → 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi
☛ PMFBY comes under which ministry? → Ministry of Agriculture
☛ Premium for horticultural crops in PMFBY? → 5%
☛ Objective of PMFBY? → Provide financial security to farmers through crop insurance

q: Which of the following rights does the MGNREGA Scheme guarantee?
qs.e: MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) is a social security scheme that guarantees the Right to work to rural households. This act was passed in 2005 and its main objective is to ensure employment in rural areas. Under this scheme, adult members of each household are provided guaranteed employment for at least 100 days per financial year. The work is based on unskilled labor such as road construction or pond digging. Rights to freedom, speech, or information are fundamental rights under the Indian Constitution, but MGNREGA specifically guarantees employment. The goal of MGNREGA is to reduce rural unemployment and provide livelihood security.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was MGNREGA enacted? → 2005
☛ How many days of employment are guaranteed per household under MGNREGA? → 100 days
☛ What type of labor does MGNREGA provide? → Unskilled labor
☛ What is the objective of MGNREGA? → Ensure rural employment
☛ Which right is MGNREGA related to? → Right to work

q: Which scheme has the government launched to support organic farming in India?
qs.e: The government launched Paramparagat Krishi Vikash Yojana (PKVY) to promote organic farming. This scheme encourages farmers to adopt natural and organic farming practices. Under PKVY, farmers receive financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare, out of which ₹31,000 is directly used for on-field inputs. The scheme is implemented under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA). PKVY aims to maintain soil fertility, reduce the use of chemical fertilizers, and promote eco-friendly farming. It also supports certification and marketing of organic products, helping farmers get better prices. The scheme focuses on forming clusters of farmers for effective implementation and resource sharing.
qs.kf:
☛ Scheme for promoting organic farming → Paramparagat Krishi Vikash Yojana (PKVY)
☛ Financial assistance under PKVY per hectare → ₹50,000
☛ PKVY comes under which mission → National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)
☛ Main benefit of organic farming → Improvement in soil fertility
☛ Full form of PKVY → Paramparagat Krishi Vikash Yojana

q: When was the Atal Pension Scheme started?
qs.e: The Atal Pension Scheme (Atal Pension Yojana) is a social security scheme launched by the Government of India to provide pension to workers in the unorganized sector. It was launched on 9 May 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, replacing the earlier Swavalamban Yojana. Under this scheme, citizens aged 18-40 years can contribute regularly and receive a monthly pension of Rs 1000 to Rs 5000 after reaching the age of 60. The government contributes 50% of the contribution, but this benefit is available only to those who joined by 1 June 2015. The scheme is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Atal Pension Scheme launched? → 9 May 2015
☛ What is the minimum age to join? → 18 years
☛ What is the maximum age? → 40 years
☛ What is the pension amount? → Rs 1000 to Rs 5000 per month
☛ Which ministry oversees it? → Ministry of Finance

q: When was 'Antyodaya Anna Yojana' launched?
qs.e: The 'Antyodaya Anna Yojana' (AAY) is a flagship food security scheme of the Government of India, launched in December 2000. It aims to provide highly subsidized food grains to the poorest families in the country. The scheme operates under the Public Distribution System (PDS) and focuses on families living below the poverty line. Eligible households receive 35 kg of wheat or rice per month at extremely low prices. Initially, the scheme covered 1 crore families, but it has been expanded over time. AAY plays a crucial role in ensuring food security for the most vulnerable sections of society, especially in rural areas.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Antyodaya Anna Yojana launched? → December 2000
☛ Under which system does it operate? → Public Distribution System (PDS)
☛ How much food grain per family per month? → 35 kg
☛ For which type of families? → Poorest of the poor (Below Poverty Line)
☛ Initial coverage? → 1 crore families

q: Which of the following schemes has Shishu, Kishore and Tarun sub-schemes?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana was launched on 8 April 2015. It has three sub-schemes: Shishu (loans up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5,00,001 to ₹10 lakh). This scheme provides funding to non-corporate, non-farm small entrepreneurs. Its objective is 'Funding the Unfunded'.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the maximum limit of Shishu loan? → ₹50,000
☛ What is the range of Kishore loan? → ₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh
☛ What is the range of Tarun loan? → ₹5,00,001 to ₹10 lakh
☛ What is the mascot of Mudra Yojana? → Mudra Phone
☛ Which ministry administers Mudra Yojana? → Ministry of Finance

q: Which government programme aims to provide employment to rural households through works related to water conservation, land development, and rural infrastructure?
o: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
qs.e: MGNREGA is a flagship scheme of the Government of India aimed at providing employment to rural households. It focuses on works related to water conservation, land development, irrigation, rural roads, and other rural infrastructure. Under this act, every rural household is guaranteed 100 days of wage employment in a financial year. Enacted in 2005, its objectives include securing rural livelihoods and conserving natural resources. The scheme emphasizes labour-intensive works and promotes the participation of women. It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was MGNREGA enacted? → 2005
☛ How many days of employment are guaranteed per household under MGNREGA? → 100 days
☛ What is the main objective of MGNREGA? → Rural employment and natural resource conservation
☛ Under which ministry does MGNREGA fall? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What types of works are included in MGNREGA? → Water conservation, land development, irrigation, rural roads

q: How do rural development programmes like the Self-Help Group (SHG) initiative contribute to gender equality in rural India?
o: By providing women with employment opportunities only
By enhancing women's access to finance, leadership roles and decision-making
qs.e: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) contribute to gender equality in rural India by providing women with access to micro-finance, leadership training, and participation in collective decision-making. These groups economically empower women, enhancing their financial independence and strengthening their capacity to make decisions within the household. Additionally, through SHGs, women take on leadership roles such as group leader or treasurer, improving their social status. This initiative goes beyond merely providing employment or education; it addresses the root causes of gender inequality by empowering women economically and socially, thereby fostering a more equitable society.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of SHG? → Self-Help Group
☛ Which ministry is SHG associated with? → Ministry of Rural Development

q: What is the role of the Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) in the implementation of the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)?
o: Monitoring the performance of startups receiving funding
Evaluating and selecting incubators for fund allocation
qs.e: Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), the role of the Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) is to evaluate and select incubators for fund allocation, not to directly fund startups. The EAC reviews applications from incubators, assesses their capability, experience, and proposed plan, and then recommends selected incubators for fund allocation. These incubators then provide seed funding to startups. The EAC does not approve individual startup funding requests, disburse funds directly, or monitor startup performance; these tasks are handled by the incubators and implementing agencies. The EAC's focus is on ensuring that capable incubators are chosen to effectively deploy the seed fund to promising startups.
qs.kf:
☛ SISFS objective → Provide seed funding to startups
☛ EAC constituted by → DPIIT
☛ EAC members → Experts, industry representatives
☛ Fund recipients → Incubators, not directly startups
☛ Monitoring → Done by incubators for startups

q: Which Indian government scheme is specifically aimed at providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households?
o: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
qs.e: MGNREGA is a flagship scheme of the Indian government that aims to provide at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households in a financial year. Enacted in 2005, it focuses on enhancing livelihood security and reducing poverty in rural areas. The work provided under this scheme is primarily unskilled manual labor such as water conservation, land development, and afforestation. Wage payments are made directly into the beneficiaries' bank accounts or post offices, ensuring transparency and timely disbursement.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of MGNREGA? → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ How many days of guaranteed employment under MGNREGA? → 100 days per year
☛ In which year was MGNREGA enacted? → 2005
☛ Through which mode is wage payment made under MGNREGA? → Bank account or post office
☛ What is the main objective of MGNREGA? → To provide employment security to rural households

q: PM – Daksh Yojana is associated with:
qs.e: PM-DAKSH Yojana (Pradhan Mantri Daksh Kaushal Vikas Yojana) is a skill development training programme launched to provide employment opportunities to youth from minority communities. Under this scheme, beneficiaries receive free skill training and are also provided placement assistance after training. It is implemented by the Ministry of Minority Affairs and aims to enhance employability among minority communities. It is not related to health measures, security, or agriculture.

q: The Skill India Mission, aimed at training over 40 crore people in India in different skills by 2022, is primarily facilitated by which of the following?
o: Both National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
qs.e: The Skill India Mission aims to train over 40 crore people in India in different skills by 2022. This mission is primarily facilitated by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). NSDC is a public-private partnership that connects training institutions and industries for skill development. PMKVY is a flagship government scheme that provides free skill training and certification to youth. Both work together to achieve the goals of the Skill India Mission. The National Career Service (NCS) mainly provides employment-related services, not training.

☛ What does PMKVY stand for? → Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana

q: What is the nature of the 'PM Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)' for the participating States/UTs and farmers?
o: Mandatory for both States/UTs and also for farmers
Voluntary for both States/UTs and also for farmers
Mandatory for States/UTs and voluntary for farmers
Voluntary for States/UTs and mandatory for farmers
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was launched in 2016. The nature of this scheme is mandatory for participating States/UTs but voluntary for farmers. Its objective is to provide financial support to farmers in case of crop failure. The scheme covers both Kharif and Rabi seasons. Farmers pay a very low premium, and the remaining amount is borne by the government. This scheme protects farmers from losses due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
qs.kf:

☛ Insured seasons → Kharif and Rabi
☛ Premium rate (Kharif) → Maximum 2%
☛ Premium rate (Rabi) → Maximum 1.5%
☛ Premium rate (commercial crops) → Maximum 5%

q: On 3rd October 2024, the Union Cabinet decided to merge all Central schemes in the agriculture sector into how many new schemes?
qs.e: On 3rd October 2024, the Union Cabinet decided to merge all Central schemes in the agriculture sector into two new schemes. These two schemes are: the Agriculture Development Scheme and the Food and Nutrition Security Scheme. The consolidation aims to simplify the implementation of schemes, ensure efficient use of resources, and provide integrated benefits to farmers. Prior to this decision, multiple separate schemes were operating in the agriculture sector, leading to overlap and inefficiency. Now, they have been merged into two main schemes. This will reduce administrative burden and enhance policy coherence.

q: Udyami Bharat, MUDRA Yojana, Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme, SFURTI and RAMP schemes are associated with the development of which sector?
qs.e: All these schemes are designed for the development of the MSME (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) sector. Udyami Bharat is an initiative to empower MSMEs. MUDRA Yojana provides loans to non-corporate small businesses. Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) offers credit support to MSMEs during COVID-19. SFURTI promotes traditional industries, and RAMP (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance) aims to enhance the competitiveness of MSMEs. These are part of the central government's strategy to boost the MSME sector.

q: What is the maximum score possible for project design evaluation in the application form process of the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)?
qs.e: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is a central scheme that provides skill training and employment to rural youth. In the application process, the maximum possible score for project design evaluation is 1400. This score assesses the quality, feasibility, and effectiveness of the proposed project, including training programs, placement strategy, and community impact. Projects scoring 1400 are given high priority, ensuring only the best-designed projects are approved. The evaluation process helps maintain high standards and maximize employment outcomes for rural youth.

☛ What types of training are provided under DDU-GKY? → Skill development and entrepreneurship

q: When was the National Food for Work Programme launched?
qs.e: The National Food for Work Programme was launched by the Government of India on 14 November 2004. Its objective was poverty alleviation and employment generation, where workers were paid food grains as wages. This programme was implemented in the 150 most backward districts of the country. Later, in 2006, it was merged with the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA). The programme was administered by the Ministry of Labour and Employment and played a crucial role in providing employment to unskilled laborers in rural areas.
qs.kf:

☛ Into which scheme was it later merged? → NREGA (2006)

☛ Which ministry administered it? → Ministry of Labour and Employment

q: National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) came into effect on 15 August. Identify the year,
qs.e: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a key social security scheme launched by the Government of India, which came into effect on 15 August 1995. It aims to provide old age, widow, and disability pensions to families living below the poverty line (BPL). Currently, NSAP includes the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS). The programme is fully funded by the central government and implemented through state governments. To avail NSAP benefits, the beneficiary must be aged 60 years or above.
qs.kf:

☛ Objective of NSAP → Provide social security to BPL families
☛ Pension schemes under NSAP → Old age, widow, disability
☛ Beneficiary age for IGNWPS → 60 years or above
☛ Funding of NSAP → By central government

q: Which flagship programme guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a year to every household?
o: Mahatama Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
qs.e: MGNREGA is a flagship programme of the Government of India that guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household. It was enacted in 2005 and implemented in 2006. The objective is to provide livelihood security in rural areas and create durable assets. The act mandates employment within 15 days of demand; if not provided, unemployment allowance is paid. At least one-third of the jobs are reserved for women. The scheme is implemented through Gram Panchayats. It is a demand-driven scheme and focuses on works like water conservation, drought proofing, and rural connectivity.
qs.kf:

☛ How many days of employment does MGNREGA guarantee per household? → 100 days
☛ What is the reservation for women in MGNREGA? → 33%
☛ What is the full form of MGNREGA? → Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
☛ Under which act is MGNREGA implemented? → National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005

q: What is the minimum amount of monthly pension permissible under Atal Pension Yojana?
qs.e: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a social security scheme by the Government of India, primarily targeting workers in the unorganized sector. Under this scheme, based on the subscriber's age and contribution, a monthly pension is guaranteed, and upon death, the spouse continues to receive the pension. The minimum monthly pension is Rs. 1,000, and the maximum is Rs. 5,000. The scheme is managed by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) and is available for individuals aged 18 to 40 years. It was launched in 2015, and the government provides a co-contribution of 50% (for 5 years) for eligible subscribers.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Atal Pension Yojana launched? → 2015
☛ What is the minimum monthly pension under APY? → Rs. 1,000
☛ What is the maximum monthly pension under APY? → Rs. 5,000
☛ Which agency manages Atal Pension Yojana? → LIC
☛ What is the minimum age to join APY? → 18 years

q: Which state launched 7-Star Gram Panchayat Rainbow Scheme?
qs.e: The 7-Star Gram Panchayat Rainbow Scheme was launched by the Government of Haryana. This innovative scheme aims to evaluate and rank gram panchayats based on their performance, assigning them a star rating from 1 to 7. The rating system encourages healthy competition among panchayats and promotes better governance and service delivery at the grassroots level. Higher-rated panchayats receive additional grants and incentives to further improve their infrastructure and facilities. The scheme is implemented under the Haryana Panchayati Raj Department and is a key initiative for rural development and strengthening local self-government. It underscores the state's commitment to transparent and performance-based governance in rural areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state launched the 7-Star Gram Panchayat Rainbow Scheme? → Haryana
☛ What is the star rating range in this scheme? → 1 to 7 stars
☛ What is the main purpose of this scheme? → To evaluate and rank gram panchayats
☛ Which department implements this scheme? → Panchayati Raj Department, Haryana
☛ Who benefits from this scheme? → Gram Panchayats

q: National Rural Employment Program (NREP) was launched -
qs.e: The National Rural Employment Program (NREP) was launched in 1980. It was initiated to generate employment and alleviate poverty in rural areas through the creation of productive assets. NREP was implemented under the Five-Year Plan and later merged with the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). The program focused on developing rural infrastructure such as roads, irrigation projects, and community assets. NREP is considered a precursor to the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
qs.kf:
☛ When was NREP launched? → 1980
☛ Which scheme did NREP merge into later? → Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)

☛ What was the main objective of NREP? → Rural employment and infrastructure development
☛ Under which Five-Year Plan was NREP launched? → Sixth Five-Year Plan

q: The PDS scheme was reorganized as a targeted PDS-
qs.e: The Public Distribution System (PDS) in India was restructured as the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) in the year 1997. The objective was to provide subsidized food grains to poor families. Under TPDS, households are categorized into Below Poverty Line (BPL) and Above Poverty Line (APL), with BPL families receiving higher subsidies. This system was introduced to ensure food security and protect vulnerable sections. State governments play a crucial role in implementing TPDS. This scheme also formed the basis for the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013. TPDS helps in stabilizing prices and ensuring access to food for the needy.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of TPDS? → Targeted Public Distribution System
☛ When was TPDS introduced? → 1997
☛ What are the household categories under TPDS? → BPL and APL

☛ What is the objective of TPDS? → To provide subsidized food grains to the poor

q: In India, irrigation projects with a Cultivable Command Area (CCA) of more than 10,000 hectares are classified as:
qs.e: In India, irrigation projects are classified based on Cultivable Command Area (CCA). Projects with a CCA of more than 10,000 hectares are categorized as Major Projects. This classification is defined by the Ministry of Water Resources. Major projects involve large dams, canal networks, and reservoirs. Their construction and maintenance are handled by the central or state government. In contrast, projects with CCA between 2,000 and 10,000 hectares are Medium, and those with less than 2,000 hectares are Minor projects. Major projects aim to provide irrigation facilities on a large scale, covering extensive agricultural areas.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the CCA for Major Irrigation Projects? → More than 10,000 hectares
☛ What is the CCA for Minor Irrigation Projects? → Up to 2,000 hectares
☛ What is the CCA for Medium Irrigation Projects? → 2,000 to 10,000 hectares
☛ Who manages Major Projects? → Central or state government
☛ What is the basis of irrigation classification in India? → Cultivable Command Area (CCA)

q: The PM-KISAN scheme launched by the Central Government falls under which category of boxes under the WTO’s Agreement on Agriculture?
qs.e: The PM-KISAN scheme (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) provides income support of Rs. 6,000 per year to small and marginal farmers. Under the WTO's Agreement on Agriculture, the Green box includes subsidies that do not distort trade or cause minimal distortion. PM-KISAN is an income support program not linked to production or prices, thus it falls under the Green box. Amber box contains production-related subsidies, Blue box includes subsidies with production limits, and Red box refers to prohibited subsidies.
qs.kf:
☛ Annual assistance under PM-KISAN → Rs. 6,000
☛ Key feature of Green box subsidies → Minimal trade distortion
☛ Examples of Green box subsidies → Income support, research, training
☛ Boxes under WTO Agreement on Agriculture → Amber, Blue, Green
☛ Prohibited subsidies are called → Red box

q: Which of the following state has implemented a women-oriented community-based poverty alleviation program 'Kudumbasree'?
qs.e: 'Kudumbashree' is a women-oriented poverty alleviation program implemented by the Government of Kerala. It focuses on organizing women living below the poverty line and empowering them economically. The program was established in 1998 and operates under the Kerala State Poverty Eradication Mission. Under Kudumbashree, women are linked to self-help groups and are trained to start small-scale enterprises. The objective is to make women self-reliant and reduce poverty through community participation. Since its inception, the model has been replicated in other states, but the original program started in Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Kudumbashree program related to? → Kerala
☛ When was Kudumbashree launched? → 1998
☛ What is the focus of Kudumbashree? → Women-oriented poverty alleviation
☛ Under which mission does Kudumbashree come? → Kerala State Poverty Eradication Mission
☛ With what are women linked in Kudumbashree? → Self-help groups

q: The 'National Pension Scheme' ('NPS') is regulated by:
qs.e: The National Pension Scheme (NPS) is a government-sponsored pension scheme designed to provide retirement income to Indian citizens. It is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), which was established in 2003 and given statutory status in 2013. NPS is open to central and state government employees, as well as all Indian citizens aged 18 to 70. The scheme offers two types of accounts: Tier I (pension account) with withdrawal restrictions, and Tier II (voluntary savings account) with more flexibility. Investments under NPS are allocated across different asset classes (E, C, G, A) based on the subscriber's choice. PFRDA oversees the scheme, sets regulations, and ensures protection of investor interests.
qs.kf:
☛ Who regulates NPS? → PFRDA
☛ When was PFRDA established? → 2003
☛ When did PFRDA get statutory status? → 2013
☛ What is Tier I account in NPS? → Pension account (restricted withdrawal)
☛ What is the minimum age for NPS? → 18 years (maximum 70 years)

q: When was the Prime Minister Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana started?
qs.e: The Prime Minister's Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMSAGY) was launched on 11 October 2014. The scheme aims at developing villages through Members of Parliament, who adopt one village in their constituency to transform it into an ideal model village. It focuses on rural development, sanitation, education, health, and infrastructure. After its launch in 2014, modifications were made in 2015 and 2016. Under this scheme, each MP selects a village to develop holistically, involving Panchayati Raj institutions and local communities. The target is to create self-sufficient and sustainable villages.
qs.kf:
☛ PMSAGY launched on? → 11 October 2014
☛ Main objective of PMSAGY? → Model village development by MPs
☛ How many villages per MP? → One (initially)
☛ Focus areas? → Rural development, sanitation, education, health
☛ Revisions in scheme? → Modifications in 2015 and 2016

q: In which year Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana was launched?
qs.e: Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY) was launched by the Government of India in 1999 as a rural development scheme. It was a restructured version of the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). The primary objective of JGSY was to develop rural infrastructure and generate employment opportunities in villages. Under this scheme, works like construction of roads, drains, bridges, school buildings, etc., were undertaken. It was a centrally sponsored scheme with 100% central assistance. Later, in 2002, this scheme was merged into the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY).
qs.kf:

☛ JGSY was a restructured version of which scheme? → Jawahar Rozgar Yojana

☛ What was the central assistance percentage in JGSY? → 100%
☛ Into which scheme was JGSY merged? → Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)

q: Which of the following schemes aims to create self-employment opportunities in rural areas?
qs.e: The Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 1995, aimed at creating self-employment opportunities in rural areas. It is implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). The scheme promotes activities like small-scale industries and handicrafts in rural areas. It provides bank loans and subsidies to unemployed youth to start their own businesses. Other options include Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana for urban areas, Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana also for rural self-employment, but REGP specifically targets rural employment generation.

☛ Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana is for which areas? → Urban areas
☛ What is the objective of REGP? → To create self-employment opportunities in rural areas

q: What is the name of the skill development programme of the Government of India?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is the flagship skill development programme of the Government of India, launched in 2015. It aims to provide industry-relevant skill training to youth and enhance their employability. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. Upon completion, trainees receive a Skill Certificate recognized by the National Skills Qualifications Framework. The National Skill Development Corporation supports the implementation. Other schemes like Atal Kaushal Vikas Yojana and Mahatma Gandhi Kaushal Yojana are different, but PMKVY is the primary central government programme. Millions of youth have been trained under PMKVY so far.

☛ Mascot of PMKVY → Koshal

☛ Current Minister of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship → Jayant Chaudhary

q: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana is for:
o: Provision of money for only BPL families
Printing of new currency after demonetisation
Provision of funding to non-corporate small business sector
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme launched by the Government of India on April 8, 2015. Its objective is to provide funding up to ₹10 lakh to the non-corporate, small business sector. The scheme is specifically designed to offer financial assistance to small entrepreneurs, traders, service providers, and self-employed individuals. Loans under PMMY are categorized into three segments: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5,00,001 to ₹10 lakh). The scheme is not limited to BPL families; any person wishing to start a small business can avail the loan. This promotes small businesses and creates employment opportunities.

☛ When was PMMY launched? → April 8, 2015
☛ What is the maximum loan amount under PMMY? → ₹10 lakh
☛ What is the limit for 'Shishu' category in PMMY? → Up to ₹50,000
☛ What is the objective of PMMY? → Funding non-corporate small businesses
☛ Which ministry administers PMMY? → Ministry of Finance

q: Who was the inspiration behind Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana?
qs.e: The Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana draws inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's concept of an ideal village. This scheme was launched in 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its aim is to promote rural development and have each Member of Parliament adopt a village to develop it as a model village. Mahatma Gandhi emphasized Gram Swaraj and self-reliant villages, which are incorporated into this scheme. Under the scheme, MPs select a village outside their constituency and develop it as a model village.

q: The 'DigiGaon' initiative was launched by the ______ Department.
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
qs.e: The 'DigiGaon' initiative was launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). This initiative aims to digitally empower rural areas under the Digital India program. It provides facilities like high-speed internet, digital education, e-health services, and digital payments in selected villages. Initially, 100 villages across the country were developed as DigiGaons. The initiative helps reduce the digital divide and strengthen the rural economy through digital means.

q: When was the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana launched with the objective of providing rural connectivity?
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India launched with the objective of providing rural connectivity. It was inaugurated on 25 December 2000 by the then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The main aim of PMGSY is to provide all-weather road connectivity to remote villages, facilitating their social and economic development. This scheme falls under the Ministry of Rural Development and has led to the construction of hundreds of thousands of kilometers of roads across the country.

q: Which of the following programs aims at self-employment for the rural poor?
o: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
qs.e: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana (DAY) aims to provide self-employment opportunities to the rural poor. This scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development and is based on the philosophy of Deendayal Upadhyaya. Under DAY, Self Help Groups (SHGs) are promoted and provided with skill training and financial assistance. Other options: National Rural Health Mission focuses on health services, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana provides housing, and Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees wage employment, not self-employment.

q: Which central government scheme is primarily aimed at providing road connectivity to rural and remote areas in India?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched in the year 2000. Its primary objective is to provide road connectivity to rural and remote areas in India. This scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. Under PMGSY, habitations with a population of more than 500 (250 in hilly areas) are connected with all-weather roads. The funding is shared between the central and state governments. PMGSY also contributes to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among other options, Setu Bharatam focuses on bridge maintenance, Bharatmala is a highway development program, and Rural Infrastructure Development Fund is managed by NABARD for rural infrastructure.
