☛ What is the main objective of PMGSY? → To provide road connectivity to rural areas

q: Which of the following programmes aims to increase soil fertility and thereby helps in production of healthy food through organic practices without the use of agro-chemicals?
qs.e: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) was launched in 2015 to promote organic farming without the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. It aims to increase soil fertility through organic practices, thereby producing healthy food. Under this scheme, farmers are organized into clusters and provided support for certification and training. Other options like Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana relates to crop insurance, Pradhan Mantri Kisan MaanDhan Yojana provides old-age pension, and Rastriya Krishi Vikas Yojana is for overall agricultural development.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of PKVY? → Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
☛ Which ministry implements PKVY? → Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
☛ What is the objective of PKVY? → To promote organic farming and increase soil fertility
☛ What assistance is provided to farmers under PKVY? → Organic certification and training
☛ How many farmers are in a cluster under PKVY? → 50 farmers

q: Which scheme launched in 2000 aims at reducing rural poverty by increasing rural connectivity?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2000. Its primary objective is to reduce rural poverty by providing all-weather road connectivity to unconnected villages in rural India. Improved road connectivity facilitates better access to markets, healthcare, education, and employment opportunities, thereby enhancing the economic condition of rural populations. The scheme focuses on connecting eligible habitations with a population of 250-500 or more as per census data. PMGSY has significantly improved rural infrastructure and contributed to poverty alleviation by enabling smoother transportation of agricultural produce and reducing isolation of remote areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of PMGSY → 2000
☛ Full form of PMGSY → Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
☛ Key objective of PMGSY → Rural connectivity to reduce poverty
☛ Type of scheme → Centrally Sponsored Scheme
☛ Matching centrally sponsored scheme for rural road connectivity → PMGSY

q: Stand Up India Scheme was launched in which of the following years?
qs.e: The Stand Up India Scheme was launched on April 5, 2016. It aims to facilitate bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises. This scheme is administered under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana and focuses on promoting entrepreneurship among marginalized sections. The loan is repayable within 7 years and includes provisions for working capital.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Stand Up India Scheme → 2016
☛ Loan amount range under the scheme → ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore
☛ Target beneficiaries → SC, ST, and women entrepreneurs
☛ Associated central scheme → Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana
☛ Objective → Promote entrepreneurship and employment generation

q: When was the National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP) launched?
qs.e: The National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP) was launched on 24th April 2019. It is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at promoting economic development in rural areas. The project focuses on increasing the income of rural households and providing them with self-employment opportunities. It is implemented in collaboration with the World Bank and places special emphasis on women-led enterprises. The project is a continuation of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) and seeks to strengthen rural livelihoods.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NRETP? → National Rural Economic Transformation Project
☛ Which ministry implements NRETP? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the objective of NRETP? → Rural income growth and self-employment
☛ With which institution is NRETP collaborated? → World Bank
☛ Which group is specially focused in NRETP? → Women entrepreneurs

q: What is the primary purpose of the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)?
o: To provide free food to rural households
To supply subsidised agricultural inputs to farmers
To skill rural youth and promote wage employment opportunities
To offer old-age pensions in villages
qs.e: The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is a national skill development scheme launched by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, on 25 September 2014. Its primary objective is to provide skill training to poor rural youth aged 15-35 years and connect them with wage employment. The scheme specifically focuses on vulnerable groups such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women. It guarantees job placement after training. This initiative helps reduce rural unemployment and strengthen the rural economy.
qs.kf:
☛ When was DDU-GKY launched? → 25 September 2014
☛ What is the target age group of DDU-GKY? → 15-35 years
☛ Which ministry administers DDU-GKY? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Which groups are the main focus of DDU-GKY? → Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women
☛ What is the aim of DDU-GKY? → To skill rural youth and promote wage employment

q: In September 2025, which State Government launched a scheme 'KFC Machinery Loan Scheme for MSMEs' offering loans up to ₹5 crore (without collateral) under certain conditions?
qs.e: In September 2025, the Government of Kerala launched the 'KFC Machinery Loan Scheme for MSMEs', offering loans up to ₹5 crore without collateral under certain conditions. This scheme aims to assist small and medium enterprises in purchasing machinery, thereby boosting employment and production. Kerala's initiative is significant for promoting industrial development and providing financial support to entrepreneurs.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state launched the KFC Machinery Loan Scheme? → Kerala
☛ What is the maximum loan amount under this scheme? → ₹5 crore
☛ What type of loan is provided? → Without collateral (uncollateralized)
☛ Who are the beneficiaries of the scheme? → MSMEs
☛ When was the scheme launched? → September 2025

q: What method does the Hill Areas Development Programme (HADP) use to increase productivity of the land?
o: Vegetative methods and changing cropping pattern
Importing high-yielding crops from plain regions
Use of chemical fertilizers and pesticide inputs
qs.e: The Hill Areas Development Programme (HADP) uses vegetative methods and changing cropping pattern to increase land productivity in hilly regions. This programme focuses on enhancing agricultural output while maintaining ecological balance. Vegetative methods include afforestation, multi-tier cropping, and soil conservation, which prevent erosion and improve soil fertility. Changing cropping pattern involves techniques like crop rotation and intercropping, ensuring sustainable land use. HADP aims to develop a cropping system suited to local resources in hilly areas, thereby boosting productivity without harming the environment.
qs.kf:
☛ Main objective of HADP → Increase agricultural productivity in hilly areas while maintaining ecological balance
☛ Examples of vegetative methods → Afforestation, multi-tier cropping, soil conservation
☛ Techniques in changing cropping pattern → Crop rotation, intercropping
☛ HADP comes under which ministry → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ When was HADP launched → 1974-75

q: What does the Food for Work Programme aim to provide to the rural poor of backward districts?
qs.e: The Food for Work Programme (FWP) was initiated by the Government of India to provide supplementary wage employment to the rural poor in backward districts. Under this program, workers were paid in food grains (such as wheat or rice) instead of cash wages. It was launched in 2000-2001 and later merged with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2006. The primary objective of FWP was to ensure food security in areas affected by drought or other natural calamities and to create employment opportunities. The works undertaken included construction or repair of community assets like roads, ponds, and schools.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Food for Work Programme launched? → 2000-2001
☛ What was the mode of payment under FWP? → Food grains (wheat/rice)
☛ Which scheme replaced FWP? → MGNREGA (2006)
☛ What was the main objective of FWP? → Food security and employment generation
☛ In which districts was FWP implemented? → Backward and drought-prone districts

q: Which system has become a cornerstone of government development policy and is tied to most rural development programs?
o: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Empowerment Scheme (MGNRES)
qs.e: MGNREGA, enacted in 2005, is a cornerstone of India's government development policy and is tied to most rural development programs. It provides a legal guarantee of 100 days of employment per rural household, strengthening the rural economy. The scheme is implemented through Gram Panchayats and focuses on both employment generation and asset creation. Other options: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan is focused on sanitation, PDS is related to food security, and MGNRES is a non-existent scheme.
qs.kf:
☛ When was MGNREGA enacted? → 2005
☛ How many days of employment is guaranteed under MGNREGA? → 100 days per year per household
☛ At what level is MGNREGA implemented? → Gram Panchayat
☛ What is the main objective of MGNREGA? → Ensuring rural employment and asset creation
☛ Which act is MGNREGA based on? → National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005

q: Which of the following government initiatives is specifically aimed at the conservation and protection of wildlife in India through habitat preservation and species-focused management?
qs.e: Project Tiger is a flagship government initiative launched in India in 1973, specifically aimed at the conservation of tigers through habitat preservation and species-focused management. Under this program, special tiger reserves are established where anti-poaching measures, habitat restoration, and community relocation are implemented. In contrast, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana focuses on rural road connectivity, Operation Flood on dairy development, and Swachh Bharat Mission on sanitation. Therefore, only Project Tiger directly addresses wildlife conservation and habitat protection. The project is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and has been instrumental in increasing India's tiger population.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Project Tiger launched? → 1973
☛ What is the main objective of Project Tiger? → Conservation of tigers and habitat management
☛ Which is India's first tiger reserve? → Corbett National Park
☛ Which body oversees Project Tiger? → National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)
☛ How many tiger reserves are under Project Tiger? → 54

q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), what is the premium rate paid by farmers for annual commercial and horticultural crops?
qs.e: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), the premium rate paid by farmers for annual commercial and horticultural crops is 5% of the sum insured. This is higher than the rates for kharif crops (2%) and rabi crops (1.5%). The remaining premium is equally shared by the central and state governments. The scheme aims to provide financial protection to farmers against crop losses due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases. It was launched in 2016 to promote sustainable agriculture and reduce farmers' distress.
qs.kf:
☛ Farmer premium rate for kharif crops under PMFBY → 2%
☛ Farmer premium rate for rabi crops under PMFBY → 1.5%
☛ Farmer premium rate for annual commercial/horticultural crops under PMFBY → 5%
☛ Who bears the remaining premium under PMFBY → Central and state governments equally
☛ Year of launch of PMFBY → 2016

q: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) launched?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is a flagship scheme of the Government of India launched on 15 July 2015. The objective of the scheme is to provide industry-relevant skill training to the youth of the country and enhance their employability. It is implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). Under PMKVY, trainees receive free training, certification, and a monetary incentive as a reward. The scheme is a part of the National Skill Development Mission (NSDM). It aims to create a skilled workforce in various sectors to meet the demands of the industry.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMKVY → Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
☛ PMKVY launch year → 2015
☛ Monetary incentive under PMKVY → ₹8,000 (first phase)
☛ Implementing ministry → Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
☛ Main focus of PMKVY training → Industry-relevant skills

q: In which year did the Union Cabinet approve the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, named as ‘Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana’?
qs.e: The Union Cabinet approved the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme in year 2025, naming it 'Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana'. The scheme is divided into three components: the first component provides one month's salary to new employees, the second incentivizes employment generation in the manufacturing sector, and the third offers government support to employers. This scheme was launched to boost employment generation and economic development.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the ELI scheme approved? → 2025
☛ What is the new name of the ELI scheme? → Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana
☛ How many components does the ELI scheme have? → Three
☛ What does the first component of ELI provide? → One month's salary
☛ What is the objective of the ELI scheme? → Employment generation and economic development

q: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was launched in which year?
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was launched in September 2020 by the central government. The scheme aims to promote sustainable development in the fisheries and aquaculture sector. It was initiated with the goal of doubling the income of fishermen and fish producers in the country. PMMSY proposes an investment of Rs. 20,050 crore, with the central share being Rs. 9,407 crore. The scheme focuses on increasing fish production to 220 lakh tonnes by 2024-25 and boosting fish exports.
qs.kf:
☛ PMMSY launch year → 2020
☛ Objective of the scheme → Doubling fishermen's income
☛ Total investment → Rs. 20,050 crore
☛ Fish production target (2024-25) → 220 lakh tonnes
☛ Central share → Rs. 9,407 crore

q: When was the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyaan (PMJUGA) started?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyaan (PMJUGA) was launched on October 30, 2024. The objective of this scheme is the holistic development of tribal-majority villages. It is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented jointly by the centre and states. Under this mission, infrastructure, education, health, skill development, and livelihood opportunities will be provided. Initially, more than 63,000 villages will be covered. The scheme will be effective from fiscal year 2025-26. The Prime Minister launched this scheme in Jharkhand during the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas celebration. Its budget is approximately ₹79,156 crore.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMJUGA → Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyaan
☛ Launch date → October 30, 2024
☛ Launch place → Jharkhand
☛ Villages to be covered → More than 63,000
☛ Total budget → Approximately ₹79,156 crore

q: What is the term used for rural self-help group (SHG) women earning ₹1 lakh or more annually?
qs.e: The term Lakhpati Didi is used for rural self-help group (SHG) women earning an annual income of ₹1 lakh or more. This term was popularized under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), a flagship program of the Government of India aimed at empowering rural women economically. The initiative encourages women to become entrepreneurs and generate sustainable income through various activities such as animal husbandry, handicrafts, and agriculture-based enterprises. The goal is to promote financial independence and self-reliance among rural women.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which mission does the Lakhpati Didi scheme fall? → DAY-NRLM
☛ What is the minimum annual income to become a Lakhpati Didi? → ₹1 lakh
☛ What is the full form of DAY-NRLM? → Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission
☛ Which group is associated with the term Lakhpati Didi? → Self-Help Groups (SHGs)
☛ Under which ministry does DAY-NRLM operate? → Ministry of Rural Development

name: Set 1 · Q1–40
sub: Govt Schemes and Policies - Housing, Urban, Infrastructure & Digital Initiatives

q: The main objective of the industry base Memorandum Scheme is _________.
o: Facilitating a relationship between future job seekers and employers
Setting up a network of technology and emerging centers
qs.e: The Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) scheme was introduced by the Government of India to promote ease of doing business in the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector. This scheme allows entrepreneurs to register their business by simply filing a simple online form, eliminating complex procedures. Its main objective is to reduce regulatory burden and facilitate starting and operating a business. The scheme falls under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and is free of cost.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main objective of Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) scheme? → Promote ease of doing business
☛ Which ministry does the UAM scheme come under? → Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
☛ What is the process of UAM registration? → Completely online and free
☛ In which year was the UAM scheme launched? → 2015
☛ Who can benefit from the UAM scheme? → Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

q: Announcement of new Foreign Trade Policy in India has been done for the year ________.
qs.e: The Government of India announced the new Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2015-20 on 1 April 2015. This policy was implemented for a period of 5 years (2015-2020). Its objective was to boost exports, ensure ease of doing business, and strengthen India's position in global competition. The FTP 2015-20 supported initiatives like 'Make in India' and 'Digital India'. The policy provided various incentives to exporters, such as MEIS (Merchandise Exports from India Scheme) and SEIS (Services Exports from India Scheme). The term of this policy lasted until 2020, after which the new FTP 2021-26 was implemented.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the main objective of FTP 2015-20? → To boost exports and ensure ease of doing business
☛ Which scheme was included under FTP 2015-20? → MEIS (Merchandise Exports from India Scheme)
☛ When did the new Foreign Trade Policy 2021-26 come into effect? → 1 April 2021
☛ Which scheme was for service exports under FTP 2015-20? → SEIS (Services Exports from India Scheme)
☛ For how many years was FTP 2015-20? → 5 years

q: According to the Integrated Energy Policy, by which year is the power demand expected to be 8,00,000 MW?
qs.e: According to the Integrated Energy Policy, India's total electricity demand is expected to reach 8,00,000 MW by the year 2031-32. This policy was formulated by the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) to ensure energy security and sustainable economic growth. It emphasizes a balanced use of energy sources including coal, gas, renewable energy, and nuclear power to meet the rising demand. The projection is based on factors such as population growth, industrialization, and urbanization.
qs.kf:
☛ Who formulated the Integrated Energy Policy? → Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog)
☛ When was the Integrated Energy Policy launched? → 2006
☛ India's current installed power capacity is approximately? → Over 400 GW
☛ What is the main objective of the Integrated Energy Policy? → Optimal utilization of all energy resources
☛ What is the renewable energy target for 2031-32? → 500 GW

q: __________ is the first e-governance project of the Government of Karnataka in land records Computerization system.
qs.e: Bhoomi is the first e-governance project of the Government of Karnataka for computerization of land records. It aims to digitize and transparently manage land records in rural areas. The project was initiated in 1991 and fully implemented by 2001. More than 20 million land records have been digitized under this project. Bhoomi was awarded the National e-Governance Award by the Government of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state owns the Bhoomi project? → Karnataka
☛ What is the main objective of Bhoomi project? → Computerization of land records
☛ In which year was Bhoomi project started? → 1991
☛ Which award was given to Bhoomi project? → National e-Governance Award
☛ Under which ministry does Bhoomi project fall? → Revenue Ministry

q: After whose name the AMRUT yojana started?
A. Mahatma Gandhi
B. Atal Bihari Vajpayee
C. B.R. Ambedkar
D. Indira Gandhi
qs.e: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) scheme is named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The scheme was launched in June 2015 with the objective of developing basic urban infrastructure such as water supply, sewerage, and green spaces in selected cities. It covers 500 cities and focuses on improving housing and urban services for the weaker sections. The full name 'Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation' reflects Vajpayee's legacy. The scheme is under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ When was AMRUT scheme launched? → 2015
☛ What does AMRUT stand for? → Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
☛ How many cities are covered under AMRUT? → 500
☛ What is the main objective of AMRUT? → Urban infrastructure development
☛ Which ministry implements AMRUT? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

q: During which financial year was Jal Kranti Abhiyan launched by the Government of India?
qs.e: The Jal Kranti Abhiyan was launched by the Government of India in the financial year 2015-16. Its objective is to promote water conservation and water efficiency. This campaign predates the Jal Shakti Abhiyan, which was launched in 2019. Jal Kranti Abhiyan focused on rainwater harvesting, rejuvenation of water bodies, and improving irrigation efficiency. The campaign was implemented in both rural and urban areas across the country. Its main aim is to address the water crisis and promote sustainable water management.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Jal Kranti Abhiyan launched? → 2015-16
☛ When was Jal Shakti Abhiyan launched? → 2019
☛ What is the objective of Jal Kranti Abhiyan? → Water conservation and efficiency
☛ Under which ministry does Jal Kranti Abhiyan fall? → Ministry of Jal Shakti
☛ What is the main focus area of Jal Kranti Abhiyan? → Rainwater harvesting

q: What is the full form of JNNURM?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Rejuvenation Mission
Jawaharlal Nehru National Utility Rural Mission
Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
Jawaharlal Nehru National Utility Renewal Mission
qs.e: The full form of JNNURM is Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission. It was a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India in 2005 to address the challenges of urban infrastructure development and provide basic services to the urban poor. The mission focused on sectors like water supply, sewerage, solid waste management, and housing. It was divided into two sub-missions: Urban Infrastructure and Governance, and Basic Services to the Urban Poor. JNNURM was later replaced by the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) in 2015.
qs.kf:
☛ When was JNNURM launched? → 2005
☛ What is the full form of JNNURM? → Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
☛ Which scheme replaced JNNURM? → AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)
☛ What sectors were focused under JNNURM? → Water supply, sewerage, solid waste management, and housing
☛ What was the objective of JNNURM? → Urban infrastructure development and provision of basic services to urban poor

q: Which one of the following programmes is associated with the development of road transport in India?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral is a major highway project in India that connects the four major cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. This project was initiated by the Government of India to develop road transport and is implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). Its objective is to promote faster and safer travel across the country. Among the other options, NREGP and MNREGA are related to rural employment, while NRHM is associated with healthcare. Hence, the Golden Quadrilateral is the programme associated with the development of road transport in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of Golden Quadrilateral → Approx 5,846 km
☛ Longest National Highway in India → NH-44 (longest, formerly NH-7)
☛ Cities covered under Golden Quadrilateral → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata
☛ Launch of Golden Quadrilateral project → In 2001 by PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ Other road transport related scheme → Bharatmala Pariyojana

q: Name the campaign launched in January 2018 by the Union Minister for the environment, forest and climate change, which lauds small positive actions performed by individuals or organisations to strengthen the cause of environmental protection.
qs.e: This campaign was launched in January 2018 by the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It aims to encourage and appreciate small positive actions by individuals or organizations to strengthen environmental protection. The Green Good Deeds campaign motivates people to adopt activities such as tree planting, water conservation, energy saving, and waste management. It is a people's movement that fosters a positive attitude towards the environment. Other options like Green Skill Development Programme and Champions of the Earth are also environment-related, but this specific campaign focuses on small deeds that make a big difference in environmental conservation.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Green Good Deeds campaign launched? → January 2018
☛ What is the objective of the Green Good Deeds campaign? → To applaud small positive actions for environmental protection
☛ Which ministry is associated with the Green Good Deeds campaign? → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ What type of initiative is the Green Good Deeds campaign? → A people's movement
☛ What activities are promoted under Green Good Deeds? → Tree planting, water conservation, energy saving, waste management

q: Saubhagya Yojana, launched by the Government of India in 2017, is related to providing:
o: funds for marriage of Dalit girls
electricity to all households in India
qs.e: Saubhagya Yojana (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) was launched in September 2017. Its objective is to provide free electricity connections to all un-electrified poor households in rural and urban areas. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Power. The target was to cover all un-electrified households by December 2018. The full name of Saubhagya Yojana is "Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana". Under this scheme, electricity connections were provided free of cost, while the cost of equipment was borne by central and state governments. This scheme aligns with Digital India and Make in India initiatives.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Saubhagya Yojana launched? → September 2017
☛ What is the objective of Saubhagya Yojana? → To provide electricity connections to all households
☛ Which ministry implements Saubhagya Yojana? → Ministry of Power
☛ What is the full name of Saubhagya Yojana? → Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana
☛ By when was the target of Saubhagya Yojana to be achieved? → December 2018

q: Which of the following institutions supported Neeranchal National Watershed Project to improve watershed management program?
qs.e: The Neeranchal National Watershed Project was supported by the World Bank. This project was launched under the Soil Conservation and Water Management mission of the Government of India. Its objective is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of watershed management programs. The project is being implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture. It focuses on natural resource management, water harvesting, and enhancing agricultural productivity. The Neeranchal project is being implemented in 6 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Telangana. It aims to strengthen rural livelihoods and ensure sustainable use of water resources.
qs.kf:
☛ Institution supporting Neeranchal project → World Bank
☛ Ministry associated with the project → Ministry of Agriculture
☛ Number of implementing states → 6
☛ Main objective → Improve watershed management
☛ Supported program → Soil Conservation and Water Management Mission

q: Which Indian scheme is funded by a 0.5% cess levied on all taxable products since Nov 2015?
qs.e: From November 2015, a 0.5% Swachh Bharat Cess was levied on all taxable goods and services. The revenue generated from this cess was used to fund activities under the Swachh Bharat Mission, such as cleanliness drives, construction of toilets, and solid waste management. The cess came into effect on 15 November 2015 and remained applicable until the implementation of GST on 1 July 2017, after which it was subsumed. The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on 2 October 2014 with the objective of making India open defecation free and improving solid waste management. Under this mission, millions of toilets were constructed and awareness about sanitation was promoted. The Swachh Bharat Cess was a dedicated funding mechanism to support these goals.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swachh Bharat Cess implemented? → 15 November 2015
☛ What was the rate of Swachh Bharat Cess? → 0.5%
☛ When was Swachh Bharat Mission launched? → 2 October 2014
☛ What happened to Swachh Bharat Cess after GST? → Subsumed/ended
☛ Main objective of Swachh Bharat Mission? → Open defecation free India

q: Which of the following rural housing schemes by the Government of India is re-structured into Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana (PMAY-G) was launched in 2015 by restructuring the earlier Indira Awas Yojana (IAY). IAY was initiated in 1985 to provide housing to the rural poor who were homeless or living in kutcha houses. PMAY-G aims to provide pucca houses to all eligible rural households by 2022. Under this scheme, financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh (₹1.30 lakh in hilly/difficult areas) is provided to beneficiaries. Other options: Rajiv Awas Yojana was for urban areas, Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana focuses on skill development, and Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana was for rural infrastructure development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMAY-G launched? → 2015
☛ When was IAY launched? → 1985
☛ What is the financial assistance under PMAY-G? → ₹1.20 lakh (plain areas)
☛ What is the target of PMAY-G? → Pucca houses for all by 2022
☛ Which scheme was restructured into PMAY-G? → Indira Awas Yojana

q: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) is related with:
qs.e: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) is a flagship program of the Government of India focused on providing basic civic amenities in urban areas. The mission aims to ensure access to water supply, sewerage, road construction, street lighting, and green spaces in cities. AMRUT aims to make cities more livable and sustainable, and it also supports the development of smart cities, but its primary focus is on basic civic amenities. The mission was launched in 2015 and covers over 500 cities.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of AMRUT → Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
☛ Launch year of AMRUT → 2015
☛ Main focus of AMRUT → Basic civic amenities
☛ Cities covered under AMRUT → Over 500
☛ Key components of AMRUT → Water, wastewater, and urban transport

q: The main aim of the 'Ganga Action Plan’ is:
o: Efficient use of Ganga water for drinking purpose
Reduction of pollution in Ganga river
Efficient use of Ganga water for irrigation
Using Ganga river for generating hydel energy
qs.e: The Ganga Action Plan (GAP) was launched in 1985 with the primary objective of reducing pollution in the Ganga river and improving its water quality. It was implemented by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). The plan focused on treating industrial and domestic wastewater that was being discharged into the river. Under Phase I (GAP-I), sewage treatment plants were established in cities across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal. Phase II (GAP-II) included additional towns. Although the plan achieved limited success, it paved the way for more comprehensive initiatives like Namami Gange.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Ganga Action Plan launched? → 1985
☛ What is the name of the first phase of Ganga Action Plan? → GAP-I
☛ Which agency implemented the Ganga Action Plan? → Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
☛ Which new scheme was launched after Ganga Action Plan? → Namami Gange
☛ What was the main focus of Ganga Action Plan? → Setting up sewage treatment plants

q: What is not the main feature of FAME-2 India Scheme?
o: It plans to support 1 million electric two wheelers, 500,000 electric three wheelers, 55,000 electric four wheelers and 7000 electric buses.
Its target is only private transport vehicles
Total outlay will be Rs. 10,000 crore
It is to encourage faster adoption of electric and hybrid vehicles
qs.e: FAME-2 scheme aims to promote adoption of electric and hybrid vehicles, but its target is not only private transport vehicles. The scheme covers public transport (electric buses), commercial vehicles (three-wheelers), and private vehicles (two-wheelers and four-wheelers). The total outlay is Rs. 10,000 crore, and it plans to support 1 million electric two-wheelers, 500,000 three-wheelers, 55,000 four-wheelers, and 7,000 buses. Saying 'only private vehicles' is incorrect because public and commercial vehicles are also included.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total outlay of FAME-2? → Rs. 10,000 crore
☛ How many electric buses are supported under FAME-2? → 7,000
☛ How many electric three-wheelers are supported under FAME-2? → 500,000
☛ What is the full form of FAME? → Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles
☛ When was FAME-2 launched? → 1 April 2019

q: When was Namami Ganges program approved?
qs.e: The Namami Gange program was approved in the year 2014 by the central government. It is a flagship scheme for the conservation and pollution control of the Ganges river. The program includes projects like sewage treatment plants, riverfront development, and biodiversity conservation along the river. Its objective is to ensure the cleanliness and continuous flow of the Ganges.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Namami Gange program launched? → 2014
☛ What is the main objective of this program? → Conservation and pollution control of Ganga
☛ Which ministry is Namami Gange under? → Ministry of Jal Shakti
☛ What is the length of River Ganga? → 2525 km
☛ Where is the source of River Ganga? → Gangotri, Uttarakhand

q: Which of the following schemes have been started to develop the poorest families?
qs.e: Self Help Group (SHG) is a scheme started for the development of the poorest families. It organizes the poor, especially women, in rural and urban areas to empower them economically. Through SHGs, members make small savings and provide loans among themselves, enabling them to start small businesses. It is part of the government's poverty alleviation and women empowerment policy. The other options - Urbanization, Make in India, and Construction of buildings - do not directly target the poorest families.
qs.kf:
☛ Which bank is associated with the term SHG? → NABARD
☛ In which year were SHGs first started? → 1992
☛ What is the main objective of SHG? → Economic development of the poor
☛ How many members are in an SHG? → 10-20
☛ When was the SHG bank linkage scheme launched? → 2000

q: What does the G2E mean in e-governance?
qs.e: In e-governance, G2E stands for Government to Employees. It refers to the digital interaction between the government and its employees, covering internal communications, payroll, training, and human resource management. The goal of G2E is to enhance efficiency and transparency in government operations. Other categories include G2C (Government to Citizens), G2B (Government to Business), and G2G (Government to Government).
qs.kf:
☛ G2C stands for → Government to Citizens
☛ G2B stands for → Government to Business
☛ G2G stands for → Government to Government
☛ G2E involves → digital services for employees
☛ Main objective of e-governance → transparency and efficiency

q: Under the Sagar Mala project, the overall set of projects were divided into how many number of pillars?
qs.e: The Sagar Mala project is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at port development and boosting the maritime economy. Under this project, the overall set of projects is divided into five pillars: Port Modernization, Port Connectivity, Port-led Industrialization, Coastal Community Development, and Coastal Tourism. This classification facilitates the holistic implementation and monitoring of the project. The Sagar Mala project seeks to accelerate economic growth in India's coastal regions and generate employment opportunities.
qs.kf:
☛ Total pillars of Sagar Mala project → 5
☛ Objective of Sagar Mala → Port modernization and coastal development
☛ Year of launch of Sagar Mala → 2015
☛ Major ports under Sagar Mala → Jawaharlal Nehru, Kandla, Chennai
☛ Key focus of Sagar Mala → Logistics efficiency and green ports

q: The Government of India launched UDAN regional connectivity scheme in the year 2016, this is related to ______ sector.
qs.e: The UDAN (Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik) scheme was launched in 2016 by the Government of India under the Ministry of Civil Aviation. Its aim is to connect remote and regional airports across the country and make air travel affordable for the common public. Under the scheme, airlines are provided financial support to promote regional connectivity. UDAN is a key component of the National Civil Aviation Policy (NCAP) 2016. The scheme has connected over 70 airports so far, making air travel accessible for smaller cities and towns.
qs.kf:
☛ First flight under UDAN scheme → Shimla to Dehradun (2017)
☛ Full form of UDAN → Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik
☛ Objective of UDAN scheme → Boost regional air connectivity
☛ Maximum fare under UDAN scheme → Rs 2,500 per seat per hour
☛ UDAN scheme operated by → Airports Authority of India (AAI)

q: Which program aims to provide houses to the rural poor in India?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) is a flagship housing scheme of the Government of India launched in 2015, aiming to provide pucca houses to all rural and urban poor by 2022. It has two components: PMAY-G (Gramin) for rural areas and PMAY-U (Urban) for urban areas. The scheme provides financial assistance to beneficiaries, with up to ₹1.20 lakh in rural areas and up to ₹2.67 lakh in urban areas. PMAY is implemented under the 'Housing for All' mission, which seeks to ensure every family has a permanent house. The scheme has been successful in increasing housing access and improving living standards for the poor.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana launched? → 2015
☛ What is the full form of PMAY? → Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana
☛ How much financial assistance is provided under PMAY-G in rural areas? → ₹1.20 lakh
☛ What is the objective of PMAY? → Provide pucca houses to all
☛ Under which mission is PMAY implemented? → Housing for All

q: The Sagarmala programme is the flagship programme to promote port-led development in the country through harnessing India’s 7,500 km long coastline. 14,500 km of potentially navigable waterways was approved by the Union cabinet in the year __________.
qs.e: The Sagarmala programme was approved by the Union Cabinet in the year 2015. It is a flagship initiative to promote port-led development, leveraging India's 7,500 km long coastline and 14,500 km of potentially navigable waterways. The programme aims to develop industrial clusters near ports, enhance connectivity, and reduce logistics costs. Key components include port modernization, new waterways, and coastal community development. Sagarmala is integrated with other initiatives like Namami Gange and inland waterway development. The programme is implemented by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Sagarmala programme launched? → 2015
☛ Length of India's coastline? → 7,500 km
☛ Length of potentially navigable waterways? → 14,500 km
☛ Main focus of Sagarmala? → Port-led development
☛ Sagarmala comes under which ministry? → Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

q: When was the 20-year road plan introduced in Independent India?
qs.e: The first 20-year road plan (Twenty-Year Road Development Plan) in Independent India was launched in 1961. It is also known as the Nagpur Road Plan. The plan aimed to develop a comprehensive road network across the country, connecting rural areas with urban centers. It set targets for road construction from 1961 to 1981, focusing on increasing road density (length of road per 100 sq km area). The plan was prepared by the Indian Roads Congress (IRC). Subsequently, the second 20-year road plan was initiated in 1981, known as the Bombay Road Plan.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first 20-year road plan introduced? → 1961
☛ What is the name of the first 20-year road plan? → Nagpur Road Plan
☛ When was the second 20-year road plan introduced? → 1981
☛ What is the name of the second 20-year road plan? → Bombay Road Plan
☛ Which body prepared these plans? → Indian Roads Congress (IRC)

q: What is the primary purpose of information kiosks set up by the government?
o: To provide free food and beverages to citizens
To offer citizens easy access to information and services such as bill payments, registrations and public information
To allow citizens to participate in online gaming competitions
To enable government employees to monitor social media activities of citizens
qs.e: Government information kiosks are set up to provide digital services to citizens. Their primary purpose is to offer easy access to government schemes, forms, bill payments, and application status. These kiosks are part of e-governance and are often operated through Common Service Centres (CSCs). They help bridge the digital divide, especially in rural areas. Citizens can register, obtain certificates, and file complaints at these kiosks. The goal is to make services accessible, transparent, and efficient.
qs.kf:
☛ Purpose of e-Governance → To make government services online and accessible
☛ Full form of CSC → Common Service Centre
☛ Digital India Mission → Launched to promote digital services
☛ Benefits of information kiosks → Time saving, transparency, easy access
☛ Services provided by kiosks → Income certificate, caste certificate, etc.

q: Which state is leading with the highest number of solar power installations under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY) by March 2025?
qs.e: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY) was launched in February 2024 to install rooftop solar panels on homes. By March 2025, Gujarat leads with the highest number of solar installations. The state's high solar potential, favorable policies, and subsidies contribute to this lead. Gujarat targets 6 GW of rooftop capacity by 2025. Under this scheme, households are promised free electricity up to 300 units per month, resulting in annual savings of ₹1,000 crores. Gujarat has historically performed well in rooftop solar programs. The scheme provides 40% subsidy for systems up to 3 kW and 20% for 3-10 kW.
qs.kf:
☛ PMSGMBY launch year → 2024
☛ Free electricity limit → 300 units per month
☛ Subsidy percentage → 40% (up to 3 kW)
☛ National target → 40 GW rooftop (by 2025-26)
☛ Key implementing agency → MNRE

q: What is the primary objective of India's 'Bharat 6G Vision', launched in March 2023?
o: Establishing India as a leader in 6G technology by 2030
Commercializing 6G services only in urban areas
qs.e: The primary objective of India's 'Bharat 6G Vision', launched in March 2023, is to establish India as a global leader in 6G technology by 2030. This vision aims to promote research, design, development, and manufacturing of 6G technology within the country. The government has set up the 'Bharat 6G Alliance' to bring together industry, academia, and research institutions. The vision focuses on self-reliance and innovation in 6G, rather than importing infrastructure from developed nations. It aims to make India a net exporter of 6G technology and services, ensuring affordable and ubiquitous connectivity across the nation.
qs.kf:
☛ Target year of Bharat 6G Vision → 2030
☛ Bharat 6G Vision launched in → March 2023
☛ Bharat 6G Alliance aims to → Boost 6G R&D
☛ Key focus of Bharat 6G Vision → Self-reliance and innovation
☛ Expected speed of 6G → 100 times faster than 5G

q: What is the focus of the Scheme of Human Resources Development in Sports?
o: Training and development of sports professionals
Building swimming pools for agile swimmers
Construction of gyms in every part of India
qs.e: The Scheme of Human Resources Development in Sports primarily focuses on training and development of sports professionals. This scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India. It aims to enhance the skills of coaches, players, physiotherapists, and other sports specialists to improve the overall quality and international competitiveness of Indian sports. Unlike infrastructure schemes, this initiative centers on human capital. Trained professionals play a vital role in nurturing talent and advancing sports performance at all levels.
qs.kf:
☛ Focus of Human Resources Development in Sports scheme → Training and development of sports professionals
☛ Ministry responsible for this scheme → Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
☛ Main objective of the scheme → To train sports experts
☛ Professionals trained include → Coaches, players, physiotherapists
☛ This scheme differs from → Sports infrastructure development

q: What is the primary goal of the Indian government's Bhashini project?
o: To create a multilingual AI platform for real-time translation among Indian languages
To establish a national database of dialects
To develop a new programming language for Indian developers
qs.e: The primary goal of the Bhashini project is to create a multilingual AI platform for real-time translation among Indian languages. It falls under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and aims to promote digital inclusion in India. The platform uses open-source technology and machine learning to facilitate communication across various Indian languages. Bhashini aims to make internet services and digital content accessible in local languages, benefiting rural and non-English speaking citizens. It is part of the 'Digital India' initiative and is expected to improve e-governance, education, and healthcare services.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry is Bhashini project under? → Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
☛ What is the primary goal of Bhashini? → To create a multilingual AI platform for real-time translation among Indian languages
☛ What technology does Bhashini use? → Open-source technology and machine learning
☛ Which initiative is Bhashini a part of? → Digital India
☛ Who will benefit from Bhashini? → Rural and non-English speaking citizens

q: Which initiative is intended to encourage domestic manufacturing and attract foreign investment?
qs.e: The Make in India initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its primary objective is to boost domestic manufacturing, attract foreign investment, and transform India into a global manufacturing hub. The initiative focuses on 25 sectors including automobiles, electronics, pharmaceuticals, defense, and railways. It liberalized FDI norms, strengthened intellectual property rights, and implemented ease of doing business reforms. As a result, FDI inflows have significantly increased, and India improved its ranking in the Global Innovation Index. The initiative also aims to create jobs and enhance skill development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Make in India launched? → 25 September 2014
☛ How many sectors are covered under Make in India? → 25 priority sectors
☛ What is the slogan of Make in India? → 'Make in India, Make for the World'
☛ Which ministry leads the Make in India initiative? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Which index improved due to Make in India? → Global Innovation Index

q: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) were established to promote export-oriented industrialisation. What is a primary incentive offered to firms operating in SEZs?
qs.e: SEZs are special economic zones created to promote export-oriented industries. Firms in SEZs are offered incentives like tax holidays (e.g., income tax exemptions) and better infrastructure (power, roads, ports). The aim is to attract foreign investment and boost exports. The SEZ Act 2005 governs these incentives. Higher import duties, strict labour laws, or ban on foreign investments are not features of SEZs.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the SEZ Act enacted? → 2005
☛ What is the main objective of SEZs? → Promote export-oriented industrialisation
☛ Where was India's first SEZ established? → Kandla, Gujarat (as APZ in 1965)
☛ What is a major tax incentive in SEZs? → Income tax exemption
☛ Which ministry administers SEZ policy? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry

q: Which of the following infrastructure initiatives is associated with urban development in India?
o: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan
Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
qs.e: The Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) is a flagship urban development initiative launched by the Government of India in 2015. Its objective is to improve basic infrastructure such as water supply, sewerage, green spaces, and urban transport in selected cities. This mission focuses on infrastructure development in urban areas. Other options: RURBAN Mission is for rural-urban areas, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) promotes solar energy in agriculture, and Managed Services Provider Scheme relates to telecommunications. Hence, AMRUT is the correct infrastructure initiative associated with urban development in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of AMRUT → Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
☛ Launch year of AMRUT → 2015
☛ Number of cities covered under AMRUT (Phase 1) → 500
☛ Main objective of AMRUT → Improvement of urban infrastructure
☛ Other urban development scheme → Smart City Mission

q: The Make in India initiative aims to boost domestic manufacturing. In which year was the 'Make in India' campaign launched?
qs.e: The Make in India campaign was launched on 25 September 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its primary objective is to transform India into a global manufacturing hub and boost employment opportunities within the country. The initiative targets 25 sectors, including automobiles, electronics, defence, and pharmaceuticals. It has played a crucial role in attracting foreign investment and improving the 'Ease of Doing Business' ranking of India. Since its launch in 2014, it has strengthened India's manufacturing capacity and is a major step towards an 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-reliant India). The campaign focuses on fostering innovation, enhancing skill development, and creating world-class infrastructure to support manufacturing.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the slogan of Make in India? → 'Make in India, Make for the World'
☛ How many sectors are covered under Make in India? → 25 sectors
☛ What is the objective of Make in India? → To make India a global manufacturing hub
☛ Which ministry is associated with Make in India? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Who launched the Make in India campaign? → Narendra Modi

q: Digital literacy is now essential for human development in the knowledge economy. Which programme was launched to promote digital literacy among rural citizens in India?
qs.e: To promote digital literacy, the Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA). Its aim is to make rural citizens digitally literate so they can use internet and digital services. This scheme is part of the Digital India initiative. BharatNet provides broadband connectivity to rural areas, while PM-WANI relates to public Wi-Fi hotspots. Under PMGDISHA, at least one member from each rural household is trained in digital literacy. This enables rural citizens to access online services, e-governance, and digital payments, enhancing their participation in the knowledge economy.
qs.kf:
☛ Rural digital literacy programme → PMGDISHA
☛ Full form of PMGDISHA → Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan
☛ Objective of Digital India → Transform India into a digitally empowered society
☛ Purpose of BharatNet → To provide broadband connectivity to rural areas
☛ PM-WANI relates to → Public Wi-Fi hotspots

q: In which of the following years was the Bharatmala Pariyojana approved by the Government of India covering a length of 34,800 km to improve connectivity and reduce logistics cost in the country?
qs.e: The Bharatmala Pariyojana was approved by the central government in 2017. It is India's largest highway development project, aiming to construct 34,800 km of national highway corridors. The project includes economic corridors, border roads, coastal roads, and other connectivity projects. Its primary objectives are to reduce logistics costs and improve connectivity across the country. The project is being implemented in five phases with a total investment of approximately Rs 5.35 lakh crore. Bharatmala Pariyojana is executed under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
qs.kf:
☛ Total length of Bharatmala Pariyojana → 34,800 km
☛ Year of approval of Bharatmala Pariyojana → 2017
☛ Total investment of Bharatmala Pariyojana → Approx Rs 5.35 lakh crore
☛ Major components of Bharatmala Pariyojana → Economic corridors, border roads, coastal roads
☛ Objective of Bharatmala Pariyojana → Reduce logistics cost and improve connectivity

q: Which initiative is associated with the construction of individual household toilets in India?
qs.e: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on 2nd October 2014. Its main objective is to eliminate open defecation. Under this initiative, individual household toilets are constructed. The government provides financial assistance for toilet construction in rural and urban areas. The scheme was launched on the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. This campaign played a major role in making India open defecation free. Swachh Bharat Mission is implemented in two phases - rural and urban. Millions of toilets have been built under it, focusing on cleanliness.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swachh Bharat Abhiyan launched? → 2nd October 2014
☛ Main objective of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? → Open defecation free India
☛ Financial assistance amount for toilet construction? → 12,000 rupees (rural areas)
☛ Who is considered the ideal of this campaign? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ How many phases of Swachh Bharat Mission? → Two phases: rural and urban

q: Infrastructure has been a key pillar for sustained growth. Which initiative was launched in 2020 to coordinate infrastructure projects in India?
qs.e: In 2020, the Indian government launched the PM Gati Shakti initiative, a National Master Plan aimed at coordinating infrastructure projects across various ministries and departments. This initiative integrates sectors such as roads, railways, airports, ports, power lines, and pipelines. A digital platform was developed under this plan, helping stakeholders plan and monitor projects in real-time. It reduces construction costs and helps complete projects on time. PM Gati Shakti is part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and focuses on enhancing logistics efficiency.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PM Gati Shakti launched? → 2020
☛ What is the main objective of PM Gati Shakti? → Coordination of infrastructure projects
☛ Under which initiative does PM Gati Shakti come? → Atmanirbhar Bharat
☛ How many ministries are involved in PM Gati Shakti? → 16
☛ What is the full name of PM Gati Shakti? → Pradhan Mantri Gati Shakti National Master Plan

q: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme is aimed at boosting manufacturing. Which of the following sectors is NOT covered under the PLI scheme?
qs.e: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme aims to boost the manufacturing sector. It covers sectors like Pharmaceuticals, Automobiles, Electronics, Textiles, Food Processing, and others. Tourism is a service sector and not related to manufacturing, hence it is not covered under the PLI scheme. The PLI scheme currently covers 14 key manufacturing sectors.
qs.kf:

☛ What is the budget for the Pharmaceuticals sector under PLI? → ₹15,000 crore

q: Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) operates under the aegis of:
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
qs.e: Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) was originally under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, but was transferred to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in 2018. It aims to provide vocational training to non-literate and neo-literate persons aged 15 years and above, especially rural and urban poor. JSS operates through voluntary organizations and runs courses aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF). As of 2023-24, there are about 300 JSSs functioning across India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main objective of JSS? → To provide vocational training to non-literate and neo-literate persons.
☛ Under which ministry does JSS operate? → Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
☛ Which ministry earlier governed JSS? → Ministry of Labour and Employment.
☛ Which framework does JSS follow? → National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).
☛ When was JSS established? → In 1967.

q: Which of the following rural housing schemes by the Government of India is re-structured into Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana?
qs.e: The Government of India launched the Indira Awas Yojana (IAY) to provide housing to the homeless and poor families in rural areas. It was restructured into the Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana (PMAY-G) in 2015-16. The goal of PMAY-G is to provide pucca houses to all eligible rural households by 2022. Beneficiaries are selected based on the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) data. The scheme provides financial assistance of up to ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh in difficult areas. Beneficiaries also receive bank loans and concessions on construction materials. Women are given co-ownership rights to the house. This restructuring aimed to enhance the effectiveness and coverage of rural housing.

☛ Full form of PMAY-G → Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana
☛ Year of restructuring → 2015-16
☛ Basis for beneficiary selection → SECC 2011
☛ Assistance amount (plain areas) → ₹1.20 lakh
☛ Right given to women → Co-ownership

q: Which of the following Civic body has been declared best performing Municipal Corporation of India under PM Awas Yojana in December 2020?
qs.e: In December 2020, the Government of India evaluated the performance of municipal corporations across the country under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY). Vishakhapatnam Municipal Corporation was declared the best performing municipal corporation. This award recognized excellence in housing development, beneficiary identification, and scheme implementation. Vishakhapatnam completed the highest number of housing units and reduced the backlog of pending houses. The scheme aims to provide affordable housing to all by 2022. Other options included Hyderabad, Chennai, and Indore, but Vishakhapatnam outperformed them.

q: What is the objective of the KUSUM programme launched by the Indian government?
o: Promotion of organic farming in the country
Providing financial security to farmers through harnessing solar energy capacities
Starts ups for women and youth
qs.e: The KUSUM (Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan) programme was launched in 2019. Its main objective is to empower farmers economically by utilizing solar energy. Under the scheme, farmers can install solar panels on their barren land to generate electricity and sell the surplus to the grid, providing them an additional income source. The scheme has three components: 1) small solar power plants, 2) solar agricultural pumps, and 3) solarization of existing pumps. The central government provides 30% subsidy, and state governments give additional subsidies. Farmers also benefit from solar pumps for irrigation, reducing dependence on diesel and grid electricity.

q: What is the name of Ganga cleanup program launched in 2014?
qs.e: In 2014, the central government launched the Namami Gange program for the cleaning and conservation of the Ganges river. It adopts an integrated approach, including sewage treatment, riverfront development, biodiversity conservation, and public awareness. The program is implemented under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Its objective is to reduce pollution in the Ganges and its tributaries and maintain continuous flow. Under Namami Gange, several projects are operational, such as sewage treatment plants and riverfront beautification.

q: What is the name of the scheme which aims to provide LED bulbs to domestic consumers at subsidized rate?
qs.e: The Ujala Scheme (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All) is a flagship initiative by the Government of India aimed at providing LED bulbs to domestic consumers at subsidized rates. Implemented by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), the scheme focuses on energy conservation and reduction of carbon emissions. Launched in 2015, it targets the distribution of 77 crore LED bulbs across the country through collaboration with DISCOMs and private companies. The scheme has significantly reduced electricity consumption and lowered electricity bills for households. It is a key part of India’s efforts to promote energy efficiency and combat climate change.
