☛ What product is distributed under the Ujala scheme? → LED bulbs

q: Samarth scheme is implemented by the Union ministry of ______
qs.e: The Samarth scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India. Its full name is 'Samarth (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector)'. It was launched in 2014 with the objective of providing skilled workforce to the textile and clothing industry. The scheme primarily targets unemployed youth, women, and traditional weavers. Under this, various training programmes are conducted to enhance employability and entrepreneurship in the textile sector.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry implements the Samarth scheme? → Ministry of Textiles
☛ What is the full name of Samarth scheme? → Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector
☛ In which year was Samarth scheme launched? → 2014
☛ What is the main objective of Samarth scheme? → Skill development in textile sector
☛ Who are the target groups of Samarth scheme? → Unemployed youth, women, and traditional weavers

q: 'Make-In-India's symbol is a lion made of ______.
qs.e: The 'Make in India' campaign's symbol is a lion made of cogs (gear teeth). This design represents India's manufacturing capability and industrial strength. The lion symbolizes courage and power, while the cogs represent gears and machinery, forming the foundation of production and growth. The symbol is part of the initiative launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2014 to promote manufacturing in India and transform the country into a global manufacturing hub.
qs.kf:
☛ Make in India launch year → 2014
☛ Animal used in the logo → Lion
☛ Component forming the lion → Cogs
☛ Campaign slogan → 'Zero Defect, Zero Effect'
☛ Associated ministry → Ministry of Commerce and Industry

q: In which year did the Government of India launch the Smart Cities Mission?
qs.e: The Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission on June 25, 2015. The mission aims to improve urban infrastructure, digital technology, and quality of life in cities. Under this mission, 100 cities are selected to be developed as smart cities. It is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Smart cities include features like smart transportation, energy management, waste management, and e-governance.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Smart Cities Mission launched? → 2015
☛ How many cities are selected under the mission? → 100
☛ Which ministry implements the Smart Cities Mission? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ What is the main objective of the Smart Cities Mission? → Improve urban infrastructure and quality of life
☛ What features are included in a smart city? → Smart transportation, energy management, waste management, e-governance

q: What is the name of the Prime Minister’s new rooftop solar power scheme launched by Shri Narendra Modi on 15 February 2024?
o: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
qs.e: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana on 15 February 2024. The scheme aims to promote solar power generation by installing rooftop solar panels on residential houses. It will provide free electricity of up to 300 units per month to households, reducing their electricity bills. The scheme involves a total investment of Rs 75,000 crore and aims to cover 1 crore families. This initiative is a major step towards making India self-reliant in renewable energy and reducing carbon emissions.
qs.kf:
☛ Full name of scheme → PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
☛ Launch date → 15 February 2024
☛ Total budget → Rs 75,000 crore
☛ Beneficiaries → 1 crore families
☛ Free electricity → Up to 300 units per month

q: The Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission on:
qs.e: The Government of India launched the Smart Cities Mission on 25 June 2015. The mission aims to promote infrastructure, digital technology, and sustainable development in urban areas. It is implemented under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. The mission selected 100 cities to be developed as smart cities. Key features include smart transportation, disaster management, energy efficiency, and e-governance. The mission was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 June 2015.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Smart Cities Mission launched? → 25 June 2015
☛ How many cities were selected under the Smart Cities Mission? → 100 cities
☛ Which ministry oversees the Smart Cities Mission? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ What is the objective of the Smart Cities Mission? → Develop urban areas with digital and infrastructure facilities
☛ Who launched the Smart Cities Mission? → Prime Minister Narendra Modi

q: To raise awareness on the safe use of digital payment services and prevent scams, which of the following institution of India launched a UPI Safety Awareness Campaign ‘Main Moorkh Nahi Hoon’?
qs.e: NPCI launched the 'Main Moorkh Nahi Hoon' UPI safety awareness campaign to promote secure digital payments and prevent scams. The campaign educates users about UPI security features and fraud prevention. NPCI is the umbrella organisation for operating retail payment systems in India and has developed services like UPI, RuPay cards, and IMPS. While RBI regulates payment systems, DSCI focuses on data security, and l4C coordinates cybercrime response, the awareness campaign was specifically launched by NPCI to protect UPI users from cyber fraud.
qs.kf:
☛ What does UPI stand for? → Unified Payments Interface
☛ Where is the headquarters of NPCI? → Mumbai
☛ Who launched the RuPay card? → NPCI
☛ Who is the regulator of digital payments in India? → RBI
☛ When was NPCI established? → 2008

q: Which of the following states is NOT covered under the Atal Bhujal Yojana?
qs.e: The Atal Bhujal Yojana (ABHY) is a central scheme launched in 2020 aimed at sustainable management and conservation of groundwater resources. The scheme covers 78 districts across 7 states. These states are Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. Jharkhand is not included in this scheme. The program is supported by the World Bank and focuses on areas experiencing groundwater depletion. Its objective is to strengthen groundwater management and promote water conservation through community participation.
qs.kf:
☛ Objective of Atal Bhujal Yojana → sustainable groundwater management and conservation
☛ Total states covered → 7 states
☛ Total districts covered → 78 districts
☛ Partner organization → World Bank
☛ Nodal ministry → Ministry of Jal Shakti

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 3
q: What was the budget allocated in the Smart City Mission for the financial year 2023-24?
qs.e: The Smart City Mission is a flagship initiative by the Government of India aimed at making cities smart and sustainable. For the financial year 2023-24, a budget of ₹8,000 crore was allocated to this mission. This budget falls under the Ministry of Urban Development and is used for various smart city projects such as digital infrastructure, transportation, and environmental sustainability. Compared to previous years, this allocation reflects the government's commitment to ensuring continuity of smart city projects. Under the mission, 100 cities have been selected so far, and many projects have been completed.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Smart City Mission launched? → 2015
☛ How many cities are covered under the mission? → 100
☛ Which ministry administers the Smart City Mission? → Ministry of Urban Development
☛ What was the budget for Smart City Mission in FY 2023-24? → ₹8,000 crore
☛ What is the primary objective of the Smart City Mission? → To make cities smart and sustainable

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3
q: What is one of the interventions included in the rural development programmes?
o: Providing road connectivity to unconnected villages
qs.e: Rural development programmes aim to improve the quality of life in rural areas. These include development of infrastructure, agriculture, education, health, and employment. Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is a key programme that provides road connectivity to unconnected villages. This enhances connectivity and facilitates access to markets, educational institutions, and health services. Urban airports, skyscrapers, and metro rail are related to urban development, not rural development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana launched? → 2000
☛ Under which ministry does PMGSY fall? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What is the rural livelihood mission called? → Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
☛ What is the rural component of Swachh Bharat Mission called? → Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)
☛ How many days of employment are guaranteed under MGNREGA per year? → 100 days

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The Digital India initiative, launched in 2015, marked a significant step in India’s postreform development trajectory. Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the Digital India initiative?
o: Digital Infrastructure as a Utility to Every Citizen
qs.e: The Digital India initiative has three pillars: Digital Infrastructure as a Utility to Every Citizen, Governance and Services on Demand, and Digital Empowerment of Citizens. Launched on July 1, 2015, by the Government of India, the aim is to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. Key focus areas include e-governance, broadband connectivity, public internet access, and digital literacy. 'Privatisation of Internet Services' is not a pillar; it is a separate policy approach. Digital India emphasizes public-private partnerships, not outright privatization.
qs.kf:
☛ Three pillars of Digital India → Digital Infrastructure, Governance & Services on Demand, Digital Empowerment of Citizens
☛ Launch date of Digital India → July 1, 2015
☛ Objective → Digitally empowered society and knowledge economy
☛ Key programmes → BharatNet, DigiLocker, e-Hospital
☛ Motto → Power to Empower

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2
q: What was the purpose of the Imperial Service Scheme (1885)?
o: To raise troops for British defence, paid by princely states
qs.e: The Imperial Service Scheme of 1885 was introduced by the British to strengthen their military forces without incurring additional costs. Under this scheme, princely states were required to maintain troops that could be used for the defense of the British Empire. These troops, known as Imperial Service Troops, were under British command and were deployed in external wars and internal security. The princely states bore the entire cost of maintaining these forces. The scheme was implemented by Lord Dufferin and significantly enhanced British military capacity in India. It was a strategic move to ensure loyalty and military support from the princely states while keeping them financially responsible for the troops.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Viceroy introduced the Imperial Service Scheme? → Lord Dufferin
☛ Who bore the cost of Imperial Service Troops? → The princely states
☛ What was the main objective of the Imperial Service Scheme? → To raise troops for British defence
☛ What were the troops raised under this scheme called? → Imperial Service Troops
☛ In which year was the Imperial Service Scheme introduced? → 1885

q: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) was launched in the year _____ by the Government of India.
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) was launched on 25 June 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its objective is to provide pucca houses to all urban poor by 2022. Under the scheme, beneficiaries receive a subsidy ranging from Rs 1.5 lakh to Rs 2.67 lakh. It has four components: ISSR, CLSS, BLC, and AHP. The scheme was designed to address the housing shortage in urban areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMAY-U → Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
☛ Ministry under PMAY-U → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ CLSS in PMAY-U stands for → Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme
☛ Target year for PMAY-U → 2022
☛ PMAY-G (Gramin) launched in → 2016

q: To attract investments from across the globe and strengthen India's manufacturing sector was the main objective of:
qs.e: Make In India initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its primary objective was to attract global investments and strengthen India's manufacturing sector. The initiative focused on 25 sectors including automobiles, defense, pharmaceuticals, and electronics. Under Make In India, FDI policies were liberalized and intellectual property rights were strengthened. The logo of the initiative features a lion. It aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Make In India launched? → 25 September 2014
☛ What is the symbol of Make In India? → Lion
☛ How many sectors are included in Make In India? → 25
☛ What is the main objective of Make In India? → Attract global investment and boost manufacturing
☛ Which ministry implements Make In India? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Under the Bharatmala Pariyojana, how many kilometres of roads are slated for development to improve border and international connectivity?
qs.e: The Bharatmala Pariyojana is a flagship road development program by the Government of India, which plans to develop 2,000 km of roads specifically to improve border and international connectivity. Launched in 2017, this project aims to connect different parts of the country through highways. The total length of roads to be constructed under the project is 34,800 km, including economic corridors, feeder routes, and border roads. The development of border roads is strategically important to strengthen trade and security with neighboring countries.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Bharatmala Pariyojana launched? → 2017
☛ What is the total length of roads under this project? → 34,800 km
☛ How many km of roads are for border connectivity? → 2,000 km
☛ What is the main objective of Bharatmala? → Development of national highways and improving connectivity
☛ Which ministry funds this project? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2
q: What is the main goal of the PM Gati Shakti initiative?
qs.e: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan is a digital platform that integrates infrastructure projects of various ministries. Its main objective is to improve coordination in the transportation and logistics sector, thereby reducing costs and increasing efficiency. It connects different modes like roads, railways, airports, ports, and pipelines. Under the plan, data from 16 ministries is linked through GIS-based mapping. This brings transparency in the planning and implementation of projects.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PM Gati Shakti launched? → 13 October 2021
☛ Under which ministry is this scheme operated? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Which technology is it based on? → GIS (Geographic Information System)
☛ How many ministries are involved? → 16
☛ What is the slogan of this scheme? → Sabka Prayas, Sabka Vikas

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 to facilitate investment, foster innovation, build best in class infrastructure and make India a hub for manufacturing, design and innovation?
qs.e: On 25 September 2014, the Government of India launched the Make in India initiative to transform India into a global manufacturing, design, and innovation hub. It aims to facilitate investment, foster innovation, build world-class infrastructure, and improve the ease of doing business. The initiative focuses on 25 sectors including automobiles, defense, pharmaceuticals, electronics, and textiles. Key measures under Make in India include liberalization of FDI policies, introduction of e-business facilities, and strengthening intellectual property rights. The initiative also emphasizes job creation and increasing the contribution of manufacturing to India's GDP. Make in India is coordinated by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
qs.kf:
☛ When was Make in India launched? → 25 September 2014
☛ What is the main objective of Make in India? → To make India a global manufacturing and innovation hub
☛ How many sectors does Make in India cover? → 25 sectors
☛ Which ministry oversees Make in India? → Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
☛ What reforms are associated with Make in India? → FDI liberalization and ease of doing business

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2
q: In which year was 'Make in India' launched by the Government of India to facilitate investment, foster innovation, enhance skill development, protect intellectual property, and build best in class manufacturing infrastructure in India?
qs.e: The ‘Make in India’ initiative was launched on September 25, 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its aim is to transform India into a global manufacturing hub. The campaign focuses on facilitating investment, fostering innovation, enhancing skill development, protecting intellectual property, and building best-in-class manufacturing infrastructure. It covers 25 sectors including automobiles, aerospace, defense, electronics, etc. This initiative is linked with other schemes like ‘Digital India’, ‘Startup India’, and ‘Skill India’. Under this, FDI policies were liberalized and ‘Ease of Doing Business’ was improved.
qs.kf:
☛ When was ‘Make in India’ launched? → September 25, 2014
☛ How many sectors are covered under ‘Make in India’? → 25
☛ What is the slogan of ‘Make in India’? → ‘Zero Defect, Zero Effect’
☛ Which ministry oversees ‘Make in India’? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ What is the objective of ‘Make in India’? → Make India a global manufacturing hub

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2
q: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), a flagship mission aimed at addressing the urban housing shortage in India, launched?
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) was launched on 25 June 2015 with the objective of providing affordable housing to all urban dwellers by 2022. The scheme is implemented in two phases: PMAY-Urban and PMAY-Rural. Under the urban component, the 'Housing for All' mission aims to construct 1.2 crore houses by 2022. Beneficiaries receive an interest subsidy of up to ₹1.5 lakh. The scheme covers economically weaker sections (EWS), low income groups (LIG), and middle income groups (MIG).
qs.kf:
☛ Launch date of PMAY Urban → 25 June 2015
☛ Main objective of PMAY → Housing for All by 2022
☛ Maximum interest subsidy under PMAY → ₹1.5 lakh
☛ Beneficiary categories under PMAY → EWS, LIG, MIG
☛ PMAY slogan → Housing for All

q: Who launched the Golden Quadrilateral Project?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral Project is an ambitious road construction program that connects four major metropolitan cities of India: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. It was launched in 2001 by the then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The project was the first phase of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP). Its total length is approximately 5,846 kilometers, comprising four/six-lane highways. The main objective of this project was to boost the Indian economy by ensuring fast and smooth transportation of goods and people across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total length of the Golden Quadrilateral? → Approx. 5,846 km
☛ Which project was it a part of? → First phase of NHDP
☛ Which four cities does it connect? → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata
☛ When was it completed? → 2012
☛ Which ministry was involved in its construction? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

q: Which of the following projects is being implemented by C-DAC, Pune?
qs.e: Project JATAN, implemented by C-DAC, Pune, is a national-level digital initiative aimed at digitizing artifacts kept in museums and cultural institutions. Under this project, high-resolution imaging and 3D scanning technologies are used to create digital records of artifacts. This not only aids in preservation but also provides online access to the general public. The project comes under the Ministry of Culture and is a significant step towards preserving Indian heritage. Other options: Project SATH-E relates to education, Project Zojila is a tunnel project, and Project BHARATMALA is a road transport project.
qs.kf:
☛ Project JATAN → Implemented by C-DAC, Pune
☛ Project SATH-E → Related to education sector
☛ Project Zojila → Tunnel construction project
☛ Project BHARATMALA → Road transport project
☛ Digitization → Of museum artifacts

q: The Bharatmala Pariyojana is associated with:
qs.e: The Bharatmala Pariyojana is an ambitious road and highway development project launched by the Government of India in 2017-18. Its primary objective is to expand and upgrade National Highways across the country, enhancing connectivity to border areas, ports, and economic corridors. The project aims to develop a highway network of approximately 34,800 km, including 24,800 km under the National Highway Development Project and the remaining 10,000 km as economic corridors and other roads. It focuses on reducing logistics costs and boosting economic growth by improving road infrastructure. The project is implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Bharatmala Pariyojana launched? → 2017-18
☛ Target road length under Bharatmala? → 34,800 km
☛ Main focus of Bharatmala? → National Highways and Economic Corridors
☛ Which ministry implements Bharatmala? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ Objective of Bharatmala? → Reduce logistics cost and improve connectivity

q: Name the compendium of Digital India which was released in 2019?
qs.e: The compendium of the Digital India programme released in 2019 is titled 'Digital Bharat, Saksham Bharat'. This compendium highlights the achievements of Digital India, focusing on digital infrastructure, e-governance, and digital literacy. The initiative aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. The title 'Digital Bharat, Saksham Bharat' emphasizes the goal of making India capable and self-reliant through digital technology. It covers various aspects such as broadband connectivity, digital services, and citizen empowerment.
qs.kf:
☛ Digital India compendium released in 2019 → Digital Bharat, Saksham Bharat
☛ Digital India launched on → 1 July 2015
☛ Pillars of Digital India → Digital infrastructure, e-services, digital literacy
☛ Objective of Digital India → Empower India digitally
☛ Schemes under Digital India → BharatNet, DigiLocker, e-Sign

q: The 'India Lounge', set up by the IBEF was inspired by the 'Make in India' programme. What does IBEF stand for?
qs.e: IBEF stands for India Brand Equity Foundation. It is an organization that works to promote Indian exports and strengthen the brand image of India globally. IBEF was established by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The 'India Lounge' is an initiative inspired by the 'Make in India' programme, showcasing Indian industries and products at international platforms. The lounge helps in promoting Indian brands at various global events, thereby enhancing the 'Brand India' image.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of IBEF? → India Brand Equity Foundation
☛ Which ministry established IBEF? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ What is the main objective of IBEF? → To promote Indian brands and increase exports
☛ Which programme inspired the 'India Lounge'? → Make in India
☛ Where is the headquarters of IBEF located? → New Delhi

q: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan is a flagship programme by the Government of India, as of September 2020. Which of the following is NOT a feature of it?
o: To facilitate the employment of migrant workers who have gone to their home states.
Many projects involving migrant workers have also been initiated for building of roads, highways, etc.
It has been initiated in 11 districts in Mission Mode.
Under this campaign, rural infrastructure would be built with the involvement of migrant workers.
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan (PMGKRA) was launched in June 2020 to provide employment to migrant workers who returned to their home states due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It was implemented in 116 districts across the country in Mission Mode, not just 11 districts. The campaign focused on building rural infrastructure through 25 categories of works, including road construction, housing, and water conservation. The scheme was for a duration of 125 days and ensured the involvement of migrant workers. Thus, Option 3 is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMGKRA launched? → June 2020
☛ How many districts were covered? → 116 districts
☛ What was the duration of the campaign? → 125 days
☛ Which workers were targeted? → Migrant workers
☛ How many categories of works were included? → 25 categories

q: Which ministry controls the 'Saubhagya Yojana' launched by the Central Government in 2017?
qs.e: The 'Saubhagya Yojana' (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) was launched by the Central Government in 2017. Its objective was to provide electricity connections to all households in rural and urban areas. The scheme is implemented under the Ministry of Power. Under this scheme, electricity connections were provided free of cost, aiming for 'electricity to every household'. It was executed by the DISCOMs (Power Distribution Companies). Later, the scheme was merged with other schemes, but its administrative control remained with the Ministry of Power. This scheme played a crucial role in increasing electricity access across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Saubhagya Yojana launched? → 2017
☛ What is the full name of Saubhagya Yojana? → Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana
☛ What was provided under Saubhagya Yojana? → Free electricity connections
☛ What was the objective of Saubhagya Yojana? → To provide electricity to all households
☛ Which ministry controls Saubhagya Yojana? → Ministry of Power

q: The objective of the 'Sagarmala Project' is to:
o: reduce logistics cost for domestic cargo and EXIM cargo
install equipment for gas and oil exploration
qs.e: The Sagarmala Project is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at developing the country's coastal regions and promoting maritime transport. Its primary objective is to reduce logistics costs for domestic and EXIM (export-import) cargo, thereby enhancing the global competitiveness of Indian goods. The project involves modernization of ports, construction of new ports, development of coastal economic zones, and strengthening of inland waterways. It also contributes to employment generation and economic growth in coastal states and union territories. By improving port connectivity and efficiency, Sagarmala aims to lower transportation costs and facilitate faster movement of goods.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Sagarmala Project launched? → 2015
☛ What is the main objective of Sagarmala? → Reduce logistics cost
☛ How many ports are being developed under Sagarmala? → More than 14
☛ Which ministry is Sagarmala associated with? → Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
☛ How many Coastal Economic Zones (CEZs) are planned under Sagarmala? → 14

q: Who among the following launched ADITI 2.0 challenges and DISC 12 to foster innovation, entrepreneurship and ‘Aatmanirbharta’ in defence during DefConnect 4.0 on 7 October 2024?
qs.e: Defence Minister Shri Rajnath Singh launched ADITI 2.0 challenges and DISC 12 at the DefConnect 4.0 event on 7 October 2024. ADITI (Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX) aims to promote innovation and startups in the defence sector. DISC 12 (Defence India Startup Challenge) identifies innovative solutions for defence problems. This initiative is crucial for achieving self-reliance in defence production under the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' campaign. Under the iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) scheme, these challenges provide opportunities to startups and entrepreneurs.
qs.kf:
☛ ADITI 2.0 launched by → Rajnath Singh
☛ DefConnect 4.0 held on → 7 October 2024
☛ Full form of DISC → Defence India Startup Challenge
☛ Full form of iDEX → Innovations for Defence Excellence
☛ Full form of ADITI → Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX

q: What year was started for 'Ganga Action Plan'?
qs.e: The Ganga Action Plan (GAP) was launched by the Government of India to control pollution in the river Ganga. It was inaugurated on 14 January 1986 by the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. The main objective was to prevent urban and industrial waste from flowing into the Ganga. In its first phase, sewage treatment plants were set up in 25 cities. This plan was implemented under the Ministry of Environment. Later, in 2014, the Namami Gange Programme was initiated for further rejuvenation.
qs.kf:
☛ Who launched Ganga Action Plan? → Rajiv Gandhi
☛ When was Ganga Action Plan launched? → 1986
☛ What was the objective of Ganga Action Plan? → To protect Ganga from pollution
☛ Which programme succeeded Ganga Action Plan? → Namami Gange (2014)
☛ Under which ministry is Ganga Action Plan? → Ministry of Environment

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following government schemes focuses on the development of urban infrastructure in India?
qs.e: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) is a flagship central scheme focused on the development of urban infrastructure in India. It was launched in 2015. The mission aims to improve basic urban facilities such as water supply, sewerage, urban transport, and green spaces. AMRUT covers more than 500 cities across the country. In contrast, MGNREGA is a rural employment guarantee scheme, RURBAN Mission focuses on rural-urban synergy, and PMGSY is a rural road development scheme. Therefore, the correct option related to urban infrastructure is AMRUT.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of AMRUT? → Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
☛ When was AMRUT launched? → 2015
☛ How many cities does AMRUT cover? → More than 500
☛ What is the main focus of AMRUT? → Urban infrastructure like water, sewerage, transport
☛ Which ministry implements AMRUT? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

q: When did the Indian Government launch the Digital India program to connect rural areas with high-speed Internet networks and improve digital literacy?
qs.e: The Digital India program was launched by the Indian government on 1 July 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society. Its key objectives include connecting rural areas with high-speed internet and improving digital literacy. The initiative, spearheaded by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aims to make government services digitally available. A major component is the BharatNet project, which connects gram panchayats through optical fiber networks. The program has nine pillars: Broadband Highways, Universal Access, Public Internet Access, e-Governance, e-Kranti, Information for All, Electronics Manufacturing, IT for Jobs, and Early Harvest Programs. Digital India also includes initiatives like DigiLocker, Umang app, and e-Health services.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the slogan of Digital India? → "Power to Empower"
☛ What is the goal of BharatNet project? → Connect all gram panchayats with broadband
☛ Which mobile app was launched under Digital India? → Digital India app
☛ How many pillars does Digital India have? → Nine
☛ Which ministry oversees Digital India? → Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

q: The Digital India programme was launched in which year to enable digital delivery of services to citizens?
qs.e: The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its objective is to deliver government services digitally to citizens. The programme focuses on three main components: digital infrastructure, digital literacy, and e-governance. It includes initiatives like BharatNet, DigiLocker, and e-Sign. The year 2015 is considered the base year for Digital India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the mascot of Digital India? → Elephant (mascot: 'Digital India Elephant')
☛ Which scheme is not part of Digital India programme? → Ayushman Bharat
☛ What is the objective of Digital India programme? → To provide digital services to citizens
☛ How many pillars are there in Digital India programme? → 9 pillars
☛ What is the tagline of Digital India programme? → Power to Empower

q: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched in which of the following years?
qs.e: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 by the Government of India. Its aim is to boost the manufacturing sector, attract foreign investment, and make India a global manufacturing hub. The campaign was initiated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It targets 25 sectors including automobiles, defence, pharmaceuticals, and electronics. The initiative focuses on improving 'Ease of Doing Business' and creating employment opportunities.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of sectors targeted under 'Make in India' → 25
☛ Slogan of the initiative → 'Make in India, Sell in India'
☛ Ministry associated → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Logo of the campaign → A lion image
☛ Launch venue → Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi

q: Which Indian government initiative has been introduced to support informal workers in urban areas?
qs.e: PM-SVANidhi (Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi) scheme was launched in June 2020. Its objective is to support informal workers in urban areas, especially street vendors, in recovering from the economic crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Under this scheme, a working capital loan of up to Rs. 10,000 is provided without any guarantee. The loan tenure is 1 year, and interest subsidy is given upon timely repayment. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Other options like Jal Shakti Abhiyan relate to water conservation, PM-KISAN is for farmers, and PM Ujjwala Yojana provides LPG connections.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PM-SVANidhi launched? → June 2020
☛ What is the maximum loan amount under PM-SVANidhi? → Rs. 10,000
☛ Which ministry implements PM-SVANidhi? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ What is the full form of PM-SVANidhi? → Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi
☛ Who is the target beneficiary of PM-SVANidhi? → Urban street vendors

q: What is the focus of the 6G research project at IIIT-Naya Raipur funded under DST’s TTDF scheme?
o: Creating an AI-driven telecom cloud platform
Developing a prototype for 6G cell-free communication
qs.e: The primary focus of the 6G research project at IIIT-Naya Raipur, funded under DST's TTDF scheme, is to develop a prototype for 6G cell-free communication. This project is part of India's ambitious plans for sixth-generation (6G) technology. TTDF, which stands for Telecom Technology Development Fund, promotes R&D in telecom technologies. Cell-free communication aims to achieve better connectivity and lower latency without traditional cellular architecture. This initiative will contribute to indigenous 6G technology development and strengthen the Digital India initiative. The prototype will address key challenges in wireless communication and pave the way for future 6G networks.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of TTDF → Telecom Technology Development Fund
☛ Focus of 6G project at IIIT-Naya Raipur → Cell-free communication prototype
☛ Advantage of cell-free communication → Lower latency and better connectivity
☛ Full form of DST → Department of Science and Technology
☛ India's 6G mission → To develop indigenous 6G technology

q: As of December 2025, under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), what is the minimum size required for a house unit provided to beneficiaries?
qs.e: Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), the minimum size of a house unit provided to beneficiaries is 25 square meters (approximately 269 square feet), as of December 2025. The scheme ensures construction of pucca houses with basic amenities such as a kitchen, toilet, and others. The central government provides financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh in hilly/difficult areas per unit. This minimum size standard is designed to provide dignified living conditions to rural families. The scheme aims to achieve 'Housing for All' in rural India by 2029.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum house unit size under PMAY-G → 25 sq. m
☛ Financial assistance in plain areas under PMAY-G → Rs. 1.20 lakh
☛ Financial assistance in hilly/difficult areas under PMAY-G → Rs. 1.30 lakh
☛ Objective of PMAY-G → Housing for All
☛ Amenities included in PMAY-G house → Kitchen, toilet

name: All Questions · Q1–41
sub: Govt Schemes and Policies - Women, Child, Social Welfare & Financial Inclusion

q: What is the risk coverage under "Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana"?
A. 2 lakh rupees
B. 1 lakh rupees
C. 1.5 lakh rupees
D. 2.25 lakh rupees
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a government-backed accident insurance scheme launched on 9 June 2015. It provides ₹2 lakh risk coverage for accidental death or total permanent disability and ₹1 lakh for partial permanent disability to individuals aged 18-70 years. The annual premium is only ₹12, which is auto-debited from the bank account. The scheme is available to all bank account holders.
qs.kf:
☛ Annual premium of PMSBY → ₹12
☛ Age limit → 18-70 years
☛ Coverage for total disability → ₹2 lakh
☛ Coverage for partial disability → ₹1 lakh
☛ Launch year → 2015

q: Government of India has introduced 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padao' programme to address the issue of -
qs.e: 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' (BBBP) scheme was launched by the Government of India on 22 January 2015. Its primary objective is to address the issue of declining child sex ratio (CSR) and to prevent gender-biased sex selection, female infanticide, and child marriage. The program focuses on ensuring the survival, protection, and education of the girl child. It is implemented through a coordinated effort of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Education. The scheme also aims to change societal mindsets and promote gender equality.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the BBBP scheme launched? → 22 January 2015
☛ What is the main objective of BBBP? → To improve the child sex ratio
☛ Which ministry is the nodal ministry for BBBP? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ Which areas are focused under BBBP? → Education, health, and safety of girl child
☛ Which ministries coordinate for BBBP? → Women and Child Development, Health, and Education

q: Which scheme was launched in 2014 to provide affordable access to financial services- bank account, credit, insurance, pension etc.?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on 28 August 2014 for financial inclusion. It aims to provide affordable access to financial services like bank account, credit, insurance, and pension. Under this scheme, accounts can be opened with zero balance, offering accident insurance cover of up to ₹5 lakh and life insurance cover of ₹2 lakh. It has significantly promoted financial inclusion in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Mascot of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana → 'Jan Dhan Sarathi'
☛ Who inaugurated Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana? → Prime Minister Narendra Modi
☛ Insurance cover under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana → ₹2 lakh life insurance and ₹5 lakh accident insurance
☛ Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is part of which trinity? → Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity
☛ Objective of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana → Provide at least one bank account to every family

q: Which of the following financial inclusion schemes was launched in June 2015 to prompt the unorganised workforce to join the National Pension Scheme?
o: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
qs.e: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) was launched in June 2015 to encourage the unorganised workforce to join the National Pension System (NPS). It is primarily targeted at workers who are not part of any organized pension scheme. Under APY, the government contributes 50% of the subscriber's contribution for 5 years, up to ₹1000 per year. The scheme is available for individuals aged 18-40 years and guarantees a minimum pension of ₹1000 per month after the age of 60. It replaced the earlier Swavalamban Yojana and is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).
qs.kf:
☛ When was Atal Pension Yojana launched? → June 2015
☛ How many years does the government contribute in APY? → 5 years
☛ Maximum age limit to join APY? → 40 years
☛ Minimum guaranteed pension under APY? → ₹1000 per month
☛ Which sector workers is APY for? → Unorganised sector

q: Which of the following statements is NOT the purpose behind Swadhar Greh Scheme?
o: Provide Government jobs to socially backward women
Shelter, food, and clothing for women in distress
Provide support to enable women to start afresh
qs.e: Swadhar Greh Scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. Its main aim is to provide temporary shelter, food, clothing, medical care, and psychological support to women in distress. This scheme targets women above 18 years who are victims of domestic violence, human trafficking, rape, family disputes, or other crises. It also focuses on rehabilitation, skill development, and economic empowerment to enable women to start afresh. The scheme does provide legal aid, but providing government jobs is not part of its objectives. The correct answer is the one statement that does not align with the scheme’s purpose.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry implements Swadhar Greh Scheme? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ What is the minimum age for women under Swadhar Greh Scheme? → 18 years
☛ In which year was Swadhar Greh Scheme launched? → 2001-02
☛ What type of scheme is Swadhar Greh? → Centrally Sponsored Scheme
☛ What is the main objective of Swadhar Greh Scheme? → Provide shelter, food, clothing, and rehabilitation to women in distress

q: Name the scheme initiated to protect elderly persons aged 60 years and above against a future fall in their interest income due to the uncertain market conditions.
qs.e: This scheme was launched to protect elderly persons aged 60 years and above against a future fall in their interest income due to uncertain market conditions. It was introduced by the Government of India in 2017. Under this scheme, senior citizens can invest a minimum of Rs. 1000 and a maximum of Rs. 15 lakh. It offers a guaranteed interest rate of 8% per annum for a period of 10 years. The scheme is administered by LIC and aims to provide stable income to the elderly.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana → 2017
☛ Administering agency → LIC
☛ Minimum investment amount → Rs. 1000
☛ Maximum investment amount → Rs. 15 lakh
☛ Guaranteed interest rate and tenure → 8% per annum, 10 years

q: Name the scheme which provides risk coverage of Rs. 2 lakhs for accidental death or full disability and Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability to people in the age group 18 to 70 years.
o: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a social security scheme by the Government of India that provides accidental insurance cover to people aged 18 to 70 years. It offers risk coverage of Rs. 2 lakhs for accidental death or full disability and Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability. This scheme is different from Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), which provides life insurance. The annual premium is very low (Rs. 20), and the amount is directly deducted from the bank account. The scheme was launched to provide affordable accidental insurance protection to the common public.

☛ What is the annual premium under PMSBY? → Rs. 20
☛ What is the cover for full disability under PMSBY? → Rs. 2 lakhs

☛ What is the age limit for PMSBY? → 18 to 70 years
☛ Which scheme provides Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability? → Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana

q: Name the scheme started by the Department of Science and Technology that provides a platform to women scientists and technologists for pursuing research in basic or applied sciences in the frontier areas of science and engineering.
qs.e: The Women Scientists Scheme-A (WOS-A) launched by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) provides a platform to women scientists and technologists to pursue research in basic or applied sciences in frontier areas of science and engineering. This scheme is aimed at women who have taken a career break and wish to re-enter research. Selected candidates under WOS-A receive a research grant for a period of three years. Additionally, WOS-B and WOS-C focus on science communication and science technology entrepreneurship, respectively. WOS-A specifically encourages basic and applied research, helping women regain their footing in the scientific community.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of WOS-A → Women Scientists Scheme-A
☛ Research duration under WOS-A → 3 years
☛ Objective of WOS-B → Science communication and outreach
☛ Objective of WOS-C → Science technology entrepreneurship
☛ Target group for WOS-A → Women scientists with career break

q: The Integrated Child Protection Scheme was launched in the year:
qs.e: The Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) was launched by the Government of India in 2009-2010. It aims to provide protection and rehabilitation to children in difficult circumstances. The scheme is under the Ministry of Women and Child Development and includes strengthening of child care institutions, adoption, and the juvenile justice system. It helps implement the provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000. Under ICPS, financial assistance is given to state governments to protect children's rights. The scheme also contributes to preventing child trafficking and child labour.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of ICPS? → Integrated Child Protection Scheme
☛ Which ministry administers ICPS? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ What is the main objective of ICPS? → To provide protection and rehabilitation to children
☛ Which act does ICPS help implement? → Juvenile Justice Act, 2000
☛ What are the provisions under ICPS? → Child care institutions, adoption, juvenile justice system

q: PAHAL Scheme is related with:
qs.e: The PAHAL scheme (Pratyaksh Hastantarit Labh) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India that involves direct transfer of LPG subsidy to consumers. Under this scheme, the subsidy amount is directly credited to the bank accounts of eligible LPG consumers, eliminating intermediaries and enhancing transparency. It was implemented nationwide in 2014 and aims to prevent misuse and diversion of subsidized LPG cylinders. The scheme is also known as DBTL (Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG). It helped the government remove millions of fake connections, leading to significant savings. This scheme is a key example of direct benefit transfer in the energy sector.
qs.kf:
☛ PAHAL scheme relates to? → Direct transfer of LPG subsidy
☛ Full name of PAHAL scheme? → Pratyaksh Hastantarit Labh
☛ When was PAHAL scheme launched? → 2014
☛ PAHAL scheme is also known as? → DBTL (Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG)
☛ How is subsidy transferred under PAHAL? → Directly to bank accounts

q: Related to 'Prime Minister Ujjwala Yojna' ______.
qs.e: Prime Minister Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May 2016. It aims to provide LPG connections to women from BPL households to promote clean cooking fuel. The scheme protects women's health and reduces environmental pollution. Beneficiaries receive a subsidy for the connection fee. Over 10 crore connections have been issued so far.

☛ Who is the beneficiary? → Women from BPL families
☛ What is the objective? → Provide LPG connections

q: The Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) program was launched in the year __________.
qs.e: The Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) program was launched in the year 1982. This program was initiated by the Government of India under the Ministry of Rural Development. Its objective was to make rural women self-reliant and improve their living standards. Under DWCRA, women were organized into groups and provided training and credit for income-generating activities. Later, this program was merged into the Swarn Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), which was launched in 1999. DWCRA played a significant role in the empowerment of rural women.
qs.kf:
☛ When was DWCRA launched? → 1982
☛ Which ministry implements DWCRA? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ What was the main objective of DWCRA? → To make rural women self-reliant
☛ Into which scheme was DWCRA later merged? → Swarn Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
☛ When was SGSY launched? → 1999

q: Which scheme of the Indian government provides lump sum ex-gratia assistance to outstanding sportspersons of yesteryears?
o: Major Dhyan Chand National Scheme for Sportsperson
Maulana Azad National Scheme for Outstanding Sportsperson
Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund for Sportspersons
qs.e: This scheme was launched by the Government of India to provide lump sum ex-gratia assistance to outstanding sportspersons of yesteryears who are in financial distress. Under this fund, financial aid is given for medical treatment, education, and other necessities. The scheme is administered by the Ministry of Sports and aims to honor and support former athletes. Other options include Major Dhyan Chand Scheme, which provides pension to sportspersons; Maulana Azad Scheme, which encourages current sportspersons; and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Protsahan Yojana, which rewards sports institutions.

☛ Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Fund objective → Financial aid to former sportspersons
☛ Major Dhyan Chand Scheme benefit → Lifetime pension to sportspersons
☛ Maulana Azad Scheme objective → Encouragement to current sportspersons
☛ Rajiv Gandhi Khel Protsahan Yojana benefit → Awards to sports institutions
☛ Administered by → Ministry of Sports

q: What is the primary aim of the ‘Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana’?
o: Providing mobile phones to rural households
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May 2016. Its primary aim is to provide free LPG connections to women from poor households, thereby protecting them from health hazards caused by smoke from traditional fuels like firewood and coal. The scheme promotes women empowerment, health safety, and environmental protection. Beneficiary families are identified based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011. Over 10 crore LPG connections have been distributed so far under this scheme.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana launched? → May 2016
☛ Who receives LPG connections under this scheme? → Women from poor households
☛ On what basis are beneficiaries identified? → SECC 2011
☛ Which type of fuel usage does the scheme aim to reduce? → Traditional fuels
☛ How many LPG connections have been distributed so far? → Over 10 crore

q: Which of the following groups is provided support under the One-Stop Centre (OSC) scheme?
o: Only women from a specific caste or religion
Only women working in government offices
Only married women in urban areas
All women and girls below 18 years of age affected by violence
qs.e: The One-Stop Centre (OSC) scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India. It aims to provide integrated support to all women and girls below 18 years of age who are affected by violence. Services include medical aid, legal assistance, psychological counseling, and temporary shelter. The scheme does not discriminate based on caste, religion, marital status, or urban/rural background. The primary objective is to offer a single point of access for all necessary services to survivors, thereby preventing further trauma. The OSC scheme plays a crucial role in addressing violence against women in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which ministry does the OSC scheme fall? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ What is the full name of OSC? → One-Stop Centre
☛ Who is eligible for assistance under OSC? → All women and girls below 18 affected by violence
☛ What services does OSC provide? → Medical, legal, psychological, and shelter services
☛ When was the OSC scheme launched? → In 2015

q: The DBT‑funded project that first produced a GMP‑grade viral vector for Indian CAR‑T research was supported under which flagship scheme?
qs.e: The DBT-funded project that first produced a GMP-grade viral vector for Indian CAR-T research was supported under the National Biopharma Mission (NBM). This mission is a flagship central sector scheme implemented by the Department of Biotechnology. The production of the viral vector is a major breakthrough for CAR-T cell therapy in India, used in cancer treatment. NBM aims to strengthen the biopharmaceutical sector and promote indigenous product development. Viral vectors are essential for genetic modification of CAR-T cells. This achievement marks a significant step toward self-reliance in gene therapy and personalized medicine in India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main objective of National Biopharma Mission? → To strengthen biopharmaceutical sector in India
☛ National Biopharma Mission comes under which ministry? → Ministry of Science and Technology
☛ What is the full form of GMP? → Good Manufacturing Practice
☛ CAR-T therapy is used for treating which disease? → Cancer
☛ What is the full form of DBT? → Department of Biotechnology

q: The government has made efforts to boost financial inclusion. Which 2014 scheme aimed to provide universal banking access in India?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on 28 August 2014 to provide universal banking access to every citizen. It is the largest financial inclusion initiative, offering zero balance accounts, RuPay debit cards, accident insurance of ₹1 lakh, and life insurance cover of ₹2 lakh. No minimum balance is required to open an account. The scheme has played a crucial role in bringing the unbanked population into the formal financial system.
qs.kf:
☛ Mascot of Jan Dhan Yojana → Bhagirath
☛ What is the logo/mascot of Jan Dhan Yojana? → Bhagirath
☛ Department under which Jan Dhan Yojana falls → Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
☛ Life insurance cover under Jan Dhan Yojana → ₹2 lakh
☛ Accident insurance cover under Jan Dhan Yojana → ₹1 lakh

q: Which year was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana launched?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on 28 August 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It is a National Mission for Financial Inclusion aimed at providing banking services to the unbanked population, including bank accounts, insurance, and pension. Under this scheme, there is no requirement of minimum balance in any bank account. Account holders receive benefits like a RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover, and overdraft facility. This scheme is a crucial step to empower economically weaker sections and bring them into the formal financial system.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch date of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana → 28 August 2014
☛ Objective of PMJDY → Financial inclusion
☛ Minimum balance required under this scheme → Zero
☛ Card provided to Jan Dhan account holders → RuPay debit card
☛ Accident insurance cover under the scheme → Rs 2 lakh

q: Which scheme of the Government of India facilitates bank loans between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore to at least one scheduled caste/ scheduled tribe borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises?
o: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
qs.e: Stand Up India Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2016. It aims to provide bank loans to Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs for setting up greenfield enterprises. Each bank branch is required to provide loans between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore to at least one SC/ST borrower and at least one woman borrower. The scheme falls under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana and promotes financial inclusion and entrepreneurship. Loans have a maximum tenure of 7 years and require no collateral. This scheme is specifically for individuals who are not already running any business.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Stand Up India Scheme launched? → 2016
☛ What is the loan range under this scheme? → Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore
☛ Who are the beneficiaries? → SC/ST and women entrepreneurs
☛ What is the maximum loan tenure? → 7 years
☛ Is collateral required? → No

q: Which of the following is a government initiated insurance scheme, administered by LIC, for rural landless households?
qs.e: This scheme is launched for rural landless households and is administered by LIC. Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (AABY) is a government insurance scheme started in 2007. It covers individuals aged 18 to 59 years. The scheme provides financial assistance of ₹30,000 on natural death and ₹75,000 on accidental death. It also offers educational grants. Janashree Bima Yojana is also administered by LIC but for various occupational groups. Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana is a health insurance scheme administered by different entities. Jeevan Umang Bima Yojana is a regular life insurance policy. Hence, the correct answer is Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana launched? → 2007
☛ What is the sum assured on natural death under this scheme? → ₹30,000
☛ What is the sum assured on accidental death? → ₹75,000
☛ Who administers this scheme? → LIC
☛ Who are the beneficiaries of this scheme? → Rural landless households

q: Which mission was launched by the Govt. of India in December 2014 to achieve full immunisation coverage for all children and pregnant women at a rapid pace?
qs.e: In December 2014, the Government of India launched Mission Indradhanush to rapidly achieve full immunisation coverage for all children and pregnant women. The mission targeted children who were left out or dropped out from routine vaccination. It provided vaccination against 7 diseases: diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, polio, tuberculosis, measles, and hepatitis B. Later, it was upgraded to the Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI). This mission significantly increased full immunisation coverage to over 90% in many areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Mission Indradhanush → 2014
☛ Target group → Children and pregnant women
☛ Number of diseases covered → 7
☛ Upgraded version → Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI)

q: How much insurance cover is available for accidental death under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?

q: One Stop Centre scheme was launched on:
qs.e: The One Stop Centre scheme was launched by the Government of India on 1st April 2015. It is implemented under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The scheme aims to provide integrated support to women affected by violence, including legal aid, medical assistance, psychological counseling, and shelter. q: Nai Roshni Scheme is a Government welfare scheme launched to empower ______ women.
qs.e: Nai Roshni Scheme is a government welfare scheme launched to empower minority women in India. It is implemented by the Ministry of Minority Affairs. The scheme aims to enhance the leadership skills, confidence, and economic independence of minority women. It provides training to women so that they can actively participate in social, economic, and political spheres. The scheme was launched in 2012-13 and is operational across the country. It focuses on the holistic development of minority women and helps them become self-reliant and empowered.

q: Which initiative of the Government of India aims to integrate various sub-schemes related to safety, security, and empowerment of women under an umbrella scheme for greater efficiency and effectiveness in India?
qs.e: Mission Shakti is an umbrella scheme of the Government of India aimed at integrating various sub-schemes related to safety, security, and empowerment of women. It consolidates existing programmes like One Stop Centre, Women Helpline, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, and others under a single framework for better resource utilization and implementation efficiency. The mission focuses on creating a safe environment for women, enhancing their participation, and promoting self-reliance.
