q: Which scheme is focussed on promoting entrepreneurship among SC/STs and women by providing loans at concessional rates?
qs.e: Stand-Up India Scheme was launched in 2016. Its main objective is to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and women. Under this scheme, bank loans ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore are provided to entrepreneurs from these categories. Loans are given at concessional rates and no collateral or guarantee is required. The scheme focuses on establishing greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors. The loan tenure is up to 7 years. Stand-Up India aims to make economically backward sections self-reliant and encourage employment generation. The scheme is implemented through State Bank of India, public sector banks, and regional rural banks.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Stand-Up India Scheme launched? → 2016
☛ What is the loan limit under Stand-Up India? → ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore
☛ Which are the target groups under Stand-Up India? → SC/ST and women
☛ Is collateral required under Stand-Up India? → No
☛ Under which scheme are greenfield enterprises established? → Stand-Up India

q: Which of the following is the coverage provided by the 'Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)' in case of partial disability?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a government insurance scheme providing coverage for accidental death or disability. Under this scheme, for partial disability, the coverage amount is ₹1 lakh, while total disability and accidental death both provide ₹2 lakh each. The scheme is available to individuals aged 18 to 70 years at an annual premium of just ₹12. Coverage is valid only for accident-related disabilities, not natural causes. Account holders in any bank or post office can avail this scheme. The scheme aims to provide affordable insurance to the masses.
qs.kf:
☛ PMSBY coverage for partial disability → ₹1 lakh
☛ PMSBY coverage for total disability → ₹2 lakh
☛ PMSBY coverage for accidental death → ₹2 lakh
☛ PMSBY annual premium → ₹12
☛ PMSBY maximum age limit → 70 years

q: With which of the following is the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana related?
o: An insurance scheme offering vehicle insurance cover for accidents due to any reason.
An insurance scheme offering life insurance cover for death due to any reason.
An insurance scheme offering education for girls.
An insurance scheme offering home insurance cover for accidents due to any reason.
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) is a life insurance scheme by the Government of India, offering ₹2 lakh cover for death due to any reason for individuals aged 18 to 50 years. The annual premium is ₹436, auto-debited from the bank account. It is administered by the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC). The scheme aims to provide financial security to low-income families. It is distinct from the accident insurance scheme (PMSBY), which covers only accidental death.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the annual premium of PMJJBY? → ₹436
☛ What is the insurance cover amount in PMJJBY? → ₹2 lakh
☛ Who administers PMJJBY? → LIC (Life Insurance Corporation)
☛ What is the age limit for PMJJBY? → 18 to 50 years
☛ What type of insurance is PMJJBY? → Life Insurance

q: The National Pension System Vatsalya (NPS Vatsalya) was launched on
qs.e: The National Pension System Vatsalya (NPS Vatsalya) was launched on 18 September 2024 by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. This scheme provides pension security for minor children, allowing parents or guardians to open accounts in their children's names. It is a special category under NPS with a minimum annual contribution of ₹1,000. When the child turns 18, the account automatically converts into a regular NPS account. The scheme aims to inculcate financial discipline and long-term saving habits among children from an early age.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch date of NPS Vatsalya → 18 September 2024
☛ Minimum annual contribution under NPS Vatsalya → ₹1,000
☛ Age at which NPS Vatsalya converts to regular NPS → 18 years
☛ NPS Vatsalya is for → Minor children
☛ Minister who launched NPS Vatsalya → Nirmala Sitharaman

q: The first two-wheeler public transport service for all women started in Gurgaon was called _______.
A. Bikxie Blue
B. Bikxie Pink
C. Bikxie Green
D. Bikxie Red
qs.e: The first two-wheeler public transport service for all women started in Gurgaon was called Bikxie Pink. This service was launched in the year 2018 with the aim of providing safe, convenient, and affordable transportation for women. Under this service, women could travel on bikes or scooties, which were specifically driven by female drivers. Bikxie Pink played a significant role in making commuting safer for women in the city.
qs.kf:
☛ In which city was Bikxie Pink service launched? → Gurgaon (Gurugram)
☛ Who is Bikxie Pink dedicated to? → Women
☛ In which year was Bikxie Pink launched? → 2018
☛ What was the aim of Bikxie Pink? → Safe and affordable transport for women
☛ Who operated Bikxie Pink vehicles? → Female drivers

q: Which of the following welfare schemes' achievements have been recongnised by the Guiness World Records?
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) has been recognized by the Guinness World Records for its achievements. Launched in August 2014, the scheme aimed to provide banking services to every citizen. Within 100 days, over 11 crore accounts were opened, which Guinness World Records recognized as the largest financial inclusion campaign. The scheme offers zero-balance accounts, RuPay cards, and accident insurance coverage. Other schemes like Kaushal Vikas, Suraksha Bima, and Krishi Sinchai are related to skill development, insurance, and irrigation, but only Jan Dhan Yojana received the Guinness record.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMJDY launched? → 28 August 2014
☛ In which category did it get the Guinness record? → Largest financial inclusion campaign
☛ Which card is provided under this scheme? → RuPay Debit Card
☛ What is the minimum balance required? → Zero balance
☛ What is the accident insurance cover under this scheme? → ₹2 lakh

q: People in the age group of ________ are eligible for the 'Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana' ('PMSBY') scheme.
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a government-backed accidental insurance scheme in India. The eligibility age for this scheme is 18 to 70 years. This means individuals between 18 and 70 years of age can avail the benefits. The scheme is available to all bank account holders with an annual premium of just ₹20, which is auto-debited from the account. In case of accidental death or permanent disability, the coverage is ₹2 lakh. The scheme operates on an opt-in basis, requiring the customer's consent. It is administered by the Ministry of Finance.
qs.kf:
☛ Annual premium of PMSBY → ₹20
☛ Insurance cover for accidental death in PMSBY → ₹2 lakh
☛ PMSBY is linked to which account → Any savings bank account
☛ PMSBY comes under which ministry → Ministry of Finance
☛ Types of disability cover in PMSBY → Two (permanent total and permanent partial)

q: Which of the following government schemes is for accident insurance?
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a government accident insurance scheme launched in 2015. It provides accidental death and permanent total disability cover of ₹2 lakh and permanent partial disability cover of ₹1 lakh to bank account holders aged 18-70 years at an annual premium of just ₹12. The scheme is auto-debited from the account and is linked to Jan Dhan accounts. Other options: Make in India is a manufacturing initiative, Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao focuses on gender ratio and education, and Atal Pension Yojana is a pension scheme for old age security.
qs.kf:
☛ Annual premium of PMSBY → ₹12
☛ Maximum accident death cover under PMSBY → ₹2 lakh
☛ Year of launch of PMSBY → 2015
☛ Eligible age group for PMSBY → 18-70 years
☛ Ministry under which PMSBY falls → Ministry of Finance

q: What is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana?
o: A small deposit scheme for the girl child.
A scheme to provide bicycles for girls studying in the 10th class.
A scheme to provide skills that give employability to women.
A scheme to develop self-defence skills in girls.
qs.e: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a small savings scheme launched by the Government of India under the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. It allows an account to be opened in the name of a girl child below 10 years of age. Minimum deposit is Rs. 250 and maximum is Rs. 1.5 lakh per year. The account matures after 21 years or upon marriage (after 18 years). Interest rate is declared quarterly by the government. The scheme provides financial security for the girl's education and marriage.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which ministry does Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana come? → Ministry of Finance
☛ What is the minimum annual deposit in this scheme? → Rs. 250
☛ When does the account mature? → 21 years or upon marriage
☛ Which campaign is this scheme linked to? → Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao
☛ Is there any tax benefit under this scheme? → Yes, under Section 80C

q: Which year was the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Yojana was launched?
qs.e: The Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme was launched on 22nd January 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Panipat, Haryana. The main objective of this scheme is to improve the child sex ratio and promote education and empowerment of girls. It is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health, and Ministry of Education. The scheme focuses on awareness campaigns at the district level and strict action against female foeticide.
qs.kf:
☛ Full name of BBBP → Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao
☛ Launch year → 2015
☛ Launch venue → Panipat, Haryana
☛ Nodal Ministry → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ Objective → Improve child sex ratio and promote girl education

q: Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP) comes into existence as a part of the _______ Five-Year Plan.
qs.e: The Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP) is a key scheme launched for the holistic development of tribal areas in India. It came into existence as a part of the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979). The main objective is to promote economic, social, and educational development of tribal communities along with infrastructure development. Under ITDP, targeted development programs are implemented through the Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP). Currently, there are 194 ITDP areas across the country. The scheme is executed by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of ITDP? → Integrated Tribal Development Project
☛ Under which plan does ITDP operate? → Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP)
☛ Which ministry oversees ITDP? → Ministry of Tribal Affairs
☛ What is the objective of ITDP? → Holistic development of tribal areas
☛ How many ITDP areas are there? → 194

q: What is the agenda behind the Government of India's flagship programme ‘Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana’?
o: To provide affordable housing to all.
To provide a minimum monthly pension of ₹1000 or ₹2000
Assured pension on a guaranteed return of 8% after making a minimum initial investment for Senior Citizen
To provide a life cover of ₹200,000 against a premium of ₹330 per annum.
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY) is a pension scheme launched by the Government of India to provide financial security to senior citizens. Under this scheme, individuals aged 60 years and above can make a minimum initial investment to receive a guaranteed annual return of 8% on their investment, ensuring a fixed pension. The scheme is available through banks and post offices. Pension payments can be made monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annually. The objective is to provide senior citizens with safe and regular income from their savings, protecting them from market risks.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PMVVY → Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana
☛ Eligibility age → 60 years and above
☛ Guaranteed return → 8% per annum
☛ Scheme tenure → 10 years
☛ Minimum investment → ₹1,562 (for monthly pension)

q: Under the new scheme for first-time Women, SC and ST entrepreneurs, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the maximum loan amount that can be availed?
qs.e: In the Union Budget 2025-26, a new scheme was announced for first-time women, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs. Under this scheme, eligible entrepreneurs can avail loans up to ₹2 crore without any collateral. The objective is to promote entrepreneurship among disadvantaged sections and support economic empowerment. This scheme complements existing initiatives like Startup India and Stand-Up India. The government has allocated sufficient funds to reach a larger number of beneficiaries.
qs.kf:
☛ Maximum loan amount under scheme → ₹2 crore
☛ Target beneficiaries → First-time women, SC and ST entrepreneurs
☛ Budget year → 2025-26
☛ Key feature → Collateral-free loan
☛ Objective → Promote entrepreneurship among disadvantaged sections

q: The NAVYA (Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls) initiative, launched on 24 June 2025, is for which age group?
qs.e: The NAVYA initiative launched on 24 June 2025 by the Ministry of Women and Child Development aims to empower adolescent girls through skill training. It is specifically designed for girls aged 16 to 18 years. This age group was chosen because it represents a critical period of school dropout and the need for vocational skills for employment. The initiative provides vocational training, life skills education, and career guidance. It helps girls achieve economic independence and a respectable position in society.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched the NAVYA initiative? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ What is the full form of NAVYA? → Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls
☛ When was NAVYA launched? → 24 June 2025
☛ What is the target age group of NAVYA? → 16-18 years
☛ What is the objective of NAVYA? → To empower adolescent girls through vocational training

q: As of December 2025, under the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), eligible account holders can access an overdraft facility of up to:
qs.e: The Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a flagship financial inclusion scheme of the Government of India, launched in 2014. Under this scheme, eligible account holders can avail an overdraft (OD) facility of up to ₹10,000. This facility is specifically applicable to accounts that have been active for at least 6 months and have regular transactions. The overdraft limit increases gradually after account opening, starting from ₹5,000 and later reaching ₹10,000. Eligibility requires the account holder to be between 18-65 years of age. As of December 2025, this limit remains ₹10,000. The scheme aims to connect the poor and disadvantaged sections with banking services.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PMJDY launched? → 28 August 2014
☛ What is the insurance cover under PMJDY? → ₹1 lakh (accident) + ₹2 lakh (life)
☛ Minimum age to open a PMJDY account? → 18 years
☛ Maximum overdraft limit under PMJDY? → ₹10,000
☛ Objective of PMJDY? → Financial inclusion

q: Which of the following is an in-situ conservation measure taken by India?
qs.e: In-situ conservation refers to the conservation of species in their natural habitats. India has implemented several projects for different species, such as Project Lion (Gir National Park, Gujarat), Project Rhino (Kaziranga National Park, Assam), and Project Elephant (various states). All these are examples of in-situ conservation because they protect animals in their natural environment. Hence, all the given options are in-situ conservation measures, making 'All of the options' the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ What is in-situ conservation? → Conservation of species in their natural habitat.
☛ Where is Project Lion located? → Gir National Park, Gujarat.
☛ In which state is Project Rhino located? → Assam (Kaziranga National Park).
☛ When was Project Elephant launched? → 1992.
☛ Examples of in-situ conservation? → National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves.

q: Tungabhadra multipurpose project has been established on the banks of the tributary of which of the following rivers?
A. Godavari
B. Krishna
C. Mahanadi
D. Indus
qs.e: The Tungabhadra multipurpose project is located on the Tungabhadra River, which is a major tributary of the Krishna River. This project is situated on the border of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and was initiated in 1953. The Tungabhadra River originates in the Western Ghats and joins the Krishna River. The main objectives of this project include irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control. The Krishna River is the second largest river in South India, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river's tributary is the Tungabhadra? → Krishna
☛ Between which states is the Tungabhadra project located? → Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
☛ Where does the Krishna River originate? → Mahabaleshwar, Western Ghats
☛ What are the main purposes of the Tungabhadra project? → Irrigation, hydropower, and flood control
☛ Which is the second largest river in South India? → Krishna

q: A scheme by the Government of India to maintain a viable population of tigers in India since 1973 is:
qs.e: The Government of India launched Project Tiger in 1973 to maintain a viable population of tigers and protect their natural habitats. It was implemented under the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972. Initially covering 9 tiger reserves, it has now expanded to over 50 reserves. The project is managed by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). Project Tiger has significantly increased the tiger population in India and is considered one of the most successful wildlife conservation programs globally.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Project Tiger launched? → 1973
☛ First 9 reserves of Project Tiger? → Corbett, Kanha, Sariska, etc.
☛ Who manages Project Tiger? → NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority)
☛ Oldest tiger reserve in India? → Corbett National Park (1936)
☛ Current number of tiger reserves under Project Tiger? → Over 50

q: What is MPLADS?
o: A scheme launched by the government of India which enables Members of Parliament to do development work in their constituencies
A scheme launched by the Madhya Pradesh government for the protection of ladies
A scheme launched by the Maharashtra and Punjab governments for legal assistance to deprived sections
A scheme launched by the Madhya Pradesh government for the protection of lions and other endangered species
qs.e: MPLADS stands for Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme. It is a central scheme launched by the Government of India in 1993 under the Ministry of Rural Development. The scheme provides an annual allocation of Rs. 5 crore to each MP to recommend development works in their constituency. The objective is to enable MPs to initiate projects based on local needs in areas such as infrastructure, education, healthcare, and community development. This empowers MPs to play a direct role in grassroots development and strengthen democratic processes. Over the years, the scheme has been continued with periodic revisions to improve transparency and implementation. It applies to both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of MPLADS? → Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme
☛ When was MPLADS launched? → 1993
☛ Annual allocation per MP under MPLADS? → Rs. 5 crore
☛ Which ministry administers MPLADS? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ Can Rajya Sabha MPs utilize MPLADS? → Yes, in the state they represent

q: PETA India started in the year ______.
qs.e: PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals) is an international animal rights organization founded in 1980. PETA India was started in the year 2000. Its headquarters is located in Mumbai. PETA India aims to prevent cruelty towards animals and protect their rights. The organization works on issues such as factory farming, fur industry, and animal testing. Since its inception in 2000, PETA India has played a significant role in animal protection in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was PETA founded? → 1980
☛ Where is PETA's headquarters? → Norfolk, Virginia, USA
☛ Where is PETA India's headquarters? → Mumbai
☛ What is the full form of PETA? → People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals
☛ When did PETA India start? → 2000

q: Considering India’s global leadership in environmental protection and climate change sectors, which organisation had chosen India as the global host for World Environment Day (WED) on 5th June 2018?
o: Internation Union for Conservation of Nature
qs.e: World Environment Day (WED) is celebrated annually on 5 June, hosted by a different country chosen by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). For 2018, UNEP selected India as the global host, with the theme 'Beat Plastic Pollution'. This recognition was part of acknowledging India's leadership in environmental protection and initiatives like the Swachh Bharat Mission. UNEP is a UN agency that sets the global environmental agenda and promotes sustainable development. The 2018 event was held in New Delhi, attracting participants from around the world. Other options like the European Environment Agency, Global Green Growth Institute, and International Union for Conservation of Nature are also environmental organizations, but the host selection for WED is solely done by UNEP.
qs.kf:
☛ When is World Environment Day celebrated? → 5 June
☛ What was the theme of WED 2018? → Beat Plastic Pollution
☛ Who selects the host for WED? → UNEP
☛ Where is UNEP headquarters located? → Nairobi, Kenya
☛ Where did India host WED 2018? → New Delhi

q: Under which ministry was the National Mission for Manuscripts established in February 2003?
qs.e: The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) was established in February 2003 under the Ministry of Tourism and Culture. Its objective is to preserve, document, and catalog India's vast manuscript heritage. The mission is implemented by the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA). NMM has documented over 5 million manuscripts across the country. It runs digitization and conservation projects for manuscripts. The mission's headquarters is located in New Delhi.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the National Mission for Manuscripts established? → February 2003
☛ Under which ministry is the National Mission for Manuscripts? → Ministry of Tourism and Culture
☛ Who implements the National Mission for Manuscripts? → Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)
☛ Where is the headquarters of the National Mission for Manuscripts? → New Delhi
☛ What is the objective of the National Mission for Manuscripts? → Preservation and documentation of manuscripts

q: Which of the following State Governments launched the plantation drive through 'Green Mahanadi Mission'?
qs.e: The Green Mahanadi Mission is an ambitious plantation drive launched by the Government of Odisha. Its objective is to increase forest cover in the Mahanadi river basin and restore environmental balance. Under this mission, large-scale afforestation is carried out, especially along the banks of the Mahanadi. This initiative helps combat climate change, conserve biodiversity, and improve the livelihoods of local communities. The Government of Odisha has implemented this mission through its Environment and Forest Department. The mission is a significant step towards rejuvenating the ecosystem of the Mahanadi river.
qs.kf:
☛ Who launched the Green Mahanadi Mission? → Odisha Government
☛ What is the aim of the Green Mahanadi Mission? → Increase forest cover in Mahanadi basin
☛ Which river is associated with the Green Mahanadi Mission? → Mahanadi
☛ What is the main focus of the Green Mahanadi Mission? → Plantation and ecological restoration
☛ What are the benefits of the Green Mahanadi Mission? → Climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation

q: Name the state government that announced its decision to ban production, distribution, advertisement and sale of e-cigarette within its territory in May 2019?
qs.e: In May 2019, the Rajasthan government announced its decision to ban the production, distribution, advertisement and sale of e-cigarettes within its territory. This step was taken considering the adverse health effects of e-cigarettes, which contain nicotine and other harmful chemicals that can lead to lung diseases and addiction. Following Rajasthan, several other states imposed similar bans. Later in 2019, the central government issued an ordinance banning the production, import, export, transport, sale and advertisement of e-cigarettes nationwide, which was enacted as a law by Parliament in 2020.
qs.kf:
☛ First state to ban e-cigarettes → Rajasthan
☛ Central government banned e-cigarettes in → September 2019 (ordinance)
☛ Name of the e-cigarette ban law → Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019
☛ Main addictive substance in e-cigarettes → Nicotine
☛ Disease caused by e-cigarette use → EVALI

q: Which year was the Parliament House Local Area Development Plan (MPLADS) started?
qs.e: The MPLADS scheme was launched by the Government of India on 23 December 1993. Its objective is to enable Members of Parliament to recommend development works in their constituencies. The scheme is available to MPs of both houses of Parliament. Each MP is allocated a sum of 5 crore rupees per year. MPLADS is implemented as a central scheme, with execution carried out by the district administration. This scheme empowers MPs to contribute to local infrastructure and community development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was MPLADS launched? → 1993
☛ What is the full form of MPLADS? → Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme
☛ Annual allocation per MP? → 5 crore rupees
☛ MPLADS comes under which ministry? → Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
☛ Who implements MPLADS? → District administration

q: Under which government initiatives are Indian athletes provided financial assistance, training support, and international exposure to prepare for the Olympics?
qs.e: The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India launched in 2014. It aims to provide targeted support to athletes who have the potential to win medals in Olympic Games. Under TOPS, athletes receive financial assistance, coaching, international exposure, and access to modern training facilities. The scheme is managed by the Ministry of Sports and covers expenses up to a specified limit. Other options: Khelo India Youth Games focuses on grassroots talent, SAI is an administrative body, and Fit India Movement promotes fitness awareness.
qs.kf:
☛ When was TOPS launched? → 2014
☛ What is the full form of TOPS? → Target Olympic Podium Scheme
☛ Who is eligible for TOPS support? → Olympic athletes with medal potential
☛ Under which ministry does TOPS come? → Ministry of Sports
☛ Who implements TOPS? → Sports Authority of India (SAI)

q: Which state launched Deepam-2 scheme to provide free LPG cylinders to eligible beneficiaries?
qs.e: The Andhra Pradesh government launched the Deepam-2 scheme to provide free LPG cylinders to eligible beneficiaries. Under this scheme, the state government provides three free LPG cylinders per year. The scheme was launched under the leadership of Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy. Its objective is to provide cooking gas facilities to poor families and protect their health. Deepam-2 is an important part of Andhra Pradesh's social welfare programs.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state launched the Deepam-2 scheme? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ How many free cylinders are provided under Deepam-2 per year? → Three
☛ What is the objective of Deepam-2 scheme? → To provide free LPG cylinders to poor families
☛ Who launched the Deepam-2 scheme? → Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy
☛ Which state implemented Deepam-1 scheme? → Andhra Pradesh

q: India's first exploration licence auction and AI-Driven Mineral Targeting Hackathon was launched in:
qs.e: The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, launched the country's first exploration licence auction and AI-Driven Mineral Targeting Hackathon in Goa. This initiative aims to increase private sector participation in mineral exploration and accelerate the discovery of mineral resources using advanced technologies like Artificial Intelligence. The auction was conducted for two mineral blocks located in Goa, focusing on identifying critical minerals. This step is a significant move towards making the country self-reliant in the mineral sector and establishing Goa as a hub for mineral exploration.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was India's first exploration licence auction launched? → Goa
☛ Which ministry conducted this auction? → Ministry of Mines
☛ How many blocks were up for auction? → Two
☛ Which technology was the hackathon based on? → Artificial Intelligence (AI)
☛ What is the main objective of this initiative? → Increase private participation and accelerate mineral exploration

q: The Human Genome Project, launched in 1990, had the goal of determining the sequence of how many billion base pairs that make up human DNA?
qs.e: The Human Genome Project (HGP), launched in 1990, was an international research initiative to sequence all approximately 3.0 billion base pairs of human DNA. Completed in 2003, it revolutionized human genetics. DNA consists of four nitrogenous bases: adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine, which pair to form base pairs. The HGP contributed significantly to medicine, biology, and disease research. Countries involved included the United States, United Kingdom, Japan, France, Germany, and China. The project revealed that the human genome contains about 20,000-25,000 genes. The HGP also advanced technologies for DNA sequencing and data analysis.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Human Genome Project launched? → 1990
☛ How many billion base pairs are in human DNA? → 3.0 billion
☛ Approximately how many genes are in the human genome? → 20,000-25,000
☛ How many types of nitrogenous bases are in DNA? → 4 (A, T, G, C)
☛ What is the full form of HGP? → Human Genome Project

q: Which of the following government initiatives was launched in 1973 to conserve a key apex predator and its ecosystem in India?
qs.e: Project Tiger is a major government initiative launched in 1973 to conserve the tiger, a key apex predator, and its ecosystem in India. It was started to address the declining tiger population and to protect their natural habitats. The project is implemented under the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and manages over 50 tiger reserves across the country, including prominent ones like Corbett, Ranthambore, and Kanha. Due to this initiative, India has seen a significant increase in tiger numbers, making it the world's largest tiger habitat. Project Tiger emphasizes both conservation of tigers and the ecological balance of their habitats.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Project Tiger launched? → 1973
☛ Which is the first tiger reserve in India? → Corbett (Uttarakhand)
☛ When was NTCA established? → 2005
☛ State with highest tiger population in India? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Main objective of Project Tiger? → Conservation of tigers and their ecosystem

q: The Planning Commission was the apex body responsible for formulating Five-Year Plans. In which year was the Planning Commission of India established?
qs.e: The Planning Commission of India was established on 15 March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India. It was a non-constitutional body, primarily responsible for formulating and implementing Five-Year Plans for the country's economic development. The first Chairman of the Planning Commission was Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The Commission played a pivotal role in shaping India's development strategy until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015. The correct answer is 1950.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Planning Commission established? → 15 March 1950
☛ Nature of Planning Commission? → Non-constitutional body
☛ First Chairman of Planning Commission? → Jawaharlal Nehru
☛ When was Planning Commission dissolved? → 1 January 2015
☛ Which body replaced Planning Commission? → NITI Aayog

q: When was Project Tiger launched in India?
qs.e: Project Tiger was launched in India on April 1, 1973. Its objective was to conserve the declining population of tigers and protect their natural habitats. The project was initiated by the Government of India and led to the establishment of numerous tiger reserves across the country. Initially, it covered 9 tiger reserves, which have now increased to over 50. Project Tiger is considered a successful global model for tiger conservation. It has played a vital role in increasing India's tiger population, and India now has the largest tiger habitat area in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of Project Tiger → 1973
☛ Number of initial reserves → 9
☛ Main objective of Project Tiger → Tiger conservation and habitat protection
☛ Current number of tiger reserves → More than 50
☛ India's position in tiger conservation → Largest tiger habitat area in the world

q: Which of the following tourist circuit is not included in the Swadesh Darshan scheme launched by ministry of Tourism and Culture, Government of India?
qs.e: The Swadesh Darshan scheme was launched by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India in 2014-15. Under this scheme, 15 theme-based tourist circuits have been developed, which include Sufi Circuit, Eco Circuit, and Coastal Circuit. Mountain Circuit is not part of this scheme. The objective of the scheme is to promote tourism and develop infrastructure in various regions of the country. Other circuits include Buddhist, Heritage, Wildlife, Desert, Tribal, and Ramayana circuits.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Swadesh Darshan scheme launched? → 2014-15
☛ Total number of circuits under Swadesh Darshan? → 15
☛ Which of the following is a circuit under Swadesh Darshan? → Buddhist Circuit
☛ Which ministry implements Swadesh Darshan? → Ministry of Tourism
☛ What is the objective of Swadesh Darshan? → Development of theme-based tourist circuits

q: 'Project Elephant' was launched by the Government of India in the year ________.
qs.e: Project Elephant was launched by the Government of India in 1992. It aims to provide a comprehensive strategy for the conservation and management of elephants. The project is administered by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Its main focus includes protecting elephant habitats, mitigating human-elephant conflict, and monitoring elephant populations. The project covers 14 states in India. Elephants are protected under the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972. The elephant census is conducted every 5 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Project Elephant launched in which year? → 1992
☛ Which ministry oversees Project Elephant? → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Under which Act are elephants protected in India? → Wildlife Protection Act, 1972
☛ How many states does Project Elephant cover? → 14 states
☛ How often is the elephant census conducted? → Every 5 years

q: Project Tiger was first initiated in India in the year-
qs.e: Project Tiger is a major wildlife conservation initiative by the Government of India, launched on April 1, 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand. Its primary objective was to protect the declining population of tigers and conserve their natural habitats. Under this project, tiger reserves were established and special wildlife management efforts were undertaken. Initially, 9 reserves were included, which have now increased to over 50. Project Tiger received support from the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) as well. It is considered one of India's most successful conservation programs and is regarded as a global model for tiger conservation.

☛ First tiger reserve under Project Tiger? → Jim Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand
☛ Founding director of Project Tiger? → Kailash Sankhala
☛ When was tiger declared as National Animal of India? → April 1973
☛ Main objective of Project Tiger? → Conservation of declining tiger population

q: In February 2024, Genome India Project was completed. Which of the following statements is NOT true about Genome India Project?
o: The project was funded and coordinated by the Department of Biotechnology, Govt. of India
1 million genome samples were to be collected across the country from citizens of India.
The aim was to build a reference genome and study genetic diversity among Indians.
qs.e: The Genome India Project was completed in February 2024. The project aimed to collect 10,000 genome samples, not 1 million. It was funded and coordinated by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India, and was initiated in 2020. The main objective was to create a reference genome for the Indian population and study genetic diversity. Under the project, 10,000 samples were collected from across the country. Hence, the statement about 1 million samples is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the target number of genome samples for Genome India Project? → 10,000
☛ In which year was the project initiated? → 2020
☛ In which year was the project completed? → February 2024
☛ Which department coordinated the project? → Department of Biotechnology (DBT)
☛ What was the aim of the project? → To build a reference genome and study genetic diversity

q: MATSYA 6000, a part of India’s Samudrayaan Project, is what kind of object/instrument?
qs.e: MATSYA 6000, a key component of India's Samudrayaan Project, is a manned submersible designed to reach depths of up to 6000 meters in the ocean. It can carry three people and is used for deep-sea studies, mineral exploration, and sample collection. This submersible helps in studying the deep-sea floor and is part of India's Deep Ocean Mission, which promotes environmental and scientific research. It is not just an oil mineral explorer or an autonomous underwater vehicle, but a human-operated vessel that allows scientists to directly observe and analyze the deep ocean environment. MATSYA 6000 represents a significant leap in India's marine technology capabilities.
qs.kf:
☛ Submersible built under Samudrayaan Project → MATSYA 6000
☛ Maximum depth of MATSYA 6000 → 6000 meters
☛ Difference: Manned vs. autonomous submersible → MATSYA 6000 is manned
☛ Goal of Deep Ocean Mission → Exploration of deep-sea mineral and biological resources
☛ Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) → Leads the Samudrayaan Project

q: Which plan sets targets to cover all major aspects of the economy?
qs.e: A comprehensive plan is one that sets targets covering all major aspects of the economy, including production, distribution, consumption, investment, employment, price stability, and foreign trade. It also takes into account social and institutional aspects. In contrast, a partial plan targets only specific sectors, while an imperative plan involves mandatory implementation of government-set goals. A global plan is formulated at the international level. In India, five-year plans are examples of comprehensive planning, focusing on overall development and integrating various sectors for balanced growth.
qs.kf:
☛ Which aspects are included in a comprehensive plan? → Economic, social, and institutional aspects
☛ India's five-year plans are examples of which type of plan? → Comprehensive plan
☛ What is the main feature of a partial plan? → Targets only specific sectors
☛ How are goals implemented in an imperative plan? → Mandatorily
☛ At what level is a global plan formulated? → International level

q: The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) Research Programme for 2025 is divided into how many categories?
qs.e: The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) Research Programme for 2025 is divided into three categories. These categories are: Category I (General/Open), Category II (Young Researcher/Student), and Category III (Disaster Management and Heritage). This programme is designed to promote research in heritage conservation, encourage young researchers, and focus on disaster management challenges in heritage conservation. Selected projects under this programme receive financial assistance.
qs.kf:
☛ When was INTACH established? → 1984
☛ Where is the headquarters of INTACH? → New Delhi
☛ Who are the founders of INTACH? → Pupul Jayakar and Martin Campbell
☛ Total categories in the 2025 INTACH Research Programme? → Three
☛ Full form of INTACH? → Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage

q: ______ an initiative by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, being executed by Lalit Kala Akademi and National Gallery of Modern Art, in July 2024.
qs.e: Project PARI (Public Art of India) is an initiative by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, executed by Lalit Kala Akademi and National Gallery of Modern Art. Launched in July 2024, the project aims to promote public art across the country through murals and sculptures, showcasing India's rich culture and heritage. It encourages dialogue between artists and the public, making art accessible to all. This initiative is a significant step towards integrating art into everyday public spaces.

q: In December 2008, the Government of India launched the INSPIRE Programme. The programme is related to the promotion of:
qs.e: The INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research) programme was launched in December 2008 by the Government of India. Its main objective is to promote science and technology among youth and encourage scientific thinking. The programme operates through components like INSPIRE Awards - MANAK, SEATS, FELLOWSHIP, and SCHOLARSHIP. It motivates school students and young scientists for research and innovation. q: Which scheme was started with the recommendation of the Fourth All India Whip (WHIP) Conference?
qs.e: The Youth Parliament scheme was started on the recommendation of the Fourth All India Whip Conference. This scheme is run by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. Its aim is to familiarise the youth with democratic processes and parliamentary procedures. In Youth Parliament, students simulate the proceedings of the Parliament, which develops their leadership skills, debating ability, and democratic values. The scheme was first launched in 1966.

☛ Which ministry operates the Youth Parliament scheme? → Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
☛ What is the objective of Youth Parliament? → To familiarise youth with democratic processes

q: What year was the Make-in-India policy implemented?
qs.e: The Make-in-India policy was launched by the Government of India on 25 September 2014. Its aim is to transform India into a global manufacturing hub. This initiative was started under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Make-in-India focuses on 25 sectors, including automobiles, electronics, defense equipment, pharmaceuticals, and more. Under this policy, FDI rules were liberalized to attract foreign investment and boost employment generation. The slogan of the Make-in-India campaign is "Zero Defect, Zero Effect".

☛ How many sectors are covered under Make-in-India? → 25

q: Which year was the beginning of the Land Records Modernization Program (NLRMP)?
qs.e: The National Land Records Modernization Programme (NLRMP) was launched by the Government of India in the year 2008. Its objective is to digitize land records and bring transparency in land administration. Later, it was revamped as the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP). The program is implemented in collaboration with state governments and aims at computerization of land records, survey, and online availability of records. NLRMP focuses on updating and maintaining land records to prevent disputes and improve efficiency.

☛ Renamed in 2016 as → DILRMP (Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme)

q: In which of the following months was the Project PARI (Public Art of India) initiated?
qs.e: Project PARI (Public Art of India) was initiated in July 2024. It was launched by the Ministry of Culture of the Government of India to promote public art across the country. The project aims to make Indian art and culture accessible to the masses and provide a platform to young artists. Under this initiative, murals, sculptures, and other art installations will be created in various cities. The launch event took place in New Delhi, and the project is also being promoted through digital media. PARI seeks to transform public spaces into vibrant art galleries and encourage community participation.

q: In 1987, the UNEP succeeded in forging an agreement to freeze Chlorofluorocarbons production at 1986 levels. What is the full form of UNEP?
qs.e: The full form of UNEP is United Nations Environment Programme. It was established in 1972 after the Stockholm Conference. UNEP is a UN agency that coordinates environmental activities and assists countries in implementing environmentally sound policies. In 1987, UNEP played a key role in forging the Montreal Protocol, which aimed to freeze the production of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) at 1986 levels. This agreement was a landmark step in protecting the ozone layer. The headquarters of UNEP is located in Nairobi, Kenya.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UNEP established? → 1972
☛ Where is the headquarters of UNEP? → Nairobi, Kenya
☛ What is the Montreal Protocol related to? → Protection of the ozone layer
☛ When was the Montreal Protocol adopted? → 1987
☛ What is the full form of UNEP? → United Nations Environment Programme

q: In which year did the government of India launch the Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Campaign?
qs.e: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Campaign on May 12, 2020. This campaign was launched to revive the Indian economy and make India self-reliant during the COVID-19 pandemic. A special economic package of ₹20 lakh crore was announced under this initiative. The campaign was based on five pillars: Economy, Infrastructure, System, Demography, and Demand. Its aim was to boost manufacturing, reduce imports, and encourage local industries.

q: The Earth Hour programme began in:
qs.e: Earth Hour began in 2007 in Sydney, Australia. It is organized by the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) to raise awareness about climate change and energy conservation. Participants switch off non-essential lights and electrical appliances for one hour on the last Saturday of March, from 8:30 PM to 9:30 PM local time. The first event in 2007 saw over 2.2 million people and 2,000 businesses participate. Since then, it has grown into a global movement involving millions in over 190 countries.
qs.kf:
☛ Organizer of Earth Hour → World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF)
☛ First Earth Hour location → Sydney, Australia
☛ Earth Hour date → Last Saturday of March
☛ Earth Hour timing → 8:30 PM to 9:30 PM
☛ Participants in 2007 Earth Hour → 2.2 million

q: The construction of the new Parliament building began under which of the following projects?
qs.e: The construction of the new Parliament building began under the Central Vista Project. This project is an ambitious redevelopment plan of the area from Rashtrapati Bhavan to India Gate in New Delhi. It includes the construction of a new Parliament House, Central Secretariat, and Prime Minister's residence. The foundation stone of the new Parliament building was laid on 10 December 2020 by President Ram Nath Kovind. The building will be triangular in shape and will have separate chambers for Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the foundation stone of the new Parliament building laid? → 10 December 2020
☛ What is the shape of the new Parliament building? → Triangular
☛ Which area does the Central Vista Project cover? → From Rashtrapati Bhavan to India Gate
☛ Who designed the Central Vista Project? → Rajiv Saini and Himmat Singh
☛ How many chambers will the new Parliament building have? → Separate chambers for Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

q: Which of the following functions cannot be performed by NBFCs ?
qs.e: NBFC (Non-Banking Financial Company) is registered under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1956 and plays a limited role in banking functions. NBFC can provide loans, make investments, and acquire shares, but it cannot accept demand deposits. Demand deposits are deposits that can be withdrawn immediately without prior notice, such as current accounts or savings accounts. This function is exclusively given to banks. NBFC can only accept time deposits. This distinction is a key difference between NBFCs and banks.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NBFC → Non-Banking Financial Company
☛ Regulator of NBFC → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
☛ What NBFC cannot do → Accept demand deposits
☛ What NBFC can do → Loans, investments, share acquisition
☛ Main difference between NBFC and bank → Ability to accept demand deposits

q: Who works to make 'Made in India' a label of quality?
qs.e: The India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) is a trust under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. It was established in 2003 to promote Indian brands and make 'Made in India' a label of quality. IBEF aims to strengthen the global image of Indian products and services and boost exports. It works across various sectors to highlight the capabilities and quality of Indian industries. The Annamrita Foundation is associated with mid-day meals, while the National Innovation Foundation promotes innovation and entrepreneurship. IBEF specifically focuses on brand equity and quality certification. Its initiatives include creating brand awareness and facilitating trade, thereby positioning India as a quality manufacturing hub.
qs.kf:
☛ When was IBEF established? → 2003
☛ IBEF comes under which ministry? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Main objective of IBEF? → Promote Indian brands and increase exports
☛ 'Made in India' label is associated with? → Quality and brand image
☛ Name of report published by IBEF? → India Brand Equity Foundation Report

q: The Sangameshwara Temple had been submerged in the backwaters of the Srisailam project due to heavy rainfall in the monsoon of 2024. This temple lies on the banks of which river?
qs.e: The Sangameshwara Temple is located on the banks of the Krishna River in Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh. This temple gets submerged in the backwaters of the Srisailam Project, which is built on the Krishna River. The Srisailam dam is one of India's largest hydroelectric projects. In the 2024 monsoon, heavy rainfall led to a rise in the backwater level, submerging this ancient temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple holds historical and religious significance.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is the Srisailam Project located? → Krishna River
☛ In which state is the Sangameshwara Temple located? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What type of dam is Srisailam? → Gravity dam
☛ Where is the origin of the Krishna River? → Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra
☛ What is the installed capacity of the Srisailam Project? → 1,670 MW

o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
qs.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Aushadhi Scheme (PM-JAY) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India to provide affordable and quality generic medicines. Under this scheme, Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra (PMBJK) are opened across the country, offering medicines at 50-90% lower prices compared to branded drugs. The objective is to make healthcare accessible and reduce the financial burden on citizens.

q: During recession, which type of Fiscal Policy should be used?
qs.e: During a recession, the economy experiences a decline in aggregate demand, leading to reduced output and employment. To counter this, the government adopts an expansionary fiscal policy, which involves increasing government spending and/or decreasing taxes to stimulate aggregate demand. Higher government expenditure directly boosts demand, while tax cuts leave more disposable income with consumers and businesses, encouraging consumption and investment. This policy aims to increase economic activity, reduce unemployment, and help the economy recover from the recession. Thus, expansionary fiscal policy is the appropriate response to a recessionary gap.
qs.kf:
☛ Fiscal policy used during recession → Expansionary
☛ Measures of expansionary policy → Increase government spending and decrease taxes
☛ Policy used during inflation → Contractionary fiscal policy
☛ Goal of expansionary policy → Increase aggregate demand
☛ Types of fiscal policy → Expansionary, Contractionary, Neutral

q: India celebrated Engineers Day on 15 Sep 2025 with the theme “Deep Tech & Engineering Excellence” in memory of whom?
qs.e: India celebrates Engineers Day every year on 15th September to commemorate the birth anniversary of the legendary engineer and statesman Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya. Born on 15 September 1861, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna for his contributions. In 2025, the theme was “Deep Tech & Engineering Excellence”. Sir Visvesvaraya played a key role in flood control, irrigation, and industrial development, and also served as the Diwan of Mysore.
qs.kf:
☛ When is Engineers Day celebrated? → 15 September
☛ When was Sir M. Visvesvaraya born? → 15 September 1861
☛ Which award was he given? → Bharat Ratna
☛ What was the 2025 theme? → Deep Tech & Engineering Excellence
☛ Which state's Diwan was he? → Mysore

q: What is the primary purpose of the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025?
o: To monitor national-level progress of the 17 SDGs
To allocate national funds for SDG projects
To compare Indian SDGs with other countries
qs.e: The primary purpose of the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025 is to monitor and evaluate the national-level progress of the 17 SDGs in India. This report is based on the National Indicator Framework (NIF), which includes specific indicators for each goal. It helps measure progress, identify gaps, and provide data for policy improvements. The report covers areas like education, health, poverty, and climate. It was released as part of the Economic Survey 2024-25, aiding in evidence-based policymaking and tracking India's commitment to the 2030 Agenda.

☛ Total number of SDG goals? → 17

☛ Which state leads in SDG progress according to Report 2025? → Kerala

q: Who is the Indian player to score the ﬁrst century in the Indian Premier League (IPL)?
qs.e: The first Indian to score a century in the IPL is Manish Pandey. He achieved this feat on 31 May 2008 while playing for Deccan Chargers against Bangalore, scoring an unbeaten 114 off 73 balls. q: What is the nick name of Harbhajan Singh?
qs.e: Harbhajan Singh is a famous Indian off-spin bowler. His nickname is The Turbanator, which was given due to his habit of wearing a turban and his devastating bowling impact. The nickname was coined by the Australian media during the 2001 series when he performed exceptionally well. Harbhajan is the first Indian bowler to take a hat-trick in Test cricket. He took 417 wickets in 103 Test matches. Another nickname associated with him is 'Bhajji'.

q: The word 'Dead Ball' is related to which of the following games?
qs.e: Dead Ball is an important rule in cricket. When the ball becomes not playable, the umpire declares a dead ball. This situation occurs when the ball goes out of the field after touching a batsman or fielder, or when a batsman is injured. During a dead ball, no runs can be scored, and the ball is not played again. This rule is made for the safety and fairness of the game. The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) defines the dead ball in the laws of cricket. No other game uses this term.
qs.kf:
☛ Which game has the rule of Dead Ball? → Cricket
☛ Who makes the laws of cricket? → MCC
☛ Who declares a dead ball in cricket? → Umpire
☛ What happens after a dead ball in cricket? → No runs scored
☛ Does weightlifting use the term Dead Ball? → No

qs.e: The question asks which game is not related to the action of jumping. Pole Vault involves jumping over a high bar with the help of a pole. Hurdles involves running and jumping over barriers. Swimming involves moving through water using arms and legs; it does not involve jumping. Short Run is a running race that does not require jumping. q: Against which team did Sachin Tendulkar make his 100th international century
qs.e: Sachin Tendulkar made his 100th international century against Bangladesh on 16 March 2012 during the Asia Cup. He is the only cricketer to score 100 international centuries. The century was scored at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium, Mirpur. India won the match by 87 runs. Tendulkar scored 114 runs off 141 balls. In total, he has 51 Test and 49 ODI centuries.

q: Asia Cup belongs to which of the following sports?
qs.e: The Asia Cup is an international cricket tournament played among Asian countries. It is organized by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC). The first Asia Cup was held in 1984 in the United Arab Emirates. The tournament has been played in both ODI and T20 formats. India has won the Asia Cup the most times, with seven titles, while Sri Lanka has won it six times. Pakistan and Bangladesh are also regular participants. The Asia Cup is considered the most prestigious cricket event in Asia after the World Cup.

☛ Who organizes the Asia Cup? → Asian Cricket Council (ACC)

☛ In which formats has the Asia Cup been played? → ODI and T20

q: "Maiden Over" is related to which game?
qs.e: A Maiden Over is a term used in the game of Cricket. It refers to an over (six legal deliveries) in which the bowler concedes no runs. This achievement highlights the bowler's skill and control. Other common cricket terms include stump out, bowled, run out, and LBW. The term is not used in Polo, Wrestling, or Football.
qs.kf:
☛ How many balls are in a maiden over? → Six
☛ Who bowled the most maiden overs in Test cricket? → Muttiah Muralitharan

q: Indian Cricket team played their ﬁrst ever ODI against which one of the following teams?
qs.e: Indian cricket team played its first ever One Day International (ODI) match against England in 1974. The match was played at Headingley in Leeds, and India won that match, registering their first ODI victory. At that time, the ODI format was in its early stages; the first official ODI was played in 1971. India did not play any ODI in 1971; their first ODI was in 1974 against England. This historic match marked India's entry into the ODI format and was a significant milestone for Indian cricket. Later, India won its first World Cup in 1983.
qs.kf:

☛ When was India's first ODI match played? → 1974
☛ Where was India's first ODI match played? → Leeds, Headingley

☛ When was the first official ODI match played? → 1971

q: Who became the ﬁrst Indian woman cricket player to score a century in International T20 cricket matches?
qs.e: Harmanpreet Kaur became the first Indian woman cricketer to score a century in International T20 matches. She achieved this feat by scoring 103 runs against New Zealand in 2018. Before this, no Indian woman had scored a century in T20 internationals. Harmanpreet Kaur is known for her aggressive batting and leadership skills. She has been the vice-captain of the Indian women's cricket team and has played several historic innings. This century established her as a key player in women's T20 cricket. She also scored a century in the Women's T20 World Cup against the West Indies in 2016, which was another landmark achievement.

q: With which sport is the term 'silly point' associated?
qs.e: The term 'silly point' is associated with Cricket. It is a fielding position located very close to the batsman, on the off side near the wicket. The fielder stands dangerously close to the batsman, risking injury from hard shots. The name 'silly' reflects the foolhardiness of standing so near without protection. Other fielding positions in cricket include slip, gully, point, cover, mid-wicket, long-on, long-off, etc. This position is used to catch edges or deflections off the bat. Understanding these positions is fundamental to cricket.

q: The International Cricket Council (ICC), the international governing body of Cricket founded in 1909 by representatives from England, Australia and South Africa, was initially known as:

qs.e: The International Cricket Council (ICC) was founded in 1909 by representatives from England, Australia, and South Africa. Initially, it was known as the Imperial Cricket Conference. q: The word "leg before wicket" is related to ______.
qs.e: The term "leg before wicket" is a rule in the sport of cricket. It is a method of dismissal where the batsman is given out if the ball hits his leg and the umpire believes it would have hit the wicket. This rule is defined under Law 36 of cricket. LBW decisions are often controversial and can be reviewed using the Decision Review System (DRS). The rule was first introduced in 1774 to prevent batsmen from using their legs to block the ball from hitting the stumps. It is a fundamental aspect of cricket and applies in all formats: Test, ODI, and T20.

The tournament is organized by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and features teams representing different states and regions of India. The Ranji Trophy underwent a format change in 2002-03, dividing teams into Elite and Plate groups. It is one of the most prestigious domestic cricket competitions in the world.

☛ When was the Ranji Trophy started? → 1934
☛ After whom is the Ranji Trophy named? → Ranjitsinhji

☛ What type of tournament is the Ranji Trophy? → First-class cricket

q: Which game is related to the word "bye, leg bye, no ball"?
qs.e: In cricket, the terms 'bye', 'leg bye', and 'no ball' are related to bowling and scoring. A 'bye' is awarded when the ball passes the batsman without contact and crosses the boundary or the batsmen run without the ball touching the bat or body. A 'leg bye' occurs when the ball hits the batsman's body (excluding the bat) and runs are taken, provided the batsman attempted to play a shot. A 'no ball' is an illegal delivery, such as overstepping the popping crease or a full toss above waist height, resulting in an extra run for the batting side. These terms are fundamental to cricket's rules.
qs.kf:
☛ Who has the most international centuries in cricket? → Sachin Tendulkar
☛ Which country is considered the birthplace of cricket? → England
☛ Who has the most wickets in Test cricket? → Muttiah Muralitharan
☛ Who has the most runs in ODI cricket? → Sachin Tendulkar
☛ Who scored the fastest century in T20 cricket? → Yuvraj Singh

q: In India, cricket was brought by whom?
qs.e: Cricket was introduced to India by the British East India Company. In the late 18th century, British sailors and merchants brought the game to India. The first recorded match took place in 1721 in Cambay, Gujarat, involving British sailors. In 1848, the Parsi community formed the Oriental Cricket Club, India's first cricket club. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) was founded in 1928, and India played its first Test match in 1932. Thus, cricket is a British legacy that became immensely popular in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who formed the first cricket club in India? → Parsi community (1848)
☛ When did India play its first Test match? → 1932
☛ Where was the first cricket match in India played? → Cambay, Gujarat (1721)
☛ When was BCCI founded? → 1928
☛ Who brought cricket to India? → British East India Company

q: What is the distance between the two middle stumps on the cricket pitch?
qs.e: The distance between the two middle stumps on a cricket pitch is 22 yards (20.12 meters). This is the standard length prescribed by cricket laws. The pitch length is measured from one middle stump to the other middle stump at the opposite end. This distance is also referred to as the distance between the creases. It determines the distance between the bowler and the batsman. In cricket, the pitch length is always maintained at 22 yards, irrespective of the match format. This measurement is crucial for the game as it affects the speed and bounce of the ball.
qs.kf:
☛ Distance between two middle stumps on cricket pitch → 22 yards
☛ 22 yards in meters → 20.12 meters
☛ Width of a cricket pitch → 10 feet (3.05 meters)
☛ Distance of popping crease from the stumps → 1.22 meters
☛ Length of bowling crease → 2.64 meters

q: What is the full form of LBW in context of Cricket?
qs.e: LBW stands for 'Leg before wicket'. In cricket, this is a rule by which a batsman is given out when the ball hits his leg or any part of his body and the umpire believes that the ball would have hit the wicket without any obstruction. This rule applies when the ball has not touched the bat or the hand and the batsman is on the pitch. The main purpose of the LBW rule is to prevent batsmen from using their legs to block the ball.
qs.kf:
☛ In which sport is the LBW rule used? → Cricket
☛ When was the LBW rule first introduced in Test cricket? → 1774
☛ What does 'B' in LBW represent? → Before
☛ After the ball pitches, what is checked for an LBW decision? → Whether the ball is moving towards the wicket
☛ In which format is DRS used for LBW? → International cricket

q: Which of the following created the famous game Snake Staircase?
qs.e: The famous game Snake Staircase was created in the 13th century by the Maharashtrian saint and poet Gyanadev. Originally known as 'Mokshapatam', the game was designed to impart moral and religious teachings. The ladders represented virtues, while the snakes symbolized vices. Later, during the British era, it gained popularity as 'Snakes and Ladders'. Gyanadev developed it as a tool for ethical education. Among the other options, Aryabhatta was a mathematician, Varahmihir an astronomer, and Brahmagupta a mathematician; none are associated with this game.

☛ Who created the game Snakes and Ladders? → Gyanadev
☛ What was the original name of Snakes and Ladders? → Mokshapatam
☛ In which century was this game created? → 13th century
☛ What do the ladders symbolize? → Virtues
☛ What do the snakes symbolize? → Vices

q: With which sport is the term 'Beamer' associated?
qs.e: The term 'Beamer' is associated with Cricket. It refers to a type of delivery that reaches the batsman directly at head height without bouncing. Repeated beamers can lead to the bowler being banned from bowling. The term is exclusive to cricket terminology and is not used in other sports.

q: With which of the following sports is the term 'pitcher' associated?
qs.e: The term 'pitcher' is associated with the sport of Baseball. In baseball, the pitcher is the player who throws the ball towards the batter, aiming to deliver the ball into the strike zone. The pitcher's primary role is to prevent the batter from hitting the ball effectively. This sport is especially popular in the United States and Japan. In contrast, cricket uses the term 'bowler', volleyball uses 'server', and football uses 'goalkeeper' or 'striker'.

qs.e: Mithali Raj is a legendary figure in Indian women's cricket. She became the first woman cricketer to play 200 ODIs, achieving this milestone in 2019 against South Africa. Her career spanned from 2004 to 2022, during which she set numerous records, including the longest tenure as ODI captain and most half-centuries. q: In cricket, who decides a dismissal on the basis of the replay?
qs.e: In cricket, when the on-field umpire is uncertain about a dismissal decision, he refers to the third umpire. The third umpire sits off the field and uses television replays to review footage from multiple angles. After analyzing the replays, he communicates the final decision to the on-field umpire. This system ensures accuracy in cases like run outs and stumpings, as well as catches and LBW decisions. The third umpire's role is crucial in maintaining fairness in modern cricket, particularly with the introduction of the Decision Review System (DRS).
qs.kf:

q: Which of the following is not related to the closing ceremony of the race?
qs.e: In the closing ceremony of a race, athletes perform specific actions after crossing the finish line. Shoulder Shrug is raising the shoulders, often seen during the finish. Dip is leaning the torso forward to cross the finish line. Run Through is continuing to run without stopping after the line. All three are related to the closing ceremony. Approach Run is the preparatory phase before the start of the race, such as gaining speed, and is not a post-finish action. Hence, it is not related to the closing ceremony.

qs.e: The first ICC World Twenty20 was held in 2007 in South Africa. The final match was played between India and Pakistan. India won the match by 5 runs to become the first T20 World Cup champion. qs.e: The World Series Cup was a competition in ODI cricket originally organized by Australian media mogul Kerry Packer in 1977. It was part of his breakaway World Series Cricket (WSC), featuring many top international players. This tournament was not organized by official cricket bodies like the Australian Cricket Board or the International Cricket Conference. Packer's WSC introduced innovations such as colored clothing, floodlights, and white balls, which later became standard in ODI cricket. The World Series Cup was a key event in the WSC, which lasted from 1977 to 1979 before being resolved with the establishment of World Series Cricket Limited.

qs.e: In cricket, 'silly point', 'slip', and 'gully' are fielding positions near the batsman. Silly point is very close to the batsman on the off side, slip is beside the wicketkeeper, and gully is behind square on the off side. These positions are used to catch edges or deflections.

q: In cricket, which of the following terms is used when a bowler dismisses three batsmen with consecutive deliveries?
qs.e: In cricket, when a bowler dismisses three batsmen with three consecutive deliveries, it is called a Hat-trick. The term originated in cricket and was later adopted by other sports. It was first used in 1858 for H.H. Stephenson. A hat-trick is considered a significant achievement for a bowler and is recorded in both Test and ODI formats. q: Which of the following term is used in cricket when a batsman is dismissed without scoring any runs in a cricket match?
qs.e: In cricket, when a batsman is dismissed without scoring any runs, it is called a duck. The term derives from the shape of a duck's egg, which resembles zero. 'Century' refers to scoring 100 runs, 'boundary' is a hit for four or six runs, and 'over' is a set of six balls. A 'golden duck' occurs when a batsman is dismissed on the very first ball. This term is used in cricket statistics to denote a batsman's score of zero.

qs.e: The maximum duration of modern Olympic Games is 16 days. This rule is set by the International Olympic Committee (IOC). q: The five rings connected to the Olympic flag represent the __________ of the world.
qs.e: The Olympic flag features five interlocking rings in five colors: blue, yellow, black, green, and red on a white background. These rings represent the five continents of the world: Africa, America, Asia, Australia, and Europe. The design was created by Pierre de Coubertin in 1913 and adopted in 1914. The white background symbolizes peace. The interlocking of the rings represents the unity and friendship among all continents through the Olympic Games. Each ring's color does not correspond to a specific continent; instead, all six colors (including the white background) can be found in the flags of all participating nations. The Olympic motto "Citius, Altius, Fortius" (Faster, Higher, Stronger) also promotes this spirit of unity.

☛ When was the Olympic flag adopted? → 1914.
☛ Who designed the Olympic flag? → Pierre de Coubertin.
☛ What does the white background represent? → Peace.

Besides basketball, dribbling is also used in football and hockey, but in basketball it is an integral part of offense. Players practice dribbling to improve their speed, agility, and ball control. q: How many players are there in a soccer team?
qs.e: In football (soccer), each team consists of 11 players: 1 goalkeeper and 10 outfield players. This rule is set by the International Football Association Board (IFAB). The number ensures strategic balance and game dynamics on the field. If a team has fewer than 7 players, the match is abandoned. Substitutions are allowed up to 3 (or 5 in some competitions), but only 11 players can be on the field at a time. This rule is a result of the evolution of modern football, emphasizing fairness and competitiveness. The 11-player setup has been standard since the late 19th century and is universally followed in professional and amateur matches.
qs.kf:

☛ Number of goalkeepers → 1
☛ Number of outfield players → 10
☛ Condition for match abandonment → Less than 7 players
☛ Maximum substitutions (normal) → 3

q: The duration of the football match in which the extra time is not counted, how much is it?
qs.e: A standard football match consists of two halves of 45 minutes each, totaling 90 minutes of regular play. This duration excludes extra time, which is added only in knockout matches if the score is tied. Extra time consists of 30 minutes divided into two 15-minute halves. During regular time, the referee may add stoppage time for injuries or delays, but this does not change the core duration. Therefore, without counting extra time, the duration of a football match is 90 minutes.
qs.kf:

☛ How many halves are in extra time? → Two halves of 15 minutes each

qs.e: Jump ball is a method used to begin or resume play in basketball. It involves the referee tossing the ball into the air between two opposing players, who then try to tap it to their teammates.
