name: All Questions · Q1–35
sub: Books & Authors - Ancient & Medieval Texts, Epics and Authors

q: The Panchatantra fables are thought to be composed by
A. Mullah Nasruddin B. Vishnu Sharma C. King Sudharshan D. Tenali Raman
qs.e: The Panchatantra is a renowned ancient Indian collection of interrelated animal fables in Sanskrit verse and prose. It is traditionally attributed to Vishnu Sharma, a scholar and author who is believed to have composed it around the 3rd century BCE. The fables were written to instruct the princes in statecraft, ethics, and practical wisdom through engaging stories with moral lessons. The text uses animals as characters to convey complex human behaviors and values. In contrast, Mullah Nasruddin is a humorous figure in Middle Eastern folklore, Tenali Raman was a court jester in the Vijayanagara Empire, and King Sudharshan is not a known figure associated with the Panchatantra. Hence, the correct answer is Vishnu Sharma.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed the Panchatantra? → Vishnu Sharma
☛ Which literature does Panchatantra belong to? → Sanskrit literature
☛ What is the purpose of Panchatantra stories? → To teach princes statecraft and ethics
☛ What characters are used in Panchatantra? → Animals and birds
☛ Which court was Tenali Raman associated with? → Vijayanagara Empire

q: Who wrote the famous Sanskrit play Svapnavasavadattam?
qs.e: The famous Sanskrit play Svapnavasavadattam was written by Bhasa. This play is based on the love story of King Udayana and Vasavadatta. Bhasa is regarded as one of the greatest playwrights in Sanskrit literature, with a collection of 13 plays known as the 'Bhasanatakachakra'. The play beautifully blends love, pathos, politics, and diplomacy. The dream scene of Vasavadatta is depicted with great emotional depth. Among the other options, Shudraka wrote 'Mrichchhakatikam', Jayadev wrote 'Gita Govinda', and Kalidas wrote 'Abhigyan Shakuntalam'.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous play of Bhasa? → Svapnavasavadattam
☛ Total plays of Bhasa? → 13 (Bhasanatakachakra)
☛ Other plays of Bhasa? → Pancharatra, Madhyamavyayoga, Urubhanga, etc.
☛ Author of Gita Govinda? → Jayadev
☛ Author of Mrichchhakatikam? → Shudraka

q: Who wrote the medieval-era epic poem “Padmavat"?
qs.e: The medieval epic poem "Padmavat" was written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. It is a significant work of Hindu literature from the Bhakti period, composed in the Awadhi language. The poem narrates the story of King Ratansen and Queen Padmavati. Jayasi wrote this epic around 1540 CE. It is not based on the Persian tale of 'Padmini Charitra' but is influenced by oral traditions. Jayasi was a Sufi poet, and his works blend love and spirituality.
qs.kf:
☛ Who composed "Padmavat"? → Malik Muhammad Jayasi
☛ In which language is "Padmavat" written? → Awadhi
☛ Which literary period does "Padmavat" belong to? → Bhakti period
☛ Malik Muhammad Jayasi belonged to which sect? → Sufi
☛ "Padmavat" narrates the story of which king and queen? → Ratansen and Padmavati

q: Who wrote the play 'Mudrarakshasa'?
qs.e: The play 'Mudrarakshasa' is a famous Sanskrit drama written by Vishakhadatta. It was composed around the 6th century AD and depicts the ascent of Chandragupta Maurya to the throne and the diplomacy of his minister Chanakya (Kautilya). The main characters include Chanakya, Chandragupta, and Rakshasa (the former minister of the Nanda dynasty). The play highlights political strategy, diplomacy, and intelligence. Other options: Somadeva is known for 'Kathasaritsagara', Bodhayan for Shulba Sutras, and Kalidas for 'Abhijnanasakuntalam' among others.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for Chanakya → Kautilya or Vishnugupta
☛ Guru of Chandragupta Maurya → Chanakya
☛ Main theme of Mudrarakshasa → Politics and diplomacy
☛ Another famous play by Vishakhadatta → Devichandraguptam
☛ Main characters in Mudrarakshasa → Chanakya, Chandragupta, Rakshasa

q: Which one of the following books was written by Vishnu Sharma?
qs.e: Vishnu Sharma authored the Panchatantra, a collection of ancient Indian fables that impart moral and political lessons through animal characters. The other options: Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana, Arthashastra by Chanakya, and Indica by Megasthenes. The Panchatantra has been translated into many languages and has influenced global literature. It remains a classic text on statecraft and human behavior.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of Panchatantra → Vishnu Sharma
☛ Author of Rajatarangini → Kalhana
☛ Author of Arthashastra → Chanakya
☛ Author of Indica → Megasthenes
☛ Panchatantra's purpose → To teach moral and political wisdom

q: Who composed 'The Dashakumaracharita' or 'Tales of Ten Princes'?
qs.e: The 'Dashakumaracharita' or 'Tales of Ten Princes' was composed by Dandin in the Sanskrit language. It is a prose narrative (gadya kavya) that recounts the adventurous stories of ten princes. Dandin was a prominent Sanskrit author who also wrote 'Kavyadarsha', a foundational work on poetics. The tales in this work are filled with elements of adventure, romance, and intrigue, showcasing the princes' bravery and wit. Dandin's style is noted for its elaborate descriptions and complex sentences. The Dashakumaracharita is considered an important example of Sanskrit prose literature and provides insights into ancient Indian society and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Composer of Dashakumaracharita → Dandin
☛ Language → Sanskrit
☛ Genre → Prose narrative (Gadya Kavya)
☛ Another major work by Dandin → Kavyadarsha
☛ Meaning of Dashakumaracharita → Tale of Ten Princes

q: Which of the following wrote the ancient scientific book on surgery?
qs.e: In ancient India, Sushruta is considered the father of surgery. He wrote the "Sushruta Samhita", the oldest scientific book on surgery. It describes over 300 surgical procedures, more than 125 surgical instruments, plastic surgery, and cataract surgery. Sushruta was a disciple of sage Vishwamitra and taught medicine at Kashi University. Bhaskar II was a mathematician, Pingal a prosodist, and Varahamihir an astronomer.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of surgery? → Sushruta
☛ How many surgical procedures are described in Sushruta Samhita? → Over 300
☛ Which is the famous ancient Indian medical treatise? → Sushruta Samhita
☛ When was Sushruta Samhita written? → Around 600-800 BCE
☛ What are the three main texts of Ayurveda? → Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya

q: Who is the author of 'Natyashastra'?
qs.e: Natyashastra is the most ancient treatise on Indian performing arts, including theatre, dance, and music. Its author is Bharat Muni. This text systematically covers all aspects of drama, such as rasa (emotion), bhava (expression), mudra (gestures), and stagecraft. It is believed that Bharat Muni composed this work at the request of the gods. The Natyashastra is divided into 36 chapters and is written in Sanskrit. It is considered the foundation of Indian classical dance and music. Bharat Muni is revered as the 'father of Natyashastra'. This scripture not only guides theatrical performances but also provides deep insights into human emotions and aesthetics.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the author of Natyashastra? → Bharat Muni
☛ How many chapters are in Natyashastra? → 36
☛ What is the language of Natyashastra? → Sanskrit
☛ Bharat Muni is known as the father of which scripture? → Natyashastra
☛ How many rasas are described in Natyashastra? → 8 (though later 9 are recognized)

q: Who is the author of 'Ramcharitmanas'?
qs.e: The author of 'Ramcharitmanas' is Goswami Tulsidas. This epic was written in Awadhi language and is considered the greatest rendition of the story of Lord Rama. Tulsidas was born in 1532 CE in Rajapur village, Uttar Pradesh. He also wrote other works like 'Vinay Patrika', 'Gitavali', and 'Dohavali'. 'Ramcharitmanas' is often referred to as an encyclopedia of Indian culture. Tulsidas is revered as a saint-poet and a devotee-poet.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language is Ramcharitmanas written? → Awadhi
☛ What is the birthplace of Tulsidas? → Rajapur (Uttar Pradesh)
☛ Who was the guru of Tulsidas? → Narharidas
☛ How many cantos are there in Ramcharitmanas? → 7 cantos
☛ Another famous work of Tulsidas? → Vinay Patrika

q: 'Yoga Sutra' was written by whom?
qs.e: The Yoga Sutra was written by Patanjali. This text is the foundational scripture of Yoga philosophy, compiling the principles and practices of yoga into concise aphorisms. Patanjali is regarded as the father of Yoga Darshana. The text describes Ashtanga Yoga (eight-limbed yoga), which includes Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana, and Samadhi. It was composed around 200-400 BCE. Patanjali is also credited with writing the Mahabhashya (commentary on Panini's grammar), though some scholars consider them different individuals. Nagasena, Kanada, and Vasumitra are other philosophers known for different works. Kanada founded the Vaisheshika school, while Nagasena is known for the Milinda Panha.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote the Yoga Sutra? → Patanjali
☛ How many sutras are in the Yoga Sutra? → 196 sutras
☛ Which text describes Ashtanga Yoga? → Yoga Sutra
☛ In which language did Patanjali write the Yoga Sutra? → Sanskrit
☛ What is another famous work attributed to Patanjali? → Mahabhashya

q: Name the famous literary personality who has authored the book named 'Rajatarangini'.
qs.e: Rajatarangini is a historical chronicle written by Kalhana in the 12th century. It is written in Sanskrit verse and describes the history of the kings of Kashmir. Kalhana completed this work in 1148-1149 CE. The book is divided into eight tarangas (chapters). It is considered one of the most important sources of ancient Indian historiography. Jaimini authored Mimamsa Sutra, Vishakhadatta authored Mudrarakshasa, and Kautilya authored Arthashastra.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Rajatarangini? → Kalhana
☛ In which language is Rajatarangini written? → Sanskrit
☛ How many chapters (tarangas) are in Rajatarangini? → Eight
☛ When was Rajatarangini composed? → 12th century (1148-49 CE)
☛ Which region's history does Rajatarangini cover? → Kashmir

q: Which classical Sanskrit play was written by Kalidasa?
qs.e: Abhijnana-Shakuntalam is a classical Sanskrit play written by the renowned poet Kalidasa. It tells the love story of King Dushyanta and the nymph Shakuntala. Kalidasa is often called the Shakespeare of India, and this play is considered his masterpiece. The other options: Mudrarakshasa was written by Vishakhadatta, Svapnavasavadattam by Bhasa, and Mrichchhakatika by Shudraka. Kalidasa's major works include Abhijnana-Shakuntalam, Kumarasambhava, Raghuvamsha, Meghaduta, and Malavikagnimitra.
qs.kf:
☛ What is Kalidasa's most famous play? → Abhijnana-Shakuntalam
☛ Who wrote Mudrarakshasa? → Vishakhadatta
☛ Who wrote Svapnavasavadattam? → Bhasa
☛ Who wrote Mrichchhakatika? → Shudraka
☛ What is Kalidasa known as? → Shakespeare of India

q: Who wrote Gita Govinda?
qs.e: The Gita Govinda was composed by the Sanskrit poet Jayadeva in the 12th century. This lyrical poem depicts the love between Radha and Krishna. It consists of 12 cantos and is famous for its Ashtapadis (eight-line stanzas). Jayadeva hailed from Odisha and was a devotee of Lord Vishnu. The work is considered a masterpiece of Vaishnava literature and has been widely translated.
qs.kf:
☛ Language of Gita Govinda → Sanskrit
☛ Total cantos in Gita Govinda → 12
☛ Alternative name of Gita Govinda → Ashtapadi
☛ Theme of Gita Govinda → Love of Radha and Krishna
☛ Jayadeva's birthplace → Odisha

q: Who wrote the great Indian literary works 'Meghdoot' and 'Abhijanam Shakuntalam'?
qs.e: 'Meghdoot' and 'Abhijanam Shakuntalam' are works of the great Sanskrit poet Kalidas. He is often regarded as the Shakespeare of Indian literature. 'Abhijanam Shakuntalam' is a play based on the love story of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala. 'Meghdoot' is a lyrical poem in which a Yaksha sends a message to his wife through a cloud. Other notable works by Kalidas include 'Kumarasambhava', 'Raghuvansha', 'Malavikagnimitram', and 'Vikramorvashiyam'. He flourished during the Gupta period and is known for his beautiful depiction of nature and human emotions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the famous drama of Kalidas? → Abhijanam Shakuntalam
☛ What is the messenger used in 'Meghdoot'? → A cloud
☛ By what other name is Kalidas known? → Kavi Kulguru
☛ Who are the main characters in Abhijanam Shakuntalam? → Shakuntala and King Dushyanta
☛ Which is the longest epic by Kalidas? → Raghuvansham

q: Who wrote the 'Brihat Samhita', a collection of scientific information on diverse subjects?
qs.e: 'Brihat Samhita' is a seminal work by the ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer Varahamihira. This text covers a wide range of subjects including astrology, astronomy, meteorology, architecture, and geology. Varahamihira was born in 505 CE in Ujjain and was a prominent scholar during the Gupta period. He also authored 'Panchasiddhantika', which explains five astronomical systems. His contributions are highly regarded in the history of Indian science. The Brihat Samhita is considered an encyclopedic work that provides scientific knowledge on diverse subjects.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Brihat Samhita? → Varahamihira
☛ Varahamihira belonged to which period? → Gupta period
☛ Varahamihira's birthplace? → Ujjain
☛ Another work by Varahamihira? → Panchasiddhantika
☛ Subjects covered in Brihat Samhita? → Astrology, astronomy, meteorology, architecture, geology

q: Who is the author of the Panchatantra collection of fables?
qs.e: The Panchatantra is an ancient Indian collection of interrelated animal fables in Sanskrit verse and prose. It was composed by Vishnu Sharma, a scholar and teacher. According to tradition, he wrote these stories to teach moral values and political wisdom to the three dull-witted sons of King Amarashakti. The work is considered a 'nitishastra' or book of wise conduct. Each story imparts practical life lessons through the actions of animals. The Panchatantra has been translated into many languages worldwide and is one of the most translated literary works.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language was the Panchatantra originally written? → Sanskrit
☛ What is the main theme of the Panchatantra? → Ethics and politics (Niti)
☛ Who made the most famous translation of the Panchatantra into Arabic? → Abdullah Ibn al-Muqaffa
☛ How many tantras (sections) are there in the Panchatantra? → 5
☛ In what form are the Panchatantra stories presented? → Animal dialogues

q: 'Ratnavali' was written by:
qs.e: 'Ratnavali' is a Sanskrit play written by Harshavardhana (Emperor Harsha). Harshavardhana was a famous ruler of the 7th century who made Kannauj his capital. He was not only a skilled politician but also a great literary figure. Apart from 'Ratnavali', he also wrote plays like 'Nagananda' and 'Priyadarshika'. This play is a love story depicting the union of King Udayana and Ratnavali. Kalidas, Premchand, and Surdas are not the authors of this play.
qs.kf:
☛ Plays written by Harshavardhana → Ratnavali, Nagananda, Priyadarshika
☛ Harshavardhana's dynasty → Pushyabhuti dynasty
☛ Harshavardhana's capital → Kannauj
☛ Chinese traveler contemporary to Harsha → Hiuen Tsang
☛ Harshavardhana's reign period → 606 CE to 647 CE

q: Who was the author of Padmaavat?
qs.e: Padmaavat is an epic poem written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi around 1540 AD. It is composed in the Awadhi language. The story revolves around the Rajput queen Padmavati and Sultan Alauddin Khalji. This work is a significant piece of Sufi love poetry in Hindi literature.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote Padmaavat? → Malik Muhammad Jayasi
☛ In which language was Padmaavat written? → Awadhi
☛ What genre is Padmaavat? → Sufi love poetry
☛ Which Sultan is related to Padmaavat? → Alauddin Khalji
☛ Malik Muhammad Jayasi belongs to which period? → Bhakti period

q: Who wrote the epic 'Buddhacharitam'?
qs.e: The epic Buddhacharitam was written by Ashvaghosha, a renowned Buddhist scholar, poet, and philosopher. It is a Sanskrit epic that narrates the life story of Gautama Buddha, from his birth to his Mahaparinirvana, comprising 28 chapters. Ashvaghosha was a contemporary of the Kushana king Kanishka and is also known for other works like 'Saundarananda' and 'Shariputraprakarana'. The Buddhacharitam is considered one of the earliest biographies of Buddha and is highly regarded in Buddhist literature.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of Buddhacharitam → Ashvaghosha
☛ Court of Ashvaghosha → Kanishka
☛ Language of Buddhacharitam → Sanskrit
☛ Other work of Ashvaghosha → Saundarananda
☛ Number of chapters in Buddhacharitam → 28

q: Who is the author of Ashtadhyayi, an ancient Sanskrit book?
qs.e: Ashtadhyayi is an ancient Sanskrit grammar text authored by Panini. Panini is regarded as the father of Sanskrit grammar. This work was composed around 500 BCE and systematically presents the rules of phonetics, morphology, syntax, and semantics of the Sanskrit language. Ashtadhyayi consists of 8 chapters and 4,000 sutras. Panini's contribution to ancient Indian grammatical tradition is unparalleled, and his work is considered a foundation for modern linguistics. Among the other options, Ashtavakra was a sage, Patanjali authored the Yoga Sutras and Mahabhashya, and Charaka wrote the Charaka Samhita (Ayurveda).
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the author of Ashtadhyayi? → Panini
☛ Who is known as the father of Sanskrit grammar? → Panini
☛ How many sutras are in Ashtadhyayi? → 4,000
☛ Which text did Patanjali write? → Yoga Sutras and Mahabhashya
☛ Charaka Samhita is related to which field? → Ayurveda

q: Match the following correctly. List – I List - II a. Panini
1. Maalvikagnimitram b. Hala
2. Mahabhashya c. Kalidas
3. Ashtadyayi d. Patanjali
4. Gaathasaptshati
qs.e: Panini authored Ashtadyayi, a foundational Sanskrit grammar text. Hala, a Satavahana king, compiled Gaathasaptshati in Prakrit. Kalidasa wrote the play Maalvikagnimitram. Patanjali composed Mahabhashya, a commentary on Panini's Ashtadyayi. Hence, the correct matching is a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2.
qs.kf:
☛ Panini's work → Ashtadyayi
☛ Hala's work → Gaathasaptshati
☛ Kalidasa's play → Maalvikagnimitram
☛ Patanjali's work → Mahabhashya
☛ Mahabhashya comments on → Ashtadyayi

q: Who among the following composed the treatise, 'Mahabhashya'?
qs.e: The treatise Mahabhashya was composed by Patanjali. It is a renowned commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi, which is a foundational text of Sanskrit grammar. In Mahabhashya, Patanjali explains and elaborates on Panini's sutras, often incorporating the Varttikas of Katyayana. This work is considered one of the most important texts in the field of Sanskrit grammar. Patanjali is also believed to be the author of the Yoga Sutras, though it is a different work. Mahabhashya clarifies grammatical rules with numerous examples and is essential for the study of Sanskrit.
qs.kf:

q: Who has written the book "Annequiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations"?

In this book, he introduced concepts such as the invisible hand, division of labor, and the free market. This work laid the foundation of classical economics. Smith argued that individual self-interest leads to social welfare. He opposed government intervention and advocated for free trade. His ideas significantly influenced economic thought and policy.

In "Mahabhasya", Patanjali explains and elaborates on the rules of Panini, providing deep insights into the structure and usage of the Sanskrit language. Patanjali is also known for authoring the Yoga Sutras, making him a key figure in both grammar and yoga philosophy. This work is considered the most ancient and authoritative grammar of Sanskrit, influencing both Vedic and classical Sanskrit. Panini's systematic approach and use of meta-rules make Ashtadhyay a masterpiece of linguistic analysis. It remains a core text for the study of Sanskrit grammar.

'Kavyadarsha' is considered one of the three foundational texts on Sanskrit poetics, alongside Bhamaha's 'Kavyalankara' and Vamana's 'Kavyalankarasutra'. ☛ Language of Rajashekharacharitra → Telugu
☛ Empire associated with Mallana → Vijayanagara
☛ Theme of Rajashekharacharitra → Wars and loves of Rajashekhara

q: Which of the following pairs of author and their work is correctly matched?
qs.e: Among the given options, only the pair of Sharat Chandra Chatterjee and his work Devdas is correctly matched. 'Devdas' is a famous Bengali novel by Sharat Chandra Chatterjee, depicting a story of love and separation. Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote 'Anandamath', while 'Kamayani' is by Jaishankar Prasad. Munshi Premchand authored novels like 'Godan' and 'Gaban', whereas 'Madhushala' is by Harivansh Rai Bachchan. Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Gitanjali' and 'Gora', not 'Anandamath'. Thus, the only correctly matched pair is Sharat Chandra Chatterjee – Devdas.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous work of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee → Anandamath
☛ Author of 'Kamayani' → Jaishankar Prasad
☛ Major work of Munshi Premchand → Godan
☛ Writer of 'Madhushala' → Harivansh Rai Bachchan
☛ Work of Rabindranath Tagore → Gitanjali

q: Devdas, a famous novel, was written by:
qs.e: The famous novel "Devdas" was written by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay. Published in 1917, it is considered a masterpiece of Indian literature, depicting a tragic love triangle between Devdas, Parvati, and Chandramukhi. Sarat Chandra was one of the greatest writers in Bengali literature, with other notable works including "Shrikanta", "Charitrahin", and "Pather Dabi". Rabindranath Tagore wrote "Gitanjali", Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote "Anandamath", and Samudragupta was a historical king.
qs.kf:
☛ Author of "Devdas" → Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
☛ Year of publication of "Devdas" → 1917
☛ Language of Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay → Bengali
☛ Author of "Shrikanta" → Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
☛ Author of "Gitanjali" → Rabindranath Tagore

q: Who authored 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'?
qs.e: The book 'The Indian War of Independence 1857' was authored by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. Written in 1909, this book portrays the 1857 revolt as India's First War of Independence. Savarkar argued that the revolt was a coordinated national uprising rather than a mere mutiny. The British government banned the book due to its revolutionary content. Savarkar was a prominent freedom fighter and Hindutva ideologue. He was sentenced to life imprisonment and sent to Cellular Jail in Andaman.
qs.kf:
☛ 1857 revolt → First War of Indian Independence
☛ Other book by Savarkar → Hindutva: Who is a Hindu
☛ Leader of 1857 revolt → Bahadur Shah Zafar
☛ Savarkar's imprisonment → Andaman Cellular Jail
☛ Savarkar's birth → 28 May 1883

q: The book “Poverty and Un-British Rule in India”, which compiled evidence from British official sources to explain India’s economic drain, was authored by whom?
qs.e: Dadabhai Naoroji authored the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' in 1901, where he used official British data to prove the continuous outflow of wealth (economic drain) from India under British rule. He argued that British policies systematically impoverished India by draining its resources. Naoroji also made the first estimate of India's national income and demonstrated that British rule kept India underdeveloped. This book became the foundation of economic nationalism in the Indian freedom movement. Naoroji was also the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is considered the father of 'Economic Nationalism' in India? → Dadabhai Naoroji
☛ When did Dadabhai Naoroji make the first estimate of India's national income? → 1876
☛ What was Naoroji's estimate of the poverty line per capita? → ₹12 per year (1890s)
☛ Who was the Congress President during the Partition of Bengal (1905)? → Gopal Krishna Gokhale
☛ Which famous books did R. C. Dutt write? → 'Indian Economy' and 'The Economic History of India'

q: Who among the following wrote the book, ‘The Inheritance of Loss’?
qs.e: The book ‘The Inheritance of Loss’ was written by Kiran Desai. Published in 2006, it won the Man Booker Prize the same year. Kiran Desai is the daughter of the renowned author Anita Desai. The novel is set against the backdrop of India and America, exploring themes of colonialism, globalization, and identity. Kiran Desai became the youngest woman to win the Booker Prize at the age of 35.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote ‘The Inheritance of Loss’? → Kiran Desai
☛ Which prestigious award did Kiran Desai win? → Man Booker Prize
☛ Who is the mother of Kiran Desai? → Anita Desai
☛ In which year was ‘The Inheritance of Loss’ published? → 2006
☛ At what age did Kiran Desai become the youngest woman to win the Booker Prize? → 35 years

q: Who wrote the book 'Reenchantment - Masterworks of Sculpture in Village Temples of Bihar and Orissa'?
qs.e: The book 'Reenchantment - Masterworks of Sculpture in Village Temples of Bihar and Orissa' is written by Robert N. Linrothe. This book documents the masterpieces of sculpture found in rural temples of Bihar and Odisha. Linrothe is a renowned art historian specializing in Himalayan and Indian art. The book is a significant contribution to the study of regional temple architecture and sculpture, highlighting the artistic richness of village temples.
qs.kf:
☛ Who wrote 'Reenchantment'? → Robert N. Linrothe
☛ Which states are focused on in the book? → Bihar and Odisha
☛ What is Linrothe's expertise? → Himalayan and Indian art history
☛ What is the subject of the book? → Masterworks of sculpture in village temples
☛ Does the book cover temple architecture? → Yes, it studies temple architecture and sculpture

q: Who was the author of 'Amar Sonar Bangla', the national anthem of Bangladesh?
qs.e: The national anthem of Bangladesh, 'Amar Sonar Bangla', was written by Rabindranath Tagore. This song was composed in 1905 during the protest against the partition of Bengal. It was officially adopted as the national anthem of Bangladesh in 1972. Tagore is also the author of India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' and was the first Asian Nobel laureate in Literature. His poetry and music remain deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of both countries.
qs.kf:
☛ Title of Bangladesh's national anthem → Amar Sonar Bangla
☛ Author of Bangladesh's national anthem → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ Year adopted as national anthem → 1972
☛ Occasion for which it was written → Against the partition of Bengal (1905)
☛ Author of India's national anthem → Rabindranath Tagore

q: Which of the following is the famous composition of Aryabhatta?
qs.e: Aryabhatta was a great Indian mathematician and astronomer. His famous composition is Aryabhatti, a Sanskrit treatise on mathematics and astronomy. It covers topics like trigonometry, algebra, arithmetic, and planetary motion. Aryabhatta made significant contributions to the development of zero and the decimal system. He accurately measured the Earth's circumference and scientifically explained solar eclipses. Aryabhatti contains 108 verses divided into four chapters. This work is considered the foundation of Indian mathematics and astronomy.
qs.kf:
☛ Aryabhatta's famous work → Aryabhatti
☛ Aryabhatta's contribution → Mathematics and astronomy
☛ Number of verses in Aryabhatti → 108
☛ Aryabhatta discovered → Zero and decimal system
☛ Aryabhatta's field of work → Mathematics and astronomy

q: Who among the following gave sharp criticism of imperialism, termed as 'drain of wealth', which was a milestone in the mainstream Indian independence movement?
qs.e: Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, criticizing the continuous outflow of wealth from India under British rule. His book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' elaborates this idea. He demonstrated that Britain was exploiting India, transferring India's wealth to Britain. This theory became a cornerstone of the Indian national movement. Naoroji was the first Indian member of the British Parliament and shaped Indian economic nationalism.
qs.kf:
☛ Propounder of Drain of Wealth theory → Dadabhai Naoroji
☛ Book describing Drain of Wealth → Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
☛ First Indian member of British Parliament → Dadabhai Naoroji (Liberal Party)
☛ Birth of Dadabhai Naoroji → 1825, Navsari, Gujarat
☛ Impact of Drain of Wealth theory → Inspired Indian economic nationalism and Swadeshi movement

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Commemorated on National Science Day, CV Raman established key scientific platforms in India. The scientific journal founded by him was _______.
qs.e: CV Raman founded the Indian Journal of Physics (IJP) in 1926, which became a key platform for promoting physics research in India. National Science Day (February 28) commemorates his discovery of the Raman Effect. Raman also contributed to establishing institutions like the Indian Institute of Science and the Raman Research Institute. IJP played a vital role in giving the Indian physics community global recognition.
qs.kf:
☛ When is National Science Day celebrated? → February 28
☛ What is CV Raman's famous discovery? → Raman Effect
☛ In which year did Raman get the Nobel Prize? → 1930
☛ Who got India's first Nobel Prize? → Rabindranath Tagore (1913)
☛ Research institute founded by CV Raman? → Raman Research Institute, Bangalore

name: Set 1 · Q1–46
sub: Static GK - Art, Culture, Music, Dance & Festivals

q: Kalamkari painting is related to which state?
qs.e: Kalamkari is a traditional hand-painted or block-printed cotton textile art, primarily practiced in the districts of Srikakulam, Krishna, Guntur, and Prakasam in Andhra Pradesh. This art form uses natural dyes and mainly depicts mythological stories, Ramayana, Mahabharata, and traditional designs. The term 'Kalamkari' is derived from 'kalam' (pen) and 'kari' (craftsmanship), meaning work done with a pen. It flourished under the patronage of the Mughals and the Golconda Sultanate in the 17th century. In 2008, Kalamkari received the Geographical Indication (GI) tag, highlighting its significance as a valuable heritage of Indian handicrafts.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is the origin of Kalamkari? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What types of dyes are used in Kalamkari? → Natural dyes
☛ When did Kalamkari get GI tag? → 2008
☛ What does the word Kalamkari mean? → Craftsmanship done with a pen
☛ What is mainly depicted in Kalamkari? → Mythological stories

q: Which of the following is NOT a/an UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi?
qs.e: The Elephanta Caves are located near Mumbai, Maharashtra, and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, but they are not in Delhi. Delhi has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Humayun's Tomb (1993), Qutub Minar (1993), and Red Fort (2007). All three are recognized as World Heritage Sites. Therefore, among the given options, Elephanta Caves is not located in Delhi, making it the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ First UNESCO site in Delhi → Humayun's Tomb (1993)
☛ Site with tallest minar → Qutub Minar (72.5 m)
☛ Builder of Red Fort → Shah Jahan
☛ State of Elephanta Caves → Maharashtra
☛ Total UNESCO sites in Delhi → 3

q: Which of the following is India's ﬁrst speaking movie?
qs.e: India's first talking movie is Alam Ara, directed by Ardeshir Irani and released in 1931. It was a Hindi/Urdu language film and was screened at the Majestic Cinema in Mumbai. The film starred Master Vithal and Zubeida in lead roles. Alam Ara is considered a landmark in Indian cinema history as it ended the era of silent films and introduced sound films. The movie had 7 songs and its popularity gave a new direction to the Indian film industry.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is India's first talking movie? → Alam Ara
☛ When was Alam Ara released? → 1931
☛ Who directed Alam Ara? → Ardeshir Irani
☛ Who were the lead actors in Alam Ara? → Master Vithal and Zubeida
☛ How many songs were in Alam Ara? → 7

q: Hawa Mahal is a palace in ______.
qs.e: Hawa Mahal is a famous historical palace located in Jaipur, the capital city of Rajasthan. It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh. This palace is renowned for its 953 windows (jharokhas) made of red and pink sandstone. The design of Hawa Mahal resembles a crown (mukut), inspired by Lord Krishna's crown. It is an exquisite example of Rajput architecture and is also called the Palace of Winds. The main purpose of the palace was to allow royal ladies to observe street life without being seen, as the windows provided ventilation and privacy.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Hawa Mahal? → Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh
☛ What is Hawa Mahal also known as? → Palace of Winds
☛ How many windows does Hawa Mahal have? → 953
☛ In which city is Hawa Mahal located? → Jaipur
☛ In which year was Hawa Mahal built? → 1799

q: Classical musician TR Mahalingam is associated with which musical instrument?
qs.e: TR Mahalingam, popularly known as 'Mali', was a renowned Indian classical musician associated with the flute. Born in 1926 in Tamil Nadu, he was a exponent of the Carnatic style of music. He is often referred to as the 'magician of the flute' for his extraordinary skill. Mahalingam elevated the flute to a prominent solo instrument in classical concerts. He was known for his unique style, developed without formal training, and introduced innovative techniques that enhanced the expressiveness of the instrument. His contributions have left a lasting impact on Carnatic music.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument is TR Mahalingam associated with? → Flute
☛ What is the musical style of TR Mahalingam? → Carnatic classical
☛ What is the nickname of TR Mahalingam? → Mali
☛ What title was given to TR Mahalingam? → Magician of the flute
☛ Where was TR Mahalingam born? → Tamil Nadu

q: Classical musician Shivkumar Sharma is associated with which musical instrument?
qs.e: Shivkumar Sharma was a renowned Indian classical musician who popularized the Santoor in Indian classical music. The Santoor is a stringed instrument played with wooden mallets. Originally a folk instrument from Kashmir, Sharma adapted it for raga-based classical music by modifying its technique and playing style. He received the Padma Shri in 2001 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2000. Shivkumar Sharma's name is synonymous with the Santoor, as he elevated its status in the world of classical music.
qs.kf:
☛ What metal strings are used in Santoor? → Steel and bronze
☛ What is used to play the Santoor? → Wooden mallets
☛ In which year did Shivkumar Sharma receive the Padma Shri? → 2001
☛ What is Shivkumar Sharma's famous album? → Call of the Valley
☛ What is the alternative name for Santoor? → Shatatantri Veena

q: Classical musician Vilayat Khan is associated with which musical instrument?
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (A) Sitar

q: Name of the painter of famous painting, ‘Mahishasura’.
qs.e: The painter of the famous painting 'Mahishasura' is Tyeb Mehta. This painting was created in 1969 and depicts Mahishasura (the buffalo-headed demon). Tyeb Mehta was a prominent Indian modern artist and was awarded the Padma Shri in 1985. His painting 'Mahishasura' was sold at auction for 26 crore rupees in 2018. Tyeb Mehta was a member of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group, and his art often reinterpreted mythological themes with a modern perspective.
qs.kf:
☛ Tyeb Mehta's famous painting → Mahishasura
☛ Award received by Tyeb Mehta → Padma Shri (1985)
☛ Art group associated with Tyeb Mehta → Bombay Progressive Artists' Group
☛ Auction price of Mahishasura (2018) → 26 crore rupees
☛ Birth year of Tyeb Mehta → 1925

q: Al-Haram Mosque is the largest mosque in the world. It is situated in:
qs.e: Al-Haram Mosque, also known as Masjid al-Haram, is the largest mosque in the world. It is located in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. The mosque encloses the Kaaba, the holiest site in Islam. Muslims from around the world come here to perform Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages. The mosque is undergoing constant expansion and currently has a capacity of about 2 million worshippers.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the largest mosque in the world? → Masjid al-Haram (Mecca)
☛ What holy site is inside Masjid al-Haram? → Kaaba
☛ In which country is Masjid al-Haram located? → Saudi Arabia
☛ Where are Hajj and Umrah performed? → Masjid al-Haram in Mecca
☛ Which is the second largest mosque? → Masjid al-Nabawi (Medina)

q: Which of these is NOT a type of string musical instrument?
qs.e: String instruments produce sound by vibrating strings. Bass (double bass), Violin, and Cello are all string instruments that are typically bowed or plucked. In contrast, the Tuba is a brass instrument, which produces sound through the vibration of air inside a metal tube and has no strings. It is the largest and lowest-pitched member of the brass family, commonly used in orchestras and bands.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument is an example of a brass instrument? → Tuba, trumpet, French horn
☛ What material are strings typically made of in string instruments? → Metal or nylon
☛ How many strings does a violin have? → Four
☛ What category does the cello belong to? → String instrument
☛ What is the typical height of a double bass? → About 1.8 meters

q: Mrinal Sen, who passed away on 30 December 2018, was an eminent personality in the field of-
qs.e: Mrinal Sen was a renowned Indian film director and screenwriter, considered a pioneer of Indian parallel cinema. Born on May 14, 1923, he gained recognition for socially realistic films like Bhuvan Shome, Khandhar, Akash Kusum, and Charulata. He was a contemporary of Satyajit Ray and Ritwik Ghatak, and his films highlighted political and social issues. In the 1970s-80s, his works received both national and international acclaim. He was honored with the Padma Bhushan and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. Mrinal Sen was a towering figure in the Indian film industry.
qs.kf:
☛ Which film movement was Mrinal Sen associated with? → Parallel cinema
☛ Highest film award received by Mrinal Sen? → Dadasaheb Phalke Award
☛ Famous film by Mrinal Sen? → Bhuvan Shome (1969)
☛ Prominent contemporaries of Mrinal Sen? → Satyajit Ray and Ritwik Ghatak
☛ Civilian honor awarded to Mrinal Sen? → Padma Bhushan (1981)

q: Which of these places was founded in 1577 by Guru Ram Das?
qs.e: Guru Ram Das, the fourth Sikh Guru, founded the city of Amritsar in 1577. He succeeded Guru Amar Das and was the father of Guru Arjan Dev. He laid the foundation of the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib), which was later completed by Guru Arjan Dev. Amritsar is the holiest city in Sikhism. Before its establishment, the area was a forest surrounding a lake. Guru Ram Das developed this site into a religious and social center.
qs.kf:
☛ City founded by Guru Ram Das → Amritsar
☛ Who started the construction of the Golden Temple → Guru Ram Das
☛ Year of Amritsar's foundation → 1577
☛ Guru Ram Das was which Sikh Guru → Fourth
☛ Who completed the Harmandir Sahib → Guru Arjan Dev

q: Which country has won the maximum number of Oscar awards to date in the category of foreign films? A. Italy B. France
C. Japan D. Spain
qs.e: In the category of Best International Feature Film at the Oscars, Italy has won the most awards, with a total of 14 wins. This is the highest among all countries. Notable Italian winners include Federico Fellini's 8½, Vittorio De Sica's Bicycle Thieves, and Giuseppe Tornatore's Cinema Paradiso. France is second with 12 wins, followed by Japan with 5 and Spain with 4. The category was introduced in 1956, and Italian films have consistently been recognized for their artistic excellence and storytelling. Italy's dominance reflects its strong cinematic tradition and cultural influence.
qs.kf:
☛ Country with most Oscars (Foreign Film) → Italy (14 wins)
☛ Second most Oscars in this category → France (12 wins)
☛ First Italian film to win → La Strada (1956)
☛ Year the category started → 1956
☛ Director with most wins in this category → Federico Fellini (4 wins)

q: Who directed India's first publicly released film, Raja Harishchandra?
A. V G Dhamale
B. V Shantaram
C. Bimal Roy
D. Dada Saheb Phalke
qs.e: India's first publicly released film Raja Harishchandra (1913) was directed by Dada Saheb Phalke, who is regarded as the father of Indian cinema. The film was based on a mythological story and was screened at the Coronation Cinema in Bombay. Phalke purchased a Bioscope from London in 1912 and began film production. Raja Harishchandra was a silent film with a runtime of approximately 40 minutes. To honor Phalke's contribution, the Government of India instituted the Dada Saheb Phalke Award, the highest award in Indian cinema.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Raja Harishchandra released? → 1913
☛ Who is the father of Indian cinema? → Dada Saheb Phalke
☛ What type of film was Raja Harishchandra? → Silent film
☛ Who was the lead actor in the film? → D.D. Dabholkar
☛ When was the Dada Saheb Phalke Award instituted? → 1969

q: Pakistani film industry is known as _______ A. Pollywood
B. Lollywood C. Kollywood D. Mollywood
qs.e: The Pakistani film industry is known as Lollywood. This name is derived from Lahore, the city where most film production takes place in Pakistan. The term 'Lollywood' is a combination of 'Lahore' and 'Hollywood'. The industry primarily produces films in Urdu and Punjabi languages. Among the other options, Pollywood refers to the Punjabi film industry, Kollywood refers to the Tamil film industry, and Mollywood refers to the Malayalam film industry.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of Pakistani film industry → Lollywood
☛ Main center of Lollywood → Lahore
☛ Main languages in Lollywood → Urdu and Punjabi
☛ Name of Punjabi film industry → Pollywood
☛ Name of Tamil film industry → Kollywood

q: Which of the following is NOT a monument in Uttar Pradesh?
qs.e: Safdarjung Tomb is located in Delhi, not in Uttar Pradesh. It is a Mughal-era tomb built in 1754 AD by Shuja-ud-Daula for his father Safdarjung. It is situated on Lodhi Road in the Nizamuddin area. Other options: Bara Imambara is in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, showcasing Awadhi architecture. Sarnath Stupa is near Varanasi, where Gautam Buddha gave his first sermon. Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage site in Agra on the banks of the Yamuna River.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Safdarjung Tomb located? → Delhi
☛ In which city is Bara Imambara? → Lucknow
☛ Sarnath Stupa is associated with which religion? → Buddhism
☛ Along which river is Taj Mahal situated? → Yamuna
☛ Who built Safdarjung Tomb? → Shuja-ud-Daula

q: As of October 2020, which of the following is NOT on the World Heritage list?
qs.e: As of October 2020, India has 38 UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Agra Fort (1983), Elephanta Caves (1987), and Konark Sun Temple (1984) are on the World Heritage list. Hawa Mahal, a historic palace in Jaipur, was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh. It is also called the 'Palace of Winds'. It is made of red sandstone and has 953 small windows. Hawa Mahal had not been granted UNESCO World Heritage status as of October 2020. The city of Jaipur was declared a World Heritage Site in 2019, but Hawa Mahal individually was not listed.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Agra Fort declared a World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ In which state are the Elephanta Caves located? → Maharashtra
☛ Who built the Konark Sun Temple? → Narasinghdeva I
☛ How many windows does Hawa Mahal have? → 953
☛ When did Jaipur city receive UNESCO World Heritage status? → 2019

q: With which of the following musical instruments was V Balsara associated?
qs.e: V. Balsara (Wilfred Balsara) was a renowned Indian pianist, often called the 'Piano Man of India'. He popularized Indian classical music by performing it on the piano. He belonged to the Parsi community and performed on many international stages. V. Balsara developed a unique style by fusing Indian music with the Western instrument piano. For his contributions, he was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1970. Jal Tarang, Sarangi, and Mandolin are not associated with him.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument is V. Balsara associated with? → Piano
☛ What is V. Balsara popularly known as? → Piano Man of India
☛ Which award did V. Balsara receive? → Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 1970
☛ Jal Tarang is what type of instrument? → Percussion instrument made of water-filled bowls
☛ Sarangi is what type of instrument? → Bowed string instrument

q: _______ was India's first indigenously made film in colour.
qs.e: Kisan Kanya (1937) is India's first indigenously made colour film. Directed by Mohan Bhavnani, it was produced using the Cine-Color process. The film highlighted the plight of farmers under British rule. In contrast, Raja Harishchandra (1913) was India's first silent film, and Alam Ara (1931) was the first talkie. Chhota Chetan is a 1998 Indian animated film. Thus, Kisan Kanya holds the distinction of being the first colour film.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first colour film → Kisan Kanya (1937)
☛ India's first silent film → Raja Harishchandra (1913)
☛ India's first talkie → Alam Ara (1931)
☛ Director of Kisan Kanya → Mohan Bhavnani
☛ Technique used in Kisan Kanya → Cine-Color

q: Which Mughal monument was designed by Ustad Ahmad Lahori and declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1983?
qs.e: The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It was designed by the famous architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori. Located in Agra on the banks of the Yamuna River, its construction began in 1632 and was completed in 1648. The main dome is 73 meters high. The Taj Mahal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1983. It is an exquisite example of Mughal architecture and is considered one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the construction of Taj Mahal begin? → 1632
☛ Who designed the Taj Mahal? → Ustad Ahmad Lahori
☛ When was Taj Mahal declared a UNESCO World Heritage site? → 1983
☛ Which river is the Taj Mahal located on? → Yamuna
☛ What is the height of the main dome of Taj Mahal? → 73 meters

q: Which city of India celebrates the famous Elephant Festival annually on the day of Holi?
qs.e: The city of Jaipur in India celebrates the famous Elephant Festival annually on the day of Holi. This festival is organized at the Jantar Mantar and Chaugan area of Jaipur. It features a parade of decorated elephants, elephant races, polo matches, and cultural performances. The festival is organized by the Rajasthan Tourism Department and is very popular among tourists. The Elephant Festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Elephant Festival celebrated? → Jaipur
☛ On which festival day is the Elephant Festival celebrated? → Holi
☛ Who organizes the Elephant Festival? → Rajasthan Tourism Department
☛ What activities are part of the Elephant Festival? → Elephant parade, races, polo
☛ Which state's festival is the Elephant Festival? → Rajasthan

q: Which of the following musical instruments is not Indo-Islamic in origin?
qs.e: Veena is an ancient Indian string instrument that has been part of Indian musical tradition since the Vedic period. It is purely Indian in origin, not Indo-Islamic. In contrast, Sitar, Rabab, and Tabla were introduced or developed during the Mughal period with Persian and Central Asian influences. Sitar evolved from the Persian setar, Rabab came from Afghanistan and Central Asia, and Tabla was developed in Mughal courts. Therefore, Veena is the only instrument listed that is not of Indo-Islamic origin, as it predates Islamic influence and remains a core part of classical Indian music.
qs.kf:
☛ In which Veda is the veena mentioned? → Samaveda
☛ Which instrument did the sitar evolve from? → Persian setar
☛ During which Mughal emperor's reign was the tabla developed? → Akbar
☛ Which country's traditional instrument is the rabab? → Afghanistan
☛ How many major types of veena are in Indian classical music? → Two (Saraswati veena, Vichitra veena)

q: In which Indian fort would you find the Musamman Burj?
qs.e: The Musamman Burj is an octagonal tower located inside the Red Fort of Agra. It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan and is situated near the Diwan-i-Khas. The tower offers a stunning view of the Taj Mahal, and it is believed that Shah Jahan spent his final days here, gazing at the Taj. The Musamman Burj is constructed from white marble and is adorned with exquisite carvings, representing a fine example of Mughal architecture. This structure is also known as the Saman Burj or the Jewel Tower.
qs.kf:
☛ In which fort is the Musamman Burj located? → Red Fort of Agra
☛ Who built the Musamman Burj? → Shah Jahan
☛ What is the Musamman Burj made of? → White marble
☛ Which monument is visible from the Musamman Burj? → Taj Mahal
☛ On which river is the Red Fort of Agra situated? → Yamuna River

q: Which of the following films was directed by Satyajit Ray?
qs.e: Satyajit Ray was a legendary Indian film director. He directed 'Pather Panchali' (1955), his debut film and the first part of the 'Apu Trilogy'. The film depicts the life of a poor Brahmin family in a Bengali village and won the Best Human Document award at the Cannes Film Festival. Other options: 'Kora Kagaz' was directed by Gulshan Nanda, 'Mahal' by Kamal Amrohi, and 'Pyaasa' by Guru Dutt.
qs.kf:
☛ Satyajit Ray's debut film → Pather Panchali
☛ Other parts of Apu Trilogy → Aparajito and Apur Sansar
☛ Oscar awarded to Satyajit Ray → Honorary Oscar in 1992
☛ Satyajit Ray's birth → 1921, Kolkata
☛ Satyajit Ray's death → 1992

q: Which of the following is NOT a wind musical instrument?
qs.e: Wind musical instruments produce sound by blowing air into them. Trumpet, Shehnai, and Saxophone are all wind instruments. Khol is a percussion instrument (a drum) played by hand and does not use air to produce sound. Khol is primarily used in Eastern India, especially in Bengal and Assam, for devotional and folk music. It is a double-headed drum. Hence, Khol is not a wind musical instrument.
qs.kf:
☛ Wind instruments → Flute, Shehnai, Trumpet, Saxophone, Harmonium
☛ Percussion instruments → Drum, Tabla, Mridangam, Khol, Ghungroo
☛ Khol usage → Mainly in Bengal and Assam for kirtan
☛ Shehnai maestro → Ustad Bismillah Khan
☛ Saxophone inventor → Adolphe Sax

q: UNESCO has named _______ as the World Capital of Architecture for 2020.
qs.e: UNESCO named Brazil's Rio de Janeiro as the World Capital of Architecture for 2020. The announcement was made in 2019. Rio de Janeiro is renowned for its unique architectural heritage, including modernist, colonial, and contemporary styles. The city is home to iconic landmarks such as Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain, and Maracanã Stadium. This designation was made in collaboration with the International Union of Architects (UIA). Rio de Janeiro became the first city in the world to receive this honor. The initiative aims to promote the importance of architecture and urban planning.
qs.kf:
☛ World Capital of Architecture for 2020 → Rio de Janeiro
☛ UNESCO's partner organization → International Union of Architects (UIA)
☛ Famous statue in Rio de Janeiro → Christ the Redeemer
☛ Famous stadium in Rio de Janeiro → Maracanã Stadium
☛ World Capital of Architecture program → Started in collaboration with UIA

q: Which of the following exponents does NOT play the Sitar?
qs.e: Pt Shiv Kumar Sharma is a renowned Santoor player, not a Sitar player. He popularized the Santoor in Indian classical music. The other three options are associated with the Sitar. Ustad Vilayat Khan was a legendary Sitar player representing the Imdadkhani gharana. Anoushka Shankar is an acclaimed Sitar player and daughter of Pt Ravi Shankar. Pt Ravi Shankar was an internationally renowned Sitar maestro who brought Indian classical music to global prominence. Therefore, the exponent who does NOT play the Sitar is Pt Shiv Kumar Sharma.
qs.kf:
☛ Santoor player → Pt Shiv Kumar Sharma
☛ Sitar player, Imdadkhani gharana → Ustad Vilayat Khan
☛ Sitar player, daughter of Pt Ravi Shankar → Anoushka Shankar
☛ Sitar player, Bharat Ratna → Pt Ravi Shankar
☛ Number of strings in Sitar → 20 (7 main, 13 sympathetic)

q: Dandiya is the traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
qs.e: Dandiya is the traditional folk dance of Gujarat, primarily performed during the festival of Navratri. Dancers wear colorful attire and use dandiyas (wooden sticks) to rhythmically strike each other in a group dance. It is closely associated with Garba, a folk dance performed by women. Dandiya is also known as Ras or Ras Dandiya and is believed to be inspired by Lord Krishna's Raslila. This dance is widely popular not only in Gujarat but across India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state does Garba belong to? → Gujarat
☛ Which instrument is commonly used in Dandiya? → Dhol
☛ Which goddess is worshipped during Navratri? → Durga
☛ What is the biggest festival of Gujarat? → Navratri
☛ Which dance is associated with Krishna Leela? → Ras

q: Who founded the Vijay Colony in Chittaur?
qs.e: The Vijay Colony in Chittaur was established by Rana Kumbha. Rana Kumbha was a renowned ruler of Mewar who reigned from 1433 to 1468 AD. The colony was founded to commemorate his military victories. Rana Kumbha built several important monuments, including Kumbhalgarh Fort and the Victory Tower (Vijay Stambha). The Victory Tower is located in Chittorgarh Fort and symbolizes his triumph over the rulers of Malwa and Gujarat. Rana Kumbha was a patron of art and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Victory Tower (Vijay Stambha)? → Rana Kumbha
☛ Which Mewar ruler founded Vijay Colony? → Rana Kumbha
☛ What was the reign period of Rana Kumbha? → 1433-1468 AD
☛ Who built Kumbhalgarh Fort? → Rana Kumbha
☛ Which victory does the Vijay Stambha in Chittorgarh represent? → Victory over rulers of Malwa and Gujarat

q: M.F. Hussein is famous in the area of ___________.
qs.e: M.F. Husain (Maqbool Fida Husain) was one of the most famous painters of India. He is often called the 'Picasso of India'. His paintings reflect a unique blend of Indian culture, mythology, and modern themes. Husain played a vital role in the development of Indian modern art, and his works are internationally acclaimed. He was also involved in filmmaking and acting, but his main identity remains in the field of painting. Husain had the honor of being a founding member of the 'Progressive Artists Group' in 1948.
qs.kf:
☛ Full name of M.F. Husain → Maqbool Fida Husain
☛ What is M.F. Husain known as → Picasso of India
☛ Founding member of which group → Progressive Artists Group
☛ Year awarded Padma Shri → 1955
☛ Year awarded Padma Bhushan → 1973

q: Where is the head office of Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH) located?
qs.e: The Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH) was established in 1986 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. Its head office is located in New Delhi. The primary objective of EPCH is to promote the export of Indian handicraft products and provide exporters with market access, information, and facilities. The council participates in various international fairs and exhibitions to encourage handicraft exports. Its key functions include export policy formulation, training, and capacity building.
qs.kf:
☛ EPCH establishment year → 1986
☛ EPCH regional offices → Jaipur, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai
☛ EPCH objective → To promote handicraft exports
☛ EPCH head office → New Delhi
☛ EPCH under the ministry → Ministry of Commerce and Industry

q: Surajkund International Crafts Mela is celebrated every year in the state of -
qs.e: Surajkund International Crafts Mela is held annually in Surajkund, located in the Faridabad district of Haryana. This fair takes place in February and attracts artisans and craftsmen from around the world. It was first organized in 1987 and is renowned for promoting Indian handicrafts and culture. Surajkund is also historically significant, named after the Suraj Kund lake built by King Surajmal.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Surajkund Mela held? → Haryana
☛ When did Surajkund Mela start? → 1987
☛ Which river is Surajkund near? → Yamuna
☛ Who built Suraj Kund? → Surajmal
☛ Largest fair of Haryana? → Surajkund International Crafts Mela

q: From which of the following cities did the Chikankari, work of embroidery originate?
qs.e: Chikankari is a famous embroidery style of India that originated in the city of Lucknow. This art developed during the Mughal period and was popularized by Nur Jahan. Chikankari involves delicate and fine stitches using white thread on white cotton fabric. The primary fabric used is soft muslin or chikan cloth. Lucknow has been granted a Geographical Indication (GI) tag for this craft. Other options like Ludhiana, Chamba, and Barmer are known for their own embroidery styles, but Chikankari is specifically associated with Lucknow.
qs.kf:
☛ Place of origin of Chikankari → Lucknow
☛ Who popularized Chikankari? → Nur Jahan
☛ Main fabric used in Chikankari → Muslin/Chikan
☛ City with GI tag for Chikankari → Lucknow
☛ Major stitches in Chikankari → Bakhiya, Phanda, Khatawi

q: Where is Angkor Wat?
qs.e: Angkor Wat is a world-famous temple complex located in the Angkor region of Cambodia. It was built in the 12th century by King Suryavarman II of the Khmer Empire. Originally dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu, it later became a Buddhist temple. Angkor Wat is renowned for its grand architecture and massive size, and it has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is the national symbol of Cambodia and a major tourist attraction.
qs.kf:
☛ In which country is Angkor Wat located? → Cambodia
☛ Who built Angkor Wat? → King Suryavarman II
☛ Which Hindu god was Angkor Wat originally dedicated to? → Vishnu
☛ Angkor Wat belongs to which empire? → Khmer Empire
☛ In which century was Angkor Wat built? → 12th century

q: By what other name is the 'Red Fort' known?
qs.e: The Red Fort, also known as Lal Qila, is a historic fort located in Delhi, India. It was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan starting in 1638 and completed in 1648. The fort gets its name from the red sandstone used in its construction. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and serves as the venue for the Prime Minister's annual Independence Day speech on August 15. The fort is famous for its massive walls, Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, and other examples of Mughal architecture. It symbolizes India's rich history and cultural heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Red Fort? → Shah Jahan
☛ When was construction of the Red Fort started? → 1638 AD
☛ When was the Red Fort completed? → 1648 AD
☛ What stone is the Red Fort made of? → Red sandstone
☛ Where is the Red Fort located? → Delhi

q: The Gangaur festival of Rajasthan, which is devoted to Goddess Parvati, lasts for _____ days.
qs.e: The Gangaur festival of Rajasthan is dedicated to Goddess Parvati and is celebrated for 18 days. It begins on the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Chaitra and ends on the full moon day of the same month. During this period, married women pray for a happy married life, while unmarried girls seek a good husband. The festival involves the worship of idols of Ganesh and Gangaur (Parvati) and a grand procession is taken out.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is associated with Gangaur festival? → Rajasthan
☛ Which goddess is Gangaur dedicated to? → Goddess Parvati
☛ Which two deities are worshipped in Gangaur? → Ganesh and Gangaur (Parvati)
☛ In which month is Gangaur celebrated? → Chaitra month
☛ How many days does Gangaur last? → 18 days

q: Which festival is dedicated to the worship of Lord Jagannath?
qs.e: Rath Yatra is the major festival dedicated to Lord Jagannath. It is celebrated in Puri, Odisha, where grand chariot processions of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra are taken out. The festival starts on the second day of the bright fortnight of the month of Ashadha and lasts for nine days. Devotees pull the chariots and seek blessings. Rath Yatra is also known as Gundicha Yatra. The festival is associated with Lord Jagannath's journey to his aunt's house from the temple.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Rath Yatra celebrated? → Puri, Odisha
☛ In which month does Rath Yatra occur? → Ashadha month
☛ What is another name for Rath Yatra? → Gundicha Yatra
☛ How many chariots are used in Rath Yatra? → Three chariots
☛ How many days does Rath Yatra last? → Nine days

q: In which month is the Elephanta festival organised every year by the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) to promote Mumbai tourism and culture?
qs.e: The Elephanta Festival is organised every year in the month of February by the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) on Elephanta Island, Mumbai. This two-day festival aims to promote Mumbai's tourism and rich cultural heritage. The event features classical music, dance, and theatrical performances, attracting both domestic and international tourists. It connects visitors with the historical and cultural significance of the Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for the giant Trimurti statue of Lord Shiva. The pleasant weather in February makes it an ideal time for the festival. The festival was started to boost tourism and showcase Maharashtra's cultural diversity.
qs.kf:
☛ In which month is the Elephanta Festival held? → February
☛ Who organises the Elephanta Festival? → MTDC
☛ On which island are the Elephanta Caves located? → Elephanta Island, Mumbai
☛ Which sculpture is the Elephanta Caves famous for? → Trimurti of Shiva
☛ In which year were the Elephanta Caves declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1987

q: Who built the temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
qs.e: The temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini (considered a form of Durga) was built by Vijayalaya, the founder of the Chola dynasty. This temple is located at Narthamalai in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. Vijayalaya established the Chola Empire in the 9th century and constructed this temple, which is an early example of Chola art and architecture. He is also credited with capturing Thanjavur from the Pallavas.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Chola dynasty? → Vijayalaya
☛ Where is the Nishumbhasudini temple located? → Narthamalai, Tamil Nadu
☛ In which century did Vijayalaya rule? → 9th century
☛ What was the capital of the Chola Empire? → Thanjavur
☛ Goddess Nishumbhasudini is a form of which deity? → Durga

q: The ‘Uttarayani Fair’ of Uttarakhand is related to the Indian festival of _____.
qs.e: The Uttarayani Fair of Uttarakhand is celebrated during the festival of Makar Sankranti. This festival marks the sun's entry into the Capricorn zodiac and is observed annually on January 14. The Uttarayani Fair is especially prominent in the Kumaon and Garhwal regions of Uttarakhand. On this day, devotees take holy dips in rivers and perform charitable acts. The fair is held at several locations, including Bageshwar, Rudraprayag, and Devprayag. Locally, it is also known as the Ghughutia festival. Makar Sankranti is celebrated across India under different names such as Pongal, Lohri, and Bihu.
qs.kf:
☛ Which festival is the Uttarayani Fair related to? → Makar Sankranti
☛ Where is the Uttarayani Fair held? → Uttarakhand
☛ When is Makar Sankranti celebrated? → January 14
☛ What is the local name of the Uttarayani Fair? → Ghughutia festival
☛ Which fair is associated with Makar Sankranti in Uttarakhand? → Uttarayani Fair

q: The sacred journey of Lord Jagannath with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra from the Jagannath Temple of Puri, popularly known as ‘Rath Yatra’, starts in the Hindu month of _____.
qs.e: The famous Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath, along with his brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra, from the Jagannath Temple in Puri begins every year in the Hindu month of Ashadha. This journey starts on the second day of the bright fortnight of Ashadha, known as Gundicha Marg. On this day, the deities are placed on giant chariots and pulled to the Gundicha Temple, where they stay for seven days. This festival is one of the largest chariot processions in the world and is celebrated with great fervor in Odisha. Millions of devotees gather to pull the chariots, considered a pious act.
qs.kf:
☛ In which Hindu month does Rath Yatra start? → Ashadha
☛ At which temple does Rath Yatra conclude? → Gundicha Temple
☛ How many chariots are used in Rath Yatra? → Three
☛ What is the name of Lord Jagannath's chariot? → Nandighosh
☛ What are the names of Balabhadra and Subhadra's chariots? → Taladhwaja and Darpadalana

q: When did UNESCO inscribe the Kumbh Mela in its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
qs.e: UNESCO inscribed the Kumbh Mela in its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 7 December 2017. The decision was taken during the 12th session of the Intergovernmental Committee held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Kumbh Mela is the largest religious gathering in India, held every 3 years and rotating among Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik. It symbolizes Indian spirituality and cultural unity. The festival is also associated with the mythical churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan).
qs.kf:
☛ What was India's first entry in UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list? → Yoga, 2016
☛ Which rivers are associated with Kumbh Mela sites? → Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Godavari, Shipra
☛ Which ministry organizes the Kumbh Mela? → Ministry of Jal Shakti
☛ How many intangible cultural heritage elements does India have? → 15 (as of 2024)
☛ In which year did UNESCO recognize Kumbh Mela? → 2017

q: The traditional Hindu festival of Chhath, observed by people all over Bihar, Jharkhand and parts of Uttar Pradesh, takes place after the festival of _____
qs.e: Chhath Puja is a major Hindu festival primarily celebrated in Bihar, Jharkhand, and parts of Uttar Pradesh. It is observed after the festival of Diwali, on the sixth day of the Kartik month. Diwali falls on the new moon (Amavasya), and Chhath is celebrated six days later. Devotees worship Lord Sun and Chhathi Maiya, observing a rigorous fast without water, and offer prayers (Arghya) at sunset and sunrise. The festival symbolizes environmental balance and cultural unity, and it is known for its strict rituals and devotion.
qs.kf:
☛ In which month is Chhath Puja celebrated? → Kartik month
☛ How many days after Diwali is Chhath celebrated? → 6 days
☛ Which deities are worshipped in Chhath Puja? → Lord Sun and Chhathi Maiya
☛ What is the nature of the Chhath fast? → Fasting without water (Nirjala)
☛ When is Arghya offered in Chhath Puja? → At sunset and sunrise

q: Which of the following films was NOT part of the feature film line-up at the 55th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) under the Indian Panorama section?
qs.e: The 55th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2024 featured 'Raavsaaheb', 'Aadujeevitham', and 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' in the Indian Panorama section. 'Kalki 2898 AD' was not part of this line-up, as it was not selected for the Indian Panorama despite its 2024 release. The Indian Panorama section showcases outstanding Indian cinema each year. The other three films were chosen in various categories, reflecting diversity in Indian languages and themes.
qs.kf:
☛ Venue of 55th IFFI → Goa
☛ Year of IFFI establishment → 1952
☛ Purpose of Indian Panorama section → Promote Indian cinema
☛ Organizing body of IFFI 2024 → Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
☛ Marathi film screened at IFFI → Raavsaaheb

q: The Gangasagar Mela of West Bengal, which is celebrated at the place where Ganga falls into the Bay of Bengal, is celebrated on:
qs.e: The Gangasagar Mela is held on Sagar Island in West Bengal, where the Ganges River meets the Bay of Bengal. This fair is celebrated every year on the day of Makar Sankranti, which falls in January. Millions of devotees take a holy dip at Gangasagar on this day, believing it to be highly meritorious. Makar Sankranti marks the Sun's entry into the zodiac Capricorn. This mela is one of the major pilgrimage sites in Hinduism and the sacred bath holds great significance. Other options like Holi, Kali Puja, and Durga Puja are not associated with the Gangasagar Mela.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Gangasagar Mela held? → Sagar Island, West Bengal
☛ On which day is Gangasagar Mela celebrated? → Makar Sankranti
☛ Which river meets the sea at Gangasagar? → Ganges River
☛ What is the meaning of Makar Sankranti? → Sun's entry into Capricorn
☛ In which month does Gangasagar Mela occur? → January

q: Since which year has the National Tribal Festival/Carnival been organised as an annual feature by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA)?
qs.e: The National Tribal Festival/Carnival has been organised as an annual feature by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) since 2015. This festival showcases the rich tribal culture, art, crafts, dance, and music of India. It aims to promote and preserve the heritage of tribal communities and integrate them into the mainstream. The event is usually held in New Delhi and attracts tribal artists and artisans from across the country. It also provides economic opportunities for the tribal community by offering a platform to sell their products.
qs.kf:
☛ First National Tribal Festival held → 2015
☛ Organising Ministry → Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA)
☛ Venue of the festival → New Delhi
☛ Objective → Showcase and promote tribal culture
☛ Beneficiaries → Tribal artists and artisans

name: Set 2 · Q47–92
sub: Static GK - Art, Culture, Music, Dance & Festivals

q: Indian classical ragas, by the number of notes, can be divided into _____ main categories or Jatis.
qs.e: Indian classical music divides ragas into three main categories or Jatis based on the number of notes used. These Jatis are: Audava (5 notes), Shadava (6 notes), and Sampurna (7 notes). Additionally, some ragas have mixed Jatis like Audava-Shadava or Shadava-Sampurna depending on the omission or addition of notes. This classification helps in understanding the structure and character of each raga. The Jati of a raga determines its melodic framework and is essential for proper classification in Indian classical music theory.
qs.kf:
☛ How many notes in Audava Jati? → 5 notes
☛ How many notes in Shadava Jati? → 6 notes
☛ How many notes in Sampurna Jati? → 7 notes
☛ Which Jati does Raga Yaman belong to? → Sampurna Jati
☛ Which Jati does Raga Bhupali belong to? → Audava Jati

q: In how many tone scale are all the known ragas grouped?
qs.e: In Indian classical music, all known ragas are grouped within a 12-tone scale (12 swara system). This system divides the octave (saptak) into 12 equal semitones, comprising 7 pure notes (sa, re, ga, ma, pa, dha, ni) and 5 altered notes (flat or sharp versions of re, ga, ma, dha, ni). Each raga uses a specific subset of these 12 tones. This 12-tone scale forms the foundation of Indian music theory and is the standard for raga classification. Other options like 14 or 10 tones are not prevalent in Indian music.
qs.kf:
☛ How many total tones are there in Indian classical music? → 12
☛ How many semitones are in an octave? → 12
☛ On what basis are ragas classified? → 12-tone scale
☛ How many pure notes are in the 12-tone system? → 7
☛ How many altered notes are in the 12-tone system? → 5

q: ‘Khuang’ is what type of indigenous instrument of Mizoram which occupies a very significant place in Mizo social and religious life?
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (A) Drum

q: Indian musician Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt was born at which of the following places in 1952?
qs.e: Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt was born on 27 July 1952 in Jaipur, Rajasthan. He is a renowned Indian musician known for inventing the Mohan Veena, a hybrid instrument combining guitar and veena. He has made significant contributions to Hindustani classical music and received several international awards, including the Grammy Award. He was a disciple of Pandit Ravi Shankar.
qs.kf:
☛ Vishwa Mohan Bhatt's birthplace → Jaipur
☛ Invented instrument → Mohan Veena
☛ Grammy Award year → 1994
☛ Guru → Pandit Ravi Shankar
☛ Music genre → Hindustani classical music

q: Grammy award winner, Carnatic musician Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, fondly known as Vikku, is known for his mastery of which of the following musical instruments?
qs.e: Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, fondly known as Vikku, is a renowned Carnatic musician and master of the Ghatam. The Ghatam is a clay pot used as a percussion instrument in South Indian classical music. Vikku gained international recognition for his virtuosity and was awarded a Grammy Award. He belongs to the Thanjavur tradition and learned music from his father Thetakudi Subba Rao. The Ghatam is played with hands, fingers, and wrists to produce various sounds. Vikku has collaborated with many global artists and elevated the status of the Ghatam in world music.
qs.kf:
☛ What is Ghatam made of? → Clay
☛ What is Vikku's full name? → Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram
☛ What type of instrument is Ghatam? → Percussion
☛ Which award did Vikku win? → Grammy Award
☛ In which music is Ghatam primarily used? → Carnatic music

q: Shyama Shastri, Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar, the three composer-musicians of the 18th century, are considered as the trinity of _____ classical music form of India.
qs.e: Shyama Shastri, Tyagaraja, and Muthuswami Dikshitar are known as the Trinity of Carnatic music. These three 18th-century composer-musicians laid the foundation of Carnatic classical music, which is the classical music tradition of South India. They composed thousands of devotional and classical pieces that remain popular. Carnatic music is distinct from Hindustani music and emphasizes raga (melody) and tala (rhythm). The trio's contributions include numerous kriti compositions.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is not part of the Carnatic music trinity? → Purandara Dasa
☛ Who is considered the father of Carnatic music? → Purandara Dasa
☛ What is the primary instrument in Carnatic music? → Veena
☛ How many compositions did Tyagaraja create? → About 24,000
☛ In which language did Muthuswami Dikshitar compose? → Sanskrit and Tamil

q: With which of the following musical instruments is Allauddin Khan associated in India?
qs.e: Allauddin Khan was a renowned Indian classical musician and a master of the sarod. Born in 1862, he belonged to the Maihar gharana and elevated the sarod playing to new heights. He trained many famous disciples, including his son Ali Akbar Khan and daughter Annapurna Devi, and also taught Ravi Shankar. Known for his deep understanding of ragas and unique technique, he received prestigious awards such as the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan. His notable compositions include Raga Miyan ki Todi and Raga Chandranandan.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument is Allauddin Khan associated with? → Sarod
☛ Which gharana did Allauddin Khan belong to? → Maihar gharana
☛ Who were the famous disciples of Allauddin Khan? → Ali Akbar Khan and Ravi Shankar
☛ Which awards did Allauddin Khan receive? → Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan
☛ When was Allauddin Khan born? → 1862

q: Which of the following personalities is a famous flute player of India?
qs.e: Hari Prasad Chaurasia is a famous flute player of India. He is known for his mastery of the bansuri (bamboo flute) in Hindustani classical music. He holds the title Pandit and has been honored with prestigious awards like Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan by the Government of India. While S.V. Rajarao and K.V. Prasad are renowned Carnatic music instrumentalists, and Zakir Hussain is a famous tabla player, Chaurasia is the most prominent exponent of the flute in Indian classical music. His contributions have made the bansuri a globally recognized instrument.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument is Hari Prasad Chaurasia associated with? → Flute (Bansuri)
☛ Which classical music tradition does Hari Prasad Chaurasia belong to? → Hindustani classical music
☛ Zakir Hussain is famous for which instrument? → Tabla
☛ Major awards received by Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia? → Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan
☛ What is the bamboo flute called in Hindustani classical music? → Bansuri

q: ____ is the finest form of Anibaddha sangeeta which is not restricted by meaningful words and tala.
qs.e: Alap is the finest form of Anibaddha sangeeta, which is not restricted by meaningful words and tala. It is an important part of Indian classical music where the singer or instrumentalist elaborates a raga without rhythm and lyrics. In alap, the mood and atmosphere of the raga are presented through notes. It is especially prevalent in Dhrupad singing, where it is used to showcase the depth and beauty of the raga. Compared to other options, Javali, Tilana, and Tanam are all rhythmic and have lyrics, whereas Alap is completely unbound.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the finest form of Anibaddha sangeeta? → Alap
☛ Alap is not restricted by which elements? → Meaningful words and tala
☛ In which style is Alap most prevalent? → Dhrupad
☛ Alap is an important part of which music system? → Indian classical music
☛ What type of music are Javali, Tilana, and Tanam? → Nibaddha sangeeta (rhythmic and with lyrics)

q: Which of the following personalities is NOT a well-known tabla player of India?
qs.e: Hari Prasad Chaurasia is a world-renowned flute player, not a tabla player. He is a master of Hindustani classical music. Allah Rakha, Pt. Kishan Maharaj, and Zakir Hussain are all celebrated tabla maestros. Allah Rakha belonged to the Punjab gharana. Pt. Kishan Maharaj was from the Banaras gharana. Zakir Hussain brought global recognition to tabla and won a Grammy in 2024.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous flutist → Hari Prasad Chaurasia
☛ Allah Rakha's gharana → Punjab gharana
☛ Pt. Kishan Maharaj's gharana → Banaras gharana
☛ Award won by Zakir Hussain → Grammy Award (2024)
☛ Instrument of Hari Prasad Chaurasia → Flute

q: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a highly acclaimed Indian __________ player and composer.
qs.e: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a highly acclaimed Indian sarod player and composer. He is considered one of the greatest living masters of the sarod. Born in 1945, he belongs to the Senia gharana. He has brought the sarod to the global stage and has been honored with several prestigious civilian awards such as Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan. His innovative playing style and new raga compositions are widely admired. The sarod is a prominent string instrument in Indian classical music.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument is Ustad Amjad Ali Khan associated with? → Sarod
☛ What type of instrument is the sarod? → String instrument
☛ Which gharana does Amjad Ali Khan belong to? → Senia gharana
☛ Which civilian award has Amjad Ali Khan received? → Padma Vibhushan
☛ How many strings does a sarod typically have? → 17 to 25 strings

q: ___________ dance form is also known as Ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance.
qs.e: Bharatnatyam is a classical dance form known as Ekaharya, where one dancer portrays multiple roles in a single performance. Originating from Tamil Nadu, it is one of the oldest dance forms in India, based on the Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni. Ekaharya means solo performance with multiple characters. This dance form integrates bhava (expression), raga (melody), and tala (rhythm). It was traditionally performed in temples and later adapted for stage. Other classical dances like Kathakali, Sattriya, and Kathak do not specifically use the term Ekaharya. Bharatnatyam is known for its fixed upper body, bent legs, intricate footwork, and expressive gestures (mudras).
qs.kf:
☛ Ancient name of Bharatnatyam → Dasi Attam
☛ Mudras used in Bharatnatyam → Hasta mudras
☛ Key feature of Bharatnatyam → Combination of natya, nritta and nritya
☛ State associated with Bharatnatyam → Tamil Nadu
☛ Main text of Bharatnatyam → Natya Shastra

q: Which of the following persons is very famous for his sitar playing in India?
qs.e: Pt. Ravi Shankar was a legendary sitar player from India. He popularized sitar music globally and was awarded the Bharat Ratna, Padma Bhushan, and Grammy Awards. Asad Ali Khan is known for Rudra Veena. Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt invented Mohan Veena. Zia Mohiuddin Dagar is famous for Dhrupad singing. Hence, Ravi Shankar is the most famous sitar player among the options.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument did Ravi Shankar play? → Sitar
☛ When was Ravi Shankar awarded Bharat Ratna? → 1999
☛ Which famous band did Ravi Shankar collaborate with? → The Beatles
