q: Which type of Indian cinema refers to commercial, mainstream films primarily produced in Hindi, known for their songs, drama and spectacle?
qs.e: Bollywood is the mainstream branch of Indian cinema that primarily produces films in the Hindi language. It is known for its grand song and dance sequences, dramatic storylines, and focus on audience entertainment. Bollywood films often blend romance, family values, and social issues. Based in Mumbai, it is the largest film industry in India in terms of number of films produced. As commercial cinema, it attracts audiences with big budgets and star power.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Bollywood → Mumbai, Maharashtra
☛ Specialty of Bollywood films → Songs, dance, and drama
☛ Origin of the word Bollywood → Blend of Bombay and Hollywood
☛ Largest film industry in India → Bollywood
☛ Popular name for Bollywood → Hindi cinema

q: Shambhu Maharaj, awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967, was renowned for his contribution to which of the following Indian art forms?
qs.e: Shambhu Maharaj was a renowned exponent and guru of Kathak dance. He belonged to the Lucknow Gharana and played a key role in developing Kathak as a classical dance form. He was awarded the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967, which is the highest honor in Indian arts. Shambhu Maharaj was known for his expressive abhinaya and rhythmic footwork. He contributed significantly to popularizing Kathak and giving it global recognition.
qs.kf:
☛ Shambhu Maharaj was associated with which dance form? → Kathak dance
☛ Which gharana did Shambhu Maharaj belong to? → Lucknow Gharana
☛ In which year did Shambhu Maharaj receive the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship? → 1967
☛ Kathak dance originated in which state? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ When was the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship established? → 1952

q: Who among the following is known for popularising Bharatanatyam on the global stage?
qs.e: Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904-1986) was a renowned dancer, choreographer, and spiritual leader known for reviving and popularising Bharatanatyam on the global stage. She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in 1936, which became a premier institution for teaching and promoting Bharatanatyam. Her efforts transformed Bharatanatyam, which was earlier confined to temple dances, into a respected classical dance form recognized worldwide. She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contributions to Indian classical dance.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dancer revived Bharatanatyam? → Rukmini Devi Arundale
☛ Which institution did Rukmini Devi Arundale establish? → Kalakshetra Foundation
☛ Which state is the origin of Bharatanatyam? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which award did Rukmini Devi Arundale receive? → Padma Bhushan
☛ Which deity is primarily worshipped in Bharatanatyam? → Nataraja (Shiva)

q: Which of the following states is known for the tribal settlement of the Gond community?
qs.e: The Gond community is one of the largest tribal groups in India, with significant populations in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh. Chhattisgarh is particularly known for its Gond tribal settlements, especially in the Bastar region, which is famous for its rich tribal culture and Gond heritage. The other states— Kerala, Haryana, and Punjab—do not have prominent Gond settlements. The Gond community has a distinct language, Gondi, and celebrates festivals like Madai.
qs.kf:
☛ Main habitat of Gond tribe → Central India
☛ State with largest Gond population → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Which region is famous for Gonds → Bastar
☛ Language spoken by Gond tribe → Gondi
☛ Major festival of Gond community → Madai

q: Which of the following temples was also called Black Pagoda by the Germanic Navinco?
A. Konark Temple
B. Jagannath Temple
C. Brahmeshwar Temple
D. Mukteshwar Temple
qs.e: Konark Temple was called Black Pagoda by European sailors. It is located in Odisha and dedicated to the Sun God. The temple was built by King Narasimhadeva I in the 13th century. Due to its dark color, sailors referred to it as Black Pagoda, while Jagannath Temple was called White Pagoda. Konark Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and features a huge chariot with 12 pairs of wheels. It is renowned for its architecture and artistry.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Sun Temple located? → Konark, Odisha
☛ Who built Konark Temple? → Narasimhadeva I
☛ In which century was Konark Temple built? → 13th century
☛ What was Jagannath Temple called? → White Pagoda
☛ Which god is Konark Temple dedicated to? → Sun God

q: Who among the following is a famous Santoor instrumentalist?
qs.e: Santoor is an ancient Indian string instrument, traditionally associated with Kashmir. Shiv Kumar Sharma (1938–2022) is credited with elevating the santoor to a prominent place in Hindustani classical music. He transformed this folk instrument into a concert-worthy classical instrument, pioneering its use in solo performances. A disciple of the Ravi Shankar gharana, he received prestigious awards including the Padma Shri (1986), Padma Vibhushan (2020), and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. Other options: Sajjad Hussain was a music composer, Nikhil Banerjee was a sitar maestro, and Ustad Binda Khan was a sarod player.
qs.kf:
☛ Which awards did Shiv Kumar Sharma receive? → Padma Shri, Padma Vibhushan, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award
☛ Where was Shiv Kumar Sharma born? → Jammu and Kashmir
☛ Which region is santoor associated with? → Kashmir
☛ Nikhil Banerjee is known for which instrument? → Sitar
☛ Ustad Binda Khan is known for which instrument? → Sarod

q: The Virupaksha temple at Hampi is dedicated to ______
qs.e: The Virupaksha temple located in Hampi is dedicated to Lord Shiva. This temple belongs to the period of the Vijayanagara Empire and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi. Virupaksha is a form of Shiva. The temple is situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river flows through Hampi? → Tungabhadra
☛ Hampi was the capital of which empire? → Vijayanagara Empire
☛ Virupaksha temple is built in which style? → Dravidian style
☛ Who rediscovered Hampi? → Colonel Colin Mackenzie
☛ Hampi is located in which state? → Karnataka

q: Which of the following buildings was designed by F.W. Stevens?
o: Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Formerly Victoria Terminus)
qs.e: F.W. Stevens was a prominent British architect who designed several important buildings in India. Among them, the most famous is Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), formerly known as Victoria Terminus. This is the main railway station in Mumbai and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was constructed in 1887 in the Gothic Revival style. Other options: Horniman Circle was designed by Charles St. Clair, Bombay Secretariat by John Begg, and The Town Hall, Bombay by Colonel Cowper and Thomas. Thus, F.W. Stevens designed CSMT.
qs.kf:
☛ Which famous building was designed by F.W. Stevens? → Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Victoria Terminus)
☛ In which style is CSMT built? → Gothic Revival style
☛ When was CSMT built? → 1887
☛ In which year did CSMT become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 2004
☛ Who designed the Bombay Secretariat? → John Begg

q: Which of the following Heritage sites has the Dravidian style of architecture?
qs.e: Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire in Karnataka, is renowned for its Dravidian style of architecture. Temples like the Vitthala Temple and Virupaksha Temple feature towering gopurams, intricately carved pillars, and large courtyards, which are hallmarks of Dravidian architecture. In contrast, Ellora caves represent rock-cut architecture, Khajuraho temples are in Nagara style, and Konark's Sun Temple is built in Kalinga style. The Dravidian style, prevalent in South India, is characterized by pyramid-shaped shikharas, massive gopurams, and mandapas. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage site and exemplifies this architectural tradition through its grand structures and urban planning.
qs.kf:
☛ Prime example of Dravidian style → Hampi
☛ Khajuraho temples belong to which style → Nagara style
☛ Konark Sun Temple style → Kalinga style
☛ Ellora architecture type → Rock-cut
☛ Vitthala Temple is located at → Hampi

q: Pushkar Mela is held in Pushkar. Which district does it come under?
qs.e: Pushkar Mela is held in the town of Pushkar, which falls under the Ajmer district of Rajasthan. It is the world's largest camel fair, organized on the occasion of Kartik Purnima. Pushkar is also known as 'Tirtharaj' and houses the only temple dedicated to Lord Brahma. The fair features camel trading, cultural performances, and a holy dip in the Pushkar Lake. This fair showcases the rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan and is a major tourist attraction.
qs.kf:
☛ On which lake is Pushkar Mela held? → Pushkar Lake
☛ In which month is Pushkar Mela organized? → Kartik month (November)
☛ Which god's temple is famous in Pushkar? → Lord Brahma
☛ In which state is Pushkar Mela held? → Rajasthan
☛ What is the headquarters of Ajmer district? → Ajmer

q: Minati Mishra is associated with -
qs.e: Minati Mishra is a renowned Indian Odissi dancer. She has mastered the Odissi dance form and performed it internationally. Odissi is one of the eight classical dances of India, originating from the state of Odisha. This dance style is characterized by the Tribhangi posture (body bends in three parts) and the Chauki posture. Minati Mishra trained under legends like Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and her artistry has contributed to popularizing Odissi. She has been honored with the Padma Shri award.
qs.kf:
☛ Where did Odissi dance originate? → Odisha
☛ What are the main postures in Odissi? → Tribhangi and Chauki
☛ Which dance form features the Tribhangi posture? → Odissi
☛ For which dance did Minati Mishra receive Padma Shri? → Odissi
☛ Which instruments are commonly used in Odissi? → Mardal and Pakhavaj

q: With which dance form is the noted dancer Guru Rajkumar Singhajit Singh associated?
qs.e: Guru Rajkumar Singhajit Singh is a renowned dancer and guru associated with Manipuri dance, a classical dance form from Manipur, India. He played a vital role in popularizing this dance globally. Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its graceful movements and Rasleela and Lai Haraoba performances. He was honored with the Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contributions. His work emphasized the spiritual and lyrical aspects of Manipuri dance.
qs.kf:
☛ Where did Manipuri dance originate? → Manipur
☛ What are the main forms of Manipuri dance? → Rasleela and Lai Haraoba
☛ When was Manipuri dance recognized as a classical dance? → 1952
☛ Which awards did Rajkumar Singhajit Singh receive? → Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award
☛ Which are the eight classical dances of India? → Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, Sattriya

q: Which of the following cities does NOT have the Jantar Mantar?
qs.e: Jantar Mantar are astronomical observatories built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 18th century. He constructed a total of five observatories across India – Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura. Nagpur does not have any Jantar Mantar. The Jaipur Jantar Mantar is the largest and best preserved, also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Varanasi observatory is located in the Man Mahal complex. Ujjain's observatory is also known as Ved Shala.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Jantar Mantar? → Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II
☛ How many Jantar Mantars were built? → Five (Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi, Mathura)
☛ Which is the largest Jantar Mantar? → Jaipur
☛ Which Jantar Mantar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → Jaipur
☛ What is Ujjain's Jantar Mantar also called? → Ved Shala

q: Pandit Birju Maharaj is a legendary dancer of which Indian dance form?
qs.e: Pandit Birju Maharaj is one of the most legendary dancers of the Kathak dance form. He was the leading exponent of the Lucknow Gharana and brought global recognition to Kathak. Born on 4 February 1938, he was a child prodigy in dance. He also acted and choreographed in films like 'Devdas' and 'Pakeezah'. Kathak is a classical dance style from North India, characterized by storytelling (katha), intricate footwork, and spins. It incorporates gat (movements), taal (rhythm), and abhinaya (expression). Birju Maharaj received prestigious honors including the Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. He trained many disciples and elevated Kathak to an international platform.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin place of Kathak → Uttar Pradesh
☛ Major Gharanas of Kathak → Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras, Raigarh
☛ Real name of Birju Maharaj → Brijmohan Mishra
☛ Main taal used in Kathak → Teental, Ektaal, Jhaptaal
☛ Most famous Kathak dancer → Birju Maharaj

q: Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy for music, dance and drama, was the first national academy of the arts set up by the Republic of India. This academy is located in:
qs.e: Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's first national academy of arts, established in 1952 by the Government of India. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. The academy aims to promote excellence and preserve the heritage of music, dance, and drama. It confers prestigious honors such as the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. The academy operates three major institutions: the National School of Drama in New Delhi, the Dance Centre in Kolkata, and the Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy in Imphal. Its museum, located in New Delhi, houses an extensive collection of Indian musical instruments and costumes. The akademi also organizes festivals, seminars, and research programs to support performing arts.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the current chairman of Sangeet Natak Akademi? → Sandeep Marwah
☛ Where is Sahitya Akademi located? → New Delhi
☛ Where is Lalit Kala Akademi headquartered? → New Delhi
☛ What are the three national academies of India? → Sangeet Natak Akademi, Sahitya Akademi, Lalit Kala Akademi
☛ When was Sangeet Natak Akademi established? → 1952

q: Which temple is known as 'black pagoda'?
qs.e: The Konark Sun Temple is famously known as the 'Black Pagoda'. Located in Odisha, India, it was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I. This temple is dedicated to the Sun God and is renowned for its unique architecture resembling a massive chariot with 12 wheels and seven horses. It has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The name 'Black Pagoda' originates from its dark stone construction, giving it a blackish appearance. The temple is a masterpiece of Kalinga architecture and attracts numerous tourists and devotees worldwide.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Konark Sun Temple located? → Odisha
☛ Which deity is the Konark Sun Temple dedicated to? → Sun God
☛ Which king built the Konark Sun Temple? → King Narasimhadeva I
☛ How many wheels does the Konark Sun Temple chariot have? → 12
☛ In which century was the Konark Sun Temple built? → 13th century

q: Which of the following pairs is correct?
qs.e: Tijara Mandir is an ancient Jain temple located in Alwar district of Rajasthan, dedicated to Lord Parshvanath. The Venkateswara Temple is in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, not Odisha. The Lingraj Temple is in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, not Madhya Pradesh. The Khajuraho Temple is in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, not Andhra Pradesh. Thus, only the pair Tijara Mandir-Rajasthan is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Venkateswara Temple → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Lingraj Temple → Odisha
☛ Tijara Mandir → Rajasthan
☛ Khajuraho Temple → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Tijara Mandir belongs to which religion? → Jainism

q: When were the caves of Bhimbetka discovered?
qs.e: The caves of Bhimbetka are located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. They were discovered in 1957-58 by Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar. This site provides significant evidence of prehistoric human life. The caves contain rock paintings from the Paleolithic to the Medieval period. Bhimbetka was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003. It is under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Bhimbetka located? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Who discovered Bhimbetka? → Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar
☛ When was Bhimbetka declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 2003
☛ How many caves are there in Bhimbetka? → About 750
☛ Which river is near Bhimbetka? → Betwa River

q: With which dancing form is the noted classical dancer Shovana Narayan associated?
qs.e: Shovana Narayan is a renowned Indian classical dancer associated with Kathak. She has given global recognition to this dance form. She is a recipient of the Padma Shri and represents the Jaipur Gharana of Kathak. She also served for many years in the Indian Administrative Service. Her style blends traditional elements with contemporary experimentation.
qs.kf:
☛ Shovana Narayan is associated with which dance form? → Kathak
☛ Which award was given to Shovana Narayan? → Padma Shri
☛ To which gharana does Shovana Narayan belong? → Jaipur Gharana
☛ Which service did Shovana Narayan serve in? → Indian Administrative Service
☛ Which state is the origin of Kathak dance? → Uttar Pradesh

q: To which of the following deities is the Dilwara Temple in Mount Abu dedicated?
qs.e: The Dilwara Temple located in Mount Abu is a renowned Jain pilgrimage site. This temple is dedicated to Adinath (also known as Rishabhadeva), the first Tirthankara of Jainism. The Dilwara Temple complex consists of five temples, the most prominent being the Vimal Vasahi Temple (dedicated to Adinath), the Luna Vasahi Temple (dedicated to Neminath), and others. These temples are world-famous for their exquisite marble carvings and architectural brilliance. They were built between the 11th and 13th centuries. This site is located in the Sirohi district of Rajasthan. The Dilwara Temples hold significance for both the Digambara and Svetambara sects of Jainism.
qs.kf:
☛ Which religion is Dilwara Temple associated with? → Jainism
☛ In which state is Dilwara Temple located? → Rajasthan
☛ Which stone is predominantly used in the construction of Dilwara Temple? → Marble
☛ To which Tirthankara is the Vimal Vasahi Temple dedicated? → Adinath
☛ In which district is Mount Abu situated? → Sirohi

q: Which of the following places is known for the world's largest Camel Fairs in India?
qs.e: Pushkar, located in Rajasthan, is famous for the world-renowned Pushkar Camel Fair. This fair is held around Kartik Purnima and attracts thousands of camels, horses, and other livestock for trading. It is one of the largest livestock fairs in India and draws tourists from around the world. Pushkar is also known for the Brahma Temple and Pushkar Lake. Other options: Jhalawar is known for its historical forts; Kolayat in Bikaner has a lake and fair, but the world record for the largest camel fair belongs to Pushkar. Gangapur is a small town.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Pushkar Camel Fair held? → Rajasthan, Pushkar
☛ When is the Pushkar Camel Fair held? → Kartik (October-November)
☛ Which lake is located in Pushkar? → Pushkar Lake (man-made)
☛ Which deity is the famous temple in Pushkar dedicated to? → Brahma
☛ Which is the largest livestock fair in India? → Pushkar Camel Fair

q: Which South Inida classical dance form literally means 'Story-Play'?
qs.e: Kathakali is a major classical dance form of Kerala. The term 'Kathakali' is derived from 'Katha' (story) and 'Kali' (play), literally meaning 'Story-Play'. This dance-drama style presents mythological stories through intricate facial expressions, hand gestures (mudras), and eye movements. Kathakali is characterized by elaborate costumes, colorful makeup, and rhythmic music. Bharatanatyam is a Tamil Nadu dance focused on expression and gestures. Kathak is a North Indian narrative dance, while Mohiniyattam is a graceful female-centric dance from Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the literal meaning of Kathakali? → Story-Play
☛ Which state is Kathakali from? → Kerala
☛ What are the main mediums of expression in Kathakali? → Mudras and eye movements
☛ How many major costume types are there in Kathakali? → Five (Pachcha, Kathi, Minukka, etc.)
☛ Who is considered the founder of Kathakali? → King Manavela (16th century)

name: Set 4 · Q139–184
sub: Static GK - Art, Culture, Music, Dance & Festivals

q: The Indian dance form "Manipuri' mostly portrays themes based on:
qs.e: Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India. It is primarily based on Raslila, depicting the love and devotion of Lord Krishna and the Gopis. This dance style originated from the state of Manipur. It features gentle movements, circular hand gestures, and restrained expressions. Traditional attire for women includes a loose skirt and veil. Manipuri dance is deeply influenced by the Vaishnava tradition, focusing on Krishna devotion. It highlights themes of love, devotion, and spirituality.
qs.kf:
☛ Main theme of Manipuri dance → Krishna-Gopis and Raslila
☛ Religion associated with Manipuri dance → Vaishnavism
☛ Primary instrument in Manipuri dance → Pung (drum)
☛ Place of origin of Manipuri dance → Manipur
☛ Manipuri dance's use of Natya Shastra → Not followed

q: 'Ugadi' is a festival celebrated in the Indian state of:
qs.e: Ugadi is primarily celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka. It marks the Telugu and Kannada New Year. The word 'Ugadi' means 'beginning of an era' and occurs on the first day of the Chaitra month according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar. People perform Panchanga Shravana (listening to the annual almanac) and prepare a special dish called Ugadi Pachadi, which is a mixture of six tastes. This festival also signifies the onset of spring.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state celebrates Ugadi as a major festival? → Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
☛ Ugadi marks which New Year? → Telugu and Kannada New Year
☛ In which month is Ugadi observed? → Chaitra month
☛ What is the special dish prepared on Ugadi? → Ugadi Pachadi
☛ What is the meaning of Ugadi? → Beginning of an era

q: The _____film "Koozhangal" has won the Tiger award at the 50th International Film Festival Rotterdam 2021.
qs.e: The film "Koozhangal" is a Tamil-language film that won the Tiger Award at the 50th International Film Festival Rotterdam 2021. This award is one of the most prestigious categories given in the competition section. The film was directed by P.S. Vinothraj and is based on domestic violence and social issues in a village in South India. The Rotterdam International Film Festival (IFFR) is one of Europe's leading film festivals, known for promoting independent and innovative cinema. "Koozhangal" gained international recognition for its storytelling and artistic presentation.
qs.kf:
☛ Language of "Koozhangal" film → Tamil
☛ Director's name → P.S. Vinothraj
☛ Award name → Tiger Award
☛ Film festival → 50th International Film Festival Rotterdam 2021
☛ Theme of film → Domestic violence and social issues

q: As per UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India, identify the incorrect pair as per the year of inclusion.
qs.e: Sanchi Stupa was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989, not 1988. Located in Madhya Pradesh, it is an important Buddhist monument built by Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. The other options are correctly paired: Red Fort Delhi (2007), Agra Fort (1983), and Fatehpur Sikri (1986). Sanchi Stupa is renowned for its stupas, sculptures, and gateways (toranas). It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.
qs.kf:
☛ UNESCO inscription year of Sanchi Stupa → 1989
☛ First UNESCO site in India → Agra Fort (1983)
☛ Red Fort Delhi inscription year → 2007
☛ Fatehpur Sikri inscription year → 1986
☛ Total UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India (2024) → 43

q: The ‘Sangai’ festival is celebrated in awhich of the following states of India?
qs.e: The Sangai festival is celebrated in the state of Manipur. This festival is organized to promote awareness and conservation of the Sangai deer, which is the state animal of Manipur and is found exclusively in the Loktak Lake region. The festival is held annually in the month of November and features cultural events, sports competitions, and environmental awareness activities. It showcases the rich cultural heritage of Manipur and emphasizes wildlife conservation.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Sangai festival celebrated? → Manipur
☛ Which state has the Sangai deer as its state animal? → Manipur
☛ Where is the Sangai deer found? → Loktak Lake, Manipur
☛ When is the Sangai festival celebrated? → November
☛ In which state is Loktak Lake located? → Manipur

q: Religious teacher Miyan Mir of the period between 1600 – 1700 belonged to:
qs.e: Miyan Mir (1550-1635) was a renowned Sufi saint associated with Lahore, Punjab. He belonged to the Qadiri order and was known for his religious tolerance. He played a significant role during the reign of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. He was a contemporary of Guru Arjan Dev (the fifth Sikh Guru) and had a cordial relationship with him. Miyan Mir laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar. Hence, he belonged to Punjab.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Sufi order was Miyan Mir associated with? → Qadiri
☛ Which temple foundation was laid by Miyan Mir? → Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)
☛ Which Mughal emperor was contemporary to Miyan Mir? → Jahangir and Shah Jahan
☛ With which Guru was Miyan Mir associated? → Guru Arjan Dev
☛ Which city is the birthplace of Miyan Mir? → Lahore

q: With which musical instrument is the noted musician Mrs. N. Rajam associated?
qs.e: Mrs. N. Rajam is a renowned violin player. She is considered the first woman to play the violin in the Hindustani classical music style. She established the violin in Hindustani classical music. She was trained by the great musicians of the Maihar gharana and gained international fame with her unique playing style. The violin is originally a Western instrument, but N. Rajam adapted it to Indian classical music. She has been honored with Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the famous violinist? → N. Rajam
☛ Which style of violin does N. Rajam play? → Hindustani classical music
☛ Which gharana is N. Rajam associated with? → Maihar gharana
☛ Which honors did N. Rajam receive? → Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan
☛ Who is credited with using the violin in Indian classical music? → N. Rajam

q: Where is the UNESCO world heritage site, Kandariya Mahadev temple located?
qs.e: Kandariya Mahadev temple is located in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was built by the Chandela dynasty in the 11th century and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple is renowned for its stunning architecture and intricate carvings. Among the Khajuraho group of Hindu and Jain temples, Kandariya Mahadev is the largest and most magnificent, standing about 31 meters tall with 84 shikharas (spires).
qs.kf:
☛ Which dynasty built Kandariya Mahadev temple? → Chandela dynasty
☛ What architectural style are Khajuraho temples built in? → Nagara style
☛ Which river flows near Khajuraho? → Ken River
☛ What was the capital of the Chandela dynasty? → Mahoba
☛ How many temples are there in Khajuraho? → About 25

q: With which musical instrument was the noted musician Ustad Bismillah Khan associated?
qs.e: Ustad Bismillah Khan was a renowned shehnai player from India. He was born in 1916 in Dumraon, Bihar. He elevated the shehnai to a place of importance in classical music. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001. He was a towering figure in Indian classical music.
qs.kf:
☛ Which instrument did Ustad Bismillah Khan play? → Shehnai
☛ Which highest civilian award did Ustad Bismillah Khan receive? → Bharat Ratna (2001)
☛ Where was Ustad Bismillah Khan born? → Dumraon, Bihar
☛ Who is credited with popularizing the shehnai in classical music? → Ustad Bismillah Khan
☛ What other major awards did Ustad Bismillah Khan receive? → Padma Shri (1961), Padma Bhushan (1968), Padma Vibhushan (1980)

q: The world's largest camel fair is held each October at __________ in Rajasthan.
qs.e: The Pushkar Camel Fair is the world's largest camel fair, held annually in October-November in Pushkar, Rajasthan. It takes place on the banks of Pushkar Lake and starts on Kartik Purnima. The fair lasts about a week and attracts thousands of camels for trading. It also features competitions like camel races, longest mustache contests, and folk dances. Pushkar is often called the 'city of fairs'. The fair is a major cultural event showcasing Rajasthan's heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ On the banks of which lake is Pushkar fair held? → Pushkar Lake
☛ In which month is Pushkar Camel Fair held? → October-November
☛ What is the other name of Pushkar Camel Fair? → Pushkar Mela
☛ Which is the largest animal fair in Rajasthan? → Pushkar Camel Fair
☛ Pushkar is located in which district? → Ajmer

q: In which of the following states are the Ellora caves located?
qs.e: The Ellora Caves are located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, India. These caves are associated with Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. There are 34 caves, with the most famous being the Kailash Temple (Cave 16), which is a massive monolithic structure carved out of a single rock. Ellora has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The caves were built during the rule of the Rashtrakuta, Pratihara, and Kalachuri dynasties.
qs.kf:
☛ How many caves are there in Ellora? → 34
☛ Which is the most famous cave in Ellora? → Kailash Temple (Cave 16)
☛ Which river is near Ellora Caves? → Karnataki River
☛ When were Ellora Caves built? → 6th to 10th century
☛ Which religion is not associated with Ellora? → Islam

q: Which of these festivals is celebrated with dances like Dandiya and Garba?
qs.e: Navratri is a major Hindu festival dedicated to the goddess Durga. It is celebrated with great enthusiasm across India, especially in Gujarat. During this festival, traditional folk dances like Garba and Dandiya are performed at night. Garba involves circular movements and clapping, while Dandiya is a stick dance using colorful sticks. These dances symbolize devotion to the goddess and celebrate her power. Navratri lasts for nine nights, followed by Dussehra. Among the other options, Baisakhi is a harvest festival of Punjab, Bihu is an Assamese festival, and Shivratri is dedicated to Lord Shiva. None of these feature Garba or Dandiya dances.
qs.kf:
☛ Which festival is associated with Dandiya and Garba dances? → Navratri
☛ Who is worshiped during Navratri? → Goddess Durga
☛ Which festival follows Navratri? → Dussehra
☛ What are the popular folk dances of Gujarat? → Garba and Dandiya
☛ Baisakhi is the main festival of which state? → Punjab

q: The traditional harvesting festival celebrated in Assam is-
qs.e: Bohag Bihu is the main harvesting festival of Assam, celebrated in mid-April marking the Assamese New Year. It lasts for three days and involves traditional dance, music, and feasting. Bihu is an integral part of Assamese culture. Pongal is a festival of Tamil Nadu, Tusu Parab is celebrated in Jharkhand and West Bengal, while Makar Sankranti is observed across India. Bohag Bihu is also known as Rongali Bihu and is the most joyous of the three Bihu festivals.
qs.kf:
☛ Which festival of Assam is related to harvest? → Bohag Bihu
☛ In which month is Bohag Bihu celebrated? → April
☛ Which festival marks the Assamese New Year? → Bohag Bihu
☛ Which traditional dance is performed during Bihu? → Bihu dance
☛ What are the three Bihu festivals of Assam? → Bohag, Kongali, Magh

q: Which of the following statements is/are true for the Carnatic Music in India? 1.Gitam is the simplest type of composition. 2.Khayal is a part of Carnatic Classical music. 3.Padas are scholarly compositions in Telugu and Tamil languages.
qs.e: Carnatic music is a major style of Indian classical music. Gitam is the simplest type of composition, often used for beginners with basic lyrics and raga. Padas are scholarly compositions in Telugu and Tamil languages, expressing devotion and complex themes. Khayal is not part of Carnatic music; it belongs to Hindustani classical music. Thus, only statements 1 and 3 are true.
qs.kf:
☛ Simplest composition in Carnatic music → Gitam
☛ Khayal belongs to which music system? → Hindustani classical music
☛ Languages of Padas in Carnatic music → Telugu and Tamil
☛ Scholarly Carnatic composition → Pada
☛ Difference between Hindustani and Carnatic → Khayal is Hindustani, not Carnatic

q: Which of the following is a form of folk music?
qs.e: Naworia-geet is a famous form of folk music from Madhya Pradesh, especially prevalent in the Bundelkhand and Nimar regions. These songs are primarily sung by farmers and laborers during strenuous work in fields or construction sites for entertainment and motivation. Group singing and rhythm play a significant role. Other options: Sufiana kalam is a classical music style, Bhand pather is a folk theatre or dance form, and Dhrupad is a major genre of classical music. Thus, only Naworia-geet is a pure form of folk music.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous folk music of Madhya Pradesh → Naworia-geet
☛ Naworia-geet sung by → Farmers and laborers
☛ Main region of Naworia-geet → Bundelkhand and Nimar
☛ Sufiana kalam belongs to which music → Classical music
☛ Dhrupad is a genre of which music → Classical music

q: To which Gharana did the renowned singer Girija Devi, known for her 'Thumri' renditions, belong?
qs.e: Girija Devi, famously known as the 'Queen of Thumri', was a renowned Indian classical vocalist. She belonged to the Benaras Gharana. The Benaras Gharana is a major school of Hindustani classical music, known for its renditions of Thumri, Bhajan, and Kajri. Girija Devi carried forward the traditions of this gharana and gave international recognition to Thumri singing. She was honored with prestigious awards like Padma Shri (1972) and Padma Bhushan (1989). The Benaras Gharana emphasizes bandish and bol-banao (embellishment of lyrics), and Girija Devi enriched this style with her captivating performances.
qs.kf:
☛ Major award associated with Girija Devi → Padma Shri (1972), Padma Bhushan (1989)
☛ Title of Girija Devi → Queen of Thumri
☛ Key style of Benaras Gharana → Thumri, Bhajan, Kajri
☛ Death of Girija Devi → 2017
☛ Birth of Girija Devi → 1929, Varanasi

q: Which of the following indigenous tribes celebrates the Mopin festival?
qs.e: The Mopin festival is celebrated by the Galo tribe in the state of Arunachal Pradesh, India. This festival is held after the harvest season and involves the worship of Mopin, the goddess of prosperity. It is celebrated in the month of April and includes traditional dances, songs, and community feasts. The Galo tribe is one of the major tribes of Arunachal Pradesh with a distinct cultural heritage. The purpose of the Mopin festival is to pray for prosperity and peace. This festival reflects the rich culture of India's diverse indigenous communities.
qs.kf:
☛ Tribe associated with Mopin festival → Galo
☛ State where Galo tribe resides → Arunachal Pradesh
☛ Deity worshipped in Mopin festival → Goddess of Prosperity (Mopin)
☛ Main purpose of Mopin festival → Prosperity and peace
☛ Time of Mopin festival celebration → April month

q: Which Carnatic vocalist was popularly known as the 'Nightingale of India'?
qs.e: MS Subbulakshmi was a renowned Carnatic vocalist, popularly known as the 'Nightingale of India'. She was born in 1916 in Madurai. She was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award. She mastered both Carnatic music and Meera bhajans. Her famous renditions include 'Vishnu Sahasranamam' and 'Bhaja Govindam'. She also performed at the United Nations. She passed away in 2004.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first musician to receive Bharat Ratna? → MS Subbulakshmi
☛ Who is known as the 'Nightingale of India'? → MS Subbulakshmi
☛ Which Carnatic vocalist was famous for Meera bhajans? → MS Subbulakshmi
☛ Who was the first Indian musician to perform at the United Nations? → MS Subbulakshmi
☛ Where was MS Subbulakshmi born? → Madurai

q: Onam festival is celebrated in which of the following states of India?
qs.e: Onam is the most significant and largest festival of the Indian state of Kerala. It is celebrated to welcome the legendary King Mahabali, whose spirit is believed to visit the state during this time. The festival features elaborate flower decorations called pookalam, traditional attire like the Onam sari, cultural performances, and a grand feast known as the Onam sadya. Onam falls in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August-September). Kerala is known for its rich culture and traditions, and Onam exemplifies this heritage. The other options—Maharashtra, Arunachal Pradesh, and Gujarat—do not celebrate Onam as their primary festival.
qs.kf:
☛ Biggest festival of Kerala → Onam
☛ Onam is celebrated in honour of which king? → King Mahabali
☛ What is the flower decoration called during Onam? → Pookalam
☛ Onam falls in which Malayalam month? → Chingam
☛ Classical dance forms of Kerala → Kathakali and Mohiniyattam

q: Which of the following compositions reflects the devotional form of Carnatic music?
qs.e: Devara Nama is a devotional composition in Carnatic music, dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is composed in the Kannada language and sung by the 'Haridasa' saints. This style incorporates devotion, philosophy and moral teachings. Alha and Pandavani are folk song styles from North India, while Hori is associated with Holi. The main purpose of Carnatic music is to express devotion and spirituality towards God, and Devara Nama reflects this tradition.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language is Devara Nama composed? → Kannada
☛ To which god is Devara Nama dedicated? → Shiva
☛ Alha songs are associated with which region? → Uttar Pradesh/Bihar
☛ Pandavani style is based on which epic? → Mahabharata
☛ Hori is associated with which festival? → Holi

q: Which of the following musical forms is intimately related to classical Carnatic music?
qs.e: Gitam is a fundamental and ancient form of Carnatic music, mentioned in texts like Sangeeta Ratnakara. It is a simple, rhythmic composition that combines lyrics and raga. Gitam is used for initial training and is a hallmark of Carnatic music. Wanvun, Bhand Pather, and Firdost are associated with Kashmiri, Kashmiri folk, and Central Asian folk music respectively, not with classical Carnatic music.
qs.kf:
☛ Simplest composition type in Carnatic music → Gitam
☛ Primary use of Gitam → For beginners practice
☛ Ancient text mentioning Gitam → Sangeeta Ratnakara
☛ Language of Gitam composition → Telugu, Sanskrit, Kannada
☛ Other forms of Carnatic music → Varnam, Kirthanam

q: Who among the following was a classical Hindustani singer?
qs.e: Begum Akhtar (1914-1974) was a renowned classical Hindustani singer, known as the 'Mallika-e-Ghazal' (Queen of Ghazals). She specialized in ghazal, dadra, and thumri styles. In contrast, MS Subbulakshmi and V Sheshanna were associated with Carnatic classical music, while TK Iyengar was a violinist in the Carnatic tradition. Begum Akhtar was awarded the Padma Shri in 1968 and the Padma Bhushan posthumously in 1975. She was one of the few female Hindustani classical singers to popularize the ghazal style. Her deep, emotive voice and expressive style made her an enduring icon in Indian classical music.
qs.kf:
☛ By which title is Begum Akhtar known? → Mallika-e-Ghazal
☛ In which year did Begum Akhtar receive the Padma Shri? → 1968
☛ Which music style is Begum Akhtar associated with? → Hindustani classical music (ghazal, thumri, dadra)
☛ MS Subbulakshmi is associated with which musical tradition? → Carnatic classical music
☛ For which instrument is TK Iyengar famous? → Violin (Carnatic music)

q: The stone used for the construction of the Basilica of Bom Jesus in Goa was brought from which of the following places?
qs.e: The Basilica of Bom Jesus in Goa is a famous church built in the 16th century. The stone used for its construction was brought from Bassein (Vasai), which is now in Maharashtra. Bassein was part of the Portuguese colony at that time and was known for its stone. The basilica is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and houses the remains of St. Francis Xavier. It is an excellent example of Portuguese Baroque architecture. Other options like Hamirpur, Jaipur, and Gaya are not related. Thus, the correct answer is Bassein.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Basilica of Bom Jesus located? → Goa
☛ Whose relics are kept in the Basilica of Bom Jesus? → St. Francis Xavier
☛ What architectural style is the Basilica of Bom Jesus? → Portuguese Baroque
☛ In which year was the Basilica of Bom Jesus declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1986
☛ What is the present name of Bassein? → Vasai

q: Mopin Festival is celebrated in which state of India?
qs.e: Mopin Festival is a major agricultural festival celebrated by the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. It is observed to ensure a good harvest and prosperity. The festival involves traditional dances, music, and rituals. The main ritual is the worship of Goddess Mopin Impi, who is believed to be the deity of grain and wealth. This festival is celebrated in the month of April.
qs.kf:
☛ Which tribe celebrates the Mopin Festival? → Galo tribe
☛ In which state is the Mopin Festival celebrated? → Arunachal Pradesh
☛ In which season is the Mopin Festival celebrated? → Spring (April)
☛ Which goddess is worshipped during Mopin Festival? → Goddess Mopin Impi
☛ On what basis is the Mopin Festival celebrated? → Agriculture and harvest

q: Which musical instrument is commonly associated with Rajasthani folk music?
qs.e: Morchang is a traditional Rajasthani folk musical instrument commonly associated with the folk music of Rajasthan. It is a type of mouth harp or Jew's harp that is placed in the mouth and played by plucking a metal tongue. Morchang is widely used in Rajasthani folk songs and dances like Ghoomar and Gair. Tabla is a classical instrument, Shehnai is an auspicious wind instrument, and Dholak is also popular but not specifically tied to Rajasthan as Morchang is. Therefore, Morchang is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the state instrument of Rajasthan? → Morchang
☛ What type of instrument is Morchang? → Wind instrument (mouth harp)
☛ Which instrument is used in Gair dance? → Dhol and Morchang
☛ What metal is used in Morchang? → Iron or brass
☛ Where did Morchang originate? → Rajasthan

q: Who among the following renowned musicians is celebrated for popularising the unique instrument known as the 'Sarod' and is considered one of the most famous maestros of the Senia Shahjahanpur gharana?
qs.e: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a world-renowned Sarod player who popularised this instrument globally. He belongs to the sixth generation of the Senia Shahjahanpur gharana. His father, Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan, was also a famous Sarod maestro. Amjad Ali Khan introduced innovations in Sarod playing and composed several new ragas like Madhukant and Shivkant. He has been honoured with Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan. He is also the founder of the Amjad Ali Khan Sarod Foundation.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous Sarod player of Senia gharana → Ustad Amjad Ali Khan
☛ Major awards received by Amjad Ali Khan → Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan
☛ Category of Sarod instrument → String instrument
☛ Ragas composed by Amjad Ali Khan → Madhukant, Shivkant
☛ Origin of Senia Shahjahanpur gharana → Descendants of Mian Tansen

q: Who among the following Carnatic music composers is known for his compositional contributions in Telugu and Sanskrit languages, particularly in praise of Lord Rama?
qs.e: Tyagaraja is one of the Trinity of Carnatic music, known for his compositions primarily in Telugu and Sanskrit languages. He wrote hundreds of kirtanas and musical compositions in praise of Lord Rama, showcasing deep devotion and musical brilliance. His works like 'Endaro Mahanubhavulu' and 'Evari Mata' are classics. Tyagaraja is revered as a 'Rama Bhakta' and his contributions have enriched Carnatic music. His compositions remain widely performed and studied.
qs.kf:
☛ Tyagaraja's major composition → 'Pancharatna Kriti'
☛ Language of Tyagaraja's works → Telugu and Sanskrit
☛ Tyagaraja's patron deity → Lord Rama
☛ Carnatic music Trinity → Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri
☛ Instrument associated with Tyagaraja → Tambura

q: The term ‘Pallavi’ relates to the first or the second thematic lines of the composition in which of the following music?
qs.e: In Carnatic music, a composition typically has three main sections: Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam. The Pallavi is the first section, presenting the main theme of the composition. It is followed by the Anupallavi, which develops the theme further, often in higher registers. The Charanam is the final section, which may incorporate phrases from the Pallavi and Anupallavi. This structure is distinct from Hindustani music. Pallavi literally means 'sprout' or 'beginning', reflecting its role as the opening part. Carnatic music is a system of classical music from South India, known for its intricate compositions called kritis. The Pallavi is a crucial element in Carnatic concerts, especially in ragam-tanam-pallavi renditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Sections of Carnatic composition → Pallavi, Anupallavi, Charanam
☛ Pallavi position → First part of the composition
☛ Anupallavi → Second part, often in higher notes
☛ Charanam → Final section, may repeat Pallavi and Anupallavi phrases
☛ Meaning of Pallavi → Sprout or beginning

q: The traditional folk music of Uttar Pradesh, featuring soulful melodies and often performed during weddings and festive occasions, is known as:
qs.e: The traditional folk music of Uttar Pradesh is Kajari, which is primarily sung during the month of Saawan. Known for its soulful melodies, it is often performed at weddings and festive occasions. Kajari songs express themes of nature, love, and separation. It is prominently sung in Mirzapur, Varanasi, and other parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. Maand is the folk music of Rajasthan, Baul of West Bengal, and Panihari of Rajasthan and Malwa regions. Hence, Kajari is an integral part of Uttar Pradesh's cultural heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous folk music of Uttar Pradesh → Kajari
☛ In which month is Kajari sung? → Saawan
☛ Folk music of Rajasthan → Maand
☛ Folk music of West Bengal → Baul
☛ Panihari is folk music of which region? → Rajasthan and Malwa

q: Bhajan Lal Sharma took oath on 15 December 2023 as the Chief Minister of which of the following states of India?
qs.e: Bhajan Lal Sharma took oath as the Chief Minister of Rajasthan on 15 December 2023. He is a leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The swearing-in ceremony was held in Jaipur. Before him, Ashok Gehlot served as Chief Minister. In the 2023 assembly elections, the BJP won a majority, and Bhajan Lal Sharma was chosen as Chief Minister. He is an MLA from the Bayana Assembly constituency. Bhajan Lal Sharma was born on 2 October 1967. He is the 23rd Chief Minister of Rajasthan.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the current Chief Minister of Rajasthan? → Bhajan Lal Sharma (since December 2023)
☛ Which party does Bhajan Lal Sharma belong to? → Bharatiya Janata Party
☛ Which constituency does Bhajan Lal Sharma represent? → Bayana
☛ Who was the 22nd Chief Minister of Rajasthan? → Ashok Gehlot
☛ When was Bhajan Lal Sharma born? → 2 October 1967

q: Who was the first musician from Asia to be honoured with the Ramon Magsaysay Award for contributions to Carnatic music?
qs.e: MS Subbulakshmi was a renowned Carnatic vocalist. She was honored with the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1974, becoming the first Asian musician to receive this prestigious award. She received the award under the category of 'Public Service'. She was also the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award. Her contributions to Carnatic music brought it global recognition. Her voice was often described as divine. The Ramon Magsaysay Award is considered the 'Nobel Prize of Asia'.
qs.kf:
☛ First Asian musician to receive Ramon Magsaysay Award? → MS Subbulakshmi
☛ Year of MS Subbulakshmi's Ramon Magsaysay Award? → 1974
☛ Year of MS Subbulakshmi's Bharat Ratna? → 1998
☛ Ramon Magsaysay Award is from which country? → Philippines
☛ MS Subbulakshmi is associated with which music genre? → Carnatic music

q: Which of the following styles of Thumri singing is meant to be fairly slow and staid?
qs.e: Thumri is a semi-classical vocal form in Hindustani classical music. The Benaras gharana is known for its slow, staid, and expressive style of Thumri singing. It employs techniques like bol-banav and bol-bant to bring out the emotional depth of the lyrics. In contrast, the Punjab gharana Thumri is faster and more vigorous, while the Agra gharana is more influenced by Dhrupad. Assam does not have a distinct Thumri style. Benarasi Thumri emphasizes themes of love and separation and is typically sung in a slow tempo. This style developed under the patronage of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah and shows influences of Kathak dance. Its measured, emotive delivery makes it distinctly different from other Thumri styles.
qs.kf:
☛ Thumri's Benaras gharana → Known for slow and staid singing style.
☛ Techniques used in Benarasi Thumri → Bol-banav and bol-bant.
☛ Other Thumri gharanas → Punjab (fast), Agra (Dhrupad-influenced).
☛ Historical patron of Benarasi Thumri → Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.
☛ Main emotions in Benarasi Thumri → Love and separation.

q: 'Nada' is a musical sound in the Carnatic Classical Music, which is of two kinds; 'Ahata' and '_______'
qs.e: In Carnatic classical music, 'Nada' refers to musical sound. It is classified into two types: Ahata and Anahata. Ahata Nada is the sound produced through a musical instrument or vocal cords, involving physical vibration such as strings or membranes. It is audible and results from physical action. In contrast, Anahata Nada is the internal sound that occurs without any physical vibration. It requires meditation and inner concentration to perceive. This concept is considered the basis of spiritual music and is associated with the idea of 'Nada Brahma' (sound as divine). Therefore, the correct option is Anahata.
qs.kf:
☛ What are the two types of Nada? → Ahata and Anahata
☛ How is Ahata Nada produced? → Through instruments or vocal cords
☛ What is Anahata Nada? → Internal sound without physical vibration
☛ What is the meaning of 'Nada' in Carnatic music? → Musical sound
☛ What is needed to hear Anahata Nada? → Meditation and concentration

q: Who among the following was the Architect of the building 'St. Francis Church' in Kochi?
qs.e: The St. Francis Church in Kochi is the oldest European church in India, built by the Portuguese in 1503. Its architect was Pedro Alvarez De Cabral, a Portuguese navigator and explorer who discovered Brazil and played a key role in establishing Portuguese colonies in India. The church is located in the Fort Kochi area of Kochi and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its walls feature ancient frescoes and historical artifacts. The church also holds the tomb of Vasco da Gama, who was originally buried there before his remains were taken to Portugal.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the oldest European church in India? → St. Francis Church, Kochi
☛ When was St. Francis Church built? → In 1503
☛ Who was the architect of St. Francis Church? → Pedro Alvarez De Cabral
☛ Which country did Pedro Alvarez De Cabral belong to? → Portugal
☛ Where is St. Francis Church located? → Fort Kochi, Kochi

q: Who among the following is related to ‘khayal’ in classical Hindustani music?
qs.e: Amir Khusrau (1253-1325) was a renowned Sufi poet and musician, credited with the invention of the khayal style of singing. Khayal is a major genre of Hindustani classical music, which developed in North India. Amir Khusrau combined Persian and Indian musical traditions to create forms like khayal, tarana, and qawwali. He lived under the patronage of Delhi Sultanate rulers and is often called the father of Indian music. The other options: Ziauddin Barani (historian), Abu'l Hasan al Hujwiri (Sufi saint), and Amir Hasan Sijzi (Sufi scholar) are not related to khayal.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the originator of khayal style? → Amir Khusrau
☛ Khayal is a genre of which classical music? → Hindustani classical music
☛ Who invented the tarana style? → Amir Khusrau
☛ Who is credited with inventing the sitar? → Amir Khusrau
☛ Which Sufi saint was the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya? → Amir Khusrau

q: When was St. Francis Church building constructed in Kochi?
qs.e: The St. Francis Church in Kochi was built in 1503. It is the oldest European church in India, constructed by the Portuguese. Located in the Fort Kochi area, it was originally known as St. Bartholomew Church and later renamed St. Francis Church. Its historical significance also lies in the fact that Vasco da Gama, who died in Kochi in 1524, was initially buried in this church before his remains were taken to Portugal. The church symbolizes the arrival of Christian missionaries and Portuguese colonialism in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest European church in India → St. Francis Church, Kochi
☛ Year of construction of St. Francis Church → 1503
☛ Location of the church → Fort Kochi, Kerala
☛ Who was buried in this church → Vasco da Gama
☛ Original name of the church → St. Bartholomew Church

q: Who among the following historical musicians is credited with formulating the Sarali Varisa and Sapta Tala Alankaras in the Carnatic Music?
qs.e: Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) is regarded as the father (Pitamaha) of Carnatic music. He formulated the Sarali Varisa (basic exercises) and Sapta Tala Alankaras (rhythmic patterns) to systematize music education. These compositions help beginners develop understanding of notes and rhythm. Purandara Dasa laid the foundation of Carnatic music, and his contributions are still recognized in music pedagogy. Among the other options, Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Annamacharya are also great composers, but Purandara Dasa is the originator of these fundamental exercises.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of Carnatic music? → Purandara Dasa
☛ Who composed Sarali Varisa? → Purandara Dasa
☛ Who created Sapta Tala Alankaras? → Purandara Dasa
☛ When was Purandara Dasa born? → 1484
☛ When did Purandara Dasa die? → 1564

q: Who among the following exceptional musicians, unable to complete formal schooling, emerged as a musical genius and innovator, credited with inventing the Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi, and Navamukhi ragas?
qs.e: M Balamuralikrishna was a legendary Carnatic vocalist, instrumentalist, and composer. Despite not completing formal schooling, he emerged as a musical genius and innovator. He is credited with inventing new ragas such as Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi, and Navamukhi. These ragas are multi-faceted and bring novelty to music. He also created new talas. His compositions are in Telugu, Sanskrit, and other languages. Balamuralikrishna received honors like Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous Carnatic vocalist → M Balamuralikrishna
☛ Inventor of new ragas → Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi, Navamukhi
☛ Major honors → Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan
☛ Language → Compositions in Telugu, Sanskrit
☛ Other contributions → Created new talas

q: Which of the following states is known for the dance form Jhoori which is connected with Jhoomar and involves both men and women singing and dancing?
qs.e: The Jhoori dance is a folk dance of Himachal Pradesh associated with Jhoomar. It is performed during weddings and festivals, where both men and women sing and dance together. This dance is popular in the districts of Kullu, Mandi, and Sirmaur. The songs in Jhoori are based on love, romance, and social themes, similar to the vibrant and participatory nature of Jhoomar. Among the other options, Punjab is known for Bhangra, Assam for Bihu, and Rajasthan for Ghoomar.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dance of Himachal Pradesh is related to Jhoomar? → Jhoori
☛ Who participates in Jhoori dance? → Both men and women
☛ In which districts is Jhoori dance mainly performed? → Kullu, Mandi, Sirmaur
☛ Which is the most famous folk dance of Himachal Pradesh? → Nati
☛ Which is the popular dance of Punjab? → Bhangra

q: Which of the following is NOT a Gharana of classical Hindustani music?
qs.e: In Hindustani classical music, Gharanas refer to distinct musical traditions and styles. The Agra Gharana, Gwalior Gharana, and Kirana Gharana are prominent Hindustani Gharanas. The Thanjavur Gharana, however, is actually a major Gharana of Carnatic music, a system of classical music from South India, associated with the Thanjavur region in Tamil Nadu. It is not part of Hindustani music. Some other well-known Hindustani Gharanas include Patiala, Maihar, Benares, Jaipur- Atrauli, and Rampur-Sahaswan. Thus, the correct answer is Thanjavur Gharana.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest Gharana of Hindustani music → Gwalior Gharana
☛ Gharana known for Khayal gayaki → Kirana Gharana
☛ Gharana associated with Dhrupad style → Agra Gharana
☛ Major Gharana of Carnatic music → Thanjavur Gharana
☛ Period when Gharana system emerged → 16th century

q: Known for its rich cultural heritage, which of the following is India's first UNESCO 'City of Literature'?
qs.e: Kozhikode (formerly Calicut), a coastal city in Kerala, was declared India's first UNESCO 'City of Literature' in 2023. Known for its rich literary and cultural heritage, the city has a long history of Malayalam literature, with many renowned writers and poets. It received this recognition under the UNESCO Creative Cities Network, which acknowledges cities worldwide for their outstanding contributions in fields like literature, music, film, arts, crafts, design, and gastronomy. This achievement highlights Kozhikode's literary tradition and cultural vibrancy.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first UNESCO City of Literature → Kozhikode
☛ Kozhikode is located in which state? → Kerala
☛ How many categories are there in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network? → 7 (Literature, Music, Film, Arts, Crafts, Design, Gastronomy)
☛ What was the former name of Kozhikode? → Calicut
☛ Which was India's first UNESCO Creative City? → Jaipur (for Crafts & Folk Arts)

q: Which of the following is NOT part of India's 12 forts nominated for UNESCO World Heritage under the title 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India' for 2024-25?
qs.e: For the 2024-25 UNESCO World Heritage nomination, India has proposed the 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India', which includes 12 forts that represent the military architecture and strategic importance of the Maratha Empire. The nominated forts include Raigad (the capital of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj), Salher (the highest Maratha fort), and Rajgad (the first capital of the Maratha Empire). Karnala Fort, located in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, is a hill fort but is not part of this list. UNESCO submitted the Maratha Military Landscapes as a serial nomination, covering a group of 12 forts that showcase Maratha military prowess. Therefore, Karnala Fort is not among them.
qs.kf:
☛ How many forts from India are nominated for UNESCO World Heritage 2024-25 under Maratha Military Landscapes? → 12
☛ A key fort included in the Maratha Military Landscapes → Raigad
☛ A key fort included in the Maratha Military Landscapes → Rajgad
☛ A key fort included in the Maratha Military Landscapes → Salher
☛ What is the title of the UNESCO nomination? → 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India'

q: Who among the following developed the notation system for Hindustani classical music?
qs.e: Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande (1860-1936) developed the standardized notation system for Hindustani classical music. He systematized the theoretical aspects of Indian music and authored a series of books called 'Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati'. His notation system represented notes using syllables (sa, re, ga, ma, pa, dha, ni) and employed symbols for octaves. He also classified numerous ragas and created the 'thaat' system, grouping ragas into 10 parent scales. Bhatkhande founded the Marwar Music College and received the title 'Sangeetacharya'.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of Hindustani music notation? → Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande
☛ When was Bhatkhande born? → 1860
☛ How many thaats did Bhatkhande classify? → 10
☛ Which institution did Bhatkhande establish? → Marwar Music College
☛ Bhatkhande's famous book series? → Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati

q: The Rudra Veena is predominantly associated with which genre of Hindustani music?
qs.e: The Rudra Veena is an ancient Indian string instrument, predominantly associated with the Dhrupad genre of Hindustani classical music. Dhrupad is considered the oldest form of Hindustani music, characterized by solemn, slow compositions. The deep and resonant sound of the Rudra Veena complements the meditative nature of Dhrupad, making it a favored instrument in this style. The instrument consists of two large resonating gourds attached to a long hollow tube with metal frets and strings. Historically, it was used in temples and royal courts. Today, the Rudra Veena continues to be taught in the Beenkar tradition and is exclusively used for Dhrupad performances.
qs.kf:
☛ Which genre of Hindustani music is Rudra Veena associated with? → Dhrupad
☛ What is the primary instrument used in Dhrupad? → Rudra Veena
☛ What is a Rudra Veena player called? → Beenkar
☛ Which is the oldest form of Hindustani classical music? → Dhrupad
☛ How many gourds does a Rudra Veena have? → Two

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1
q: The female counterpart of the male Bhangra is called:
qs.e: Bhangra is a famous male folk dance from Punjab, traditionally performed during the harvest season. Its female counterpart is Giddha, also a folk dance of Punjab. In Giddha, women wear colorful attire and perform with claps and songs, symbolizing joy and celebration. It is commonly performed at festivals and weddings. Among the other options, Ghoomar is from Rajasthan, Kalbelia is from the Kalbelia community of Rajasthan, and Garba is from Gujarat. Hence, the female counterpart of male Bhangra is Giddha.
qs.kf:
☛ Bhangra is the folk dance of which state? → Punjab
☛ Giddha is the folk dance of which state? → Punjab
☛ Ghoomar is the folk dance of which state? → Rajasthan
☛ Kalbelia is the dance of which community? → Kalbelia community of Rajasthan
☛ Garba is the folk dance of which state? → Gujarat

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1
q: In which of the following dance forms vocal music is not used?
qs.e: Chhau is a major folk dance form from West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha. This dance style is primarily based on martial arts and theatrical presentation, using instrumental music but no vocal music. In contrast, Bharatanatyam, Odissi, and Kathak are classical dances that regularly incorporate vocal music. Chhau uses instruments like dhol, nagara, and shehnai. It often depicts heroic tales and mythological stories. The dance is performed during festivals like Chaitra Parva.
qs.kf:
☛ Main instrument used in Chhau? → Dhol
☛ Types of Chhau dance? → Seraikela, Purulia, Mayurbhanj
☛ Which dance requires masks? → Chhau
☛ Is vocal music used in Chhau? → No
☛ States associated with Chhau? → West Bengal, Jharkhand, Odisha
