☛ Location of Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre → Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala

q: Which place was called the “nursery of the Bengal army"?
qs.e: Awadh was called the 'nursery of the Bengal army'. During the British rule, most soldiers recruited into the Bengal Army came from the Awadh region. This area was known for its fertile land and martial skills. The British East India Company preferred to recruit farmers and landlords from Awadh as soldiers. Before the revolt of 1857, Awadh was the largest recruitment area for the Bengal Army. The sepoys recruited from here were considered disciplined and loyal. This tradition continued even after the annexation of Awadh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which place was called the nursery of the Bengal army? → Awadh
☛ What was the largest recruitment area for the Bengal Army before the 1857 revolt? → Awadh
☛ When was Awadh annexed by the British? → 1856
☛ What was the capital of Awadh? → Lucknow
☛ Which castes were predominant in the Bengal Army? → Brahmins and Rajputs

q: The first chairman of ISRO was:
qs.e: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established in 1969. The first chairman of ISRO was Dr Vikram Sarabhai, who is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme. He founded the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) in 1962, which later evolved into ISRO. Dr Vikram Sarabhai's contributions to space science and technology are unparalleled. His efforts made India a serious spacefaring nation. Prof Satish Dhawan later became the chairman of ISRO, and Dr K Kasturirangan and Prof UR Rao were also prominent scientists.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first chairman of ISRO? → Dr Vikram Sarabhai
☛ When was INCOSPAR established? → 1962
☛ When was ISRO established? → 1969
☛ Who is known as the father of the Indian space programme? → Dr Vikram Sarabhai
☛ Who succeeded Dr Vikram Sarabhai as chairman of ISRO? → Prof Satish Dhawan

q: As of October 2020, who is the CEO of Google?
qs.e: As of October 2020, the CEO of Google was Sunder Pichai. He became CEO of Google in August 2015 when the company restructured under Alphabet. He is also the CEO of Alphabet, Google's parent company. Sunder Pichai was born in Chennai, India and earned a degree in Metallurgical Engineering from IIT Kharagpur. He later earned an M.S. from Stanford University and an MBA from Wharton School. He joined Google in 2004 and played a key role in developing several major products including the Chrome browser, Chrome OS, and Android.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the current CEO of Google? → Sunder Pichai
☛ Who is the CEO of Alphabet Inc.? → Sunder Pichai
☛ When did Sunder Pichai become CEO of Google? → August 2015
☛ Where was Sunder Pichai born? → Chennai, India
☛ Where did Sunder Pichai earn his MBA? → Wharton School

q: Which of the following Indian pairs has won the Miss Universe title?
qs.e: India has won the Miss Universe title twice. The first Indian to win was Sushmita Sen in 1994, and the second was Lara Dutta in 2000. Lara Dutta later became a Bollywood actress. Sushmita Sen also worked in films and is known for her fitness. Other Indian beauty queens like Aishwarya Rai (Miss World 1994) and Diana Hayden (Miss World 1997) have won Miss World, not Miss Universe. Reita Faria won Miss World in 1966. Thus, only two Indian women have won Miss Universe: Sushmita Sen and Lara Dutta.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Indian Miss Universe? → Sushmita Sen (1994)
☛ Who was the second Indian Miss Universe? → Lara Dutta (2000)
☛ Who won Miss Universe 2023? → Sheynnis Palacios (Nicaragua)
☛ How many times has India won Miss World? → 6 times
☛ After 1994, when did India next win Miss Universe? → 2000 by Lara Dutta

q: Which of the following was founded by Sir Stamford Raffles?
qs.e: Sir Stamford Raffles was a British statesman and official of the East India Company. He founded Singapore in 1819, which became a major trading hub and British colony. Raffles developed Singapore as a strategic port on the Strait of Malacca. His contributions were crucial in shaping Singapore into a modern and prosperous city-state. Among the options, only Singapore is associated with Raffles. Hong Kong was colonized by Britain in 1841, Mumbai was acquired from the Portuguese, and Kuala Lumpur was founded in 1857.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded Singapore? → Sir Stamford Raffles
☛ Which company was Raffles associated with? → British East India Company
☛ Year of Singapore's founding → 1819
☛ On which strait is Singapore located? → Strait of Malacca
☛ Which museum did Raffles establish? → Raffles Museum (now National Museum of Singapore)

q: Who started the first Topographical Survey in India?
qs.e: The first Topographical Survey in India was started by Major James Rennel. He was the Surveyor General of the British East India Company and conducted the survey of Bengal and Bihar from 1767 to 1777. His work was published as the 'Bengal Atlas', which was the first scientific map of India. Later, William Lambton started the Great Trigonometrical Survey, but the beginning of the topographical survey is credited to James Rennel.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Surveyor General of India? → Major James Rennel
☛ Who published the Bengal Atlas? → Major James Rennel
☛ Who started the Great Trigonometrical Survey? → William Lambton
☛ When did the first topographical survey in India begin? → 1767
☛ Under which survey was Mount Everest's height measured? → Great Trigonometrical Survey

q: Who was the secretary of UNO between the year 1997-2006?
qs.e: From 1997 to 2006, the seventh Secretary-General of the United Nations was Kofi Annan. He was a citizen of Ghana and the first African to serve as Secretary-General, completing two terms (1997-2006). During his tenure, the UN focused on peacekeeping, human rights, and the Millennium Development Goals. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001. Before him, Boutros Boutros-Ghali served (1992-1996), and after him, Ban Ki-moon (2007-2016) took office.
qs.kf:
☛ First African UN Secretary-General → Kofi Annan
☛ Kofi Annan's term → 1997-2006
☛ Kofi Annan received Nobel Peace Prize → 2001
☛ Secretary-General after Kofi Annan → Ban Ki-moon
☛ Kofi Annan's nationality → Ghana

q: Who was the second person to land on the moon?
qs.e: The first person to land on the moon was Neil Armstrong, who stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission. The second person was Buzz Aldrin, who landed on the moon in the same mission. Aldrin and Armstrong spent about 2.5 hours on the lunar surface, while Michael Collins orbited the moon in the command module. Buzz Aldrin played a key role in planting the American flag and conducting scientific experiments on the moon. Charles Conrad was the third person on Apollo 12, Alan Shepard the fifth on Apollo 14, and Alan Bean the fourth on Apollo 12.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first person to walk on the moon? → Neil Armstrong
☛ Who was the command module pilot of Apollo 11? → Michael Collins
☛ Who was the third person to land on the moon? → Charles Conrad
☛ In which year was the Apollo 11 mission launched? → 1969
☛ What is Buzz Aldrin's full name? → Edwin Eugene Aldrin Jr.

q: Who among the following scaled Mount Everest 24 times and set a world record?
qs.e: Kami Rita Sherpa scaled Mount Everest 24 times, setting a world record. He is a Nepali Sherpa who first reached the summit of Everest in 1994. Most of his ascents have been during the spring season. Born in 1970 in the Solukhumbu district, his father was also a Sherpa guide who died in an Everest accident in 1992. Kami Rita Sherpa holds the record for the most climbs of Everest. This achievement is a significant milestone in mountaineering history.
qs.kf:
☛ Record for most Everest ascents → Kami Rita Sherpa
☛ Person who climbed Everest 24 times → Kami Rita Sherpa
☛ Kami Rita Sherpa's birth year → 1970
☛ Kami Rita Sherpa's birthplace → Solukhumbu district, Nepal
☛ Height of Mount Everest → 8,848 meters

q: Who among the following artists is NOT a painter?
qs.e: Rukmini Devi was a renowned classical dancer and choreographer, especially in Bharatanatyam. She played a vital role in reviving Indian arts and founded the Kalakshetra Foundation, but she was not a painter. In contrast, Amrita Sher-Gil was a pioneering painter, often called 'India's Frida Kahlo'. Nandalal Bose was a prominent painter and a disciple of Rabindranath Tagore, who modernized Indian miniature painting. Jamini Roy was a celebrated painter who drew inspiration from folk art, particularly Bengali motifs. Rukmini Devi's contribution lies in dance, not painting.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dancer is famous for Bharatanatyam? → Rukmini Devi
☛ What was Amrita Sher-Gil's main art form? → Painting
☛ Who was Nandalal Bose a disciple of? → Rabindranath Tagore
☛ Which style did Jamini Roy adopt in painting? → Folk art
☛ Which institution did Rukmini Devi establish? → Kalakshetra Foundation

q: The first woman of Indian origin to travel into space was:
qs.e: Kalpana Chawla was the first woman of Indian origin to travel to space. She was born in 1962 in Karnal, Haryana. She earned a degree in aeronautical engineering from Punjab Engineering College and later moved to the US for advanced studies. She went to space in 1997 as a mission specialist on the Space Shuttle Columbia. Tragically, she died in the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003. Sunita Williams is another astronaut of Indian origin, but Kalpana Chawla was the first. Her contributions to space exploration are remembered worldwide.
qs.kf:
☛ First woman of Indian origin in space → Kalpana Chawla
☛ First Indian woman in space → Kalpana Chawla (Indian origin)
☛ Birthplace of Kalpana Chawla → Karnal, Haryana
☛ Missions flown by Kalpana Chawla → STS-87 (1997) and STS-107 (2003)
☛ Space Shuttle Columbia disaster date → February 1, 2003

q: An additional margin added to a page layout to compensate for the part of the paper made unusable by the binding process is called:
qs.e: Gutter margin is the extra space added to the inner edge of a page to compensate for the part of the paper that becomes unusable due to the binding process (such as stapling, spiral binding, or gluing). This margin ensures that the text or images are not cut off or hidden after binding. It is especially important in books, magazines, and multi-page documents. Most print and layout software (e.g., MS Word, Adobe InDesign) provides gutter margin settings. It is sometimes also called binding margin.
qs.kf:
☛ Purpose of gutter margin → Compensate for unusable paper due to binding
☛ Where is gutter margin added → To the inner edge of the page
☛ Other name for gutter margin → Binding margin
☛ Where gutter margin is used → Books, magazines, multi-page documents
☛ Software providing gutter margin setting → MS Word, Adobe InDesign, etc.

q: Who was the 1st Indian to be elected to the leadership of Communist International?
qs.e: Manabendra Nath Roy (1887-1954) was an Indian revolutionary and communist leader. He was the first Indian to be elected to the leadership of the Communist International (Comintern). He played a key role in founding the Communist Party of India in Tashkent in 1920. He became a member of the Comintern's Executive Committee and worked to spread communism in Asia. Roy authored several articles on nationalism and anti-imperialism. Later, he broke from Marxism and developed the philosophy of Radical Humanism.
qs.kf:
☛ First Indian leader of Communist International → Manabendra Nath Roy
☛ Founding of Communist Party of India → 1920, Tashkent
☛ Member of Comintern Executive Committee → Manabendra Nath Roy
☛ Roy's later philosophy → Radical Humanism
☛ Roy's birth year → 1887

q: The members of the society of Khudai Khidmatgars were popularly known as _________.
qs.e: The Khudai Khidmatgar society was founded in 1929 by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan. Its members wore red shirts, hence they were popularly known as 'Red Shirts'. This movement was active in the North-West Frontier Province (now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) of India. Ghaffar Khan was also called the 'Frontier Gandhi'. The organization was known for its non-violent resistance and played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Khudai Khidmatgar → Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
☛ Other name of Red Shirt movement → Khudai Khidmatgar
☛ Known as Frontier Gandhi → Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
☛ Award conferred on Ghaffar Khan → Bharat Ratna (1987)
☛ Main principle of Khudai Khidmatgars → Non-violence

q: The word 'sharia' is related to which religion?
qs.e: Sharia is a fundamental religious law of Islam, known as Sharia law. It is based on the Quran and Hadith, and governs all aspects of a Muslim's life, including prayer, fasting, marriage, divorce, and business. The term 'sharia' means 'path' or 'way', providing moral and religious guidance to Muslims. It is a central concept in Islam, a monotheistic religion founded on the teachings of Prophet Muhammad. Other religions such as Christianity, Sikhism, and Hinduism do not use the term sharia in their doctrines.
qs.kf:
☛ Which religion is Sharia law associated with? → Islam
☛ What is the basis of Sharia? → Quran and Hadith
☛ What is the meaning of the word 'sharia'? → Path or way
☛ What are the main scriptures of Islam? → Quran and Hadith
☛ Who is the founder of Islam? → Prophet Muhammad

q: 'World Religion Day' is observed on the ________ of January.
qs.e: World Religion Day is observed on the 3rd Sunday of January every year. The day aims to promote interfaith understanding and harmony among different religions. It was initiated in 1950 by the Baháʼí Faith. The founder of the Baháʼí Faith is Baháʼu'lláh. The main objective of this day is to encourage religious unity and tolerance. It is celebrated worldwide by various religious communities through special programs and events.
qs.kf:
☛ Which religion started World Religion Day? → Baháʼí Faith
☛ Who is the founder of the Baháʼí Faith? → Baháʼu'lláh
☛ What is the main objective of World Religion Day? → Religious unity and tolerance
☛ In which month is this day observed? → January
☛ When was World Religion Day first observed? → 1950

q: Which great personality of the world was also known as 'Fuehrer'?
qs.e: Adolf Hitler (1889-1945) was the dictator of Germany who was known as 'Führer', which means 'leader' in German. He was the head of the Nazi Party and served as Chancellor of Germany from 1933 to 1945. He initiated World War II and the Holocaust, resulting in the genocide of millions of Jews and others. The title 'Führer' became synonymous with his personality cult and totalitarian rule. He was also the author of 'Mein Kampf'.
qs.kf:
☛ With whom is the title 'Führer' associated? → Adolf Hitler
☛ Which party did Hitler lead? → Nazi Party
☛ When did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany? → 1933
☛ What is the name of Hitler's autobiography? → Mein Kampf
☛ When did World War II take place? → 1939-1945

q: Who is considered as the father of Indian surgery?
qs.e: Sushruta is regarded as the father of Indian surgery. He was an ancient Indian physician and surgeon who authored the Sushruta Samhita, a comprehensive text on surgery. The Samhita describes over 300 surgical procedures, 120 surgical instruments, and various surgical techniques. Sushruta detailed complex surgeries like cataract, plastic surgery, and rhinoplasty (nose surgery). While Charaka is known as the father of Ayurveda, and Vaghbhata and Atreya are other eminent scholars in Ayurveda, Sushruta's contributions to surgery remain unparalleled.
qs.kf:
☛ Text composed by Sushruta → Sushruta Samhita
☛ Number of surgical procedures in Sushruta Samhita → Over 300
☛ Nose surgery described by Sushruta → Rhinoplasty
☛ Who is called father of Ayurveda → Charaka
☛ Main ancient Indian text on surgery → Sushruta Samhita

q: Who was the first person to land on the moon?
qs.e: The first person to land on the moon was Neil Armstrong. He stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission. This historic event marked a milestone in human space exploration. He was accompanied by Edwin Aldrin, who became the second person on the moon, while Michael Collins orbited in the command module. Armstrong's famous quote, "That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind," is still remembered. Alan Bean went to the moon on Apollo 12, and Rakesh Sharma is an Indian astronaut who participated in a Soviet space mission.
qs.kf:
☛ First person to land on the moon → Neil Armstrong
☛ Apollo 11 launch year → 1969
☛ Second person to walk on the moon → Edwin Aldrin
☛ Apollo 11 command module pilot → Michael Collins
☛ Neil Armstrong's famous quote → "That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind"

q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of Great Britain?
qs.e: The first woman Prime Minister of Great Britain was Margaret Thatcher, who served from 1979 to 1990. She was the leader of the Conservative Party and known for her tough policies, termed 'Thatcherism'. Hillary Clinton was a US Secretary of State, Cherie Blair is the wife of former UK PM Tony Blair, and Imelda Marcos was the First Lady of the Philippines. Thatcher won three consecutive elections and was the longest-serving British Prime Minister of the 20th century. Her tenure included the Falklands War and economic reforms aimed at reducing inflation and privatization.
qs.kf:
☛ First woman PM of Great Britain → Margaret Thatcher
☛ Thatcher's tenure → 1979-1990
☛ Thatcher's party → Conservative Party
☛ Famous policy → Thatcherism
☛ Major war during her time → Falklands War

name: Set 3 · Q101–149
sub: Static GK - Awards, Honours, Firsts & Personalities

q: Who among the following is revered as 'Karnataka Sangita Pitamaha'?
qs.e: Purandara Dasa is revered as the 'Karnataka Sangita Pitamaha' (Grandfather of Carnatic Music) because he systematized the teaching of Carnatic music. He devised the basic lessons (Sarali, Janti, Alankara) for beginners, which are still used today. He composed thousands of devotional songs (Kriti) mainly in Kannada and Sanskrit. He played a key role in the Bhakti movement and made music accessible to the common people. His contributions earned him this title. Other great composers like Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Annamacharya are not given this specific title.
qs.kf:
☛ Karnataka Sangita Pitamaha → Purandara Dasa
☛ Languages of Purandara Dasa's compositions → Kannada and Sanskrit
☛ Movement associated with Purandara Dasa → Bhakti movement
☛ Number of compositions by Purandara Dasa → Thousands
☛ Basic lessons devised by Purandara Dasa → Sarali, Janti, Alankara

q: _____ was/is the first Indian to enter space.
A. Kalpana Chawla
B. Rakesh Sharma
C. Sunita Williams
D. Ravish Malhotra
qs.e: Rakesh Sharma is the first Indian citizen to enter space. He traveled aboard the Soviet spacecraft Soyuz T-11 in 1984 and spent 7 days, 21 hours, and 40 minutes in space. He famously told then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi that India looked "Saare Jahan Se Achcha" (better than the entire world). While Kalpana Chawla and Sunita Williams are also notable astronauts, they were American citizens of Indian origin. Ravish Malhotra is a trained astronaut but never flew to space. Sharma's achievement marked India's entry into manned spaceflight.
qs.kf:
☛ First Indian astronaut → Rakesh Sharma
☛ Rakesh Sharma's mission → Soyuz T-11 (1984)
☛ First Indian woman astronaut (Indian origin) → Kalpana Chawla (American)
☛ First Indian woman astronaut (Indian citizen) → None yet
☛ Rakesh Sharma's famous quote → "Saare Jahan Se Achcha..."

q: Who is sometimes referred to as 'Payyoli Express'?
qs.e: P.T. Usha is called the 'Payyoli Express' because she hails from Payyoli village in Kerala. She is one of India's most celebrated athletes, known for her performance in the 400m hurdles at the 1984 Olympics, where she finished fourth. She has won multiple gold medals at the Asian Games. She was awarded the Arjuna Award in 1985 and the Padma Shri in 1985. Born on 27 June 1964, she remains an inspiration in Indian athletics. Her nick name reflects her speed and her hometown.
qs.kf:
☛ Birthplace of P.T. Usha → Payyoli, Kerala
☛ Nickname of P.T. Usha → Payyoli Express
☛ Main event of P.T. Usha → 400m hurdles
☛ Major awards of P.T. Usha → Arjuna Award 1985, Padma Shri 1985
☛ Olympic performance of P.T. Usha → 4th place in 1984 Los Angeles Olympics

q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
qs.e: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission. He stepped onto the lunar surface, followed by Buzz Aldrin, who became the second. Armstrong famously said: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." This historic achievement was a major milestone in the Space Race, demonstrating American technological superiority during the Cold War. Before Apollo 11, Armstrong served as a naval aviator and test pilot. The mission's third crew member, Michael Collins, orbited the Moon in the command module while Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the surface.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the commander of Apollo 11? → Neil Armstrong
☛ Who was the second person to walk on the Moon? → Buzz Aldrin
☛ What year did Apollo 11 launch? → 1969
☛ What famous words did Armstrong say? → "One small step, one giant leap"
☛ Who was the third crew member of Apollo 11? → Michael Collins

q: The famous explorer _________ wanted to come to India, but instead landed on the shores of America.
qs.e: Christopher Columbus was an Italian explorer who worked under the patronage of the Spanish monarchs. He set out to find a western sea route to Asia (India). In 1492, he crossed the Atlantic Ocean and reached the Caribbean islands (Bahamas). He believed he had arrived in India, so he called the native inhabitants 'Indians.' In reality, he had landed on the shores of America. Columbus made four voyages but never realized he had discovered a new continent. This event marked the beginning of European colonization and the Columbian Exchange.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of Columbus's first voyage → 1492
☛ Under whose patronage did Columbus sail? → King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella of Spain
☛ First island Columbus landed on → Bahamas (San Salvador)
☛ Who correctly identified Columbus's discovery as a new continent? → Amerigo Vespucci
☛ Islands named after India → West Indies

q: Who founded the famous Vikramashila University in the 9th century?
qs.e: The famous Vikramashila University was established in the 9th century by King Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty. It was located in present-day Bhagalpur district of Bihar and became a major center for Buddhist education, especially tantric Buddhism. It was considered the second most important Buddhist learning center after Nalanda University. Dharmapala founded it at a place called Vikramashila on the banks of the Ganges River. The university flourished for about 400 years until it was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji in the 12th century.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Vikramashila University → Dharmapala
☛ Dharmapala belonged to which dynasty → Pala dynasty
☛ Vikramashila University was located on the banks of which river → Ganges
☛ Who destroyed Vikramashila University → Bakhtiyar Khilji
☛ Founder of the Pala dynasty → Gopala

q: Who was the first chairman of Sangeet Natak Akademi?
qs.e: Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, established in 1952. Its first chairman was PV Rajamannar, a distinguished jurist and art enthusiast. He served from 1952 to 1953. The academy was founded to preserve and promote Indian culture and arts. Currently, Shekhar Sen is its chairman. The academy annually presents the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, one of the highest honors for artists.
qs.kf:
☛ First chairman of Sangeet Natak Akademi → PV Rajamannar
☛ Year of establishment of Sangeet Natak Akademi → 1952
☛ Year of first Sangeet Natak Akademi Award → 1952
☛ Headquarters of Sangeet Natak Akademi → New Delhi
☛ Current chairman → Shekhar Sen

q: National Education Day is observed on 11 November to celebrate the birthday of which Indian leader?
qs.e: National Education Day is celebrated every year on 11 November to commemorate the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, a prominent freedom fighter and India's first Minister of Education. He was born on 11 November 1888 in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. He served as the Minister of Education from 1947 to 1958 and played a key role in shaping India's education system, including the establishment of IITs and the UGC. In 1992, the Government of India declared 11 November as National Education Day to honor his contributions to education.
qs.kf:
☛ Birthplace of Maulana Azad → Mecca, Saudi Arabia
☛ Tenure as Education Minister → 1947–1958
☛ Institutions established → IITs, UGC, AICTE
☛ Year of declaration as National Education Day → 1992
☛ Nickname → Maulana Azad

q: Eleanor Roosevelt, who was the chairperson of UDHR, belonged to which country?
qs.e: Eleanor Roosevelt was the First Lady of the United States of America and a prominent human rights activist. She chaired the UN Human Rights Commission from 1946 to 1951 and played a central role in drafting the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), which was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948. Eleanor Roosevelt called the UDHR the "Magna Carta of all mankind". She was the wife of US President Franklin D. Roosevelt and actively advocated for social justice and human rights throughout her life.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UDHR adopted? → 10 December 1948
☛ Who played a key role in drafting UDHR? → Eleanor Roosevelt
☛ Which country's first lady was Eleanor Roosevelt? → USA
☛ How many languages has UDHR been translated into? → Over 500
☛ What is UDHR often called? → Magna Carta of all mankind

q: Long Radio waves were discovered by
qs.e: Guglielmo Marconi discovered long radio waves. In 1895, he successfully transmitted signals using radio waves, and in 1901, he sent the first transatlantic radio message. For these achievements, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1909. While Heinrich Hertz experimentally proved the existence of radio waves, Marconi is credited with their practical application and long-distance transmission.
qs.kf:
☛ Year Marconi received Nobel Prize? → 1909
☛ Scientist who proved existence of radio waves? → Heinrich Hertz
☛ First transatlantic radio communication year? → 1901
☛ Full name of Marconi? → Guglielmo Marconi
☛ Frequency range of radio waves? → 3 kHz to 300 GHz

q: Who among the following is NOT related to Apple Inc. as its co-founder?
qs.e: Apple Inc. was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne. Ronald Wayne later left the company. Mark Zuckerberg is the co-founder of Facebook (now Meta), which is not related to Apple. Hence, he is not among the co-founders of Apple.
qs.kf:
☛ Who are the co-founders of Apple? → Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne
☛ In which year was Apple founded? → 1976
☛ How many days did Ronald Wayne work at Apple? → 12 days
☛ What is Steve Jobs' full name? → Steve Paul Jobs
☛ What is Steve Wozniak known for? → Designing Apple I and Apple II computers

q: Who was the Englishman who came to India, taught Philosophy in St Stephen’s College and later was known as ‘Deenbandhu’?
qs.e: CF Andrews (Charles Freer Andrews) was an English missionary and social reformer who came to India in 1904. He taught Philosophy at St Stephen's College in Delhi. He became a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and actively participated in the Indian freedom movement. Andrews also worked for the rights of Indians in South Africa. Due to his deep love and service for the people of India, he was given the title 'Deenbandhu' (Friend of the Poor).
qs.kf:
☛ What is CF Andrews popularly known as? → Deenbandhu
☛ Which college did CF Andrews teach at? → St Stephen's College, Delhi
☛ In which year did CF Andrews come to India? → 1904
☛ Who was CF Andrews a close associate of? → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ What is the full name of CF Andrews? → Charles Freer Andrews

q: Who is known as the founder of Sattriya dance of Assam?
qs.e: Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam, founded by the great saint-poet Shankardev in the 15th century. It is associated with the Vaishnava Bhakti movement and was originally performed by male monks in monasteries called Sattras. Shankardev integrated it into 'Ankia Naat' and 'Bhaona' theatrical traditions. Sattriya was recognized as a classical dance of India in 2000. Other options: Chaitanya is linked to Bengal's Bhakti movement, Tara Devi was a Pandwani singer, and Birju Maharaj is a renowned Kathak exponent.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Sattriya dance from? → Assam
☛ Who is the founder of Sattriya dance? → Shankardev
☛ Which dance got classical status in 2000? → Sattriya
☛ Shankardev is associated with which religious movement? → Vaishnava Bhakti movement
☛ Where is Sattriya traditionally performed? → Sattras (monasteries)

q: Who is famous in the name of Nightingale of India?
qs.e: Sarojini Naidu is famously known as the 'Nightingale of India' (Bharat Kokila). She was a prominent freedom fighter, politician, and poet. Born on 13 February 1879 in Hyderabad, she became the first Indian woman president of the Indian National Congress and later the first governor of the United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) after independence. Her poetry, mainly in English, earned her the title 'Nightingale' due to its lyrical beauty. The other options—Kamala Nehru, Indira Gandhi, and the Queen of Jhansi—are not associated with this epithet.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is called the Nightingale of India? → Sarojini Naidu
☛ When was Sarojini Naidu born? → 13 February 1879
☛ Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman president of which organization? → Indian National Congress
☛ After independence, Sarojini Naidu became the governor of which state? → United Provinces (Uttar Pradesh)
☛ In which language did Sarojini Naidu primarily write poetry? → English

q: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was related to which of the following religious sects?
qs.e: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1533) was a prominent Vaishnava saint and reformer. He founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism, centered on devotion to Lord Krishna. He popularized the practice of sankirtan (congregational chanting). Born in Bengal, he spent most of his life in Jagannath Puri. His teachings are based on the philosophy of achintya bheda-abheda, which accepts both distinction and unity between the devotee and the Lord. Among the other options, Shaiva worships Lord Shiva, Kapalika is a tantric sect, and Tantra is related to esoteric practices. Thus, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu belonged to the Vaishnava sect.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Chaitanya Mahaprabhu born? → 1486 AD
☛ Who founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism? → Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
☛ Which devotional practice did Chaitanya Mahaprabhu popularize? → Sankirtan
☛ Where was the main center of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu? → Jagannath Puri
☛ What is the philosophy of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu called? → Achintya Bheda-Abheda

q: Hangul, also known as Kashmir Stag, can be found in ______________.
qs.e: Hangul, also known as the Kashmir Stag, is primarily found in Dachigam National Park in Jammu and Kashmir. It is an endangered species listed on the IUCN Red List and is the state animal of Jammu and Kashmir. Dachigam National Park, located about 22 km from Srinagar, is the main natural habitat of the Hangul. This deer is a subspecies of the red deer and faces threats from habitat loss and poaching. Other options like Chandoli, Dudhwa, and Campbell Bay are national parks but do not host Hangul populations.
qs.kf:
☛ Scientific name of Hangul → Cervus elaphus hanglu
☛ State animal of Jammu and Kashmir → Hangul
☛ Where is Hangul found → Dachigam National Park
☛ Year of establishment of Dachigam National Park → 1981
☛ Family of Hangul → Cervidae

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which of the following is known as the 'Steel City of India'?
qs.e: Jamshedpur is known as the Steel City of India. Founded by Jamsetji Tata, it houses Tata Steel (formerly TISCO), India's oldest and largest steel plant. The city is located in the state of Jharkhand. Pilani is famous for the Birla Institute of Technology. Indore is a major commercial center in Madhya Pradesh. Ankaleswar is an industrial area in Gujarat.
qs.kf:
☛ Steel City of India → Jamshedpur
☛ First steel plant in India → Tata Steel, Jamshedpur (1907)
☛ Founder of Jamshedpur → Jamsetji Tata
☛ State where Jamshedpur is located → Jharkhand
☛ Largest steel producer in India → Tata Steel

q: Which leader adopted Orthodox Christianity as the official religion of Russia”
qs.e: Vladimir the Great, ruler of Kievan Rus, adopted Orthodox Christianity as the official religion in 988 AD. This event is known as the 'Baptism of Rus'. He received Christianity from the Byzantine Empire, which influenced Russian culture and the church. This strategic and religious decision helped connect Russia with Eastern Europe and Asia. Vladimir abandoned paganism and baptized his subjects en masse, laying the foundation of Christianity in Russia.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Christianity officially become the religion of Russia? → 988 AD
☛ Which empire influenced the Baptism of Rus? → Byzantine Empire
☛ In which city did Vladimir the Great adopt Christianity? → Kiev
☛ What is the main center of Orthodox Christianity? → Moscow
☛ Which dynasty did Vladimir the Great belong to? → Rurik Dynasty

q: The ‘Father of Indian Space Program’ is _________.
o: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
qs.e: Dr. Vikram Ambalal Sarabhai is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Program.' He played a key role in establishing the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in 1962. He emphasized the application of space science for national development. Under his leadership, the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) was established in 1963. Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam is called the 'Missile Man of India,' while Prof. Satish Dhawan served as ISRO chairman. Dr. K. Kasturirangan also served as ISRO chairman.
qs.kf:
☛ Father of Indian Space Program → Dr. Vikram A. Sarabhai
☛ First satellite launch → Aryabhata (1975)
☛ First ISRO chairman → Dr. Vikram Sarabhai
☛ India's first satellite → Aryabhata
☛ Establishment of Thumba Rocket Station → 1963

q: Who among the following became the first tourist to space by spending $20 million for 8 days in orbit?
qs.e: Dennis Tito became the first private space tourist when he traveled to the International Space Station (ISS) in 2001 aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. He paid $20 million for an 8-day stay in orbit. Tito, an American engineer and former NASA employee, financed his trip through his company, Wilshire Associates. His journey marked the beginning of space tourism, opening the door for future private space travelers. Prior to Tito, only government-trained astronauts had visited space. His mission was a milestone in commercial spaceflight.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first space tourist? → Dennis Tito
☛ How many days did Dennis Tito spend in space? → 8 days
☛ How much did he pay for the trip? → $20 million
☛ Which spacecraft carried him? → Soyuz
☛ Which space station did he visit? → International Space Station (ISS)

q: _______ was the world's first female astronaut.
A. Svetlana Savitskaya
B. Valentina Tereshkova
C. Sally Ride
D. Judith Resnik
qs.e: Valentina Tereshkova was the world's first female astronaut. She orbited Earth alone on June 16, 1963, aboard Vostok 6. She was part of the Soviet space program and became the first woman to go to space. Svetlana Savitskaya was the second female astronaut and the first woman to perform a spacewalk. Sally Ride was the first American female astronaut, and Judith Resnik was also an American astronaut. This question relates to space science and general knowledge.
qs.kf:
☛ First female astronaut → Valentina Tereshkova (1963)
☛ First woman to spacewalk → Svetlana Savitskaya (1984)
☛ First American female astronaut → Sally Ride (1983)
☛ Youngest astronaut in space → Valentina Tereshkova (age 26)
☛ Soviet mission Vostok 6 → Tereshkova's mission

q: Who is the current Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha? (According to 2016) A. Mallikarjun Kharge B. Ghulam Nabi Azad
C. Rahul Gandhi D. Derek O'Brien
qs.e: In 2016, the Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha was Ghulam Nabi Azad. He is a member of the Indian National Congress and represents Jammu and Kashmir in Rajya Sabha. The Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha is the leader of the largest opposition party with at least 55 seats. Ghulam Nabi Azad held this position from 2014 to 2021.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the position of Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha created? → 1969
☛ Who was the first Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha? → Shyam Nandan Prasad Mishra
☛ Minimum seats required for Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha? → 10% of total (approx 55)
☛ Tenure of Ghulam Nabi Azad as LoP in Rajya Sabha? → 2014-2021
☛ Who is the current (post-2021) Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha? → Mallikarjun Kharge

q: Which of the following cities was called 'Designnadu' in ancient times?
A. Kollam
B. Mysore
C. Madurai
D. Chittor
qs.e: In ancient times, the city of Kollam was called Designnadu. It is a major port city located in the state of Kerala. Historically, Kollam has been a prominent center of trade and commerce. It is also known as Quilon. The city is situated on the coast of the Arabian Sea and has been a hub for the trade of spices, silk, and other goods since ancient times. References to Kollam can be found in the writings of ancient Greek and Roman travelers. Hence, the correct answer is Kollam.
qs.kf:
☛ Ancient name of Kollam → Designnadu
☛ Kollam is in which state → Kerala
☛ Kollam is also known as → Quilon
☛ Kollam is situated on the coast of which sea → Arabian Sea
☛ Kollam is famous for → Spice trade

q: Who was the first person to obtain a spectrum by passing light through a prism?
qs.e: Sir Isaac Newton was the first person to obtain a spectrum by passing light through a prism in 1666. He demonstrated that white light splits into seven colors: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red. This experiment laid the foundation for the wave theory of light. Newton's work in optics is considered a milestone, and he published his findings in his book Opticks in 1704. The experiment proved that light is a mixture of different wavelengths, which later led to the development of spectroscopy.
qs.kf:
☛ Who discovered dispersion of light? → Isaac Newton
☛ How many colors are in a spectrum? → Seven (VIBGYOR)
☛ When was Newton's book Opticks published? → 1704
☛ Who is the father of wave theory of light? → Christiaan Huygens
☛ How many colors are in white light? → Seven

q: How many basic elements (Tatvas) have been described by early Indian philosophers to classify matter?
qs.e: In ancient Indian philosophy, especially in Samkhya and Vaisheshika schools, matter is classified into five basic elements known as Panchamahabhuta. These are: Earth (solid), Water (liquid), Fire (energy), Air (gas), and Ether/Space (Akasha). These elements are considered the fundamental building blocks of all physical matter. The Vaisheshika school also accepts these five elements, with Akasha being eternal and all-pervading. This classification system is foundational to ancient Indian scientific thought and later influenced systems like Ayurveda. Thus, early Indian philosophers described five basic elements to classify matter.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of basic elements in Samkhya philosophy for matter → Five
☛ Elements included in Panchamahabhuta → Earth, Water, Fire, Air, Ether
☛ Vaisheshika school's basic elements of matter → Five Mahabhuta
☛ Indian philosophy's number of elements distinct from modern science's four states → Five
☛ Ether element is also known as → Akasha or Space

q: Chainsoo is a famous food preparation of the state of_____.
qs.e: Chainsoo is a famous traditional dish from the state of Uttarakhand. It is particularly popular in the Kumaon and Garhwal regions. Chainsoo is made from black gram (urad dal) which is soaked, ground, and then cooked slowly in ghee over a low flame. This dish is rich in protein and is typically eaten with rice or roti. In the hilly areas of Uttarakhand, it is especially consumed in winter as it provides warmth to the body. Chainsoo is also included in traditional feasts and festivals of Uttarakhand. Thus, Chainsoo is a famous food preparation of Uttarakhand.
qs.kf:
☛ Chainsoo is a dish of which state? → Uttarakhand
☛ Which dal is used to make Chainsoo? → Black gram or urad dal
☛ What is the famous non-vegetarian dish of Uttarakhand? → Kapla
☛ What is another famous dish of Uttarakhand? → Phaanu
☛ Which dish is consumed in winter in Uttarakhand? → Chainsoo

q: Who is known as the founder of Himachal Pradesh?
qs.e: Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar is known as the founder of Himachal Pradesh. He was the first Chief Minister of the state and played a crucial role in its formation. On 25 January 1971, Himachal Pradesh was granted full statehood, largely due to his efforts. He was a skilled politician and social reformer, initiating several development schemes for the region. His contribution to the creation and progress of Himachal Pradesh is highly respected, making him the recognized founder of the state.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh? → Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar
☛ When did Himachal Pradesh get full statehood? → 25 January 1971
☛ When did Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar die? → 2 May 1981
☛ What is the capital of Himachal Pradesh? → Shimla
☛ Who is the current Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh? → Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu

q: Bengal famine occurred in the year _________.
qs.e: The Bengal famine occurred in the year 1943, also known as the Bengal Famine of 1943. It happened during World War II and was caused by British colonial policies, food shortages, and war-related factors. An estimated 3 to 3.5 million people died from starvation and related diseases. It is considered one of the most devastating famines in Indian history. The major causes included food grain crisis, rice shortage in Bengal, and diversion of resources for war efforts by the British government. The famine also strengthened the Indian independence movement.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Bengal Famine occur? → 1943
☛ Who was the Governor-General of British India during the Bengal Famine? → Lord Wavell
☛ What was the estimated death toll of the Bengal Famine? → 3-3.5 million
☛ Which famous book is related to the Bengal Famine? → 'Hunger and Famine' (by Amartya Sen)
☛ Which major famine occurred in India during World War II? → Bengal Famine of 1943

q: Queen Padmavati is related to which city?
qs.e: Queen Padmavati is associated with Chittaurgarh, a historic city in Rajasthan. She was the wife of King Ratan Singh of Chittaurgarh. Her story of beauty and valor is famous in medieval Indian history. Alauddin Khilji, the Sultan of Delhi, attacked Chittaurgarh to obtain Queen Padmavati. This event is described in the epic Padmavat, written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. To protect her honor, Queen Padmavati committed jauhar (self-immolation), which became a symbol of Rajput tradition. Chittaurgarh is also known for the Chittor Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage site. The legend of Padmavati has been depicted in various literary works and films.
qs.kf:
☛ Which city is associated with Queen Padmavati? → Chittaurgarh
☛ Who was the husband of Queen Padmavati? → King Ratan Singh
☛ Which Sultan attacked Chittaurgarh for Padmavati? → Alauddin Khilji
☛ Who wrote the epic Padmavat? → Malik Muhammad Jayasi
☛ What practice did Queen Padmavati adopt? → Jauhar (self-immolation)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Who among the following was a radical rationalist and iconoclast in Maharashtra?
qs.e: Gopal Ganesh Agarkar (1856-1895) was a prominent social reformer, educationist, and radical rationalist in Maharashtra. He was associated with the iconoclastic movement and fiercely criticized social orthodoxies, religious superstitions, and Brahminical dominance. He founded the newspaper 'Sudharak' and advocated for women's education, widow remarriage, and abolition of caste system. He was a colleague of Lokmanya Tilak but later parted ways due to differences over conservative approaches. Agarkar played a key role in establishing the 'New English School' and 'Deccan Education Society'. He is known as a 'social revolutionary' and 'rationalist leader' of Maharashtra.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Gopal Ganesh Agarkar born? → 1856
☛ Which newspaper did Gopal Ganesh Agarkar found? → Sudharak
☛ Which social reform movement was Gopal Ganesh Agarkar associated with? → Iconoclastic movement
☛ Which educational institution was Gopal Ganesh Agarkar associated with? → New English School
☛ Who was Gopal Ganesh Agarkar a colleague of? → Lokmanya Tilak

q: Who was the first Indian Director of the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore?
qs.e: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore was established in 1909 with the efforts of Jamsetji Tata and Maharaja Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV of Mysore. Its first director was Morris Travers (1909-1914), a British scientist. The first Indian director was Sir C V Raman (Chandrashekhara Venkata Raman), who served from 1933 to 1937. C V Raman is renowned for discovering the Raman Effect, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930. His tenure at IISc was significant for advancing research. Later, Sir J C Ghosh became director from 1939 to 1948.
qs.kf:
☛ First Director of IISc Bangalore? → Morris Travers (1909)
☛ First Indian Director? → C V Raman (1933)
☛ Discovery of Raman Effect? → C V Raman (1928)
☛ Nobel Prize for C V Raman? → 1930
☛ Director of IISc in 1949? → Sir J C Ghosh

q: Who was considered as 'father of All Indian Services'?
qs.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is known as the 'father of All India Services'. As India's first Home Minister, he laid the foundation of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and other central services. In 1946, when the Interim Government was formed, Patel ensured the creation of a strong and unified administrative framework. He believed that civil services are the backbone of the nation and should remain free from political influences. His efforts led to the passage of the All India Services Act in 1947, which gave constitutional protection to IAS and IPS. Patel is also known as the 'Iron Man of India' and played a crucial role in integrating princely states into the Indian Union.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of All India Services? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Who passed the All India Services Act 1947? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Who gave constitutional protection to IAS and IPS? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Who was the last Governor General of India? → C. Rajagopalachari
☛ Who was the first Home Minister of independent India? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

q: The statue of the world famous Gomateshwar is located in which of the following states?
qs.e: The world-famous Gomateshwar statue is located in Shravanabelagola, Hassan district of Karnataka state. This 57-feet tall monolithic statue is dedicated to Lord Bahubali (Gomateshwar), built in 981 CE by Chamundaraya, a minister of the Ganga dynasty. It is carved out of a single granite rock and is one of the largest Jain statues in the world. Every 12 years, a grand anointment ceremony called Mahamastakabhisheka is performed, where the statue is bathed with milk, saffron, and other holy substances. This statue is a major pilgrimage site for Jains.
qs.kf:
☛ Gomateshwar statue belongs to which religion → Jainism
☛ Who built the Gomateshwar statue → Chamundaraya
☛ Where is Gomateshwar statue located → Shravanabelagola, Karnataka
☛ Height of Gomateshwar statue → 57 feet
☛ Anointment ceremony of Gomateshwar statue is called → Mahamastakabhisheka

q: What is the nickname of Shoaib Akhtar?
qs.e: Shoaib Akhtar, the former Pakistani fast bowler, was nicknamed 'Rawalpindi Express' due to his immense speed. He was born in Rawalpindi, and his bowling speed was as fast as an express train. He set a world record by bowling at 161.3 km/h during the 2003 World Cup. Known for his aggressive bowling and long hair, Akhtar played international cricket from 1998 to 2011. 'The Wall' is the nickname of Rahul Dravid, while 'Jamie' and 'Flying Man' belong to other cricketers. Shoaib Akhtar remains one of the fastest bowlers in cricket history.
qs.kf:
☛ Shoaib Akhtar's nickname → Rawalpindi Express
☛ Shoaib Akhtar's fastest delivery → 161.3 km/h
☛ Shoaib Akhtar's birthplace → Rawalpindi, Pakistan
☛ Shoaib Akhtar's international career → 1998-2011
☛ Rahul Dravid's nickname → The Wall

q: Raja Ravi Varma was a famous _______.
qs.e: Raja Ravi Varma (1848-1906) was a renowned Indian painter known for his realistic and emotive depictions of scenes from Indian mythology and epics. He is celebrated for blending Western painting techniques with Indian subjects, making art accessible to the masses. His famous works include 'Shakuntala', 'Lakshmi', 'Saraswati', and 'Birth of Ganesh'. He established a lithograph press to reproduce his paintings widely. In 2013, his painting 'Bai in the Moonlight' was auctioned for ₹6.9 crore. His contributions have left a lasting impact on Indian art, bridging traditional and modern styles.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Raja Ravi Varma born? → 1848
☛ Which is a famous painting by Raja Ravi Varma? → Shakuntala
☛ Which art style did Raja Ravi Varma adopt? → Realism
☛ Which press did Raja Ravi Varma establish? → Lithograph press
☛ What title was Raja Ravi Varma awarded? → Raja

q: Who among the following was the Architect of the 'Victoria Memorial' in India?
qs.e: The Victoria Memorial in Kolkata was designed by the British architect William Emerson. Built in memory of Queen Victoria, it was opened to the public in 1921. Emerson designed it in the Indo-Saracenic style, blending Mughal, Rajput, and Gothic architectural elements. The memorial is located in the Maidan area of Kolkata and now serves as a museum. It is made of white Makrana marble, sourced from Rajasthan. Emerson also designed other notable structures, such as Crawford Market in Mumbai. The construction began in 1906 under the supervision of Lord Curzon, then Viceroy of India. The memorial's dome is inspired by the Taj Mahal, while the overall design reflects a fusion of Indian and British styles.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Victoria Memorial located? → Kolkata
☛ When did construction of Victoria Memorial begin? → 1906
☛ What is the architectural style of Victoria Memorial? → Indo-Saracenic
☛ To whom is Victoria Memorial dedicated? → Queen Victoria
☛ What is the source of marble used in Victoria Memorial? → Makrana, Rajasthan

q: If Ram is from Kushalya, then Karna is from _______
A. Draupadi
B. Ganga
C. Vrushali
D. Kunti
qs.e: Ram's mother was Kushalya, similarly Karna's mother was Kunti. Kunti was the wife of Pandu and she invoked the Sun God using a mantra given by sage Durvasa to give birth to Karna. Karna was born before her marriage, hence he is called Kuntiputra. Among the other options, Draupadi was the wife of the Pandavas, Ganga was the mother of Bhishma, and Vrushali was Karna's wife. Therefore, the correct answer is Kunti.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was Karna's father? → Sun God
☛ Who gave the boon to Kunti? → Sage Durvasa
☛ Who was Karna's wife? → Vrushali
☛ Who was Bhishma's mother? → Ganga
☛ Who was Draupadi married to? → Five Pandavas

q: Who among the following is known as the 'Meera of Modern India'?
qs.e: Mahadevi Verma was a renowned Hindi poetess, known as the 'Meera of Modern India' for her devotional and love-filled compositions. She was a leading figure of the Chhayavaad era and her works reflect devotion and separation towards God, similar to Meera. Her notable poetry collections include 'Neerja', 'Sandhyagit', and 'Deepshikha'. She was honored with prestigious awards like Padma Bhushan and Jnanpith. Her poems often explore themes of love, nature, and spirituality.
qs.kf:
☛ Famous work of Mahadevi Verma → 'Neerja', 'Sandhyagit'
☛ Award received by Mahadevi Verma → Padma Bhushan, Jnanpith
☛ Birth of Mahadevi Verma → 1907, Faridabad
☛ Death of Mahadevi Verma → 1987
☛ Style of Mahadevi Verma → Chhayavaadi poetry

q: Who was the UNO's first Secretary-General from the African continent?
qs.e: The first Secretary-General of the United Nations from the African continent was Boutros Boutros-Ghali from Egypt. He served from 1992 to 1996. Dag Hammarskjöld was from Sweden, Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of Britain, and Kurt Waldheim was from Austria. Boutros-Ghali was the sixth Secretary-General and the first Arab and African to hold the post. His tenure faced crises like the Rwandan genocide and the Bosnian War.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first UN Secretary-General? → Trygve Lie (Norway)
☛ Who served the longest as Secretary-General? → Dag Hammarskjöld (8 years)
☛ Who was the first Asian Secretary-General? → U Thant (Myanmar)
☛ Who was the first woman Secretary-General? → None yet
☛ Boutros Boutros-Ghali belonged to which country? → Egypt

q: Who was the first chairman of ISRO?
qs.e: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established on August 15, 1969. Its first chairman was Vikram Sarabhai, who is widely regarded as the father of the Indian space program. He founded the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) and launched India's first rocket in 1963. Sarabhai also served as the chairman of the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR). His visionary leadership laid the foundation for India's remarkable achievements in space exploration.
qs.kf:
☛ When was ISRO established? → August 15, 1969
☛ Who was the second chairman of ISRO after Vikram Sarabhai? → M. G. K. Menon
☛ Who is known as the father of the Indian space program? → Vikram Sarabhai
☛ Where is Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station located? → Kerala
☛ What is the full form of INCOSPAR? → Indian National Committee for Space Research

q: Which of the following cities is also known as 'Blue City'?
qs.e: Jodhpur is known as the 'Blue City' because the houses in the old city are painted in blue color. This color helps in reducing the heat of the sun and keeping mosquitoes away. Jodhpur is the second largest city in Rajasthan and is also called the capital of Marwar. The city is famous for its historical forts and palaces, most notably the Mehrangarh Fort. Jaipur is called the 'Pink City', Bikaner the 'Red City', and Udaipur the 'Lake City'.
qs.kf:
☛ Which city in India is known as 'Pink City'? → Jaipur
☛ Which city in India is known as 'Lake City'? → Udaipur
☛ Which city in India is known as 'Golden City'? → Jaisalmer
☛ Which city in India is known as 'Sun City'? → Jodhpur
☛ On which river is Jodhpur located? → Luni River

q: Who was the first European president of the Indian National Congress?
qs.e: The first European president of the Indian National Congress was George Yule. He presided over the 1888 session in Allahabad. George Yule was a British-born businessman associated with a prominent trading house in Calcutta. In the early years of Congress, there were several British members, but Yule was the first European to be elected as president. Subsequently, Alfred Webb (1894) and Annie Besant (1917) also became presidents. A.O. Hume was the founder of Congress but never served as its president.
qs.kf:
☛ First European president of INC → George Yule (1888, Allahabad)
☛ Founder of INC → A.O. Hume (1885)
☛ First woman president of INC → Annie Besant (1917)
☛ First Indian president of INC → Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (1885)
☛ First session of INC → 1885, Bombay

q: Which of the following is/are correct about C. Vijayaraghavachariar?
I. He was called ‘The Hero of Salem’.
II. He was known as the ‘Lion of North India’.
qs.e: C. Vijayaraghavachariar was a prominent Indian National Congress leader and freedom fighter. He was born in 1852 in Salem district, Tamil Nadu. He presided over the 1920 Nagpur session of the Congress. He was called 'The Hero of Salem' for leading the Salt Satyagraha in Salem. He was not known as the 'Lion of North India'; that title belongs to Lala Lajpat Rai. Hence, statement I is correct, and statement II is incorrect.
qs.kf:

☛ Lion of North India → Lala Lajpat Rai
☛ President of 1920 Congress Session → C. Vijayaraghavachariar (Nagpur)
☛ Birthplace of C. Vijayaraghavachariar → Salem, Tamil Nadu
☛ Death of C. Vijayaraghavachariar → 1943

q: Who among the following received the Padma Vibhushan award for his contribution to Indian classical dance?
qs.e: Birju Maharaj was a renowned Indian Kathak dancer and guru. He made invaluable contributions to Indian classical dance, especially Kathak. He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1986, which is India's second highest civilian award. Born on 4 February 1938, he belonged to the Kalka-Bindadin Gharana. Through his dance, he gave global recognition to Indian culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Birju Maharaj is known for which dance form? → Kathak
☛ In which year was he awarded Padma Vibhushan? → 1986
☛ Which gharana did Birju Maharaj belong to? → Kalka-Bindadin Gharana
☛ Padma Vibhushan is which highest civilian award in India? → Second
☛ Which state is the origin of Kathak dance? → Uttar Pradesh

q: Who among the following established the famous Nrityagram institution in Bengaluru?
qs.e: The Nrityagram institution was founded by Protima Gauri in 1990 at Hessaraghatta, near Bengaluru. It is a dance gurukul dedicated to preserving and promoting Indian classical dances, especially Odissi. Protima Gauri was a renowned Odissi dancer, and she revived the traditional guru-shishya parampara at Nrityagram. The institution is now a major cultural center hosting regular performances and training.
qs.kf:

☛ Where is Nrityagram located? → Hessaraghatta, near Bengaluru

☛ When was Nrityagram established? → 1990

q: Dr. Shankarbaba Pundlikrao Papalkar is known for his dedication to improving the lives of:
qs.e: Dr. Shankarbaba Pundlikrao Papalkar dedicated his life to improving the lives of disabled and destitute children. He established the 'Shankarbaba Papalkar Multispecialty Hospital and Research Center' in Maharashtra, which provides free medical services. He was a social worker who devoted his entire life to serving underprivileged children. His efforts were recognized with several awards.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state did Dr. Shankarbaba Papalkar belong to? → Maharashtra
☛ What was his main area of work? → Welfare of disabled and destitute children
☛ What is the name of the institution he founded? → Shankarbaba Papalkar Multispecialty Hospital and Research Center

☛ How was his service recognized? → Honored with various awards

q: In the fiscal year 2024-25, the total remittances sent home by Indians overseas set a new record of:
qs.e: In the fiscal year 2024-25, the total remittances sent home by Indians overseas set a new record of 135.46 billion dollars. This exceeded the previous year's figure of 122.57 billion dollars. India is the world's largest recipient of remittances. The increase is primarily due to the growing number of Indian diaspora in the US and Gulf countries and their higher incomes. This remittance inflow strengthens India's foreign exchange reserves and boosts domestic demand, playing a crucial role in the economy.
qs.kf:
☛ Record Indian remittances in FY 2024-25 → 135.46 billion dollars
☛ India's rank as remittance recipient → First globally
☛ Main reason for remittance growth → Higher income in US and Gulf countries
☛ Remittance figure for FY 2023-24 → 122.57 billion dollars
☛ Impact of remittances on economy → Strengthens foreign exchange reserves

q: Who was popularly known as the 'Payyoli Express' in Indian sports history?
qs.e: In Indian sports history, the 'Payyoli Express' was the nickname of PT Usha. Payyoli is a village in Kerala, where she was born. She is a renowned Indian sprinter who won a gold medal in the 1984 Asian Games in the 400 meters hurdles. She is also known as the 'Queen of Indian Athletics'. She represented India in many international competitions and won multiple medals.
qs.kf:
☛ Payyoli Express → PT Usha
☛ Full name of PT Usha → Pilavullakandi Thekkerambil Usha
☛ Birthplace of PT Usha → Payyoli, Kerala
☛ Gold medal event of PT Usha in 1984 Asian Games → 400 meters hurdles
☛ Award received by PT Usha → Padma Shri (1985)

q: Who among the following is famous for composing kritis known for their contemplative nature and emphasis on capturing the essence of the raga through a slow, richly ornamented style?
qs.e: Mutthuswami Dikshitar is one of the trinity of Carnatic music, renowned for his contemplative and meditative compositions that emphasize capturing the essence of the raga through a slow, richly ornamented style. His kritis are set in slow tempo (vilamba laya) and use intricate gamakas. He composed primarily in Sanskrit and Tamil, using the mudra 'Guruguha'. A master of the veena, Dikshitar's works are known for their philosophical depth and adherence to classical raga structure.
qs.kf:
☛ Who are the trinity of Carnatic music? → Thyagaraja, Mutthuswami Dikshitar, Shyama Sastri
☛ What is the mudra used in Dikshitar's compositions? → Guruguha
☛ Which instrument was Dikshitar proficient in? → Veena
☛ What is the typical tempo of Dikshitar's kritis? → Slow (vilamba laya)
☛ In which languages did Dikshitar primarily compose? → Sanskrit and Tamil

name: Set 1 · Q1–49
sub: Static GK - Science, Technology, Inventions & Space

q: What is the mass of the Earth?
qs.e: The mass of Earth is approximately 5.972 × 1024 kg. This value is based on scientific measurements and is determined using Earth's gravitational force and other astronomical parameters. Earth's mass is crucial for comparison among planets in the solar system. For instance, Earth's mass is about 18 times that of Mercury. This value is related to Earth's density and size; the average density of Earth is about 5.514 g/cm3. The mass is calculated using the gravitational constant and Earth's radius. Understanding Earth's mass helps in studying its gravitational field and orbital mechanics.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the mass of Earth? → 5.972 × 1024 kg
☛ What is the average density of Earth? → 5.514 g/cm3
☛ Earth's mass is how many times that of Mercury? → About 18 times
☛ What parameters determine Earth's mass? → Gravitational force and astronomical measurements
☛ Earth's mass is how many times less than the Sun's? → About 333,000 times less

q: Who discovered the US
qs.e: ✅ Correct Answer: (B) Christopher Columbus

q: A ______ map converts color intensity or grayscale information to heights to give the appearance that features are raised above the surface, like embossed letters.
qs.e: A bump map is a type of map that converts color intensity or grayscale information into heights. It is used in 3D graphics and texture mapping to create the illusion of relief or depth on a surface without changing the actual geometry. It makes features appear raised or embossed, like embossed letters. Other options such as shade (light-shadow), tone (color value), and tint (color lightness) are not suited for this purpose.
qs.kf:
☛ What is a bump map used for? → To simulate surface relief in 3D graphics
☛ What information does a bump map use? → Grayscale or color intensity
☛ What effect does a bump map create? → Makes surface appear raised
☛ Difference between bump map and normal map? → Bump map uses grayscale, normal map uses RGB
☛ Principle behind bump map? → Manipulates light reflection

q: Who invented the blue jeans?
qs.e: The blue jeans were invented by Levi Strauss in 1873. He was a German-American businessman who, along with Jacob Davis, patented the riveted pants. The patent used metal rivets to strengthen the cloth, making it suitable for miners and farmers. The denim fabric was dyed blue with indigo dye, which was durable and practical. Levi Strauss & Co. remains a leading jeans manufacturer today.
qs.kf:
☛ Inventor of blue jeans → Levi Strauss
☛ Co-inventor of blue jeans → Jacob Davis
☛ Patent year → 1873
☛ Fabric used → Denim
☛ Dye color → Indigo (blue)

q: A ‘compass’ is used to draw:
qs.e: A compass is a geometrical instrument used to draw circles and arcs. It consists of two arms: a sharp needle (to set the center point) and a pencil or drawing tip (to trace the curve). A compass is also used in various geometric constructions, such as bisecting angles, drawing perpendiculars, and measuring distances. To draw a straight line, a ruler is used; to draw a rectangle or triangle, a ruler and protractor are used.
qs.kf:
☛ Use of a compass → to draw circles and arcs
☛ Number of arms in a compass → two
☛ Tool used to draw a straight line → ruler
☛ Tool used to measure angles → protractor
☛ Use of compass in geometry → construction and measurement

q: The PSLV-C45 was launched from the second launch pad of the-
qs.e: PSLV-C45 was a Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle launched by ISRO on April 1, 2019. It was launched from the second launch pad of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) in Sriharikota. This mission was the 47th flight of the PSLV and deployed EMISAT along with several other satellites. SDSC is India's primary spaceport, from where all major launches take place. Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre is a research center in Thiruvananthapuram, while Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station is used for small rockets.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first PSLV launch? → 1993
☛ What was the main payload of PSLV-C45? → EMISAT
☛ Where is Satish Dhawan Space Centre located? → Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh
☛ When did the second launch pad become operational? → 2005
☛ What type of mission was PSLV-C45? → Satellite launch

q: When is 'World Environment Day' observed?
qs.e: World Environment Day is observed annually on June 5. It was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972 during the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment, and first celebrated in 1973. The day aims to raise awareness about environmental protection and encourage global action. Each year, a specific theme is chosen; for example, the 2024 theme was 'Land Restoration, Desertification and Drought Resilience'. The day is marked by events such as tree planting, clean-up campaigns, and policy announcements worldwide. It serves as a platform for governments, organizations, and individuals to address pressing environmental issues.
qs.kf:
☛ When was World Environment Day first celebrated? → 1973
☛ What was the theme of World Environment Day 2024? → Land Restoration, Desertification and Drought Resilience
☛ Where is the headquarters of UNEP located? → Nairobi, Kenya
☛ Which conference led to the creation of World Environment Day? → Stockholm Conference, 1972
☛ When is Earth Day observed? → April 22

q: The Fiber Grid internet system was introduced by which Chief Minister in India?
qs.e: The Fiber Grid internet system was introduced by Chandrababu Naidu, the former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh. This ambitious project aims to connect all villages in the state with high-speed internet through optical fiber cables. The initiative provides broadband connectivity to rural areas, enhancing access to digital services, education, and healthcare. It is considered a part of the Digital India campaign and a key step towards digitally empowering Andhra Pradesh. Chandrababu Naidu presented it as a priority scheme for the state's development, focusing on bridging the digital divide between urban and rural regions. The Fiber Grid project significantly boosts the state's digital infrastructure.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state launched the Fiber Grid project? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ What is the aim of Fiber Grid? → To connect villages with high-speed internet
☛ Which technology is used in Fiber Grid? → Optical fiber
☛ Fiber Grid is part of which national initiative? → Digital India
☛ Who is the current Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh? → Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy

q: When was the Central Pollution Control Board constituted?
qs.e: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was constituted in 1974 under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. It functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The primary objective of CPCB is to control water and air pollution and enforce environmental standards. It also provides technical assistance to State Pollution Control Boards. The headquarters of CPCB is located in Delhi. This board plays a crucial role under the Environment Protection Act, 1986 as well.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which act was CPCB constituted? → Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
☛ Which ministry does CPCB work under? → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Where is the headquarters of CPCB? → Delhi
☛ When was the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act enacted? → 1981
☛ When was the Environment Protection Act enacted? → 1986

q: Which of the following is the unit of measurement of the “Ecological Footprint”?
qs.e: The ecological footprint measures the biologically productive land and water area required by human activities. It is expressed in global hectares, where one global hectare equals one hectare with world-average productivity. This unit allows comparison of resource consumption and waste generation across different countries and individuals. The ecological footprint concept was developed by Mathis Wackernagel and William Rees at the University of British Columbia in the early 1990s. It is used to assess humanity's demand on the planet's ecosystems against Earth's biocapacity.
qs.kf:
☛ Unit of ecological footprint → Global hectare (gha)
☛ One global hectare → One hectare with global average productivity
☛ Abbreviation for global hectare → gha
☛ Founder of ecological footprint concept → Mathis Wackernagel
☛ Ecological overshoot day → Date when humanity's resource consumption exceeds Earth's annual capacity

q: Which of the following mobile applications won the Platinum under Best Mobile App category in Digital India Awards 2018?
qs.e: The eCourts Services mobile app won the Platinum award under the Best Mobile App category at the Digital India Awards 2018. This app is part of the Indian judiciary's digitization initiative, providing citizens with court-related information and services such as case status, court dates, and judgments. The award was conferred by the government under the Digital India mission, which aims to make services digitally accessible. Among the other options, Skill Pill, Moodle Mobile, and E.Learning Age are education-related apps but did not win this award. The eCourts app has significantly improved transparency and efficiency in the judicial system.
qs.kf:
☛ Platinum winner of Best Mobile App at Digital India Awards 2018 → eCourts Services
☛ Ministry associated with eCourts Services app → Ministry of Law and Justice
☛ Digital India Awards started in → 2016
☛ Main purpose of eCourts app → Digitalizing court services
☛ Mascots of Digital India campaign → DigiBabu and DigiMaim

q: __________ become the first police force in the country to digitize all malkhanas, rooms for keeping seized arms and ammunition.
qs.e: Delhi Police became the first police force in the country to digitize all malkhanas (rooms for storing seized arms and ammunition). This initiative was undertaken under the guidance of the Ministry of Home Affairs, adopting digital lockers and barcoding systems for better management. The digitization enhances transparency and improves tracking of seized items. It is a significant step in cyber security and data management within law enforcement.
qs.kf:
☛ Delhi Police malkhana digitization project → First police force in India
☛ Malkhana stores → Seized arms and ammunition
☛ Technology used → Barcoding and digital lockers
☛ Key benefit → Enhanced transparency and tracking
☛ Overseeing ministry → Ministry of Home Affairs

q: Which of the following astrologers was taken under house arrest for supporting Heliocentrism? A. Nicolaus Copernicus
B. Galileo Galilei
C. Johannes kepler
D. Friedrich Bessel
qs.e: Galileo Galilei was placed under house arrest in 1633 by the Catholic Church for supporting heliocentrism, the theory that the Sun is the center of the universe. He used his telescope to observe celestial bodies and publicly defended Nicolaus Copernicus's heliocentric model, which contradicted the Church's geocentric view. Galileo was tried for heresy, forced to recant his views, and spent the rest of his life under house arrest. His work laid the foundation for modern astronomy.
qs.kf:
☛ Galileo Galilei → Placed under house arrest for supporting heliocentrism.
☛ Heliocentrism → The theory that the Sun is the center of the solar system.
☛ Nicolaus Copernicus → First to propose heliocentrism.
☛ Johannes Kepler → Formulated laws of planetary motion.
☛ Friedrich Bessel → Known for measuring stellar parallax.

q: What was the code name of the nuclear tests conducted by India in Pokhran in 1998?
A. Operation Desert storm
B. Operation Vijay
C. Operation Shakti
D. Operation Kaboom
qs.e: The code name of the nuclear tests conducted by India in Pokhran in 1998 was Operation Shakti. The tests were carried out on 11 and 13 May 1998 at the Pokhran test range in Rajasthan, involving five nuclear explosions. This made India a nuclear weapons state. The tests were conducted under the leadership of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Following Operation Shakti, India declared itself a nuclear weapon state. The tests led to international sanctions, especially from the United States. Operation Shakti remains a significant milestone in India's defense and scientific achievements.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Operation Shakti conducted? → 1998
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during Pokhran-II? → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ When was India's first nuclear test? → 1974
☛ What was the code name of the 1974 test? → Smiling Buddha
☛ In which state is Pokhran located? → Rajasthan

q: Which one does not belong to the group?
A. Panda Global
B. Rabbit
C. Avast
D. Kaspersky
qs.e: Panda Global, Avast, and Kaspersky are all well-known antivirus software companies that work in the field of computer security. Whereas Rabbit is an animal and has no connection with cyber security. Therefore, Rabbit does not belong to this group. This question is based on general knowledge and cyber security. In such questions, one option often belongs to a different category, which needs to be identified.
