q: When is World AIDS Day celebrated each year?
A. 1 December
B. 1 January
C. 14 February
D. 8 March
qs.e: World AIDS Day is observed every year on 1 December. It was first declared in 1988 by the World Health Organization (WHO). The day aims to raise awareness about HIV/AIDS, show support for people living with HIV, and commemorate those who have died from AIDS-related illnesses. A red ribbon is worn as a symbol of solidarity. HIV attacks the immune system, weakening the body's ability to fight infections. Although there is no cure, antiretroviral therapy can manage the virus. The day also focuses on reducing stigma and promoting prevention, testing, and treatment.
qs.kf:
☛ World AIDS Day → 1 December
☛ Virus causing AIDS → HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)
☛ First declared by WHO → 1988
☛ Symbol of AIDS awareness → Red Ribbon
☛ Main effect of AIDS → Destroys immune system

q: What is the APGAR scale?
A. Scale to measure the height of mountains
B. Time Measuring Scale
C. Scale to determine the physical condition of a newborn
D. Longevity scale
qs.e: APGAR scale is used to assess the physical condition of a newborn immediately after birth. It was developed by Dr. Virginia Apgar in 1952. The scale is based on five parameters: Appearance (skin color), Pulse (heart rate), Grimace (reflex response), Activity (muscle tone), and Respiration (breathing effort). Each parameter is scored 0, 1, or 2, giving a total score from 0 to 10. The test is performed at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth. A high score indicates good health of the baby. This scale is not used for measuring mountain height, time, or longevity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who invented the APGAR scale? → Dr. Virginia Apgar
☛ How many parameters are in the APGAR scale? → Five
☛ What is the maximum score per parameter in the APGAR scale? →2
☛ When is the APGAR test performed after birth? → At 1 and 5 minutes
☛ What does APGAR stand for? → Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration

q: World Wetland day is celebrated every year on _______February.
A. 2nd
B. 3rd
C. 4th
D. 5th
qs.e: World Wetlands Day is celebrated annually on 2nd February. This day marks the anniversary of the signing of the Ramsar Convention in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran. The convention aims to promote the conservation and wise use of wetlands. Wetlands are vital ecosystems that support biodiversity, water purification, flood control, and climate regulation. India has over 75 Ramsar sites. Each year, a specific theme is chosen to highlight the importance of wetlands. The day serves as a reminder of the urgent need to protect these natural habitats from degradation and loss.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Ramsar Convention signed? → 2nd February 1971
☛ Where is the Ramsar Convention headquarters? → Gland, Switzerland
☛ Which Indian state has the most Ramsar sites? → Tamil Nadu
☛ What was India's first Ramsar site? → Keoladeo National Park (1981)
☛ What was the theme of World Wetlands Day 2024? → Wetlands and Human Wellbeing

q: In which year did Ole Romer measure the speed of light for the first time in history?
qs.e: The speed of light was first measured by Danish astronomer Ole Romer in 1676. He observed the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io and deduced that light travels at a finite speed. According to his calculation, light takes about 22 minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth (modern value is 8 minutes 20 seconds). This measurement was a landmark in astronomy. Romer estimated the speed of light to be approximately 220,000 km/s, which is lower than the modern value of about 300,000 km/s, but it was the first successful attempt.
qs.kf:
☛ First scientist to measure speed of light → Ole Romer (1676)
☛ Modern value of speed of light → 299,792,458 m/s
☛ Method used to measure speed of light → Eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io
☛ Symbol for speed of light → c
☛ Medium with highest speed of light → Vacuum

q: First human who got married in space is: A. Yuri Denver
B. Yuri Johnson C. Yuri Malenchenko D. David Malenchenk
qs.e: Yuri Malenchenko is a Russian cosmonaut who became the first person to get married in space on August 10, 2003. While aboard the International Space Station (ISS), he married Ekaterina Dmitrieva, a U.S. citizen, via a video link. The marriage was legally registered in Texas, United States. Born on December 22, 1961, Malenchenko has participated in multiple space missions. This event is a unique and significant milestone in the history of space exploration.
qs.kf:
☛ First person to get married in space → Yuri Malenchenko
☛ Date of marriage → August 10, 2003
☛ Place of marriage → International Space Station (ISS)
☛ Medium of marriage → Video link
☛ Spouse name → Ekaterina Dmitrieva

q: When was the ASLV used in India for the first time?
qs.e: The ASLV (Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle) was India's first experimental satellite launch vehicle developed by ISRO. Its first launch was attempted on 24 March 1987 from Sriharikota. However, this mission failed. ASLV was designed to place small satellites into low Earth orbit. It played a crucial role in India's space program and paved the way for more advanced launch vehicles like PSLV.
qs.kf:
☛ First successful launch of ASLV → 1992 with ASLV-D3
☛ First satellite launched by ASLV → SROSS-1 (failed in 1987)
☛ Last launch of ASLV → 1994 with ASLV-D4
☛ Payload capacity of ASLV → 150 kg satellite into 400 km orbit
☛ Vehicle developed after ASLV → PSLV (first launch in 1993)

q: Apollo 11, the first artificial satellite that landed humans on the moon, was launched in which year?
qs.e: Apollo 11 mission was launched on July 16, 1969, and landed on the moon on July 20, 1969. It was the first manned mission to land humans on the moon. The mission included Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins. Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the moon. This mission was operated by the American space agency NASA.
qs.kf:
☛ Apollo 11 launch year → 1969
☛ Date of moon landing → July 20, 1969
☛ First person to walk on the moon → Neil Armstrong
☛ Other astronauts in the mission → Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins
☛ Space agency → NASA

q: Thomas Clifford Allbutt is associated with the invention of:
A. X ray Machine
B. Clinical Thermometer
C. Stethoscope
D. Microscope
qs.e: Thomas Clifford Allbutt was a renowned English physician who invented the first practical Clinical Thermometer in 1866. Earlier thermometers were very long and took about 20 minutes to measure body temperature. Allbutt's thermometer was smaller and could record temperature accurately in just 5 minutes. This invention was a major advancement in medical science. The X-ray machine was invented by Wilhelm Röntgen, the stethoscope by René Laennec, and the microscope by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek. Thus, Allbutt is associated with the clinical thermometer.
qs.kf:
☛ Inventor of Clinical Thermometer → Thomas Clifford Allbutt
☛ Inventor of Stethoscope → René Laennec
☛ Inventor of X-ray Machine → Wilhelm Röntgen
☛ Inventor of Microscope → Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
☛ Nationality of Thomas Allbutt → British (English)

q: Antonio Meucci is associated with the invention of:
A. Telephone
B. automobile
C. LED
D. Industrial Robot
qs.e: Antonio Meucci was an Italian inventor who made significant contributions to the development of the telephone. He demonstrated a device for voice communication in 1854, which he called the 'teletrofono'. Although Alexander Graham Bell received the first commercial telephone patent, the US Congress recognized Meucci's contribution in 2002, crediting him with the invention of the telephone. This technological innovation revolutionized the field of communication, laying the foundation for modern telephony. Meucci's work involved creating a voice-communication link by using electricity to transmit sound through wires.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of Meucci's invention → Teletrofono
☛ Who patented the telephone → Alexander Graham Bell
☛ Year US Congress recognized Meucci → 2002
☛ Meucci's nationality → Italian
☛ Year of first telephone demonstration → 1854

q: The Kyoto protocol was entered into force in the year:
qs.e: The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions. It was adopted in 1997 but entered into force only after at least 55 countries, representing 55% of global emissions, ratified it. This condition was met in 2005 when Russia ratified the protocol. Thus, the Kyoto Protocol came into effect on 16 February 2005. It was the first legally binding agreement under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to combat climate change. Developed countries were assigned emission reduction targets under this protocol.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Kyoto Protocol adopted? → 1997
☛ When did the Kyoto Protocol enter into force? → 2005
☛ Which country's ratification allowed Kyoto Protocol to enter into force? → Russia
☛ Objective of Kyoto Protocol? → Reduce greenhouse gas emissions
☛ Kyoto Protocol is related to which framework? → UNFCCC

q: Which of the following is the first animal to go to into spatial orbit on board the Soviet Sputnik 2?
A. Laika,a dog
B. Albert, a mouse
C. Belka, a monkey
D. Baker, a rabbit
qs.e: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2 on November 3, 1957, carrying a dog named Laika, making her the first animal to enter Earth's orbit. The mission aimed to test whether a living being could survive the pressures and weightlessness of space travel. Laika spent a few hours in orbit but died due to overheating and stress. This mission was a crucial step in space exploration, paving the way for human spaceflight. The other options are incorrect: Albert was a monkey, Belka was a dog that flew later, and Baker was a monkey.
qs.kf:
☛ First animal to orbit Earth → Laika (dog)
☛ Year of Sputnik 2 launch → 1957
☛ Purpose of Laika's mission → Test effects of space travel
☛ Cause of Laika's death → Overheating and stress
☛ First animals in space → Fruit flies (1947, USA)

q: When was the GSLV used in India for the first time?
qs.e: India's GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) was first used on April 18, 2001 to launch the GSAT-1 satellite into a geosynchronous orbit. This mission was a major milestone for the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) as it marked India's capability to launch heavy satellites into geostationary orbit. Although the first launch was not fully successful, it laid the foundation for future developments like GSLV Mk2 and GSLV Mk3. The vehicle uses a cryogenic engine in its upper stage. Hence, the correct answer is 2001.
qs.kf:
☛ First GSLV launch of India → April 18, 2001
☛ Payload of first GSLV → GSAT-1 satellite
☛ Developer of GSLV → ISRO
☛ Fuel used in GSLV's upper stage → Cryogenic engine
☛ Purpose of GSLV → Placing satellites in geostationary orbit

q: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.' By whom it is said?
qs.e: The iconic quote was spoken by American astronaut Neil Armstrong on July 20, 1969, as he became the first human to set foot on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission. He was the mission commander. This event marked a monumental achievement in human history, as it was the first time a person landed on a celestial body other than Earth. Armstrong's words highlighted the scientific and cultural significance of the mission. He was accompanied by Edwin Buzz Aldrin, who also walked on the Moon, while Michael Collins orbited above in the command module. The Moon landing was a key victory for the United States in the Space Race against the Soviet Union.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first Moon landing? → July 20, 1969
☛ Who was the commander of Apollo 11? → Neil Armstrong
☛ Who was the second person to walk on the Moon? → Buzz Aldrin
☛ What was the name of the Apollo 11 mission's lunar module? → Eagle
☛ Which country first landed humans on the Moon? → United States of America

q: World Environment Day is celebrated on
A. 5th April
B. 15th May
C. 5th June
D. 15th July
qs.e: World Environment Day is celebrated annually on 5th June. It was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972. The first celebration took place in 1974. The day aims to raise global awareness about environmental protection and encourage political attention. Each year, a specific theme is chosen to highlight pressing environmental issues. The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) leads the organization of events. Countries worldwide, including India, organize various activities and campaigns on this day. This observance serves as a platform for individuals, communities, and governments to take action towards a sustainable future.

☛ When was the first World Environment Day? → 1974
☛ When was World Environment Day established? → 1972
☛ Who leads World Environment Day? → UNEP
☛ What is the aim of World Environment Day? → To raise awareness about environmental protection

q: World No-Tobacco Day falls on
A. 1st May
B. 31st May
C. 1st June
D. 30th June
qs.e: World No-Tobacco Day is observed annually on 31st May. It was established by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1987 to raise awareness about the dangers of tobacco use. Tobacco causes over 8 million deaths each year globally. The day aims to protect people from tobacco-related diseases such as lung cancer, heart disease, and stroke. The WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) is a key treaty for tobacco control.

☛ WHO tobacco control treaty → FCTC

q: The 103rd Indian annual Science Congress was held in
A. Bengaluru
B. Mysore
C. New Delhi
D. Lucknow
qs.e: The 103rd Indian Science Congress was held in Mysore. The Indian Science Congress (ISC) is a prestigious annual convention, founded in 1914. It provides a platform for scientists and researchers across the country. The 103rd session took place in 2016 at the University of Mysore, Mysore. The theme was "Science and Technology for Inclusive Development." Previous sessions were held in various cities, but for the 103rd, Mysore was chosen as the venue.

☛ Main objective of the Indian Science Congress? → Promote scientific research

q: National Science Day falls on
A. 26th February
B. 27th February
C. 28th February
D. 29th February
qs.e: National Science Day is celebrated every year on 28th February to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by the Indian physicist Sir C.V. Raman, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1930. The day aims to promote scientific temper, awareness, and appreciation of scientific achievements. It was first observed in 1987. The Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, selects a theme each year, such as 'Science for Global Wellbeing'.
qs.kf:
☛ When is National Science Day celebrated? → 28th February
☛ Who discovered the Raman Effect? → Sir C.V. Raman
☛ In which year did Sir C.V. Raman get the Nobel Prize? → 1930
☛ When was the first National Science Day observed? → 1987
☛ Which department organizes National Science Day? → Department of Science and Technology

q: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) was established in:
qs.e: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) was established on 29 July 1957 as an autonomous intergovernmental organization. Its headquarters is located in Vienna, Austria. The IAEA aims to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and prevent its military application. It was established under the auspices of the United Nations as part of the 'Atoms for Peace' initiative. The organization plays a crucial role in nuclear safety, security, and technical cooperation. As of 2025, the IAEA has 178 member states. It also monitors the implementation of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).
qs.kf:
☛ IAEA Headquarters → Vienna, Austria
☛ IAEA Established Year → 1957
☛ IAEA Objective → Promote peaceful use of nuclear energy and non-proliferation
☛ IAEA established under which initiative → Atoms for Peace
☛ Number of IAEA member states (as of 2025) → 178

q: Ban Ki-Moon, the eighth Secretary General of UN, is from:
qs.e: Ban Ki-moon served as the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations from 2007 to 2016. He is a diplomat from South Korea, born on 13 June 1944 in Chungju, South Korea. He previously served as South Korea's Minister of Foreign Affairs and played a key role in nuclear disarmament talks on the Korean Peninsula. He was the first Asian Secretary-General since U Thant. Under his leadership, the UN focused on climate change, the Sustainable Development Goals, and gender equality. His tenure emphasized global cooperation and multilateralism.
qs.kf:
☛ Who succeeded Ban Ki-moon as UN Secretary-General? → António Guterres
☛ Ban Ki-moon's birthplace? → Chungju, South Korea
☛ Ban Ki-moon's tenure? → 2007 to 2016
☛ First Asian UN Secretary-General? → U Thant (Burma)
☛ Key initiative under Ban Ki-moon? → Promoting Sustainable Development Goals

q: The earlier name of Bhabha Atomic Research Center was________.
o: Indira Gandhi Center for Atomic Research
Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited
qs.e: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is India's premier nuclear research facility. It was established by Dr. Homi J. Bhabha and was originally called the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET). After Dr. Bhabha's death in 1966, it was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in his honor. It is located at Trombay, Mumbai and functions under the Department of Atomic Energy. Major research reactors like Apsara, Cirus, and Dhruva are situated here.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of BARC? → Bhabha Atomic Research Centre
☛ Where is BARC located? → Trombay, Mumbai
☛ Who was the first director of BARC? → Dr. Homi J. Bhabha
☛ Which was the first nuclear reactor in BARC? → Apsara
☛ Under which department does BARC function? → Department of Atomic Energy

q: ISRO has established the _______, at Bharati station, Antarctica, for receiving IRS data.
qs.e: ISRO has established the AGEOS (Antarctic Ground Station for Earth Observation Satellites) at Bharati station, Antarctica, for receiving IRS (Indian Remote Sensing Satellite) data. This station enables continuous data reception from earth observation satellites in polar regions. AGEOS is operated by NRSC (National Remote Sensing Centre). Due to its location in Antarctica, it provides better coverage for polar-orbiting satellites. NCAOR (National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research) is not related to this station. IMGEOS is not a valid station. Hence, the correct option is AGEOS.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of AGEOS? → Antarctic Ground Station for Earth Observation Satellites
☛ Which organization operates AGEOS? → NRSC (National Remote Sensing Centre)
☛ Where is AGEOS located? → Bharati station, Antarctica
☛ What is the purpose of AGEOS? → To receive IRS (Indian Remote Sensing Satellite) data
☛ What is the full form of NCAOR? → National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research

q: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre is located at:
qs.e: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) is located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. It is the lead centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) responsible for the design and development of satellite launch vehicles. VSSC was established in 1963 under the guidance of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. Major launch vehicles like PSLV and GSLV were developed here. The centre is situated near the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS). It plays a crucial role in India's space program.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is ISRO headquarters located? → Bengaluru
☛ Where is Satish Dhawan Space Centre located? → Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh
☛ Where is Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre located? → Valiamala, Thiruvananthapuram
☛ Where is U R Rao Satellite Centre located? → Bengaluru
☛ Where is Space Applications Centre located? → Ahmedabad

q: In which year did India conduct its second nuclear test in Pokhran?
qs.e: India conducted its second nuclear test in 1998 at Pokhran, Rajasthan. This test was codenamed Operation Shakti and took place on May 11 and 13, 1998. It included five nuclear explosions, one of which was a thermonuclear device. This test declared India as a nuclear weapon state and led to international sanctions. India's first nuclear test was conducted in 1974 at the same location, codenamed Smiling Buddha.
qs.kf:
☛ When was India's first nuclear test? → 1974
☛ What is Operation Shakti related to? → 1998 nuclear tests
☛ Pokhran is located in which state? → Rajasthan
☛ How many explosions were in India's 1998 test? → Five
☛ What was the codename of the 1974 test? → Smiling Buddha

q: Which of the following satellites is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory?
qs.e: Astrosat is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, launched on 28 September 2015 aboard PSLV-C30. It carries five instruments capable of observing in ultraviolet, visible, X-ray, and gamma-ray bands. Developed by ISRO, it marked a milestone in Indian astronomy. Prior to Astrosat, India had satellites like INSAT and IRS for communication and Earth observation, but no dedicated astronomical observatory. Astrosat has significantly contributed to India's self-reliance in space-based astrophysics.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first multi-wavelength space observatory → Astrosat
☛ Astrosat launch year → 2015
☛ Launch vehicle → PSLV-C30
☛ Wavelength bands observed by Astrosat → UV, visible, X-ray, gamma-ray
☛ Developer of Astrosat → ISRO

q: Which was the first vehicle to soft-land safely on the surface of the Moon?
qs.e: The first vehicle to safely soft-land on the Moon's surface was the Soviet Union's Luna 9. It landed on February 3, 1966, and transmitted the first photographic images from the lunar surface to Earth. Prior to this, Luna 2 (1959) had crash-landed on the Moon. Apollo 17 (1972) was a crewed mission, while Sputnik 25 (1963) and Ranger 6 (1964) failed. Luna 9's success marked a milestone in lunar exploration, paving the way for subsequent Soviet Luna series and the American Surveyor program.
qs.kf:
☛ First spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon → Luna 9 (1966)
☛ First human-made object to reach the Moon → Luna 2 (1959)
☛ First human to walk on the Moon → Neil Armstrong (Apollo 11, 1969)
☛ First American spacecraft to land on the Moon → Surveyor 1 (1966)
☛ India's Moon soft-landing mission → Chandrayaan-3 (2023)

q: Which of the following scientist have no contribution in the Nuclear field in India?
qs.e: Homi J Bhabha is considered the father of the Indian nuclear program. Sekhar Basu played a key role in India's nuclear submarine program and reactor design. Raja Ramanna led the Pokhran nuclear test. C N R Rao is a renowned chemist whose work is in solid-state chemistry and nanotechnology, but he has no contribution in the nuclear field.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of the Indian nuclear program? → Homi J Bhabha
☛ Who led the Pokhran nuclear test (1974)? → Raja Ramanna
☛ Who was associated with India's nuclear submarine program? → Sekhar Basu
☛ In which field is C.N.R. Rao famous? → Solid-state chemistry and nanotechnology
☛ What was India's first nuclear reactor? → Apsara

q: Who was the Chairman of Atomic Energy Commission at the time of India’s First nuclear Test at Pokhran in 1974?
qs.e: India's first nuclear test was conducted on May 18, 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan, codenamed 'Smiling Buddha'. At that time, Homi Sethna was the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission. He served from 1972 to 1983. Raja Ramanna was the director of the nuclear test, while Rajagopala Chidambaram and APJ Abdul Kalam were key team members. Homi Sethna was a renowned chemical engineer and played a crucial role in India's nuclear program. Under his leadership, the test was successfully conducted.
qs.kf:
☛ Codename of 1974 Pokhran test → Smiling Buddha
☛ Test director → Raja Ramanna
☛ Atomic Energy Commission Chairman (1972-1983) → Homi Sethna
☛ Date of test → 18 May 1974
☛ Prime Minister at time of test → Indira Gandhi

q: The first Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) of India in 1964 was a Collaborative venture between Atomic Energy of _______ Ltd and NPCIL of India.
qs.e: India's first Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) was established in 1964 as a collaborative venture between Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd (AECL) and India's NPCIL. This reactor is located at Rajasthan and is known as the Rajasthan Atomic Power Station (RAPS). It was part of the India-Canada nuclear agreement aimed at boosting nuclear power generation in India. The reactor uses natural uranium as fuel and heavy water (D2O) as both moderator and coolant. This partnership laid the foundation for the development of PHWR technology in India.
qs.kf:
☛ With which country did India collaborate for the first PHWR? → Canada
☛ Where was the first PHWR installed? → Rajasthan (RAPS)
☛ What fuel is used in PHWR? → Natural uranium
☛ What serves as moderator in PHWR? → Heavy water (D2O)
☛ What is the full form of NPCIL? → Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd

q: Who predicted 'nuclear technology is going to be very essential and not just in the power sector but for other societal uses intended for betterment of life'?
qs.e: The father of India's nuclear program, Homi J Bhabha, predicted that nuclear technology would become essential not only for power generation but also for other societal applications like medicine, agriculture, and industry. He envisioned that nuclear energy would provide a clean and affordable source of power, crucial for developing nations. Bhabha founded the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) and laid the foundation for India's three-stage nuclear program. He strongly advocated for the peaceful use of nuclear energy. His foresight helped India achieve self-reliance in nuclear technology. His prediction highlighted the transformative potential of nuclear science beyond just electricity.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is known as the father of India's nuclear program? → Homi J Bhabha
☛ Who established BARC? → Homi J Bhabha
☛ Name of India's first nuclear reactor? → Apsara
☛ Which institute did Homi Bhabha found? → Tata Institute of Fundamental Research
☛ Who emphasized peaceful uses of nuclear energy? → Homi J Bhabha

q: When is National Pollution Prevention Day observed in India?
qs.e: National Pollution Prevention Day is observed annually on December 2nd in memory of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1984). This day aims to raise awareness about pollution control and environmental protection. It is organized by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The day focuses on preventing industrial accidents and reducing pollution-related damage. The Bhopal gas leak is considered one of the world's worst industrial disasters, involving the release of methyl isocyanate gas. The observance emphasizes the importance of disaster preparedness and sustainable industrial practices.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year did the Bhopal Gas Tragedy occur? → 1984
☛ Which gas leaked during the Bhopal Gas Tragedy? → Methyl isocyanate (MIC)
☛ Which ministry organizes National Pollution Prevention Day? → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Which company was responsible for the Bhopal Gas Tragedy? → Union Carbide
☛ What is the main objective of National Pollution Prevention Day? → Pollution control and awareness

q: Which of the following dates is commemorated as National Technology Day in India?
qs.e: India observes National Technology Day annually on May 11. This day commemorates the successful Pokhran-II nuclear tests conducted in 1998, also known as Operation Shakti. On this day, India detonated five nuclear devices with code names Shakti-1 and Shakti-2. The day honors the country's scientific and technological achievements. The tests were carried out under the leadership of then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The celebration of National Technology Day began in 1999. It symbolizes India's self-reliance and scientific progress.
qs.kf:
☛ Pokhran-II test code name → Operation Shakti
☛ Prime Minister during Pokhran-II → Atal Bihari Vajpayee
☛ First National Technology Day → 1999
☛ Pokhran-I test year → 1974
☛ Pokhran-I code name → Smiling Buddha

q: UN World Wildlife day is celebrated on ______.
qs.e: United Nations World Wildlife Day is celebrated annually on 3rd March. This day aims to raise awareness about the protection of wild animals and plants globally. It marks the anniversary of the signing of CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) in 1973. The day was established by the United Nations General Assembly through a resolution adopted on 20 December 2013. Its main theme highlights the threats to species survival due to wildlife crimes and human activities. Each year, a specific theme is chosen to focus on various aspects of wildlife conservation, such as digital innovation or sustainable development.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of World Wildlife Day → 3rd March
☛ Full form of CITES → Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
☛ Year of signing of CITES → 1973
☛ Year UN General Assembly established this day → 2013
☛ Theme of World Wildlife Day 2024 → Connecting People and Planet: Digital Innovation in Wildlife Conservation

q: The mission on Nano Science and Technology (Nano Mission) was launched in ________.
qs.e: The Mission on Nano Science and Technology (Nano Mission) was launched by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India in May 2007. Its objective is to promote research and development in the field of nanotechnology, develop infrastructure, and build human resources. The mission was initially launched for a period of five years and has been extended subsequently. Under this mission, centers of excellence in nanoscience were established and various research projects were funded. It aims to make India a global leader in nanotechnology.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Nano Mission launched? → 2007
☛ Under which ministry/department does the Nano Mission fall? → Department of Science and Technology (DST)
☛ What is the main objective of the Nano Mission? → Research and development in nanotechnology
☛ What was the initial duration of the Nano Mission? → Five years
☛ What was established under the Nano Mission? → Centers of Excellence

q: Who among the following joined the 969 Railway Engineer Regiment of Territorial Army (TA) in 2011? She was the first female jawan in the Indian Army.
qs.e: Sapper Shanti Tigga was the first female jawan in the Indian Army. She made history by joining the 969 Railway Engineer Regiment of the Territorial Army (TA) in 2011. She hailed from West Bengal and came from a military family. Shanti Tigga served as a Rifleman and was later promoted to the rank of Lance Naik. Tragically, she died in 2012. This was a historic moment for women in the army, as earlier women were only recruited as officers.
qs.kf:
☛ First female jawan in Indian Army → Sapper Shanti Tigga
☛ Joined as Rifleman → 969 Railway Engineer Regiment (TA), 2011
☛ Home state → West Bengal
☛ Later promoted to → Lance Naik
☛ Shanti Tigga died in → 2012

name: Set 2 · Q50–98
sub: Static GK - Science, Technology, Inventions & Space

q: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was introduced in India in:
qs.e: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in India in 1981. This act was formulated to prevent, control, and reduce air pollution, and to improve air quality. It was enacted following the 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment. The act established the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards to implement pollution control measures. It sets emission standards for industries and requires them to obtain licenses. The act is crucial for environmental protection and public health. It empowers authorities to take legal action against violators and to monitor air quality across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act enacted? → 1981
☛ What is the central board under this act? → Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
☛ Main objective of the act? → Prevention and control of air pollution
☛ Which international conference influenced this act? → Stockholm Conference 1972
☛ What is required from industries under this act? → Licenses and compliance with standards

q: Which Indian born Scottish inventor pioneered the development of the cash machine also called Automated Teller Machine (ATM)?
qs.e: John Shepherd-Barron was an Indian-born Scottish inventor who pioneered the development of the ATM (Automated Teller Machine). He was born in 1925 in Shillong, India. He installed the world's first ATM in 1967 at a Barclays Bank branch in Enfield, London. This ATM used cheques instead of plastic cards. Later, the modern ATM card was invented by James Goodfellow. John Shepherd-Barron was awarded the OBE (Order of the British Empire) in 2005 for his invention.
qs.kf:
☛ When and where was the first ATM installed? → 1967, London (Enfield) at Barclays Bank
☛ Who invented the ATM? → John Shepherd-Barron
☛ Where was the first ATM that accepted banknotes installed? → The first ATM used cheques, not banknotes
☛ Who invented the ATM card? → James Goodfellow
☛ Which honour was awarded to John Shepherd-Barron? → OBE (Order of the British Empire)

q: In which of the following states the Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were used for the first time in India?
qs.e: The first use of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) in India took place in 1982 in the Paravoor assembly constituency of Kerala. It was a pilot project covering only 50 polling booths. Subsequently, trials were conducted in some booths of Delhi in 1983 and in Jaipur, Rajasthan in 1984. However, the widespread use of EVMs across the country began in 1998. The Election Commission of India has been a pioneer in promoting the use of EVMs for free and fair elections.
qs.kf:
☛ Where were EVMs first used in India? → Paravoor, Kerala
☛ When was the first EVM use? → 1982
☛ How many booths in the first pilot? → 50 booths
☛ When did EVMs start being used widely? → 1998
☛ Who introduced EVMs in India? → Election Commission of India

q: What ingredient is put in bread to make it rise?
qs.e: Yeast is added to bread dough to make it rise. Yeast is a type of fungus that carries out fermentation. When mixed with flour and water, it consumes sugars and produces carbon dioxide gas. This gas forms small bubbles in the dough, causing it to expand and become light and spongy after baking. The most commonly used yeast in bread making is Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). Without yeast, bread would be dense and flat.
qs.kf:
☛ Main ingredient for bread rising → Yeast
☛ Process by which yeast raises bread → Fermentation
☛ Gas produced by yeast → Carbon dioxide
☛ Type of organism yeast is → Unicellular fungus
☛ Yeast species used in bread industry → Saccharomyces cerevisiae

q: In which year was the Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology established?
qs.e: The Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology (RRCAT) was established in the year 1984 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. It functions under the Department of Atomic Energy of India and is dedicated to research in advanced technologies, particularly laser and accelerator technology. The centre is named after the renowned Indian physicist Dr. Raja Ramanna. It plays a vital role in the development of nuclear science and technology in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of establishment of RRCAT → 1984
☛ Location of RRCAT → Indore, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Governing department → Department of Atomic Energy
☛ Main research areas → Laser and accelerator technology
☛ Named after → Dr. Raja Ramanna

q: Where is one of the lead centers of Indian Space Research Organization, Satish Dhawan Space Centre located?
qs.e: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) is a major lead center of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), located in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. It serves as India's primary spaceport. Several important missions have been launched from here, including the Chandrayaan series and Mangalyaan. SDSC was earlier known as Sriharikota Range (SHAR) and was renamed in 2002 in honor of former ISRO chairman Satish Dhawan. The center is generally referred to as Sriharikota or SHAR.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest launch center of ISRO → Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)
☛ Old name of SDSC → Sriharikota Range (SHAR)
☛ SDSC named after whom → Dr. Satish Dhawan
☛ Location of SDSC → Sriharikota island, Andhra Pradesh
☛ First satellite launched from SDSC → Bhaskara-1 (1979)

q: In which year did India launch an imaging satellite called the Technology Experiment Satellite (TES)?
qs.e: India launched the Technology Experiment Satellite (TES) on 22 October 2001 using the PSLV-C3 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. This imaging satellite was primarily designed to provide high-resolution imagery for both civilian and military applications. TES captured images with a 1-meter resolution, which was a remarkable achievement for India at that time. The satellite was developed by ISRO and played a key role in advancing self-reliance in space technology. The TES mission also included on-orbit testing and validation of various technologies.
qs.kf:
☛ Which agency developed the TES imaging satellite? → ISRO
☛ Which rocket launched TES? → PSLV-C3
☛ What was the resolution of TES? → 1 meter
☛ TES is what type of satellite? → Technology Experiment Satellite
☛ Which was India's first technology experiment satellite? → TES

q: Which of the following ministries launched a theme song 'Hawa Aane De' on air pollution in 2019?
qs.e: In 2019, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change launched a theme song 'Hawa Aane De' for air pollution awareness. This song was introduced under the Swachh Vayu Abhiyan (Clean Air Campaign), aiming to educate the public about the impacts of air pollution and preventive measures. The song was composed and sung by renowned artists to ensure wide reach. Through this initiative, the ministry encouraged citizens to take actions to reduce pollution, such as using public transport and reducing waste burning. The song emphasized the importance of clean air for health and environment.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched the song 'Hawa Aane De'? → Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Under which campaign was this song introduced? → Swachh Vayu Abhiyan
☛ Which song was launched for air pollution awareness? → Hawa Aane De
☛ What is the primary function of the Environment Ministry? → Environmental protection and climate change
☛ What is the objective of Swachh Vayu Abhiyan? → Improve air quality

q: Which of the following organisations incorporated New Space India Limited (NSIL) on March 6, 2019, for commercially utilising research development activities in the area of space?
qs.e: New Space India Limited (NSIL) was incorporated by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on March 6, 2019. It is a government company functioning under ISRO, with the primary objective of commercially utilizing research and development activities in the space sector. NSIL brings ISRO's technological and scientific capabilities to the market, including satellite manufacturing, launch services, and commercialization of space products. It was formed to promote private participation in the space sector and act as ISRO's commercial arm. It operates under the Department of Space of the Government of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of NSIL located? → Bengaluru, Karnataka
☛ What is the administrative body of NSIL? → Department of Space
☛ Who controls NSIL? → ISRO
☛ What is the purpose of NSIL? → Commercialization of space research
☛ In which year was NSIL established? → March 6, 2019

q: Name the Metro Rail Corporation which has become the first ever project in the country to receive power generated from a waste-to-energy plant.
qs.e: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has become the first project in the country to receive power generated from a waste-to-energy plant. The plant is located at Ghodapur in Delhi and is operated by the East Delhi Municipal Corporation. This initiative will not only help in waste disposal but also generate clean energy. DMRC has signed an agreement to purchase 550 kilowatts of electricity from this plant, which will be used for metro operations. This step is a significant move towards urban waste management and promoting renewable energy. Delhi Metro is already known for its eco-friendly initiatives like regenerative braking systems and solar energy usage.
qs.kf:
☛ First metro to get power from waste-to-energy plant → Delhi Metro
☛ Ghodapur plant operated by → East Delhi Municipal Corporation
☛ Power purchased by DMRC → 550 kilowatts
☛ Other environmental initiatives of Delhi Metro → Regenerative braking and solar energy
☛ Main benefit of waste-to-energy → Waste disposal and clean energy generation

q: Internet was started in India on:
qs.e: Internet was started in India on 15th August 1995. On this day, the country was connected to the internet via video conferencing. This service was provided by VSNL (Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited). Initially, the internet speed was very slow and limited to a few cities. Gradually, it expanded and today India is one of the largest internet user bases in the world. This date coincides with India's Independence Day, making it even more significant.
qs.kf:
☛ Company that launched internet service in India → VSNL
☛ First city to be connected to the internet in India → Delhi
☛ Year of establishment of VSNL → 1986
☛ Number of internet users in India (2023) → Approximately 800 million
☛ Launch of mobile internet in India → 2009 (3G)

q: In which year was the World Happiness Report published for the first time?
qs.e: The World Happiness Report was first published in 2012. It is published by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN). The report ranks countries based on their happiness levels, measured by factors such as GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption. The first report did not name Finland as the happiest country; Finland topped the rankings in later years.
qs.kf:
☛ Who publishes the World Happiness Report? → United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)
☛ Which is the happiest country in the 2024 report? → Finland
☛ How many factors measure happiness? → 6 (GDP, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity, corruption perception)
☛ Which was the happiest country in the first report? → Denmark
☛ Based on which survey is the report prepared? → Gallup World Poll

q: The first nuclear bomb experiment test in India was carried out in the year:
qs.e: India's first nuclear bomb test was conducted in 1974 at Pokhran (Rajasthan), codenamed 'Smiling Buddha'. The test took place on 18 May 1974, making India a nuclear weapon state. It involved the detonation of an 8 kiloton nuclear device. The project, initiated under Nehru's guidance, was led by Dr. Raja Ramanna. After this test, India conducted its second nuclear test in 1998, known as Pokhran-II or Operation Shakti.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the codename of Pokhran-I test? → Smiling Buddha
☛ What was the yield of Pokhran-I explosion? → 8 kilotons
☛ When was India's second nuclear test conducted? → 1998 (Pokhran-II)
☛ In which state was Pokhran test conducted? → Rajasthan
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during Pokhran-I? → Indira Gandhi

q: What is the full form of EVM?
qs.e: The full form of EVM is Electronic Voting Machine. It is used in elections to simplify and make the voting process transparent. The EVM was invented under the guidance of the Election Commission of India. It was first used in India in 1982 in the Parur assembly constituency of Kerala as a trial. The EVM consists of two units: the Control Unit and the Balloting Unit. This machine is battery-operated and does not require any external electrical connection. EVMs have made the voting process more secure and efficient.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of EVM? → Electronic Voting Machine
☛ When was EVM first used in India? → 1982
☛ What are the two main parts of an EVM? → Control Unit and Balloting Unit
☛ How is the EVM powered? → Battery
☛ Under whose guidance was EVM invented? → Election Commission of India

q: 'World Environment Day' is annually celebrated on _______.
qs.e: World Environment Day is celebrated annually on 5th June. It was established by the United Nations in 1972 following the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment. The day aims to raise global awareness about environmental protection and encourage action. Each year, a specific theme is chosen to focus on pressing environmental issues. For example, the theme for 2023 was "Beat Plastic Pollution". This day mobilizes governments, organizations, and citizens worldwide to take positive environmental actions, from tree planting to clean-up campaigns. It serves as a reminder of our collective responsibility to safeguard the planet for future generations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was World Environment Day established? → 1972
☛ When was the first World Environment Day celebrated? → 1973
☛ What was the theme of World Environment Day 2023? → Beat Plastic Pollution
☛ Which organization coordinates World Environment Day? → United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
☛ In which year was the Stockholm Conference held? → 1972

q: The International Day of Light is observed on:
qs.e: The International Day of Light is observed annually on 16th May. It was proclaimed by UNESCO and first celebrated in 2018. The date was chosen to commemorate the first successful operation of a laser by physicist Theodore Maiman on 16th May 1960. The laser is a special form of light that has revolutionized science, medicine, communication, and industry. The day aims to highlight the importance of light and light-based technologies in various fields, promoting global awareness and appreciation of their contributions to society.
qs.kf:
☛ When is International Day of Light observed? → 16th May
☛ Who invented the first laser? → Theodore Maiman
☛ When was the laser invented? → 1960
☛ Which organization proclaimed the International Day of Light? → UNESCO
☛ What is the purpose of the International Day of Light? → To promote the importance of light and laser technology

q: In recognition technology OMR is used, what does M stand for?
qs.e: OMR stands for Optical Mark Recognition. It is a technology used to read hand-made marks on paper. The 'M' in OMR stands for Mark. OMR is primarily used for evaluating answer sheets in competitive exams. This technology uses optical sensors to detect marks on paper and converts them into digital data. OMR machines work with high accuracy and speed, enabling the evaluation of large numbers of answer sheets in a short time. In addition, OMR is used in surveys, opinion polls, and data collection. The technology relies on predefined positions where marks are expected, making it efficient for standardized testing. OMR is distinct from OCR (Optical Character Recognition), which reads printed text rather than marks.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of OMR? → Optical Mark Recognition
☛ OMR is mainly used for? → Evaluating answer sheets
☛ What type of sensor is used in OMR? → Optical sensor
☛ Which similar technology is used for reading printed text? → OCR (Optical Character Recognition)
☛ Is OMR a pen-based system? → No, it is a penless system

q: The Indian Air Force was established on:
qs.e: The Indian Air Force was established on 8 October 1932 as an auxiliary air force of the British Empire. It initially consisted of only 5 pilot officers and 19 airmen. The first flight took place on 1 April 1933 with No. 1 Squadron formed with 5 pilots and Westland Wapiti aircraft. After independence, it was renamed the Indian Air Force on 26 January 1950. 8 October is celebrated annually as Air Force Day.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first chief of the Indian Air Force? → Air Marshal Sir Thomas Elmhirst
☛ Who was the first Indian chief of the Indian Air Force? → Air Marshal Subroto Mukerjee
☛ When is Air Force Day celebrated? → 8 October
☛ When was the Air Force renamed after independence? → 26 January 1950
☛ How many pilots initially? → 5 officers

q: When did India carry out the first nuclear test at Pokhran?
qs.e: India conducted its first nuclear test on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan. The test was codenamed 'Smiling Buddha'. It was a peaceful nuclear explosion intended to demonstrate India's nuclear capability. At the time of the test, Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister, and Dr. Raja Ramanna was the chief scientist heading the project. The test was supported by the Department of Atomic Energy and the Indian Army.
qs.kf:
☛ Codename of Pokhran-I test → Smiling Buddha
☛ Prime Minister during the first nuclear test → Indira Gandhi
☛ Chief scientist of the nuclear test → Dr. Raja Ramanna
☛ Year of Pokhran-II tests → 1998
☛ Location of India's first nuclear test → Pokhran, Rajasthan

q: Which of the following has developed world's first malaria vaccine for the World Health Organization?
qs.e: The world's first malaria vaccine recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) is RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix), developed by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK). This vaccine targets Plasmodium falciparum, the deadliest malaria parasite. In 2021, WHO approved its widespread use among children in sub-Saharan Africa. The vaccine reduces severe malaria cases and deaths. GSK developed it in collaboration with the PATH Malaria Vaccine Initiative. It is a significant milestone in malaria control.
qs.kf:
☛ Who developed the first malaria vaccine? → GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)
☛ What is the name of the malaria vaccine? → RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)
☛ When did WHO approve it? → 2021
☛ Which parasite does it target? → Plasmodium falciparum
☛ What age group is it for? → Children aged 5 to 17 months

q: What is the name of India’s first planned manned space flight?
qs.e: Gaganyaan is India's first planned manned space flight, being developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). The mission aims to send three astronauts into Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and bring them back safely. Under the Gaganyaan program, unmanned test flights will be conducted first, followed by the crewed mission. This mission will make India the fourth country to send humans into space. The name Gaganyaan is derived from Sanskrit words 'Gagan' (sky) and 'Yaan' (vehicle). The mission will use the LVM3 rocket. It represents a significant step in India's space exploration efforts.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of India's first manned space flight → Gaganyaan
☛ Number of astronauts in Gaganyaan mission → Three
☛ Rocket used for Gaganyaan → LVM3
☛ Organisation developing Gaganyaan → ISRO
☛ India will become the ___ country to send humans to space → Fourth

q: When did the Central Industrial Security Force come into existence in India?
qs.e: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) is one of the central armed police forces of India. It came into existence in 1969 under an Act of Parliament, the CISF Act, 1968. Its primary objective is to provide security to public sector undertakings and industrial establishments. It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs and its headquarters is located in New Delhi. Presently, CISF provides security not only to government but also to private establishments, airports, nuclear plants, and critical infrastructure. It is considered the largest industrial security force in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ When was CISF established? → 1969
☛ Under which ministry does CISF come? → Ministry of Home Affairs
☛ Where is the headquarters of CISF? → New Delhi
☛ Under which act was CISF established? → CISF Act, 1968
☛ What does CISF stand for? → Central Industrial Security Force

q: The approach based on the idea that 'organisms which are more distantly related will accumulate a greater number of differences in their DNA' is called?
qs.e: The given idea is that organisms which are more distantly related will accumulate more differences in their DNA. This concept is central to Molecular phylogeny, which uses DNA, RNA, or protein sequences to infer evolutionary relationships. It is based on the molecular clock hypothesis, which assumes that mutations in DNA accumulate at a roughly constant rate over time. Thus, closely related species show fewer differences, while distantly related ones show many. This approach contrasts with the morphological approach, which relies on physical traits. Molecular phylogeny has become a powerful tool in modern biology to construct phylogenetic trees.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the basis of molecular phylogeny? → Comparison of DNA, RNA, or protein sequences
☛ What does the molecular clock assume? → Mutation rate is constant over time
☛ What does morphological approach rely on? → Physical characteristics
☛ What does phylogeny mean? → Evolutionary history
☛ Which tool is used in molecular phylogeny? → DNA sequencing

q: The laws of inheritance were discovered by:
qs.e: The laws of inheritance were discovered by Gregor Mendel. Mendel was an Austrian scientist who conducted experiments on pea plants and formulated the basic principles of heredity. His laws include the Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation, and Law of Independent Assortment. Mendel's work was rediscovered in the early 20th century by Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von Tschermak. Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution, while Archibald Garrod worked on metabolic disorders.
qs.kf:
☛ On which plant did Mendel perform his experiments? → Pea plant
☛ According to Mendel, how do genes segregate during gamete formation? → Equally
☛ What does the Law of Dominance state? → One trait is dominant over another
☛ The Law of Independent Assortment is related to: → Independent distribution of two or more genes
☛ Who rediscovered Mendel's work? → Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, Erich von Tschermak

q: World Bamboo Day is celebrated every year on ______.
qs.e: World Bamboo Day is celebrated every year on 18th September to raise awareness about the importance of bamboo, its cultural, economic, and environmental benefits. Bamboo is a fast-growing plant that helps in oxygen production and carbon absorption. It is used in construction, furniture, paper, and textiles. The first World Bamboo Day was observed in Thailand in 2009. In India, bamboo is often called 'green gold'.
qs.kf:
☛ When is World Bamboo Day celebrated? → 18th September
☛ What is bamboo often called in India? → Green gold
☛ Where was the first World Bamboo Day celebrated? → Thailand
☛ What type of plant is bamboo? → Fast-growing grass
☛ In which sectors is bamboo used? → Construction, furniture, paper

q: Which of the following is a part of 'global commons'?
qs.e: Global commons refer to resources or areas that do not fall under the jurisdiction of any single nation and are shared for the benefit of all humanity. These include Antarctica, the high seas, outer space, and the atmosphere. Antarctica is governed by the Antarctic Treaty System, which prohibits military activities, mining, and nuclear tests, dedicating the continent to scientific research and environmental protection. Asia, Australia, and Africa are continents under the sovereignty of individual states, thus they are not part of global commons.
qs.kf:
☛ Areas included in global commons → Antarctica, high seas, outer space, atmosphere
☛ Treaty governing Antarctica → Antarctic Treaty (1959)
☛ Purpose of Antarctic Treaty → Peaceful use and scientific cooperation
☛ Concept of global commons → Shared resources beyond national sovereignty
☛ Prohibited activities in Antarctica → Military operations, mining, nuclear tests

q: Gateway of India was built in which of these architectural styles in Mumbai?
qs.e: The Gateway of India in Mumbai was built between 1911 and 1924. Its design was prepared by architect George Wittet. The monument is built in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style, which blends Hindu, Islamic, and British architectural elements. This style features domes, minarets, lattice windows, and arches. The Gateway of India was constructed to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary to India in 1911. It is made of yellow basalt stone and is one of the major tourist attractions in Mumbai.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Gateway of India completed? → 1924
☛ Who was the architect of the Gateway of India? → George Wittet
☛ Which stone is the Gateway of India made of? → Yellow basalt
☛ Why was the Gateway of India built? → To commemorate the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary
☛ Which elements are blended in Indo-Saracenic style? → Hindu, Islamic, and British architectural elements

q: Which of the following options represents "freehand exercise"?
qs.e: Freehand exercise refers to exercises performed without any equipment, using only one's body weight. Calisthenics is a system of exercise that includes movements like push-ups, sit-ups, squats, and other physical activities that require no apparatus. The term originates from Greek words 'kallos' (beauty) and 'sthenos' (strength). Among the other options, Silambam is an Indian martial art that involves a staff, Snooker is a cue sport, and Swordsmanship is a weapon-based sport. Thus, Calisthenics correctly represents freehand exercise.
qs.kf:
☛ Another name for freehand exercise → Calisthenics
☛ Origin of the word Calisthenics → Greek language
☛ Main element used in Calisthenics → Body weight
☛ Silambam is related to → Martial art
☛ Snooker is which type of game → Cue sport

q: Which of the following countries is called 'Land of white elephant'?
qs.e: Thailand is called the 'Land of White Elephant'. The white elephant is considered sacred and a royal symbol in Thailand. Elephants hold great cultural significance and are the national animal of the country. The white elephant symbolizes power, prosperity, and good luck. In Thailand, these elephants are legally protected and used in religious and cultural ceremonies. Among the options, India, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia are not known by this name.
qs.kf:
☛ Former name of Thailand → Siam
☛ Capital of Thailand → Bangkok
☛ Currency of Thailand → Baht
☛ National animal of Thailand → Elephant
☛ National fruit of Thailand → Mangosteen

q: In which of the following states, snow can be experienced in India?
qs.e: Snowfall in India mainly occurs in the Himalayan regions. Uttarakhand includes high Himalayan peaks and hill stations like Kedarnath, Badrinath, Auli, and Munsiyari, which experience heavy snowfall in winter. Tamil Nadu is located in the south and has a tropical climate, so no snowfall occurs there. Rajasthan has a desert climate and Gujarat has a moderate climate, both without snowfall. The high-altitude areas of Uttarakhand have temperatures below freezing, allowing snowfall. None of the other options are Himalayan states.
qs.kf:
☛ State with maximum snowfall in India → Jammu and Kashmir
☛ Famous hill station in Uttarakhand for snowfall → Auli
☛ Himalayan states experiencing snowfall → Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh
☛ Highest mountain location in India with snowfall → Siachen Glacier
☛ Temperature required for snowfall → Below 0°C

q: How much water can a camel store in its hump?
o: It does not store water at all
qs.e: A camel does not store water in its hump; instead, the hump stores fat (adipose tissue). This fat serves as an energy source when food is scarce. Water is stored in the camel's bloodstream and tissues, not in the stomach. Camels can drink up to 40-50 litres of water at once, which is then distributed throughout their body. The fat in the hump also produces metabolic water when broken down, helping the camel survive long periods without drinking. The common misconception that camels store water in their humps is false; the hump is primarily for energy storage.
qs.kf:
☛ What does a camel's hump store? → Fat (adipose tissue)
☛ How much water can a camel drink at once? → 40-50 litres
☛ Scientific name of a one-humped camel? → Camelus dromedarius
☛ What is the use of fat in a camel's hump? → Energy and metabolic water
☛ What shape are camel's red blood cells? → Oval (helps in water balance)

q: NASA is the space agency of -
qs.e: NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) is the space agency of the United States of America. It was established on July 29, 1958. NASA is an independent agency under the U.S. government responsible for space research, aeronautics, and space exploration. It has contributed to Apollo missions (sending humans to the Moon), Space Shuttle program, Hubble Space Telescope, Mars rover missions (such as Perseverance and Curiosity), and the International Space Station. NASA's headquarters is located in Washington D.C. Currently, its primary goals include the Artemis program to return humans to the Moon and a future mission to Mars.
qs.kf:
☛ NASA full form → National Aeronautics and Space Administration
☛ NASA establishment year → 1958
☛ NASA headquarters → Washington D.C., USA
☛ NASA's most famous mission → Apollo 11 (first Moon landing, 1969)
☛ NASA's Artemis program → Return humans to the Moon (by 2025)

q: Which of the following is the first National Park established in India?
qs.e: The first National Park established in India is Corbett National Park, founded in 1936 as Hailey National Park. It was later renamed Ramganga National Park and finally Corbett National Park. Located in Uttarakhand, it is known for Bengal tiger conservation and is part of Project Tiger. Periyar is in Kerala, Velavadar in Gujarat, and Bandipur in Karnataka.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first National Park → Corbett National Park (1936)
☛ Corbett's original name → Hailey National Park
☛ State of Corbett National Park → Uttarakhand
☛ India's largest National Park → Hemis (Ladakh)
☛ Project Tiger started → 1973, from Corbett

q: In which forests did the Khond tribe live in the 19th century?
qs.e: In the 19th century, the Khond tribe mainly inhabited the forests of Odisha. This is a prominent Scheduled Tribe primarily found in Odisha's Kandhamal, Ganjam, Balasore, and Mayurbhanj districts. The Khond tribe is known for its unique cultural traditions, including the Meria sacrifice practice, which the British attempted to abolish in the 19th century. This tribe mainly depends on agriculture and forest produce. Odisha has the largest population of Khonds, while smaller groups are also found in Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state are the Khond tribe found most? → Odisha
☛ Which notorious practice was associated with the Khond tribe? → Meria sacrifice
☛ What is the primary source of income for the Khond tribe? → Agriculture and forest produce
☛ Which is the main region of the Khond tribe? → Kandhamal (Odisha)
☛ Under which category is the Khond tribe classified in India? → Scheduled Tribe

q: When did the Indian Wildlife Protection Act come into force?
qs.e: The Indian Wildlife Protection Act was enacted by Parliament in 1972 and came into force on September 9, 1972. Its aim is to protect endangered species of wildlife, birds, and plants. The Act provides for the establishment of wildlife sanctuaries and national parks. It categorizes species under Schedules I to IV, offering varying degrees of protection. The Act also prescribes stringent penalties for wildlife offenses. In 2022, the Act was amended to further strengthen punishment provisions. This legislation is a cornerstone of biodiversity conservation in India. It covers all aspects of wildlife management, including hunting restrictions, trade bans, and habitat protection. The Act also empowers state governments to declare protected areas.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Wildlife Protection Act come into force? → 1972
☛ How many schedules are there in this Act? → 6 schedules
☛ Which is India's first national park? → Jim Corbett National Park
☛ When was Project Tiger launched? → 1973
☛ When was the latest amendment to the Wildlife Protection Act? → 2022

q: When did the program related to tiger conservation 'Project Tiger' start?
qs.e: Project Tiger is a major tiger conservation program launched by the Government of India on April 1, 1973. Its objective is to halt the declining tiger population and conserve their habitats. The program is responsible for establishing and managing tiger reserves in India. Starting with 9 reserves initially, it now covers 53 tiger reserves. As a result, India has seen a significant increase in its tiger population. The program is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). India has the largest tiger habitat area in the world, and Project Tiger is considered a successful conservation model globally.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Project Tiger launched? → 1973
☛ Who was the first director of Project Tiger? → Kailash Sankhala
☛ Which was the first sanctuary under Project Tiger? → Jim Corbett
☛ What is the main objective of Project Tiger? → Tiger conservation and habitat protection
☛ What does NTCA stand for? → National Tiger Conservation Authority

q: Presently, which of the following advanced molecular methods is used to develop crops with enhanced traits and resilience?
qs.e: CRISPR-Cas9 is an advanced molecular method that allows precise genome editing. This technique is used to develop crops with enhanced traits such as drought tolerance, disease resistance, and improved yield. CRISPR-Cas9 targets a specific DNA sequence and uses the Cas9 enzyme to cut the DNA, enabling gene knockout or modification. Compared to traditional methods like artificial pollination, natural selection, and hybrid seed technology, CRISPR-Cas9 is faster, more accurate, and can introduce novel traits. It has revolutionized agricultural biotechnology.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of CRISPR → Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats
☛ Function of Cas9 → It is an endonuclease enzyme that cuts DNA
☛ Origin of CRISPR-Cas9 → It is derived from a bacterial defense system
☛ First CRISPR-edited crop → Mushroom (Agaricus bisporus)
☛ Other applications of CRISPR-Cas9 → Human disease treatment and gene therapy

q: Match the items in List I with those in List II, and select the correct answer using the codes provided below.

List I (Elephant Corridors) List II (State) (1) Durpong-Doimukh at Khundakhuwa (A) Andhra Pradesh (2) Deosur Corridor (B) Assam (3) Jamui- Jhajha- Chakayi (C) Bihar (4) Nagdhara-Baraud (D) Chhattisgarh
qs.e: Elephant corridors are routes used for elephant movement across states. The Durpong-Doimukh at Khundakhuwa corridor is located in Andhra Pradesh, crucial for elephant conservation in the Eastern Ghats. The Deosur Corridor is in Assam, facilitating elephant movement in the northeastern region. The Jamui-Jhajha-Chakayi corridor is in Bihar, known for elephant routes in the Santhal Pargana area. The Nagdhara-Baraud corridor is in Chhattisgarh, connecting forest areas in central India. Conserving these corridors is vital to reduce human-elephant conflict and maintain elephant populations. The correct matching is 1-(A), 2-(B), 3-(C), 4-(D).
qs.kf:
☛ Durpong-Doimukh corridor → Andhra Pradesh
☛ Deosur corridor → Assam
☛ Jamui-Jhajha-Chakayi corridor → Bihar
☛ Nagdhara-Baraud corridor → Chhattisgarh
☛ Main objective of elephant corridors → Safe movement of elephants

q: Which of the following are the categories to measure the level of Human Development of the countries?
1. Very High
2. Medium
3. Low
4. Below Average
qs.e: The Human Development Index (HDI) classifies countries into four categories: Very High, High, Medium, and Low. Among the given options, 'Very High', 'Medium', and 'Low' are valid HDI categories, whereas 'Below Average' is not a recognized category in the HDI classification. HDI is calculated based on three dimensions: life expectancy, education, and per capita income. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the HDI report annually. Although 'High' is a valid category, it is not listed in the options, but 'Very High', 'Medium', and 'Low' are correctly included as categories.
qs.kf:
☛ What does HDI stand for? → Human Development Index
☛ What are the three dimensions of HDI? → Life expectancy, education, per capita income
☛ Who releases the HDI report? → UNDP
☛ Which country has the highest HDI? → Switzerland (as per 2023-24 report)
☛ What are the four HDI categories? → Very High, High, Medium, Low

q: What was the significant event that took place during the seventy-ninth session of the UN General Assembly in 2024?
qs.e: During the seventy-ninth session of the UN General Assembly in 2024, the 'Summit of the Future' was held. This high-level meeting aimed to strengthen international cooperation to address global challenges such as climate change, poverty, inequality, and the digital divide. At the summit, member states adopted a new declaration called the 'Pact for the Future', which focused on accelerating the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and reforming the multilateral system. The summit also served as a platform for discussions on issues like Security Council reform and digital cooperation.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Summit of the Future held? → 2024
☛ What was the main objective of the summit? → To enhance cooperation for global challenges
☛ Which declaration was adopted at the summit? → Pact for the Future
☛ During which session of which body was the summit held? → UN General Assembly
☛ What is the summit related to? → Sustainable Development Goals

q: As of October 2024, what is India's renewable energy capacity?
qs.e: As of October 2024, India's total renewable energy capacity has reached 201.45 GW. This includes solar energy (about 90 GW), wind energy (about 48 GW), hydropower (about 52 GW), and bioenergy (about 11 GW). The Government of India has set a target of 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030 and has already surpassed the interim target of 200 GW. This achievement of 201.45 GW places India among the global leaders in renewable energy.
qs.kf:
☛ India's 2030 renewable target → 500 GW
☛ Solar energy capacity (2024) → ~90 GW
☛ Wind energy capacity (2024) → ~48 GW
☛ Hydropower capacity (2024) → ~52 GW
☛ Bioenergy capacity (2024) → ~11 GW

q: India is known to have approximately what percentage of the animal species found worldwide according to the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)?
qs.e: India is home to approximately 7.5% of the world's animal species, as per the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI). India boasts immense biodiversity, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fishes, and invertebrates. ZSI regularly catalogues and classifies species. This percentage places India among the 17 mega-diverse countries globally. India's diverse ecosystems, such as the Himalayas, Western Ghats, and coral islands, contribute to this richness. However, many species are threatened and require conservation efforts.
qs.kf:
☛ Percentage of animal species found in India → 7.5%
☛ Percentage of plant species in India → about 8%
☛ Number of mammal species in India → about 440
☛ Number of bird species in India → about 1300
☛ Total number of mega-diverse countries → 17

q: India Post’s Speed Post service was introduced in:
qs.e: India Post launched the Speed Post service in 1986. It is an express mail service that ensures fast delivery of letters and parcels between major cities. The primary objective of Speed Post was to provide customers with a reliable and time-bound service. It has become one of the most popular services of India Post. Under Speed Post, tracking of postal items is also available. Currently, Speed Post is available across almost all parts of the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When was India Post's Speed Post service introduced? → 1986
☛ In which year was Speed Post service launched? → 1986
☛ What is the name of India Post's express service? → Speed Post
☛ What is the main objective of Speed Post? → Fast and reliable delivery
☛ Does Speed Post provide tracking facility? → Yes

q: Manjira is a solid instrument made of ________.
qs.e: Manjira is a solid percussion instrument made of metal. It consists of two small metal plates or bowls that are struck together to produce sound. This instrument is commonly used in devotional music, bhajans, and folk traditions. It is held in the hands and played by clashing the pair. Manjira has been an integral part of Indian classical and folk music for centuries. Besides common metals, it is often made of brass or bronze to produce a clear, resonant sound.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of instrument is Manjira? → Percussion instrument
☛ What material is Manjira made of? → Metal (brass/bronze)
☛ Where is Manjira used? → Bhajans, kirtans, and folk music
☛ How is Manjira played? → By striking two metal plates together
☛ Where is Manjira popular? → Across India

q: Which of the following approaches is associated with Prof. Amartya Sen, as per which building human capabilities in the areas of health, education and access to resources is the key to human development?
qs.e: The Capability Approach, developed by Prof. Amartya Sen, measures human development not by income or commodity availability, but by people's real freedoms and capabilities to achieve well-being. This approach emphasizes building human capabilities in areas like health, education, and access to resources. According to Sen, the goal of development is to expand people's functionings (achievements) and capabilities (freedom to achieve), enabling them to lead lives they value. This approach also influenced the creation of the Human Development Index (HDI).
qs.kf:
☛ Approach associated with Amartya Sen → Capability Approach
☛ Key to human development → Health, education, and access to resources
☛ Core of Capability Approach → Real freedoms of people
☛ Contribution to HDI → Amartya Sen and Mahbub ul Haq
☛ Difference between functionings and capabilities → Functionings are achievements; capabilities are freedom to achieve

q: When was the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity established in India?
qs.e: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) was established in India in 2005 under Section 110 of the Electricity Act, 2003. It is a quasi-judicial body that hears appeals against orders of electricity regulatory commissions. APTEL's headquarters is in New Delhi. Its objective is to ensure speedy dispute resolution in the power sector. The tribunal consists of a Chairperson and up to three other members. The establishment of APTEL provided an independent platform to challenge regulatory decisions in the electricity sector, thereby enhancing transparency and efficiency.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of APTEL? → Appellate Tribunal for Electricity
☛ Under which act was APTEL constituted? → Electricity Act, 2003
☛ What is the establishment year of APTEL? → 2005
☛ Where is the headquarters of APTEL? → New Delhi
☛ Against whose orders does APTEL hear appeals? → Electricity Regulatory Commissions

q: How much FDI did India attract between April 2014 and June 2024?
qs.e: India attracted a total of $689.88 billion in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) between April 2014 and June 2024. This figure is based on official data released by the Government of India. The increase in FDI inflows during this period is primarily attributed to policy reforms and a favorable investment climate created by the government. FDI is crucial for the Indian economy as it provides capital, technology, and employment opportunities. India attracted foreign investment through initiatives like Make in India, Digital India, and other measures.

☛ Under which policy were FDI norms relaxed? → Make in India

☛ What is the main reason for increase in FDI inflows? → Policy reforms

q: In which of the following years did Vodafone start its journey in India?
qs.e: Vodafone started its journey in India in the year 2007 when it acquired Hutchison Essar and launched its brand Vodafone. This acquisition was worth approximately 11 billion USD, one of the largest deals in the Indian telecom sector at that time. Vodafone began its services in India under the name "Vodafone India" and gradually became one of the leading telecom operators in the country. After entering in 2007, Vodafone rapidly expanded its customer base and introduced several innovations, such as mobile wallets and data services. However, later in 2020, Vodafone merged with Idea Cellular, forming Vodafone Idea Limited (Vi).

☛ Which company did Vodafone acquire to enter India? → Hutchison Essar
☛ What was the estimated value of Vodafone's acquisition in 2007? → 11 billion USD
☛ With which company did Vodafone merge? → Idea Cellular
☛ What is the name of the merged company? → Vodafone Idea Limited (Vi)

q: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was a result of which global conference?
qs.e: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was a key outcome of the Earth Summit (United Nations Conference on Environment and Development - UNCED) held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in 1992. This international treaty has three main objectives: the conservation of biological diversity, the sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources. The Earth Summit was attended by leaders from over 150 countries and resulted in several landmark agreements, including the CBD and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The CBD entered into force on 29 December 1993 and currently has 196 parties.
qs.kf:
☛ Earth Summit year and location → 1992, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
☛ Main objectives of CBD → Conservation, sustainable use, and benefit sharing
☛ Full name of Earth Summit → United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED)
☛ Number of parties to CBD → 196 (nearly all UN members)
☛ CBD entered into force → 29 December 1993

q: In which State has India’s first integrated API Green Hydrogen and 2G Ethanol plant been established?
qs.e: India's first integrated API (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient) Green Hydrogen and 2G Ethanol plant has been established in the Una district of Himachal Pradesh. The aim of this plant is to promote clean energy and achieve self-reliance in the pharmaceutical sector. The plant will use green hydrogen for API production, which will help reduce carbon emissions. Additionally, 2G ethanol will be produced from agricultural waste, ensuring both environmental protection and economic benefits. This project aligns with the Government of India's green energy and biofuel policies.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the first integrated API Green Hydrogen and 2G Ethanol plant located? → Himachal Pradesh (Una)

q: Which convention, ratified in 1998, seeks to protect the environment and human health by encouraging shared responsibility and cooperation in the global trade of pesticides and hazardous chemicals?
qs.e: The Rotterdam Convention, ratified in 1998, is a multilateral environmental agreement that promotes shared responsibility and cooperation in the international trade of pesticides and hazardous chemicals. Its goal is to protect human health and the environment from potential harm. The convention is based on the Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure, which requires exporters to obtain the consent of importing countries before shipping certain chemicals. This empowers developing nations to make informed decisions about hazardous imports. The convention lists approximately 50 chemicals and is also known as the 'PIC Convention'. It operates under the auspices of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). The Rotterdam Convention complements the Basel and Stockholm Conventions in the sound management of chemicals.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the key principle of the Rotterdam Convention? → Prior Informed Consent (PIC)
☛ Under which two organizations does the Rotterdam Convention operate? → UNEP and FAO
