qs.e: India is not a member of NATO. NATO is a military alliance established in 1949. India is a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the United Nations (UN), and the G20. The SCO was founded in 2001 and India became a full member in 2017. India is a founding member of the United Nations and has been a member since 1945. India is also a member of the G20, an international forum established in 1999.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NATO established? → 1949
☛ When did India join the SCO? → 2017
☛ When was the United Nations founded? → 1945
☛ When was the G20 formed? → 1999
☛ Where is NATO headquarters located? → Brussels, Belgium

q: What is G-7?
o: 7 IMF-described advanced economies in the world
qs.e: G-7, or the Group of Seven, is an intergovernmental organization consisting of the world's 7 major advanced economies. These include Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The group was formed in 1975, and its main purpose is to discuss and coordinate global economic issues. G-7 countries represent about 50% of global wealth and a significant share of global GDP. However, it is an informal group with no permanent secretariat. Russia was added in 1997 but was expelled in 2014 after its annexation of Crimea, making it G-7 again.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of G-7 → Group of Seven
☛ Number of member countries in G-7 → 7
☛ Year of formation of G-7 → 1975
☛ Only Asian country in G-7 → Japan
☛ Country expelled from G-7 → Russia (in 2014)

q: What is the correct full form of MPEG from below?
qs.e: MPEG stands for Moving Picture Experts Group. It is an international standardization group that develops standards for audio and video compression. It was established in 1988 by ISO and IEC. MPEG standards include MPEG-1, MPEG-2, MPEG-4, MPEG-7, and MPEG-21. MPEG-1 is used in VCDs, MPEG-2 in DVDs and digital TV, and MPEG-4 in streaming media and Blu-ray discs.
qs.kf:
☛ When was MPEG established? → 1988
☛ Where is MPEG-2 used? → DVDs and digital TV
☛ Where is MPEG-4 used? → Streaming media
☛ Which organizations jointly set up MPEG? → ISO and IEC
☛ Which is the most popular MPEG standard? → MPEG-4

q: Which one of these comprises the Golden Quadrilateral?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral is a major highway network in India that connects the four metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. It was the first phase of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), started in 2001. The total length of the Golden Quadrilateral is approximately 5,846 km. The project aims to improve road connectivity and boost economic development between these cities. The network includes National Highways such as NH 2, 8, 4, 5, 6, and others. It is a vital part of India's road transport infrastructure.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Golden Quadrilateral launched? → 2001
☛ What is the total length of the Golden Quadrilateral? → Approximately 5,846 km
☛ Which national highways are part of the Golden Quadrilateral? → NH 2, 8, 4, 5, 6, etc.
☛ Under which project does the Golden Quadrilateral fall? → National Highways Development Project (NHDP)
☛ Which cities are connected by the Golden Quadrilateral? → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata

q: Who coined the phrase 'Survival of the fittest'?
qs.e: Herbert Spencer coined the phrase 'Survival of the fittest' in his book Principles of Biology (1864). It became synonymous with Charles Darwin's theory of natural selection. Spencer applied this concept to society, laying the foundation for Social Darwinism. Darwin later adopted the phrase but did not coin it. Spencer is regarded as a key 19th-century thinker who applied evolutionary ideas to sociology.
qs.kf:
☛ Who coined 'Survival of the fittest'? → Herbert Spencer
☛ Which book first contained this phrase? → Principles of Biology
☛ Who proposed Social Darwinism? → Herbert Spencer
☛ Who gave the theory of natural selection? → Charles Darwin
☛ What is Darwin's major work? → On the Origin of Species

q: As of 30th November 2020, how many countries are members of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
qs.e: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and is headquartered in Washington D.C. As of 30 November 2020, the IMF has a total of 190 member countries. The organization works to promote global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and international trade. Member countries contribute to the Fund and can receive loans when needed. Among the newest members are Andorra (2020) and Monaco. Together with the World Bank, the IMF influences global economic policies.
qs.kf:
☛ When was IMF established? → 1944
☛ Where is the IMF headquarters? → Washington D.C.
☛ What is the objective of IMF? → Global monetary cooperation
☛ Which country became a new member of IMF in 2020? → Andorra
☛ At which conference was IMF founded? → Bretton Woods

q: An artificial leaf to create fuel from sunlight was developed by which Indian organisation?
qs.e: An artificial leaf to create fuel from sunlight was developed by CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research), India's largest research and development organization. This technology mimics the process of photosynthesis to produce fuels like hydrogen using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. The artificial leaf is a significant innovation in clean energy, capable of reducing dependence on fossil fuels. CSIR operates a network of 38 laboratories across India, focusing on diverse scientific fields. BITS Pilani, IIT Mumbai, and DRDO were not involved in this specific project.
qs.kf:
☛ Which organization developed the artificial leaf? → CSIR
☛ Which process does the artificial leaf mimic? → Photosynthesis
☛ What fuel can the artificial leaf produce? → Hydrogen
☛ How many labs does CSIR have? → 38
☛ What does CSIR stand for? → Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

q: Select the correctly matched pair (organisation with their headquarters) from the following pairs.
qs.e: UNIDO (United Nations Industrial Development Organization) has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. This is the correctly matched pair. Other options are incorrect: UNESCO headquarters is in Paris, ILO in Geneva, and IMF in Washington D.C. UNIDO works to promote industrial development. Its headquarters is located at the Vienna International Centre. The organization was established in 1966 and became a specialized agency of the United Nations in 1985.
qs.kf:
☛ UNESCO headquarters → Paris
☛ ILO headquarters → Geneva
☛ UNIDO headquarters → Vienna
☛ IMF headquarters → Washington D.C.
☛ WHO headquarters → Geneva

q: Which organisations have launched Blue Dot hubs to boost protection for children and families on the move across Europe?
qs.e: UNICEF and UNHCR jointly launched Blue Dot hubs to boost protection for children and families on the move across Europe. These hubs are established at key points along migration routes to provide safe spaces, information, legal assistance, and psychosocial support to children and families. The initiative aims to ensure the safety and well-being of displaced populations, particularly children. UNICEF focuses on children's rights and protection, while UNHCR is responsible for safeguarding refugees and asylum seekers. This partnership reflects a comprehensive approach to addressing the refugee and migrant crisis, ensuring that vulnerable groups receive essential services and protection.
qs.kf:
☛ Who launched Blue Dot hubs? → UNICEF and UNHCR
☛ Main objective of Blue Dot hubs? → Protection of migrant children and families
☛ Full form of UNHCR? → United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
☛ Headquarters of UNICEF? → New York, USA
☛ Where are Blue Dot hubs located? → Along migration routes in Europe

q: Which of the following ration cards is issued to the poorest of India?
qs.e: Antyoday Card is issued to the poorest families in India under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY). This scheme was launched in 2000. Eligible families receive 35 kg of subsidized food grains per month at highly concessional rates. BPL Card is for families below the poverty line, while APL Card is for those above the poverty line. The Antyoday Card targets the most deprived sections, including landless laborers, Scheduled Caste/Tribe families, and urban slum dwellers.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Antyodaya Anna Yojana launched? → 2000
☛ How much food grains do Antyoday card holders get per month? → 35 kg
☛ What does BPL stand for? → Below Poverty Line
☛ What does APL stand for? → Above Poverty Line
☛ Under which scheme is Antyoday Card issued? → Antyodaya Anna Yojana

q: Indian Statistical Institute was founded in the city of _________.
qs.e: The Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) was founded in 1931 by Professor Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in the city of Calcutta (now Kolkata). It is a premier research and teaching institute in India specializing in statistics, mathematics, and data science. In 1959, it was declared an institute of national importance by an act of the Indian Parliament. The institute offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs in statistics. The headquarters of ISI is located in Kolkata, with additional centers in Delhi, Bengaluru, and Chennai.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded ISI? → Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis
☛ In which year was ISI founded? → 1931
☛ When was ISI declared an institute of national importance? → 1959
☛ Where is the headquarters of ISI? → Kolkata
☛ Which cities have ISI centres? → Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai

q: Where is the headquarters of BALCO Aluminum Company located?
qs.e: BALCO (Bharat Aluminium Company) has its headquarters located in New Delhi. It is a government-owned company under the Government of India. BALCO is a leading producer of aluminium, and its plant is situated in Korba, Chhattisgarh. The corporate office in New Delhi manages the administrative and managerial functions of the company.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of BALCO → Bharat Aluminium Company Limited
☛ Headquarters of BALCO → New Delhi
☛ Plant location of BALCO → Korba, Chhattisgarh
☛ Ownership → Government of India (Public Sector)
☛ Product → Aluminium and aluminium products

q: When was the World Trade Organization established?
qs.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established on 1 January 1995. It succeeded the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which was a provisional agreement. Unlike GATT, the WTO is a permanent organization with a stronger dispute resolution mechanism. Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. The WTO had 123 founding members. Its main objectives include reducing trade barriers and resolving trade disputes among member nations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was WTO established? → 1 January 1995
☛ Where is WTO headquarters? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Number of founding members of WTO? → 123
☛ WTO succeeded which agreement? → GATT
☛ When was GATT established? → 1947

q: Which of the following is related to Nairobi negotiations?
qs.e: The Nairobi negotiations refer to the 10th Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organization (WTO), held in Nairobi, Kenya, in December 2015. The key outcome of these negotiations was the agreement to eliminate agricultural export subsidies by developed countries, a major step under the Doha Development Agenda. The talks also aimed to expand the Information Technology Agreement and address other trade issues. Thus, the Nairobi negotiations are directly associated with the World Trade Organization, not the United Nations, World Economic Forum, or World Bank.
qs.kf:
☛ Which organization is associated with the Nairobi negotiations? → World Trade Organization (WTO)
☛ Where was WTO's 10th Ministerial Conference held? → Nairobi, Kenya
☛ What was the main issue in the Nairobi negotiations? → Elimination of agricultural export subsidies
☛ In which year did the Nairobi negotiations take place? → 2015
☛ What is the Doha Development Agenda related to? → Trade issues of developing countries

q: The maximum number of part-time members in the NIT commission is-
qs.e: The NIT Commission was established to oversee and guide the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT). The commission can have a maximum of two part-time members, appointed by the central government. These members are experts in education, science, or related fields. The commission is headed by a Chairperson, while other members include both full-time and part-time members. The limited number of part-time members ensures efficient decision-making processes.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the maximum number of part-time members in the NIT Commission? → Two
☛ For which organization was the NIT Commission established? → NCERT
☛ Who appoints the part-time members of the NIT Commission? → Central Government
☛ Who heads the NIT Commission? → Chairperson
☛ How many types of members are there in the NIT Commission? → Full-time and part-time

q: How many training camps are there in India?
qs.e: India has a total of 62 National Training Camps established across the country to promote various sports. These camps are part of the Khelo India program and provide high-level training to young athletes. Each camp focuses on a specific sport such as athletics, football, hockey, badminton, etc. The aim of these camps is to identify talented athletes and prepare them for competition at national and international levels. The Sports Authority of India (SAI) oversees the functioning of these camps and provides necessary resources.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of National Training Camps → 62
☛ Which body operates these camps → Sports Authority of India (SAI)
☛ Main program under which camps operate → Khelo India
☛ Objective → Training and preparation of young athletes
☛ Focus areas → Various sports like athletics, football, hockey

q: Which country is called the 'Indestructible union of destructible states'?
qs.e: India is called the 'Indestructible union of destructible states'. This phrase is derived from the interpretation of Article 1 of the Indian Constitution, which describes India as a 'Union of States'. The states in India do not have the right to secede, making the union indestructible, while states themselves can be destructible (their boundaries can be altered). This differs from the United States, where states can potentially secede. The Indian Union is a permanent and indestructible entity, symbolizing unity in diversity. The term emphasizes the stability and integrity of India's federal structure, where the central government has the power to reorganize states, but the union itself remains intact.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of union is India? → Indestructible union of states
☛ What does Article 1 of Indian Constitution say? → India is a Union of States
☛ Which country is called 'Indestructible union of destructible states'? → India
☛ Do Indian states have the right to secede? → No
☛ What is the nature of Indian Union? → Indivisible and indestructible

q: When was the first universal council fully convened?
qs.e: The first universal council, also known as the World Parliament of Religions, was fully convened in the year 1893 in Chicago, USA. It was organized on the occasion of the Chicago World's Fair. The council brought together representatives from various religions to discuss religious unity and tolerance. From India, Swami Vivekananda participated and delivered his historic speech that gained worldwide attention. This council was a significant step towards interfaith dialogue and global harmony.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of the first universal council → 1893
☛ Location of the first universal council → Chicago
☛ Indian figure associated with the first universal council → Swami Vivekananda
☛ Alternative name of the first universal council → World Parliament of Religions
☛ Year of the Chicago World's Fair → 1893

q: The overuse of public asset sources is called ________________.
qs.e: This concept was introduced by Garrett Hardin in 1968. When a resource is available to all and no one owns it privately, each individual maximizes its use for personal gain, leading to overexploitation and depletion. For example, overgrazing on public pastures destroys the grassland. This problem illustrates the failure of collective action. Solutions include cooperative management, government regulation, or privatization.
qs.kf:
☛ Tragedy of Commons → Overuse of public resources
☛ Proposed by → Garrett Hardin (1968)
☛ Examples → Public pastures, fisheries, air pollution
☛ Solutions → Cooperative management, government regulation, privatization
☛ Related concept → Collective action problem

q: Where is the headquarters of "Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)" located?
qs.e: The headquarters of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is located in New Delhi. TRAI was established in 1997 as a attached office of the Department of Telecommunications. Its primary objective is to regulate and develop telecommunication services in India. TRAI is an independent regulatory body that works to promote competition among telecom service providers and protect consumer interests. Additionally, TRAI plays a crucial role in setting standards and regulations for the telecom sector.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of TRAI → Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
☛ Establishment year of TRAI → 1997
☛ Headquarters of TRAI → New Delhi
☛ Current Chairman of TRAI (as of Jan 2025) → Dr. P.D. Vaghela
☛ Function of TRAI → Regulation of telecom services

q: What is the full form of ITTF in sports?
qs.e: The full form of ITTF is International Table Tennis Federation, the global governing body for the sport of table tennis. It was founded in 1926 and its headquarters is located in Lausanne, Switzerland. ITTF organizes the World Table Tennis Championships, World Cup, and table tennis events at the Olympic Games. Table tennis became an Olympic sport at the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Currently, over 226 countries are members of ITTF. The federation sets the rules and regulations for the sport.
qs.kf:
☛ ITTF Headquarters → Lausanne, Switzerland
☛ ITTF Founded Year → 1926
☛ Table Tennis in Olympics → 1988, Seoul
☛ Origin of Table Tennis → England
☛ Color of table tennis ball → White or orange

q: In which year was the Pondicherry Legislative Assembly established?
qs.e: The Pondicherry Legislative Assembly was established in 1963. After Pondicherry became a Union Territory of India, the Government of India passed the Pondicherry Legislative Assembly Act, 1963 to create the assembly. It consists of 30 members directly elected by the people. The first election was held in 1964, leading to the formation of the first assembly. The term of the assembly is 5 years. Pondicherry is one of the Union Territories of India that has a legislative assembly.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of members in Pondicherry Assembly → 30
☛ Term of Pondicherry Assembly → 5 years
☛ First election year → 1964
☛ Status of Pondicherry → Union Territory
☛ Establishment Act → Pondicherry Legislative Assembly Act, 1963

q: Who was the first passenger to travel the world through the ship?
qs.e: Ferdinand Magellan was a Portuguese explorer who led the first circumnavigation of the Earth under the Spanish flag. The expedition started in 1519 and was completed in 1522, although Magellan died in the Philippines in 1521. His fleet comprised five ships, but only one, the 'Victoria', returned. This voyage proved that the Earth is round and established a route connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Magellan is considered the first person to circle the globe, even though he died during the journey. His expedition opened new doors for maritime exploration and global trade.
qs.kf:
☛ Who led the first expedition to circumnavigate the world? → Ferdinand Magellan
☛ How many ships were in Magellan's fleet? → Five
☛ Which ship returned from Magellan's expedition? → Victoria
☛ In which year was the circumnavigation completed? → 1522
☛ Where did Magellan die? → Philippines

q: India, United Nations (UNO) member of which year?
qs.e: India became a founding member of the United Nations in 1945. On June 26, 1945, 50 countries signed the UN Charter in San Francisco, including India. Despite being under British rule, India was granted separate membership. The Charter came into force on October 24, 1945. The UN headquarters is in New York. India has consistently supported the UN for peace and development.
qs.kf:
☛ Date of signing of UN Charter → 26 June 1945
☛ Date of UN establishment → 24 October 1945
☛ UN headquarters → New York, USA
☛ Number of founding member states of UN → 51 (Poland joined later)
☛ India is a founding member of UN → 1945

q: Which of these organisations is NOT a United Nations specialized agency?
qs.e: United Nations specialized agencies are autonomous international organizations working with the UN through cooperative agreements. FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) and WHO (World Health Organization) are UN specialized agencies. ILO (International Labour Organization) is also a specialized agency. However, ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is a regional organization and not a UN specialized agency. ASEAN was founded in 1967 and its members are from Southeast Asia. It focuses on regional economic, political, and security cooperation.
qs.kf:
☛ Which UN agency deals with food? → FAO
☛ How many UN specialized agencies are there? → 15
☛ When was ILO established? → 1919
☛ Where is WHO headquarters? → Geneva
☛ Where is ASEAN headquarters? → Jakarta

q: Where was FIFA 2018 held?
qs.e: The FIFA 2018 World Cup was the 21st edition of the tournament, held in Russia from June 14 to July 15, 2018. It was the first time the tournament took place in Eastern Europe, and the first time it was hosted by Russia. Matches were played across 12 stadiums in 11 cities, including Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Kazan. The final was played at Luzhniki Stadium in Moscow, where France defeated Croatia 4-2 to win the title. The tournament featured 32 teams and saw the first use of VAR (Video Assistant Referee) technology.
qs.kf:
☛ Host country of FIFA 2018 → Russia
☛ Final stadium of FIFA 2018 → Luzhniki Stadium, Moscow
☛ Winner of FIFA 2018 → France
☛ Runner-up of FIFA 2018 → Croatia
☛ Technology used for the first time in FIFA 2018 → VAR (Video Assistant Referee)

q: When was the Calotype Society (Photographic Club) established?
qs.e: The Calotype Society, a photographic club, was established in 1847 AD. It is considered the world's first photographic club. It was founded in Edinburgh. The club's name was based on the calotype process, which was developed by William Henry Fox Talbot. The calotype process used a paper negative and played a significant role in the development of photography. This club was an important milestone in the history of photography.
qs.kf:
☛ World's first photographic club → Calotype Society (1847)
☛ Inventor of calotype process → William Henry Fox Talbot
☛ Calotype process used → paper negative
☛ Location of Calotype Society founding → Edinburgh
☛ Early photography year → 1839 (announcement of daguerreotype)

q: The full form of 'SLR' is-
qs.e: The full form of SLR is Statutory Liquidity Ratio. It is a key monetary policy tool regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). SLR is the minimum percentage of a bank's total demand and time liabilities that must be maintained in the form of gold, cash, or government securities. Its primary objective is to ensure liquidity in banks and protect depositors' interests. The current SLR rate is 18%. SLR differs from CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio), as CRR is maintained only in cash. SLR also helps banks invest in government securities, aiding in fiscal management.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of SLR? → Statutory Liquidity Ratio
☛ Who regulates SLR in India? → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
☛ What is the main purpose of SLR? → To maintain bank liquidity
☛ In which assets can banks maintain SLR? → Gold, cash, government securities
☛ What is the current SLR rate? → 18%

q: Where is the "Indian Institute of Economics" located?
qs.e: The Indian Institute of Economics is located in Hyderabad, Telangana. It is a renowned research and teaching institute specializing in economics. Established in 1963, it is affiliated with the University of Hyderabad. The institute aims to promote economic research and contribute to policy formulation. Among the other options, Kolkata houses the Indian Statistical Institute, Raipur hosts the National Institute of Technology, and Mumbai has the Tata Institute of Social Sciences. Hence, the correct answer is Hyderabad.
qs.kf:
☛ Location of Indian Institute of Economics → Hyderabad
☛ Year of establishment of Indian Institute of Economics → 1963
☛ Affiliation of Indian Institute of Economics → University of Hyderabad
☛ Famous institute in Kolkata → Indian Statistical Institute
☛ Famous institute in Mumbai → Tata Institute of Social Sciences

sub: Static GK - Organisations, Abbreviations & Full Forms

q: Under whom does the Archaeological Survey of India come?
qs.e: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) functions under the Ministry of Culture of the Government of India. It was established in 1861 by Alexander Cunningham. ASI is responsible for the conservation, excavation, and research of monuments, archaeological sites, and remains of national importance. It plays a vital role in the management and promotion of India's archaeological heritage. The Ministry of Culture is responsible for the preservation and promotion of Indian culture, art, and heritage, of which ASI is a key component.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of ASI? → New Delhi
☛ In which year was the Archaeological Survey of India established? → 1861
☛ Who founded the ASI? → Alexander Cunningham
☛ Which is the oldest protected monument? → Sanchi Stupa
☛ How many protected monuments are under ASI? → More than 3,600

q: Which prominent Indian economist, known for his role as Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, passed away on 1st November 2024 at the age of 69 years?
qs.e: Bibek Debroy was a prominent Indian economist, known for his role as Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister. He passed away on 1st November 2024 at the age of 69 years. He was renowned for his contributions to Indian economic policy and reforms. He also served as a member of NITI Aayog. Debroy authored several books, including a translation of the Gita. He was an advocate of trade liberalization and economic growth. His work played a significant role in shaping India's economic policies.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM? → Bibek Debroy
☛ When did Bibek Debroy pass away? → 1st November 2024
☛ At what age did Bibek Debroy die? → 69 years
☛ Which institution did Bibek Debroy serve as a member? → NITI Aayog
☛ Which scripture did Bibek Debroy translate? → The Gita

q: Ramanuja, who propounded the doctrine of Vishishtadvaita and who believed that the best means of attaining salvation was through intense devotion to Vishnu, was born in which Indian state in the 11 th Century?
qs.e: Ramanuja was born in the 11th century at Shriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu. He propounded the doctrine of Vishishtadvaita, which is a qualified monism. According to this philosophy, Brahman (Vishnu) is saguna (with attributes) and personal. Ramanuja emphasized bhakti (intense devotion) and surrender to Vishnu as the best means to attain salvation. He wrote the Shri Bhashya, a commentary on the Brahma Sutras. His followers are known as Sri Vaishnavas. Ramanuja's philosophy is distinct from Advaita as it maintains a difference between the individual soul and Brahman while also asserting their ultimate unity.
qs.kf:
☛ Ramanuja's birthplace → Shriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu
☛ Ramanuja's philosophy → Vishishtadvaita
☛ Major work by Ramanuja → Shri Bhashya
☛ Followers of Ramanuja → Sri Vaishnavas
☛ Path to salvation according to Ramanuja → Bhakti (surrender)

q: When was the Inland Waterways Authority set up for the development, maintenance and regulation of national waterways in India?
qs.e: The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) was set up in 1986 by an Act of Parliament. Its primary function is the development, maintenance, and regulation of national waterways. IWAI handles navigation, dredging, and infrastructure projects to promote water transport. Currently, India has 111 notified national waterways, many of which are operational under IWAI. The authority functions under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of IWAI establishment → 1986
☛ Headquarters of IWAI → Noida, Uttar Pradesh
☛ First national waterway of India → NW1 (Ganga River), declared in 1986
☛ Ministry under which IWAI falls → Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
☛ National Waterways Act → Amended in 2007

q: Which organization is primarily responsible for promoting free trade among nations?
qs.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is a global organization that regulates trade between nations and promotes free trade. Established in 1995 and headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, its primary objective is to reduce trade barriers and ensure fair competition. The WTO provides a forum for negotiating trade agreements and resolving disputes. In contrast, the IMF focuses on monetary stability and financial assistance, the World Bank provides loans for development projects, and the UN deals with international peace and security. Thus, the WTO is the key organization responsible for promoting free trade among nations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the WTO established? → 1995
☛ Where is the WTO headquarters located? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ What was the predecessor of the WTO? → GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade)
☛ How many member countries are in the WTO? → 164 (as of 2023)
☛ Which was the latest ministerial conference held by the WTO? → MC13 in Abu Dhabi, 2024

q: Hal Chhath in Bihar is celebrated on the ______ day of the Krishna Paksha of the Bhadra month.
qs.e: Hal Chhath in Bihar is celebrated on the sixth day of the Krishna Paksha of the Bhadra month. This festival is primarily observed by farmers, who worship their ploughs and agricultural tools. The festival is dedicated to Lord Sun and is celebrated for the prosperity of crops. Hal Chhath is also known as Kisan Chhath. It is especially popular in the Mithila region and among the Bhojpuri community. People stand in rivers or ponds and offer arghya to the sun. During the fast, a clay plough is made and worshipped.
qs.kf:
☛ In which month is Hal Chhath celebrated? → Bhadra month
☛ In which paksha is Hal Chhath celebrated? → Krishna Paksha
☛ To whom is Hal Chhath dedicated? → Lord Sun
☛ What is another name for Hal Chhath? → Kisan Chhath
☛ In which state is Hal Chhath prominent? → Bihar

q: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), which is often seen in the news, is located in ____________.
qs.e: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) is located in Manila, the capital of the Philippines. Established in 1966, ADB aims to promote economic growth and poverty reduction in the Asia-Pacific region. The bank has 68 member countries, including 49 regional and 19 non-regional members. The current president of ADB is Masatsugu Asakawa. ADB provides loans, grants, and technical assistance for various development projects. India is a major member and borrower of ADB. The bank plays a crucial role in infrastructure development and sustainable growth in the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank? → Manila, Philippines
☛ When was ADB established? → 1966
☛ Who is the current president of ADB? → Masatsugu Asakawa
☛ How many member countries does ADB have? → 68
☛ What is the main objective of ADB? → Poverty reduction and economic development

q: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a trailblazer in the world of _____.
qs.e: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a pioneering figure in the revival and popularization of Indian classical dance, especially Bharatnatyam. She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai in 1936, which became a major center for learning and training in Bharatnatyam. Her efforts helped bring this dance form from the temples to the global stage. She was also a member of the Rajya Sabha and received the Padma Bhushan award for her contributions to the arts.
qs.kf:
☛ Which dance style was revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale? → Bharatnatyam
☛ Who established the Kalakshetra Foundation? → Rukmini Devi Arundale
☛ Which award was given to Rukmini Devi Arundale? → Padma Bhushan
☛ What was the traditional venue for Bharatnatyam? → Temples
☛ Which house of Parliament was Rukmini Devi Arundale a member of? → Rajya Sabha

q: The National Extension scheme was initially launched for a period of _________ years.
qs.e: The National Extension Scheme was a significant initiative launched in India for agricultural and rural development. It was launched on 2 October 1953. The initial duration of this scheme was set at three years to achieve its objectives of increasing agricultural production and improving living standards in rural areas. Later, this scheme was merged into the Community Development Programme. The main aim was to make rural communities self-reliant and disseminate modern farming techniques.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the National Extension Scheme launched? → 2 October 1953
☛ What was the initial duration of the National Extension Scheme? → three years
☛ Which sector did the National Extension Scheme relate to? → agriculture and rural development
☛ Into which programme was the National Extension Scheme later merged? → Community Development Programme
☛ What was the objective of the National Extension Scheme? → rural uplift and increasing agricultural production

q: Who was the first ruler who tried to take his message to the people through inscriptions?
qs.e: The Mauryan emperor Ashoka (268-232 BCE) was the first ruler to use inscriptions to communicate his message to the people. His edicts, inscribed on rocks and pillars, spread the principles of Dhamma across the Indian subcontinent. These inscriptions were written in Prakrit, Greek, and Aramaic languages, using the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts. Ashoka aimed to instruct common people on moral and social conduct, marking the beginning of a tradition of epigraphic records in India.
qs.kf:
☛ In which language are most of Ashoka's inscriptions written? → Prakrit
☛ What script is predominantly used in Ashoka's rock edicts? → Brahmi
☛ Which Ashokan edict is famous for summarizing Dhamma? → Second Major Rock Edict
☛ Which religion did Ashoka embrace after the Kalinga War? → Buddhism
☛ Which Ashokan pillar features the Lion Capital? → Sarnath Pillar

q: Which international organisation supports globalisation and free trade?
qs.e: WTO (World Trade Organization) is an international organization that supports globalization and free trade. It was established on 1 January 1995 as the successor to GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade). Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. It has 164 member countries (as of 2024). WTO works to reduce trade barriers, provide dispute resolution, and enforce trade rules. Among other options, WHO deals with health, UNESCO with education and culture, and IMF with financial stability.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of WTO? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Which was the predecessor organization of WTO? → GATT
☛ When was WTO established? → 1 January 1995
☛ How many member countries does WTO have? → 164 (as of 2024)
☛ What is the main objective of WTO? → To promote free trade

q: Which of the following Acts aims to prevent money laundering in India?
qs.e: In India, the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) was enacted in 2002 to prevent money laundering. It came into effect on July 1, 2005. The Act defines the offense of laundering illegal money and prescribes strict punishment. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) is responsible for investigation and action under this Act. Among other options, SEBI regulates the securities market, FEMA deals with foreign exchange management, and FCRA controls organizations receiving foreign contributions. PMLA also provides for attachment and confiscation of property involved in money laundering.
qs.kf:
☛ When did PMLA come into force? → July 1, 2005
☛ Which agency investigates under PMLA? → Enforcement Directorate (ED)
☛ What is the full form of PMLA? → Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
☛ Maximum punishment for money laundering? → 7 years imprisonment and fine
☛ In which year was PMLA enacted? → 2002

q: Which of the following colonial-era buildings in Chennai serves as the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation?
qs.e: Ripon Building is a colonial-era structure in Chennai that serves as the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation. Completed in 1913, it was named after Lord Ripon, the then Viceroy of India. The building follows Neo-Classical architecture and is located in the Park Town area of Chennai. It houses the administrative offices of the municipal corporation and is a prominent historical landmark in the city. The building is known for its distinctive white facade and clock tower.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Greater Chennai Corporation → Ripon Building
☛ Year of construction of Ripon Building → 1913
☛ Named after which Viceroy → Lord Ripon
☛ Architectural style of Ripon Building → Neo-Classical
☛ Location of Ripon Building → Park Town, Chennai

q: India achieved a historic feat by winning the presidency of which international organisation for the first time through the voting process?
qs.e: India achieved a historic feat by winning the presidency of the International Institute of Administrative Sciences (IIAS) for the first time through the voting process. This organization is a leading body in the field of administrative sciences, established in 1930. India's administrative reforms and contributions to global governance were recognized. IIAS promotes administrative studies, policy-making, and governance improvements. This achievement is a matter of pride for India as it marks the first time an Indian was elected to this position through voting.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of establishment of IIAS → 1930
☛ Headquarters of IIAS → Brussels, Belgium
☛ Indian President of IIAS → Shri Amitabh Kant
☛ Full form of IIAS → International Institute of Administrative Sciences
☛ Objective of IIAS → Promote administrative sciences

q: Who laid the foundation stone of the Bageshwar Dham Medical and Science Research Institute in Madhya Pradesh?
qs.e: Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of the Bageshwar Dham Medical and Science Research Institute in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh. The institute is being established in collaboration with Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, the head of Bageshwar Dham. Its aim is to provide medical facilities and promote scientific research in the region. The institute will be equipped with modern medical equipment and research facilities. This project is expected to boost local employment and improve healthcare services. Prime Minister Modi emphasized the importance of investment in health and education during the event.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Bageshwar Dham Medical and Science Research Institute located? → Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh
☛ Who is the head of Bageshwar Dham associated with this institute? → Dhirendra Krishna Shastri
☛ When was the foundation stone laid? → 2023
☛ What are the focus areas of this institute? → Medical and Science Research
☛ Which state does Prime Minister Narendra Modi belong to? → Gujarat

q: Which of the following is a private sector organisation in India?
qs.e: TISCO (Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited) is a private sector organisation, established in 1907 by Jamsetji Tata. It is part of the Tata Group and is one of the oldest and largest private steel companies in India. On the other hand, SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited) is a public sector undertaking owned by the Government of India. ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is also a public sector undertaking involved in the exploration and production of oil and gas. Indian Railways is completely under government ownership and is a public sector undertaking. Thus, only TISCO is a private sector organisation.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of TISCO? → Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited
☛ In which year was TISCO established? → 1907
☛ Who established TISCO? → Jamsetji Tata
☛ Is SAIL a public sector undertaking? → Yes
☛ Which sector does Indian Railways belong to? → Public sector

q: The foreign exchange crisis forced India to seek external support. Which institution provided India a loan during the 1991 crisis?
qs.e: In 1991, India faced a severe foreign exchange crisis, with forex reserves sufficient for only two weeks of imports. To tackle this crisis, the Indian government sought a loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The IMF provided an emergency loan of $2.2 billion to India, subject to conditions such as economic reforms and liberalization. This loan helped India overcome the forex crisis and paved the way for economic reforms. While the World Bank and ADB also provided loans later, the initial loan in 1991 was from the IMF. The WTO is a global trade organization and does not provide loans.
qs.kf:
☛ How many weeks of imports could India's forex reserves cover in 1991? → Two weeks
☛ How much loan (in billion dollars) did the IMF give to India in 1991? → $2.2 billion
☛ Who was the chief architect of India's 1991 economic reforms? → Dr. Manmohan Singh
☛ Where is the headquarters of IMF located? → Washington D.C., USA
☛ Who was the Prime Minister of India during the 1991 crisis? → P. V. Narasimha Rao

q: Who among the following is the first African woman to assume office as the Commonwealth Secretary General in April 2025?
qs.e: Shirley Botchwey is a prominent Ghanaian politician and diplomat. In April 2025, she became the first African woman to assume office as the Commonwealth Secretary General. Before this, she served as Ghana's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Minister of Defence. Her appointment is seen as a symbol of Africa's growing influence in the Commonwealth. She succeeded Patricia Scotland, who was the first female Secretary General. Shirley Botchwey's term will be from 2025 to 2030.
qs.kf:
☛ First African woman to become Commonwealth Secretary General → Shirley Botchwey
☛ Term of Commonwealth Secretary General → 4 years
☛ Current Commonwealth Secretary General (after 2025) → Shirley Botchwey
☛ Country of Shirley Botchwey → Ghana
☛ Headquarters of Commonwealth → London

q: The PM SVANidhi scheme is available for beneficiaries belonging to only those States/UTs which have notified rules and a scheme under the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, _________.
qs.e: The PM SVANidhi scheme provides affordable loans to street vendors to restart their businesses post-COVID-19 pandemic. This scheme is available only for beneficiaries belonging to those States/UTs which have notified rules and a scheme under the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. The Act provides legal recognition and protection to street vendors. Section 38 of the Act empowers state governments to make rules. States must notify rules under this Act to avail the benefits of PM SVANidhi scheme. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Street Vendors Act passed? → 2014
☛ Full name of PM SVANidhi scheme? → Pradhan Mantri Street Vendors AtmaNirbhar Nidhi Yojana
☛ Which ministry implements PM SVANidhi scheme? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
☛ Maximum loan amount under PM SVANidhi first tranche? → Rs. 10,000
☛ Who has the power to make rules under the Street Vendors Act, 2014? → State Government

q: As of 1 May 2025, who among the following is not a full-time member of the 16th Finance Commission?
qs.e: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, with Dr. Arvind Panagariya as its chairman. Its full-time members include Annie George Mathew, Ajay Narayan Jha, and Dr. Manoj Panda. Dr. Soumya Kanti Ghosh is not a member of this commission. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280 that recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the central and state governments. The 16th Finance Commission will cover a five-year period starting from 1 April 2026. It is required to submit its report by 31 October 2025.
qs.kf:
☛ Chairman of 16th Finance Commission → Dr. Arvind Panagariya
☛ Full-time members of 16th Finance Commission → Annie George Mathew, Ajay Narayan Jha, Dr. Manoj Panda
☛ Finance Commission formed under → Article 280 of Constitution
☛ 16th Finance Commission tenure → 2026-2031
☛ Report submission deadline for 16th FC → 31 October 2025

q: Rural electrification has been a longstanding priority to support livelihoods and education in villages. Which scheme aimed to achieve 100% household electrification in rural India?
qs.e: The Government of India launched the Saubhagya Yojana (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) in September 2017 to provide electricity connections to all rural households. The scheme aimed for 100% household electrification in rural India, building on previous initiatives like the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana. Saubhagya provides free electricity connections, improving livelihoods, education, and healthcare access in villages. The scheme achieved its target of 100% rural household electrification by October 2018. It was later extended to cover tribal households as well. Saubhagya replaced earlier schemes and was a key step towards universal energy access.
qs.kf:
☛ Scheme for rural household electrification → Saubhagya Yojana
☛ Full name of Saubhagya Yojana → Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana
☛ Launch year of Saubhagya Yojana → 2017
☛ Facility provided under Saubhagya Yojana → Free electricity connection
☛ Areas covered under Saubhagya Yojana → Rural and tribal areas

q: Which government-owned organisation is primarily responsible for electricity transmission in India?
o: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
qs.e: The primary responsibility for electricity transmission in India lies with Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID). It is a Central Public Sector Undertaking (CPSU) under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. Established in 1989, it operates and maintains the inter-state and inter-regional transmission system across the country. POWERGRID manages over 50% of India's total installed transmission capacity and operates the National Grid, which connects five regional grids, enabling efficient power exchange. The company is responsible for developing high-voltage transmission lines, substations, and associated infrastructure. It plays a crucial role in ensuring reliable and stable power supply across states.
qs.kf:
☛ Which government organisation is responsible for inter-state power transmission in India? → Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
☛ When was POWERGRID established? → 1989
☛ Under which ministry does POWERGRID operate? → Ministry of Power
☛ How many regional grids does the National Grid connect? → Five
☛ What is the highest voltage transmission line level in India? → 765 kV

q: In May 2025, the central government extended the tenure of Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) director Praveen Sood for a period of __________.
qs.e: In May 2025, the central government extended the tenure of CBI director Praveen Sood by 1 year. The decision was taken on the recommendation of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). Praveen Sood is a 1986 batch IPS officer from the Karnataka cadre. His original appointment was for two years in May 2023, which was to end in May 2025. The government extended his tenure based on the recommendation of a committee chaired by LC Gupta. The CBI director's tenure can be extended up to a maximum of 5 years. The extension was made under the Delhi Police Special Establishment Act.
qs.kf:
☛ Selection committee for CBI director → PM, Chief Justice, and Lok Sabha Speaker
☛ Establishment of CBI → 1 April 1963, not by an Act of Parliament
☛ CBI headquarters → New Delhi
☛ CBI motto → Industry, Impartiality, Integrity
☛ Tenure of CBI director → Maximum 5 years

q: When is World Cancer Day celebrated?
A. 4 February
B. 5 March
C. 12 May
D. 23 August
qs.e: World Cancer Day is observed every year on 4 February. It was initiated in 2000 during the World Cancer Summit held in Paris. The day is organized by the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC). Its aim is to raise awareness about cancer, promote its prevention, detection, and treatment. According to the World Health Organization, cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. The day emphasizes collective efforts to control the disease globally. The theme for World Cancer Day 2024 is "Close the Care Gap".
qs.kf:
☛ When is World Cancer Day celebrated? → 4 February
☛ When and where was it initiated? → 2000, Paris
☛ Which organization organizes it? → Union for International Cancer Control (UICC)
☛ What is the theme of World Cancer Day 2024? → "Close the Care Gap"
☛ According to WHO, cancer is one of the leading causes of what? → Death

q: Who formed the Deshbandhu new youth association?
A. Lakshmi Sahgal
B. N. G. Ranga
C. Kanneganti Hanumanthu
D. Tirupur Kumaran
qs.e: The Deshbandhu New Youth Association was formed by Tirupur Kumaran in 1928 at Tirupur, Tamil Nadu. This organization aimed to mobilize youth against British rule and accelerate the freedom movement. Tirupur Kumaran sacrificed his life in 1932 during a flag march when he was fatally injured by police lathi charge. He is also known as 'Kumaran' and is remembered as a martyr of the Indian independence struggle.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Deshbandhu New Youth Association → Tirupur Kumaran
☛ Death of Tirupur Kumaran → 1932 during a flag march
☛ Birthplace of Tirupur Kumaran → Tirupur, Tamil Nadu
☛ Nickname of Tirupur Kumaran → Kumaran
☛ Year of formation of Deshbandhu New Youth Association → 1928

q: Where is the headquarters of United Nations Security Council located?
qs.e: The headquarters of the United Nations Security Council is located in New York City, as part of the United Nations Headquarters complex in Manhattan. It has been based there since the UN's founding in 1945. The Security Council is a principal organ responsible for maintaining international peace and security, while the General Assembly and Secretariat are also located in the same complex. Council meetings are held regularly at the headquarters, and its functions include passing resolutions and authorizing peacekeeping missions.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the UN headquarters located? → New York
☛ Which are the permanent members of the Security Council? → US, UK, France, Russia, China
☛ When was the first Security Council meeting held? → 1946
☛ Which is the largest UN organ? → General Assembly
☛ How many non-permanent members are in the Security Council? → 10

q: When was the first Passenger train run in India?
qs.e: India's first passenger train ran on April 16, 1853. It traveled from Bori Bunder station in Mumbai to Thane, covering a distance of about 34 kilometers. The train was operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR) and carried 400 passengers. The locomotives used were named Sultan, Sindh, and Sahib. This historic journey marked the beginning of the Indian Railways, which later became the largest railway network in Asia.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the first passenger train run? → April 16, 1853
☛ Between which stations did the first train run? → Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane
☛ Which company operated the first train? → Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR)
☛ How many passengers were on the first train? → 400 passengers
☛ What were the names of the locomotives? → Sultan, Sindh, and Sahib

q: Which year was the construction of Jama Masjid of Delhi completed?
qs.e: The construction of Jama Masjid of Delhi was commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. It began in 1650 AD and was completed in 1656 AD. The mosque is built with red sandstone and marble. Among its three gates, the eastern gate was reserved for the royal family. The mosque has a capacity of about 25,000 worshippers and features three domes. The construction was supervised by Mir Abad Sardar Khan. The main prayer hall is 60 meters long.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Jama Masjid? → Shah Jahan
☛ When did Jama Masjid construction start? → 1650 AD
☛ What is the capacity of Jama Masjid? → About 25,000 people
☛ How many gates does Jama Masjid have? → Three
☛ Who supervised the construction of Jama Masjid? → Mir Abad Sardar Khan

q: Who founded India's three stage Nuclear Power Programme ?
qs.e: India's three-stage nuclear power programme was established by Dr. Homi Bhabha. The programme is designed to ensure long-term energy security for the country. The first stage involves Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) using natural uranium. The second stage uses Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs) that produce plutonium. The third stage involves thorium-based reactors, leveraging India's abundant thorium reserves. This programme aims to maximize energy production from thorium. Dr. Homi Bhabha is regarded as the father of India's nuclear programme.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the father of India's three-stage nuclear programme? → Dr. Homi Bhabha
☛ Which reactors are used in the first stage? → Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)
☛ Which reactors are involved in the second stage? → Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs)
☛ Which fuel is used in the third stage? → Thorium
☛ Of which institute was Dr. Homi Bhabha the founder? → Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)

q: Which agency was created by the United Nations to provide emergency food and health care to children and mothers in the countries affected by World War II?
qs.e: After World War II, the United Nations established UNICEF (United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund) in 1946 to provide emergency food and health care to children and mothers in affected countries. Its headquarters is in New York. In 1953, its name was changed to United Nations Children's Fund, but the acronym UNICEF remained. It is a specialized agency of the UN that works for child rights, education, health, and nutrition. UNESCO deals with education, science, and culture, IMF provides economic cooperation, and WHO is the global health agency.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UNICEF established? → 1946
☛ Where is UNICEF headquartered? → New York
☛ What is the full form of UNICEF? → United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (now United Nations Children's Fund)
☛ What does UNICEF work for? → Child rights, education, health, and nutrition
☛ Which organization received the Nobel Peace Prize for children? → UNICEF (1965)

q: How many organisations are a part of the United Nations in India ?
qs.e: There are a total of 26 United Nations organizations/agencies operating in India. These work in various sectors like education, health, agriculture, labour, development, environment, etc. Major ones include UNESCO, WHO, FAO, ILO, UNDP, UNICEF, UNHCR, WFP, UN Women, UNFPA, UNEP, UNIDO, IFAD, UNODC, UN-Habitat, UNCTAD, ICAO, IMO, ITU, UPU, WMO, WIPO, World Bank, IMF, IAEA and UNWTO. All of these run various programmes in collaboration with the Government of India.
qs.kf:
☛ How many UN agencies are active in India? → 26
☛ What is the number of UN organizations in India? → 26
☛ Which UN organization is related to education? → UNESCO
☛ Which UN organization is related to health? → WHO
☛ Which UN organization works for child rights? → UNICEF

q: Where was 11th WTO Ministerial Meeting organized?
qs.e: The 11th World Trade Organization (WTO) Ministerial Meeting was held in Buenos Aires, Argentina from 10-13 December 2017. This meeting was crucial for discussing global trade rules, including issues such as agricultural subsidies, fisheries, and e-commerce. Member countries emphasized balancing the interests of developing nations. Argentina, a major South American country, provided the platform for these international trade negotiations. The WTO headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland, but ministerial meetings are organized in different member countries to promote inclusivity.
qs.kf:
☛ WTO Headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ WTO established → 1 January 1995
☛ Current WTO Director-General → Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
☛ Total WTO member countries → 164 (as of 2024)
☛ 12th WTO Ministerial Meeting → Geneva, Switzerland (2022)

q: Which of the following organizations' headquarters is NOT correctly matched?
qs.e: Among the given options, the headquarters of OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is located in Vienna, Austria, not in Zurich. The other organizations are correctly matched: NATO headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium, World Bank in Washington D.C., USA, and UNICEF in New York, USA. OPEC was founded in 1960 in Baghdad and moved its headquarters to Vienna in 1965. It coordinates oil policies among major oil-producing countries.
qs.kf:
☛ OPEC headquarters → Vienna, Austria
☛ NATO headquarters → Brussels, Belgium
☛ World Bank headquarters → Washington D.C., USA
☛ UNICEF headquarters → New York, USA
☛ OPEC founded year → 1960 (Baghdad)

q: FTTP stands for:
qs.e: FTTP stands for Fiber To The Premises. It is a broadband network architecture where optical fiber is run directly to the user's premises, such as a home or business. This technology provides high-speed internet access and offers greater bandwidth and reliability compared to traditional copper cables. FTTP is often referred to as FTTH (Fiber To The Home) or FTTB (Fiber To The Building). It is a key application of fiber optic communication.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of FTTP? → Fiber To The Premises
☛ On which technology is FTTP based? → Fiber optics
☛ What is FTTP used for? → High-speed internet
☛ What is a type of FTTP? → FTTH (Fiber To The Home)
☛ Where does the fiber go in FTTP? → To the user's premises

q: Who among the following stepped down as the Director-General of the World Trade Organization on 31st Aug 2020?
qs.e: Roberto Azevedo stepped down as the Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO) on August 31, 2020. He was a Brazilian diplomat who assumed office on September 1, 2013, succeeding Pascal Lamy. His term was scheduled to end on August 31, 2021, but he resigned early amid the COVID-19 pandemic and global trade tensions. After his resignation, Yonov Frederick Agah served as the interim Director-General. The WTO headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland, and it was established on January 1, 1995. During Azevedo's tenure, negotiations on e-commerce and fisheries subsidies were key priorities. He was praised for his efforts to modernize the organization.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is WTO headquarters? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ When was WTO established? → January 1, 1995
☛ Who was WTO DG before Azevedo? → Pascal Lamy
☛ Who was interim DG after Azevedo? → Yonov Frederick Agah
☛ How many member countries in WTO? → 164

q: According to the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2019, which university/institute ranked No.1 in India in overall Category?
qs.e: According to the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2019, the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras secured the first position in the overall category. NIRF was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (now Ministry of Education). It ranks institutions on parameters like teaching, research, graduation outcomes, outreach, and innovation. In 2019, IIT Madras retained the top spot for the second consecutive year, reflecting its excellent academic and research performance. The second rank went to IIT Delhi, and third to IIT Bombay.
qs.kf:
☛ NIRF 2019 overall rank 1 → IIT Madras
☛ NIRF 2019 rank 2 → IIT Delhi
☛ NIRF 2019 rank 3 → IIT Bombay
☛ NIRF launched → 2015 by MHRD
☛ NIRF ranking parameters → Teaching, research, graduation outcomes, outreach, innovation

q: Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA) at ________ will be the first institution with Institution of National Importance (INI) status in the AYUSH Sector.
qs.e: The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), located in Jamnagar (Gujarat), is the first institution in the AYUSH sector to be granted the status of an Institution of National Importance (INI). It was established in the year 2020 under the Ministry of AYUSH and was awarded INI status through an Act of Parliament. Before this, no AYUSH institution had received this status. ITRA aims to provide high-quality education, research, and medical services in Ayurveda. This step is significant for promoting Ayurveda globally.
qs.kf:
☛ First AYUSH institution to get INI status → ITRA, Jamnagar
☛ Year of establishment of ITRA → 2020
☛ Ministry under which ITRA operates → Ministry of AYUSH
☛ Authority granting INI status → Act of Parliament
☛ Jamnagar is in which state → Gujarat

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of SAARC?
qs.e: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was established in 1985. Its member countries are: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan. Malaysia is located in Southeast Asia and is not a member of SAARC. Malaysia is a member of ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations). Therefore, among the given options, Malaysia is not a member of SAARC.
qs.kf:
☛ SAARC headquarters → Kathmandu, Nepal
☛ Number of founding members of SAARC → 7
☛ Latest country added to SAARC → Afghanistan (2007)
☛ SAARC emblem → Elephant
☛ ASEAN headquarters → Jakarta, Indonesia

q: Who was the founding director of BARC Mumbai?
qs.e: Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha, widely regarded as the father of the Indian nuclear program, founded the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) in Mumbai in 1954 and served as its first director. He also established the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and the Atomic Energy Commission of India. A brilliant physicist, he shaped India's nuclear energy policy. Under his leadership, India's first nuclear reactor, APSARA, achieved criticality. BARC remains India's premier nuclear research facility.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was BARC established? → 1954
☛ What is the full form of BARC? → Bhabha Atomic Research Centre
☛ What is the name of India's first nuclear reactor? → APSARA
☛ Who founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)? → Homi J. Bhabha
☛ Who was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission of India? → Homi J. Bhabha

q: Which of the following countries is not a member of the World Bank Group?
qs.e: The World Bank Group consists of 189 member countries. Cuba is not a member of the World Bank Group. Cuba withdrew its membership from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund in 1960. In contrast, Canada, China, and the USA are members of the World Bank Group. The World Bank Group includes five institutions: the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association, the International Finance Corporation, the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes. Despite being a member of the United Nations, Cuba is not part of the World Bank Group.
qs.kf:
☛ World Bank Group Headquarters → Washington D.C., USA
☛ President of World Bank Group → Ajay Banga (current)
☛ World Bank established → 1944 (Bretton Woods Conference)
☛ Capital of Cuba → Havana
☛ Initial aim of World Bank → Assist reconstruction after World War II

q: Which one of the following is NOT a research reactor of the BARC?
qs.e: BARC (Bhabha Atomic Research Centre) has several research reactors including Apsara (India's first nuclear reactor), KAMINI (world's only uranium-233 based reactor), and ZERLINA (zero-energy reactor). DAMINI is the name of an indigenous nuclear power plant located at Kalpakkam, not a research reactor of BARC. Apsara was refurbished and recommissioned in 2018. KAMINI is used for neutron radiography. ZERLINA was used for neutron scattering studies. Hence, DAMINI is not a research reactor of BARC.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first nuclear reactor → Apsara (BARC)
☛ Uranium-233 based reactor → KAMINI (BARC)
☛ Zero-energy reactor → ZERLINA (BARC)
☛ What is DAMINI → Nuclear power plant at Kalpakkam
☛ BARC location → Mumbai, Tarapur

q: In which year was the International Labour Organisation (ILO) established?
qs.e: The International Labour Organisation (ILO) was established in 1919 as part of the Treaty of Versailles. It was originally an agency of the League of Nations and later became a specialized agency of the United Nations in 1946. The ILO's primary goals include promoting workers' rights, enhancing employment opportunities, and fostering social justice. Its headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. The ILO is known for its tripartite structure, where governments, employers, and worker representatives participate equally. It was the first international organization to set labor standards and has influenced labor laws worldwide. The ILO received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969 for its efforts to improve peace and social justice.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the ILO headquarters? → Geneva
☛ In which year did the ILO become a UN specialized agency? → 1946
☛ What type of structure does the ILO have? → Tripartite (government, employers, workers)
☛ When did the ILO win the Nobel Peace Prize? → 1969
☛ Which treaty led to the establishment of the ILO? → Treaty of Versailles

q: Which is NOT an agency of United Nations?
qs.e: The Red Cross International Committee (ICRC) is not a United Nations agency; it is an independent humanitarian organization. World Health Organization (WHO), International Labour Organization (ILO), and Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) are all specialized agencies of the UN. WHO deals with health, ILO with labor standards, and FAO with food and agriculture. The ICRC was founded in 1863 and provides humanitarian aid during wars, while UN agencies work with member states.
qs.kf:
☛ Which UN agency works on child education? → UNICEF
☛ Which UN financial agencies are there? → IMF and World Bank
☛ Where is UNESCO headquarters? → Paris
☛ Where is ILO headquarters? → Geneva
☛ Where is FAO headquarters? → Rome

q: What is the full form of UNESCO?
o: Union National Employment Scheme Concerning Organization
United Nations Economic, Social and Communal Organization
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
qs.e: The full form of UNESCO is United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It was founded on 16 November 1945 and its headquarters is located in Paris, France. UNESCO aims to promote international cooperation in education, science, and culture. It is known for protecting World Heritage Sites, promoting universal access to education, and supporting scientific research. UNESCO has 193 member states and is a specialized agency of the United Nations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UNESCO founded? → 16 November 1945
☛ Where is UNESCO headquarters? → Paris, France
☛ How many member states does UNESCO have? → 193
☛ What type of organization is UNESCO? → Specialized agency of the United Nations
☛ What is the main function of UNESCO? → International cooperation in education, science, and culture

name: Set 4 · Q133–176
sub: Static GK - Organisations, Abbreviations & Full Forms

q: Which of the following nation is NOT a member of the BIMSTEC organisation?
qs.e: BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) is a regional organization comprising Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan. Its objective is to promote technical and economic cooperation among member countries. Maldives is not a member of this organization. BIMSTEC was established in 1997 and its headquarters is in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The organization has a total of 7 member nations. It serves as a bridge between South Asia and Southeast Asia.
qs.kf:
