☛ Headquarters of BIMSTEC → Dhaka, Bangladesh
☛ Total members in BIMSTEC → 7
☛ Establishment year of BIMSTEC → 1997
☛ Full form of BIMSTEC → Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation

q: The headquarter of the Archaeological Survey of India is located in:
qs.e: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is the premier organization under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, responsible for archaeological surveys, excavations, and conservation of monuments. Its headquarters is located at New Delhi on Tilak Marg. Established in 1861 by Sir Alexander Cunningham, ASI maintains over 3,600 ancient monuments across the country. It has 29 circle offices spread throughout India.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of ASI → New Delhi
☛ Founder of ASI → Sir Alexander Cunningham
☛ Ministry under which ASI works → Ministry of Culture
☛ Year of establishment of ASI → 1861
☛ Number of monuments protected by ASI → Over 3,600

q: The headquarters of the World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) is located at:
qs.e: The World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for promoting tourism and coordinating global tourism policies. Its headquarters is located in Madrid, Spain. UNWTO was established in 1975 and is the leading international organization in the field of tourism. It focuses on sustainable tourism development, economic growth, and cultural preservation. Currently, it has 159 member states. Madrid was chosen as the headquarters due to Spain's global leadership in the tourism industry and its geographical location.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of UNWTO? → World Tourism Organization
☛ When was UNWTO established? → 1975
☛ Which organization's specialized agency is UNWTO? → United Nations (UN)
☛ Who is the current Secretary-General of UNWTO? → Zurab Pololikashvili
☛ In which city is the headquarters of UNWTO located? → Madrid, Spain

q: Name the vehicle developed by DRDO to detect and dispose a bomb.
qs.e: Daksh is an automated robotic vehicle developed by DRDO for detecting and disposing bombs. It is used by the Army, paramilitary forces, and security agencies. The vehicle is equipped with a robotic arm that can lift suspicious objects and place them in a safe container. It features advanced sensors and cameras to detect explosives. Daksh has been deployed in Mumbai attacks and other counter-terrorism operations. It was designed and developed at the Research Centre Imarat in Bengaluru.
qs.kf:
☛ DRDO-developed bomb disposal vehicle → Daksh
☛ Organization that developed Daksh → DRDO
☛ Key feature of Daksh → Robotic arm and sensors
☛ Users of Daksh → Army and security forces
☛ Development location of Daksh → Bengaluru

q: In which year did India join the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
qs.e: India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in 2017. The SCO is a permanent intergovernmental organization founded in 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan were invited to join in 2015 at the Ufa summit and were granted full membership at the Astana summit in 2017. The SCO's headquarters is located in Beijing, China, and its primary objectives include combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism. The organization has since expanded to include Iran and several observer states.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of SCO establishment → 2001
☛ SCO headquarters → Beijing, China
☛ Year India became full member of SCO → 2017
☛ Current number of SCO member states (as of 2024) → 9
☛ Primary objective of SCO → Combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism

q: Who said the following? "No society can surely by flourishing and happy, of which the far greater part of the members are poor and miserable."
qs.e: This statement was made by the renowned economist Adam Smith in his book "An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations" (1776). This book is considered the foundation of modern economics. Smith argued that the prosperity of a society depends on the well-being of all its members, not just the wealthy class. He is also famous for the Invisible Hand theory, which explains market self-regulation. This quote reflects Smith's views on social justice and economic inequality.
qs.kf:
☛ Adam Smith's famous book → An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
☛ Adam Smith's theory → Invisible Hand
☛ Adam Smith is known as → Father of Economics
☛ Adam Smith's birth year → 1723
☛ Adam Smith's death year → 1790

q: The United Nations organisation was set up through the signing of the United Nations Charter by ______ states.
qs.e: The United Nations Organisation (UNO) was established on 24 October 1945. Its Charter was signed by 50 countries in San Francisco on 26 June 1945, and Poland later signed, bringing the total to 51 founding member states. It was created after World War II to maintain international peace and security. Most of the 51 founding members were from Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Currently, the UN has 193 member states.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UNO established? → 24 October 1945
☛ When was UN Charter signed? → 26 June 1945
☛ Where is UN headquarters? → New York, USA
☛ Current number of UN members? → 193
☛ What is the purpose of UN? → Maintain international peace and security

q: For how many years are the non-permanent members of the UN Security Council (UNSC) elected?
qs.e: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has 15 members, of which 5 are permanent (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) and 10 are non-permanent. Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for a term of 2 years. Every year, 5 non-permanent members are elected, and no member can be re-elected immediately. This arrangement is outlined under Article 23 of the UN Charter. The selection of non-permanent members is based on geographical distribution to ensure representation from all regions.
qs.kf:
☛ Total UNSC members → 15 (5 permanent + 10 non-permanent)
☛ Term of non-permanent members → 2 years
☛ Veto power in UNSC → 5 permanent members
☛ Non-permanent members elected each year → 5
☛ UNSC headquarters → New York

q: In which year was the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) introduced in India?
qs.e: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) was launched in India on 2nd October 1975. It is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The primary objective of ICDS is to improve the nutrition, health, and education of children aged 0-6 years, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. The program is implemented through Anganwadi centers. ICDS is one of the world's largest community-based child development programs. It provides services like supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-ups, and pre-school education.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of ICDS? → Integrated Child Development Services
☛ Which ministry oversees ICDS? → Ministry of Women and Child Development
☛ What are ICDS centers called? → Anganwadi centers
☛ For which age group is ICDS targeted? → 0-6 years
☛ When was ICDS launched? → 1975

q: Who said the following words? "The United Nations was not created to take humanity to heaven, but to save it from hell."
qs.e: This famous statement was made by Dag Hammarskjold, the second Secretary-General of the United Nations. He defined the UN's role as preventing destructive wars and conflicts, rather than creating an ideal world. Hammarskjold served as UN Secretary-General from 1953 to 1961. He played a key role in peacekeeping and diplomatic efforts during the Cold War, helping to resolve crises such as the Suez Crisis and the Congo Crisis. He was posthumously awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1961. This quote reflects the UN's practical and peace-focused approach.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Secretary-General of the UN was Dag Hammarskjold? → Second
☛ How many years did Dag Hammarskjold serve? → 1953-1961
☛ In which year did he win the Nobel Peace Prize? → 1961
☛ Who was the first Secretary-General of the UN? → Trygve Lie
☛ Which Secretary-General was Kurt Waldheim? → Fourth

q: When was the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) established?
qs.e: The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) was established in 2010 as an international organization. Its headquarters is located in Seoul, South Korea. GGGI aims to promote green growth in developing countries, which seeks to integrate economic development with environmental sustainability. The organization transformed into an international organization in 2012 through an international treaty. GGGI assists governments in policy formulation, capacity building, and investment. India is also a member of GGGI.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of GGGI? → Seoul, South Korea
☛ What is the main objective of GGGI? → Promoting green growth
☛ When did GGGI become an international organization? → 2012
☛ What does GGGI stand for? → Global Green Growth Institute
☛ Is India a member of GGGI? → Yes

q: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (UN Organization-HQ)?
qs.e: The headquarters of UNEP (United Nations Environment Programme) is in Nairobi, Kenya, not Geneva. The UNEP Europe Office is located in Geneva, but not the headquarters. UNITAR (United Nations Institute for Training and Research) has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) is headquartered in New York, USA. UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) has its headquarters in Paris, France. Thus, only the first pair is incorrectly matched.
qs.kf:
☛ UNEP Headquarters → Nairobi, Kenya
☛ UNITAR Headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ UNICEF Headquarters → New York, USA
☛ UNESCO Headquarters → Paris, France
☛ UNDP Headquarters → New York, USA

q: Where is the headquarters of International Committee of the Red Cross situated?
qs.e: The headquarters of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is located in Geneva, Switzerland. ICRC is a humanitarian organization founded in 1863. Its primary mission is to protect victims of armed conflicts and war. It operates under the Geneva Conventions. ICRC has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize three times (1917, 1944, 1963).
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of ICRC → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Year of ICRC establishment → 1863
☛ Founder of Red Cross movement → Henry Dunant
☛ Nobel Prizes won by ICRC → 1917, 1944, 1963
☛ Treaty associated with ICRC → Geneva Conventions

q: Where is the headquarters of SAARC Development Fund (SDF) established by SAARC nations?
qs.e: The SAARC Development Fund (SDF) was established in 2005 by the SAARC nations to promote regional cooperation and finance development projects. Its headquarters is located in Thimphu, Bhutan. The fund is governed by a Board of Governors comprising representatives from all SAARC member states. The first chairperson of SDF is from Bhutan. The SDF supports projects in areas such as poverty alleviation, education, health, and infrastructure within the SAARC region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of SAARC? → Kathmandu, Nepal
☛ When was SAARC established? → 8 December 1985
☛ Which country holds the first chairperson of SDF? → Bhutan
☛ How many member countries are in SAARC? → 8
☛ What are the colors of the SAARC emblem? → Green and Blue

q: The United Nations adopted the 'Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States' in ______.
qs.e: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States on 12 December 1974. This charter was drafted at the insistence of developing countries to establish fair rules in international economic relations. It includes principles such as the economic sovereignty of states, control over natural resources, and equitable trade. The charter is considered a part of the New International Economic Order (NIEO). It is notable that the UN General Assembly adopted it in 1974, while a related resolution on economic rights and duties was passed in 1976.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States adopted? → 1974
☛ Which body adopted this charter? → United Nations General Assembly
☛ Which economic order is this charter related to? → New International Economic Order (NIEO)
☛ What was the purpose of this charter? → To define the economic rights and duties of states
☛ Which charter includes full sovereignty over natural resources? → Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States

q: World Health Organization (WHO) gave its Tobacco Control Award for the year 2019 to the health department of the Indian state of ______.
qs.e: The World Health Organization (WHO) awarded its Tobacco Control Award for the year 2019 to the health department of Rajasthan, India. This award recognizes outstanding contributions to tobacco control. Rajasthan was honored for its effective implementation of tobacco control laws under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), including strict enforcement of smoking bans and promotion of tobacco-free cities. The state's awareness campaigns and policy measures significantly reduced tobacco use. This recognition highlights India's efforts in combating tobacco-related health issues. Rajasthan's success serves as a model for other states in tobacco control.
qs.kf:
☛ Indian state that received WHO Tobacco Control Award 2019 → Rajasthan
☛ Key legislation for tobacco control in Rajasthan → COTPA
☛ Full form of COTPA → Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act
☛ WHO headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ WHO establishment date → 7 April 1948

q: What is the full form of GEO?
qs.e: The full form of GEO is Geostationary Earth Orbit. It is a circular orbit located approximately 35,786 kilometers above the Earth's equator. Satellites in this orbit travel at the same rotational speed as the Earth, making them appear stationary relative to a fixed point on the ground. This unique property makes GEO ideal for communication satellites, weather satellites, and broadcasting services. Other options like Geography Earth Orbit or Geostructure Element Orbit are incorrect as GEO specifically refers to a geostationary orbit, which is a type of geosynchronous orbit. GEO is widely used in satellite telecommunications because it allows continuous coverage of a specific region.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of GEO? → Geostationary Earth Orbit
☛ What is the altitude of GEO? → Approximately 35,786 km
☛ Why do GEO satellites appear stationary? → Due to matching Earth's angular velocity
☛ What are the main applications of GEO? → Communication, meteorology, and broadcasting
☛ Over which line are GEO satellites positioned? → Equator

q: When was the name 'United Nations' coined?
qs.e: The name United Nations was first used on 1 January 1942, when 26 countries signed the Declaration by United Nations during World War II to fight together against the Axis powers. The name was suggested by US President Franklin D. Roosevelt. In 1945, the San Francisco Conference formally adopted the name, and the United Nations Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Declaration by United Nations signed? → 1 January 1942
☛ Who suggested the name United Nations? → Franklin D. Roosevelt
☛ When did the UN Charter come into force? → 24 October 1945
☛ When was the San Francisco Conference held? → 1945
☛ Where is the headquarters of the United Nations? → New York

q: Which country is NOT member of the 'SAARC'?
qs.e: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) is a regional organization founded in 1985. Its 8 members are: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan. Iran is not a member, but an observer country. SAARC headquarters is in Kathmandu, Nepal. The organization aims to promote economic, social, and cultural cooperation in South Asia.
qs.kf:
☛ SAARC headquarters → Kathmandu, Nepal
☛ SAARC founded year → 1985
☛ Founding members of SAARC → 7 countries (Afghanistan joined later)
☛ Observer countries of SAARC → China, Iran, Japan, South Korea, USA
☛ Full form of SAARC → South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation

q: Which of the following countries is a member of OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries)?
o: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
qs.e: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has been a member of OPEC since 2016. Brazil, India, and Japan are not OPEC members. OPEC was founded in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. Its headquarters is in Vienna, Austria. Currently, OPEC has 13 members, including Algeria, Angola, Ecuador, Gabon, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Venezuela, and DRC. The inclusion of DRC highlights the importance of oil production in Africa.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is OPEC's headquarters? → Vienna, Austria
☛ Which are OPEC's founding members? → Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela
☛ Which African country is the newest OPEC member? → Democratic Republic of the Congo (2016)
☛ When was OPEC founded? → 1960
☛ How many members does OPEC currently have? → 13

q: Ngozi Okonjo Iweala of _______ has been appointed as first female chief of WTO in Feb, 2021.
qs.e: In February 2021, Nigeria's Ngozi Okonjo Iweala was appointed as the first female Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO). She is the first woman and the first African to hold this position. She previously served as Nigeria's Finance Minister and Foreign Minister. Her term began on March 1, 2021. The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. This appointment was seen as a major step for women leadership in international trade.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the first female chief of WTO? → Ngozi Okonjo Iweala
☛ Which country does Ngozi Okonjo Iweala belong to? → Nigeria
☛ Where is the headquarters of WTO? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ When was WTO established? → 1995
☛ Who was the first Director-General of WTO? → Peter Sutherland

q: Select the option that shows the correct match of an organisation and its headquarters.
qs.e: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. ESO (European Southern Observatory) is based in Garching, Germany. INTERPOL's headquarters is in Lyon, France. WHO (World Health Organization) is also headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, not Paris. Hence, only the match of GATT is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ WHO headquarters → Geneva
☛ INTERPOL headquarters → Lyon
☛ GATT headquarters → Geneva
☛ ESO headquarters → Garching
☛ WTO headquarters → Geneva

q: Which of the following does a Bandicoot refer to ?
qs.e: A Bandicoot is an automated robot designed for cleaning drainage systems. It can remove sludge, garbage, and other blockages from drains and pipelines. The robot was developed under the Swachh Bharat Mission to protect human sanitation workers from hazardous conditions. Bandicoot was created by the company Genrobotics and has revolutionized manhole cleaning. It operates unmanned, reducing accidents during cleaning operations. This innovation addresses the critical issue of manual scavenging and promotes safe waste management practices.
qs.kf:
☛ What is Bandicoot robot used for? → Cleaning drainage and manholes
☛ Who developed Bandicoot robot? → Genrobotics
☛ Which mission is Bandicoot related to? → Swachh Bharat Mission
☛ What type of robot is Bandicoot? → Drainage-cleaning robot
☛ What is the main advantage of Bandicoot? → Safety of human sanitation workers

q: Which one of the following is a member of BRICS?
qs.e: BRICS is an international organization comprising five major emerging economies: Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. The name is an acronym formed from the first letters of these countries. BRICS was established in 2009 and aims to promote economic cooperation, trade, and investment among member nations. Canada and Bhutan are not members of this group. Indonesia is also not a BRICS member, although it is an emerging economy. The headquarters of BRICS is located in Shanghai, China, and it works towards reforming global economic governance.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of BRICS? → Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa
☛ When was BRICS established? → 2009
☛ Where is the headquarters of BRICS? → Shanghai, China
☛ Which is the newest member of BRICS? → South Africa (joined in 2010)
☛ What is the objective of BRICS? → To promote economic cooperation and development

q: The correct full form of ISCII from the below is:
o: International Standard Code for Information Interchange
Indian Standard Code for Information Interchange
Indian Standard Code for International Interaction
International Standard Code for Indian Interaction
qs.e: The full form of ISCII is Indian Standard Code for Information Interchange. It is an Indian encoding system developed for Indian languages. ISCII supports 11 Indian scripts including Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Assamese. It is an extension of ASCII and is used for data interchange. ISCII was standardized in 1983 by the Bureau of Indian Standards. It served as a precursor to Unicode and played a significant role in the computerization of Indian languages.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of ISCII? → Indian Standard Code for Information Interchange
☛ How many Indian scripts does ISCII support? → 11
☛ What is ISCII related to? → Encoding of Indian languages
☛ When was ISCII standardized? → 1983
☛ ISCII is an extension of which code? → ASCII

q: In which year was the Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) instituted in India?
qs.e: The Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) was instituted in India in 1992. Introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), it allowed partial market determination of the exchange rate. Under LERMS, 40% of foreign exchange earnings were sold at the market rate, while the remaining 60% was sold at the official rate. This system was part of the economic reforms following the 1991 balance of payments crisis. Later, in 1993, India adopted a unified exchange rate system, making the rupee fully convertible. LERMS played a crucial role in integrating India into the global economy.
qs.kf:
☛ When was LERMS implemented? → 1992
☛ Who introduced LERMS? → RBI
☛ What percentage of foreign exchange was sold at market rate under LERMS? → 40%
☛ Which system was adopted in 1993? → Unified exchange rate system
☛ LERMS was part of which reforms after the 1991 crisis? → Economic reforms

q: Who is one of the founders of the Red Cross society?
qs.e: Jean Henry Dunant was a Swiss businessman and humanitarian who played a key role in founding the Red Cross Society in 1863. After witnessing the suffering of wounded soldiers at the Battle of Solferino in 1859, he wrote 'A Memory of Solferino', proposing a neutral organization to provide relief. His efforts led to the establishment of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in Geneva in 1863. In 1901, Dunant was awarded the first Nobel Peace Prize. The Red Cross symbol, a red cross on a white background, represents neutrality and humanitarian aid. Among the other options, Von Herring was a military officer, Carolina Millan was a fashion designer, and B. Skinner was a psychologist.
qs.kf:
☛ Red Cross founded → 1863 in Geneva
☛ ICRC headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Jean Henry Dunant awarded → First Nobel Peace Prize (1901)
☛ Red Cross symbol → Red cross on white background
☛ Inspiration → Battle of Solferino (1859)

q: Where is the headquarters of United Nations System Staff College located?
qs.e: The United Nations System Staff College (UNSSC) is a key training institution for staff of the United Nations system. Its headquarters is located in Turin, Italy. Established in 2002, the UNSSC operates under the United Nations Secretariat. It provides learning and development opportunities to enhance capacity building within the UN system. Turin also houses the United Nations Intercity Training Centre, which organizes training activities. The UNSSC focuses on areas such as leadership, sustainable development, and human rights. It serves as a hub for knowledge sharing and professional development for UN personnel worldwide.
qs.kf:
☛ UNSSC Headquarters → Turin, Italy
☛ UNSSC Establishment Year → 2002
☛ UNSSC operates under → United Nations Secretariat
☛ Full form of UNSSC → United Nations System Staff College
☛ Objective of UNSSC → Capacity building of UN staff

q: _______ is the largest producer of crude oil and natural gas in India.
qs.e: The largest producer of crude oil and natural gas in India is the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC). ONGC is a state-owned company involved in exploration, production, and refining of oil and gas. Its headquarters is located in Dehradun. ONGC contributes approximately 70% of India's total crude oil production and about 80% of its natural gas production. Major production areas include Mumbai High, Gujarat, and Assam. ONGC was established in 1956. NTPC is related to power generation, SAIL to steel, and BHEL to heavy electrical equipment, making them incorrect options.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of ONGC → Dehradun
☛ Establishment year of ONGC → 1956
☛ Largest producer of crude oil in India → ONGC
☛ Major production area of ONGC → Mumbai High
☛ Full form of ONGC → Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited

q: What kind of organisation is NATO(North Atlantic Treaty Organization)?
qs.e: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is an intergovernmental military alliance established on 4 April 1949 under the North Atlantic Treaty (Washington Treaty). Its primary purpose is collective defense and security cooperation, whereby an attack on one member is considered an attack on all (Article 5). It currently has 31 member countries and its headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium. It is a military alliance, not a technology, cultural, or economic group.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NATO established? → 4 April 1949
☛ Where is NATO headquarters located? → Brussels, Belgium
☛ Which article of NATO provides for collective defense? → Article 5
☛ Which is the newest member country to join NATO in 2023? → Finland
☛ How many current member countries does NATO have? → 31

q: United Nations General Assembly passed a resolution in the year ______ for establishing the UNIDO.
qs.e: The United Nations General Assembly passed a resolution in the year 1966 to establish UNIDO (United Nations Industrial Development Organization). It is a specialized agency that promotes industrial development, poverty eradication, and sustainable development goals. UNIDO's headquarters is located in Vienna, Austria. Its objective is to accelerate industrial development in developing countries and economies in transition. The organization encourages sustainable industrialization through technical assistance, policy advice, and standardization. UNIDO became a specialized agency of the United Nations in 1985.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is UNIDO headquarters? → Vienna, Austria
☛ When did UNIDO become a specialized agency? → 1985
☛ Full form of UNIDO? → United Nations Industrial Development Organization
☛ Main objective of UNIDO? → Promote sustainable industrial development
☛ Who does UNIDO work for? → Developing countries and economies in transition

q: Which among the following countries is not the member of ASEAN?
qs.e: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is a regional organization of Southeast Asian countries, established on 8 August 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration. Its founding members are Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. Later, Brunei (1984), Vietnam (1995), Laos and Myanmar (1997), and Cambodia (1999) joined. Currently, ASEAN has 10 member states. India is not a member of ASEAN, but it participates in ASEAN+3 (China, Japan, South Korea) and the East Asia Summit (EAS). India and ASEAN established sectoral dialogue partnership in 1992 and full dialogue partnership in 1996. In 2012, it was upgraded to a strategic partnership.
qs.kf:
☛ When was ASEAN established? → 8 August 1967
☛ Where is ASEAN headquarters? → Jakarta, Indonesia
☛ How many members does ASEAN have? → 10
☛ What is India's relation with ASEAN? → Strategic Partner (not member)
☛ Which is the newest member of ASEAN? → Cambodia (1999)

q: Headquarters of United Nations University is situated in ______.
qs.e: The headquarters of the United Nations University (UNU) is located in Tokyo, Japan. Established in 1973, UNU is an academic and research institution of the United Nations, focusing on global issues such as peace, development, and human welfare. It was created by a resolution of the UN General Assembly to contribute to the resolution of pressing global problems through research and knowledge dissemination. While UNU has numerous institutes and programs worldwide, its main campus and central office remain in Tokyo. The university plays a crucial role in fostering international cooperation and generating policy-relevant knowledge.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of establishment of UNU → 1973
☛ Main objective of UNU → Study and solution of global problems
☛ Current Rector of UNU → Tashihiro Tsuchiya (from June 2024)
☛ City of UNU headquarters → Tokyo, Japan
☛ UNU is part of which organization → United Nations

q: Where is the headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) situated?
qs.e: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) is a military alliance established in 1949. Its headquarters is located in Brussels, the capital of Belgium. NATO's primary objective is to provide collective security and military cooperation among its member nations in the North Atlantic region. The alliance initially had 12 founding members, including the United States, the United Kingdom, France, and Canada. Currently, there are 31 member countries. Brussels is also known as the headquarters of the European Union (EU), but NATO's headquarters is separate.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NATO founded? → 4 April 1949
☛ Where is NATO headquarters located? → Brussels, Belgium
☛ What is NATO's core principle? → Collective defense (Article 5)
☛ How many founding members did NATO have? → 12
☛ When did India become a NATO member? → India has never been a NATO member

q: In which of the following cities, United Nation's subsidiary regional headquarters is NOT opened?
qs.e: The United Nations (UN) has several subsidiary regional headquarters across the world, but Rome does not host any such subsidiary regional headquarters. The major regional UN headquarters are located in Geneva (Switzerland), Vienna (Austria), and Nairobi (Kenya). Geneva hosts the European headquarters of UN and numerous agencies; Vienna houses the UN International Centre and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA); Nairobi hosts the UN Office at Nairobi (UNON), which serves as the UN headquarters in Africa. While Rome is home to specialized UN agencies like FAO, WFP, and IFAD, these are independent agency headquarters and not subsidiary regional headquarters of the UN itself. Therefore, among the options, Rome is the city where a UN subsidiary regional headquarters is not opened.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the UN European headquarters located? → Geneva
☛ Which UN body is associated with the Vienna office? → IAEA
☛ What is the full form of UNON? → United Nations Office at Nairobi
☛ Which UN agency has its headquarters in Rome? → FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization)
☛ How many major UN regional headquarters are there? → Four (New York, Geneva, Vienna, Nairobi)

q: Who founded "Ramakrishna Mission" in 1897?
qs.e: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897. It is a spiritual and philanthropic organization based on the ideals of Ramakrishna Paramhansa. Its headquarters is located at Belur Math, West Bengal. The mission aims to promote education, healthcare, social service, and religious tolerance. Swami Vivekananda established this mission after his famous speech at the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago (1893). The organization is renowned worldwide for its humanitarian work.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Ramakrishna Mission founded? → 1897
☛ Where is the headquarters of Ramakrishna Mission? → Belur Math, West Bengal
☛ Who was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramhansa? → Swami Vivekananda
☛ Where did Swami Vivekananda speak at the World Parliament of Religions? → Chicago (1893)
☛ What is the main work of Ramakrishna Mission? → Social service and education

q: Which year was the Central Rural Sanitation program started?
qs.e: The Central Rural Sanitation Programme (CRSP) was launched in 1986 by the Government of India. Its primary objective was to provide sanitation facilities in rural areas and eliminate the practice of open defecation. The programme was implemented under the Ministry of Rural Development. Later, in 1999, it was restructured into the Total Sanitation Campaign, and in 2014, the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) was launched. CRSP provided financial assistance to rural households for constructing toilets, improving sanitation coverage.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Central Rural Sanitation Programme (CRSP) launched? → 1986
☛ Under which ministry was CRSP implemented? → Ministry of Rural Development
☛ In which year was CRSP converted into the Total Sanitation Campaign? → 1999
☛ When was Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) launched? → 2014
☛ What was the main objective of CRSP? → To provide rural sanitation facilities and stop open defecation

q: _________ mode is used whenever either end of the security association is a security gateway.
qs.e: Tunnel mode is used in IPsec security associations when at least one end is a security gateway. In this mode, the entire original IP packet is encrypted and authenticated, and then encapsulated in a new IP header. This ensures secure communication between gateways, such as in VPNs. Unlike Transport mode, which only protects the payload, Tunnel mode hides the entire packet. It provides network layer security and is widely used in virtual private networks to connect different sites securely over the internet.
qs.kf:
☛ IPsec Tunnel mode → Encrypts entire IP packet and adds new header.
☛ IPsec Transport mode → Encrypts only payload, not header.
☛ Tunnel mode use → When either end of security association is a security gateway.
☛ VPN use → Tunnel mode is used in site-to-site VPNs.
☛ Transport mode use → Used for end-to-end communication between two hosts.

q: The headquarter of Wildlife Institute of India is located at-
qs.e: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) was established in 1982 and its headquarters is located in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It is an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. The primary functions of WII include wildlife research, management, and education. It conducts various courses related to wildlife conservation. The institute has made significant contributions to tiger conservation and biodiversity. WII has also prepared management plans for several national parks and sanctuaries across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Establishment year of Wildlife Institute of India → 1982
☛ Headquarters of Wildlife Institute of India → Dehradun
☛ Ministry under which Wildlife Institute of India falls → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Main course offered at Wildlife Institute of India → Post Graduate Diploma in Wildlife Management
☛ Headquarters of WWF-India → New Delhi

q: When will the tenure of Chief Justice of India Ranjan Gogoi end?
qs.e: The tenure of former Chief Justice of India Ranjan Gogoi ended on 17 November 2019. He became the 46th Chief Justice of India on 3 October 2018. His tenure lasted about 13 months. During his tenure, he delivered several landmark judgments, including the Ayodhya dispute, Rafale deal, and Cabinet Mission role. He was succeeded by Justice S.A. Bobde on 18 November 2019. As per the Indian Constitution, the retirement age for a Chief Justice is 65 years. Ranjan Gogoi was born on 18 November 1954.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the 46th Chief Justice of India? → Ranjan Gogoi
☛ Who succeeded Ranjan Gogoi as CJI? → S.A. Bobde
☛ What is the retirement age of a Chief Justice? → 65 years
☛ When was Ranjan Gogoi born? → 18 November 1954
☛ Which CJI delivered the verdict on Ayodhya dispute? → Ranjan Gogoi

q: In which of the following cities is the Indian Institute of Petroleum situated?
qs.e: The Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) is located in Dehradun. It is a premier laboratory under the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), specializing in research on petroleum and natural gas. Established in 1959, IIP focuses on crude oil exploration, gas processing, and fuel quality improvement. The other options, Kochi, Kandla, and Visakhapatnam, are major port cities in India, but IIP is situated in Dehradun, the capital of Uttarakhand.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Indian Institute of Petroleum located? → Dehradun
☛ Under which council does IIP fall? → CSIR
☛ When was IIP established? → 1959
☛ What is the primary research area of IIP? → Petroleum and natural gas
☛ Dehradun is the capital of which state? → Uttarakhand

q: The World bank comprises of __________.
qs.e: The World Bank was established in 1944 under the Bretton Woods Conference. It primarily consists of IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development) and IDA (International Development Association). IBRD provides loans to middle-income countries, while IDA offers concessional loans to the poorest nations. The World Bank Group includes five institutions: IBRD, IDA, IFC (International Finance Corporation), MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency), and ICSID (International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes). WTO and GATT are trade-related organizations, while IMF is a separate Bretton Woods institution.
qs.kf:
☛ Main components of World Bank → IBRD and IDA
☛ IBRD established → 1944, Bretton Woods Conference
☛ Total institutions in World Bank Group → 5
☛ Provides concessional loans to poor countries → IDA
☛ Finances the private sector → IFC

q: Which food safety management system published in 2005 provides a framework for organisations to manage food safety?
qs.e: ISO 22000 is an international food safety management system published in 2005. It provides a framework for organizations to identify, control, and manage food safety hazards along the food chain. The standard integrates the principles of HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) with management system elements. It applies to any organization involved in the food chain, regardless of size. The latest version of ISO 22000 was released in 2018. Other options: ISO 9000 relates to quality management, ISO 14000 to environmental management, and ISO 17025 to testing laboratories.
qs.kf:
☛ Which international standard is for food safety management system? → ISO 22000
☛ In which year was ISO 22000 published? → 2005
☛ ISO 22000 is based on which principles? → HACCP
☛ When was the latest version of ISO 22000 released? → 2018
☛ ISO 14000 is related to which management? → Environmental management

q: The group of North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) has how many member countries, as on 30 September 2024?
qs.e: As of 30 September 2024, NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) has 32 member countries. NATO was founded in 1949 and its headquarters is located in Brussels. The latest member is Sweden, which joined in March 2024, following Finland which joined in April 2023. NATO is a military alliance based on the principle of collective defense, meaning an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. Currently, 32 countries from Europe and North America are members.
qs.kf:
☛ NATO founding year → 1949
☛ NATO headquarters → Brussels, Belgium
☛ Newest NATO member (2024) → Sweden
☛ Collective defense clause → Article 5
☛ Finland joined NATO → April 2023

q: Who among the following reinterpreted verses from the Koran to argue for women’s education?
qs.e: Mumtaz Ali (1860-1935) was an Indian Muslim reformer who reinterpreted verses from the Koran to argue for women's education. He presented Quranic verses in a way that showed women's education is essential in Islam. He is known for advocating Muslim women's rights and education. In his book 'Huqooq-e-Niswan', he explained women's rights with reference to the Quran. He was associated with the Aligarh Movement and emphasized women's education. He believed that educated mothers can reform society.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the name of Mumtaz Ali's book? → Huqooq-e-Niswan
☛ Which movement was Mumtaz Ali associated with? → Aligarh Movement
☛ Who reinterpreted Quranic verses for women's education? → Mumtaz Ali
☛ What is Begum Anis Kidwai known for? → Freedom fighter and social worker
☛ What is Baji Jamalunnisa known for? → Pioneer of Muslim women's education

q: In September 2024, who among the following launched the Jan Sunwai Portal of the Department of Commerce, designed to streamline communication between stakeholders and authorities?
qs.e: In September 2024, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal launched the Jan Sunwai Portal of the Department of Commerce. This portal is designed to streamline communication between stakeholders and authorities, enabling direct dialogue for grievance redressal and policy transparency. Through this portal, individuals can submit suggestions or complaints, ensuring timely resolution. It is a step under the Digital India initiative, making administration more accountable and efficient.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched the Jan Sunwai Portal? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Who is the minister who launched the portal? → Piyush Goyal
☛ What is the main objective of the portal? → Streamline communication between stakeholders and authorities
☛ When was the portal launched? → September 2024
☛ Which initiative is it a part of? → Digital India

q: Who assumed charge as Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff in October 2023?
qs.e: In October 2023, Vice Admiral Tarun Sobti assumed charge as Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff (DCNS). He succeeded Vice Admiral R. Hari Kumar who retired from the post. Vice Admiral Tarun Sobti is a specialist in communication and information systems and previously served as Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Naval Command. He was trained at the Indian Naval Academy and joined the Indian Navy in 1988. His appointment marks a significant change in the top command of the Indian Navy.
qs.kf:
☛ Deputy Chief of Naval Staff (Oct 2023) → Vice Admiral Tarun Sobti
☛ Previous Deputy Chief of Naval Staff → Vice Admiral R. Hari Kumar
☛ Specialisation of Vice Admiral Tarun Sobti → Communication and Information Systems
☛ Year of joining Navy → 1988
☛ Previous Position → Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Western Naval Command

q: In August 2024, Grinson George was appointed as the director of which of the following institutions?
o: Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), Ernakulam
ICAR-Central Institute of Research on Cotton Technology, Mumbai
qs.e: In August 2024, senior scientist Grinson George was appointed as the director of ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), Ernakulam. He was previously a principal scientist at CMFRI and has worked on the coastal ecosystem of the Bay of Bengal. CMFRI, under ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research), is a premier institute for marine fisheries research. Its headquarters is located in Kochi, Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ Which institute appointed Grinson George as director? → ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), Ernakulam
☛ Full form of CMFRI? → Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute
☛ CMFRI comes under which organization? → ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research)
☛ Headquarters of CMFRI? → Kochi, Kerala
☛ Field of Grinson George? → Marine ecology and fisheries research

q: In which of the following years were Union Territories (UT) introduced in India?
qs.e: The Union Territories (UTs) in India were introduced in the year 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. This act reorganized the country into states and union territories, placing certain areas directly under the central government's administration. The constitutional provisions for UTs are covered under Articles 239 to 242 of the Indian Constitution. Initially, 6 Union Territories were created. The system was a result of the linguistic reorganization of states. The President of India administers the UTs through an Administrator or Lieutenant Governor.
qs.kf:
☛ When were Union Territories first introduced in India? → 1956
☛ Who administers Union Territories? → President
☛ Which Articles cover Union Territories? → Articles 239-242
☛ What is the head of a Union Territory called? → Lieutenant Governor or Administrator
☛ How many Union Territories are there in India currently? → 8

q: When was the Disinvestment Commission established in India?
qs.e: The Disinvestment Commission in India was established in 1996. It was formed to streamline the process of selling government stakes in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). The commission's main objectives were to recommend disinvestment policies, evaluate the financial health of PSUs, and prepare attractive proposals for investors. Before its formation, the disinvestment process was unplanned. After the economic reforms of 1991, disinvestment was promoted, but the commission was set up only in 1996. It recommended the disinvestment of several PSUs, generating revenue for the government and increasing private participation. The commission played a key role in shaping India's disinvestment strategy.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Disinvestment Commission established? → 1996
☛ What was the main objective of the Disinvestment Commission? → To recommend disinvestment of PSUs
☛ In which year did India's first disinvestment take place? → 1991-92
☛ Which ministry handles the current disinvestment policy? → Ministry of Finance
☛ Who was the chairman of the Disinvestment Commission? → G.V. Ramakrishna

q: Who among the following was the Architect of the 'Basilica of Bom Jesus' in India?
qs.e: The Basilica of Bom Jesus located in Goa, India, was built between 1594 and 1605. Its architects were Julião Simão and Domingos Fernandes, who were of Portuguese origin. The church is built in the Baroque style and houses the remains of St. Francis Xavier. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is one of the oldest churches in Goa.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Basilica of Bom Jesus located? → Goa
☛ When was the Basilica of Bom Jesus built? → 1594-1605
☛ Whose relics are kept in the Basilica of Bom Jesus? → St. Francis Xavier
☛ In which style is the Basilica of Bom Jesus built? → Baroque style
☛ Which organization protects the Basilica of Bom Jesus? → UNESCO World Heritage

q: Which organisation conducted the study on background radiation levels in Kerala?
qs.e: The coastal regions of Kerala have naturally high background radiation due to the presence of thorium in monazite sands. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) conducted a comprehensive study to assess the radiation levels and their health effects on the local population. BARC is India's premier nuclear research institute under the Department of Atomic Energy. The study evaluated biological effects and found no significant increase in cancer rates despite high natural radiation. This research provides crucial data for radiation safety and management of monazite resources. BARC's findings help in understanding long-term low-dose radiation exposure and formulating safety guidelines for similar environments globally.
qs.kf:
☛ Which mineral causes high background radiation in Kerala? → Monazite (thorium)
☛ What is the full form of BARC? → Bhabha Atomic Research Centre
☛ Under which department does BARC function? → Department of Atomic Energy
☛ What was the main objective of the Kerala radiation study? → Health impact assessment
☛ Which radioactive element is found in monazite sand? → Thorium

q: Who was the chairman of the National Commission on Farmers (NCF) when it was constituted on 18 November 2004 in India?
qs.e: The National Commission on Farmers (NCF) was constituted on 18 November 2004 by the Government of India to address the problems faced by farmers. Its chairman was MS Swaminathan, a renowned agricultural scientist known as the father of the Green Revolution in India. The commission submitted five reports covering issues like farmers' income, credit, irrigation, market access, and climate change. Swaminathan's recommendations shaped farmer welfare policies. Among other options, Krishnaswamy Kasturirangan is a space scientist, Chakravarthi Rangarajan is an economist, and Verghese Kurien is associated with the dairy industry.
qs.kf:
☛ Chairman of NCF → MS Swaminathan
☛ When was NCF constituted? → 18 November 2004
☛ MS Swaminathan is known as → Father of Green Revolution in India
☛ Number of reports submitted by NCF → Five
☛ Full name of MS Swaminathan → Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan

q: In which year was the World Trade Organization, which has promoted globalisation across nations, established?
qs.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established on January 1, 1995, as the successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which had been in effect since 1948. The WTO aims to liberalize international trade and resolve trade disputes among member nations. Its headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. With 164 member countries, the WTO accounts for about 98% of global trade. The organization has played a key role in promoting globalization by reducing trade barriers and fostering economic integration. India is a founding member of the WTO.
qs.kf:
☛ WTO establishment year → 1995
☛ WTO headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Predecessor organization of WTO → GATT
☛ Total member countries in WTO → 164
☛ Main objective of WTO → Liberalize international trade

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 3
q: In which year did Francois Martin establish Pondicherry, which later emerged as the Headquarters of the French in India?
qs.e: Francois Martin established Pondicherry in 1674. He was the first Governor of the French East India Company and developed Pondicherry as a major trading center. It later emerged as the Headquarters of the French in India. Pondicherry remained a French colony until 1954, when it was merged with India. The other options are 1794, 1762, and 1612, but 1674 is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Pondicherry → Francois Martin
☛ Year of establishment of Pondicherry → 1674
☛ Headquarters of French in India → Pondicherry
☛ First Governor of French East India Company → Francois Martin
☛ Year of merger of Pondicherry with India → 1954

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (11/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following is/are correct with respect to the World Trade Organization (WTO)?

1. WTO agreements cover trade in goods as well as services to facilitate international trade. 2. It aims to remove tariff as well as non-tariff barriers and provide greater market access to all member countries.
3. India has kept its commitments towards liberalisation of trade, made in the WTO, by removing quantitative restrictions on imports and reducing tariff rates.
qs.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international organization that regulates trade between member countries. Its agreements cover trade in goods as well as services, such as GATT and GATS. The WTO aims to reduce tariff and non-tariff barriers and provide greater market access to all members. India has fulfilled its commitments under the WTO by removing quantitative restrictions on imports and reducing tariff rates. Hence, all three statements are correct.
qs.kf:
☛ WTO Headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ WTO established → 1 January 1995
☛ WTO member countries → 164 (as of 2024)
☛ WTO key agreements → GATT (goods), GATS (services), TRIPS (intellectual property)
☛ WTO principle → Non-discrimination (Most Favoured Nation and National Treatment)

q: In December 2024, which industrial company was certified as a ‘Great Place to Work’?
qs.e: In December 2024, SAIL was certified as a 'Great Place to Work'. This certification reflects high standards of employee experience and work culture. SAIL is India's leading iron and steel producing company, headquartered in New Delhi. The certification underscores the company's commitment to workplace quality and employee well-being.

☛ Year of establishment of SAIL? → 1954

q: Where is the headquarters of the National Turmeric Board, which was established in 2025?
qs.e: The National Turmeric Board was established in 2025 by the Government of India to promote turmeric growers and boost turmeric exports. Its headquarters is located in Nizamabad, Telangana, which is a major turmeric-producing region in the country. The board aims to promote cultivation, processing, marketing, and research of turmeric. This initiative was taken to enhance self-reliance in turmeric production and increase export capacity.

q: What was the total financial allocation for the Department of Rural Development for FY 2024-25, as per the Demand of Grants 2024-25 Analysis?
qs.e: For FY 2024-25, the Union Budget allocated ₹1.77 lakh crore to the Department of Rural Development, higher than the previous year's ₹1.60 lakh crore. This allocation aims to improve infrastructure, employment generation, and living standards in rural areas. Key schemes include MGNREGA, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin), Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, and Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana. MGNREGA received ₹86,000 crore, a major portion of the total allocation. Additionally, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) has a provision of ₹54,500 crore. This allocation reflects the government's increasing focus on rural development.

☛ Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) allocation for FY 2024-25 → ₹54,500 crore
☛ Major scheme under Department of Rural Development → Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of BIMSTEC?
qs.e: BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) is a regional organization comprising seven member countries: Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Bhutan, and Nepal. It was established in 1997. Maldives is not a member of BIMSTEC. The primary objective of BIMSTEC is to promote economic cooperation, technical partnerships, and trade. Its secretariat is headquartered in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

☛ What is the full form of BIMSTEC? → Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
☛ When was BIMSTEC established? → 1997

☛ How many members does BIMSTEC have? → Seven
☛ Which country is not a founding member of BIMSTEC? → Bhutan and Nepal joined later

q: Where is the Central Potato Research Institute of India located?
qs.e: India's Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) is located in Shimla. Established in 1949, it functions under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). Its primary objectives include developing high-yielding potato varieties, improving production technologies, and managing diseases. CPRI has released over 60 potato varieties suitable for different agro-climatic regions. The institute also has regional research stations in Patna, Jalandhar, Modipuram, and other locations. CPRI plays a key role in India's potato production, which is the third largest in the world.

☛ CPRI comes under which organization? → ICAR
☛ When was CPRI established? → 1949
☛ How many potato varieties has CPRI developed? → Over 60
☛ Where are other regional centers of CPRI? → Patna, Jalandhar, Modipuram, etc.

q: Where are the headquarters of the OECD is located?
qs.e: The headquarters of the OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) is located in Paris, France. It was established in 1961 to promote economic cooperation and development among its member countries. Currently, it has 38 member nations. The headquarters is situated at Château de la Muette in Paris.

q: The National Rural Health Mission was launched in the year:
qs.e: The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) was launched by the Government of India on 12 April 2005 under the leadership of then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. Its primary aim is to improve the availability, accessibility, and quality of healthcare services in rural areas. NRHM places special emphasis on reducing maternal and infant mortality rates and controlling fertility rates. Key initiatives include the appointment of ASHA workers, strengthening of Primary Health Centres (PHCs), and conducting immunization drives. In 2013, NRHM was merged into the National Health Mission (NHM), which also includes the urban health mission. This flagship program has significantly contributed to public health in rural India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NRHM launched? → 2005
☛ What is the full form of NRHM? → National Rural Health Mission
☛ What was the main focus of NRHM? → Rural healthcare improvement

☛ Which community worker was appointed under NRHM? → ASHA

q: The inter-governmental-tready-based organisation having its headquarters in India is:
qs.e: ISA (International Solar Alliance) is an inter-governmental treaty-based organisation with its headquarters in India. It was founded in 2015 during COP21 in Paris by India and France. Its headquarters is located in Gurugram, Haryana. ISA aims to promote solar energy expansion and foster cooperation among member countries. Currently, over 100 countries are members of ISA. Other options: NATO headquarters in Brussels, ATS is not a known inter-governmental organisation, and OECD headquarters in Paris.
