q: Who coined the word "Artificial Intelligence"?
qs.e: The term Artificial Intelligence (AI) was first coined by John McCarthy in 1956 at the Dartmouth Conference. He is widely recognized as the father of AI for his pioneering work. The conference is considered the birthplace of AI as a field. John McCarthy also made significant contributions to computer science, including the development of the programming language LISP. His work laid the foundation for modern AI research and development.
qs.kf:
☛ Who coined the term AI? → John McCarthy
☛ Where was the first AI conference held? → Dartmouth College, 1956
☛ What programming language did John McCarthy develop? → LISP
☛ In which year was the term AI coined? → 1956
☛ Who is known as the father of AI? → John McCarthy

q: In which year was the Setu Bharatam Programme launched?
qs.e: The Setu Bharatam Programme was launched in 2016 by the Government of India. Its objective was to make bridges on national highways stronger and safer. Under this scheme, 208 old bridges were targeted for replacement and over 1500 bridges for repair. The programme was executed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. The main aim was to improve traffic safety and prevent bridge collapse incidents. All bridges were prioritized based on their structural strength under Setu Bharatam.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was Setu Bharatam launched? → 2016
☛ What was its objective? → Strengthen and secure bridges
☛ Which ministry implemented it? → Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
☛ How many bridges were targeted for replacement? → 208
☛ What was the focus of Setu Bharatam? → Traffic safety and bridge repair

q: How many countries are the members of OPEC as of November 2020?
qs.e: OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, had 13 member countries as of November 2020. It was founded in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. Later, Qatar (1961), Indonesia (1962), Libya (1962), UAE (1967), Algeria (1969), Nigeria (1971), Ecuador (1973), Gabon (1975), Angola (2007), Equatorial Guinea (2017), and Congo (2018) joined. However, some countries left or rejoined. By November 2020, OPEC had 13 permanent members: Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Venezuela, Algeria, Angola, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Libya, Nigeria, and UAE. Since 2020, Ecuador left in 2020, reducing the count to 12 as of 2024. OPEC aims to coordinate petroleum policies among member countries.
qs.kf:
☛ OPEC headquarters → Vienna, Austria
☛ OPEC founded → 14 September 1960
☛ OPEC founding members → 5 countries (Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela)
☛ OPEC members as of 2024 → 12 countries (Ecuador left in 2020)
☛ OPEC+ includes → Russia, Mexico, etc. (non-members)

q: The expression 'Aaya Ram,, Gaya Ram' become popular in political vocabulary in India to describe:
qs.e: The expression 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' became popular in Indian political vocabulary to describe the trend of defection (party switching). This phrase is associated with Gaya Lal, a legislator from Haryana who changed parties multiple times in 1967. It is said that he changed parties three times in a single day, giving rise to this saying. This incident highlighted the problem of defection in Indian politics and later led to the enactment of the Anti-Defection Law in 1985. The term is used for any politician who frequently switches parties.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is associated with 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram'? → Gaya Lal
☛ In which year did this incident take place? → 1967
☛ Gaya Lal was a legislator of which state? → Haryana
☛ Which law was enacted as a result of this incident? → Anti-Defection Law (1985)
☛ The Anti-Defection Law is added to which schedule of the Constitution? → Tenth Schedule

q: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations Organization (UNO)?
qs.e: The first Secretary-General of the United Nations Organization (UNO) was Trygve Lie. He was a Norwegian statesman who served from 1946 to 1952. Trygve Lie played a key role in the establishment of the UN and his tenure saw major events like the Korean War and the Berlin Blockade. Later, Dag Hammarskjöld became the second, U Thant the third, and Kurt Waldheim the fourth Secretary-General. The Secretary-General is the chief administrative officer of the UN and is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council.
qs.kf:
☛ First Secretary-General of UNO → Trygve Lie
☛ Country of Trygve Lie → Norway
☛ Term of Trygve Lie → 1946-1952
☛ Second Secretary-General of UNO → Dag Hammarskjöld
☛ Current UNO Secretary-General → António Guterres

q: The United Nations has ________ principal organs.
qs.e: The United Nations has 6 principal organs established by its Charter. They are: the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the Secretariat, the International Court of Justice, and the Trusteeship Council (currently suspended). The General Assembly comprises all 193 member states, while the Security Council has 15 members, including 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members. The International Court of Justice is located in The Hague, Netherlands. These organs oversee the functioning of the UN and are responsible for maintaining international peace and security.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of principal organs of UN → 6
☛ Largest organ → General Assembly
☛ Organ responsible for peace and security → Security Council
☛ Headquarters of International Court of Justice → The Hague, Netherlands
☛ Currently suspended organ → Trusteeship Council

q: Select the option with the INCORRECT full form for the corresponding acronyms.
o: CITES : Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
C-DAC : Centre for Development of Advanced Computing
CHOGM : Commonwealth Heads of Government Ministries
qs.e: The full form of CHOGM is Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, not "Ministries". CHOGM is a biennial summit of heads of government (prime ministers or presidents) from Commonwealth nations. CITES stands for Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, which is correct. CCI stands for Competition Commission of India, correct. C-DAC stands for Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, also correct. Therefore, only the full form of CHOGM is incorrectly stated in the options.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of CITES? → Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
☛ What is the full form of CCI? → Competition Commission of India
☛ What is the full form of C-DAC? → Centre for Development of Advanced Computing
☛ What is the correct full form of CHOGM? → Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting
☛ How often is CHOGM held? → Every two years

q: What does the acronym SMPS stand for?
qs.e: SMPS stands for Switched-Mode Power Supply. It is a high-efficiency power supply that uses a switching regulator to convert input voltage to the desired output voltage. Compared to traditional linear power supplies, it is smaller, lighter, and more efficient. It is widely used in computers, televisions, chargers, and other electronic devices. SMPS uses MOSFETs or transistors for fast switching, reducing energy loss.
qs.kf:
☛ SMPS full form → Switched-Mode Power Supply
☛ Main component used in SMPS → MOSFET or transistor
☛ Efficiency of SMPS → 80-90% (higher than linear supply)
☛ Application of SMPS → Computers, chargers, TVs, adapters
☛ Advantage of SMPS → Light weight, compact size, high efficiency

q: India is an associate member of _________.
qs.e: India is an associate member of SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Area). SAFTA came into force in 2006 with the aim of reducing trade barriers among SAARC countries. India is a founding member of SAFTA and plays an active role in promoting economic integration in South Asia. ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is not an associate member; India is a dialogue partner of ASEAN. LAIA (Latin American Integration Association) and NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement) are not relevant to India. Thus, India is an associate member of SAFTA.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of SAFTA → South Asian Free Trade Area
☛ Year SAFTA came into force → 2006
☛ SAFTA is associated with which organization → SAARC
☛ Type of membership India holds in SAFTA → Associate member
☛ Main objective of SAFTA → Promote free trade in South Asia

q: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) was established in:
qs.e: India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is a premier military research institute, established in 1958 by the Government of India. It functions under the Ministry of Defence and its headquarters is located in New Delhi. DRDO's primary objective is to develop advanced defence technologies and weapon systems for the Indian Armed Forces. The organisation has contributed to several significant projects, including Agni and Prithvi missiles and the Tejas fighter aircraft. Prior to DRDO's establishment, defence research was carried out by various smaller organisations, but in 1958 all these were integrated to form a single autonomous entity.
qs.kf:
☛ When was DRDO established? → 1958
☛ Under which ministry does DRDO function? → Ministry of Defence
☛ Where is the headquarters of DRDO? → New Delhi
☛ Major missile developed by DRDO? → Agni, Prithvi
☛ Full form of DRDO? → Defence Research and Development Organisation

q: How many members are there in the Security Council of the UN as of October 2020?
qs.e: The United Nations Security Council has a total of 15 members, consisting of 5 permanent members (China, France, Russia, UK, USA) and 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms. Each permanent member holds veto power. Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly, with consideration given to regional groups. As of October 2020, this structure remains unchanged.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of permanent members of Security Council → 5
☛ Term of non-permanent members → 2 years
☛ Who holds veto power? → Permanent members
☛ Who elects non-permanent members? → General Assembly
☛ Total members in Security Council → 15

q: Who among the following replaced Pahlaj Nihalani as the Chairperson of Central Board of Film Certification?
qs.e: Prasoon Joshi replaced Pahlaj Nihalani as the Chairperson of the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). Joshi is a renowned lyricist, screenwriter, and advertising professional. He was appointed as the CBFC chairperson in March 2017 for a three-year term, which was later extended. He has received several awards, including the National Film Award and the Padma Shri. He resides in Mumbai and has written lyrics for many Bollywood films. Under his leadership, the CBFC has taken steps to streamline certification processes.
qs.kf:
☛ When was CBFC established? → 1952
☛ Where is CBFC headquartered? → Mumbai
☛ When did Pahlaj Nihalani become CBFC chairperson? → 2015
☛ Which award was given to Prasoon Joshi? → Padma Shri (2015)
☛ What was the former name of CBFC? → Board of Film Censors

q: Headquarters of International Maritime Organization (IMO) is located at:
qs.e: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for regulating shipping. Its headquarters is located in London, United Kingdom. Established in 1948 in Geneva, the IMO moved to London in 1958. It sets global standards for maritime safety, security, and environmental protection. All member states convene in London for meetings. The other options, Washington (IMF headquarters), New York (UN headquarters), and Geneva (WHO, ILO), are incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ When was IMO established? → 1948
☛ IMO is a specialized agency of which organization? → United Nations
☛ What is the main purpose of IMO? → Maritime safety and environmental protection
☛ Where is the headquarters of IMO located? → London
☛ What is the title of the head of IMO? → Secretary-General

q: What is the overall length of Golden Quadrilateral in India?
qs.e: The Golden Quadrilateral is a major highway network in India that connects four metropolitan cities - Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata. Its total length is 5846 km. This project was implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The Golden Quadrilateral was the first phase of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP). The network consists of four to six-lane highways. It plays a crucial role in boosting road transport and traffic in India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the total length of Golden Quadrilateral? → 5846 km
☛ Which cities does Golden Quadrilateral connect? → Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata
☛ Which agency implements Golden Quadrilateral? → NHAI
☛ Golden Quadrilateral is part of which project? → NHDP
☛ How many lanes does Golden Quadrilateral have? → Four to six lanes

q: The 'Bretton Woods Twins' refers to the two multilateral organisations created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944. They are ______ and ______.
qs.e: The Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 established the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, collectively known as the 'Bretton Woods Twins'. The IMF aims to promote global monetary cooperation and provide assistance to countries facing balance of payments crises. The World Bank provides long-term loans and technical assistance for economic development in developing countries. WTO was established in 1995, and the United Nations was founded in 1945, so these are not products of the Bretton Woods Conference. Thus, the correct pair is IMF and World Bank.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Bretton Woods Conference held? → 1944
☛ Where is the IMF headquarters located? → Washington D.C.
☛ What was the original name of the World Bank? → International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
☛ When did the Bretton Woods system end? → 1971
☛ In which year was the WTO established? → 1995

q: United Nations was established in:
qs.e: The United Nations Organization (UNO) was established on 24 October 1945, when the UN Charter was ratified by 51 countries. It was formed after World War II to maintain international peace and security. Its predecessor, the League of Nations, was founded in 1920 but failed to prevent the war. The UN headquarters is located in New York. It has six principal organs: the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Secretariat, International Court of Justice, and Trusteeship Council.
qs.kf:
☛ When is UN Day celebrated? → October 24
☛ When was the UN Charter signed? → June 26, 1945
☛ Who was the first UN Secretary-General? → Trygve Lie (Norway)
☛ Who is the current UN Secretary-General? → António Guterres
☛ How many member states are in the UN? → 193

q: What is the full form of BARC?
qs.e: The full form of BARC is Bhabha Atomic Research Center. It is India's premier nuclear research institute, established in 1954. It is named after the renowned Indian scientist Dr. Homi J. Bhabha. BARC headquarters is located in Mumbai. This institution conducts research in areas such as nuclear energy, reactor design, radiation safety, and nuclear medicine. It is the backbone of India's nuclear energy program.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of BARC → Mumbai, Maharashtra
☛ Establishment year of BARC → 1954
☛ BARC named after → Dr. Homi J. Bhabha
☛ BARC comes under which ministry → Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)
☛ First director of BARC → Dr. Homi J. Bhabha

q: Since July 2016, World Trade Organisation (WTO) has ______ members.
qs.e: In July 2016, Afghanistan joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) as its 164th member. The WTO was established in 1995 and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. It sets global trade rules and resolves trade disputes. Currently, the WTO has 164 member countries, which account for about 98% of global trade. India is a founding member of the WTO. The most recent members are Afghanistan (2016) and Liberia (2016). The highest decision-making body of the WTO is the Ministerial Conference, which meets every two years.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the WTO headquarters located? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ When was the WTO established? → 1995
☛ What is the highest body of the WTO? → Ministerial Conference
☛ Which country became the 164th WTO member? → Afghanistan
☛ Which countries joined the WTO in 2016? → Afghanistan and Liberia

q: When is the 'world health day' celebrated?
qs.e: World Health Day is celebrated annually on 7th April. This date marks the anniversary of the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948. The primary purpose of this day is to raise awareness about global health issues. Each year, the WHO selects a specific theme, such as 'Universal Health Coverage' or 'Our Planet, Our Health'. Governments, NGOs, and communities worldwide organize activities like health education programs, screening camps, and policy advocacy on this day. It serves as a platform to highlight pressing health challenges and mobilize action towards achieving better health outcomes for all.
qs.kf:
☛ When was WHO established? → 1948
☛ Where is WHO headquarters? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Who decides the theme of World Health Day? → World Health Organization
☛ When was World Health Day first celebrated? → 1950
☛ What does WHO stand for? → World Health Organization

q: Which of the following organisation completed the 50th year of their establishment in 2019?
qs.e: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established on 15 August 1969. In 2019, ISRO completed 50 years of its establishment. ISRO is India's premier space agency, responsible for space research and technology development. It was founded under the leadership of Vikram Sarabhai. ISRO has gained global recognition through successful missions like Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, and satellite launches. Among the other options, HAL (1940), BARC (1954), and DRDO (1958) were established earlier, so they did not complete 50 years in 2019.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the founder of ISRO? → Vikram Sarabhai
☛ Where is ISRO's headquarters located? → Bengaluru, Karnataka
☛ What was ISRO's first satellite? → Aryabhata (1975)
☛ Who is the current chairman of ISRO? → S. Somanath
☛ What is the full form of ISRO? → Indian Space Research Organisation

q: Name the Punjabi Muslim, who was a student at Cambridge and who coined the term 'Pak - Stan' in 1933?
qs.e: Chaudhary Rehmat Ali was a Punjabi Muslim who studied at Cambridge University. In 1933, he coined the term 'Pak-Stan' (later Pakistan) in his pamphlet 'Now or Never'. He advocated for a separate homeland for Muslims in South Asia, combining regions like Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh, and Balochistan. Although he was among the early proponents of the Pakistan movement, he did not live to see the creation of Pakistan in 1947; he died in 1951. His contribution is significant as he provided the name that later became the official name of the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Who coined the term Pakistan? → Chaudhary Rehmat Ali
☛ Which pamphlet did Rehmat Ali publish in 1933? → Now or Never
☛ In which year was the term Pak-Stan coined? → 1933
☛ Which university did Rehmat Ali attend? → Cambridge
☛ From which region did Rehmat Ali belong? → Punjab

q: The Secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was set up at __________ in 1987.
qs.e: The Secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in 1987 at Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal. SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The founding members are Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Later, in 2007, Afghanistan was added. The main objectives of SAARC include promoting economic cooperation, social progress, and regional integration in South Asia. The Secretariat is headed by a Secretary-General and coordinates the meetings and activities of the association.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the SAARC headquarters located? → Kathmandu, Nepal
☛ When was SAARC founded? → 1985
☛ When was the SAARC Secretariat established? → 1987
☛ How many founding members does SAARC have? → 7 (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka)
☛ Which country joined SAARC later? → Afghanistan (2007)

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC)?
qs.e: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has 5 permanent members: USA, UK, France, Russia, and China. These are the victorious nations of World War II and possess veto power. Japan is not a permanent member of the UNSC; it can only be elected as a non-permanent member. Japan has pushed for UN reforms and a permanent seat but has not succeeded. Other non-permanent members are elected for two-year terms.
qs.kf:
☛ Number of permanent members of UNSC → 5
☛ Term of non-permanent members of UNSC → 2 years
☛ Who has veto power in UNSC → Permanent members
☛ Headquarters of UNSC → New York
☛ Is Japan a permanent member of UNSC → No

q: FIFA stands for:
o: Federation Internationale de Freestyle Swimming Association
qs.e: FIFA stands for Federation Internationale de Football Association, which is a French term. It was founded on May 21, 1904 in Paris, France. Its headquarters is located in Zurich, Switzerland. FIFA is the highest governing body of world football and organizes major tournaments like the FIFA World Cup. The current president of FIFA is Gianni Infantino. The abbreviation FIFA is derived from the French name, which is why it does not match the English translation.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of FIFA? → Zurich, Switzerland
☛ When was FIFA founded? → May 21, 1904
☛ Who is the current president of FIFA? → Gianni Infantino
☛ Which major tournament is organized by FIFA? → FIFA World Cup
☛ In which language is the full name of FIFA? → French

name: Set 6 · Q221–264
sub: Static GK - Organisations, Abbreviations & Full Forms

q: Where was the Commonwealth Games 2018 held?
qs.e: The 2018 Commonwealth Games were held in Gold Coast, Australia. These were the 21st Commonwealth Games, took place from 4 to 15 April 2018. A total of 71 nations participated and competed in 18 sports. Australia topped the medal table with 198 medals (80 gold). India finished third with 66 medals (26 gold). It was the second time Australia hosted the Games, previously in 2006 Melbourne. The Carrara Stadium was the main venue. The Games were officially opened by Prince Charles. The mascot was Borobi, a koala bear. This event marked a successful edition with high participation and competitive spirit.
qs.kf:
☛ Where were the 2022 Commonwealth Games held? → Birmingham, England
☛ Where were the first Commonwealth Games in 1930 held? → Hamilton, Canada
☛ What was the mascot of 2018 Commonwealth Games? → Borobi (Koala)
☛ Where is the headquarters of Commonwealth Games? → London, England
☛ When did India first participate in Commonwealth Games? → 1934

q: What is the expansion of BHIM?
qs.e: BHIM stands for Bharat Interface for Money. It is a UPI-based payment app developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It was launched on 31 December 2016. BHIM allows users to make instant transactions using bank accounts, UPI ID, or QR codes. It is part of the Digital India initiative to promote cashless transactions. BHIM is named after B. R. Ambedkar.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the expansion of BHIM? → Bharat Interface for Money
☛ Who developed BHIM? → NPCI
☛ When was BHIM launched? → 31 December 2016
☛ Which payment system does BHIM use? → UPI
☛ Who is BHIM named after? → B. R. Ambedkar

q: What is the driving force and executive body of the European Union (EU)?
qs.e: The driving force and executive body of the European Union (EU) is the European Commission. It proposes and implements EU policies, ensures compliance with EU laws, and manages the EU budget. The Commission consists of 27 members (one from each country), known as Commissioners. Its headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium. The Commission represents the interests of the EU and works alongside the European Parliament and the Council. Other options: Court of Auditors handles financial audits; Council of the European Union represents ministers of member states; European Parliament is the legislative body.
qs.kf:
☛ President of the European Commission → Ursula von der Leyen
☛ Number of European Commissioners → 27 (one per country)
☛ Headquarters of European Commission → Brussels, Belgium
☛ Legislative bodies of the EU → European Parliament and Council
☛ Highest judicial institution of the EU → European Court of Justice

q: _____ on 9 September 2024 emphasised that safety and social audits of cities and institutions should be carried out to get a better idea about the lags and issues that currently exist in terms of ensuring women’s safety in India.
o: The All India Federation of Women Lawyers (AIFWL)
qs.e: On 9 September 2024, the NHRC emphasised conducting safety and social audits of cities and institutions to identify gaps in ensuring women's safety in India. The NHRC is a statutory body formed under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It aims to protect and promote human rights. Women's safety remains a critical issue, and the NHRC regularly issues recommendations. These audits will help policymakers formulate effective measures. The NHRC's proactive role underscores its commitment to addressing systemic issues affecting women.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NHRC established? → 1993
☛ Who heads the NHRC? → Former Chief Justice of India as Chairperson
☛ What is NHRC's role in women's safety? → Advisory and monitoring
☛ Purpose of social audit? → Assess policy effectiveness
☛ Full name of human rights act? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993

q: Which organisation partnered with NABARD to organise the 'Climate Changemakers' dialogue in August 2024?
o: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
qs.e: In August 2024, NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) partnered with GIZ to organise the 'Climate Changemakers' dialogue. The dialogue aimed to discuss innovative solutions to combat climate change. GIZ is a German development agency working globally for sustainable development. NABARD provides financial support for rural development in India. Under this partnership, both organisations will work towards climate-resilient agriculture and livelihoods.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NABARD? → National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
☛ Where is the headquarters of GIZ? → Bonn, Germany
☛ When was NABARD established? → 1982
☛ Name the climate change convention? → UNFCCC
☛ What sector does GIZ work in? → Sustainable development and international cooperation

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 3
q: How many Indian States and Union Territories have a coastline as per the Annual Report 2022-23 of the Ministry of Home Affairs?
qs.e: According to the Annual Report 2022-23 of the Ministry of Home Affairs, India has 9 states and 4 union territories with a coastline. The states with a coastline are: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal. The union territories are: Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Puducherry, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It is notable that Lakshadweep is also a union territory with a coastline but is not included in this report. The total coastline length is approximately 7,516.6 km.
qs.kf:
☛ State with the longest coastline → Gujarat (approx. 1,600 km)
☛ State with the smallest coastline → Goa (approx. 160 km)
☛ Number of union territories with coastline → 4 (as per report)
☛ Total coastline of India → 7,516.6 km
☛ Total number of states with coastline → 9

q: Microsoft Corporation was founded in
qs.e: Microsoft Corporation was founded on April 4, 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. The company initially developed an interpreter called Altair BASIC for the Altair 8800 microcomputer. It later became the world's largest software company, with flagship products like Windows operating system and Microsoft Office suite. In 1981, Microsoft released MS-DOS operating system, which powered the IBM PC. Other options: 1979 (incorrect), 1981 (incorrect), and 1965 (incorrect).
qs.kf:
☛ Who are the founders of Microsoft? → Bill Gates and Paul Allen
☛ What was Microsoft's first product? → Altair BASIC
☛ When was the first version of Windows released? → 1985
☛ Where is Microsoft's headquarters located? → Redmond, Washington, USA
☛ Who is the current CEO of Microsoft? → Satya Nadella

q: An event happening once in 4 years is described as
qs.e: The term 'quadrennial' means 'occurring every four years'. It is derived from Latin 'quadri-' (four) and 'ennial' (year). 'Biennial' means every two years, 'triennial' means every three years, and 'perennial' means throughout the year or every year. Therefore, an event happening once in four years is described as 'quadrennial'.
qs.kf:
☛ Biennial → Event happening every 2 years
☛ Triennial → Event happening every 3 years
☛ Quadrennial → Event happening every 4 years
☛ Perennial → Event happening every year or continuously
☛ Olympic Games → Example of quadrennial event

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice located?
qs.e: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, established in 1945. Its headquarters is located in The Hague, Netherlands, where it has been functioning since 1946. The Court's main role is to settle legal disputes between states and provide advisory opinions on international law. The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected for terms of 9 years. It is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of ICJ → The Hague (Netherlands)
☛ Year of establishment of ICJ → 1945
☛ Total number of judges in ICJ → 15
☛ Term of judges → 9 years
☛ ICJ is an organ of → United Nations

q: SAARC comprises how many Member States?
qs.e: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was established in 1985. It comprises 8 member states: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan. Afghanistan was admitted as the 8th member in 2007. Its headquarters is located in Kathmandu, Nepal. SAARC aims to promote economic development, social progress, and regional cooperation in South Asia.
qs.kf:
☛ SAARC headquarters → Kathmandu, Nepal
☛ SAARC founding year → 1985
☛ SAARC founding members → 7 countries (excluding Afghanistan)
☛ SAARC newest member → Afghanistan (2007)
☛ SAARC full form → South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation

q: Which of the United Nation's organization has the International Institute of Educational Planning at Paris as its Part?
qs.e: The International Institute of Educational Planning (IIEP) is a part of UNESCO. It was founded in 1963 and is headquartered in Paris, France. The main objective of IIEP is to strengthen educational planning and management in member countries. The institute provides training to policymakers, planners, and managers and conducts education policy research. UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) was established in 1945. UNESCO has also been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for its contributions to education.
qs.kf:
☛ IIEP headquarters → Paris, France
☛ IIEP foundation year → 1963
☛ UNESCO headquarters → Paris, France
☛ UNESCO foundation year → 1945
☛ UNESCO Director-General → Audrey Azoulay

q: What is the full form of WCED (also known as Brundtland Commission) formed by the United Nations for sustainable development?
o: World Commission on Environment and Development
qs.e: The full form of WCED is World Commission on Environment and Development. It was established by the United Nations in 1983 to address sustainable development issues. The commission was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, then Prime Minister of Norway, hence it is commonly known as the Brundtland Commission. In 1987, the commission published the report 'Our Common Future', which defined sustainable development as 'development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs'. The commission focused on balancing environmental protection with economic development.
qs.kf:
☛ Who chaired the Brundtland Commission? → Gro Harlem Brundtland
☛ Which report was published by WCED? → Our Common Future
☛ What is the full form of WCED? → World Commission on Environment and Development
☛ In which report was sustainable development defined? → Our Common Future report
☛ When was WCED established? → 1983

q: Which organization was established on 15 July 1948 with the motto 'Unity and Discipline'?
qs.e: The National Cadet Corps (NCC) was established on 15 July 1948 with the motto 'Unity and Discipline'. Its aim is to develop discipline, patriotism, and leadership among youth. The NCC was formed under the Indian Defence Act, driven by the need to provide military training to young people after independence. Its headquarters is in New Delhi and it operates with the cooperation of all three armed forces. RIMC (1922), NDA (1954), and Indian Military Academy (1932) were established in different years.
qs.kf:
☛ Establishment date of NCC → 15 July 1948
☛ Motto of NCC → Unity and Discipline
☛ Headquarters of NCC → New Delhi
☛ Act related to NCC → Indian Defence Act
☛ Objective of NCC → Develop discipline, patriotism, and leadership in youth

q: Where is the headquarters of Geological Survey of India located?
qs.e: The headquarters of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) is located in Kolkata. Established in 1848, it functions under the Ministry of Mines. GSI is the premier organization in India conducting geological surveys, assessment of mineral resources, and geological studies. Its key functions include geological mapping, mineral exploration, seismic studies, and evaluation of groundwater resources. While GSI has regional offices across the country, its headquarters remains in Kolkata.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Geological Survey of India → Kolkata
☛ Year of establishment → 1848
☛ Ministry under which it works → Ministry of Mines
☛ Main functions → Geological mapping and mineral exploration
☛ Regional offices → Across the country

q: Which one of the following bodies are NOT Bretton Woods Institutions?
qs.e: The Bretton Woods Conference, held in 1944, led to the establishment of two major institutions: the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. These are collectively known as the Bretton Woods Institutions. The United Nations is a separate international organization established in 1945 at the San Francisco Conference. The United Nations is not part of the Bretton Woods system. The IMF and World Bank focus on global financial stability and development, while the UN focuses on peace, security, and human rights. Therefore, among the options, only the United Nations is not a Bretton Woods Institution. Options 2 and 3 (IMF and World Bank) are indeed Bretton Woods Institutions.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Bretton Woods Conference held? → 1944
☛ Which are the Bretton Woods Institutions? → IMF and World Bank
☛ Where is the IMF headquartered? → Washington D.C., USA
☛ What is the main purpose of the World Bank? → Provide loans to developing countries
☛ When was the United Nations established? → 1945

q: In which year was the European Union established?
qs.e: The European Union was established on 1 November 1993 when the Maastricht Treaty came into force. The treaty was signed in 1992 but became effective in 1993. The EU replaced the European Economic Community (EEC) and laid the foundation for a single market, a common currency (the euro), and a common foreign policy. The EU currently has 27 member states and its headquarters is in Brussels.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Maastricht Treaty signed? → 1992
☛ Which are the main institutions of the EU? → European Commission, Parliament, Council
☛ What is the common currency of the EU? → Euro
☛ Where is the EU headquarters located? → Brussels
☛ How many member states does the EU have currently? → 27

q: Who among the following in NOT the founding members of the United Nation?
qs.e: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945 with 51 founding members. These were countries that had signed the Declaration by United Nations (1942) or participated in the San Francisco Conference (1945). Germany was not among them, as it was divided into four occupation zones after World War II. Germany later joined the UN in 1973. USA and France are founding members. Cuba is also a founding member, having signed the Charter in 1945.
qs.kf:
☛ UN establishment date → 24 October 1945
☛ Number of founding members → 51
☛ UN Charter signing location → San Francisco
☛ Germany's UN membership year → 1973
☛ Newest UN member → South Sudan (2011)

q: India joined the UNO in the year:
qs.e: India is a founding member of the United Nations Organization (UNO). The UN was established on 24 October 1945, and India joined it in the same year on 30 October 1945. At that time, India was under British rule but was granted separate membership. India signed the United Nations Charter. After independence, India continued as a member of the UN.
qs.kf:
☛ UNO establishment year → 1945
☛ UNO establishment day → 24 October 1945
☛ India joined UNO → 30 October 1945
☛ Founding members of UNO → 51 countries (including India)
☛ Current UNO members → 193 countries

q: Who was the head of the committee of the Draft National Education Policy (NEP) 2019?
qs.e: The head of the committee for the Draft National Education Policy (NEP) 2019 was Dr. K. Kasturirangan. He is a renowned Indian space scientist and former chairman of ISRO. This committee drafted the new education policy, which was approved by the government in 2020. NEP 2020 includes major reforms such as the 5+3+3+4 school structure replacing the 10+2 system and a 4-year undergraduate program in higher education. The Kasturirangan Committee emphasized a holistic and multidisciplinary approach to education.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the chairman of the drafting committee of NEP 2020? → Dr. K. Kasturirangan
☛ Kasturirangan is the former chairman of which organization? → ISRO
☛ What is the new school structure in NEP 2020? → 5+3+3+4
☛ What is the minimum duration of undergraduate programs in NEP 2020? → 4 years
☛ In which year was NEP 2020 implemented? → 2020

q: What is the full form of BHIM?
qs.e: The full form of BHIM is Bharat Interface for Money. It is a UPI-based payment app developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). Named after Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, BHIM allows users to make direct transactions from their bank accounts. It was launched in December 2016 to promote digital payments after demonetization. The app is available on both Android and iOS platforms, requiring only a mobile number and bank account to operate. Other options like 'Intraface' or 'Bheem' are incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of BHIM? → Bharat Interface for Money
☛ Who developed BHIM? → NPCI
☛ BHIM is based on which payment system? → UPI (Unified Payments Interface)
☛ When was BHIM launched? → December 2016
☛ Who is BHIM named after? → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

q: Who among the following designed 7, Lok Kalyan Marg?
qs.e: 7, Lok Kalyan Marg (formerly 7, Race Course Road) is the official residence of the Prime Minister of India. This building was designed by the renowned British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens. Lutyens is famous for planning New Delhi and designing many important buildings such as Rashtrapati Bhavan (Viceroy's House) and India Gate. 7, Lok Kalyan Marg is a large mansion housing the Prime Minister's office and residence. Lutyens designed this building in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style, which blends Indian and Western elements. Although several renovations have taken place over time, the original structure remains Lutyens' design.
qs.kf:
☛ Who designed 7, Lok Kalyan Marg? → Sir Edwin Lutyens
☛ Who were the chief architects of New Delhi? → Sir Edwin Lutyens and Sir Herbert Baker
☛ Who designed Rashtrapati Bhavan? → Sir Edwin Lutyens
☛ Who designed India Gate? → Sir Edwin Lutyens
☛ What was the earlier name of 7, Lok Kalyan Marg? → 7, Race Course Road

q: In which year did India join the United Nations?
qs.e: India is a founding member of the United Nations. The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945, and India signed the UN Charter on 30 October 1945, thus joining the UN in 1945. India is one of the 51 original founding members of the United Nations. India became a member of the UN even before its independence from British rule.
qs.kf:
☛ UN foundation day → 24 October 1945
☛ Number of founding members of UN → 51
☛ India signed UN Charter on → 30 October 1945
☛ UN headquarters → New York, USA
☛ India joined UN as → founding member in 1945

q: What is the name of the intergovernmental military alliance between 30 European and North American countries?
qs.e: NATO, which stands for North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is an intergovernmental military alliance between 30 European and North American countries. It was established on April 4, 1949, with the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C. The core principle of NATO is collective defense, as outlined in Article 5, which states that an attack on one member is an attack on all. NATO's headquarters are located in Brussels, Belgium. The alliance aims to ensure military cooperation and collective security among its members.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NATO founded? → 1949
☛ Where is NATO headquarters located? → Brussels
☛ What is the core principle of NATO? → Collective defense
☛ How many members does NATO have? → 30
☛ Which article covers collective defense? → Article 5

q: In December 2018, the United Nations declared 7th June as:
qs.e: In December 2018, the United Nations General Assembly declared 7 June as World Food Safety Day. The aim is to raise awareness about the importance of food safety and its impact on human health, economic development, and sustainable development. This day was first observed in 2019 and is led by FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) and WHO (World Health Organization). Food safety is a global issue concerning safe food supply chains and prevention of foodborne diseases.
qs.kf:
☛ What day did the UN declare 7 June as? → World Food Safety Day
☛ When was World Food Safety Day first observed? → 2019
☛ Which two organizations lead this day? → FAO and WHO
☛ What issues does Food Safety Day focus on? → Safe food supply and prevention of foodborne diseases
☛ Where is the headquarters of FAO? → Rome, Italy

q: In which of the following years was the Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI) formed?
qs.e: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) was established in the year 1927. It was founded on the call of Mahatma Gandhi to promote Indian interests in trade and industry. FICCI is the largest and oldest industry organization in India. Its first president was G.D. Birla. The headquarters of FICCI is located in New Delhi. This organization acts as a bridge between the government and industry and influences economic policies. FICCI was established with the aim of protecting Indian industries from foreign competition and promoting indigenous industries.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded FICCI? → On the call of Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Who was the first president of FICCI? → G.D. Birla
☛ Where is the headquarters of FICCI? → New Delhi
☛ What is the full form of FICCI? → Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry
☛ What is the objective of FICCI? → To promote Indian industry and trade

q: Which of the following is the full form of SIDBI?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India
Small Industries and Domestic Bank of India
Small Inter Development Bank of India
Small Indian Development Bank for Industry
qs.e: The full form of SIDBI is Small Industries Development Bank of India. It is a financial institution established in 1990 under an Act of Parliament. SIDBI's primary objective is to provide financial assistance and development services to small-scale industries. Its headquarters is located in Lucknow. SIDBI offers loans, refinancing, and promotional support to small industries, thereby fostering their growth. It operates under the guidelines of the Reserve Bank of India and the Government of India. SIDBI plays a crucial role in the small industry sector by contributing to employment generation and economic development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was SIDBI established? → 1990
☛ Where is SIDBI's headquarters? → Lucknow
☛ What is the main objective of SIDBI? → Financial assistance to small industries
☛ What is the full form of SIDBI? → Small Industries Development Bank of India
☛ Under which act was SIDBI established? → Act of Parliament

q: United Nation Development Programme (UNDP) was founded in the year____.
qs.e: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) was established in 1965. It is a global development agency of the United Nations, working to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and promote sustainable development. Headquartered in New York, UNDP helps countries achieve their development goals. It is known for publishing the Human Development Index (HDI), which measures the development level of nations. Before its founding in 1965, the UN lacked a dedicated agency for development activities. UNDP operates in over 170 countries, providing technical assistance and policy advice.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is UNDP headquarters located? → New York
☛ What is the main aim of UNDP? → Poverty eradication and sustainable development
☛ Which index is associated with UNDP? → Human Development Index (HDI)
☛ When was UNDP founded? → 1965
☛ What type of agency is UNDP under the UN? → Development agency

q: Union Territory Pondicherry was renamed as Puducherry?
qs.e: The proposal to rename Pondicherry to Puducherry was passed in 2006. The name change was made to reflect the original name 'Puducherry' (new village) in Tamil language. Puducherry is a Union Territory comprising four regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam. The renaming aimed to promote local culture and move away from the French colonial legacy. The Indian government amended the constitution in 2006 to officially change the name of the Union Territory. This decision was part of a broader effort to restore indigenous names across India.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the old name of Puducherry? → Pondicherry
☛ When did Puducherry become a Union Territory? → 1963
☛ What are the official languages of Puducherry? → Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, French
☛ How many seats are in the Puducherry Legislative Assembly? → 33
☛ What is the area of Puducherry? → 492 square km

q: The United Nations Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) were announced in the year _______________.
qs.e: The United Nations Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) were announced in September 2000 at the UN Millennium Summit. It was attended by 189 countries and set 8 major goals: eradication of poverty, education, gender equality, reduction of child mortality, improvement of maternal health, combating HIV/AIDS and other diseases, environmental sustainability, and global partnership. The deadline was set for 2015. The MDGs were later replaced by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
qs.kf:
☛ Year MDGs were announced? → 2000
☛ Deadline for MDGs? → 2015
☛ Number of MDGs? → 8
☛ Replaced by? → SDGs
☛ Year SDGs were adopted? → 2015

q: India's telecom revolution is a major outcome of liberalisation. Which regulatory authority was established in 1997 to oversee the telecom sector?
qs.e: To oversee the telecom sector in India, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was established in 1997 as a result of liberalisation. TRAI is an independent regulatory body responsible for ensuring competition, consumer protection, and tariff setting in telecommunications. It regulates licensing, interconnection, and quality of service standards for telecom service providers. TRAI played a crucial role in the mobile revolution and making call rates affordable in India. In contrast, SEBI regulates stock markets, NABARD focuses on agricultural development, and IRDAI oversees insurance. TRAI's headquarters is in New Delhi, and its chairman is appointed by the central government. It has significantly contributed to the growth of India's telecom sector.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Telecom Regulatory Authority of India established? → 1997
☛ Full form of TRAI? → Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
☛ Headquarters of TRAI? → New Delhi
☛ Who sets telecom tariffs in India? → TRAI
☛ Who appoints the chairman of TRAI? → Central Government

q: As per Nov 2020, How many countries have membership in the World Trade Organisation?
qs.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international organization that sets the rules for global trade. As of November 2020, the WTO had a total of 164 member countries. It was established on 1 January 1995 and its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. The main objective of the WTO is to reduce trade barriers and facilitate trade among member nations. India is a founding member of the WTO. After November 2020, some new countries have joined, such as Comoros and Timor-Leste, but as of November 2020, the membership count was 164.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of WTO? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ When was WTO established? → 1 January 1995
☛ What type of member is India in WTO? → Founding member
☛ Number of WTO member countries as of Nov 2020? → 164
☛ What was the predecessor organization of WTO? → GATT

q: How many non-permanent members does the UN Council have?
qs.e: The United Nations Security Council consists of 15 members in total, comprising 5 permanent members (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) and 10 non-permanent members. The non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for a two-year term, with 5 members elected each year. These members are chosen based on geographical distribution: 5 from Africa and Asia, 2 from Latin America, 1 from Eastern Europe, and 2 from Western Europe and other states. Non-permanent members do not possess veto power but can vote on Council resolutions. The Council is responsible for maintaining international peace and security.
qs.kf:
☛ Total members of UN Security Council? → 15
☛ Number of permanent members? → 5
☛ Term of non-permanent members? → 2 years
☛ How many non-permanent members elected each year? → 5
☛ Which members have no veto power? → Non-permanent members

q: Who was the eighth Secretary-General of UN?
qs.e: The eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations was Ban Ki-Moon from South Korea. He served two terms from 1 January 2007 to 31 December 2016. Prior to this, he was the Foreign Minister of South Korea. Ban Ki-Moon is known for his work on peacekeeping and climate change. Antonio Guterres is the ninth Secretary-General. Kofi Annan was the seventh and U Thant was the third Secretary-General.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Secretary-General of UN? → Trygve Lie
☛ Who is the current Secretary-General of UN? → Antonio Guterres
☛ Who served the longest as Secretary-General? → U Thant (10 years, 2 months)
☛ Who was the only African Secretary-General? → Kofi Annan
☛ Which country did Ban Ki-Moon belong to? → South Korea

q: Which country became the 164th member of World Trade Organization on 29 July 2016?
qs.e: On 29 July 2016, Afghanistan became the 164th member of the World Trade Organization (WTO). The WTO is an international organization that regulates global trade rules. Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. Afghanistan's accession gave the WTO broader representation, especially from the South Asia region. This was a significant step for developing countries in terms of trade facilitation and economic integration. Afghanistan had been negotiating for membership since 2004. WTO members account for approximately 98% of global trade.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the WTO established? → 1 January 1995
☛ Where is the WTO headquarters? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ Who is the current WTO Director-General? → Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
☛ How many members does the WTO have? → 164 (as of 2016)
☛ Which agreement preceded the WTO? → GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade)

q: The Postal Index Number (PIN) is a six digit code used by Indian postal department, what does the first two digit of the code (taken together) stands for:
o: Sub region or one of the postal circles
qs.e: The Postal Index Number (PIN) is a six-digit code used by the Indian postal department. The first digit of the PIN indicates the postal zone (India is divided into 9 zones). The second digit indicates the sub-zone, and together, the first two digits represent a specific postal circle or sub-region. The third digit denotes the district, while the last three digits identify the delivery post office. For example, in PIN 110001, the first digit 1 represents the Delhi zone, and the second digit 1 indicates the sub-zone. Thus, the first two digits stand for a sub-region or one of the postal circles.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of PIN → Postal Index Number
☛ Total digits in PIN → 6
☛ First digit represents → Postal zone
☛ Last three digits represent → Delivery post office
☛ Third digit represents → District

q: Which was the first Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) to be established?
qs.e: The first Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) to be established in India is IIT Kharagpur, founded in 1951. It is located in Kharagpur, West Bengal, and was declared an institute of national importance under the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961. After IIT Kharagpur, other IITs such as IIT Bombay (1958), IIT Kanpur (1959), IIT Delhi (1961), and IIT Madras (1959) were established. This institute has been a pioneer in technical education in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the first IIT in India? → IIT Kharagpur
☛ When was IIT Kharagpur established? → 1951
☛ In which state is IIT Kharagpur located? → West Bengal
☛ Under which act was IIT Kharagpur declared an institute of national importance? → IIT Act, 1961
☛ Which IIT is the oldest? → IIT Kharagpur

q: What is the feature of ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) organisation?
o: It deals with the practical use of space technology such as geodesy, satellite based telecommunications, etc.
It handles testing, assembly and integration of liquid propulsion control packages.
It applies remote sensing technology to manage natural resources.
It is used to launch sounding rockets.
qs.e: ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC), located at Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu, is a key facility of ISRO dedicated to the development and testing of liquid propulsion systems. It handles the testing, assembly and integration of liquid engines and propulsion control packages. This ensures that propulsion components used in launch vehicles and satellites meet high standards. Thus, the feature of IPRC is focused on liquid propulsion activities, not on telecommunications, remote sensing, or sounding rocket launches.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) located? → Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu
☛ What is the main function of IPRC? → Testing, assembly and integration of liquid propulsion control packages
☛ IPRC is a part of which organization? → ISRO
☛ Where are liquid propulsion engines tested? → IPRC, Mahendragiri
☛ What type of propulsion is IPRC related to? → Liquid propulsion

q: Which committee is constituted by the Government if population of a particular area exceeds 3 lakh?
qs.e: Under the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992), the formation of ward committees in municipalities is mandatory. If the population of a particular ward in a municipal corporation or municipality exceeds 3 lakh, a ward committee is constituted for that area. This committee is responsible for planning and monitoring development activities at the local level. The ward committee includes elected councilors from that ward and some nominated members. Its purpose is to ensure prompt resolution of citizens' problems. The committee acts as a bridge between the municipal body and the residents, facilitating grassroots democracy and effective governance.
qs.kf:
☛ 74th Constitutional Amendment relates to → Municipalities
☛ Three categories of Municipalities → Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat
☛ Population threshold for Ward Committee → More than 3 lakh
☛ Main function of Ward Committee → Local development and problem redressal
☛ Year of Municipal Act passed → 1992

q: The 3rd Global Potato Conclave, organised by the Indian Potato Association (IPA) in collaboration with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi and ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh and International Potato Centre (CIP), Lima, Peru, was held in ____ from 28th to 31st January 2021
qs.e: The 3rd Global Potato Conclave was held from 28th to 31st January 2021 in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. It was organised by the Indian Potato Association (IPA) in collaboration with ICAR, New Delhi, ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Shimla, and the International Potato Centre (CIP), Lima, Peru. The conclave aimed to discuss innovations in potato production, processing, and value chains. Gujarat is a major potato-producing state in India, providing a suitable platform for this global event. The gathering brought together farmers, scientists, and industry stakeholders to share knowledge and advancements.
qs.kf:
☛ First Global Potato Conclave → 1998 in New Delhi
☛ Second Global Potato Conclave → 2014 in New Delhi
☛ Indian Potato Association (IPA) founded → 1973
☛ Scientific name of potato → Solanum tuberosum
☛ Largest potato-producing state in India → Uttar Pradesh

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a part of the European Union?
qs.e: The European Union (EU) is a political and economic union of 27 European countries. Its member states include Germany (1957, founding member), Greece (1981), and Hungary (2004). Argentina is located in South America and is not part of the European Union; instead, it is a member of Mercosur. EU member states share a single market, a customs union, and common policies. Non-European countries like Argentina cannot be EU members.

q: In the context of provident fund, UAN stands for:
qs.e: UAN stands for Universal Account Number, issued by EPFO. It is a 12-digit unique number that links all PF accounts of an employee. With UAN, workers can track, withdraw, or transfer their PF online. It provides portability, so changing jobs does not require a new PF account. EPFO has made UAN mandatory to enhance transparency and reduce fraud. This system allows employees to manage their provident fund easily through the digital portal.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of UAN? → Universal Account Number
☛ How many digits in UAN? → 12 digits
☛ Which organization issues UAN? → EPFO
☛ Main benefit of UAN? → Links all PF accounts under one number
☛ Is UAN mandatory? → Yes, by EPFO

q: The securities and exchange board of India was established in_____.
qs.e: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was established in 1992. It is the regulator of the Indian stock market. SEBI was established under the SEBI Act, 1992. Its headquarters is in Mumbai. The main objective of SEBI is to protect the interests of investors and to promote the securities market. Earlier, in 1988, SEBI was created as a non-statutory body, but it got legal status in 1992. The first chairman of SEBI was G.V. Ramakrishna.
qs.kf:
☛ When was SEBI established? → 1992
☛ Where is the headquarters of SEBI? → Mumbai
☛ Who was the first chairman of SEBI? → G.V. Ramakrishna
☛ When was the SEBI Act passed? → 1992
☛ What is the full form of SEBI? → Securities and Exchange Board of India

q: Which organisation is termed as 'a Child of War'?
qs.e: The League of Nations is termed as 'a Child of War' because it was established after the end of World War I. It was the first international organization created to maintain world peace. It was founded in 1920 under the Treaty of Versailles. Its headquarters was in Geneva, Switzerland. However, it failed to prevent World War II and was dissolved in 1946. The United Nations (UNO) was established to replace it. UNESCO and UNICEF are specialized agencies of the United Nations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the League of Nations established? → 1920
☛ Where is the headquarters of the League of Nations? → Geneva
☛ Which organization replaced the League of Nations? → United Nations (UNO)
☛ UNESCO is related to which fields? → Education, Science and Culture
☛ What is the full form of UNICEF? → United Nations Children's Fund

q: Who introduced the concept of biodiversity hotspot?
qs.e: The concept of biodiversity hotspot was introduced by Norman Myers in 1988. It is a strategy to identify areas with high levels of endemic species and severe habitat loss. Initially, Myers identified 10 hotspots, later expanded to 34 by Conservation International. To qualify as a hotspot, a region must meet two criteria: it must contain at least 1,500 species of endemic vascular plants and have lost more than 30% of its original habitat. This concept is crucial in conservation biology as it helps prioritize limited resources for protecting the most threatened ecosystems.
qs.kf:
☛ Proponent of biodiversity hotspot concept → Norman Myers
☛ Total officially recognized hotspots globally → 34
☛ Hotspots located in India → Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sundaland
☛ Year when hotspot concept was first introduced → 1988
☛ Minimum endemic plant species required for hotspot → 1500

q: What is the full form of IRDAI?

Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
Insurance Research And Development Aid of India
Insurance Regulation And Development Aid of India
