q: Which of the following years was declared by the United Nations as the "International Year of Biodiversity"?
qs.e: The United Nations declared 2010 as the 'International Year of Biodiversity'. Its aim was to raise global awareness about the importance of biodiversity and promote conservation efforts. This year marked a significant milestone in achieving the targets of the Convention on Biological Diversity. Several global events and campaigns were organized during this period. Later, 2011-2020 was declared as the International Decade on Biodiversity. The UN initiated this to highlight the indispensable role of biodiversity for ecosystem balance and human well-being. The campaign was led by UNEP and the CBD Secretariat.
qs.kf:
☛ International Year of Biodiversity → 2010
☛ International Decade on Biodiversity → 2011-2020
☛ Headquarters of Convention on Biological Diversity → Montreal, Canada
☛ UNEP full form → United Nations Environment Programme
☛ Biodiversity Day → May 22

q: What is the full form of EDD in banking sector?
qs.e: In the banking sector, the full form of EDD is Enhanced Due Diligence. It is a higher level of customer scrutiny applied to high-risk clients such as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) or those conducting large transactions. Its primary aim is to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. EDD is more thorough than standard due diligence and includes verifying the source of funds, nature of business, and purpose of transactions. It is a crucial part of KYC (Know Your Customer) regulations and is mandatory under guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of EDD? → Enhanced Due Diligence
☛ EDD applies to which customers? → High-risk customers
☛ What is the main purpose of EDD? → Prevent money laundering and terrorist financing
☛ EDD is related to which regulations? → KYC (Know Your Customer) regulations
☛ Which bank issues guidelines for EDD? → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

q: What is the full form of FDI?
qs.e: The full form of FDI is Foreign Direct Investment. It refers to an investment made by a firm or individual in one country into business interests located in another country, with the aim of establishing control or significant influence. FDI is a key driver of economic growth, facilitating capital inflow, job creation, and technology transfer. In India, FDI is regulated by the DIPP (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade). The main types of FDI are greenfield investment (new projects) and brownfield investment (purchase of existing assets).
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of FDI? → Foreign Direct Investment
☛ Who regulates FDI in India? → DIPP
☛ What are the two main types of FDI? → Greenfield and Brownfield
☛ What is the objective of FDI? → Obtaining control or significant influence
☛ Effect of FDI on economy? → Capital inflow, employment, technology transfer

q: Which was the last country to join BRICS?
qs.e: BRICS is an international organization that expanded in 2011 when South Africa joined the group. Previously, the group was known as BRIC (Brazil, Russia, India, China). After South Africa's inclusion, the name changed to BRICS. It is the only member from the African continent. South Africa's accession enhanced the group's global influence and strengthened cooperation among developing nations.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the former name of BRICS? → BRIC
☛ Which country last joined BRICS? → South Africa (2011)
☛ Who are the founding members of BRICS? → Brazil, Russia, India, China
☛ Who coined the term BRICS? → Jim O'Neill (2001)
☛ Where is the headquarters of BRICS? → Shanghai, China

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 3
q: The NK Singh Committee, which was formed in 2016, was associated with which of the following?
o: Reviewing the trade deficit in India
qs.e: The NK Singh Committee was formed in 2016 to review the FRBM Act, 2003. This committee recommended new targets for fiscal deficit and debt management. It emphasized strengthening the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework. Based on its report, the government set rules to keep the fiscal deficit below 3% of GDP and reduce the debt-to-GDP ratio. The committee also recommended the establishment of an autonomous fiscal council. NK Singh is a former Finance Secretary of India and a member of the Planning Commission.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the FRBM Act enacted? → 2003
☛ What is the full form of FRBM? → Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management
☛ What fiscal deficit target did NK Singh Committee suggest? → 3% of GDP
☛ What position did NK Singh hold? → Finance Secretary of India
☛ What is the FRBM Act related to? → Fiscal discipline

q: As of Nov 2020, who is the Secretary General of the United Nations?
qs.e: The Secretary-General of the United Nations is the head of the UN Secretariat. As of November 2020, Antonio Guterres held this position. He is a former Prime Minister of Portugal and assumed office on 1 January 2017. His term is five years and he was reappointed for a second term in 2021. The Secretary-General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council. Promoting global peace, development, and human rights is his primary responsibility.
qs.kf:
☛ Current UN Secretary-General → Antonio Guterres (as of 2024)
☛ Term of Secretary-General → 5 years (renewable)
☛ First Secretary-General → Trygve Lie (Norway)
☛ Who appoints the Secretary-General → General Assembly on Security Council recommendation
☛ Headquarters → New York, USA

q: When was INSAT 1B commissioned?
qs.e: INSAT 1B was India's second national satellite, launched on August 30, 1983, using the American rocket Delta 3910. It was part of the INSAT-1 series, designed for telecommunications, meteorology, and broadcasting services. Although fully operational by 1984, it was commissioned in 1983. INSAT 1B revolutionized satellite communication in India and served until 1990. After the failure of its predecessor INSAT 1A (1982), INSAT 1B strengthened India's space program.
qs.kf:
☛ Launch year of INSAT 1B → 1983
☛ First successful satellite of INSAT-1 series → INSAT 1B
☛ Launch vehicle of INSAT 1B → Delta 3910
☛ Operational period of INSAT 1B → 1983-1990
☛ Year of INSAT 1A failure → 1982

q: Which of the following countries is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council?
qs.e: The United Nations Security Council has five permanent members: USA, UK, France, Russia, and China. These permanent members possess veto power. India, Japan, and Canada are non-permanent members. China has been a permanent member since 1971.
qs.kf:
☛ How many permanent members does UNSC have? → 5
☛ Who has veto power in UNSC? → Permanent members
☛ Where is UNSC headquarters? → New York
☛ How many times has India been a non-permanent member of UNSC? → 8 times
☛ When did China join UNSC? → 1971

q: As of Nov 2020, who is the President of the World Bank?
qs.e: As of November 2020, David R. Malpass is the President of the World Bank. He assumed office in April 2019. The World Bank is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to developing countries. Its headquarters is located in Washington D.C. David Malpass is an American economist and former Treasury official. He is the 13th President of the World Bank. He was nominated by US President Donald Trump. The World Bank Group comprises five institutions: IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID. Its primary goals are poverty eradication and promoting shared prosperity.
qs.kf:
☛ Current President of World Bank (as of 2024) → Ajay Banga
☛ Headquarters of World Bank → Washington D.C., USA
☛ Founding members of World Bank → 44 countries (1944 Bretton Woods Conference)
☛ Primary goal of World Bank → Poverty eradication
☛ Five institutions of World Bank Group → IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID

q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC located?
qs.e: The headquarters of OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is located in Vienna, the capital of Austria. It was founded in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. OPEC's main objectives are to coordinate and unify petroleum policies among member countries, stabilize oil markets, and ensure fair returns for producers. Currently, it has 13 member countries. The headquarters was originally in Geneva but was moved to Vienna in 1965.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of OPEC establishment → 1960
☛ Number of founding members of OPEC → 5
☛ Former headquarters of OPEC → Geneva
☛ Current number of OPEC members → 13
☛ Main objective of OPEC → Stabilize oil markets

q: Which organisation has been the successor of GATT?
qs.e: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) was an international trade agreement signed in 1947 aimed at reducing trade barriers among member countries. After the Uruguay Round negotiations, the WTO (World Trade Organization) was established on January 1, 1995, as the successor to GATT. Unlike GATT, which dealt only with trade in goods, the WTO covers trade in services, intellectual property rights, and dispute resolution. It serves as a permanent organization to regulate global trade rules and settle trade disputes. The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and currently has 164 member countries. It plays a crucial role in facilitating international trade and ensuring a level playing field for all members.
qs.kf:
☛ When was GATT established? → 1947
☛ Where is the WTO headquarters located? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ When was WTO established? → 1 January 1995
☛ How many member countries does WTO have? → 164
☛ What was the last round of GATT called? → Uruguay Round

q: Which of the following organisations deals with formulation and implementation of global trade?
qs.e: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international organization that deals with the formulation and implementation of global trade rules. It was established on 1 January 1995 and its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. The main objectives of the WTO are to reduce trade barriers, resolve disputes, and facilitate smooth trade among member countries. Currently, the WTO has 164 member countries. The IMF deals with financial stability, WHO deals with health, and ILO deals with labor standards.
qs.kf:
☛ When was WTO established? → 1 January 1995
☛ Where is the headquarters of WTO? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ How many member countries does WTO have? → 164
☛ Which was the predecessor of WTO? → GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade)
☛ Which organization resolves global trade disputes? → WTO

q: In 2018, which nuclear reactor did BARC re-commission with double capacity compared to its earlier version?
qs.e: In 2018, Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) re-commissioned India's first nuclear reactor Apsara. Its upgraded version, Apsara-U, had double the capacity of the original. The original Apsara reactor started in 1956 and was shut down in 2010. The new reactor features higher neutron flux and improved safety systems. It is a research reactor used for nuclear science and material testing. This re-commissioning strengthened India's nuclear research capabilities.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first nuclear reactor → Apsara (1956)
☛ Location of Apsara reactor → Trombay, Mumbai
☛ Capacity of Apsara-U → Double the original
☛ Full form of BARC → Bhabha Atomic Research Centre
☛ Type of Apsara reactor → Research reactor

q: Which of the following date is observed as World Clean Up Day?
qs.e: World Clean Up Day is observed annually on September 15. The main goal of this day is to raise awareness about cleanliness and promote waste management. It is supported by the United Nations and was first formally observed in 2018. On this day, volunteers across the globe conduct cleanup drives to reduce litter and pollution.
qs.kf:
☛ When is World Clean Up Day observed? → September 15
☛ What is the purpose of World Clean Up Day? → Waste management and cleanliness awareness
☛ Which organization supports World Clean Up Day? → United Nations
☛ When was the first World Clean Up Day observed? → 2018
☛ What activity is held on World Clean Up Day? → Community cleanup drives

q: WTO is a world organisation. Which of the following statements about WTO is INCORRECT?
o: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria is the organisation's seventh Director-General.
Its top decision-making body is the Ministerial Conference.
Its full form is World Transport Organisation.
It deals with the rules of trade between nations.
qs.e: The full form of WTO is World Trade Organisation, not World Transport Organisation. WTO was established in 1995 following the Uruguay Round negotiations. Its headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. It sets the rules of trade between member nations and helps resolve disputes. The top decision-making body is the Ministerial Conference, which meets every two years. The current Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria, who is the first woman and first African to hold this position.
qs.kf:
☛ When was WTO established? → 1995
☛ Where is WTO headquarters? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ What is the top decision-making body of WTO? → Ministerial Conference
☛ Who is the current Director-General of WTO? → Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria)
☛ What is the full form of WTO? → World Trade Organisation

q: Which of the following statements about the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is INCORRECT?
o: An aim of the Association is to accelerate economic growth, social progress and cultural development in the region.
ASEAN was established on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok.
It comprises a group of ten member states as of 2019.
It started with three original member countries.
qs.e: ASEAN was established on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok through the ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration). The founding members were five countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. Later, Brunei (1984), Vietnam (1995), Laos and Myanmar (1997), and Cambodia (1999) joined, making a total of ten member states. The aim of ASEAN is to accelerate economic growth, social progress, and cultural development in the region. Therefore, the statement that it started with three original member countries is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ ASEAN establishment date → 8 August 1967
☛ Establishment place → Bangkok, Thailand
☛ Founding document → ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration)
☛ Original member count → Five
☛ Current member count → Ten

q: Which of the following is NOT involved in organising the Global Bio India - 2021 event?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
qs.e: Global Bio India - 2021 was a major biotechnology event organized by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Science and Technology, and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC). It aimed to position India as a global leader in biotechnology. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was not involved in organizing this event as it primarily deals with healthcare services, policy-making, and disease control, rather than industry-focused biotechnology events. The event focused on promoting innovation, startups, and collaboration in the biotechnology sector.
qs.kf:
☛ Who organized Global Bio India 2021? → Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology, and BIRAC
☛ What was the aim of Global Bio India 2021? → To make India a global leader in biotechnology
☛ What does BIRAC stand for? → Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council
☛ Under which ministry does the Department of Biotechnology come? → Ministry of Science and Technology
☛ What is the main function of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare? → Managing healthcare services, policy-making, and disease control

q: The words like chishti, suhrawardi and pyadasi are related to which of the following religions?
qs.e: The terms Chishti, Suhrawardi, and Pyadasi are all associated with the Sufi tradition, which is the mystical dimension of Islam. Chishti and Suhrawardi are names of major Sufi orders (silsilas), while Pyadasi refers to a 'foot traveler' or a wandering ascetic common in Sufi practice. Sufism emphasizes inner purity, devotion, and direct experience of God. Other options such as Nathpati relate to Hindu yogic traditions, Vaishnav refers to a Hindu sect, and Islam as a whole is too broad; these terms are specifically linked to the Sufi path within Islam.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Chishti order? → Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti
☛ Who founded the Suhrawardi order? → Sheikh Shihabuddin Suhrawardi
☛ Famous Chishti saint in India? → Nizamuddin Auliya
☛ What does Sufi mean? → One who wears wool (symbol of purity)
☛ What is popular Sufi musical style? → Qawwali

q: When and where was SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) formed?
qs.e: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was established on December 8, 1985 in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The founding members are India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, and the Maldives. Later, Afghanistan joined in 2007. The headquarters of SAARC is located in Kathmandu, Nepal. The organization aims to promote economic, social, and cultural cooperation among South Asian countries. The first summit was also held in Dhaka.
qs.kf:
☛ SAARC establishment date → December 8, 1985
☛ SAARC headquarters → Kathmandu, Nepal
☛ Founding members of SAARC → 7 countries (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives)
☛ Later joined member → Afghanistan (2007)
☛ SAARC emblem → Seven clasped hands with lotus flowers

q: The Defence Research and Development Organisation’s headquarters is located in ______.
qs.e: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is a premier agency under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, responsible for developing advanced defence technologies. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. Established in 1958, DRDO operates more than 50 laboratories across the country, focusing on areas such as missiles, avionics, naval systems, and land combat. Key achievements include the development of Agni, Prithvi, and BrahMos missiles. The current chairman of DRDO is Samir Kamat. The organisation plays a crucial role in enhancing India's military capabilities through indigenous research and development.
qs.kf:
☛ When was DRDO established? → 1958
☛ Who is the current chairman of DRDO? → Samir Kamat
☛ How many laboratories does DRDO have? → More than 50
☛ Major missile developed by DRDO? → Agni, Prithvi, BrahMos
☛ DRDO is under which ministry? → Ministry of Defence

q: How many cities were selected in 2016 first batch to be develop as smart cities of India?
qs.e: The Government of India launched the Smart City Mission in 2015 with the aim of making urban areas smart through infrastructure, technology, and sustainable development. Under this mission, the first batch of 20 cities was selected and announced in January 2016. These cities were chosen from across the country, including Bhubaneswar, Pune, Jaipur, Surat, Kochi, Ahmedabad, Indore, and others. The selection process was competitive, evaluating proposals submitted by municipal corporations. The mission aims to develop these cities over a period of five years. The first batch set the foundation for the subsequent selection of more cities, with a total of 100 cities planned under the mission.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Smart City Mission launched? → 2015
☛ How many cities were selected in the first batch? → 20
☛ Which city was the first selected in the first batch? → Bhubaneswar
☛ How many cities are to be developed under the Smart City Mission? → 100
☛ Which ministry oversees the Smart City Mission? → Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

q: INTERPOL has its headquarters in ______
qs.e: INTERPOL stands for the International Criminal Police Organization. Its headquarters is located in Lyon, France. The organization was established in 1923 in Vienna, Austria, but later moved to Lyon. It aims to facilitate international police cooperation and control transnational crimes. With 195 member countries, it is the world's largest international police organization. The headquarters in Lyon houses the General Secretariat, which coordinates operations across the globe. INTERPOL does not have its own law enforcement agents but provides a platform for countries to share information and work together.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of INTERPOL → International Criminal Police Organization
☛ Headquarters of INTERPOL → Lyon, France
☛ Establishment year of INTERPOL → 1923
☛ Members of INTERPOL → 195 countries
☛ Objective of INTERPOL → International police cooperation

q: Which Indian organisation has the motto 'Strength's origin is in Science'?
qs.e: DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) is India's premier defence research organisation, with the motto 'Strength's origin is in Science'. It was established in 1958 and its headquarters is located in New Delhi. DRDO aims to develop cutting-edge defence technologies and weapons systems for the Indian armed forces. It plays a leading role in the research and development of various missiles, radars, electronic warfare systems, and other defence equipment. DRDO has developed missile systems like Agni, Prithvi, and BrahMos.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of DRDO → Defence Research and Development Organisation
☛ Establishment year of DRDO → 1958
☛ Headquarters of DRDO → New Delhi
☛ Missiles developed by DRDO → Agni, Prithvi, BrahMos
☛ Motto of DRDO → Strength's origin is in Science

q: The dissolution of the Soviet Union began in which of the following years?
qs.e: The dissolution of the Soviet Union formally began in 1991. The process accelerated after the failed August Coup in 1991, which weakened the authority of reformist President Mikhail Gorbachev. Multiple republics declared independence, and on 8 December 1991, Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus signed the Belavezha Accords, declaring the Soviet Union dissolved and establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). The Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union officially dissolved itself on 26 December 1991, marking the end of the Cold War era. Key events of 1991, including the coup and subsequent declarations, led to the disintegration of one of the world's two superpowers.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Berlin Wall fall? → 1989
☛ Who was the President of the Soviet Union? → Mikhail Gorbachev
☛ Full form of CIS? → Commonwealth of Independent States
☛ Official dissolution date of Soviet Union? → 26 December 1991
☛ Reforms introduced by Gorbachev? → Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring)

q: Where is the headquarters of 'Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority' (PFRDA)?
qs.e: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is a statutory body of the Government of India responsible for the regulation and development of pension funds. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. PFRDA was established as a regulator in 2003 and later given statutory status by an Act of Parliament in 2013. It regulates the National Pension System (NPS) and facilitates pension services for all citizens and employees. PFRDA plays a key role in pension reforms and ensuring investor protection in the financial services sector.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of PFRDA → New Delhi
☛ Year of establishment of PFRDA → 2003
☛ Year of statutory status for PFRDA → 2013
☛ System regulated by PFRDA → National Pension System (NPS)
☛ Full form of PFRDA → Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Who specifically paints the Pithora artworks?
qs.e: Pithora artworks are mainly created by the tribal communities of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, especially the Bhil and Rathwa tribes. The artists who paint these artworks are called Lakhara. This traditional wall painting includes images of horses, elephants, and deities. The Lakhara art is passed down through generations and is part of religious rituals.
qs.kf:
☛ Which tribe is associated with Pithora painting? → Bhil and Rathwa
☛ Which colors are mainly used in Pithora painting? → Red, yellow, green, blue
☛ On which occasion is Pithora painting made? → Weddings and festivals
☛ Which animal is most commonly depicted in Pithora painting? → Horse
☛ Which state's folk art is Pithora painting? → Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh

q: Which organization takes care of Sick or failing industries in India?
o: The Board of Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
qs.e: In India, the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) is the statutory body that takes care of sick or failing industries. It was established in 1987 under the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 (SICA). The primary objective of BIFR is to detect sick industrial companies, suggest measures for their revival, and if revival is not possible, recommend their closure. BIFR examines the financial health of companies and prepares revival schemes. While the Reserve Bank of India handles monetary policy and IDBI provides industrial finance, and HDFC focuses on housing finance, BIFR specifically deals with the reconstruction of sick units. Thus, BIFR is the key institution for managing failing industries in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of BIFR → Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
☛ Under which Act was BIFR established? → SICA, 1985
☛ Headquarters of BIFR → New Delhi
☛ Criterion for a sick company → Accumulated losses exceeding net worth
☛ Full form of SICA → Sick Industrial Companies Act

q: The Microsoft Corporation was founded at ____________ in 1975.
qs.e: The Microsoft Corporation was founded on April 4, 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States. Initially, the company developed a BASIC interpreter for the Altair 8800 microcomputer. Microsoft later moved its headquarters to Redmond, Washington in 1986. Cupertino, California is the headquarters of Apple; Nihonbashi, Tokyo is a Japanese business district; and Bellevue, Washington is home to companies like Amazon. Thus, the correct answer is Albuquerque, New Mexico.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year did Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft? → 1975
☛ Where is Microsoft's current headquarters located? → Redmond, Washington, United States
☛ What was the first operating system developed by Microsoft? → MS-DOS (1981)
☛ What is Microsoft's most popular operating system? → Windows
☛ When did Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen pass away? → October 15, 2018

q: The headquarters of which of the following international organisation is situated at Washington DC?
o: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)
qs.e: The headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is located in Washington DC, United States. The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference to promote global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and provide economic assistance to member countries. Other options: ECB headquarters is in Frankfurt, Germany; OECD is in Paris, France; and ILO is in Geneva, Switzerland. Therefore, only the IMF has its headquarters in Washington DC.
qs.kf:
☛ IMF headquarters → Washington DC, USA
☛ ECB headquarters → Frankfurt, Germany
☛ OECD headquarters → Paris, France
☛ ILO headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ IMF establishment → 1944, Bretton Woods Conference

q: Which among the following organisations is the best example of an agreement between oligopolists?
qs.e: In an oligopoly market, a few large producers can agree to control prices and output. OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is the best example of such an agreement, as it is a cartel of oil-producing countries that coordinates oil production to influence prices. UNESCO deals with education and culture, WHO with health, and UNO with international peace. These are intergovernmental organizations but not examples of oligopolistic agreements. OPEC members limit oil production to affect prices, which is a characteristic of oligopoly collusion.
qs.kf:
☛ Characteristic of oligopoly market → Few large firms, product differentiation, entry barriers
☛ OPEC founding year → 1960
☛ OPEC headquarters → Vienna, Austria
☛ Meaning of cartel → Formal agreement among producers
☛ Number of OPEC member countries (2023) → 13

q: It is the oldest trade union organisation in India.
qs.e: The oldest trade union in India is the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), founded on October 31, 1920. Its formation was led by prominent leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. AITUC was affiliated with the Indian National Congress and is now supported by the CPI (Communist Party of India). Other major unions include INTUC (1947), BMS (1955), and CITU (1970), all of which were established later.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest trade union in India → AITUC
☛ AITUC founded in year → 1920
☛ Political party affiliated with AITUC → CPI
☛ INTUC founded in year → 1947
☛ Political party affiliated with BMS → BJP / RSS

q: Which of the following is NOT a correct pair of a UN organ and its headquarters?
o: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) - Paris
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) - The Hague
qs.e: Among the given options, the WHO headquarters is not in New York. The WHO headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. The other pairs are correct: UNESCO headquarters is in Paris, ICJ headquarters is in The Hague, and IAEA headquarters is in Vienna. WHO is a specialized agency of the United Nations concerned with international public health. It was established in 1948. Thus, the correct pair is WHO - Geneva, not New York.
qs.kf:
☛ WHO headquarters → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ United Nations headquarters → New York, USA
☛ UNESCO headquarters → Paris, France
☛ ICJ headquarters → The Hague, Netherlands
☛ IAEA headquarters → Vienna, Austria

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scheme of Jan Shikshan Sansthan of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)?
o: It focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in the districts through skilling/upskilling
It focuses on creation of a pool of master trainers
It is implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)
It focuses to improve the occupational skills and technical knowledge of the non/neo literates and persons having rudimentary level of education
qs.e: The Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) aims to provide vocational skills to non-literates, neo-literates, and persons with rudimentary education. It also focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in districts. The scheme is implemented through Jan Shikshan Sansthans, not through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). ITIs are separate institutions for industrial training. Hence, this statement is incorrect. While the scheme also aims to create a pool of master trainers, its implementation is not via ITIs.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry oversees Jan Shikshan Sansthan? → Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)
☛ What is the main objective of JSS? → Provide vocational skills to non/neo literates
☛ How is JSS implemented? → Through Jan Shikshan Sansthans, not ITIs
☛ What does JSS focus on? → Identifying and promoting traditional skills
☛ Who are the beneficiaries of JSS? → Non-literates, neo-literates, and persons with basic education

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)?
qs.e: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is a regional organization comprising 10 countries in Southeast Asia. Its founding members are Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. Later, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia joined. India is not a member of ASEAN, but it participates in ASEAN+3 (China, Japan, South Korea) and the East Asia Summit (EAS). India has a trade and strategic partnership with ASEAN but is not a full member of the organization.
qs.kf:
☛ When was ASEAN established? → 8 August 1967
☛ Where is the ASEAN Secretariat located? → Jakarta, Indonesia
☛ How many member countries does ASEAN have? → 10
☛ Which countries are part of ASEAN+3? → China, Japan, South Korea
☛ What is India to ASEAN? → Dialogue Partner

q: Name the person who had a major influence in the field of Algebra in India.
qs.e: The ancient Indian mathematician Aryabhata (476-550 CE) made seminal contributions to algebra. His work Aryabhatiya contains algebraic formulas, solutions to quadratic equations, and arithmetic progressions. Aryabhata also played a key role in developing the concept of zero and the decimal system. He was the first to calculate pi (π) accurately to 3.1416. While Brahmagupta also contributed to algebra, Aryabhata's influence is more foundational. Varahamihira was an astronomer, and Charaka an Ayurvedic physician. Aryabhata is often called the father of algebra in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the famous book of Aryabhata? → Aryabhatiya
☛ What value of pi did Aryabhata give? → 3.1416
☛ To which period did Aryabhata belong? → Gupta period
☛ Who is called the father of algebra in India? → Aryabhata
☛ Who introduced the concept of zero? → Aryabhata

q: Who among the following was the founder of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)?
qs.e: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was founded by Vikram Sarabhai in 1969. He is regarded as the father of the Indian space program. In 1962, he established the Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR), which later evolved into ISRO. Sarabhai emphasized the use of space technology for national development. Satish Dhawan was the third chairman of ISRO. Homi J. Bhabha was the father of the Indian nuclear program. APJ Abdul Kalam contributed to ISRO but was not the founder.
qs.kf:
☛ When was ISRO established? → 1969
☛ When was INCOSPAR renamed to ISRO? → 1969
☛ Birthplace of Vikram Sarabhai? → Ahmedabad, Gujarat
☛ Headquarters of ISRO? → Bengaluru, Karnataka
☛ Where is Satish Dhawan Space Centre located? → Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh

q: Which ministry in the Indian Government launched Mission Sudarshan Chakra in 2025?
qs.e: Mission Sudarshan Chakra was launched in 2025 by the Ministry of Defence of the Indian Government. The mission aims to strengthen cyber security capabilities and ensure national security against digital threats. It will be operated by the Defence Cyber Agency (DCA) under the Ministry of Defence. The focus is on protecting critical information infrastructure and countering cyber attacks. This is a significant step for India's national security.
qs.kf:
☛ Which ministry launched Mission Sudarshan Chakra? → Ministry of Defence
☛ What is the objective of Mission Sudarshan Chakra? → Strengthen cyber security
☛ In which year was Mission Sudarshan Chakra launched? → 2025
☛ Which agency operates Mission Sudarshan Chakra? → Defence Cyber Agency (DCA)
☛ Mission Sudarshan Chakra is related to which field? → Cyber security

q: India adopted the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in which year?
qs.e: The United Nations adopted the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in September 2015, setting a 15-year agenda from 2016 to 2030. India, as a member state, adopted these 17 goals and 169 targets in the same year. The SDGs succeeded the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), which were in place from 2000 to 2015. India has since aligned its national policies and programs with the SDGs, aiming for progress in areas like poverty eradication, education, health, climate action, and equality. The NITI Aayog serves as the nodal agency for SDG implementation in India. The adoption of SDGs marked a global commitment to sustainable development, balancing economic, social, and environmental dimensions.
qs.kf:
☛ How many goals are there in SDG? → 17 goals and 169 targets
☛ What is the time period for SDG? → 2016 to 2030
☛ Which goals did SDG replace? → Millennium Development Goals (MDGs)
☛ Who is the nodal agency for SDG in India? → NITI Aayog
☛ Where was the SDG summit held? → United Nations Headquarters, New York

q: In which year did India sign the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement and become a founding member of WTO?
qs.e: India signed the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement and became a founding member in 1995. The WTO was established on January 1, 1995, as the successor to the GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade), which was formed in 1948. The WTO aims to regulate international trade and provide a rules-based trading system. India has been a founding member of the WTO and is a party to all its agreements. The WTO headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. Currently, the WTO has 164 members. India participates in the WTO as a developing country and actively protects its trade interests in negotiations.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was WTO established? → 1995
☛ Where is the WTO headquarters located? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ In which year was GATT established? → 1948
☛ Current number of WTO members? → 164
☛ India's membership category in WTO? → Developing country

q: In which year did India officially join the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) as a full member?
qs.e: India officially became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) on June 9, 2017. This decision was taken at the Astana Summit, where both India and Pakistan were granted membership. The SCO was founded in 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. The organization focuses on security, economic cooperation, and anti-terrorism measures. India was initially an observer member (2005) before becoming a full member. The SCO headquarters is located in Beijing. Currently, the SCO has 9 member states.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of SCO located? → Beijing
☛ When was SCO founded? → 2001
☛ How many founding members does SCO have? → 6
☛ When did India become an observer member of SCO? → 2005
☛ How many current members does SCO have? → 9

q: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2025, which pollutant was identified as the primary cause of increased respiratory illnesses due to air pollution?
qs.e: According to the WHO's 2025 data, PM2.5 is the primary cause of respiratory illnesses due to air pollution. These fine particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, leading to diseases such as asthma, bronchitis, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Major sources include vehicle emissions, industrial activities, and combustion of fossil fuels. The WHO has issued strict guidelines to reduce PM2.5 levels globally due to its severe health impacts.
qs.kf:
☛ PM2.5 stands for → Particulate Matter 2.5
☛ Diameter of PM2.5 particles → 2.5 micrometers or less
☛ Major source of PM2.5 → Vehicle emissions and industrial smoke
☛ Disease caused by PM2.5 → Asthma, bronchitis, COPD
☛ WHO safe level for PM2.5 → 24-hour average of 15 µg/m³

q: Who among the following was a prominent disciple of Ramanuja’s Sri Vaishnava tradition who played a significant role in spreading its Bhakti teachings to North India?
qs.e: Ramananda was a prominent disciple of Ramanuja's Sri Vaishnava tradition who played a key role in spreading Bhakti teachings to North India. He established his center in Varanasi (Kashi) and made the path of devotion accessible to all castes. His disciples included notable saints like Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna, Sain, and Pipa. Ramananda emphasized devotion to Lord Rama as the supreme deity. His efforts significantly influenced the Bhakti movement in North India, promoting equality and love for God beyond social barriers. He is considered a bridge between the southern and northern Bhakti traditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was Ramananda's guru? → He is considered a disciple of Raghavananda, who was a follower of Ramanuja's tradition.
☛ Which deity is central in Ramananda's devotion? → Lord Rama (an incarnation of Vishnu).
☛ Where did Ramananda primarily preach? → Varanasi (Kashi).
☛ Who are famous disciples of Ramananda? → Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna, Sain, Pipa, etc.
☛ Which tradition does Ramananda belong to? → Sri Vaishnava tradition (Ramanuja's sampradaya).

q: Which of the following reports of the Brundtland Commission (1987) defined the concept of sustainable development?
qs.e: The Brundtland Commission was established in 1983, chaired by Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland. In 1987, the commission published the report 'Our Common Future', which defined sustainable development as 'development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.' This report emphasized the three pillars of sustainable development: economic, social, and environmental. It became a landmark for global policies. Other options like Silent Spring (1962 by Rachel Carson), Limits to Growth (1972 by the Club of Rome), and Agenda 21 (1992 from the Earth Summit) are related to sustainability but not by the Brundtland Commission.
qs.kf:
☛ Who chaired the Brundtland Commission? → Gro Harlem Brundtland
☛ What is the publication year of the Brundtland Report? → 1987
☛ Which report defined sustainable development? → Our Common Future
☛ What are the three pillars of sustainable development? → Economic, Social, Environmental
☛ Who wrote 'Silent Spring'? → Rachel Carson

q: Trans-Siberian Railway connects St. Petersburg to ________.
qs.e: The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world, connecting Moscow to Vladivostok. It spans approximately 9,289 km, linking the European part of Russia to the Pacific Ocean coast. Although the question mentions St. Petersburg, the main line runs from Moscow to Vladivostok. This railway traverses the Siberia region of Russia and holds immense economic and strategic importance. The other options - Kaliningrad, Volgograd, and Sochi - are located in western Russia and are not directly connected by this line.
qs.kf:
☛ Length of Trans-Siberian Railway → Approximately 9,289 km
☛ Cities connected by this railway → Moscow and Vladivostok
☛ Ocean it reaches → Pacific Ocean
☛ Construction started in → 1891
☛ Country where it is located → Russia

q: Which among the following is the name of the currency of Poland?
qs.e: The currency of Poland is the Zloty, denoted by the code PLN. It has been in circulation since 1924 and is subdivided into grosz (1 zloty = 100 groszy). Poland is a member of the European Union but has not yet adopted the Euro. The other options are incorrect: Kina is the currency of Papua New Guinea, Dinar is used in several countries (e.g., Iran, Jordan), and Balboa is the currency of Panama.
qs.kf:
☛ Currency of Poland → Zloty (PLN)
☛ Capital of Poland → Warsaw
☛ Official language of Poland → Polish
☛ Largest city of Poland → Warsaw
☛ Poland joined EU → 2004

q: What is the currency of Malaysia?
qs.e: The official currency of Malaysia is the Malaysian Ringgit (MYR), symbolized as RM. It is subdivided into 100 sen. The central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, issues and controls the ringgit. The ringgit is also used in trade across several Southeast Asian countries. The other options are incorrect because Malaysia does not use the dinar, dollar, or euro; the dollar is primarily used in the US and Canada, the dinar in Arab countries, and the euro in the European Union.
qs.kf:
☛ Currency of Malaysia → Malaysian Ringgit (MYR)
☛ Symbol of Ringgit → RM
☛ Central Bank of Malaysia → Bank Negara Malaysia
☛ Subdivision of Ringgit → 1 Ringgit = 100 sen
☛ Capital of Malaysia → Kuala Lumpur

q: What is the currency name of Brazil?
qs.e: Brazil is the largest country in South America, and its official currency is the Brazilian real. It was introduced in 1994 to replace the old currency, the cruzeiro. The symbol for the real is R$, and its ISO code is BRL. One real is subdivided into 100 centavos. The currency is issued by Brazil's central bank, the Banco Central do Brasil. Other options like ringgit (Malaysia), rand (South Africa), and peso (several Latin American countries) are incorrect. The name "real" comes from the Portuguese word for "royal."
qs.kf:
☛ What is the currency of Brazil? → Brazilian real
☛ What is the ISO code of Brazilian real? → BRL
☛ Which is the central bank of Brazil? → Banco Central do Brasil
☛ How many centavos are in one real? → 100
☛ In which year was the real introduced? → 1994

q: What is the currency name of Switzerland?
qs.e: The official currency of Switzerland is the Swiss Franc (CHF), a symbol of the country's stable economy. It is issued and controlled by the Swiss National Bank (SNB). The Swiss Franc is often regarded as a safe-haven currency, especially during times of global economic uncertainty. This currency is not only used in Switzerland but also in the neighboring principality of Liechtenstein. The Swiss Franc is subdivided into 100 Rappen (German) or 100 Centimes (French). Banknotes are available in various denominations, and coins are minted in different values.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the currency of Switzerland? → Swiss Franc (CHF)
☛ Which bank issues the Swiss Franc? → Swiss National Bank
☛ What is the subunit of the Swiss Franc? → Rappen or Centimes
☛ Which currency is considered a safe-haven currency globally? → Swiss Franc
☛ Besides Switzerland, where is the Swiss Franc used? → Liechtenstein

q: In which year was the Eiffel Tower built, to celebrate the 100-year anniversary of the French Revolution?
qs.e: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution. It was constructed between 1887 and 1889 and opened to the public on March 31, 1889. The tower was designed by the company of Gustave Eiffel and served as the centerpiece of the 1889 Paris World's Fair. It stands 300 meters tall and was the tallest structure in the world at that time. Originally intended as a temporary structure, it was later preserved as a major tourist attraction.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the French Revolution occur? → 1789
☛ What is the height of the Eiffel Tower? → 300 meters
☛ Who designed the Eiffel Tower? → Gustave Eiffel
☛ In which city is the Eiffel Tower located? → Paris
☛ For which event was the Eiffel Tower built? → 1889 World's Fair

q: Indian currency notes are printed in which place?
A. New Delhi
B. Bombay
C. Nashik
D. Agra
qs.e: In India, currency notes are issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), but their printing is done by government-owned companies: Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited (BRBNMPL) and Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited (SPMCIL). The major printing presses are located in Nashik (Maharashtra), Dewas (Madhya Pradesh), Salboni (West Bengal), and Mysuru (Karnataka). The India Security Press in Nashik, under SPMCIL, is the oldest and most prominent note-printing facility. Other options like New Delhi, Bombay, and Agra do not have any currency printing press.
qs.kf:

☛ Main agencies for note printing → SPMCIL and BRBNMPL
☛ Press located in Dewas → Bank Note Press, Dewas
☛ Salboni press is in which state → West Bengal
☛ Mysuru press belongs to → BRBNMPL

q: 'Euro' is the currency of
A. UK
B. Sweden
C. Euro Zone
D. Denmark
qs.e: The Euro (€) is the official currency of the European Union (EU), but not all EU members use it. The Euro is used by the Euro Zone, which consists of those EU member states that have adopted the euro as their national currency. Currently, 20 EU countries are part of the Euro Zone. The UK (UK) never adopted the euro and left the EU after Brexit. Sweden rejected the euro in a referendum, while Denmark has an opt-out from adopting it.
qs.kf:

☛ Number of Euro Zone members (2024) → 20

q: Who is credited for manufacturing and marketing jeans?
A. Levi Strauss B. Arthur Wellesley C. Mary Phelps D. Lyman Blake
qs.e: Levi Strauss was a German-American businessman who, along with Jacob Davis, started manufacturing and marketing blue jeans in 1873. They patented the use of metal rivets on the corners of trousers to make them stronger. Levi Strauss & Co. was founded in 1853 and remains a global leader in denimwear. Jeans were originally designed for miners and laborers but later became a fashion staple. Strauss's innovation revolutionized workwear and casual fashion.
qs.kf:
☛ Inventor of jeans → Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis
☛ Patent year for riveted trousers → 1873
☛ Founding year of Levi Strauss & Co. → 1853
☛ Original purpose of jeans → Durable trousers for miners and laborers
☛ Nationality of Levi Strauss → German-American

q: Who made the first chocolate bar?
A. Nestle
B. The Harshey Company
C. Joseph Fry & Sons.
D. Pearson's
qs.e: The first chocolate bar was made in 1847 by Joseph Fry & Sons. They mixed cocoa butter, cocoa powder, and sugar to form a solid bar. Before this, chocolate was only consumed as a drink. Joseph Fry & Sons was a major British chocolate company that revolutionized the chocolate industry. Later, in 1875, Daniel Peter created the milk chocolate bar. Hershey Company and Nestle came later. Pearson's was also a chocolate manufacturer, but the first chocolate bar was made by Joseph Fry & Sons.
qs.kf:
☛ Who made the first chocolate bar? → Joseph Fry & Sons
☛ When was the first chocolate bar made? → 1847
☛ Who made the first milk chocolate bar? → Daniel Peter (1875)
☛ What was the first chocolate bar made of? → Cocoa butter, cocoa powder, sugar
☛ How was chocolate consumed before the chocolate bar? → As a drink

q: Kwality Ltd, a processor of dairy products in India has plants in which of these states of India?
qs.e: Kwality Ltd is a prominent dairy product processing company in India, known for processing milk, curd, paneer, and other dairy items. Its main production units are located in the state of Haryana, specifically in Gurugram (formerly Gurgaon) and Manesar. These plants are recognized for producing high-quality dairy products. Kwality Ltd holds a significant position in the Indian dairy industry, and its products are available nationwide. Being situated in Haryana provides the company advantages in terms of raw milk supply and market access, contributing to its operational efficiency and growth.

☛ Year of establishment of Kwality Ltd → 1992

☛ Role of Kwality Ltd in dairy industry → Leading supplier of processed milk and dairy products

q: Who has recently been appointed as the Chief of New Development Bank of BRICS country, has also served as the chairman of Infosys Ltd., and was non-Executive chairman of ICICI Bank in the past?
A. K.V. Kamath

His appointment is significant for India and the global financial sector.

☛ First president of NDB → Kundapur Vaidyanath Kamath (India)

q: The Rupee sign ‘₹’ was adopted by Government of India in the year
qs.e: The Indian Rupee sign '₹' was adopted by the Government of India on July 15, 2010. It was designed by Dr. Uday Kumar, a student at IIT Guwahati. The sign is a combination of the Devanagari letter 'र' and the Roman letter 'R'. It was chosen as the national currency symbol through a public competition. Prior to its adoption, the rupee was denoted by 'Rs' or 'Re'. The adoption of this symbol gave the Indian rupee a distinct identity, similar to other major currencies like the US dollar ($) and the euro (€). The symbol is used on currency notes, coins, and in financial transactions. It represents India's economic strength and cultural heritage.
qs.kf:
☛ Designer of Rupee sign → Dr. Uday Kumar
☛ Date of adoption → July 15, 2010
☛ Basis of Rupee sign → Devanagari 'र' and Roman 'R'
☛ Unicode of Rupee sign → U+20B9
☛ First use on currency → 2011

q: After 9/11 tragedy, the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in New York is called
A. New World Trade Center
B. Empire State Building
C. One World Trade Center
D. World Trade Complex
qs.e: The World Trade Center Twin Towers were destroyed in the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001. The rebuilt complex is called One World Trade Center (also known as Freedom Tower). It stands 1,776 feet tall, symbolizing the year of American independence, 1776. The construction was completed in 2014, and it is the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere.
qs.kf:

☛ Inauguration of One World Trade Center → 2014
☛ One World Trade Center is also known as → Freedom Tower
☛ Buildings destroyed in 9/11 attack → Twin Towers
☛ Architect of One World Trade Center → David Childs

q: _______ built the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel at Mumbai by integrating Indian and European styles.
qs.e: The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, located in Mumbai, is a historic five-star hotel. It was built by Jamsetji Tata, the pioneer of Indian industry and founder of the Tata Group. The hotel opened on 16th December 1903. It uniquely blends Indian and European architectural styles. Jamsetji Tata envisioned this hotel as a prestigious establishment for Indians. Today, the hotel stands as a symbol of India's cultural heritage and is one of the country's most iconic hotels.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel? → Jamsetji Tata
☛ When was the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel opened? → 16th December 1903

☛ Who is the founder of the Tata Group? → Jamsetji Tata
☛ Which hotel integrates Indian and European architectural styles? → Taj Mahal Palace Hotel

q: With which Chinese technology company has the Trump Administration banned the US government agencies from doing business?
qs.e: The Trump Administration banned US government agencies from doing business with Huawei, citing national security concerns. Huawei is China's largest telecommunications equipment company and a leader in 5G technology. The US alleged that Huawei could conduct espionage for the Chinese government, though Huawei denied these claims. Under the ban, US agencies cannot purchase Huawei equipment or services. This move was part of the broader US-China technology rivalry. Huawei was added to the Entity List, restricting its access to US technology. The ban significantly impacted Huawei's global business but also spurred its push for self-reliance in chips and software.

☛ Who is the founder of Huawei? → Ren Zhengfei
☛ Where is Huawei headquartered? → Shenzhen, China

☛ Who are Huawei's main competitors? → Ericsson, Nokia

q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA) was introduced in the year _______.
qs.e: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA) was passed by the Indian Parliament in the year 2003. It was enacted to impose fiscal discipline on the government by setting targets to reduce fiscal deficit and revenue deficit. Under this act, the government is required to present annual financial statements and medium-term fiscal policy statements in the Parliament. The primary objective of FRBMA is to ensure fiscal stability and transparent management of public finances in the country. Although the act came into effect in 2004, it was passed in 2003. The act was amended in 2018 to allow more flexibility in meeting fiscal targets under certain conditions.
qs.kf:
☛ When was FRBMA passed? → 2003
☛ When did FRBMA come into effect? → 2004
☛ Main objective of FRBMA? → Fiscal discipline
☛ What statements are presented under FRBMA? → Annual financial statement and medium-term fiscal policy statement
☛ In which year was FRBMA amended? → 2018 (amendment)

q: Name of the region where "The Great Depression of 1929" started.
qs.e: The Great Depression of 1929 originated in North America, specifically in the United States of America. It began with the stock market crash on Black Tuesday, October 29, 1929, on Wall Street. This economic depression lasted through the 1930s and affected the entire world. Unemployment soared, many banks failed, and industrial production declined sharply. To combat the depression, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt implemented the New Deal policies, which aimed at relief, recovery, and reform.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Great Depression start? → 1929
☛ What was Black Tuesday? → October 29, 1929 stock market crash
☛ Who was US President during the Great Depression? → Herbert Hoover (1929-33), then Franklin Roosevelt
☛ Who started the New Deal? → Franklin D. Roosevelt
☛ What was the global impact of the Great Depression? → Worldwide economic downturn

q: In which year was the first radio programme broadcast in India?
qs.e: The first radio broadcast in India took place in 1923 in Bombay (now Mumbai). It was initiated by the Radio Club of Bombay, which operated a temporary studio from the then Presidency Magazine. Following this, the Indian Broadcasting Company (IBC) was formed in 1927, which was later taken over by the government. In 1936, All India Radio (AIR) was established, which continues to provide broadcasting services. This first broadcast is considered a milestone in Indian radio history. Thus, 1923 is the year of the first radio programme in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first radio broadcast in India? → 1923
☛ From which city was the first broadcast? → Bombay (Mumbai)
☛ Which body conducted the first broadcast? → Radio Club of Bombay
☛ When was All India Radio (AIR) established? → 1936
☛ When was Indian Broadcasting Company (IBC) formed? → 1927

q: In the year ________ the Suez Canal was opened and this further strengthened Bombay's link with the world economy.
qs.e: The Suez Canal was opened in the year 1869. This canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, significantly shortening the sea route between Europe and Asia. Its opening made the port of Bombay (now Mumbai) even more important, as it revolutionized the transport of goods from India to Europe. This strengthened Bombay's link with the world economy. The canal was built under the leadership of French engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps. Located in Egypt, the Suez Canal remains a vital artery for global trade even today.
qs.kf:
☛ In which year was the Suez Canal opened? → 1869
☛ Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect? → Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea
☛ Who was the main engineer behind the Suez Canal? → Ferdinand de Lesseps
☛ In which country is the Suez Canal located? → Egypt
☛ Which Indian port benefited from the opening of the Suez Canal? → Bombay (Mumbai)

q: Kuna is the currency of which one of the following countries?
qs.e: Kuna (HRK) was the official currency of Croatia from 1994 until 2023, when it was replaced by the Euro. The word "kuna" means "marten" in Croatian, referencing the historical use of marten pelts as currency. Among the options, Kenya uses the Kenyan shilling, United Arab Emirates uses the dirham, and Sudan uses the Sudanese pound. Croatia adopted the Euro on January 1, 2023, making the Kuna obsolete. The currency was subdivided into 100 lipa.

☛ ISO code of Kuna → HRK
☛ Current currency of Croatia (since 2023) → Euro
☛ Subunit of Kuna → Lipa
☛ Capital of Croatia → Zagreb

q: India's first biofuel-powered flight landed at IGI Airport in New Delhi from ______ in 2018.
qs.e: India's first biofuel-powered flight landed at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport in New Delhi from Dehradun on August 26, 2018. The flight was operated by SpiceJet Airlines using a Bombardier Q400 aircraft. The biofuel was derived from jatropha seeds and supplied by Indian Oil Corporation (IOC). This flight marked a significant step towards sustainable aviation fuel usage in India.

☛ What was the departure point of the biofuel flight? → Dehradun

☛ Which airline operated the flight? → SpiceJet

q: In which year was the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), better known as the World Bank, established to help Europe recover from the devastation of World War II?
qs.e: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference held in New Hampshire, USA. Its primary purpose was to help rebuild Europe after the devastation of World War II. Later, its focus shifted to providing loans for development projects in developing countries. IBRD is part of the World Bank Group, which consists of five institutions. It aims to reduce poverty and promote economic development by providing long-term loans. Its headquarters is located in Washington, D.C. Currently, IBRD has 189 member countries.

☛ When was IBRD established? → 1944
☛ At which conference was IBRD established? → Bretton Woods Conference
☛ How many institutions are in the World Bank Group? → Five

☛ How many member countries does IBRD have? → 189

q: Where is the central AGMARK laboratory located in India?
qs.e: The central AGMARK laboratory of India is located in Nagpur, Maharashtra. This laboratory functions under the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). AGMARK is a quality certification mark issued by the Government of India for agricultural products, ensuring their quality standards. The laboratory conducts tests on food grains, spices, oilseeds, fruits, and vegetables. Apart from this central lab, there are several regional laboratories across the country. The AGMARK Act was enacted in 1937.

q: The East-West Corridor under National Highway Development Project is from:
qs.e: Under the National Highway Development Project (NHDP), the East-West Corridor connects Silchar (Assam) to Porbandar (Gujarat). It is approximately 3,300 km long and aims to link eastern and western India. NHDP was launched in 1998 and comprises four main components: Golden Quadrilateral, East-West Corridor, North-South Corridor, and other national highways. The East-West Corridor connects northeastern states to the western coast, enhancing economic integration and transport capacity. It is managed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
qs.kf:

☛ Cities connected by North-South Corridor → Srinagar to Kanyakumari
☛ Total length of Golden Quadrilateral → Approximately 5,846 km
☛ Year of NHDP launch → 1998
☛ State where Silchar is located → Assam

q: The United States has labeled which country a 'currency manipulator' in December 2020?
qs.e: In December 2020, the US Treasury Department labeled Vietnam a currency manipulator under the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015. The allegation was that Vietnam was devaluing its currency (dong) to boost exports, harming US industries like textiles and footwear. The US also cited Vietnam's large trade surplus with the US as a concern. Previously, China had been labeled a currency manipulator but was removed in 2020. This action escalated bilateral trade tensions. Vietnam's central bank was accused of intervening in foreign exchange markets to keep the dong weak, which the US argued was unfair to American exports.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Vietnam labeled a currency manipulator? → December 2020
☛ Which US department issues the currency manipulator list? → Treasury Department
☛ What is Vietnam's currency called? → Dong
☛ Which country was removed from the currency manipulator list in 2019? → China
☛ What is the main purpose of currency manipulation? → To make exports cheaper

q: Which of the following was the first official international step to protect the environment?
qs.e: The 1972 Stockholm Conference (UN Conference on the Human Environment) was the first official international step to protect the environment. It focused on global environmental issues and led to the creation of UNEP (United Nations Environment Programme). The Nairobi Declaration was in 1982, the Earth Summit in 1992, and the Vienna Convention in 1985 for ozone layer protection. The Stockholm Conference linked environment to human rights and laid the foundation for sustainable development.
qs.kf:
☛ First environmental conference → Stockholm (1972)
☛ Organization established at Stockholm → UNEP
☛ Year of Nairobi Declaration → 1982
☛ Earth Summit held in → Rio de Janeiro (1992)
☛ Purpose of Vienna Convention → Ozone layer protection

q: The currency of Malaysia is _______.
qs.e: The official currency of Malaysia is the Malaysian Ringgit (ISO code: MYR), symbolized as RM. It is subdivided into 100 sen. The currency is issued by the Bank Negara Malaysia, the country's central bank. Other options are incorrect: Euro is the currency of the European Union, Peso is used in the Philippines and several Latin American countries, and Kwacha is the currency of Zambia and Malawi.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Malaysia → Kuala Lumpur
☛ Head of government of Malaysia → Prime Minister (current: Anwar Ibrahim)
☛ Official language of Malaysia → Malay (Bahasa Malaysia)
☛ Central bank of Malaysia → Bank Negara Malaysia
☛ Currencies of Southeast Asian countries → Indonesia: Rupiah, Thailand: Baht, Vietnam: Dong

q: Which of the following does NOT come under Infrastructure?
qs.e: Infrastructure refers to the physical and organizational structures required for the economic development and quality of life of a country or region. It includes facilities such as Electricity, Transportation (roads, railways, airports), and Sewage (wastewater systems), which fulfill basic societal needs and support production. Entertainment (e.g., cinemas, parks) is a social activity but is not considered essential infrastructure because it does not directly relate to economic or livelihood needs. In economics, infrastructure is the foundation for production and services, while entertainment is a non-essential service.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the main purpose of infrastructure? → Economic development and improved living standards
☛ Example of physical infrastructure? → Roads, power grids, pipelines
☛ What comes under social infrastructure? → Education, healthcare services
☛ Which sector is NOT part of infrastructure? → Entertainment
☛ Why is investment in infrastructure important? → To boost productivity and employment

q: Which of the following is a drought-tolerant crop?
qs.e: Millet is a drought-tolerant crop, grown in low rainfall areas. It can be cultivated in both Rabi and Kharif seasons, but mainly as a Kharif crop. Millet has a deep root system that helps absorb moisture, making it suitable for arid and semi-arid regions. In contrast, rice, sugarcane, and jute require more water. In India, millet is primarily grown in Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat. It is rich in nutrients and is also known as a coarse grain.
qs.kf:
☛ Which season is millet mainly cultivated in? → Kharif
☛ Which Indian state is the largest producer of millet? → Rajasthan
☛ What type of grain is millet? → Coarse grain
☛ What kind of root system does millet have? → Deep
☛ What is the scientific name of millet? → Pennisetum glaucum

q: Which of the following is India's largest oil company?
qs.e: India's largest oil company is Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), a public sector undertaking. Headquartered in New Delhi, IOCL is involved in refining crude oil, marketing petroleum products, and petrochemicals. It is listed in the Fortune Global 500 and has the largest refining capacity in India. While Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum are also major players, IOCL surpasses them in size and revenue. Oil and Natural Gas Company (ONGC) is primarily an exploration and production company, not a refining company. Thus, the largest oil company is IOCL.
qs.kf:
☛ Company with largest refining capacity in India → Indian Oil Corporation Limited
☛ Headquarters of Indian Oil → New Delhi
☛ IOCL is listed in which index? → Fortune Global 500
☛ Largest oil exploration and production company → Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC)
☛ Oldest oil company in India → Indian Oil Corporation (established in 1959)

q: Every year 'ease of doing business index' is released. It is released by:
qs.e: Every year the 'Ease of Doing Business Index' is released by the World Bank Group. This index measures the regulatory environment and ease of starting and operating a business across different countries. It was first published in 2003. The index covers key areas such as starting a business, dealing with construction permits, getting electricity, registering property, getting credit, protecting minority investors, paying taxes, trading across borders, enforcing contracts, and resolving insolvency. The World Bank Group's headquarters is in Washington, D.C., USA. The index aims to encourage countries to adopt better regulations for businesses and is widely used as a benchmark for economic reforms.
qs.kf:
☛ Which organization releases the Ease of Doing Business Index? → World Bank Group
☛ When was the index first introduced? → 2003
☛ What is the headquarters of World Bank Group? → Washington, D.C.
☛ How many institutions are part of World Bank Group? → 5
☛ What is the main objective of World Bank? → Poverty alleviation and development assistance

q: The World Bank has tied with which bank to enable secondary bond trading recorded on Blockchain?
qs.e: The World Bank has partnered with the Commonwealth Bank of Australia to enable secondary bond trading recorded on blockchain. This initiative aims to enhance the efficiency of digital bond issuance and trading. Using blockchain technology improves transaction transparency, security, and speed. The World Bank previously issued blockchain-based bonds known as 'Bond-i'. This partnership promotes digitization in global financial markets and could revolutionize the traditional bond market.
qs.kf:
☛ World Bank's partner for blockchain-based secondary bond trading → Commonwealth Bank of Australia
☛ First blockchain bond issued by World Bank → Bond-i (2018)
☛ Key benefit of blockchain bonds → Transparency and security
☛ Headquarters of Commonwealth Bank of Australia → Sydney, Australia
☛ Smart contracts used in blockchain technology → Automated execution

q: What does World Trade Organisation (WTO) promote?
qs.e: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) is an international body that regulates and promotes multi-lateral trade among member countries. Its key objective is to reduce trade barriers and ensure smooth, predictable, and free trade. WTO was established on January 1, 1995, as a result of the Uruguay Round negotiations. Its headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland. It provides a platform for resolving trade disputes and helps member countries bring transparency to trade policies. WTO does not promote unilateral trade, global peace, or financial support; its focus is on strengthening the multi-lateral trade system.
qs.kf:
☛ When was WTO established? → January 1, 1995
☛ Where is the headquarters of WTO? → Geneva, Switzerland
☛ What is the main objective of WTO? → To reduce trade barriers
☛ Is WTO the successor of GATT? → Yes
☛ How many member countries does WTO have? → 164

q: Food grains like wheat and rice bought by the government through the Food Corporation of India (FCI) are called ___________.
qs.e: The Government of India purchases wheat and rice from farmers at the Minimum Support Price (MSP) through the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to ensure food security. This procured grain is called buffer stock. Buffer stock is used to distribute food grains at subsidized rates to the poor under the Public Distribution System (PDS) and to control market prices. It is a crucial measure to ensure food security. FCI handles the storage, transport, and distribution of grains across the country. There is no fixed quantity for buffer stock, but the government maintains it as per requirements.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Food Corporation of India (FCI) established? → 1965
☛ Who recommends the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for buffer stock procurement? → Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
☛ At what price is grain given under the Public Distribution System (PDS)? → Lower than the central pool price
☛ What is the main objective of buffer stock? → Food security and price stability
☛ What is the approximate storage capacity of FCI? → Over 100 million tonnes

q: What is the full form of autonomous body NDTL under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports?
qs.e: The full form of NDTL is National Dope Testing Laboratory. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. Established in 1995, NDTL is responsible for anti-doping activities in sports. It is recognized by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and tests samples of athletes for prohibited substances. Located in New Delhi, it plays a key role in India's National Anti-Doping Policy.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NDTL? → National Dope Testing Laboratory
☛ Under which ministry does NDTL function? → Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
☛ When was NDTL established? → 1995
☛ Which international body recognizes NDTL? → WADA
☛ Where is NDTL located? → New Delhi

q: The 'Revamped public distribution system' (RPDS) was started in the year ____________________.
qs.e: The Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS) was launched in the year 1992. Its aim was to provide food grains at subsidized rates to people living in remote and backward areas of the country. RPDS was introduced to address the shortcomings of the earlier PDS and to ensure that subsidized grains reach the poor. Under this system, wheat, rice, and other essential commodities were distributed to targeted communities. Later, in 1997, the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) replaced RPDS. The implementation of RPDS was mainly focused on rural areas and played a significant role in strengthening food security. It covered areas with poor infrastructure and high poverty rates, ensuring that vulnerable populations had access to affordable food.
qs.kf:
☛ Year RPDS was launched → 1992
☛ Full form of RPDS → Revamped Public Distribution System
☛ Objective of RPDS → Provide food grains to remote and backward areas
☛ Scheme that replaced RPDS → Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS), 1997
☛ Main items distributed under RPDS → Wheat, rice

q: Which of the following is a member of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)?
qs.e: OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is an intergovernmental organization founded in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. Its main objective is to coordinate petroleum policies and ensure fair prices for member countries. Libya joined OPEC in 1962 and is one of its key members. India, the USA, and South Africa are not members of OPEC. Currently, OPEC has 13 member countries, including Algeria, Angola, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, and Venezuela.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of OPEC? → Vienna, Austria
☛ When was OPEC founded? → 1960
☛ How many founding members does OPEC have? → 5 (Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela)
☛ How many total members does OPEC currently have? → 13
☛ When did Libya join OPEC? → 1962

q: India has set up Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) in ______
qs.e: India set up Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) in 1965 at Kandla, Gujarat. Its objective was to promote exports and attract foreign investment. EPZs are special economic zones where tax exemptions and other incentives are provided for manufacturing and exports. After the success of Kandla EPZ, India established more EPZs, which later evolved into SEZs (Special Economic Zones). This was a significant milestone in India's export policy.
qs.kf:
☛ Asia's first EPZ → Kandla, Gujarat (1965)
☛ Full form of EPZ → Export Processing Zone
☛ Main objective of EPZ → Boost exports and attract FDI
☛ EPZ later transformed into → SEZ (Special Economic Zone)
☛ SEZ policy implemented in → 2005

q: What year did the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) come into being?
qs.e: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) came into effect in 1948. It was created to reduce international trade barriers and lower tariffs. GATT was signed by 23 countries. It was replaced by the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 1995. Key negotiating rounds under GATT include the Uruguay Round (1986-1994), which led to the formation of the WTO.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of GATT? → General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
☛ When was GATT signed? → 1947
☛ When did GATT come into effect? → 1948
☛ Which organization replaced GATT? → WTO (1995)
☛ Initial member countries of GATT? → 23

q: Where is the only airport in Lakshadweep?
qs.e: The only airport in the union territory of Lakshadweep is located on Agatti Island. It is called Agatti Airport (IATA: AGX, ICAO: VOAT). This small airport connects primarily to Bangalore and Kochi via flights operated by Air India. Since most other islands are not connected by air, water transport is the primary mode of travel within the archipelago. The airport was originally built by the Indian Coast Guard and later opened for civilian use. It plays a vital role in tourism and local connectivity. The runway length is about 1.2 km, making it suitable for smaller aircraft like ATR 72.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the only airport in Lakshadweep? → Agatti Airport
☛ What is the IATA code of Agatti Airport? → AGX
☛ What is the capital of Lakshadweep? → Kavaratti
☛ How many islands are there in Lakshadweep? → 36 (inhabited: 10)
☛ Which is the largest island of Lakshadweep? → Minicoy

q: The head office of the Asian Development Bank is located in-
qs.e: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) is located in Manila, the capital of the Philippines. ADB was established in 1966 and currently has 68 member countries. Its primary goal is to promote economic development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region. ADB provides loans, technical assistance, and grants to developing member countries. The headquarters is situated in the city of Mandaluyong, Metro Manila. The current president of ADB is Masatsugu Asakawa.
qs.kf:
☛ ADB establishment year → 1966
☛ ADB headquarters → Manila, Philippines
☛ ADB current president → Masatsugu Asakawa
☛ ADB member countries → 68
☛ ADB objective → Economic development in Asia-Pacific

q: Where is the famous fishing ground "Grand Bank" located?
qs.e: Grand Bank is the world's largest and most famous fishing ground, located in the North Atlantic Ocean off the southeastern coast of Newfoundland (Canada). It is formed at the meeting point of the cold Labrador Current and the warm Gulf Stream, which creates ideal conditions for plankton growth, attracting large numbers of fish. Major fish species include cod, haddock, flounder, and herring. The Grand Banks have historically been one of the richest fishing areas in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Grand Bank located? → Off the coast of Newfoundland
☛ Which currents meet at Grand Bank? → Labrador Current and Gulf Stream
☛ What is the main reason for abundant fish at Grand Bank? → Plankton abundance
☛ Which is the main fish species found at Grand Bank? → Cod
☛ Grand Bank is near which country? → Canada

q: What is the currency name of Kuwait?
qs.e: The official currency of Kuwait is the Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD). It is one of the highest-valued currencies in the world. The Kuwaiti Dinar is subdivided into 1000 fils. The Central Bank of Kuwait issues this currency. The high value of the Kuwaiti Dinar is due to Kuwait's large oil reserves and strong economy. Kuwait is a major oil-producing country located in the Middle East.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest valued currency in the world → Kuwaiti Dinar
☛ Subunit of Kuwaiti Dinar → 1 Dinar = 1000 Fils
☛ Central Bank issuing currency in Kuwait → Central Bank of Kuwait
☛ Capital of Kuwait → Kuwait City
☛ Official language of Kuwait → Arabic

q: What is the currency of the United Kingdom (Great Britain and Northern Ireland)?
qs.e: The official currency of the United Kingdom is the Pound Sterling (GBP), often simply called the 'pound'. It is one of the oldest currencies still in use and a major reserve currency in the global financial market. One pound is subdivided into 100 pence. The Bank of England is responsible for issuing and controlling the currency. The symbol for the pound sterling is '£'. Despite leaving the European Union, the pound maintains a strong position. Other options like Dinar, Dollar, and Ringgit are currencies of various Arab nations, the United States, and Malaysia respectively.
qs.kf:
☛ Currency name of UK → Pound Sterling (GBP)
☛ Symbol of Pound → £
☛ Number of pence in one pound → 100
☛ Bank issuing the currency → Bank of England
☛ Other currencies used in UK → None (only pound)
