He sailed around the Cape of Good Hope in Africa to reach India. The Kappad beach still has a monument commemorating this event. His arrival opened the spice trade routes and changed the course of Indian history.
qs.kf:
☛ Vasco da Gama's arrival in India → 1498, Kappad, Kerala
☛ Patron of Vasco da Gama → King Manuel I of Portugal
☛ First European to reach India by sea → Vasco da Gama
☛ First Portuguese settlement in India → Goa (1510)
☛ Modern name of Kappad → Kozhikode, Kerala

q: Capital of Nagaland is
A. Dimapur
B. Kohima
C. Kokokchung
D. Tezpur
qs.e: The capital of Nagaland is Kohima. It is the largest city and administrative center of the state. Kohima became the capital when Nagaland was granted statehood in 1963. The city is situated on the hills, about 74 km from Dimapur. Kohima is famous for the Hornbill Festival, which showcases Naga culture. The Battle of Kohima during World War II is a historic site here. Other options: Dimapur is the largest city but not the capital; Mokokchung is a district; Tezpur is in Assam.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Nagaland → Kohima
☛ Largest municipality in Nagaland → Dimapur
☛ Hornbill Festival venue → Kohima (Nagaland)
☛ Famous WWII battle site → Battle of Kohima
☛ Nagaland statehood date → 1 December 1963

q: What is the national dress of Japan?
A. Chador
B. Kilt
C. Sarong
D. Kimono
qs.e: The national dress of Japan is the Kimono, a traditional garment worn by both men and women. It is characterized by long sleeves, a T-shaped design, and is wrapped around the body and tied with a sash called an Obi. Kimonos are typically worn on special occasions such as weddings, festivals, and tea ceremonies. Option A 'Chador' is a traditional dress of Iran, Option B 'Kilt' is from Scotland, and Option C 'Sarong' is from Southeast Asia. Therefore, Kimono is the correct national dress of Japan.
qs.kf:
☛ Japan's national dress → Kimono
☛ Belt worn with Kimono → Obi
☛ Japan's national flower → Cherry Blossom (Sakura)
☛ Japan's currency → Yen
☛ Japan's national sport → Sumo Wrestling

q: Which district of India has become the first district in the country to have a high-speed rural broadband network under NOFN?
A. Bhopal
B. Chennai
C. Idukki
D. Mysore
qs.e: Idukki district of Kerala has become the first district in India to have a fully operational high-speed rural broadband network under the National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) scheme. The NOFN aims to provide high-speed internet connectivity to rural areas through optical fibre. This project is now known as BharatNet. Idukki achieved this milestone by connecting all its villages with optical fibre, enabling better access to education, healthcare, and digital services for rural communities. This achievement marks a significant step in the Digital India mission's rural broadband expansion.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NOFN? → National Optical Fibre Network
☛ What is NOFN now called? → BharatNet
☛ Which ministry implements the BharatNet project? → Ministry of Communications (DoT)
☛ What is the objective of NOFN? → To provide high-speed broadband connectivity to rural areas via optical fibre
☛ In which state is Idukki district located? → Kerala

q: Which Prime Minister of India has hoisted the national flag from Red Fort most often?
A. Indira Gandhi
B. Jawahar Lal Nehru
C. Manmohan Singh
D. Atal Bihari Vajpayee
qs.e: Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India, holds the record for hoisting the national flag from the Red Fort the most times. He hoisted the flag 16 times consecutively from 1947 to 1964. Indira Gandhi did it 11 times, Manmohan Singh 10 times, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee 6 times. The tradition began in 1947 when Nehru first hoisted the flag on Independence Day. Nehru's record remains unbroken to this day.
qs.kf:
☛ PM with most flag hoistings → Jawaharlal Nehru (16 times)
☛ Second most flag hoistings → Indira Gandhi (11 times)
☛ First to hoist flag at Red Fort → Jawaharlal Nehru (1947)
☛ Tradition started in → 1947
☛ Vajpayee's flag hoistings → 6 times

q: Where is Parks Observatory located?
A. USA
B. US
C. Russia
D. Australia
qs.e: Parkes Observatory is a famous radio telescope located in Australia, specifically in the state of New South Wales. It is operated by CSIRO (Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation) and is one of the world's largest radio telescopes. It is used for astronomical research and played a crucial role in receiving transmissions from the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969. The observatory has been instrumental in advancing radio astronomy, discovering many pulsars and galaxies. It remains a key facility for scientific research in space and astronomy.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Parkes Observatory located? → Australia
☛ In which state is Parkes Observatory located? → New South Wales
☛ Who operates Parkes Observatory? → CSIRO
☛ Which mission did Parkes Observatory support in 1969? → Apollo 11
☛ What type of telescope is Parkes Observatory? → Radio telescope

q: In which country did the Hotaki dynasty flourish?
A. Sri Lanka
B. China
C. Nepal
D. Afghanistan
qs.e: The Hotaki dynasty was an Afghan dynasty founded by Mirwais Hotak. It flourished in the region of Afghanistan from 1709 to 1738. The Hotaki dynasty rebelled against the Safavid Empire and made Kandahar its capital. The most famous rulers of this dynasty were Mirwais Hotak and his son Mahmud Hotak, not Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani). Mahmud Hotak captured Isfahan in 1722, ending the Safavid dynasty. However, the dynasty was short-lived and ended in 1738 after the invasion of Nader Shah. The Hotaki dynasty played a significant role in the history of Afghanistan.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded the Hotaki dynasty? → Mirwais Hotak
☛ What was the capital of the Hotaki dynasty? → Kandahar
☛ Against which empire did the Hotaki dynasty rebel? → Safavid Empire
☛ Who ended the Hotaki dynasty? → Nader Shah
☛ Which city did Mahmud Hotak capture? → Isfahan

name: Set 2 · Q48–94
sub: Static GK - Geography, States, Places & Heritage

q: Which city is known as the City of Pearls?
qs.e: Hyderabad is known as the 'City of Pearls' due to its historic pearl industry and pearl jewelry trade. Located on the Deccan Plateau, it was a major center for pearl trading under the Nizams. Even today, Hyderabad attracts tourists with landmarks like Charminar, Mecca Masjid, and Golconda Fort. It is also called the 'City of Biryani' and is the capital of Telangana. Hyderabad has emerged as a major hub for information technology. The city is famous for its rich history, culture, and cuisine.
qs.kf:
☛ Which city is known as 'Garden City'? → Bengaluru
☛ Which city is known as 'Pink City'? → Jaipur
☛ Which city is known as 'City of Lakes'? → Udaipur
☛ Which city is known as 'Silicon Valley of India'? → Bengaluru
☛ Which city is known as 'Diamond City'? → Surat

q: A flag of Malaysia, comprises a field of ______ alternating red and white stripes.
qs.e: The flag of Malaysia comprises a field of 14 alternating red and white stripes, representing the 13 states and the Federal Territory of Malaysia. In the upper left canton, a dark blue background features a yellow crescent and a 14-pointed star (also called the 'Star of Federation'). The 14 points of the star symbolize the unity of the 13 states and the federal territory. The blue color signifies unity of the people, yellow represents the monarchy, red signifies courage, and white stands for purity. The flag is known as Jalur Gemilang, meaning 'Stripes of Glory'. It was adopted on August 16, 1963, and is a symbol of the nation's independence and sovereignty.
qs.kf:
☛ How many stripes are on the flag of Malaysia? → 14
☛ What is the name of the Malaysian flag? → Jalur Gemilang
☛ What color is the canton of the Malaysian flag? → Dark blue
☛ How many points does the star on the Malaysian flag have? → 14
☛ When was the Malaysian flag adopted? → August 16, 1963

q: Russian Sukhoi 24 (SU-24) flight was shot down in November 2015 by
A. Syria
B. North Korea
C. Afghanistan
D. Turkey
qs.e: In November 2015, a Russian Sukhoi SU-24 fighter jet was shot down by the Turkish Air Force near the Syria-Turkey border. Russia claimed the aircraft was in Syrian airspace, while Turkey asserted it had violated Turkish airspace. This incident led to heightened tensions between Russia and Turkey, with Russia imposing economic sanctions on Turkey. The event occurred in the context of Russian military intervention in the Syrian civil war.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country shot down the SU-24? → Turkey
☛ When did the incident occur? → November 2015
☛ Which country did the SU-24 belong to? → Russia
☛ What airspace violation did Turkey allege? → Turkish airspace
☛ What type of sanctions did Russia impose on Turkey? → Economic sanctions

q: The famous Nek Chand's Rock Garden is located in
A. Srinagar
B. Jammu
C. Chandigarh
D. Shimla
qs.e: Nek Chand's Rock Garden is a unique park located in Chandigarh, built by Nek Chand Saini using discarded items like broken pots, glass, stones, and other waste materials. It is famous for its sculptures and structures made entirely from recycled materials. Nek Chand was a government employee who secretly built the garden, which was later opened to the public in 1976. Today, it is one of the major tourist attractions in Chandigarh, drawing millions of visitors annually for its artistic and environmental significance.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Nek Chand's Rock Garden located? → Chandigarh
☛ Who built the Rock Garden? → Nek Chand Saini
☛ When was the Rock Garden opened to the public? → 1976
☛ What is the Rock Garden made of? → Waste and discarded materials
☛ Which state is Chandigarh the capital of? → Punjab and Haryana

q: Which of the following states has the giant squirrel as its state animal?
qs.e: The state animal of Maharashtra is the Indian Giant Squirrel, locally called Shekru. This species is found mainly in the forests of central India and is known for its bright colors and large size. The Maharashtra government declared it the state animal in 1985. It is arboreal and feeds on fruits, seeds, and leaves. Conservation efforts are ongoing in various wildlife sanctuaries of Maharashtra. In contrast, the state animal of Goa is the Gaur, Himachal Pradesh has the Snow Leopard, and Haryana has the Blackbuck.
qs.kf:
☛ State animal of Maharashtra → Indian Giant Squirrel (Shekru)
☛ State animal of Goa → Gaur
☛ State animal of Himachal Pradesh → Snow Leopard
☛ State animal of Haryana → Blackbuck
☛ Scientific name of Indian Giant Squirrel → Ratufa indica

q: In which state is the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, located?
qs.e: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) is located at Sriharikota, which lies in the Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh, along the Bay of Bengal coast. It is the primary launch center of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). From here, launch vehicles like PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3 are launched. The center is strategically located near the equator, providing an advantage for rocket launches. It was originally known as Sriharikota Range (SHAR) and was renamed in 2002 after former ISRO chairman Satish Dhawan. The facility includes multiple launch pads, a vehicle assembly building, and a mission control center.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full name of SDSC? → Satish Dhawan Space Centre
☛ Where is SDSC located? → Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh
☛ What was the old name of SDSC? → SHAR (Sriharikota Range)
☛ After whom is SDSC named? → Satish Dhawan
☛ Where is ISRO headquarters? → Bengaluru, Karnataka

q: In which city was the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) signed between India and Pakistan, in 1960?
qs.e: The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) was signed on September 19, 1960, between then Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistani President Ayub Khan. The treaty was mediated by the World Bank. The signing ceremony took place in the Pakistani city of Karachi. This treaty governs the sharing of water from the Indus River system, allocating the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India and the three western rivers (Indus, Chenab, Jhelum) to Pakistan. It is considered one of the most successful water-sharing treaties in the world and forms the basis for resolving water disputes between the two countries.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Indus Waters Treaty signed? → September 19, 1960
☛ Who mediated the treaty? → World Bank
☛ Which rivers were allocated to India? → Ravi, Beas, Sutlej
☛ Which rivers were allocated to Pakistan? → Indus, Chenab, Jhelum
☛ In which city was it signed? → Karachi

q: Sanchi Stupa is situated near the city of _________.
qs.e: Sanchi Stupa is located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, about 46 km northeast of the capital city Bhopal. This stupa was built by Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sanchi Stupa is renowned for its architecture and Buddhist art, including four beautifully carved gateways (toranas) depicting various aspects of life. It is one of the oldest stone structures in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Sanchi Stupa? → Emperor Ashoka
☛ In which state is Sanchi Stupa located? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Sanchi Stupa is associated with which religion? → Buddhism
☛ When was Sanchi Stupa built? → 3rd century BCE
☛ Which river flows near Sanchi Stupa? → Betwa River

q: Asia's largest Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip garden is situated in which city?
qs.e: Asia's largest Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden is situated in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. The garden is spread across the foothills of the Zabarwan mountains on the banks of Dal Lake. It was earlier known as Siraj Bagh and was later renamed in memory of Indira Gandhi. Every spring, the Tulip Festival is organized here, featuring millions of blooming tulips. This garden is a major tourist attraction and enhances the beauty of Kashmir.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden located? → Srinagar
☛ What was the old name of Tulip Garden? → Siraj Bagh
☛ When is the Tulip Festival held? → Spring season
☛ Which lake is the Tulip Garden situated on? → Dal Lake
☛ Which mountain foothill is the Tulip Garden located in? → Zabarwan mountains

q: Clearance of snow in high altitude areas is undertakes by:
qs.e: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) is the premier agency responsible for clearance of snow in high altitude areas in India. Established in 1960, it operates under the Ministry of Defence. BRO undertakes construction and maintenance of roads in border regions, including snow clearance operations. It is active in high altitude areas like Leh, Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh. Specialized equipment and techniques are used to remove snow, ensuring military and civilian movement. The organisation plays a vital role in maintaining connectivity in harsh winter conditions.
qs.kf:
☛ When was BRO established? → 1960
☛ Under which ministry does BRO work? → Ministry of Defence
☛ Where is BRO headquarters located? → New Delhi
☛ What is BRO's motto? → 'Roads are Lifelines'
☛ Which famous highway is built by BRO? → Leh-Manali Highway

q: On which day is World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought observed?
qs.e: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed annually on 17 June. It was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1994, the same year the UNCCD (United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification) was adopted. The day aims to promote awareness of desertification and drought issues and encourage action to prevent land degradation. It is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 15 (Life on Land), which focuses on protecting, restoring, and promoting sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems. In India, desertification is a serious problem affecting about 30% of the country's land area.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UNCCD established? → 1994
☛ Where is UNCCD headquarters located? → Bonn, Germany
☛ Which SDG target is related to desertification? → SDG 15
☛ Approximate percentage of land affected by desertification in India? → 30%
☛ Theme for this year's Desertification Day? → Land restoration and drought resilience

q: Which one country of the following was not a part of former USSR?
qs.e: The former USSR (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) was a federation of 15 republics that existed from 1922 to 1991. It included Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia. Finland was never part of the USSR; it remained an independent country, although it shared a border with the Soviet Union and fought wars during World War II. Both Moldova and Georgia were Soviet republics. Russia was the largest and dominant republic of the USSR. Therefore, Finland is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the USSR formed? → 30 December 1922
☛ When did the USSR dissolve? → 26 December 1991
☛ Who was the last leader of the USSR? → Mikhail Gorbachev
☛ Which was the largest Soviet republic? → Russia
☛ Who was the first leader of the USSR? → Lenin (as head of the Soviet state)

q: The National Informatics Centre (NIC) was established in:
qs.e: The National Informatics Centre (NIC) was established in 1976 by the Government of India. Its primary objective is to provide information technology services to government departments and promote e-governance. NIC operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. It offers services like networking, database management, and web services. The headquarters of NIC is located in New Delhi.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of NIC? → National Informatics Centre
☛ Under which ministry does NIC operate? → Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
☛ Where is the headquarters of NIC located? → New Delhi
☛ What types of services does NIC provide? → IT services, e-governance solutions
☛ What was the purpose of establishing NIC? → To provide information technology services to government departments

q: Name the place in India where one can find the Zero Mile Stone consisting of four horses and a pillar made up of sandstone.
qs.e: The Zero Mile Stone located in Nagpur is a historical monument featuring four horses and a sandstone pillar. It marks the zero mile of the Great Trunk Road, built during the British era. Constructed in the 1930s, it symbolizes the geographical center of India. The four horses represent the four cardinal directions. Nagpur is a major city in Maharashtra, famous for its oranges. The Zero Mile Stone is a popular tourist and historical attraction.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Zero Mile Stone located? → Nagpur
☛ Which stone is used in Zero Mile Stone? → Sandstone
☛ How many horses are on Zero Mile Stone? → Four
☛ Which road's zero mile is marked by Zero Mile Stone? → Great Trunk Road
☛ In which decade was Zero Mile Stone built? → 1930s

q: India's 'Statue of Unity' is situated in the state of:
qs.e: The Statue of Unity is located in the state of Gujarat, specifically in Narmada district. It is a statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, India's first Deputy Prime Minister and a freedom fighter. With a height of 182 meters, it is the tallest statue in the world. The statue stands on an island near the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada River. It was inaugurated on 31 October 2018 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The statue symbolizes national unity and integrity.
qs.kf:
☛ Whose statue is the Statue of Unity? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ What is the height of the Statue of Unity? → 182 meters
☛ Near which river is the Statue of Unity located? → Narmada River
☛ When was the Statue of Unity inaugurated? → 31 October 2018
☛ Near which dam is the Statue of Unity situated? → Sardar Sarovar Dam

q: In which of the following continent are the 6 most populated countries located?
qs.e: Out of the world's 6 most populated countries, 5 are located in Asia: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. The sixth most populated country is Nigeria in Africa, but the group of 6 most populated countries is predominantly from Asia. The Americas (North and South America) have only the United States (third largest) in the top 6. Asia accounts for about 60% of the global population, with China and India alone exceeding 2.8 billion. This makes Asia the most populous continent by a wide margin.
qs.kf:
☛ Most populous continent → Asia
☛ Second most populous continent → Africa
☛ Third most populous continent → Europe
☛ Most populous country in Asia → China
☛ Most populous country in the world → India (since 2023)

q: Megalopolis a Greek word meaning "great city", was popularised by ______ (1957).
qs.e: The word 'Megalopolis' is derived from Greek, meaning 'great city'. It was popularised in 1957 by the French geographer Jean Gottman in his book 'Megalopolis: The Urbanized Northeastern Seaboard of the United States'. Gottman used this term to describe the vast urban region along the northeastern coast of the USA, where several major cities like Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore, and Washington D.C. have merged into a continuous urban sprawl. This concept significantly influenced urban geography and planning, highlighting the emergence of large-scale metropolitan areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Who coined the term Megalopolis? → Jean Gottman (1957)
☛ Jean Gottman belonged to which country? → France
☛ Megalopolis is a word from which language? → Greek
☛ What is the literal meaning of Megalopolis? → Great city
☛ Which region did Gottman describe as a Megalopolis? → Northeastern seaboard of USA

q: Which of the following cities is known as 'The City of Palaces' India?
qs.e: Kolkata is known as the 'City of Palaces'. This nickname originates from the numerous majestic palaces and colonial buildings built during the British Raj. Landmarks like Victoria Memorial, Raj Bhavan, and Writers' Building exemplify this architectural heritage. Kolkata is also called the 'Cultural Capital', 'City of Joy', and 'London of the East'. In contrast, Jaipur is known as the 'Pink City', Lucknow as the 'City of Nawabs', and Patna as the 'City of Guru'.
qs.kf:
☛ Jaipur → Pink City
☛ Lucknow → City of Nawabs
☛ Patna → City of Guru
☛ Kolkata → City of Palaces
☛ Bengaluru → Silicon Valley of India

q: The states of Maharashtra and Gujarat were created in _________.
qs.e: The states of Maharashtra and Gujarat were formed on May 1, 1960. This resulted from the partition of the then Bombay State. Bombay State included primarily Marathi-speaking and Gujarati-speaking regions. Due to increasing demands for linguistic reorganization, the Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960 was passed. Under this act, Bombay State was divided into two separate states: Maharashtra (Marathi-speaking areas) and Gujarat (Gujarati-speaking areas). Thus, both states came into existence in 1960.
qs.kf:
☛ When were Maharashtra and Gujarat formed? → May 1, 1960
☛ From which state were Maharashtra and Gujarat created? → Bombay State
☛ When was the Bombay Reorganisation Act passed? → 1960
☛ What is the capital of Maharashtra? → Mumbai
☛ What is the capital of Gujarat? → Gandhinagar

q: Which is Asia's biggest bus terminus?
o: Tel Aviv Central Bus Stand in Tel Aviv
Port Authority Bus Terminal in New York City
Chennai Mofussil Bus Terminus in Chennai
qs.e: Chennai Mofussil Bus Terminus (CMBT), also known as Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G. Ramachandran Central Bus Stand, is the largest bus terminus in Asia. Located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, it spans an area of approximately 37 acres. The terminus was completed in 2002 and is designed to handle about 2.5 lakh passengers daily. It has over 70 platforms and provides bus services to various parts of the state as well as neighboring states. CMBT is a crucial hub in Chennai's transportation network.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest bus terminus in Asia → Chennai Mofussil Bus Terminus (CMBT)
☛ Where is CMBT located? → Chennai, Tamil Nadu
☛ Area of CMBT → Approximately 37 acres
☛ Alternative name of CMBT → Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G. Ramachandran Central Bus Stand
☛ Number of platforms in CMBT → Over 70

q: In which city is the headquarters of Indira Gandhi National Centre for Arts located?
qs.e: Indira Gandhi National Centre for Arts (IGNCA) is an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. It was established in 1985 in memory of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. IGNCA is a premier center for research, academic pursuits, and exhibitions in the field of arts and culture. It plays a vital role in the preservation and promotion of Indian art and cultural heritage. Additionally, IGNCA has a regional center in Pune.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of IGNCA → New Delhi
☛ Year of establishment of IGNCA → 1985
☛ IGNCA comes under which ministry → Ministry of Culture
☛ Regional centre of IGNCA → Pune
☛ IGNCA was established in memory of → Indira Gandhi

q: Which place in India was known as “kala pani'?
qs.e: The Andaman Islands were historically known as 'Kala Pani' (black water) due to the infamous Cellular Jail located there, where British colonial authorities exiled political prisoners. The term symbolized the harsh punishment and isolation. Other options like Gulf of Kutch, Lakshadweep, and Kerala's backwaters are not referred to as Kala Pani. The Andaman Islands are situated in the Bay of Bengal and consist of 572 islands. The Cellular Jail in Port Blair is a major landmark associated with this dark history.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Cellular Jail located? → Port Blair, Andaman
☛ Which place was called Kala Pani? → Andaman Islands
☛ Where were political prisoners sent during British rule? → Andaman Islands
☛ In which bay are the Andaman Islands located? → Bay of Bengal
☛ How many islands in Andaman & Nicobar? → 572

q: Name the Shiva temple near Taliparamba in Kerala, where women are allowed to enter only after 8 p.m. A unique feature of this temple is the absence of a flagstaff.
qs.e: The Rajarajeshwara temple near Taliparamba in Kerala is dedicated to Lord Shiva. A unique feature of this temple is the absence of a flagstaff (dhwajastambha), which is typically present in Shiva temples. Another distinct rule is that women are allowed entry only after 8 p.m., making it different from other temples. This temple is well-known for its architecture and traditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Rajarajeshwara temple located? → Near Taliparamba, Kerala
☛ Which deity is Rajarajeshwara temple dedicated to? → Lord Shiva
☛ What is the unique feature of Rajarajeshwara temple? → Absence of a flagstaff
☛ When are women allowed entry into Rajarajeshwara temple? → After 8 p.m.
☛ In which state is Rajarajeshwara temple located? → Kerala

q: The city of ________ does NOT have a Jantar Mantar.
qs.e: Jantar Mantar refers to a set of observatories built by Maharaja Jai Singh II. He constructed a total of five Jantar Mantars in India: Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi, and Mathura. Each observatory is equipped with unique instruments for astronomical observations. The city of Indore does not have a Jantar Mantar. Indore is a major city in Madhya Pradesh known for its palaces and commerce, but it does not house any Jantar Mantar. In contrast, Jaipur's Jantar Mantar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Varanasi and Ujjain also have functional observatories. These structures are significant for their architectural and scientific heritage in astronomy.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Jantar Mantar? → Maharaja Jai Singh II
☛ How many Jantar Mantars are there in India? → Five
☛ Which city's Jantar Mantar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → Jaipur
☛ What was Jantar Mantar used for? → Astronomical observations
☛ Name the cities having Jantar Mantar. → Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi, Mathura

q: Which among the following languages is one of the six official languages of the United Nations?
qs.e: The six official languages of the United Nations are Chinese, Arabic, French, English, Russian, and Spanish. These languages are used in all official UN meetings and documents. Chinese was adopted as an official language in 1946, being a significant language since the UN's inception. Hindi, Urdu, and Japanese are not official UN languages, although efforts have been made by the Indian government to grant Hindi official status. The selection of UN official languages is based on the importance and global usage of member states.
qs.kf:
☛ How many official languages does the UN have? → 6 (Chinese, Arabic, French, English, Russian, Spanish)
☛ When was Chinese made an official UN language? → 1946
☛ What are the working languages of the UN? → English and French
☛ Which official language is most spoken in the UN? → English
☛ Which UN official language is spoken by the most people worldwide? → Chinese (Mandarin)

q: Name the first month of the national calendar of India based on the Saka Era which was adopted from 22 March 1957 along with the Gregorian calendar for the official purposes.
qs.e: The national calendar of India, based on the Saka Era, was adopted on 22 March 1957. The first month of this calendar is Chaitra, which begins on 21/22 March in the Gregorian calendar. This calendar is used for official purposes alongside the Gregorian calendar. It has 365 days in a common year and a leap year every four years. The months in order are: Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyaishtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashvina, Kartika, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha, and Phalguna. Chaitra marks the start of spring and holds cultural significance in many Indian festivals.
qs.kf:
☛ Basis of National Calendar → Saka Era
☛ Adoption Date → 22 March 1957
☛ First Month → Chaitra
☛ Days in a Year → 365
☛ Leap Year Rule → Every 4 years

q: Which was the first social media site?
qs.e: Six Degrees, launched in 1997, is considered the first social media site. It allowed users to create profiles, add friends, and view friends' lists. It was based on the 'Six Degrees of Separation' theory. Friendster (2002) and Myspace (2003) came later. LinkedIn (2003) was for professional networking. Six Degrees laid the foundation for modern social media, though it shut down by 2000.
qs.kf:
☛ First social media site → Six Degrees
☛ Six Degrees launch year → 1997
☛ 'Six Degrees of Separation' proponent → Stanley Milgram
☛ Friendster launch year → 2002
☛ Myspace launch year → 2003

q: Abyssinia is the old name of which country from the following?
qs.e: Abyssinia was an ancient empire located in Africa, which is now known as Ethiopia. The name change occurred in the 20th century during the reign of Emperor Haile Selassie, when the country's official name became Ethiopia. Ethiopia is Africa's oldest independent country and was never colonized. The term Abyssinia is derived from the Arabic word "Habash," used for the people of this region. The capital of Ethiopia is Addis Ababa, which also hosts the headquarters of the African Union. Ethiopia is known for its unique history, including the Battle of Adwa in 1896, where it defeated Italian forces.
qs.kf:
☛ Old name of Ethiopia → Abyssinia
☛ Capital of Ethiopia → Addis Ababa
☛ Ancient kingdom in Ethiopia → Aksum Empire
☛ Ethiopia's independence day → May 5
☛ Abyssinia Crisis (1935) → Invasion by Italy

q: What is the name of famous petroleum site located in Gujarat?
qs.e: A major petroleum producing region in Gujarat is Ankleshwar. It is located in Bharuch district, near the Gulf of Khambhat. Oil was discovered here in the 1950s, and it is part of the Western Coastal Basin. Ankleshwar is one of the key oil fields of ONGC, producing crude oil and natural gas. Other options like Mahabaleshwar (hill station in Maharashtra), Jaileshwar and Amreshwar (temples) are not petroleum sites.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest petroleum producing region in Gujarat → Ankleshwar
☛ Ankleshwar is located in → Bharuch district, Gujarat
☛ Ankleshwar oil field belongs to which basin → Western Coastal Basin
☛ When was oil discovered in Ankleshwar → 1950s
☛ Which organization operates Ankleshwar → ONGC

q: Which of the following dance forms is correctly matched with the state to which it is associated?
qs.e: Gaur dance is a famous folk dance of Chhattisgarh, primarily performed by the Gond and Muria tribes. It is performed during weddings, festivals, and harvest seasons. Dandiya is associated with Gujarat, Lavani with Maharashtra, and Ghoomar with Rajasthan. Therefore, only Gaur-Chhattisgarh is correctly matched.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is associated with Gaur dance? → Chhattisgarh
☛ Which state is Dandiya dance from? → Gujarat
☛ Lavani is a folk dance of which state? → Maharashtra
☛ Ghoomar dance belongs to which state? → Rajasthan
☛ Which tribes perform Gaur dance? → Gond and Muria

q: Which country has sent its former Vice President Ahmed Adeeb to detention center in August 2019?
qs.e: In August 2019, former Vice President Ahmed Adeeb of Maldives was sent to a detention center. Adeeb was accused of plotting an assassination attempt against President Abdulla Yameen. He was arrested in 2015 and convicted in 2016 on charges of terrorism and treason. Maldives is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, with capital Male. It is part of South Asia and famous for tourism. This incident highlighted political turmoil in the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Maldives → Male
☛ Currency of Maldives → Maldivian Rufiyaa
☛ President of Maldives in 2019 → Ibrahim Mohamed Solih
☛ Charge against Ahmed Adeeb → Assassination attempt
☛ Official language of Maldives → Dhivehi

q: Which of the following is the first state of India to pass a law to curb lynching cases?
qs.e: The first state in India to pass a law to curb lynching cases is Manipur. The Manipur Legislative Assembly passed the Manipur Lynching (Prevention, Protection and Redressal) Bill, 2018. This bill was enacted to prevent mob violence and lynching, and to punish the offenders. The law provides for investigation of lynching incidents and compensation to victims. After Manipur, states like Rajasthan, West Bengal, and others also enacted similar laws, but Manipur was the first. This law is a significant step towards maintaining social harmony and strengthening law and order.
qs.kf:
☛ First Indian state to pass anti-lynching law → Manipur
☛ Year of Manipur Lynching Bill → 2018
☛ Central law against lynching in India → None (not yet enacted)
☛ Supreme Court's direction on lynching → To create a separate law
☛ Capital of Manipur → Imphal

q: The Indian National Flag (tricolour) was unfurled by Bhikaiji Cama in:
qs.e: The first version of the Indian National Flag was unfurled by Bhikaiji Cama on August 22, 1907, at the International Socialist Conference held in Stuttgart, Germany. The flag consisted of three colors: green, yellow, and red. The green stripe had eight lotus flowers, the yellow stripe bore the inscription 'Vande Mataram', and the red stripe depicted a sun and a crescent. Cama proclaimed it as 'the flag of Indian independence'. This event was a significant milestone in India's freedom struggle. The current tricolor, adopted in 1947, underwent several modifications since then.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Bhikaiji Cama unfurl the first Indian National Flag? → August 22, 1907
☛ Where was it unfurled? → Stuttgart, Germany
☛ What were the colors of that flag? → Green, yellow, red
☛ What was written on the yellow stripe? → 'Vande Mataram'
☛ How many lotus flowers were on the flag? → Eight

q: Which of the following is NOT a division of National Sample Survey Organisation?
qs.e: The National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) is a premier institution in India for conducting socio-economic surveys. It has four main divisions: Field Operation Division (FOD), which collects field data; Survey Design and Research Division (SDRD), which designs surveys; Data Processing Division (DPD), which processes data; and Coordination and Publication Division (CPD). National Development Agenda is not a division of NSSO; it is a government policy document. Hence, option 1 is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of NSSO → Delhi
☛ Full form of FOD → Field Operation Division
☛ Full form of SDRD → Survey Design and Research Division
☛ Full form of DPD → Data Processing Division
☛ Year of establishment of NSSO → 1970

q: Construction of the Hawa Mahal at Jaipur was inspired by the:
qs.e: Hawa Mahal, located in Jaipur, is a famous palace built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh in 1799. Its architecture was inspired by the Khetri Mahal situated in Jhunjhunu district. The structure of Hawa Mahal is five-storied and designed like a honeycomb. It features 953 small windows (jharokhas) for ventilation, allowing royal women to observe street festivals without being seen. Built with red and pink sandstone, Hawa Mahal is part of the City Palace complex. The unique design reflects a blend of Rajput and Mughal styles.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Hawa Mahal? → Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh
☛ How many windows does Hawa Mahal have? → 953
☛ What is Hawa Mahal made of? → Red and pink sandstone
☛ What is the shape of Hawa Mahal? → Five-storied (pyramidal)
☛ Which palace inspired Hawa Mahal? → Khetri Mahal at Jhunjhunu

q: How many member countries did the UNO have on its formation in 1945?
qs.e: At the time of the formation of the United Nations Organization in 1945, there were 51 member countries. Of these, 50 countries signed the UN Charter on June 26, 1945 at the San Francisco Conference. Poland, which could not sign at that time, joined later, making the total count 51. The UN officially came into existence on October 24, 1945 after ratification of the Charter. This day is celebrated as United Nations Day. The headquarters of the UN is located in New York City. Key founding members included India, China, the United States, the United Kingdom, France, and the Soviet Union. The primary objectives of the UN are maintaining international peace and security and promoting cooperation among nations.
qs.kf:
☛ Original countries that signed UN Charter → 50
☛ Total founding members of UN → 51
☛ Founding Day of UN → 24 October 1945
☛ UN Headquarters → New York
☛ Current member states of UN → 193

q: Which of the following forts is located in Tamil Nadu?
qs.e: The fort located in Tamil Nadu is Manora Fort. Situated in the Villupuram district, this fort was built in the 18th century by the French colonialists. Manora Fort is an important monument in the coastal defense history of India. Sikandra Fort is located near Agra in Uttar Pradesh, Amer Fort is in Jaipur, Rajasthan, and Jaisalmer Fort is also in Rajasthan. Thus, among the four options, only Manora Fort is situated in Tamil Nadu.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Manora Fort in? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Who built Manora Fort? → French
☛ Which district is Manora Fort in? → Villupuram
☛ Where is Sikandra Fort located? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ Where is Amer Fort located? → Rajasthan

q: What is the percentage of the paid up share capital held by the central government or by any state government or partly by the central governments and partly by one or more state governments in Public Sector Undertakings?
qs.e: As per the definition of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), the central government, state government, or both jointly must hold at least 51% of the paid-up share capital. This criterion is clearly defined under the Companies Act, 2013 and government policies. A 51% or more stake ensures government control over the company's management and decision-making. Examples of PSUs include BHEL, ONGC, and Coal India, where the government holds more than 51% equity. If the government's share falls below 51%, the entity is not classified as a PSU. Therefore, this threshold is fundamental to identifying public sector undertakings in India.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the minimum government shareholding in a PSU? → 51%
☛ Which Act defines the PSU? → Companies Act, 2013
☛ Can central and state governments together hold 51% in a PSU? → Yes
☛ Can a private company be a PSU? → No, government shareholding is mandatory
☛ What does PSU stand for? → Public Sector Undertaking

q: Which of the following is India's highest ranked City in Safest City category in the Mercer's 2019 Quality of Living Index?
qs.e: In Mercer's 2019 Quality of Living Index, Chennai was ranked as India's safest city in the 'Safest City' category. Mercer's index evaluates cities based on various factors including safety, healthcare, education, transportation, and overall quality of living. Chennai outperformed other Indian metros in safety standards, with Mumbai, Bangalore, and Delhi following. Chennai's top ranking is attributed to its lower crime rate, effective policing, and robust social safety measures. The index helps multinational companies determine compensation for expatriates based on city conditions.
qs.kf:
☛ Mercer's 2019 safest city in India → Chennai
☛ Mercer's 2019 safest city globally → Singapore
☛ Organization that released the index → Mercer
☛ Parameters considered for safety ranking → Crime rate, law enforcement, social security
☛ Second safest city in India (2019 Mercer) → Mumbai

q: In which of the following cities is the Charminar situated?
qs.e: The Charminar is an iconic historical monument located in Hyderabad, the capital city of Telangana, India. It was built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty. The name Charminar means "Four Minarets" and its architecture is a blend of Islamic and Persian styles. The monument stands on four grand arches, each topped by a minaret, with each minaret being 56 meters tall. Charminar is situated on the eastern bank of the Musi River and has become a symbol of Hyderabad's rich history and culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Charminar? → Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
☛ When was the Charminar built? → 1591 CE
☛ What is the height of the Charminar? → 56 meters
☛ On which river is the Charminar located? → Musi River
☛ Which dynasty is the Charminar associated with? → Qutb Shahi dynasty

q: Which city is popularly called the "Detroit of Asia" and the "Automobile Capital" of India?
qs.e: Chennai is popularly called the 'Detroit of Asia' and the 'Automobile Capital' of India because it is the country's major automobile manufacturing hub. The city hosts plants of Hyundai, Ford, BMW, Renault-Nissan, and Ashok Leyland. Chennai's automobile industry accounts for about 30% of India's total auto exports, producing over 1.5 million vehicles annually. The city also has several research and development centers, making it a hub for the auto sector.
qs.kf:
☛ India's largest automobile exporting city → Chennai
☛ First person to call Chennai 'Detroit of Asia' → Stanley Wolpert (historian)
☛ Major auto companies located in Chennai → Hyundai, Ford, BMW, Renault-Nissan, Ashok Leyland
☛ India's automobile hub → Chennai (Tamil Nadu)
☛ Chennai's auto industry share in India's total exports → about 30%

q: On which date is India likely to experience the shortest day of the year?
qs.e: On 22 December, the Southern Hemisphere experiences summer solstice while the Northern Hemisphere experiences winter solstice. On this day, the sun shines vertically over the Tropic of Capricorn. India is located in the Northern Hemisphere, so on 22 December the day is the shortest and the night is the longest. During the winter solstice, the tilt of the Earth's axis is maximum away from the Sun, causing less sunlight in the Northern Hemisphere. This astronomical event occurs annually on 21 or 22 December. In contrast, 21 June marks the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere.
qs.kf:
☛ When does winter solstice occur? → 21 or 22 December
☛ When is the shortest day in the Northern Hemisphere? → 22 December
☛ On which line does the sun shine vertically on 22 December? → Tropic of Capricorn
☛ When does summer solstice occur? → 21 June
☛ On which dates do equinoxes occur? → 21 March and 23 September

q: The Lion Capital pillar is located at:
qs.e: The Lion Capital, considered the top part of the Ashoka Pillar, is located at Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh. It was built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, where Lord Buddha gave his first sermon. The pillar is famous for its sculptures of four lions standing back to back and has been adopted as the National Emblem of India. The pillar is made of polished sandstone and features several carved elements, including the Dharma Chakra. Sarnath is the place where Buddha performed the Dharma Chakra Pravartana (first turning of the wheel of law).
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Lion Capital built? → 3rd century BCE
☛ Who built the Lion Capital? → Emperor Ashoka
☛ What material is the Lion Capital made of? → Polished sandstone
☛ The Lion Capital is associated with which structure? → Ashoka Pillar
☛ What is the Lion Capital adopted as? → National Emblem of India

q: When was the National Green Tribunal established by the Government of India?
qs.e: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established on 18 October 2010 by the Government of India under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. It is a specialized judicial body created for the speedy disposal of environmental disputes and matters. NGT's headquarters is in New Delhi and its members are judicial and technical experts. Its objective is to provide justice in cases related to environmental protection, forest conservation, and natural resource management. NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure and functions on the principles of natural justice.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of National Green Tribunal → New Delhi
☛ NGT Act passed → 2010
☛ First Chairman of NGT → Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta
☛ Maximum number of members in NGT → 20 (10 judicial + 10 technical)
☛ Appeal against NGT decisions → Supreme Court

q: Which of the following beaches has become the first in Asia to get the Blue Flag certification?
qs.e: Chandrabhaga beach, located in Konark, Odisha, became the first beach in Asia to receive the Blue Flag certification. This certification is awarded by the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE) based in Denmark, based on standards of environmental quality, safety, and sustainability. To earn this certification, a beach must meet 33 stringent criteria, including water quality, environmental education, and management. Chandrabhaga received this certification in October 2020, marking a significant achievement for India and Asia. Other options like Bega, Kovalam, and Marina beaches have not received this certification.
qs.kf:
☛ Which organization awards the Blue Flag certification? → FEE (Foundation for Environmental Education)
☛ In which state is Chandrabhaga beach located? → Odisha
☛ How many criteria are there for Blue Flag certification? → 33
☛ Which is the first Blue Flag beach in India? → Chandrabhaga
☛ What is the Blue Flag certification related to? → Environmental quality and safety

q: Name the state where India's longest (300 m) single-lane steel cable suspension bridge was inaugurated over river siang.
qs.e: This 300-meter long single-lane steel cable suspension bridge over the Siang River in Arunachal Pradesh is the longest in India. It was inaugurated in 2024. The bridge enhances tourism and improves connectivity for locals. The Siang River is a major river in Arunachal Pradesh, and the bridge was built by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO). The project strengthens connectivity in border areas. Constructed in a challenging terrain, it stands as a remarkable infrastructure achievement. The bridge is expected to boost economic activities and accessibility in the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is India's longest single-lane steel cable suspension bridge? → Arunachal Pradesh
☛ Which river is the bridge over? → Siang River
☛ What is the length of the bridge? → 300 meters
☛ Who built the bridge? → Border Roads Organisation (BRO)
☛ What are the benefits of this bridge? → Improved tourism and connectivity

q: Which of following country has the highest number of operational nuclear reactors currently?
qs.e: Currently, the United States has the highest number of operational nuclear reactors in the world. The US has approximately 93 operational reactors, contributing the largest share of global nuclear energy generation. It is followed by France (56 reactors) and China (55 reactors). India has 22 operational reactors. The United States leads not only in the number of reactors but also in installed capacity. This reflects the country's long-term investment and research in nuclear energy. Although China is rapidly expanding its nuclear fleet, the US currently holds the top position in terms of operational reactors.
qs.kf:
☛ Country with most operational nuclear reactors → United States (93)
☛ Second most operational reactors → France (56)
☛ Rapidly expanding nuclear capacity nation → China
☛ Number of operational reactors in India → 22
☛ Top country in global nuclear power generation → United States

name: Set 3 · Q95–141
sub: Static GK - Geography, States, Places & Heritage

q: Murudeshwar Temple is situated on Kanduka Giri in the state of_____
qs.e: The Murudeshwar Temple is located on Kanduka Giri hill in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka state, India. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, it features the world's second tallest Shiva statue (123 feet). The temple was originally built by Queen Chennammaji and later renovated. It is situated on the coast of the Arabian Sea and has a 20-story gopuram (entrance tower). The temple is not only a major Hindu pilgrimage site but also a popular tourist destination due to its architectural grandeur and scenic location.
qs.kf:
☛ Murudeshwar Temple is located in which state? → Karnataka
☛ Murudeshwar Temple is situated on which hill? → Kanduka Giri
☛ Height of Murudeshwar Shiva statue? → 123 feet
☛ Murudeshwar Temple is on the coast of which sea? → Arabian Sea
☛ Murudeshwar gopuram has how many stories? → 20

q: Forest Research Institute of India is located at_______
qs.e: The Forest Research Institute (FRI) of India is located at Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It was established in 1906 as the Imperial Forest Research Institute. It functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India. FRI was granted deemed university status in 1991. The institute is renowned for research in forestry science, forest management, and forest products. Its historic building is an example of British colonial architecture and has been declared a monument of national importance.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Forest Research Institute → Dehradun
☛ Year of establishment → 1906
☛ Administrative control → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Deemed university status granted → 1991
☛ Main research areas → Forestry science, forest management

q: Which of the following is a garrison town?
qs.e: A garrison town is a place where military troops are permanently stationed. In India, Jalandhar is a prominent garrison town with important Indian Army units located there. It is situated in the state of Punjab and holds strategic military importance. Kota in Rajasthan is known as an educational hub, Surat is a major commercial city in Gujarat, and Udaipur is a tourist destination. Among these options, only Jalandhar is recognized as a garrison town.
qs.kf:
☛ Major garrison town in India → Jalandhar
☛ Jalandhar is in which state → Punjab
☛ Garrison town is known for → Permanent army deployment
☛ Kota is famous for → Education hub
☛ Another garrison town in India → Ambala

q: Which of the following country follow more than one time zones?
qs.e: The USA follows more than one time zone. Due to its vast geographical expanse, it uses a total of 6 time zones: Eastern, Central, Mountain, Pacific, Alaska, and Hawaii-Aleutian. In contrast, China follows a single time zone (China Standard Time), India uses one time zone (IST), and Argentina also uses a single time zone (ART). Other countries like Russia, Canada, and Australia also follow multiple time zones. The time zone system in the USA is divided according to states and territories, reflecting its administrative and geographical divisions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country has the most time zones? → France (12 time zones)
☛ How many time zones does Russia follow? → 11 time zones
☛ What is China's standard time zone? → China Standard Time (UTC+8)
☛ What is India's time zone? → Indian Standard Time (UTC+5:30)
☛ What is Argentina's time zone? → Argentina Time (UTC-3)

q: Where is INS Sardar Patel Naval Base located?
qs.e: INS Sardar Patel Naval Base is located in Porbandar, Gujarat. This is an important base of the Indian Navy, named after Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Home Minister of India. The base holds strategic significance along the Gujarat coast and strengthens the Navy's presence in the western maritime region. INS Sardar Patel is primarily used for maritime patrol, search and rescue operations. It serves as a base for naval ships and aircraft.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is INS Sardar Patel located? → Porbandar, Gujarat
☛ After whom is INS Sardar Patel named? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Which state is Porbandar in? → Gujarat
☛ Where is the Indian Navy Headquarters? → New Delhi
☛ Who was India's first woman naval officer? → Captain Radhika Menon

q: India has been celebrating _______ as 'National Consumer Day'.
qs.e: India celebrates December 24 as 'National Consumer Day' every year. This day marks the enactment of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, which received the President's assent on December 24, 1986. The day aims to raise awareness about consumer rights and protect consumers from unfair trade practices. India's consumer protection law is one of the most comprehensive in the world. It is observed through awareness campaigns and programs to educate consumers.
qs.kf:
☛ When is National Consumer Day celebrated? → December 24
☛ When was the Consumer Protection Act passed? → 1986
☛ When did the Consumer Protection Act receive the President's assent? → December 24, 1986
☛ How many consumer rights are there in India? → 6
☛ When is World Consumer Rights Day celebrated? → March 15

q: Masai castes are from which of the following countries?
qs.e: The Masai tribe is primarily found in Kenya and Tanzania. They are a semi-nomadic community dependent on cattle herding. The Maasai are known for their unique culture, traditional attire, and warrior traditions. Their language, Maa, belongs to the Nilo-Saharan language family. Maasai society is structured around an age-set system, where young men undergo initiation to become warriors. Currently, the Maasai face challenges of modernization and land rights issues.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country is home to the Maasai tribe? → Kenya and Tanzania
☛ What is the main occupation of the Maasai? → Cattle herding
☛ Which language family does the Maasai language belong to? → Nilo-Saharan
☛ What system is important in Maasai society? → Age-set system
☛ What is the traditional Maasai dwelling called? → Boma

q: Which of the following countries was formerly known as Formosa?
qs.e: Formosa is the historical name for Taiwan, given by Portuguese explorers in the 16th century. The name 'Ilha Formosa' means 'beautiful island' in Portuguese. Taiwan is an island country in East Asia with Taipei as its capital. It was the main territory of the Republic of China from 1912 until 1949, when the Chinese Civil War led to the Communist Party taking over mainland China, while Taiwan retained its own government. Today, Taiwan is considered a sovereign state despite China's claims. South Korea, China, and Japan were never known as Formosa.
qs.kf:
☛ Who gave the name Formosa? → Portuguese explorers
☛ What does Formosa mean? → Beautiful island
☛ What is the capital of Taiwan? → Taipei
☛ Which war separated Taiwan from China? → Chinese Civil War (1949)
☛ Which party ruled Taiwan after 1949? → Republic of China (Kuomintang)

q: Which of the following states/UT of India has summer and winter capital?
qs.e: Jammu and Kashmir is a Union Territory of India with two capitals: Srinagar as the summer capital and Jammu as the winter capital. This arrangement is due to the region's geographical and climatic diversity. During summer, administrative offices move to Srinagar, while in winter they operate from Jammu. This practice dates back to the British era. Other states like Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand also have similar systems, but Jammu and Kashmir's dual capitals are more prominent. Sikkim, West Bengal, and Rajasthan have single capitals.
qs.kf:
☛ Summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir → Srinagar
☛ Winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir → Jammu
☛ Summer capital of Himachal Pradesh → Shimla
☛ Winter capital of Himachal Pradesh → Dharamshala
☛ Summer capital of Uttarakhand → Gairsain (Bhararisain)

q: Which of the following states is situated at the pilgrimage point of pilgrim center?
qs.e: Thirthasthal is a famous Hindu pilgrimage site located in the state of Assam, India. It is situated on the banks of the Brahmaputra River and is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. The site is known for its architecture and religious significance. Thirthasthal is mentioned in ancient texts and is an important part of Assamese culture. The other options include Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, and Nagaland, which are not associated with the location of Thirthasthal.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Thirthasthal located? → Assam
☛ On which river bank is Thirthasthal situated? → Brahmaputra
☛ Thirthasthal is dedicated to which deity? → Lord Vishnu
☛ What is the capital of Assam? → Dispur
☛ What is the largest city of Assam? → Guwahati

q: Which Indian state is inhabited by the Atmani tribe?
qs.e: The Atmani tribe is found in Madhya Pradesh, primarily in Guna and Shivpuri districts. They are also known as 'Atmani' or 'Amani' and belong to the Proto-Australoid ethnic group. Their language, Atmani, is part of the Austric language family. The tribe is recognized as a Scheduled Tribe by the Government of India. Agriculture and daily wage labor are their main occupations. The Atmani tribe is one of the smaller tribal communities in Madhya Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is home to the Atmani tribe? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ What is the main language of the Atmani tribe? → Atmani (Austric family)
☛ Which ethnic group does the Atmani tribe belong to? → Proto-Australoid
☛ What are the major tribes of Madhya Pradesh? → Gond, Bhil, Korku, Atmani, etc.
☛ What is the main occupation of the Atmani tribe? → Agriculture and labor

q: What is the capital of the Hawai Islands?
qs.e: The Hawai Islands are a state of the United States located in the Pacific Ocean. Its capital and largest city is Honolulu, situated on the island of Oahu. Honolulu means 'sheltered harbor' in the Hawaiian language. The state comprises eight main islands: Hawaiʻi (the Big Island), Maui, Oahu, Kauai, Molokai, Lanai, Niihau, and Kahoolawe. Honolulu is also known for Pearl Harbor, where a Japanese attack occurred in 1941. The city is a major center for tourism and military activities.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the capital of Hawai Islands? → Honolulu
☛ Which is the largest island in Hawai? → Hawaiʻi (Big Island)
☛ What are the official languages of Hawai? → English and Hawaiian
☛ In which ocean is Hawai located? → Pacific Ocean
☛ Where is Pearl Harbor located? → Honolulu, Hawai

q: Muscat is the capital of which of the following countries?
qs.e: Muscat is the capital of Oman, located on the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula. It is Oman's largest city and a major port. Historically, Muscat was an important trading hub. Other options: Yemen's capital is Sana'a, United Arab Emirates' capital is Abu Dhabi, and Saudi Arabia's capital is Riyadh. Thus, Oman is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Saudi Arabia → Riyadh
☛ Capital of Yemen → Sana'a
☛ Capital of United Arab Emirates → Abu Dhabi
☛ Currency of Oman → Omani Rial
☛ Muscat is located on which gulf → Gulf of Oman

q: Basilica of Bom Jesus, a world heritage site, is located.
qs.e: Basilica of Bom Jesus is a famous church located in Goa, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This church is renowned for preserving the remains of Saint Francis Xavier. It was built between 1594 and 1605 during the Portuguese rule. The architecture is an excellent example of Baroque style. The Basilica of Bom Jesus is situated in Old Goa area, known for its churches and historical significance. It attracts many pilgrims and tourists every year.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Basilica of Bom Jesus located? → Goa
☛ What architectural style is the Basilica of Bom Jesus built in? → Baroque style
☛ Whose remains are preserved in Basilica of Bom Jesus? → Saint Francis Xavier
☛ During which rule was Basilica of Bom Jesus built? → Portuguese rule
☛ Is Basilica of Bom Jesus a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → Yes

q: What do you mean by an atheist state?
qs.e: An atheist state refers to a state that does not recognize any religion officially and remains neutral in religious matters. It differs from a secular state because a secular state respects all religions equally, while an atheist state opposes or discourages religion. For example, communist countries like the former Soviet Union and China promoted state atheism. In such a state, religious activities may be restricted or controlled. The concept of an atheist state is based on the complete separation of religion and state, where the state rejects religion.
qs.kf:
☛ Main principle of an atheist state → Complete separation of religion from state
☛ Religious freedom in an atheist state → Limited or prohibited
☛ Secular state vs atheist state → Secular respects all religions; atheist opposes religion
☛ Example → Former Soviet Union
☛ Goal of an atheist state → Eliminate the influence of religion

q: In which city is the "Hawa Mahal" located?
qs.e: Hawa Mahal is a famous historical monument located in Jaipur, the capital city of Rajasthan. It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh. Known as the 'Palace of Winds', it is a unique five-story structure made of red and pink sandstone. The palace features 953 small latticed windows (jharokhas) that allow cool air to circulate, giving it the name 'Hawa Mahal'. It is situated at the main entrance of the City Palace and extends directly to the Zenana Deodi (women's chambers). The Hawa Mahal is an excellent example of Rajput architecture and is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Jaipur.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Hawa Mahal? → Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh

q: Where is the famous 'Cellular Jail' located?
qs.e: The famous Cellular Jail (Kala Pani) is located in Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It was built by the British between 1896 and 1906 to imprison Indian freedom fighters. The jail has seven wings radiating from a central tower, giving it a cellular appearance. Notable prisoners include Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, Batukeshwar Dutt, and many other revolutionaries. Today, it serves as a national memorial and is open to tourists. The jail symbolizes the brutal colonial repression and the sacrifices of Indian freedom fighters.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Cellular Jail completed? → 1906
☛ Who designed the Cellular Jail? → Colonel Thomas Frederick
☛ How many cells are in the Cellular Jail? → 698
☛ Why is Cellular Jail called 'Kala Pani'? → Because it is a remote island surrounded by sea
☛ What is the Cellular Jail today? → A national memorial

q: Which of the following is a hot air?
qs.e: Harmaton is a hot and dry wind that blows along the coast of West Africa. It originates from the Sahara Desert and flows towards the Guinea coast, significantly raising temperatures. In contrast, Mistral is a cold wind in France, Santa Carna is a warm but humid wind in South America, and a blizzard is a cold storm. Therefore, Harmaton is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Harmaton is a hot wind of which region? → West Africa
☛ Mistral is a cold wind of which country? → France
☛ Santa Carna is a warm wind of which continent? → South America
☛ What type of wind is a blizzard? → Cold
☛ Where does Harmaton originate? → Sahara Desert

q: What is that simple tool that is used to remove weeds and loosen the soil?
qs.e: The hoe is a simple agricultural tool used to remove weeds and loosen the soil. It is also known as a khuppa or khurpi. It consists of a long wooden handle with a metal blade attached at a right angle. Hoes are primarily used in small farms and gardening. They help in weed control and soil aeration by cutting weeds and stirring the soil. Farmers use hoes to remove grass between crops and make the soil friable. Other options: Cultivator (a farm implement for tilling), Planters (used for planting seeds), and Sickle (used for harvesting crops) are incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Simplest tool for weed removal → Hoe
☛ Use of hoe → Removing weeds and loosening soil
☛ Other names of hoe → Khurpi, Khuppa
☛ Parts of hoe → Wooden handle and metal blade
☛ Main area of hoe use → Small farms and gardening

q: In which state the eulk sari was born?
qs.e: The Eulk Sari is associated with the state of Karnataka. It is a traditional silk saree primarily woven in the Mysore and Dharwad regions. The Eulk Sari is known for its fine weave, lightweight feel, and glossy texture. It is made from threads obtained from silkworms. This saree is considered a symbol of Karnataka's identity and is part of the state's cultural heritage. Traditionally, the Eulk Sari is handwoven and worn on special occasions.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is the origin of Eulk Sari? → Karnataka
☛ In which regions of Karnataka is Eulk Sari mainly woven? → Mysore and Dharwad
☛ What is the Eulk Sari made of? → Silk threads from silkworms
☛ What is a key feature of Eulk Sari? → Fine weave and lightweight
☛ What is the significance of Eulk Sari? → Cultural identity of Karnataka

q: The Hindustan Antibiotics Limited Factory is located in ________.
qs.e: Hindustan Antibiotics Limited is India's first antibiotic production unit, established in 1954 at Pimpri-Chinchwad, Pune. It is a public sector undertaking and is renowned for the production of medicines like penicillin. The company played a crucial role in making India self-reliant in antibiotic drugs. The plant is located in the state of Maharashtra.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Hindustan Antibiotics Limited established? → 1954
☛ What type of enterprise is it? → Public sector undertaking
☛ Where is it located? → Pimpri-Chinchwad, Pune
☛ Which drug is it famous for producing? → Penicillin
☛ In which state is it located? → Maharashtra

q: Which of the following is the largest waterfall in the world?
qs.e: Angel Falls is the highest waterfall in the world, located in Venezuela. Its total height is about 979 meters (3,212 feet), with a continuous drop of 807 meters (2,648 feet). It is named after Jimmy Angel, an American pilot who discovered the falls in 1933. The falls are situated in Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Angel Falls is famous for its immense height and natural beauty. Among other options, Yosemite Falls (USA) is 739 meters, Brown Falls (New Zealand) is 836 meters, and Noah's waterfall is not a major waterfall.
qs.kf:
☛ World's highest waterfall → Angel Falls (Venezuela)
☛ Total height of Angel Falls → 979 meters
☛ Continuous drop height → 807 meters
☛ Discoverer → Jimmy Angel (1933)
☛ National Park → Canaima National Park (UNESCO)

q: What is the State bird of Assam?
qs.e: The state bird of Assam is the White-winged Wood Duck, scientifically known as Asarcornis scutulata. This rare species is found in the Brahmaputra Valley and surrounding wetland areas of Assam. It inhabits forest streams, ponds, and swamps. Conservation efforts are carried out by the state government and various organizations to protect this endangered bird. Other options include Parrot, Swan, and Owl, but none of these are the state bird of Assam.
qs.kf:
☛ State bird of Assam → White-winged Wood Duck
☛ State animal of Assam → One-horned Rhinoceros
☛ State flower of Assam → Kopou Phul (Foxtail Orchid)
☛ State tree of Assam → Hollong (Artocarpus chapalasha)
☛ Capital of Assam → Dispur

q: What is the capital of Afghanistan?
qs.e: The capital of Afghanistan is Kabul. It is the largest city of the country and serves as its economic, cultural, and political center. Situated along the Kabul River, the city has historically been a significant hub. Afghanistan is located in South Asia and shares borders with Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and China. Its currency is the Afghani and its official languages are Pashto and Dari. Kabul lies at an elevation of about 1,790 meters above sea level.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest city of Afghanistan → Kabul
☛ Official languages of Afghanistan → Pashto and Dari
☛ Currency of Afghanistan → Afghani
☛ Neighboring countries of Afghanistan → Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, China
☛ River on which Kabul is located → Kabul River

q: Which is the capital city of Nagaland?
qs.e: The capital city of Nagaland is Kohima. It is the largest city in the state and serves as the administrative headquarters. Kohima is known for its natural beauty, war history, and the Hornbill Festival. The city is situated on the banks of the Doyang River (often referred to as Dhansiri in some contexts). Nagaland has 16 districts, with Kohima, Dimapur, and Mokokchung being major ones. Kohima is often called the 'City of Hills'. The predominant language spoken here is Angami Naga. The old name of Kohima was Kewhira. In 1878, the British established a garrison here. Kohima is also famous for the Kohima War Cemetery from World War II.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Nagaland → Kohima
☛ River of Nagaland → Doyang (Dhansiri)
☛ Famous festival of Nagaland → Hornbill Festival
☛ Old name of Kohima → Kewhira
☛ Total districts in Nagaland → 16

q: Which country is known as the "Land of the rising sun"?
qs.e: Japan is known as the "Land of the Rising Sun" because the Japanese name for the country, "Nippon" or "Nihon", means "origin of the sun". This name reflects Japan's eastern location relative to China, from where the sun appears to rise. Japan is an island nation located in the Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Tokyo, and it is famous for its technological advancement, rich culture, and natural beauty. The national flag of Japan also depicts the sun.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Japan → Tokyo
☛ Currency of Japan → Yen
☛ National sport of Japan → Sumo wrestling
☛ Highest mountain in Japan → Mount Fuji
☛ Type of government in Japan → Constitutional monarchy

q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
qs.e: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam and the second-largest city in the country. It is located in the northern part of Vietnam in the Red River Delta region. Hanoi serves as the political, cultural, and educational center of Vietnam. It was founded in 1010 AD by Emperor Ly Thai To. Ho Chi Minh City is the largest city and economic hub, but Hanoi is the capital. Hanoi is home to many historical sites such as Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, One Pillar Pagoda, and Hoan Kiem Lake.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Vietnam → Hanoi
☛ Largest city of Vietnam → Ho Chi Minh City
☛ Hanoi founded in → 1010 AD
☛ Currency of Vietnam → Vietnamese Dong (VND)
☛ Countries bordering Vietnam → China, Laos, Cambodia

q: Which is the capital city of Arunachal Pradesh?
qs.e: The capital city of Arunachal Pradesh is Itanagar. It is located in the southeastern part of the state and derives its name from 'Ita' (brick) and 'nagar' (city). Itanagar was declared the capital of Arunachal Pradesh in 1974. The city is situated at the foothills of the Himalayas and has a subtropical climate. It houses important government buildings such as the Legislative Assembly, Raj Bhavan, and the State Museum. Teju, Tawang, and Rowing are other prominent towns in the state, but Itanagar is the capital.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar
☛ Itanagar became capital in → 1974
☛ Largest city of Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar
☛ Itanagar name derived from → brick and city

q: Which is the national tree of India?
qs.e: The national tree of India is the Banyan Tree (Ficus benghalensis), which holds immense cultural and religious significance. Its expansive branches and aerial roots symbolize immortality and long life. The banyan tree is often associated with wisdom and is revered in Indian traditions. It was declared the national tree in 1950 for its deep-rooted presence in Indian heritage and ecology.

☛ Scientific name of Banyan → Ficus benghalensis
☛ Year declared national tree → 1950
☛ Family of Banyan → Moraceae

q: In which state is the Ondantpuri University located?
qs.e: Ondantpuri University is located in the state of Bihar. This university is associated with Jainism and is known as a center for Jain education. Ondantpuri is an ancient site situated in the Lakhisarai district of Bihar. This place is famous as a Jain pilgrimage and houses Jain temples and educational institutions. The name Ondantpuri reflects the historical significance of the region. It is one of the prominent Jain educational institutions in India.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Ondantpuri University located? → Bihar
☛ Ondantpuri is associated with which religion? → Jainism

☛ Which is a major Jain educational institution in India? → Ondantpuri University

q: What is the capital of Japan?
qs.e: The capital of Japan is Tokyo, a major city located in East Asia. It serves as the economic, cultural, and political center of Japan. Tokyo officially became the capital after the Meiji Restoration in 1868, replacing Kyoto. It is the most populous metropolitan area in the world, with approximately 37 million residents. The city is known for blending modernity and tradition and is home to many international organizations.
qs.kf:

☛ Currency of Japan → Yen
☛ Highest mountain in Japan → Mount Fuji
☛ Largest island of Japan → Honshu

q: What is the capital of Spain?
qs.e: The capital of Spain is Madrid, located in the central part of the country. It is the largest city in Spain and serves as the political, economic, and cultural hub. Madrid became the capital in 1561 under King Philip II. Among the other options, Barcelona, Seville, and Grenada are important cities but not the capital. Madrid is one of the most visited cities in the world, known for its art museums, architecture, and vibrant culture.
qs.kf:

☛ When did Madrid become the capital of Spain? → 1561
☛ What is the largest city in Spain? → Madrid
☛ Which Spanish city is a major port? → Barcelona
☛ What is the national sport of Spain? → Football

q: Which among the following was declared the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
qs.e: Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956 on linguistic basis. After the bifurcation of Telangana in 2014, Andhra Pradesh needed a new capital. In 2015, the state government declared Amravati as the capital. It is located in Guntur district and lies on the banks of the Krishna River. Its name is inspired by the ancient Amravati Stupa, an important Buddhist center. The capital region also includes Vijayawada and Guntur cities. Amravati is being developed as a smart city.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the capital of Andhra Pradesh? → Amravati
☛ On which river is Amravati located? → Krishna River
☛ What is the ancient name of Amravati? → Dhanyakataka
☛ Amravati is in which district? → Guntur district
☛ Which was the former capital of Andhra Pradesh? → Hyderabad (1956-2014)

q: Which is the capital of the Netherlands?
qs.e: The capital of the Netherlands is Amsterdam, although the government and parliament are located in The Hague. Amsterdam is the largest city in the country and serves as its economic and cultural hub. It is famous for its canals, museums, and historic buildings. The other options: VLANTA is a fictional name, Rotterdam is a major port city but not the capital, and Port Louis is the capital of Mauritius. The name Amsterdam is derived from the dam on the Amstel River.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Netherlands → Amsterdam
☛ Location of parliament in Netherlands → The Hague
☛ Currency of Netherlands → Euro
☛ Official language of Netherlands → Dutch
☛ Major port of Netherlands → Rotterdam

q: Which is the capital of Turkey?
qs.e: The capital of Turkey is Ankara, located in the central part of the country. After the establishment of the Turkish Republic in 1923, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk moved the capital from Istanbul to Ankara. Ankara is the second-largest city in Turkey and serves as the administrative and political center, housing the Turkish parliament, presidential palace, and major government offices. Historically, Ankara was also known as Angora.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the currency of Turkey? → Turkish Lira
☛ Which continent is Turkey located in? → Asia and Europe (Eurasia)
☛ Who is the current President of Turkey? → Recep Tayyip Erdogan
☛ What is the largest city in Turkey? → Istanbul
☛ What is the official language of Turkey? → Turkish

q: What is the capital of Uruguay?
qs.e: Uruguay is a country in South America, and its capital is Montevideo. It is also the largest city and chief port of the country, located on the northern bank of Rio de la Plata. Montevideo serves as the economic, cultural, and administrative center of Uruguay. Uruguay borders Brazil to the north and Argentina to the west. The official language of Uruguay is Spanish. The country is known for its stable democracy and high standard of living compared to other South American nations. Football is the most popular sport in Uruguay.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the currency of Uruguay? → Uruguayan peso
☛ What is the largest city of Uruguay? → Montevideo
☛ What is the official language of Uruguay? → Spanish

☛ Which countries border Uruguay? → Brazil and Argentina

q: Which of the following countries has the highest rank of Human Development Index?
qs.e: The Human Development Index (HDI) is released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It ranks countries based on three dimensions: life expectancy, education, and per capita income. Norway consistently holds the top rank in HDI, while Cuba, Pakistan, and India are ranked lower respectively. Norway's high standard of living, strong social security, and quality education keep it at the top. In the 2022 report, Norway's HDI value was 0.966.

☛ Dimensions of HDI → Health, Education, Income
☛ Top country in 2022 HDI → Norway
