☛ Largest pyramid at Giza → Pyramid of Khufu
☛ Height of Khufu's pyramid → Approximately 146.6 meters
☛ Construction period of Khufu's pyramid → 2560 BCE
☛ Three main pyramids of Egypt → Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure
☛ Alternate name of Khufu's pyramid → Great Pyramid of Giza

q: Name the cyclone that hit Odisha and West Bengal in May 2020.
qs.e: The cyclone that hit Odisha and West Bengal in May 2020 was named Amphan. It was an extremely powerful tropical cyclone originating from the Bay of Bengal. It made landfall on the coast of West Bengal on 20 May 2020, causing extensive damage. Amphan was classified as a Category 5 cyclone, with wind speeds reaching up to 260 km/h. It caused widespread destruction in Kolkata and surrounding areas. The name Amphan was contributed by Thailand.
qs.kf:
☛ Cyclone that hit Odisha and West Bengal in 2020 → Amphan
☛ Category of Cyclone Amphan → Category 5
☛ Maximum wind speed of Amphan → 260 km/h
☛ Country that named Amphan → Thailand
☛ Indian states affected by Amphan → Odisha and West Bengal

q: As per flag code of India 2002, What should be the position of the Indian flag when it is displayed along with flags of other countries in a straight line?
qs.e: India's national flag holds the highest position among all national symbols. According to the Flag Code of India 2002, when the Indian flag is displayed along with flags of other countries in a straight line, it must be placed at the extreme right end of the row. This position is considered the most honorable because, in parades and formal displays, the right side is leading. The flag should also be kept at the same height or higher than other flags. This rule reflects India's sovereignty and dignity. The code was enacted on 26 January 2002 and is legally binding under the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950.
qs.kf:
☛ Which section of the Flag Code 2002 deals with the position of flags? → Section 4.11
☛ Where is the Indian flag placed when displayed with other national flags in a row? → Extreme right
☛ If there is an odd number of flags in a row, where is the Indian flag placed? → Extreme right
☛ What is the height rule for the Indian flag relative to other flags? → Same or higher
☛ When did the Flag Code of India 2002 come into effect? → 26 January 2002

q: Which of the following state has the highest wind energy production in India?
qs.e: Tamil Nadu has the highest wind energy production in India. The state's total installed wind power capacity is over 10,000 MW, which is the largest share of the country's total wind energy. It is followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra. Major wind farms in Tamil Nadu include Muppandal and Kayathar. The state's geographical location and high wind speeds in coastal areas make it ideal for wind energy generation. According to the National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE), Tamil Nadu leads in wind power production.
qs.kf:
☛ State with highest wind energy production in India → Tamil Nadu
☛ Major wind farms in Tamil Nadu → Muppandal and Kayathar
☛ Second largest wind energy producer → Gujarat
☛ Second in installed wind capacity → Maharashtra
☛ Agency responsible for wind energy in India → National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE)

q: Which of the following is NOT a world heritage site?
qs.e: Periyar National Park, located in Kerala, is a significant wildlife sanctuary but is not recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In contrast, Kaziranga National Park (Assam), Manas Wildlife Sanctuary (Assam), and Nanda Devi National Park (Uttarakhand) are all UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Kaziranga, famous for its one-horned rhinoceros, was designated a World Heritage Site in 1985. Manas Wildlife Sanctuary received World Heritage status in 1985, while Nanda Devi National Park was inscribed in 1988. Periyar National Park is known for its elephant and tiger populations, but it is not on the World Heritage list.
qs.kf:
☛ Kaziranga is famous for which animal? → One-horned rhinoceros
☛ Manas Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which state? → Assam
☛ Nanda Devi National Park is located in which state? → Uttarakhand
☛ Periyar National Park is located in which state? → Kerala
☛ How many World Heritage Sites are in India as of 2024? → 42

q: The first livestock census in India was conducted during:
qs.e: The first livestock census in India was conducted in the year 1919-1920. This census was initiated to assess the status and number of livestock in the country. Subsequently, livestock censuses have been conducted at regular intervals. Currently, the census is conducted every 5 years by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries (DAHD). The 20th Livestock Census was conducted in 2019. The first census mainly included animals such as cattle, buffalo, goat, sheep, pig, horse, camel, etc.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first livestock census in India? → 1919-1920
☛ Which year was the 20th Livestock Census conducted? → 2019
☛ Which department conducts the livestock census? → DAHD (Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries)
☛ What is the interval of livestock census? → 5 years
☛ Which animals were included in the first livestock census? → Cattle, buffalo, goat, sheep, pig, horse, camel, etc.

q: Which of the following countries is the largest producer of gold in the world in 2019?
qs.e: In 2019, China was the world's largest producer of gold. Since 2007, China has maintained this position, surpassing South Africa. China's annual gold production has been around 380-400 tonnes. It is followed by Australia and Russia. India is a major consumer of gold but not a top producer. South Africa, once the largest producer, has seen a decline in output and is no longer in the top three. Thus, China is the correct answer as the leading gold producer in 2019.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest gold producer (2019) → China
☛ Second largest gold producer (2019) → Australia
☛ Largest gold consumer country → India
☛ When did China overtake South Africa? → 2007
☛ Top gold producing countries → China, Australia, Russia, USA

q: Which architect designed the Gateway of India located at Mumbai?
qs.e: The Gateway of India is a historic monument located in Mumbai, built during the British Raj in 1911. Its design was prepared by George Wittet, a British architect. The monument is built in the Indo-Saracenic style, blending Gujarati and Mughal architectural elements. Its construction was completed in 1924 and it was built to commemorate the visit of King George V to India. The Gateway of India is made of basalt and concrete and stands at a height of 26 meters. It is one of the major tourist attractions in Mumbai.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Gateway of India inaugurated? → 1924
☛ What style is the Gateway of India built in? → Indo-Saracenic
☛ What is the height of the Gateway of India? → 26 meters
☛ Who designed the Gateway of India? → George Wittet
☛ Where is the Gateway of India located? → Mumbai

q: National Testing Agency (NTA) was established in the year _______ to Conduct entrance examinations.
qs.e: The National Testing Agency (NTA) was established in 2017 by the Government of India as an autonomous organization. Its primary objective is to conduct major entrance examinations for admission to higher education institutions. NTA now oversees exams like JEE Main, NEET UG, and UGC NET. It first conducted JEE Main and UGC NET in 2018. NTA was formed under the Ministry of Education to ensure a transparent, fair, and efficient examination process. Its headquarters is in New Delhi.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NTA established? → 2017
☛ Which major exams does NTA conduct? → JEE Main, NEET UG, UGC NET
☛ Where is NTA headquarters located? → New Delhi
☛ When did NTA first conduct exams? → 2018
☛ Under which ministry does NTA function? → Ministry of Education

q: What is the name of India's first Railway University?
o: Institute of Rail Management of India
qs.e: India's first railway university is the National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI), established in 2018 at Vadodara, Gujarat. It is the first university in the country dedicated entirely to education, training, and research in the railway and transportation sector. Founded by the Ministry of Railways, it aims to prepare skilled professionals for the Indian Railways and promote innovation in the transportation field. The institute offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs covering subjects such as railway management, signaling, telecommunications, electrification, and civil engineering. It plays a crucial role in the modernization of Indian Railways and the development of world-class infrastructure.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first Railway University → National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI)
☛ Year of establishment → 2018
☛ Location → Vadodara, Gujarat
☛ Affiliation → Ministry of Railways
☛ Courses offered → Railway management, engineering, and research

q: The Konark Temple is situated in which state?
qs.e: The Konark Sun Temple is located in the state of Odisha, India, in the town of Konark near Puri. It was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I. The temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its design resembles a giant chariot with 12 pairs of wheels and 7 horses.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Konark Temple? → King Narasimhadeva I
☛ Which architectural style is the Konark Temple built in? → Kalinga style
☛ Which deity is the Konark Temple dedicated to? → Sun God
☛ In which year was Konark Temple declared a UNESCO site? → 1984
☛ On the bank of which river is Konark Temple located? → Chandrabhaga River

q: The Rail Coach Factory (RFC) is located in which city of Punjab?
qs.e: The Rail Coach Factory (RFC) is located in Kapurthala city of Punjab. It was established in 1986 and operates under Indian Railways. This factory is primarily known for manufacturing, repairing, and maintaining passenger coaches. It is one of the most important railway units in the state of Punjab. Kapurthala is famous for railway coach production and supplies coaches across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Rail Coach Factory located? → Kapurthala, Punjab
☛ When was RFC established? → 1986
☛ RFC comes under which organization? → Indian Railways
☛ Which railway unit is in Kapurthala? → Rail Coach Factory
☛ What are major coach factories in India? → Kapurthala, Chennai, Bangalore

q: Which of the following is NOT a correct statement?
o: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area.
Sikkim is the least populous state in India.
The state of Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014
qs.e: The capital of Mizoram is Aizawl, not Kohima. Kohima is the capital of Nagaland. Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area. Sikkim is the least populous state in India. Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014. These three statements are correct. Therefore, the incorrect statement is that the capital of Mizoram is Kohima.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Mizoram → Aizawl
☛ Capital of Nagaland → Kohima
☛ Largest Indian state by area → Rajasthan
☛ Least populous state in India → Sikkim
☛ Telangana formation date → 2 June 2014

q: Where will you find the ‘Forbidden City’?
qs.e: The Forbidden City is located in Beijing, the capital of China. It is a historic palace complex built between 1406 and 1420 during the Ming Dynasty. For over 500 years, it served as the imperial residence and political center of Chinese emperors. The name 'Forbidden' originated because commoners were prohibited from entering. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest palace complexes in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Forbidden City located? → Beijing, China
☛ Which dynasty built the Forbidden City? → Ming Dynasty
☛ When was the Forbidden City constructed? → 1406–1420 AD
☛ What is its UNESCO designation? → World Heritage Site
☛ What was the Forbidden City used for? → Imperial residence of Chinese emperors

q: The Brihadisvara temple is in which state of India?
qs.e: The Brihadisvara temple is located in the state of Tamil Nadu, in the city of Thanjavur. It was built by Raja Raja Chola I in 1010 CE. This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is one of the tallest temples made of granite, with a vimana (tower) height of about 66 meters. A notable feature is that the shadow of the vimana never falls on the ground. The temple is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture and is also known as the Thanjavur Brihadisvara Temple.
qs.kf:
☛ On which river is the Brihadisvara temple located? → Kaveri River
☛ Who built the Brihadisvara temple? → Raja Raja Chola I
☛ To which deity is Brihadisvara temple dedicated? → Lord Shiva
☛ What architectural style is Brihadisvara temple? → Dravidian style
☛ What is the main shrine of Brihadisvara temple called? → Vimanam

q: Which of the following principal organs of the United Nations is NOT situated in New York?
qs.e: The United Nations has six principal organs: the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council, Secretariat, and the International Court of Justice. Five of these are located in New York, but the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is situated in The Hague, Netherlands. It is the primary judicial organ of the UN, established in 1945. The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected by the General Assembly and Security Council for nine-year terms. It settles legal disputes between states and provides advisory opinions on international law. The court's decisions are binding on the parties involved, and it plays a crucial role in peaceful resolution of conflicts.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of ICJ → The Hague, Netherlands
☛ Number of principal organs of UN → Six
☛ Term of ICJ judges → 9 years
☛ Number of ICJ judges → 15
☛ Establishment year of ICJ → 1945

q: Which of the following tribes belongs to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
qs.e: The Sentinelese tribe inhabits the North Sentinel Island of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. They are one of the most isolated tribes in the world, with almost no contact with outsiders. Their livelihood depends on hunting and gathering. The Indian government follows a policy of non-interference to protect them. Other options: Kharwar is found in Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, Bhil in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, and Gond in central India.
qs.kf:
☛ Where do the Sentinelese tribe live? → North Sentinel Island (Andaman & Nicobar)
☛ Which is the most isolated tribe in India? → Sentinelese
☛ Where is the Kharwar tribe found? → Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand
☛ Which region is associated with the Bhil tribe? → Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat
☛ Where does the Gond tribe reside? → Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra

q: Cheraw, popularly known as bamboo dance, is a traditional cultural dance of which state?
qs.e: Cheraw, popularly known as the bamboo dance, is a traditional cultural dance of Mizoram. It is performed by the Mizo tribe using bamboo staves. Dancers step in and out of the bamboo sticks that are clapped together rhythmically. This dance is usually performed during festivals and special occasions. It involves both men and women and is a group dance. Cheraw represents the rich cultural heritage of Mizoram and is widely recognized across India.
qs.kf:
☛ Cheraw dance is associated with which state? → Mizoram
☛ What is the other name of bamboo dance? → Cheraw
☛ Which is the main folk dance of Mizoram? → Cheraw
☛ What instrument is used in Cheraw dance? → Bamboo staves
☛ Bamboo dance in India is associated with which tribe? → Mizo tribe

q: India's First Marine park is situated in:
qs.e: India's first marine park is located in the Gulf of Kutch in the state of Gujarat. It was established in the year 1980 and is known as the Marine National Park. The park spans along the coast of Jamnagar district and includes 42 islands. It is famous for its biodiversity, including mangroves, coral reefs, and dolphins. The Gulf of Mannar has the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, but it was established later. Chennai does not have a marine park. Hence, the correct answer is Gulf of Kutch.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first marine park → Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat)
☛ Year of establishment → 1980
☛ Other name → Marine National Park
☛ Area → approx. 162 sq km
☛ Key feature → Coral reefs and mangroves

q: Which of the following museum is situated in Kerala?
qs.e: Napier Museum is a renowned museum located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India. Established in 1855, it is named after Francis Napier, the Governor of Madras Presidency. The museum houses a rich collection of artifacts, sculptures, paintings, and historical objects showcasing the cultural heritage of South India. It is also famous for its unique architectural style blending Kerala, Chinese, and Mughal influences. Other options: Salar Jung Museum is in Hyderabad (Telangana), Albert Hall Museum is in Jaipur (Rajasthan), and Dakshinachitra Museum is in Chennai (Tamil Nadu). Thus, Napier Museum is the correct answer as it is the only museum located in Kerala.
qs.kf:
☛ State Museum of Kerala → Napier Museum (Thiruvananthapuram)
☛ Establishment year of Napier Museum → 1855
☛ Location of Salar Jung Museum → Hyderabad
☛ Location of Albert Hall Museum → Jaipur
☛ Location of Dakshinachitra Museum → Chennai

q: Which country's President suggested the name "United Nations"?
qs.e: The name "United Nations" was suggested by US President Franklin D. Roosevelt. It was first used in the Declaration by United Nations on 1 January 1942, when 26 nations pledged to fight together against the Axis powers. Later, in 1945, the San Francisco Conference adopted the UN Charter. Roosevelt chose this name to symbolize the unity and cooperation of nations in the fight for peace and freedom.
qs.kf:
☛ Who suggested the name United Nations? → Franklin D. Roosevelt (US President)
☛ When was the UN established? → 24 October 1945
☛ Where was the UN Charter signed? → San Francisco
☛ Where is the UN headquarters? → New York, USA
☛ Who is the current UN Secretary-General? → António Guterres

q: Which railway station is a part of UNESCO's world heritage sites?
qs.e: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus) is a historic railway station located in Mumbai. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the year 2004. It is one of the busiest railway stations in India and is built in the Victorian Gothic style. The design was prepared by British architect Frederick William Stevens. This station symbolizes India's colonial heritage and modern railway history. Other options (Lokmanya Tilak Terminus, Anand Vihar Terminus, Kolkata Terminus) are not listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
qs.kf:
☛ UNESCO World Heritage Railway Station → Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
☛ Location → Mumbai, Maharashtra
☛ Year of declaration → 2004
☛ Architectural style → Victorian Gothic
☛ Architect → Frederick William Stevens

q: Which of the following biodiversity hotspots is NOT present in India?
qs.e: India has four biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma (including Northeast India), and Sundaland (including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands). Wallacea is a biodiversity hotspot located in Indonesia and surrounding islands, which is not present in India. These hotspots are defined based on high endemism and severe habitat loss. Wallacea is known for its unique flora and fauna, such as the Komodo dragon, but it lies outside Indian territory.
qs.kf:
☛ Total biodiversity hotspots in India → 4
☛ Other name of Western Ghats → Sahyadri
☛ Indian states included in Indo-Burma hotspot → Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram
☛ Indian island group under Sundaland hotspot → Andaman and Nicobar
☛ Wallacea hotspot is located in → Indonesia

q: Vice president of USA Kamala Harris has roots in the ________ district of Tamilnadu.
qs.e: Kamala Harris, the first female Vice President of the USA, has maternal roots in the Tiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu. Her mother, Shyamala Gopalan, was a cancer researcher from a family originally from Tiruvarur district, specifically near Mayiladuthurai. Harris took office as Vice President in 2021. She is the first African-American and first Indian-American Vice President. Her father, Donald Harris, is of Jamaican descent. Tiruvarur district is located in the fertile Cauvery Delta region, known for its temples and agriculture.
qs.kf:
☛ Name of Kamala Harris's mother → Shyamala Gopalan
☛ Name of Kamala Harris's father → Donald Harris
☛ Kamala Harris's birthplace → Oakland, California
☛ Kamala Harris's position → Vice President of USA (since 2021)
☛ Major river in Tiruvarur district → Cauvery

q: Nagaland was declared as a separate state on _________.
qs.e: Nagaland was declared as a separate state on 1st December 1963. It became the 16th state of India. Nagaland was carved out of Assam. The capital of Nagaland is Kohima. The state was formed after the agreement of the Naga People's Convention. Nagaland has 16 districts. It is also known as the Switzerland of the East. The official language is English. The state is located in northeastern India.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first Chief Minister of Nagaland? → P. Shilu Ao
☛ What is the state flower of Nagaland? → Rhododendron
☛ What is the state animal of Nagaland? → Mithun
☛ What is the state tree of Nagaland? → Alder
☛ What is the largest city of Nagaland? → Dimapur

q: In which year was Hampi declared as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO?
qs.e: Hampi, located in present-day Karnataka, was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986. The site is renowned for its magnificent temples, monuments, and ruins, which exemplify the Vijayanagara architectural style. The recognition by UNESCO has helped in the conservation and promotion of tourism at Hampi.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Hampi located? → Karnataka
☛ Which empire had its capital at Hampi? → Vijayanagara Empire
☛ Who founded the Vijayanagara Empire? → Harihara and Bukka Raya
☛ Name the famous temple in Hampi. → Virupaksha Temple
☛ How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are there in India? → 40 (as of 2023)

q: When is National Consumer Day observed every year?
qs.e: National Consumer Day is observed every year on 24th December. This day commemorates the enactment of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, which provided a robust legal framework for protecting consumer rights. The day is celebrated to spread awareness about consumer rights and responsibilities among the masses. Various programs, seminars, and camps are organized across India to educate consumers. It is important to note that World Consumer Rights Day is observed on 15th March globally. The Consumer Protection Act was later replaced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 to address modern challenges. National Consumer Day highlights the significance of informed choices and grievance redressal mechanisms for consumers.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 enacted? → 24 December 1986
☛ When is World Consumer Rights Day observed? → 15 March
☛ Which is the current consumer protection law in India? → Consumer Protection Act, 2019
☛ What is the purpose of National Consumer Day? → Consumer awareness
☛ How many consumer rights are recognized in India? → Six

q: Which of the following countries has the highest male to female population ratio in the world in 2019?
qs.e: In 2019, Qatar had the highest male-to-female population ratio in the world, with approximately 266 men per 100 women. This imbalance is mainly due to the large number of foreign male migrant workers employed in the oil and gas industry. The United Arab Emirates also has a high ratio, but Qatar leads. Bhutan and Latvia have lower ratios. This ratio reflects the gender distribution of a population and is influenced by migration patterns.
qs.kf:
☛ Country with highest male-to-female ratio → Qatar
☛ Main reason for imbalance in Qatar → Foreign male workers
☛ Number of men per 100 women (Qatar, 2019) → Approximately 266
☛ Another country with high male ratio → United Arab Emirates
☛ Gender ratio in Latvia → More women

q: _______ is a bio reserve in India that is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
qs.e: The Sundarbans is a major biosphere reserve in India, located in West Bengal. It is the largest mangrove forest in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Sundarbans is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, saltwater crocodiles, and many migratory birds. It is part of the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta and covers approximately 10,000 sq km. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. The Sundarbans was designated as a Biosphere Reserve in 1984. It has unique mangrove vegetation and biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is the Sundarbans located in? → West Bengal
☛ When was Sundarbans declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1987
☛ Which tiger is found in the Sundarbans? → Royal Bengal Tiger
☛ Which is the largest mangrove forest in the world? → Sundarbans
☛ Which delta is the Sundarbans part of? → Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta

name: Set 6 · Q236–282
sub: Static GK - Geography, States, Places & Heritage

q: __________ was built by Edwin Lutyens in 1921.
qs.e: India Gate was built by Edwin Lutyens in 1921. This iconic war memorial is located in New Delhi and was erected to commemorate Indian soldiers who died in World War I. Its design is inspired by the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. The monument bears the names of over 13,300 soldiers. Lutyens designed it as a war memorial. Later, after the 1971 India-Pakistan war, the Amar Jawan Jyoti was added beneath it.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the architect of India Gate? → Edwin Lutyens
☛ In which city is India Gate located? → New Delhi
☛ When was India Gate inaugurated? → 1931
☛ What is the height of India Gate? → 42 meters
☛ When was Amar Jawan Jyoti added? → After 1971

q: In which state of India is Namdroling Monastery located?
qs.e: Namdroling Monastery, also known as the Golden Temple, is located in Bylakuppe, Mysore district of Karnataka, India. It belongs to the Nyingma sect of Tibetan Buddhism and was established in 1963 by Pema Norbu Rinpoche. The monastery houses approximately 5,000 monks and nuns, making it the largest Tibetan Buddhist teaching center in India. It is renowned for its magnificent golden statues and vibrant murals. This site is a major attraction for tourists and pilgrims.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Namdroling Monastery located? → In Mysore district of Karnataka
☛ Which sect does Namdroling Monastery belong to? → Nyingma
☛ Who established Namdroling Monastery? → Pema Norbu Rinpoche
☛ What is Namdroling Monastery also known as? → Golden Temple
☛ Which is the largest Tibetan Buddhist teaching center in India? → Namdroling Monastery

q: Rajaji National Park is located in:
qs.e: Rajaji National Park is located in the state of Uttarakhand. It lies in the foothills of the Himalayas and was established in 1983. The park is famous for elephants, tigers, leopards, and various bird species. It is situated along the banks of the Ganges River and also includes a wildlife sanctuary. The park covers an area of about 820 square kilometers and is an important part of Himalayan biodiversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Rajaji National Park located? → Uttarakhand
☛ When was Rajaji National Park established? → 1983
☛ What is the area of Rajaji National Park? → 820 sq km
☛ Along which river is Rajaji National Park situated? → Ganges River
☛ What is Rajaji National Park famous for? → Elephants and tigers

q: From which of the following countries has the aircraft Rafale been procured by Indian Defense ministry?
qs.e: The Rafale is a multirole combat aircraft manufactured by the French company Dassault Aviation. The Indian Air Force signed an agreement with France in 2016 to procure 36 Rafale jets. These aircraft are multi-role and are equipped with advanced missiles (like Meteor, SCALP) and radar systems. The Rafale enhances India's air defense capabilities. France is a major defense partner of India, and this procurement reflects the strategic ties between the two nations.
qs.kf:
☛ Country that manufactures Rafale → France
☛ First country to procure Rafale → France
☛ Year India signed Rafale deal → 2016
☛ Missile supplied with Rafale → Meteor, SCALP
☛ Role of Rafale aircraft → Multirole combat

q: The principal judicial organ of the United Nations is situated in:
qs.e: The principal judicial organ of the United Nations is the International Court of Justice (ICJ), located in Hague, Netherlands. It was established in 1945 under the UN Charter and is one of the six main organs of the UN. The ICJ settles legal disputes between states and gives advisory opinions on international law. It comprises 15 judges elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council for 9-year terms. Other options: New York (headquarters), Geneva (European office), and Vienna (IAEA) are incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ When was ICJ established? → 1945
☛ How many judges are in ICJ? → 15
☛ What is the term of ICJ judges? → 9 years
☛ Where is ICJ located? → Hague (Netherlands)
☛ What is the main function of ICJ? → Settle legal disputes between states

q: Name the capital of the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haweli.
qs.e: Dadra and Nagar Haveli is a Union Territory of India, formed after liberation from Portuguese rule in 1954. Its capital is Silvassa, located on the banks of the Daman Ganga River. In 2020, it merged with Daman and Diu to form the new Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Silvassa is known for its tribal culture and green landscapes. Among the other options, Kavaratti is the capital of Lakshadweep, Pondicherry of Puducherry, and Port Blair of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli → Silvassa
☛ Formation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli → 1954 after liberation from Portuguese
☛ Current Union Territory → Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
☛ River on which Silvassa is located → Daman Ganga River
☛ Capital of Lakshadweep → Kavaratti

q: The first Secretary General of United Nations belonged to which of the following countries?
qs.e: The first Secretary General of the United Nations was Trygve Lie, who belonged to Norway. He served from 1946 to 1952. Trygve Lie played a crucial role in the establishment of the United Nations and maintained the organization's strength during the Cold War. He also served as Norway's Foreign Minister. During his tenure, the UN dealt with crises like the Korean War. After Trygve Lie, Dag Hammarskjöld (Sweden) became the second Secretary General. The term of the UN Secretary General is five years, and the appointment is made by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the first UN Secretary General? → Trygve Lie
☛ Which country did Trygve Lie belong to? → Norway
☛ Who was the second UN Secretary General? → Dag Hammarskjöld
☛ What is the term of UN Secretary General? → Five years
☛ How is the UN Secretary General appointed? → By the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council

q: The Forest Survey of India under the ministry of Environment of India is located in which city?
qs.e: The Forest Survey of India (FSI) is a national organization under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, responsible for assessing and monitoring the forest resources of the country. Its headquarters is located in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. The FSI conducts forest cover mapping, evaluates forest health, carbon stock, and other ecosystem services. Dehradun is known as the 'Forest Capital of India' because it houses several important forest-related institutions like the Forest Research Institute (FRI) and the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM). The FSI was established in 1981 and publishes the biennial 'India State of Forest Report' (ISFR) which provides comprehensive data on forest cover, tree cover, mangrove cover, and forest types.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Forest Survey of India → Dehradun
☛ Year of establishment of Forest Survey of India → 1981
☛ Ministry under which Forest Survey of India works → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ India's largest forest research institute → Forest Research Institute (FRI), Dehradun
☛ Biennial report published by Forest Survey of India → India State of Forest Report (ISFR)

q: In which country are the Inca ruins of Machu Picchu located?
qs.e: The Inca ruins of Machu Picchu are located in Peru, a country in South America. Situated in the Andes Mountains at an altitude of approximately 2,430 meters, it was built in the 15th century by the Inca emperor Pachacuti. Machu Picchu is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. It was rediscovered in 1911 by American historian Hiram Bingham. The site is a masterpiece of Inca architecture and engineering, showcasing their advanced construction techniques and integration with the natural landscape.
qs.kf:
☛ Which civilization built Machu Picchu? → Inca
☛ Which emperor built it? → Pachacuti
☛ Year of rediscovery? → 1911
☛ Who rediscovered it? → Hiram Bingham
☛ In which mountain range is it located? → Andes

q: Which of the following monuments is NOT situated in Delhi?
qs.e: Panch Mahal is located in Fatehpur Sikri, Uttar Pradesh. It was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar and is famous for its five-storey structure. Red Fort, Agrasen Ki Baoli, and Qutub Minar are all prominent monuments situated in Delhi. Red Fort was built by Shah Jahan between 1638-1648. Agrasen Ki Baoli is an ancient stepwell associated with King Agrasen from the Mahabharata era. Qutub Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1193. Thus, the monument not situated in Delhi is Panch Mahal.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Panch Mahal located? → Fatehpur Sikri, Uttar Pradesh
☛ Who built Red Fort? → Shah Jahan
☛ Who started construction of Qutub Minar? → Qutb-ud-din Aibak
☛ Where is Agrasen Ki Baoli? → Delhi
☛ Monument built by Akbar? → Panch Mahal

q: Vivekanand Rock memorial is situated at ______.
qs.e: The Vivekananda Rock Memorial is located in Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu. It is dedicated to Swami Vivekananda, who meditated on this rock in 1892. The memorial was built in 1970 and features a meditation hall and a statue of Vivekananda. The site lies at the confluence of the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Vivekananda Rock Memorial built? → 1970
☛ Where is Vivekananda Rock Memorial situated? → Kanyakumari
☛ In which year did Swami Vivekananda meditate on this rock? → 1892
☛ To whom is Vivekananda Rock Memorial dedicated? → Swami Vivekananda
☛ Which water bodies meet at Kanyakumari? → Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Indian Ocean

q: What is the name of the Island where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 18 years of his total 27 years prison tenure?
qs.e: Nelson Mandela was arrested in 1962 for anti-apartheid activities and sentenced to life imprisonment. Out of his 27 years in prison, he spent 18 years on Robben Island, off the coast of Cape Town, South Africa. Robben Island had been used as a prison for political prisoners since the 17th century. Mandela was released in 1990 and later became the first black President of South Africa. Robben Island is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a symbol of freedom and human rights.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was Nelson Mandela imprisoned for 18 years? → Robben Island
☛ Where is Robben Island located? → South Africa
☛ Robben Island is famous for? → Prison for political prisoners
☛ When was Nelson Mandela released? → 1990
☛ What is the UNESCO status of Robben Island? → World Heritage Site

q: Where is the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park located?
qs.e: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park is located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It lies near Wandoor Beach in the South Andaman district. Established in 1983, it covers an area of 281.5 sq km. The park comprises 15 islands, including Lali, Tarmugli, John Lawrence, and Snob. It is known for its rich coral reefs, mangroves, and marine biodiversity. Species found here include green turtles, dolphins, and saltwater crocodiles. Tourists visit for snorkeling and marine life viewing. It is located about 30 km from Port Blair. This park is managed by the Forest Department of the Andaman and Nicobar Administration.
qs.kf:
☛ How many marine national parks are in India? → 5
☛ Where is Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Where is Rani Jhansi Marine National Park? → Andaman and Nicobar
☛ First marine national park in India? → Gulf of Mannar (1986)
☛ Establishment year of Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park? → 1983

q: The Kedarnath temple is located in the __________ district of Uttarakhand.
qs.e: The Kedarnath temple is located in the Rudraprayag district of Uttarakhand, India. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Situated at an altitude of 3,583 meters on the Kedarnath mountain, it is a key destination in the Char Dham pilgrimage. The temple lies near the Mandakini River in the Garhwal Himalayan region. Other options like Haridwar, Uttarkashi, and Tehri Garhwal are incorrect. The temple's construction is attributed to the Pandavas from the Mahabharata era.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river flows near the Kedarnath temple? → Mandakini
☛ Kedarnath temple is located in which mountain range? → Himalayas
☛ Who is believed to have built the Kedarnath temple? → The Pandavas
☛ What is the architectural style of Kedarnath temple? → Hindu architecture
☛ What is the position of Kedarnath in the Char Dham circuit? → Third Dham

q: 'Tara saari' is basically related to which state?
qs.e: Tara saari is a traditional handwoven saree from West Bengal, specifically made in the Murshidabad district. It is known for its fine weaving and translucent texture, using silk and cotton threads. The saree has received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Its name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'tara' (star), reflecting its shiny appearance. It represents the rich weaving heritage of Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Tara saari is related to which state? → West Bengal
☛ In which district is Tara saari made? → Murshidabad
☛ When did Tara saari get GI tag? → 2018
☛ Which threads are mainly used in Tara saari? → Silk and cotton
☛ What is the texture of Tara saari? → Translucent and fine

q: In which country is the Sinai Peninsula located?
qs.e: The Sinai Peninsula is a triangular peninsula in Egypt, located between Asia and Africa. It is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the south. Its area is about 60,000 sq km. The Sinai Peninsula is the only part of Egypt located in Asia. It is historically significant as it houses the Suez Canal, which connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. The peninsula is named after Mount Sinai, which is important in the Bible.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Sinai Peninsula located? → Egypt
☛ Which two continents does the Sinai Peninsula lie between? → Asia and Africa
☛ Which sea is to the north of the Sinai Peninsula? → Mediterranean Sea
☛ Which sea is to the south of the Sinai Peninsula? → Red Sea
☛ What important canal is located on the Sinai Peninsula? → Suez Canal

q: Hemathas is associated with which Indian state?
qs.e: Hemathas is a well-known folk dance or cultural tradition associated with the state of Assam, primarily performed by the Bodo community. It involves traditional costumes and music, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of Assam. The dance is an important part of the Bodo festivals and celebrations. Understanding the cultural diversity of Indian states is crucial for competitive exams.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Hemathas associated with? → Assam
☛ Which community performs Hemathas dance? → Bodo community
☛ What is the famous folk dance of Assam? → Bihu
☛ Which Indian state has a significant Bodo population? → Assam
☛ What is the state dance of Assam? → Bihu

q: Red Kangaroo is the national animal of which of the following nations?
qs.e: The red kangaroo is the national animal of Australia. It is the world's largest marsupial, primarily found in the arid and semi-arid regions of Australia. Australian national symbols include the kangaroo and the emu, which also appear on the country's coat of arms. The kangaroo is considered an emblem of Australian culture and identity. Among the other options, South Africa's national animal is the springbok, Chile's is the huemul (South Andean deer), and New Zealand's is the kiwi (a bird).
qs.kf:
☛ World's largest marsupial → Red kangaroo
☛ National animal of South Africa → Springbok
☛ National animal of Chile → Huemul
☛ National animal of New Zealand → Kiwi
☛ Australian national symbols → Kangaroo and emu

q: Cambodia's' Phnom Penh '(Namnpeh)' is situated on the banks of which river?
qs.e: Cambodia's capital Phnom Penh is located on the banks of the Mekong River. The Mekong is one of Southeast Asia's longest rivers, flowing from Tibet through China, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam. It is a vital source of transportation, agriculture, and fisheries for Cambodia. Phnom Penh is situated at the confluence of the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers, making it a key trade hub. The river's basin supports diverse ecosystems and numerous cultural sites.
qs.kf:
☛ Mekong River originates in → Tibet
☛ Longest river in SE Asia → Mekong
☛ Phnom Penh is on → Mekong River
☛ Countries traversed by Mekong → 6 (China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam)
☛ Cambodia's capital → Phnom Penh

q: Kerala is famous in what form-
qs.e: Kerala is famously known as 'God's Own Country' due to its breathtaking natural beauty, lush landscapes, serene backwaters, pristine beaches, and rich cultural heritage. It is one of India's top tourist destinations and is also renowned for Ayurveda, spices, and having the highest literacy rate in the country. Situated between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, Kerala enjoys unique geographical features. Its economy relies on agriculture, fisheries, and tourism. The state also boasts the highest life expectancy and Human Development Index in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Tourism slogan of Kerala → God's Own Country
☛ Capital of Kerala → Thiruvananthapuram
☛ State bird of Kerala → Great Hornbill
☛ State flower of Kerala → Kanikonna (Golden Shower)
☛ Largest city of Kerala → Kochi

q: The famous Vishwanath Jyotirlinga temple is located in.
qs.e: The famous Vishwanath Jyotirlinga temple is located in Uttar Pradesh, in the city of Varanasi (Kashi). It is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas dedicated to Lord Shiva. The Kashi Vishwanath Temple is considered one of the holiest sites in Hinduism. Situated on the banks of the Ganges River, it is believed to be the center of the city of Kashi, which is associated with liberation. The original temple was destroyed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, but was later rebuilt in 1780 by the Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar. The temple's gold dome was contributed by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in 1835. This Jyotirlinga is one of the most important pilgrimage sites for Shiva devotees.
qs.kf:
☛ One of the 12 Jyotirlingas → Vishwanath Jyotirlinga
☛ Ancient name of Varanasi → Kashi
☛ Rebuilt the temple → Ahilyabai Holkar
☛ Golden dome built by → Maharaja Ranjit Singh
☛ Temple on the banks of → Ganges River

q: What is the full form of Digital Literacy Program Direction (DISHA)?
qs.e: The full form of DISHA is Digital Literacy Campaign. It is a program launched by the Government of India to make citizens digitally literate, enabling them to use digital services. Under this program, people are trained to use computers, the internet, and other digital devices. The campaign focuses especially on rural and remote areas to reduce the digital divide.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of DISHA → Digital Literacy Campaign
☛ Which ministry oversees DISHA? → Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
☛ Objective of DISHA → To make citizens digitally literate
☛ Target of DISHA → At least one digitally literate person per family
☛ When was DISHA launched? → In 2015

q: Which of the following is NOT a world heritage site?
qs.e: Manas Wildlife Sanctuary, Kaziranga National Park, and Nanda Devi National Park are all UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Manas Sanctuary is located in Assam and was declared a World Heritage Site in 1985. Kaziranga National Park, also in Assam, is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros and was inscribed in 1985. Nanda Devi National Park, in Uttarakhand, was granted World Heritage status in 1988. However, Periyar National Park, located in Kerala, is a Tiger Reserve but is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Therefore, Periyar National Park is not a World Heritage site among the options.
qs.kf:
☛ Kaziranga National Park is famous for which animal? → One-horned rhinoceros
☛ In which state is Manas Wildlife Sanctuary located? → Assam
☛ In which year was Nanda Devi National Park declared a World Heritage Site? → 1988
☛ What type of protected area is Periyar National Park? → Tiger Reserve
☛ How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are there in India? → 42 (as of 2024)

q: In which Indian city is the largest post office located?
qs.e: The largest post office in India is the General Post Office (GPO) located in the Fort area of Mumbai. Built in 1913, it serves as the headquarters of the Indian Postal Department. The building is designed in the Gothic Revival style by architect John Begg. It is one of the largest postal service buildings from the British era. The Mumbai GPO covers an area of approximately 1.2 lakh square feet. It is not only the largest post office in India but also one of the busiest in the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Oldest post office in India → Kolkata GPO
☛ Year of first postage stamp in India → 1852
☛ Year of establishment of Indian Postal Department → 1854
☛ First female Director General of Indian Postal Service → Vandana Agrawal
☛ Highest post office in India → Hikkim, Himachal Pradesh

q: Which of the following IITs has developed a portable solar-powered cold storage device with 500 kg capacity for storing vegetables and fruits?
qs.e: IIT Madras has developed a portable solar-powered cold storage device with a capacity of 500 kg for storing vegetables and fruits. Named e-Cooler, this device is designed to help farmers keep their produce fresh for longer periods. It runs entirely on solar energy and is specifically designed for small-scale farmers. Such cold storage solutions can significantly reduce post-harvest losses and increase farmers' income. The project was led by the Rural Technology Action Group (RMEL) at IIT Madras. This technology is especially beneficial for rural areas where regular electricity supply is not available, ensuring that perishable goods can be stored efficiently without relying on the grid.
qs.kf:
☛ Developer of e-Cooler IIT → IIT Madras
☛ Storage capacity of e-Cooler → 500 kg
☛ Energy source used in e-Cooler → Solar energy
☛ Use of e-Cooler → Storage of fruits and vegetables
☛ Group leading the project → RMEL, IIT Madras

q: Which of these countries was created in the twentieth century?
qs.e: Bangladesh was established in 1971, which falls in the latter half of the twentieth century. It is a sovereign country in South Asia, formed after gaining independence from Pakistan. Prior to this, it was known as East Pakistan. The Bangladesh Liberation War was led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. In contrast, USA (1776), Japan (mythological 660 BCE), and Nepal (1768) were established before the twentieth century. Bangladesh is the eighth most populous country in the world, and its official language is Bengali.
qs.kf:
☛ When was Bangladesh's independence declared? → 26 March 1971
☛ Who led the Bangladesh Liberation War? → Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
☛ What was Bangladesh previously called? → East Pakistan
☛ What is the official language of Bangladesh? → Bengali
☛ What is the capital of Bangladesh? → Dhaka

q: What is the state animal of Andhra Pradesh?
qs.e: The state animal of Andhra Pradesh is the Blackbuck. The blackbuck is a medium-sized antelope native to the Indian subcontinent. Males have long, spiral horns, while females are hornless. This species primarily inhabits grasslands and open forests. Conservation efforts in Andhra Pradesh are specifically aimed at protecting this species. The blackbuck is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, which provides it the highest level of protection. It is also the state animal of Telangana.
qs.kf:
☛ State animal of Andhra Pradesh → Blackbuck
☛ Under which act is blackbuck listed in Schedule I? → Wildlife Protection Act, 1972
☛ Which other state has blackbuck as its state animal? → Telangana
☛ Characteristic feature of male blackbuck → Long, spiral horns
☛ Habitat of blackbuck → Grasslands and open forests

q: When was 'Victoria Memorial' built in India?
qs.e: The Victoria Memorial in Kolkata, India, was built starting in 1906. It was constructed in memory of Queen Victoria, who died in 1901. The design was prepared by William Emerson and is a fine example of Indo-Saracenic architecture. Construction began in 1906 and was completed in 1921. It was inaugurated in 1921 by the Prince of Wales (later King Edward VIII). Today, it serves as a museum and tourist attraction. The other options are incorrect: 1857 is the year of the Indian Rebellion, 1900 is not the year of Queen Victoria's death (she died in 1901), and 1806 is unrelated to the Victoria Memorial.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Victoria Memorial located? → Kolkata
☛ Who was the architect of Victoria Memorial? → William Emerson
☛ Which architectural style is Victoria Memorial an example of? → Indo-Saracenic
☛ When was Victoria Memorial completed? → 1921
☛ In whose memory was Victoria Memorial built? → Queen Victoria

q: Where is the Lalitagiri Buddhist site located?
qs.e: Lalitagiri is a major Buddhist site located in the state of Odisha, India. It is situated in Jajpur district and is famous for its Buddhist stupas, monasteries, and sculptures. Lalitagiri, along with Ratnagiri and Udayagiri, forms the 'Diamond Triangle' of Buddhist heritage. This region was an important center for the development of Buddhism, especially the Mahayana sect. Excavations here have unearthed Buddhist artifacts dating from the 3rd century BCE to the 10th century CE. The site is a significant center for Buddhist pilgrimage and archaeological study.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Lalitagiri located? → Odisha
☛ Which three Buddhist sites form the Diamond Triangle? → Lalitagiri, Ratnagiri, Udayagiri
☛ Which Buddhist sect is associated with Lalitagiri? → Mahayana
☛ In which district is Lalitagiri situated? → Jajpur
☛ From which period are the artifacts found at Lalitagiri? → 3rd century BCE to 10th century CE

q: Match the states in list I with the sex ratios as per Census 2011 in list II. List – I (State) List - II (Sex ratio as per Census 2011)
1. Uttar Pradesh a. 931
2. Bihar b. 918
3. Madhya Pradesh c. 929
4. Maharashtra d. 912
qs.e: As per Census 2011, the sex ratio (females per 1000 males) of Uttar Pradesh was 912 (d), Bihar was 918 (b), Madhya Pradesh was 931 (a), and Maharashtra was 929 (c). The national average sex ratio stood at 943, with Kerala having the highest at 1084. Both Bihar and Uttar Pradesh had sex ratios lower than the national average. Madhya Pradesh's ratio (931) was better than Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Maharashtra's ratio (929) was close to Madhya Pradesh's. This matching is commonly asked in competitive exams.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest sex ratio in 2011 → Kerala (1084)
☛ Lowest sex ratio in 2011 → Haryana (879)
☛ Sex ratio of Bihar (2011) → 918
☛ Sex ratio of Maharashtra (2011) → 929
☛ Sex ratio of Uttar Pradesh (2011) → 912

q: Which of the following countries rejoined the UNESCO in July 2023 and became its 194th member?
qs.e: In July 2023, the United States of America rejoined UNESCO after a gap of about 4 years, becoming its 194th member. The US had left UNESCO in 2018 under President Donald Trump, citing anti-Israel bias and outstanding dues. The Biden administration decided to rejoin, partly to counter China's growing influence in the organization. UNESCO is a specialized agency of the United Nations that promotes education, science, and culture to foster peace and security. Its headquarters is in Paris, France. The rejoining highlights the US commitment to multilateralism and global cooperation.
qs.kf:
☛ When was UNESCO established? → 1945
☛ Where is UNESCO headquarters located? → Paris, France
☛ What is the main objective of UNESCO? → Promote education, science, and culture for peace
☛ When did the US first leave UNESCO? → 2018
☛ Who is the current Director-General of UNESCO? → Audrey Azoulay

q: Where in India is the 'Basilica of Bom Jesus' building located?
qs.e: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is located in the state of Goa, India. It is a famous church and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The church houses the remains of St. Francis Xavier, a 16th-century Christian missionary. It is an excellent example of Baroque architecture and attracts many tourists and pilgrims every year.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Basilica of Bom Jesus located? → Goa
☛ In whose memory was this church built? → St. Francis Xavier
☛ When was it inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1986
☛ What is the architectural style of this church? → Baroque
☛ How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are there in Goa? → One (Churches and Convents of Goa)

q: Where is the Vajragiri Buddhist monastery located?
qs.e: The Vajragiri Buddhist monastery is located in the state of Odisha. It is an important Buddhist site situated in the Jajpur district. This monastery is associated with Mahayana Buddhism and served as a residential facility for Buddhist monks. Archaeological surveys have revealed Buddha statues and inscriptions at the site. The monastery flourished between the 7th and 12th centuries CE. Vajragiri is also known as Brahmagiri or Ramagiri. It was a major center for the spread of Buddhism in India.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Vajragiri Buddhist monastery located? → Odisha
☛ Which Buddhist sect is associated with Vajragiri? → Mahayana
☛ What is another name for Vajragiri? → Brahmagiri or Ramagiri
☛ In which district is Vajragiri located? → Jajpur
☛ During which period did Vajragiri flourish? → 7th to 12th century

q: Which round of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) for maternal and child health and other associated indicators was launched by the Centre in December 2023?
qs.e: In December 2023, the central government launched the sixth round of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) for indicators related to maternal and child health. NFHS is a large-scale, multi-round survey conducted by the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It collects crucial data on population, health, nutrition, and family welfare. Following NFHS-5 (2019-21), NFHS-6 aims to update the latest health indicators. The survey focuses on key areas such as maternal mortality rate, infant mortality rate, malnutrition, and family planning. The data helps in formulating health policies and programs for the country.
qs.kf:
☛ Full form of NFHS → National Family Health Survey
☛ Launch year of NFHS-6 → 2023
☛ Data collection year for NFHS-5 → 2019-21
☛ Conducting institute of NFHS → International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS)
☛ Key areas under NFHS → Maternal and child health, nutrition, family planning

q: The Mass Drug Administration Campaign to eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis is being carried out by the Government in around 63 district in 6 states. Which of the following is NOT one of those states?
qs.e: The Government of India is conducting the Mass Drug Administration (MDA) campaign to eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis (elephantiasis) in 63 districts across 6 states. These states are: Jharkhand, Karnataka, Telangana, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal. Chhattisgarh is not among these states. Under the MDA campaign, tablets of Diethylcarbamazine (DEC) and Albendazole are distributed. The goal is to eliminate filariasis by the year 2030. This campaign is being implemented under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP).
qs.kf:
☛ Which mosquito is the vector of Lymphatic Filariasis? → Culex mosquito
☛ What is the target year for filariasis elimination? → 2030
☛ Which drugs are given in MDA? → DEC and Albendazole
☛ Which state has the highest number of filariasis cases? → Bihar
☛ Under which ministry does NVBDCP come? → Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

q: Bolgatty Palace in Kochi, Kerala, India was built in the __________ architectural style.
qs.e: Bolgatty Palace is located in Kochi, Kerala and was built in the Dutch architectural style. The palace was constructed in 1744 AD by the Dutch East India Company during the period of Dutch colonization in India. It is one of the oldest Dutch palaces in Kerala. Currently, the palace is used as a hotel operated by the Kerala Tourism Development Corporation (KTDC). Dutch architecture is characterized by strong structures and simple yet attractive designs.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Bolgatty Palace located? → Kochi, Kerala
☛ When was Bolgatty Palace built? → 1744 AD
☛ Which architectural style is Bolgatty Palace built in? → Dutch
☛ Who built Bolgatty Palace? → Dutch East India Company
☛ Who manages Bolgatty Palace currently? → Kerala Tourism Development Corporation (KTDC)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1
q: Which country lies to the east of Arunachal Pradesh?
qs.e: Arunachal Pradesh is a northeastern state of India. To its east lies Myanmar (Burma). Arunachal Pradesh shares international borders with three countries: China (Tibet) to the north, Bhutan to the west, and Myanmar to the east. To the south, it borders Assam and Nagaland. The boundary with Myanmar is about 520 km long and runs along the Patkai hills. Arunachal also has a border dispute with China, known as the McMahon Line.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar
☛ Which country lies to the west of Arunachal Pradesh → Bhutan
☛ Which country lies to the north of Arunachal Pradesh → China
☛ Myanmar's state bordering Arunachal Pradesh → Kachin
☛ Number of districts in Arunachal Pradesh → 26

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1
q: What name do the Jarawa tribe use to refer to their home in the Andaman Islands?
qs.e: The Jarawa tribe of the Andaman Islands call their homes Chaddhas. These huts are made from leaves and wood, and are built in the forests of South and Middle Andaman. The Jarawa are a hunter-gatherer tribe and maintain a traditional lifestyle isolated from the outside world. They are protected by the Indian government. The term Chaddhas is derived from the Jarawa language and is a key part of their cultural identity. The Jarawa are one of the several indigenous tribes of the Andaman Islands, along with the Sentinelese, Onge, and Great Andamanese.
qs.kf:
☛ Where does the Jarawa tribe live? → Andaman Islands
☛ What is the home of the Jarawa called? → Chaddhas
☛ Which language family does the Jarawa belong to? → Andamanese
☛ What is the main livelihood of the Jarawa? → Hunting and gathering
☛ Name other tribes of the Andaman Islands. → Sentinelese, Onge, Great Andamanese

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 2
q: What type of shrine is the Neeramankara Temple located in Nemam, Kerala, in India known to be?
qs.e: The Neeramankara Temple located in Nemam, Kerala, is known to be of the Sandhara type. In Sandhara temples, the sanctum sanctorum is surrounded by an enclosed ambulatory path (pradakshina patha), which is enclosed by a wall. This distinguishes it from Nirandhara temples, which lack such a path. The Neeramankara Temple represents South Indian architecture and is built in the Kerala style. In Sandhara temples, devotees can perform circumambulation, while in Nirandhara temples, the sanctum is directly visible from outside. Hence, this temple falls under the Sandhara category.
qs.kf:
☛ Sandhara temple definition → Sanctum with enclosed ambulatory path
☛ Nirandhara temple definition → Sanctum without ambulatory path
☛ Sarvatobhadra temple → Symmetric temple with doors on all four sides
☛ Mandapa type → Open pillared hall
☛ Neeramankara temple location → Nemam, Kerala

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (20/06/2025) Shift 2
q: In January 2025, Wing Commander Akshay Saxena received the Vayu Sena Medal for his role in anti-piracy operations conducted in which of the following regions?
qs.e: In January 2025, Wing Commander Akshay Saxena was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal (VSM) for his role in anti-piracy operations in the Arabian Sea. These operations were part of joint efforts by the Indian Navy and Air Force to combat piracy, involving aerial surveillance and strikes against pirates. The Arabian Sea is a crucial maritime route and has been a hotspot for piracy. The Indian Air Force used helicopters and surveillance aircraft in these missions, leading to a reduction in piracy incidents. Wing Commander Saxena's leadership and strategic planning were highly commended. His recognition highlights the importance of anti-piracy operations in ensuring maritime security in the region.
qs.kf:
☛ Who received Vayu Sena Medal for anti-piracy operations in Arabian Sea? → Wing Commander Akshay Saxena
☛ In which year was the medal awarded? → January 2025
☛ Region of operations? → Arabian Sea
☛ Which forces were involved? → Indian Navy and Air Force
☛ Why is Arabian Sea prone to piracy? → It's a major maritime route

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (20/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Which body took suo motu cognisance of the news titled 'Experts are alarmed as 350 turtles was ashore dead till January 15', published on 16 January 2025?
qs.e: The news titled 'Experts are alarmed as 350 turtles was ashore dead till January 15' was published on 16 January 2025. The National Green Tribunal (NGT) took suo motu cognisance of this incident. NGT is a specialised tribunal established for the effective and speedy disposal of cases related to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources. It has the authority to hear cases involving substantial questions relating to the environment. The tribunal's chairperson is a retired judge of the Supreme Court of India. In this case, NGT acted promptly by taking suo motu cognisance and sought reports from the concerned authorities to ensure necessary action is taken to prevent such incidents in the future.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the National Green Tribunal established? → 2010
☛ Under which act was NGT established? → National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
☛ Who is the chairperson of NGT? → A retired Supreme Court judge
☛ What types of cases does NGT hear? → Cases related to the environment
☛ Where is the headquarters of NGT? → New Delhi

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (20/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which Union Territory of India has the longest coastline as per the 2022-23 Annual Report of the Ministry of Home Affairs?
qs.e: According to the 2022-23 Annual Report of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Union Territory with the longest coastline in India is the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, measuring approximately 1,962 km. It is located in the Bay of Bengal and consists of 572 islands. The second longest is Lakshadweep (132 km), situated in the Arabian Sea. Daman and Diu has a coastline of about 42 km, while Puducherry has 45 km. This report is crucial for coastal security and maritime border management.
qs.kf:
☛ Indian state with the longest coastline → Gujarat (1,600 km)
☛ Indian state with the shortest coastline → Goa (160 km)
☛ Indian state with the longest maritime boundary → Gujarat
☛ Total coastline length of India → 7,516.6 km
☛ Capital of Andaman and Nicobar Islands → Port Blair

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 1
q: An astronomical observation site, Jantar Mantar, which is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which State?
qs.e: Jantar Mantar, an astronomical observatory located in Jaipur, Rajasthan, was built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II between 1728 and 1734 CE. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and houses 19 astronomical instruments, including the Samrat Yantra, Jai Prakash Yantra, and Ram Yantra. The observatory is renowned for measuring astronomical positions and time calculation. India has five such observatories: Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi. The Jaipur observatory is the largest and best-preserved among them.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Jantar Mantar located? → Rajasthan (Jaipur)
☛ Who built Jantar Mantar? → Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II
☛ When was Jantar Mantar built? → 1728-1734 CE
☛ What is the main instrument of Jantar Mantar? → Samrat Yantra
☛ How many Jantar Mantars are there in India? → 5 (Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, Varanasi)

q: National Handloom day is celebrated every year on ________.
qs.e: India celebrates National Handloom Day every year on 7 August to honor the handloom industry and the contributions of weavers. It was first launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chennai in 2015. The date marks the beginning of the Swadeshi Movement in 1905, which was started in protest of the partition of Bengal and promoted the use of indigenous goods. The day aims to create awareness about the handloom sector and improve the economic condition of weavers. Handloom is a significant part of India's cultural heritage and provides employment to millions.
qs.kf:
☛ When is National Handloom Day celebrated? → 7 August
☛ In which year was National Handloom Day first observed? → 2015
☛ Who launched National Handloom Day? → Prime Minister Narendra Modi
☛ When did the Swadeshi Movement start? → 1905
☛ Handloom industry falls under which sector? → Cottage industry

q: Which of the following is NOT the capital of the corresponding country?
qs.e: Sydney is the largest city in Australia, but it is not the capital. The capital of Australia is Canberra. New Delhi is the capital of India, Ottawa is the capital of Canada, and Cairo is the capital of Egypt. Hence only the Sydney-Australia pair is incorrect.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Australia → Canberra
☛ Capital of India → New Delhi
☛ Capital of Canada → Ottawa
☛ Capital of Egypt → Cairo
☛ Largest city in Australia → Sydney

q: Which supersonic cruise missile is named after the Indian river Brahmaputra and the Russian river Moskva?
qs.e: BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile named after the Brahmaputra river of India and the Moska river of Russia. It is developed by the joint venture BrahMos Aerospace between India and Russia. The missile has a speed of up to Mach 2.8, making it one of the fastest supersonic cruise missiles in the world. BrahMos is designed for use by all three armed forces – army, navy, and air force. Its range varies from 290 km to 800 km, and it can be launched from various platforms including ships, submarines, aircraft, and land-based launchers.
qs.kf:
☛ Which two rivers is the BrahMos missile named after? → Brahmaputra and Moskva
☛ What is the speed of the BrahMos missile? → Mach 2.8
☛ What type of missile is BrahMos? → Supersonic cruise missile
☛ Which countries are involved in BrahMos development? → India and Russia
☛ What is the range of BrahMos missile? → 290 km to 800 km

q: Silao Khaja is a traditional delicacy of _______ which got Geographical Indication (GI) tag in December 2018.
qs.e: Silao Khaja is a traditional delicacy of Silao town in Nalanda district of Bihar. It received the Geographical Indication (GI) tag in December 2018. This sweet snack is made from wheat flour, ghee, and sugar. Silao Khaja is known for its flaky texture and long shelf life. Before receiving the GI tag, it was locally famous, but now it has gained national and international recognition. The tag has promoted Bihar's food culture.
qs.kf:
☛ Silao Khaja is associated with which state? → Bihar
☛ When did Silao Khaja get GI tag? → December 2018
☛ Silao town is located in which district? → Nalanda, Bihar
☛ What are the main ingredients of Silao Khaja? → Wheat flour, ghee, sugar
☛ Which Bihar delicacy got GI tag in 2018? → Silao Khaja

name: Set 7 · Q283–329
sub: Static GK - Geography, States, Places & Heritage

q: According to the United Nations which year is considered as the International Year of Indigenous Languages?
qs.e: The United Nations declared 2019 as the International Year of Indigenous Languages. Its aim was to focus on the preservation and promotion of endangered indigenous languages worldwide. UNESCO led this initiative, stating that more than 40% of the approximately 6,700 languages globally are at risk of extinction. During the year, numerous events and activities were organized to raise awareness about the importance of these languages and their role in cultural heritage. This initiative was a crucial step towards protecting the rights of indigenous communities and their linguistic diversity.
qs.kf:
☛ International Year of Indigenous Languages → 2019
☛ Leading organization for this year → UNESCO
☛ Objective → Preservation and promotion of indigenous languages
☛ Next decade declared → International Decade of Indigenous Languages (2022–2032)
☛ Global language endangerment → Over 40% of 6,700 languages are at risk

q: Which of the following is NOT included in UNESCO'S list of World Heritage Sites in India?
qs.e: UNESCO's World Heritage List includes 43 sites in India. Sanchi Stupa (1989), Bhimbetka rock shelters (2003), and Khajuraho temples (1986) are all UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Anand Bhavan in Prayagraj (Allahabad) is a historic building associated with the Nehru family, but it is not listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Anand Bhavan was built in the 1930s and now serves as a museum. Hence, this option is correct.
qs.kf:
☛ First UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India (1983) → Ajanta, Ellora, Agra Fort, Taj Mahal
☛ Newest Indian site added to UNESCO (2024) → Moidam (Assam)
☛ Total UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India (2024) → 43
☛ Bhimbetka rock shelters located in which state → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Khajuraho temples located in which state → Madhya Pradesh

q: In which of the following cities is the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) located?
qs.e: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) is located in Hyderabad, Telangana. It is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, providing ocean data and information services. INCOIS was established in 1999 and plays a crucial role in ocean forecasting, tsunami warnings, fisheries advisories, and marine resource management. It is also a hub for global ocean data sharing.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of INCOIS? → Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
☛ Which ministry does INCOIS belong to? → Ministry of Earth Sciences
☛ When was INCOIS established? → 1999
☛ Where is INCOIS located? → Hyderabad
☛ What is the function of INCOIS? → Providing ocean data and information services

q: On which date is the National Voters’ Day celebrated in India?
qs.e: National Voters' Day is celebrated annually on 25th January in India. This day marks the foundation day of the Election Commission of India, which was established on 25th January 1950. The aim of this day is to encourage citizens, especially youth, to participate in the democratic process and to raise awareness about the importance of voting. It was first celebrated in 2011 under the initiative of then President Pratibha Patil. On this day, new voters are provided with their Voter ID cards and various awareness programs are organized across the country to promote voter education and electoral participation.
qs.kf:
☛ When is National Voters' Day celebrated? → 25th January
☛ When was the Election Commission of India established? → 25th January 1950
☛ In which year did National Voters' Day start? → 2011
☛ Who initiated the first National Voters' Day? → Pratibha Patil
☛ What is the main objective of Voters' Day? → To motivate youth to vote

q: Chholiya dance form is associated with _____ state.
qs.e: Chholiya is a traditional folk dance form from the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand. It is performed mainly during wedding processions and festivals, where dancers wield swords and shields, showcasing martial skills. This dance is not associated with Haryana, Rajasthan, or Bihar. Efforts are being made to include it in the UNESCO heritage list. Instruments like dhol, damau, and turhi accompany the dance. It is primarily performed by the Kshatriya community.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Chholiya dance associated with? → Uttarakhand
☛ On which occasion is Chholiya performed? → Weddings
☛ Which instruments are used in Chholiya dance? → Dhol, Damau, Turhi
☛ Other folk dances of Uttarakhand? → Jhodha, Chancheri
☛ Where is the Kumaon region located? → Uttarakhand

q: Which of the following monuments is NOT located in the state of Madhya Pradesh?
qs.e: Janjira Fort is located in the state of Maharashtra, not in Madhya Pradesh. It is a sea fort situated in the Arabian Sea near Murud village. Bhandhavgarh Fort, Gwalior Fort, and Asirgarh Fort are all located in Madhya Pradesh. Bhandhavgarh Fort is in Umaria district, Gwalior Fort in Gwalior city, and Asirgarh Fort in Burhanpur district. Thus, Janjira Fort is not situated in Madhya Pradesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest fort in Madhya Pradesh → Gwalior Fort
☛ Bhandhavgarh Fort is in which district → Umaria
☛ Asirgarh Fort is on which river → Tapti River
☛ Janjira Fort is in which state → Maharashtra
☛ Gwalior Fort architecture style → Hindu and Islamic

q: Cyclone "Pabuk" originated in which region?
qs.e: Cyclone Pabuk originated in the Gulf of Thailand in the year 2019. It was a tropical cyclone that affected Thailand, Vietnam, and Malaysia. The cyclone occurred in January 2019 and was named by Laos. The Gulf of Thailand is a part of the South China Sea, which is connected to the Pacific Ocean. Cyclone Pabuk brought heavy rainfall, flooding, and strong winds to the region.
qs.kf:
☛ When did Cyclone Pabuk occur? → 2019
☛ Which country named Cyclone Pabuk? → Laos
☛ What type of cyclone was Pabuk? → Tropical cyclone
☛ Which countries were affected by Cyclone Pabuk? → Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia
☛ The Gulf of Thailand is part of which sea? → South China Sea

q: Statue of Liberty is located in which city?
qs.e: The Statue of Liberty is a iconic statue located in New York City, USA. It stands on Liberty Island in New York Harbor. It was a gift from France to the United States in 1876 to commemorate the centennial of American independence. The statue was designed by Frederic Auguste Bartholdi and dedicated in 1886. It is made of copper and stands 93 meters tall. The statue holds a torch in its right hand and a tablet in its left hand inscribed with the date of American independence. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and symbolizes freedom and democracy.
qs.kf:
☛ Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the US? → France
☛ When was the Statue of Liberty dedicated? → 1886
☛ Who designed the Statue of Liberty? → Frederic Auguste Bartholdi
☛ What is the height of the Statue of Liberty? → 93 meters
☛ On which island is the Statue of Liberty located? → Liberty Island

q: In which of the following countries, the Old Faithful Geyser is found?
qs.e: The Old Faithful Geyser is located in Yellowstone National Park, which lies in the state of Wyoming, USA. It is famous for its regular and predictable eruptions, occurring approximately every 60 to 110 minutes. Yellowstone is the world's first national park, established in 1872, and contains more than half of the world's geysers. Old Faithful erupts a powerful jet of water and steam, reaching heights of 30-55 meters. Thus, this geyser is found only in the USA.
qs.kf:
☛ In which national park is Old Faithful Geyser located? → Yellowstone National Park
☛ In which country is Yellowstone located? → United States of America
☛ When was Yellowstone established? → 1872
☛ How high does Old Faithful erupt? → 30-55 meters
☛ What percentage of the world's geysers are in Yellowstone? → Over 50%

q: The India's largest wind farm cluster is located in which state?
qs.e: India's largest wind farm cluster is located in the state of Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu is a leading state in wind energy production, with major wind farms established in districts like Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli, Kanyakumari, Coimbatore, and Tirupur. The state has an installed wind energy capacity of over 8,000 megawatts, making it the largest wind energy producer in the country. It is followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra. Prominent wind farms such as 'Muppandal' and 'Pallam' are located in Tamil Nadu.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest wind farm cluster in India? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Second largest wind energy producing state? → Gujarat
☛ Where is the Muppandal wind farm located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Tamil Nadu's installed wind energy capacity? → Over 8,000 MW
☛ Tamil Nadu's share in India's total wind energy capacity? → About 30%

q: Earth Hour is organized by-
qs.e: Earth Hour is organized by the World Wildlife Fund (WWF). It is a global environmental campaign that began in 2007. The initiative encourages individuals and communities to turn off non-essential lights for one hour to raise awareness about climate change. WWF is an international non-governmental organization focused on wildlife conservation and environmental sustainability. Earth Hour is held annually on the last Saturday of March.
qs.kf:
☛ Who organizes Earth Hour? → World Wildlife Fund (WWF)
☛ When did Earth Hour start? → 2007
☛ What is done during Earth Hour? → Lights are turned off for one hour
☛ What is the purpose of Earth Hour? → Raise awareness about climate change
☛ On which date is Earth Hour observed? → Last Saturday of March

q: Where is India's first hi-tech forensic lab, which was recently inaugurated, located?
qs.e: India's first hi-tech forensic lab has been inaugurated in Delhi. This lab comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is equipped with modern technologies such as DNA analysis, digital forensics, and cyber crime investigation. The purpose of this lab is to ensure quick and accurate investigation in criminal cases. It is located in the national capital region and is equipped with state-of-the-art instruments. This will enhance the capability of investigation agencies and speed up the analysis of forensic evidence.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first hi-tech forensic lab → Located in Delhi
☛ Its inauguration → Recently done by the Union Home Minister
☛ Lab features → DNA, digital, and cyber forensic facilities
☛ Lab objective → Quick and accurate investigation of criminal cases
☛ This lab → Works under the Ministry of Home Affairs

q: The 29th Conference of Parties (COP-29) of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change from 11–22 November 2024 was held in ______________.
qs.e: The 29th Conference of Parties (COP-29) of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change was held from 11 to 22 November 2024 in Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan. The conference focused on climate finance, carbon markets, and adaptation measures. It was presided over by Mukhtar Babayev. COP-29 is considered crucial for achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. Delegates from over 190 countries participated in this event in Baku.
qs.kf:
☛ COP-29 venue → Baku, Azerbaijan
☛ President of COP-29 → Mukhtar Babayev
☛ COP-29 dates → 11-22 November 2024
☛ Full form of COP → Conference of Parties
☛ COP-29 deals with → Climate change
