q: In India, a city with a population of less than 10,000 and more than 5000 is classified as which type of class town?
qs.e: According to the Census of India 2011, towns are classified into six classes based on population. Class V includes towns with a population between 5,000 and 9,999. Towns with a population of 10,000 or more fall under Class IV, while those with less than 5,000 are classified as Class VI. This classification aids in administrative planning and development of urban areas.
qs.kf:
☛ Class I town population range → 100,000 or more
☛ Class II town population range → 50,000 to 99,999
☛ Class III town population range → 20,000 to 49,999
☛ Class IV town population range → 10,000 to 19,999
☛ Class VI town population range → Less than 5,000

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Where is the Indian naval air station INS Baaz located?
qs.e: The Indian naval air station INS Baaz is located on Great Nicobar Island, which is the southernmost part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. INS Baaz was commissioned in 2012 and strengthens India's surveillance and strategic presence in the Indian Ocean. It operates naval Dornier aircraft and helicopters and is strategically positioned near the Malacca Strait.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is INS Baaz located? → Great Nicobar Island
☛ When was INS Baaz commissioned? → 2012
☛ Which island group is Great Nicobar part of? → Andaman and Nicobar Islands
☛ What type of aircraft operate from INS Baaz? → Dornier and helicopters
☛ Which ocean is INS Baaz near? → Indian Ocean

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1
q: According to the office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, a city with a population exceeding 10 million is classified as which type of urban settlement?
qs.e: According to the office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, a city with a population exceeding 10 million is classified as a Mega City. This classification defines the size of urban settlements and aids in planning and resource allocation. Cities falling under this category include major metropolises like Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, and Pune. It is important to note that the term 'Metropolitan City' generally refers to cities with a population of more than 1 million, whereas 'Mega City' specifically refers to those with over 10 million population. This classification is crucial for urban development and administrative planning.
qs.kf:
☛ Population threshold for Mega City → Over 10 million
☛ Population threshold for Metropolitan City → Over 1 million
☛ Most populous city in India → Mumbai
☛ Definition of Mega City → 10 million+ population
☛ Classifying authority → Registrar General and Census Commissioner

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Narcondam Island is located in:
qs.e: Narcondam Island is located in the Andaman Sea, which is part of the northeastern Indian Ocean. It is a small volcanic island belonging to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, a union territory of India. The island covers an area of about 6.8 square kilometers and is a dormant volcano, with its last eruption occurring approximately 100,000 years ago. Narcondam is renowned for its biodiversity, particularly the Narcondam hornbill (Rhyticeros narcondami), a bird species found exclusively on this island. Administratively, it falls under the North Andaman district. The island is a protected area and a popular site for researchers and nature enthusiasts due to its unique ecological significance.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Narcondam Island located? → Andaman Sea
☛ Which union territory does Narcondam Island belong to? → Andaman and Nicobar Islands
☛ Which unique bird species is found only on Narcondam Island? → Narcondam hornbill
☛ What type of island is Narcondam? → Volcanic island
☛ What is the status of the Narcondam volcano? → Dormant

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 2
q: According to the Economic Survey 2022-23 (data of 2021), what percentage of India's population resides in rural areas?
qs.e: According to the Economic Survey 2022-23 (based on 2021 data), approximately 65% of India's population resides in rural areas. This indicates that India is still a predominantly rural economy. The high percentage of rural population underscores the need for focusing on agriculture, rural development, and infrastructure. According to the 2021 census data, there is a declining trend in rural population, but it still remains the majority. The urbanization rate is slow, and the government is emphasizing rural employment, health, and education.
qs.kf:
☛ Percentage of rural population in India (2021) → 65%
☛ Percentage of urban population (2021) → 35%
☛ Reason for decline in rural population → Urbanization and migration
☛ State with highest urbanization → Goa (62%)
☛ State with lowest urbanization → Himachal Pradesh (10%)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 2
q: Dhordo, the venue of Rann Utsav (from December, 2024 to February, 2025), is located in which Indian state and near what geographical feature?
qs.e: Dhordo is situated in the Indian state of Gujarat, near the Rann of Kutch – a vast salt marsh. It serves as the venue for the annual Rann Utsav, which runs from December to February. The Rann of Kutch is a seasonally dry salt desert located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, known for its white salt landscapes and cultural richness. This festival showcases local crafts, folk dances, and cuisine, attracting tourists from across the world.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Rann Utsav held? → Dhordo in Kutch district, Gujarat
☛ Near which geographical feature is Dhordo located? → Rann of Kutch
☛ Which state has the Rann of Kutch? → Gujarat
☛ What is the duration of Rann Utsav? → December to February
☛ What type of landform is the Rann of Kutch? → Salt marsh (salt desert)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 2
q: In which state of India is the Bhil tribal community found in large numbers?
qs.e: The Bhil tribe is one of the largest tribal communities in India. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra. Madhya Pradesh has the highest population of the Bhil tribe. These tribal communities reside in hilly and forest areas. Their language is Bhil which belongs to the Indo-Aryan language family. The main occupations of the Bhils are agriculture and hunting. Their major festivals include Gol and Bhagoria.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state has the largest Bhil population? → Madhya Pradesh
☛ What is the language of the Bhil tribe? → Bhili
☛ What is a major festival of the Bhil tribe? → Bhagoria
☛ What is the main occupation of the Bhil community? → Agriculture and hunting
☛ Which language family does Bhili belong to? → Indo-Aryan

q: Find the odd one out in relation world heritage sites.
qs.e: Rashtrapati Bhavan is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site, while the other three are. Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (Mumbai) was declared a World Heritage Site in 2004. Taj Mahal (Agra) has been a World Heritage Site since 1983. Sun Temple (Konark) was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1984. Rashtrapati Bhavan, located in New Delhi, is the official residence of the President of India but does not hold UNESCO World Heritage status. Hence, it is the odd one out among the given options.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → Rashtrapati Bhavan
☛ Year Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus became a World Heritage Site? → 2004
☛ Year Taj Mahal became a World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ Year Konark Sun Temple became a World Heritage Site? → 1984
☛ City where Rashtrapati Bhavan is located? → New Delhi

q: Find the odd one out.
qs.e: Silent Valley, Indus valley, and Damodar valley are located in India, while Santa Clara Valley is in the United States (California). Silent Valley is a national park in Kerala. Indus valley is the valley of the Indus river, spanning India and Pakistan. Damodar valley is famous for its coal fields in West Bengal and Jharkhand. Santa Clara Valley is known as Silicon Valley and is outside India.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Silent Valley in? → Kerala
☛ Which river is associated with Indus valley? → Indus river
☛ What is Damodar valley known for? → Coal fields
☛ What is the other name of Santa Clara Valley? → Silicon Valley
☛ Which country is Silicon Valley in? → United States of America

q: National Air Quality Index is determined on the basis of concentration of ________ pollutants.
qs.e: The National Air Quality Index (NAQI) is a standard for measuring air quality in India. It is determined based on the concentration of 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb (Lead). For each pollutant, a health-based sub-index is calculated, and the final AQI equals the worst sub-index among them. This system classifies air quality into six categories (Good to Severe).
qs.kf:
☛ Number of pollutants in NAQI → 8
☛ Primary parameters of NAQI → PM2.5 and PM10
☛ Number of AQI categories → 6 (Good to Severe)
☛ Implementing agency of NAQI → CPCB
☛ City with highest AQI (commonly) → Delhi

q: Which dynasty had its capital at Chittorgarh?
qs.e: Sisodia dynasty ruled over Mewar with its capital at Chittorgarh. Chittorgarh is a historic fort and city in Rajasthan, serving as a major political center during the Sisodia rule. Famous rulers of this dynasty include Maharana Pratap and Rana Kumbha. The Sisodia clan was a branch of the Guhil dynasty that governed the Mewar region. Chittorgarh remained under Sisodia control, though it faced attacks from the Delhi Sultanate and Mughals at various times. The Chauhan, Hada, and Rather dynasties are other Rajput clans but they did not have their capital at Chittorgarh.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the founder of the Sisodia dynasty of Mewar? → Rana Hammir Singh
☛ On which river is Chittorgarh fort located? → Banas River
☛ Famous Sisodia ruler who fought the Battle of Haldighati? → Maharana Pratap
☛ Who first attacked Chittorgarh? → Alauddin Khilji
☛ Which famous pillar was built by Rana Kumbha? → Kirti Stambha

q: Which is the 29th state of India created in 2014?
qs.e: Telangana became the 29th state of India on 2 June 2014, formed by bifurcating Andhra Pradesh. It was created under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014. Hyderabad served as the joint capital for both states initially, but later became the capital of Telangana, while Amaravati was developed as the capital of Andhra Pradesh. Telangana is the 11th largest state by area in India. The movement for a separate Telangana state was led by K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR), who became its first Chief Minister. The state was formed after decades of agitation and political struggle. The demand was primarily based on issues of regional development and cultural identity of the Telangana region.
qs.kf:
☛ Latest state formed in India → Telangana
☛ Year of formation of Telangana → 2014
☛ Capital of Telangana → Hyderabad
☛ First Chief Minister of Telangana → K. Chandrashekar Rao
☛ State from which Telangana was carved out → Andhra Pradesh

q: Where is the Sabarimala temple located?
qs.e: The Sabarimala Temple is located in the Pathanamthitta district of Kerala, India. It is dedicated to Lord Ayyappa and situated in the Western Ghats mountain ranges. This temple is a major Hindu pilgrimage center, attracting millions of devotees each year. The temple is known for its 41-day rigorous penance called Mala Dharan observed before pilgrimage. It is also famous for its unique traditions and the controversy regarding entry of women.
qs.kf:
☛ Which state is Sabarimala Temple located in? → Kerala
☛ Sabarimala Temple is dedicated to which deity? → Lord Ayyappa
☛ Which district is the temple in? → Pathanamthitta
☛ How many days of penance are required before pilgrimage? → 41 days
☛ Sabarimala is situated in which mountain range? → Western Ghats

q: Where are the Elephanta caves situated?
qs.e: The Elephanta Caves are located on Gharapuri Island in the Arabian Sea, near Mumbai, Maharashtra. These caves are a collection of cave temples primarily dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. They were built between the 5th and 7th centuries. The most famous sculpture is the Trimurti, a three-faced bust of Shiva. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Portuguese named it Elephanta after a stone elephant statue.
qs.kf:
☛ On which island are the Elephanta Caves located? → Gharapuri Island
☛ What is the famous sculpture in Elephanta Caves? → Trimurti (three-faced Shiva)
☛ To which religion do the Elephanta Caves belong? → Hinduism (Shiva)
☛ During which centuries were the caves built? → 5th-7th centuries
☛ Which organization declared it a World Heritage Site? → UNESCO

q: Which is the state that leads in the list of monuments of national importance in South India declared by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)?
qs.e: In the list of monuments of national importance in South India declared by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Karnataka leads with the highest number of monuments. Karnataka has over 500 monuments of national importance, the highest among South Indian states. It is followed by Tamil Nadu with around 400 monuments. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana together have about 300 monuments, while Kerala has the fewest, around 100. Key monuments in Karnataka include Hampi, Belur, Halebidu, and Pattadakal. ASI protects a total of about 3700 monuments of national importance across India.
qs.kf:
☛ Highest national monuments in South India → Karnataka
☛ Second highest in South India → Tamil Nadu
☛ Famous monument site in Karnataka → Hampi
☛ ASI headquarters → Kolkata
☛ Total national importance monuments in India → About 3700

q: Where is the Radio Astronomy Centre of India located?
qs.e: The Radio Astronomy Centre (RAC) of India is located in Udhagamandalam (Ooty), Tamil Nadu. It is a major division of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA). The centre operates one of the world's largest heliographic cosmic ray telescopes and a radio telescope known as the Ooty Radio Telescope (ORT). Established in 1970, it primarily conducts research in millimetre wave and sub-millimetre astronomy for mapping carbon monoxide and other molecular clouds. The high altitude and clear weather of Ooty make it an ideal location for radio astronomy observations.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is India's first radio telescope located? → Udhagamandalam (Ooty)
☛ Which institute does the Radio Astronomy Centre belong to? → Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA)
☛ Where is the National Radio Astrophysics Centre located? → Pune
☛ Where is the Planetary Radar Astronomy Centre located? → Thumba
☛ Which centre conducts heliographic cosmic ray experiments? → Udhagamandalam

q: Sabarimala Sri Ayyappa temple is situated in the state of:
qs.e: Sabarimala Sri Ayyappa temple is located in the Pathanamthitta district of Kerala state. This temple is dedicated to Lord Ayyappa and is a major Hindu pilgrimage site. It is situated in the hills of the Western Ghats and is traditionally visited after observing a 41-day fasting period called Mandalam. The temple is one of the most famous in Kerala, attracting millions of devotees each year. Male devotees wear black clothing, while women were traditionally barred from entering during menstruation, a restriction lifted by the Supreme Court in 2018.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Sabarimala temple located? → Pathanamthitta, Kerala
☛ Who is worshipped at Sabarimala? → Lord Ayyappa
☛ How long is the Sabarimala pilgrimage? → 41 days (Mandalam)
☛ In which forest is Sabarimala temple situated? → Western Ghats (Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary)
☛ What color of clothing is worn at Sabarimala? → Black or blue

q: In which of the following regions is Mount Kailash situated?
qs.e: Mount Kailash, also known as Kailash Parvat, is situated in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It is a part of the Himalayan mountain range and has an elevation of 6,638 meters above sea level. This mountain is considered sacred in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and the Bon religion. In Hinduism, it is believed to be the abode of Lord Shiva. The circumambulation around Mount Kailash, known as Kailash Parikrama, is a significant pilgrimage. It is located near Lake Manasarovar, which is also considered holy. Geologically, Kailash is composed of metamorphic rocks and has not been climbed by any mountaineer to date.
qs.kf:
☛ In which country is Mount Kailash located? → Tibet (China)
☛ What is the height of Mount Kailash? → 6,638 meters
☛ Which sacred lake is near Mount Kailash? → Lake Manasarovar
☛ In Hinduism, which deity resides on Mount Kailash? → Lord Shiva
☛ In which religion is Kailash considered an 'Asana'? → Jainism

q: Which of the following is NOT a correct pair of a country and its capital?
qs.e: The capital of Kazakhstan is Astana (now Nur-Sultan), while Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan. The other three pairs are correct: Bahamas capital is Nassau, Libya capital is Tripoli, and Belgium capital is Brussels. This question tests knowledge of countries and their capitals, a key part of general awareness. Kazakhstan is the largest country in Central Asia, while Kyrgyzstan is also located in Central Asia.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Kazakhstan → Nur-Sultan (Astana)
☛ Capital of Kyrgyzstan → Bishkek
☛ Capital of Bahamas → Nassau
☛ Capital of Libya → Tripoli
☛ Capital of Belgium → Brussels

q: In which of the following cities is the Forest Survey of India located?
qs.e: The Forest Survey of India (FSI) is headquartered in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It operates under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and assesses the forest resources of the country. FSI publishes the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) every two years, providing data on forest cover and carbon stock. Dehradun is also known for the Indian Forest Service (IFS) and the Forest Research Institute (FRI). The city is a hub for national forest policy and conservation efforts. Other options: Delhi houses the forest ministry, Lucknow has a regional office, and Kolkata hosts the Zoological Survey of India.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of Forest Survey of India → Dehradun
☛ Ministry under Forest Survey of India operates → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Publication frequency of India State of Forest Report → Two years
☛ Location of Indian Forest Service (IFS) → Dehradun
☛ Location of Forest Research Institute (FRI) → Dehradun

q: The Suez Canal, which is very significant for commerce, was constructed in which of the following countries?
qs.e: The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway in Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. Constructed between 1859 and 1869 under the leadership of French engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps, it serves as a crucial maritime route for commerce between Asia and Europe, eliminating the need to navigate around Africa. The canal is approximately 193.30 kilometers long and is one of the world's busiest waterways. In 1956, Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the canal, leading to the Suez Crisis. The canal is a vital source of revenue for Egypt and a key geopolitical asset.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the Suez Canal located? → Egypt
☛ Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect? → Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea
☛ When was the Suez Canal completed? → 1869
☛ Who nationalized the Suez Canal? → Gamal Abdel Nasser
☛ What is the length of the Suez Canal? → Approximately 193.30 km

q: India's first costume museum is situated at ________.
qs.e: India's first costume museum is located in Panaji, Goa. This museum is dedicated to costume and textiles, featuring historical garments and fabrics. It was established by the Goa government to promote culture and heritage. It serves as a major tourist and cultural attraction in Goa.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first costume museum → located in Panaji, Goa
☛ India's first national costume museum → in Goa
☛ State bird of Goa → bulbul
☛ Largest city of Goa → Panaji
☛ Goa became a state → 30 May 1987

q: The Institute of Forest Biodiversity (IFB) is situated in _______.
qs.e: The Institute of Forest Biodiversity (IFB) is a regional centre under the Forest Survey of India (FSI) located in Hyderabad. It focuses on the conservation, research, and management of forest biodiversity. The institute studies various ecosystems and plant species, aiming to ensure sustainable use of forest resources and conservation of biodiversity. IFB covers the southern and central parts of India and operates under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
qs.kf:
☛ Headquarters of IFB → Hyderabad
☛ Area covered by IFB → Southern and Central India
☛ Ministry associated with IFB → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
☛ Headquarters of Forest Survey of India → Dehradun
☛ Primary function of IFB → Forest biodiversity research and conservation

q: In economics terminology, NSDL stands for :
qs.e: NSDL stands for National Securities Depositories Limited. It is India's first and largest depository, established in 1996. Its primary function is to hold and transfer securities like shares and debentures in electronic form. NSDL enhanced transparency and security in the stock market through demat accounts. Its main promoters include IDBI Bank, Unit Trust of India (UTI), and National Stock Exchange (NSE). Without NSDL, modern stock market operations would be impossible.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NSDL established? → 1996
☛ Where is the headquarters of NSDL? → Mumbai
☛ Who are the main promoters of NSDL? → IDBI Bank, UTI, NSE
☛ What type of institution is NSDL? → Depository (securities holding)
☛ What is the full form of NSDL? → National Securities Depositories Limited

q: The national calendar based on the Saka Era, with Chaitra as its first month, was adopted from the year:
qs.e: India's national calendar is based on the Saka Era, with Chaitra as its first month. It was adopted on 22 March 1957, which corresponded to the start of Saka Year 1879. This calendar is used alongside the Gregorian calendar and has a duration of 365 days. It is also called the Indian National Calendar. It was formulated by the Calendar Reform Committee chaired by the eminent scientist Meghnad Saha. The committee recommended that the calendar be implemented from 1 Chaitra 1879 Saka (22 March 1957). The calendar has 365 days in a common year and 366 days in a leap year.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of adoption of national calendar → 1957
☛ First month of Saka calendar → Chaitra
☛ Chairman of Calendar Reform Committee → Meghnad Saha
☛ Alternate name of national calendar → Indian National Calendar
☛ Number of days in a common year → 365

q: Where was Vikramshila University located?
qs.e: Vikramshila University was a prominent ancient center of learning in India, established by King Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty in the late 8th century. It was located in present-day Bihar state, in Bhagalpur district. The university was renowned for the study of Buddhism and particularly emphasized tantric education. It was considered the second most important Buddhist learning center after Nalanda University. The university was destroyed in the 12th century during the invasion of Bakhtiyar Khilji.
qs.kf:
☛ Who founded Vikramshila University? → Dharmapala
☛ On which river is Vikramshila located? → Ganga
☛ What type of education was emphasized at Vikramshila? → Tantric education
☛ Who destroyed Vikramshila? → Bakhtiyar Khilji
☛ Which dynasty was associated with Vikramshila? → Pala dynasty

q: The capital of Cuba is-
qs.e: The capital of Cuba is Havana, a major port city located on the coast of the Caribbean Sea. Havana is the largest city in Cuba and serves as its cultural, economic, and political center. It was founded in 1515 by Spanish colonists. The city is known for its colonial architecture, vintage cars, and rich musical heritage. Cuba is a Caribbean island nation located south of the United States. Other options: Cairo is the capital of Egypt, Brazilian refers to the former capital of Brazil, and Kyoto is a city in Japan.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Cuba → Havana
☛ National sport of Cuba → Baseball
☛ Currency of Cuba → Cuban peso
☛ Major religion in Cuba → Christianity (Catholic)
☛ Famous revolutionary leader from Cuba → Fidel Castro

q: In which of these cities is the Iron Pillar of Mehrauli located?
qs.e: The Iron Pillar of Mehrauli is located in Delhi, specifically in the Mehrauli area. It is about 7 meters tall and weighs 6 tons. It was built during the Gupta period under the reign of Chandragupta II. The pillar is famous for its rust-resistance, having not rusted for over 1600 years. Its composition includes 98% iron. Originally dedicated to Vishnu, it bears an inscription in Sanskrit.
qs.kf:
☛ Height of Mehrauli Iron Pillar → 7 meters
☛ Period of Iron Pillar construction → Gupta period
☛ Deity dedicated to Iron Pillar → Vishnu
☛ Weight of Iron Pillar → 6 tons
☛ Language of inscription on Iron Pillar → Sanskrit

q: Which of the following countries has more than one standard meridian?
qs.e: The USA is the only country among the options that has more than one standard meridian. This is because the USA spans a vast longitudinal extent of about 4,700 km from east to west, covering four time zones: Eastern, Central, Mountain, and Pacific. Each time zone uses a different standard meridian: Eastern at 75°W, Central at 90°W, Mountain at 105°W, and Pacific at 120°W. Smaller countries like Japan, India, and Afghanistan have limited east-west extent and thus fall within a single time zone, using only one standard meridian each. However, some other large countries like Russia and Canada also have multiple standard meridians, but among the given options, only the USA qualifies.
qs.kf:
☛ How many standard meridians does the USA have? → Four main (Eastern, Central, Mountain, Pacific)
☛ What is the easternmost standard meridian of the USA? → 75°W (Eastern Time)
☛ What is the westernmost standard meridian of the USA? → 120°W (Pacific Time)
☛ What is the standard meridian of India? → 82.5°E
☛ What is the standard meridian of Japan? → 135°E

q: Itanagar is the capital of -
qs.e: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh. It is located in Papum Pare district and is the largest city in the state. Arunachal Pradesh is a state in Northeast India, bordering China, Myanmar, and Bhutan. The state was formed on 20 February 1987. The name Itanagar derives from Ita (brick) and nagar (city), referring to ancient brick forts. The city is known for its natural beauty and cultural diversity.
qs.kf:
☛ Capital of Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar
☛ Largest city of Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar
☛ District where Itanagar is located → Papum Pare
☛ Formation day of Arunachal Pradesh → 20 February 1987
☛ Borders of Arunachal Pradesh → China, Myanmar, Bhutan

q: Name the capital of Pakistan. A. Rawalpindi B. Islamabad
C. Karachi D. Lahore
qs.e: The capital of Pakistan is Islamabad. It is located in the northeastern part of the country on the Potohar Plateau. It was built in the 1960s to replace Karachi as the capital. Situated near the Margalla Hills, the city is known for its greenery and modern planning. Rawalpindi is a nearby city that served as the interim capital during the construction. Karachi is the largest city and economic hub of Pakistan, while Lahore is the capital of Punjab province. Major institutions like the Parliament House, Prime Minister's Office, and Faisal Mosque are located in Islamabad.
qs.kf:
☛ Establishment of Pakistan → 1947
☛ First capital → Karachi
☛ Current capital → Islamabad
☛ Presidential Palace → Islamabad
☛ Largest city → Karachi

q: What is total forest cover of India as per ISFR report 2019?
o: 24.39% of the total geographical area of the country
21.67% of the total geographical area of the country
24.16% of the total geographical area of the country
21.05% of the total geographical area of the country
qs.e: As per ISFR 2019, the total forest cover of India is 7,12,249 sq km, which is 21.67% of the country's geographical area. The report also states tree cover of 95,027 sq km (2.89%) and total forest & tree cover of 8,07,276 sq km (24.56%). Compared to the 2017 assessment, forest cover has increased by 5,188 sq km. The state with the largest forest cover is Madhya Pradesh (77,482 sq km), while Mizoram has the highest percentage of forest cover (85.41%).
qs.kf:
☛ Increase in forest cover in ISFR 2019 (sq km) → 5,188
☛ State with largest forest cover → Madhya Pradesh
☛ State with smallest forest cover → Haryana
☛ Tree cover percentage in ISFR 2019 → 2.89%
☛ State with highest forest cover percentage → Mizoram

q: Which public sector company provides helicopter service for the use of tourists in hilly areas?
qs.e: Pawan Hans Limited is a public sector company that provides helicopter services for tourists in hilly and remote areas of India. It operates in regions like Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and the northeastern states. The company is headquartered in Noida and functions under the Ministry of Civil Aviation. Air India primarily offers fixed-wing aircraft services, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited manufactures aircraft, and Global Vectra Helicorp is a private sector company. Pawan Hans also provides services for oil and gas exploration, emergency medical evacuation, and charter flights.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which ministry does Pawan Hans Limited operate? → Ministry of Civil Aviation
☛ Where is the headquarters of Pawan Hans Limited? → Noida, Uttar Pradesh
☛ What type of services does Pawan Hans Limited provide? → Helicopter services (tourist, charter, emergency)
☛ Which is the major public sector helicopter service company in India? → Pawan Hans Limited
☛ When was Pawan Hans Limited established? → 1985

q: The National Library of India is situated at:
qs.e: The National Library of India is situated in Kolkata. It is the largest library in India, located at Belvedere Estate. It was established in 1836 as the Calcutta Public Library and was renamed the National Library in 1948. It functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. The library holds millions of books, manuscripts, rare texts, and newspapers in various languages. It is considered the national treasure of India and one of the most important research institutions in the country. The library also serves as a depository for all publications published in India under the Delivery of Books and Newspapers Act.
qs.kf:
☛ Location of National Library of India → Kolkata
☛ Largest library in India → Kolkata
☛ National Library comes under which ministry → Ministry of Culture
☛ Former name of National Library → Calcutta Public Library
☛ Estate where National Library is located → Belvedere Estate

q: What is the name of India's first research station located at the International Arctic Research Base Ny-Alesund Svalbard, Norway?
qs.e: India's first Arctic research station is Himadri, located at the International Arctic Research Base Ny-Alesund Svalbard, Norway. It was established in 2008. Himadri focuses on research in climate change, glaciology, atmospheric sciences, and biodiversity in the Arctic region. It is part of India's polar research program, operated by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR). Besides Himadri, India's Antarctic research stations are Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri, and Bharathi.
qs.kf:
☛ India's first Arctic research station → Himadri
☛ Location of Himadri → Ny-Alesund Svalbard, Norway
☛ Year of establishment of Himadri → 2008
☛ Operating agency for Himadri → NCPOR
☛ Antarctic research stations of India → Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri, Bharathi

q: The 'Amar Jawan Jyoti' (Flame of the Immortal Soldier) was installed at the _________ in January 1972.
qs.e: The Amar Jawan Jyoti is a memorial flame that burns in memory of India's martyred soldiers. It was installed at India Gate, New Delhi in January 1972. The flame was inaugurated by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in remembrance of the soldiers who died in the 1971 India-Pakistan war. The Jyoti is situated on a black marble pedestal, which has an inverted rifle with a soldier's helmet on top. The Amar Jawan Jyoti was built to keep alive the memory of the Indian army's sacrifice. In 2022, the flame was merged with the National War Memorial flame.
qs.kf:
☛ Amar Jawan Jyoti installation date → January 1972
☛ Who inaugurated Amar Jawan Jyoti → Prime Minister Indira Gandhi
☛ Amar Jawan Jyoti dedicated to which war martyrs → 1971 India-Pakistan war
☛ What is placed on the Amar Jawan Jyoti pedestal → Inverted rifle and a helmet
☛ Where was Amar Jawan Jyoti merged in 2022 → National War Memorial

q: Juhu Beach in Mumbai is a part of the:
qs.e: Juhu Beach in Mumbai is a part of the Arabian Sea. The Arabian Sea is a northwestern part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by the Arabian Peninsula to the west, Iran and Pakistan to the north, and India to the east. It lies along the western coast of India, with states such as Maharashtra, Goa, and Kerala having coastlines on it. Juhu Beach is a popular beach located in the western suburbs of Mumbai. The Arabian Sea has saline water and is important for fishing and trade. Its maximum depth is about 4,652 meters.
qs.kf:
☛ Which is the longest beach in India? → Marina Beach, Chennai (Bay of Bengal)
☛ Which sea is Goa's coastline in? → Arabian Sea
☛ Which is the largest sea in the Indian Ocean? → Arabian Sea
☛ Which sea is on the western coast of India? → Arabian Sea
☛ Which city is Juhu Beach in? → Mumbai

q: The precautionary principle was first introduced in
o: The First International Conference on Protection of the North Sea
qs.e: The precautionary principle was first introduced in 1987 at the First International Conference on the Protection of the North Sea. This principle states that if an activity poses a threat to the environment or human health, preventive measures should be taken even in the absence of full scientific certainty. Later, in 1992, it was included as Principle 15 of the Rio Declaration at the Earth Summit. The Kyoto Protocol deals with climate change, and the Vienna Convention relates to the protection of the ozone layer.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the precautionary principle first introduced? → North Sea Conference (1987)
☛ Which principle of the Rio Declaration includes the precautionary principle? → Principle 15
☛ When was the Earth Summit held? → 1992, Rio de Janeiro
☛ The Kyoto Protocol is related to? → Climate change
☛ The Vienna Convention is related to? → Ozone layer protection

q: What kind of a state is Delhi?
o: National Capital Region and Union Territory
qs.e: Delhi is a special state in India, designated as the National Capital Territory (NCT) under the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act 1991. It is a Union Territory with a elected legislative assembly and council of ministers, but subjects like police, land, and public order are under the control of the central government. It does not have full statehood and functions as a semi-state. Although administered by a Chief Minister and assembly, the central government has special powers through the President's rule. Thus, it is both a Union Territory and a National Capital Region.
qs.kf:
☛ Constitutional status of Delhi → National Capital Territory
☛ When 69th Amendment Act enacted → 1991
☛ Subjects not with Delhi government → Police, Land, Law and Order
☛ Administrator of Delhi → Lieutenant Governor (appointed by Centre)
☛ Delhi Assembly strength → 70 members

q: International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) was created in _________ for rural poverty reduction in developing Countries.
qs.e: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) was established in 1977. It is a specialized agency of the United Nations headquartered in Rome. IFAD's primary goal is to reduce rural poverty in developing countries and enhance agricultural productivity. Its creation was recommended by the 1974 World Food Conference, leading to an agreement in 1976, and IFAD officially came into existence on 30 November 1977. The organization provides financial support and technical assistance to smallholder farmers, landless people, and rural women. IFAD member countries are categorized into three groups: OECD, OPEC, and developing countries.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is the headquarters of IFAD located? → Rome, Italy
☛ What type of organization is IFAD? → Specialized agency of the United Nations
☛ Which conference recommended the establishment of IFAD? → 1974 World Food Conference
☛ What is the objective of IFAD? → Reduce rural poverty in developing countries
☛ How many categories of member countries are there in IFAD? → Three (OECD, OPEC, developing countries)

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Which of the following is an example of a Tier I city in India
qs.e: In India, cities are classified into Tier I, II, and III based on economic activity, population, and infrastructure. Tier I cities are the most developed, including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, and Pune. These cities serve as national and global economic hubs. Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal and a major port city, is known for its cultural heritage and financial activities. Tier I cities offer a high standard of living, better infrastructure, and more employment opportunities. They attract significant investment and have well-developed transport networks.
qs.kf:
☛ How many Tier I cities does India have? → 8
☛ Which are the newest Tier I cities added? → Pune and Ahmedabad
☛ Which organization classifies Tier I cities? → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
☛ Which river is Kolkata located on? → Hooghly River
☛ Which city is known as the financial capital of India? → Mumbai

q: Which of the following cities has emerged as the most important centre with nearly half the cotton mills of the state located there?
qs.e: Coimbatore is a major industrial city in Tamil Nadu, often called the 'Manchester of South India'. Nearly half of the state's cotton mills are located here, making it the most important centre for the cotton textile industry. The city is renowned for its textile industry, especially cotton textiles. Coimbatore houses many large cotton mills that contribute significantly to employment and the economy. Other options like Bengaluru, Madurai, and Chennai are also industrial cities, but Coimbatore leads in the number of cotton mills. Thus, this city is the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Which city is known as the Manchester of South India? → Coimbatore
☛ Which is the largest centre of cotton mills in Tamil Nadu? → Coimbatore
☛ What is the major industry in Coimbatore? → Cotton textile industry
☛ In which Indian state is Coimbatore located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which river flows through Coimbatore? → Noyyal River

q: Since 2008, the United Nations is running a program REDD to create awareness for the importance of carbon stored in the forests, reduction of carbon emissions and investment in low carbon development. What does REDD stand for?
o: Recycling Energy from Deforestation and Forest Degradation
Renewable Energy from Disintegration and Forest Degradation
Reducing Emissions from Disintegration and Forest Degradation
Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation
qs.e: REDD stands for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation. It is a United Nations program launched in 2008 to create awareness about the importance of carbon stored in forests and to reduce carbon emissions from deforestation and forest degradation. REDD provides incentives for developing countries to protect and sustainably manage their forests. It plays a critical role in climate change mitigation as forests act as carbon sinks. The program promotes investment in low carbon development and recognizes the value of forest carbon. Among the options, only the fourth option correctly uses 'Deforestation' and 'Degradation', matching the full form of REDD.
qs.kf:
☛ What does REDD stand for? → Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation
☛ When was REDD launched? → 2008
☛ Which organization runs REDD? → United Nations
☛ What is the main goal of REDD? → Reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation
☛ REDD contributes to which area? → Climate change mitigation

q: The ______ sector is the largest sector of India, contributing to a Gross Value Added (GVA) of ₹92.26 lakh crore in 2018-19.
qs.e: The service sector is the largest contributor to the Indian economy. In 2018-19, its Gross Value Added (GVA) was ₹92.26 lakh crore, accounting for about 55% of the total GVA. The service sector includes activities such as IT, telecommunications, banking, tourism, education, and healthcare. This sector plays a crucial role in employment and GDP growth. Agriculture and manufacturing sectors contribute relatively less. The service sector has also shown high growth rates, helping India emerge as a global service hub.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest sector in India (by GVA) → Service sector
☛ GVA of service sector in 2018-19 → ₹92.26 lakh crore
☛ Major sub-sectors included in services → IT, banking, tourism
☛ Second largest sector in India → Manufacturing
☛ Share of service sector in total GVA → Approximately 55%

q: When did Bangladesh emerge as an independent country?
qs.e: Bangladesh was part of Pakistan as East Pakistan. In 1971, the Liberation War took place between the Pakistani army and Bangladeshi freedom fighters (Mukti Bahini). After India's intervention, Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971, leading to the birth of Bangladesh. Bangladesh emerged as a secular democracy and Sheikh Mujibur Rahman became its first Prime Minister. Bangladesh gained membership in the United Nations in 1974.
qs.kf:
☛ Who was the leader of the Bangladesh Liberation War? → Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
☛ Who was the first President of Bangladesh? → Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
☛ When is the National Day of Bangladesh celebrated? → March 26
☛ When is Victory Day of Bangladesh? → December 16
☛ What is the capital of Bangladesh? → Dhaka

q: In which of the following cities is the Mahakaleshwar temple situated?
qs.e: The Mahakaleshwar temple is located in the city of Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple is renowned for its unique south-facing (dakshinamukhi) tradition, which distinguishes it from other Shiva temples. The present structure was built in the 18th century by the Maratha rulers. Ujjain was known as Ujjayini in ancient times and was the capital of King Vikramaditya. The temple is situated on the banks of the Kshipra River and is considered highly sacred in Hinduism. On the occasion of Mahashivaratri, special prayers and fairs are held here.
qs.kf:

☛ Where is Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga? → Srisailam, Andhra Pradesh
☛ Where is Vishwanath temple (Kashi)? → Varanasi
☛ Where is Rameswaram temple? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Where is Kedarnath temple? → Uttarakhand

q: Which is the newest state of India?
qs.e: The newest state of India is Telangana, formed on 2 June 2014. It was carved out of Andhra Pradesh and became the 29th state of India. No new state has been formed after Telangana. The capital of Telangana is Hyderabad, which also served as the joint capital with Andhra Pradesh. The main reason for the formation of Telangana was regional development and cultural identity. The state is known for its IT industry and historical sites like Charminar and Golconda Fort.

q: Kanpur, a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, is an example of which type of town?
qs.e: Kanpur is a major industrial town in Uttar Pradesh, famous worldwide for its leather industry. It houses numerous leather factories, textile mills, and chemical industries. Kanpur is often called the 'Manchester of the East'. The city is situated on the banks of the Ganges River and has a high population density due to industrial development. Kanpur also has defense production facilities like the Ordnance Factory. This city does not fall under administrative or recreational categories but is classified as an industrial town because of its heavy industrial activities.

☛ On which river is Kanpur situated? → Ganges River

☛ Which is the largest industrial city in Uttar Pradesh? → Kanpur

q: The holy city of Mecca is located in _____.
A. UAE
B. Saudi Arab
C. Qatar
D. Abu Dhabi
qs.e: Mecca is the holiest city in Islam and is located in the Hejaz region of Saudi Arabia. It is the birthplace of Prophet Muhammad and home to the Kaaba, the direction of prayer for Muslims worldwide. Millions of Muslims visit Mecca annually for Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages. Saudi Arabia's capital is Riyadh, and the country is known for its oil reserves and Islamic heritage sites. The city of Medina, another holy site, is also located in Saudi Arabia.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Medina located? → Saudi Arabia
☛ What is the holiest site in Islam? → Kaaba (Mecca)
☛ What is the capital of Saudi Arabia? → Riyadh
☛ In which city is Hajj performed? → Mecca
☛ Where is the Kaaba located? → Mecca

q: Which one of the following is the tallest statue in the world?
qs.e: The tallest statue in the world is the 'Statue of Unity', located in Gujarat, India. It stands at a height of 182 metres (597 feet), making it the world's tallest statue. It was unveiled on 31 October 2018, on the 143rd birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The statue is situated near the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada River. The second tallest statue is the 'Spring Temple Buddha' in China, with a height of 128 metres. The 'Statue of Liberty' in the USA is 93 metres tall, and the 'Great Buddha of Thailand' is 92 metres tall. The Statue of Unity is made of bronze and steel and is built with earthquake-resistant technology. It symbolises national unity and is a major tourist attraction.
qs.kf:
☛ World's tallest statue → Statue of Unity (India)
☛ Height of Statue of Unity → 182 metres
☛ Location of Statue of Unity → Gujarat, India (Narmada district)
☛ Unveiling date of Statue of Unity → 31 October 2018
☛ Statue of Unity is dedicated to → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

q: Where is the famous Somnath temple located?
A. Tamil Nadu
B. Uttar Pradesh
C. Gujarat
D. Rajasthan
qs.e: The famous Somnath Temple is located in the Gujarat state of India, in the Saurashtra region. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, it is considered the first among the 12 Jyotirlingas. The temple has a rich ancient history, with references found in the Rigveda. It was looted and destroyed multiple times by foreign invaders, most notably by Mahmud of Ghazni. The current structure was rebuilt in 1951 under the efforts of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The temple is situated on the coast of the Arabian Sea, adding to its grandeur.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is Somnath Temple located? → Gujarat
☛ To which god is Somnath dedicated? → Lord Shiva
☛ Which Jyotirlinga is Somnath considered? → First Jyotirlinga
☛ Who rebuilt the Somnath Temple? → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Which water body is the Somnath Temple near? → Arabian Sea

q: Since the year _______, flame of Amar Jawan Jyoti is continuously burning under the famous monument of India Gate at New Delhi.
qs.e: The Amar Jawan Jyoti is located under the famous monument India Gate in New Delhi. This eternal flame is dedicated to the soldiers who sacrificed their lives in the 1971 India-Pakistan war. The flame was inaugurated on 26 January 1972 by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and has been burning continuously ever since. India Gate was originally built to commemorate Indian soldiers who died in World War I, but the Amar Jawan Jyoti was added later after the 1971 war. It serves as a national war memorial symbolizing the sacrifice of Indian soldiers.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Amar Jawan Jyoti situated? → India Gate, New Delhi
☛ Who inaugurated Amar Jawan Jyoti? → Prime Minister Indira Gandhi
☛ When was Amar Jawan Jyoti inaugurated? → 26 January 1972
☛ Which war is Amar Jawan Jyoti dedicated to? → 1971 India-Pakistan war
☛ Why was India Gate originally built? → To commemorate Indian soldiers who died in World War I

q: Gurdwara Panja Sahib is located in ____________.
qs.e: Gurdwara Panja Sahib is located in Hasan Abdal, Punjab province, Pakistan. It is one of the most sacred Sikh pilgrimage sites. The name 'Panja Sahib' refers to the handprint of Guru Nanak Dev on a rock. According to tradition, Guru Nanak stopped a rolling boulder with his hand, leaving his palm imprint. This gurdwara holds immense religious significance for Sikhs, who visit it from around the world. The site is associated with a miracle and is a symbol of faith. Hassan Abdal is a city in the Rawalpindi District of Punjab, Pakistan.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Gurdwara Panja Sahib located? → Hasan Abdal, Pakistan
☛ Which Guru is associated with this Gurdwara? → Guru Nanak Dev
☛ What is special in Panja Sahib? → Handprint of Guru Nanak
☛ Which religion's shrine is this? → Sikhism
☛ In which province is Hasan Abdal? → Punjab, Pakistan

q: Qila Mubarak monument is situated in_____.
qs.e: Qila Mubarak monument is located in the Punjab state of India, specifically in the Patiala district. This historic fort was built in the 18th century by Baba Ala Singh, the founder of the Patiala princely state. Its architecture is a blend of Mughal and Rajput styles. The fort houses several palaces and durbar halls, including the prominent Durbar Hall and Moti Bagh Palace. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India and is open to tourists.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built Qila Mubarak? → Baba Ala Singh
☛ In which district is Qila Mubarak located? → Patiala
☛ Who was the founder of Patiala state? → Baba Ala Singh
☛ Which architectural styles blend in Qila Mubarak? → Mughal and Rajput
☛ Which body protects Qila Mubarak? → Archaeological Survey of India

q: World water day is observed on -
qs.e: World Water Day is observed annually on March 22. The day aims to raise awareness about the importance of freshwater and advocate for the sustainable management of water resources. It was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1993. Each year has a specific theme, such as "Water and Climate Change" or "Groundwater: Making the Invisible Visible". The day encourages global efforts for water conservation and access to clean water.
qs.kf:
☛ World Water Day date → March 22
☛ First celebrated in → 1993
☛ Organized by → United Nations
☛ Purpose → Freshwater importance and conservation
☛ 2023 Theme → Accelerating Change

q: Which of the following countries is the youngest country in terms of the lowest median age for the year 2024?
qs.e: According to 2024 data, Niger has a median age of approximately 14.8 years, making it the youngest country in the world. This is due to high birth rates and low life expectancy, resulting in a large proportion of children and young people. Among the other options, Iraq has a median age of about 20.5 years, Palestine about 21.8 years, and Afghanistan about 18.6 years. Niger is a poor country located in the Sahel region of Africa, where lack of education and healthcare keeps the demographic structure young. This is a result of high fertility rates and declining mortality rates.
qs.kf:
☛ World's youngest country (2024) → Niger
☛ Median age of Niger (2024) → Approximately 14.8 years
☛ Continent of Niger → Africa
☛ Country with highest median age (2024) → Japan (approx 48 years)
☛ Major age group in Niger's population → 0-14 years

q: Which city is Known as 'Venice of the East' Where the City Palace is located?
qs.e: Udaipur is known as the 'Venice of the East' due to its lakes and canals. It is located in Rajasthan. The City Palace is situated in Udaipur and is a major tourist attraction. The construction of City Palace was started by Maharana Udai Singh II and later expanded by successive rulers. It is located on the banks of Lake Pichola. Among other options, Mumbai is known as the 'City of Dreams', Mysore is known for its palaces, and Manali is a hill station.
qs.kf:
☛ Which city is known as the 'Venice of the East'? → Udaipur
☛ Which is the famous lake in Udaipur? → Lake Pichola
☛ Who founded the City Palace in Udaipur? → Maharana Udai Singh II
☛ In which state is Udaipur located? → Rajasthan
☛ On the banks of which river is Udaipur situated? → Berach River

q: Which of the following is one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, organized at the confluence of two mighty rivers, the Ganga and Gandak?
qs.e: The Sonepur Fair is one of Asia's largest cattle fairs. It is held in Sonepur, Bihar, at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak rivers. The fair begins on Kartik Purnima and lasts for about a month. It is famous for its massive cattle trade, particularly of elephants. Thousands of cattle, camels, horses, and other animals are bought and sold here. The fair also holds cultural and religious significance.
qs.kf:
☛ At the confluence of which rivers is the Sonepur Fair held? → Ganga and Gandak
☛ On which day does the Sonepur Fair start? → Kartik Purnima
☛ In which state is the Sonepur Fair organized? → Bihar
☛ Which animal trade is Sonepur Fair especially famous for? → Elephants
☛ Which is the largest cattle fair in Asia? → Sonepur Fair

q: Which Indian city is known as the “Silicon Valley of India” due to its thriving IT services sector?
qs.e: Bengaluru is called the 'Silicon Valley of India' because it is the country's largest IT export hub. It houses headquarters of major companies like Infosys, Wipro, and TCS. After the IT boom in the 1990s, the city became a center of technological innovation. The capital of Karnataka is also known as the 'Garden City'. India's first Software Technology Park was established here.
qs.kf:
☛ Silicon Valley of India → Bengaluru
☛ Largest IT exporter city in India → Bengaluru
☛ Garden City → Bengaluru
☛ Capital of Karnataka → Bengaluru
☛ India's first Software Technology Park → Bengaluru

q: _________ or ‘Dance of an Enchantress’ is a solo dance, performed primarily by women, in the state of Kerala.
qs.e: Mohiniyaattam is a classical solo dance form from Kerala, predominantly performed by women. Its name literally means 'Dance of an Enchantress', and it is associated with the Mohini avatar of Lord Vishnu in Hindu mythology. This dance form is based on the Lasya style, which emphasizes graceful and feminine expressions. Mohiniyaattam incorporates both abhinaya (expressive acting) and nritta (pure dance). It is recognized as a classical dance by the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi.
qs.kf:
☛ Meaning of Mohiniyaattam → 'Dance of an Enchantress'
☛ State associated with Mohiniyaattam → Kerala
☛ Mohiniyaattam is linked to which avatar → Mohini avatar of Lord Vishnu
☛ Primary style used in Mohiniyaattam → Lasya
☛ Famous exponent of Mohiniyaattam → Smt. Kalamandalam Kalyaniyikutty Amma

q: Which of the following is the largest solar park in India as of 2025?
qs.e: Bhadla Solar Park, located in Rajasthan's Jodhpur district, is the largest solar park in India as of 2025, with an installed capacity of 2,245 MW. The park is spread near Bhadla village and is operated by public sector companies. The second largest is Pavagada Solar Park in Karnataka with a capacity of 2,050 MW. Kurnool Solar Park in Andhra Pradesh has 1,000 MW and Rewa Solar Park in Madhya Pradesh has 750 MW capacity. Bhadla Solar Park plays a crucial role in India's renewable energy goals and is among the world's largest solar parks.
qs.kf:
☛ Largest solar park in India (2025) → Bhadla Solar Park
☛ Installed capacity of Bhadla Solar Park → 2,245 MW
☛ Second largest solar park → Pavagada Solar Park (2,050 MW)
☛ Location of Bhadla Solar Park → Jodhpur district, Rajasthan
☛ Capacity of Rewa Solar Park → 750 MW

q: According to the World Population Review Report, 2024, which of the following regions of the world has the highest population density?
qs.e: According to the World Population Review Report 2024, South-Central Asia (which includes India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, etc.) has the highest population density. This region has about 308 people per square kilometer, making it the most densely populated region in the world. In comparison, North America has about 20, Central Africa about 40, and Western Europe about 180 persons per sq km. The high density of South-Central Asia is due to fertile plains, presence of rivers, and an agriculture-based economy. India and Bangladesh are the most densely populated countries in this region.
qs.kf:
☛ Region with highest population density → South-Central Asia
☛ Population density of South-Central Asia → Approximately 308 persons per sq km
☛ Region with lowest population density → North America
☛ Population density of Western Europe → Approximately 180 persons per sq km
☛ Most densely populated country in South-Central Asia → Bangladesh

q: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which Indian State/UT?
qs.e: The Taj Mahal is located in the city of Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Yamuna River. It was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1632 and 1653 in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. The structure is made of white marble and its architecture is a blend of Persian, Islamic, and Indian styles. The Taj Mahal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. It is one of India's most famous monuments and attracts millions of tourists every year. It is also listed among the Seven Wonders of the World.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Taj Mahal? → Shah Jahan
☛ On the banks of which river is the Taj Mahal located? → Yamuna
☛ When was the construction of the Taj Mahal started? → 1632 CE
☛ When was the Taj Mahal inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ What material is the Taj Mahal made of? → White marble

q: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is renowned as the chief architect of which UNESCO World Heritage Site?
qs.e: Ustad Ahmad Lahori was a renowned Mughal architect, known as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal. The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Agra, India. It was commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Built from white marble, its construction began in 1632 CE and was completed in 1653 CE. It is considered one of the Seven Wonders of the World. Besides Lahori, Persian architect Ustad Isa is also credited with contributing to its design. The Taj Mahal is famous for its symmetrical architecture and beauty, attracting millions of visitors annually. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
qs.kf:
☛ Who built the Taj Mahal? → Shah Jahan
☛ In which year did Taj Mahal become a UNESCO World Heritage Site? → 1983
☛ Who was the chief architect of the Taj Mahal? → Ustad Ahmad Lahori
☛ Which river is the Taj Mahal located on? → Yamuna River
☛ What is the height of the Taj Mahal? → 73 meters

q: Consider a hypothetical population of rabbits experiencing logistic growth. If the carrying capacity of their environment is 1000 individuals and the current population is 500, what would you expect to happen to the population?
o: The population will decline rapidly due to resource depletion.
The population will continue to grow exponentially without any constraints.
The population will experience a sudden crash followed by a rapid rebound.
The population growth will slow down and eventually stabilize near the carrying capacity.
qs.e: This question is based on the logistic growth model. When the population is at half the carrying capacity (500/1000), the growth rate is at its maximum. However, as the population approaches the carrying capacity, the growth rate slows down due to limited resources. Eventually, the population stabilizes around the carrying capacity, where birth and death rates balance. Exponential growth only occurs when resources are unlimited. Therefore, the population will slow and stabilize.
qs.kf:
☛ Logistic growth equation → dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K)
☛ What is carrying capacity (K)? → The maximum population size that the environment can sustain indefinitely
☛ When is growth rate maximum in logistic growth? → When N = K/2
☛ Exponential vs Logistic growth → Exponential: unlimited resources; Logistic: limited resources
☛ Reason for population stabilization → Resource limitation and competition

q: The National Small Industries Corporation was established in India in _____.
qs.e: The National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) was established in India in the year 1955. It is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India. The primary objective of NSIC is to promote, support and foster the growth of small industries in the country. It provides technical assistance, marketing support, and financial aid to small entrepreneurs. NSIC was set up before the first Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, which emphasized the development of small-scale industries. The corporation also helps small enterprises in obtaining preference in government procurement policies and assists in exporting their products. NSIC plays a vital role in the overall industrial development of India by nurturing the small-scale sector.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of establishment of National Small Industries Corporation → 1955
☛ NSIC comes under which ministry → Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
☛ Headquarters of NSIC → New Delhi
☛ First Industrial Policy Resolution of India was announced in → 1956
☛ Organization promoting small industries in India → NSIC

q: Which of the following statements is correct about the literacy of India between 2001 and 2011?
o: Female literacy has risen faster than male literacy.
Male literacy and female literacy have risen parallelly.
Male literacy has risen faster than female literacy.
Male literacy has declined whereas female literacy has risen.
qs.e: Between 2001 and 2011, India's literacy rate saw significant improvement. During this period, the female literacy rate increased from 54.16% to 65.46%, while the male literacy rate rose from 75.26% to 82.14%. Female literacy grew by about 11.3 percentage points, compared to about 6.9 percentage points for males. This clearly shows that female literacy rose faster than male literacy. This was a result of government efforts like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and initiatives promoting girls' education. The gender gap also narrowed from 21.7 percentage points to 16.7 percentage points.
qs.kf:
☛ What was the increase in India's overall literacy rate between 2001 and 2011? → 64.8% to 74.0% (about 9.2 percentage points)
☛ What was India's female literacy rate in 2011? → 65.46%
☛ What was India's male literacy rate in 2011? → 82.14%
☛ How much did the gender gap in literacy narrow between 2001 and 2011? → 21.7% to 16.7% (5 percentage points)
☛ Which state recorded the highest literacy rate in 2011? → Kerala (highest) and Bihar (lowest)

q: The census in India is conducted once in ten years under the legal authority of the Census Act ____________.
qs.e: The census in India is conducted under the legal authority of the Census Act, 1948. This Act empowers the Government of India to conduct a census every ten years. It was enacted in 1948, and the first census of independent India was held in 1951. Before this, there was no legal basis for the census. The census collects demographic, economic, and social data, which aids in planning and policy-making. The 1948 Act remains the foundation for census operations in India today.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the first census in India conducted? → 1872
☛ When was the first census of independent India held? → 1951
☛ In which year was the Census Act enacted? → 1948
☛ How often is the census conducted in India? → Every 10 years
☛ What is the legal basis for the census in India? → Census Act, 1948

q: The metro City which hasn't undergone a name change since independence is_____.
qs.e: After independence, many metro cities in India underwent name changes, but Delhi has never been renamed. Calcutta was renamed to Kolkata, Madras to Chennai, and Bombay to Mumbai. Delhi is the capital of India and has retained its name since ancient times. It is situated on the banks of the Yamuna River and is part of the National Capital Region (NCR). Delhi is home to many historical landmarks such as Red Fort, Qutub Minar, and India Gate.
qs.kf:
☛ Which city was renamed from Calcutta to Kolkata? → Capital of West Bengal
☛ What is the current name of Madras? → Chennai
☛ What is the current name of Bombay? → Mumbai
☛ Which river flows through Delhi? → Yamuna River
☛ What is the capital of India? → Delhi

q: In June 2019, the ancient Buddhist site ______ located in Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh was declared as a 'protected area of national importance' by Archaeological Survey of India.
qs.e: Chaukhandi Stupa is an ancient Buddhist stupa located in Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh. In June 2019, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) declared it a 'protected area of national importance'. This stupa marks the spot where Lord Buddha met his first five disciples. It was originally built during the Gupta period and later renovated during the reign of Mughal emperor Akbar. The Dhamek Stupa is also located in Sarnath, but it was built around 500 CE. The Dharmarajika Stupa is in Sanchi, while the Sanchi Stupa is in Madhya Pradesh. Chaukhandi Stupa is about 12 meters high and stands on a platform. It is one of the oldest surviving stupas in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Chaukhandi Stupa located? → Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh
☛ When was Chaukhandi Stupa declared a protected area of national importance? → June 2019
☛ What event does Chaukhandi Stupa mark? → Buddha's meeting with his first five disciples
☛ During which period was Chaukhandi Stupa built? → Gupta period
☛ Which other famous Buddhist stupa is located in Sarnath? → Dhamek Stupa

q: Which of the following coastal features in India is believed to have submerged due to tectonic or sea-level changes, as referenced in Indian mythology and archaeology?
qs.e: Dwaraka, located near Gujarat, is an ancient city mentioned in the Mahabharata and Puranas. Archaeological surveys and marine excavations have revealed that the original city submerged due to tectonic activities and sea-level rise. It is a significant site in Indian archaeology. Excavations led by Dr. S.R. Rao have found evidence of submerged walls, pillars, and artifacts under the sea. This discovery supports the historicity of the Mahabharata period.
qs.kf:
☛ Ancient name of Dwaraka → Dwaravati
☛ Primary epic mentioning Dwaraka → Mahabharata
☛ Key archaeologist of Dwaraka excavations → Dr. S.R. Rao
☛ Reason for Dwaraka's submergence → Tectonic movement and sea-level rise
☛ Modern location of Dwaraka → Devbhumi Dwaraka district, Gujarat

q: In 2025, Bagram Air Base, the largest air base mentioned in the news after U.S. President Donald Trump’s bid to retake it, is located in which country?
qs.e: Bagram Air Base is the largest military airbase in Afghanistan, located in the Parwan Province of eastern Afghanistan. It was used by the U.S. military from 2001 to 2021 for counter-terrorism operations. After the U.S. withdrawal in 2021, it came under Taliban control. In 2025, it made headlines following reports of President Trump's attempt to retake the base. The airbase is situated about 40 km north of Kabul and is strategically significant. Originally built by the Soviet Union in the 1950s, it served as a key hub for Soviet operations during the Soviet-Afghan War. The base has multiple runways and can accommodate large aircraft.
qs.kf:
☛ Bagram Air Base is located in which province? → Parwan
☛ Bagram Air Base is in which country? → Afghanistan
☛ Who originally built Bagram Air Base? → Soviet Union in the 1950s
☛ When did the U.S. leave Bagram Air Base? → 2021
☛ Bagram Air Base was used in which war? → War in Afghanistan (2001-2021)

q: The Donkarayi Power House is located in which of the following states of India?
qs.e: The Donkarayi Power House is a hydroelectric power plant located in the state of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is situated on the right bank of the Srisailam Dam across the Krishna River. The installed capacity of this project is 250 megawatts. The Donkarayi Power House was built by the Government of Andhra Pradesh and plays a crucial role in the state's power supply. This plant operates in conjunction with the Srisailam Left Bank Power House.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is the Donkarayi Power House located on? → Krishna River
☛ What is the installed capacity of Donkarayi Power House? → 250 MW
☛ Which dam is the Donkarayi Power House associated with? → Srisailam Dam
☛ In which state is the Donkarayi Power House located? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ In which state is the Srisailam Dam located? → Andhra Pradesh

q: In which district of Gujarat is the Harappan archaeological site of Dholavira, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, situated?
qs.e: Dholavira is a major archaeological site of the Harappan civilization, located in Kutch district of Gujarat. It is situated on the Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann of Kutch. Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021, Dholavira is renowned for its advanced water management system, including large reservoirs and step wells, as well as its unique urban planning. The site yielded the longest known inscription in the Harappan script. It is one of the five largest Harappan sites and provides significant evidence of the civilization's engineering prowess.
qs.kf:
☛ Which river is near Dholavira? → Luni River (seasonal)
☛ Who discovered Dholavira? → J.P. Joshi (1967-68)
☛ Famous water structure at Dholavira? → Step well
☛ Year Dholavira became UNESCO World Heritage? → 2021
☛ Ancient name of Dholavira? → Believed to be 'Koot'

q: According to 2011, which of the following Union Territories of India is the lowest sex ratio state?
qs.e: According to the 2011 census, among the Union Territories of India, Daman and Diu has the lowest sex ratio with 618 females per 1000 males. This is significantly lower than the national average of 943. Delhi has a sex ratio of 868, Andaman and Nicobar Islands have 876, while Lakshadweep has 946. The low sex ratio in Daman and Diu is primarily due to a high number of male migrants and social practices like son preference. This region was previously part of Goa, Daman and Diu, but became a separate Union Territory in 1987 after Goa attained statehood.
qs.kf:
☛ Lowest sex ratio UT in 2011 → Daman and Diu (618)
☛ Highest sex ratio UT in 2011 → Puducherry (1037)
☛ National sex ratio of India in 2011 → 943
☛ Year of formation of Daman and Diu → 1987
☛ Capital of Daman and Diu → Daman

q: Who is known as 'Modern Manu'?
qs.e: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar is known as 'Modern Manu' because he drafted the Indian Constitution, which, like the ancient Manusmriti, provides rules for society. He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and is regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'. Born on April 14, 1891, in Madhya Pradesh, he converted to Buddhism in 1956. He worked tirelessly for the upliftment of the depressed classes. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.
qs.kf:
☛ Chief architect of Indian Constitution → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ First Dalit and only person with M.A., Ph.D. in civil service → Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
☛ Famous books → 'Annihilation of Caste', 'The Problem of the Rupee'
☛ Highest civilian award → Bharat Ratna (1990, posthumous)

q: Kiran Bedi is the present Lieutenant Governor of-
qs.e: Kiran Bedi is the present Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry. She is India's first woman IPS officer and was sworn in as the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry on 28 May 2016. Before this appointment, she served as the Commissioner of Delhi Police and Director General of Prisons in Tamil Nadu. Kiran Bedi is considered a 1972 batch IPS officer of the Tamil Nadu cadre. Puducherry is a union territory where the position of Lieutenant Governor plays a significant role. The other options—Karnataka, Goa, and Kerala—are states that have Governors appointed.

☛ What type of territory is Puducherry? → Union Territory

q: Captain Amarinder Singh is the present Chief Minister of ________.
qs.e: Captain Amarinder Singh is the former Chief Minister of Punjab. He served as the Chief Minister of Punjab from 16 March 2017 to 18 September 2021. He is a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a former military officer. Punjab, a state in northwestern India, is known for its rich cultural heritage and agricultural economy. Amarinder Singh began his political career as a legislator from Patiala and later became Chief Minister. He played a significant role in maintaining law and order and advancing development projects in the state.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the current Chief Minister of Punjab? → Bhagwant Mann
☛ What is the capital of Punjab? → Chandigarh
☛ What is the state bird of Punjab? → Falcon

☛ What is the official language of Punjab? → Punjabi

q: What is ' Planet Nine'?
A. Planet in the Comet Galaxy
B. A planet in Andromeda Galaxy
C. A planet where the 'Star Wars' series took place
D. A large icy planet proposed in the outer Solar System
qs.e: 'Planet Nine' is a hypothetical planet proposed to orbit in the outer Solar System beyond Neptune. It is a large icy planet with a mass about 10 times that of Earth. Its existence is inferred from the unusual orbits of distant Kuiper Belt objects. Astronomers Konstantin Batygin and Mike Brown proposed it in 2016. Planet Nine has not been directly observed, but its gravitational influence suggests its presence. It is believed to be a super-Earth type planet, composed mainly of rock and ice. Its predicted orbital period is around 10,000 to 20,000 years.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is Planet Nine proposed to be located? → Outer Solar System beyond Neptune
☛ What is the estimated mass of Planet Nine? → About 10 Earth masses
☛ Who proposed Planet Nine? → Batygin and Brown (2016)
☛ How is Planet Nine detected? → Through its gravitational effects
☛ What type of planet is Planet Nine? → Icy planet

q: Before 1971,in which year did the India-Pakistan war take place?
qs.e: Before 1971, the India-Pakistan war took place in 1965. This war, caused by the Kashmir dispute, is considered the second India-Pakistan war. The 1965 war did not result in a decisive victory for either side, and after UN intervention, the Tashkent Agreement was signed. Additionally, the first India-Pakistan war occurred in 1947-48, and the third war in 1971 led to the creation of Bangladesh. Among the options, the 1962 war was between India and China, not India and Pakistan.
qs.kf:
☛ 1947-48 India-Pakistan war → First war
☛ 1965 India-Pakistan war → Second war

q: Tashkent Declaration followed Indo-Pak war of
qs.e: The Tashkent Declaration was signed after the 1965 India-Pakistan war. It was signed on January 10, 1966 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. The agreement aimed to restore peace and ceasefire between the two nations. It was signed by India's then Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistan's President Ayub Khan. The Soviet Union's Premier Leonid Brezhnev mediated the agreement. Sadly, Shastri died in Tashkent on the same night. The Tashkent Declaration is not related to the wars of 1947, 1971, or 1999.

q: Name the Chinese President who visited India in 2015.
A. Xi Jinping
B. Hu Jintao
C. Jiang Zemin
D. Li Xian Ning
qs.e: Chinese President Xi Jinping visited India in September 2015. This was his first visit to India as President. The visit gave a new direction to India-China relations. Hu Jintao (2003-2013) and Jiang Zemin (1993-2003) are former presidents. Li Xian Ning is not a Chinese president.

q: Which Indian state has decided to implement Bharat Net service that will connect all gram panchayats through optical fiber?
A. Maharashtra
B. Punjab
C. Tamil Nadu
D. Uttar Pradesh
qs.e: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to implement the Bharat Net service, which will connect all gram panchayats through optical fiber. This initiative is part of the central government's ambitious Bharat Net project aimed at providing broadband connectivity to rural areas. Uttar Pradesh, being the largest state in India with the highest number of gram panchayats, stands to benefit significantly. The project aims to bridge the digital divide and improve access to e-governance, education, and healthcare services in rural regions. Implementing Bharat Net in Uttar Pradesh will connect millions of rural residents, enabling them to access high-speed internet and various digital services. The project is being executed by BSNL and other agencies under the Department of Telecommunications.

q: Where is Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden?
A. Darjeeling
B. Mysore
C. Srinagar
D. Chandigarh
qs.e: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden is located in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. It is the largest tulip garden in Asia and was opened to the public in 2007. The garden is named after former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It is situated at the foothills of the Zabarwan mountain range and on the banks of Dal Lake. Every year, the Tulip Festival is held here, attracting tourists and showcasing a variety of colorful tulips.

q: Who was the first Asian woman of Indian origin to be elected as mayor in the United Kingdom (UK) on 12 May 2015?
A. Ranjit Kaur Dheer B. Inderjeet Singh C. Sukhwinder Kaur D. Harbhajan Kaur Dheer
qs.e: On 12 May 2015, Harbhajan Kaur Dheer was elected mayor of Wolverhampton in the United Kingdom, becoming the first Asian woman of Indian origin to hold this position in the UK. Born in Punjab, India, she moved to the UK in the 1960s. Before becoming mayor, she was active in local politics as a member of the Labour Party. Her election marked a significant milestone for the Indian-origin community in the UK. She is known for her work in women's empowerment and community service. Harbhajan Kaur Dheer's achievement inspired many and highlighted the growing political participation of ethnic minorities in British politics.

q: Who is number 1 in the Forbes 2016 ranking of World’s billionaires?

qs.e: In the Forbes 2016 list of world's billionaires, Bill Gates ranked first with a net worth of approximately $75 billion. q: Who among the following was NOT a chief minister before he/she became the Prime Minister of India?
A. Morarji Desai
B. Charan Singh
C. Indira Gandhi
D. V.P. Singh
qs.e: Indira Gandhi never served as a chief minister before becoming Prime Minister. She became PM in 1966, prior to which she was the Minister of Information and Broadcasting in Lal Bahadur Shastri's cabinet. In contrast, Morarji Desai (Bombay State, 1952-56), Charan Singh (Uttar Pradesh, 1967-68), and V.P. Singh (Uttar Pradesh, 1980-82) were all chief ministers before becoming Prime Minister. Indira Gandhi was the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru and served as Congress President in 1959. Her political career bypassed the chief minister role largely due to her father being the first PM of India. She is also the only woman Prime Minister of India so far.
