q: What is the local name given to the parliament of Pakistan?
A. Majilis
B. Majilis-e-Shoora
C. Saeima-e-majlis
D. Jatia Parliament
qs.e: The parliament of Pakistan is locally known as Majilis-e-Shoora. This name is derived from Urdu, where 'Majilis' means assembly and 'Shoora' means consultative council. The parliament is bicameral, consisting of the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house). The President is not part of parliament but gives assent to bills. The Majilis-e-Shoora was established under the 1973 Constitution. Other options: 'Majilis' is a generic term for assembly, 'Saeima' is the parliament of Latvia, and 'Jatia Parliament' is the parliament of Bangladesh.
qs.kf:
☛ Local name of Pakistan's parliament → Majilis-e-Shoora
☛ Total seats in Pakistan's National Assembly → 342
☛ Location of Pakistan's parliament building → Islamabad
☛ Year of Pakistan's Constitution enforcement → 14 August 1973
☛ Type of parliamentary system in Pakistan → Bicameral

q: Which of the following statues in an icon of freedom designed by a French Sculptor?
A. Statue of Unity
B. Statue of Liberty
C. Statue of Law
D. Statue of Zeus
qs.e: The Statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi. It is an iconic symbol of freedom and was gifted to the United States by France, dedicated on October 28, 1886. Its full name is 'Liberty Enlightening the World'. Located at the entrance of New York Harbor, the statue holds a torch in its right hand and a tablet inscribed with the date July 4, 1776. The statue is 151 feet tall and made of copper. The internal framework was designed by Gustave Eiffel.

q: Alassane Ouattara is:

B. The President of Indonesia
C. The President of Malaysia
D. The Vice President of Maldives
qs.e: Alassane Ouattara is the current President of Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire). He assumed office in 2010 and was re-elected in 2015 and 2020. An economist by training, he previously served as Deputy Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Ivory Coast is a major cocoa-producing country in West Africa. Ouattara's presidency has focused on economic reforms and infrastructure development.

q: The code name of India - Pakistan kargil war was ________.
A. Operation Blue Star
B. Operation Vijay
C. Operation Viraat
D. Operation Kargil
qs.e: The India-Pakistan Kargil War, fought in 1999, had the code name Operation Vijay. This war took place in the Kargil district of Jammu and Kashmir, when Pakistani soldiers and infiltrators illegally entered Indian territory. The Indian Army launched this operation to evict them, which lasted about two months and ended with India's victory. Operation Vijay means "Operation Victory", symbolizing India's success in this conflict.

q: Shimla Agreement 1972 between India & Pakistan was signed in A. Barne's Court B. Ellerslie Building C. Viceregal Lodge
D. Gorton Castle
qs.e: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between India and Pakistan on 2 July 1972 at Barne's Court in Shimla. It was signed by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. This agreement aimed to establish peace after the 1971 war and resolve the Kashmir issue through bilateral negotiations. Other historic buildings in Shimla include Ellerslie Building, Viceregal Lodge, and Gorton Castle, but the Shimla Agreement was specifically signed at Barne's Court. The agreement emphasized respect for the Line of Control and non-interference in internal affairs.

q: Who served as the first Deputy Prime Minister of independent India?
A. K. Kamaraj
B. Morarji Desai
C. Sardar Vallabhbai Patel
D. C. Rajagopalachari
qs.e: The first Deputy Prime Minister of independent India was Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He served in this position from 1947 to 1950. He was also the Home Minister and played a crucial role in integrating princely states into India. He is known as the Iron Man of India. He was born on 31st October 1875 in Nadiad, Gujarat, and actively participated in the Indian freedom movement.

q: As of October 2020, who is the Vice President of India?
qs.e: As of October 2020, the Vice President of India was M Venkaiah Naidu. He assumed office on 11 August 2017. He is the 13th Vice President of India. Earlier, he served as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh and a senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party. The Vice President holds a term of 5 years and is also the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. q: Which of the following IITs has been declared one among the seven Eat Right Campus by FSSAI?
qs.e: FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India) has identified seven campuses under its 'Eat Right Campus' initiative, with IIT Gandhinagar being one of them. This initiative aims to promote healthy and safe food practices. Selected campuses ensure nutritionally balanced meals, reduce food waste, and maintain hygiene standards. q: Demonetisation was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on:
qs.e: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced demonetisation on November 8, 2016, at 8:00 PM in a televised address to the nation. The move invalidated old ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes as legal tender. Its primary objectives were to curb black money, corruption, and counterfeit currency. The decision led to a temporary cash crunch in the economy but was hailed as a significant step towards economic reforms and transparency.

q: Which of the following is the correct full form of 'MRTP' in MRTP Act 1969?

q: Name the first country of the Soviet Republic (USSR) to declare its independence.
qs.e: The first country to declare independence from the Soviet Union (USSR) was Lithuania. On 11 March 1990, Lithuania declared its independence from the USSR. This move was part of the Baltic states' independence movement. Lithuania had been annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940 and sought to restore its sovereignty. This event accelerated the dissolution of the Soviet Union, as other republics soon followed. Lithuania's independence was finally recognized by the Soviet Union in September 1991. The declaration marked a significant step in the collapse of the USSR, which officially dissolved on 26 December 1991.

☛ First country to declare independence from USSR → Lithuania
☛ Date of independence declaration → 11 March 1990
☛ Region of Lithuania → Baltic region
☛ Formal dissolution of USSR → 26 December 1991

q: Who among the following got elected as the Head of the State for four times?
qs.e: Vladimir Putin has been elected as the President (Head of State) of Russia four times. He was first elected in 2000, re-elected in 2004, again in 2012, and for the fourth time in 2018. Boris Yeltsin served as President only twice (1991 and 1996). Dmitry Medvedev served as President once (2008–2012), and Viktor Zubkov served as Prime Minister, not President. In Russia, the presidential term is 6 years, and a person can serve a maximum of two consecutive terms; however, Putin won four elections with an interval (2008–2012 when Medvedev was President).

☛ When did Putin first assume the presidency? → 2000

☛ Which position did Dmitry Medvedev hold? → President (2008– 2012)

qs.e: Satyendra Nath Bose is NOT related to the Indian Space Program. He was a renowned physicist known for his contributions to Bose-Einstein statistics and the discovery of bosons. q: Which architect has designed the India Gate in New Delhi?
qs.e: India Gate, originally known as the 'All India War Memorial', was designed by the renowned British architect Edwin Lutyens. This monument was built in memory of Indian soldiers who died in World War I and the Afghan Wars. Lutyens also designed several other important landmarks in New Delhi, including the Rashtrapati Bhavan and the Central Vista. The construction of India Gate began in 1921 and was completed in 1931. Beneath it lies the Amar Jawan Jyoti, which was added after the 1971 war.

q: CRY is an organisation that works for the:

q: In 2016, who became the second woman Prime Minister of Great Britain?
qs.e: In 2016, Theresa May became the second woman Prime Minister of Great Britain. The first was Margaret Thatcher (1979-1990). May took office after David Cameron resigned. She was the leader of the Conservative Party and served from July 2016 to July 2019. Her tenure was dominated by the Brexit process. May is a significant figure in British politics.

☛ Theresa May's tenure → 2016-2019
☛ Theresa May's party → Conservative Party

q: The word ‘comet’ comes from the ancient ________ word, which means long-haired star.
qs.e: The word 'comet' comes from the ancient Greek word 'komē tē s', meaning 'long-haired star'. Ancient Greek astronomers described comets as 'hairy stars' due to their glowing tails. The term was later adopted into Latin and then into English as 'comet'. Greek civilization made significant contributions to astronomy, and many celestial terms originate from the Greek language. Comets are composed of ice, dust, and rock; when they approach the Sun, they release gas and dust, forming a bright tail that can extend millions of kilometers. The study of comets provides insights into the early solar system.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the scientific nickname of a comet? → Dirty snowball.
☛ What is the orbital period of Halley's Comet? → About 76 years.
☛ What are comets made of? → Ice, dust, and rock.
☛ What does a comet produce near the Sun? → A tail of gas and dust.
☛ Which is the most famous comet? → Halley's Comet.

q: 'Operation Vijay' is associated with which of the following wars?
qs.e: During the Kargil War in 1999, the Indian Army launched 'Operation Vijay' to evict infiltrators who had crossed the Line of Control and occupied strategic heights in the Kargil district of Jammu and Kashmir. The operation aimed to push back Pakistani soldiers and militants. Indian forces successfully regained control of the territory, with the Indian Air Force also playing a crucial role in providing air support. The operation concluded with India restoring its sovereignty over the occupied regions. This war is significant as it demonstrated India's military capabilities and resolve.

q: The Government of India celebrates_______ every year as ‘Civil Services Day’ for the civil servants to rededicate themselves to the cause of citizens and renew their commitment to public service and excellence in work.
qs.e: India celebrates 21 April every year as Civil Services Day. On this occasion, the Prime Minister presents Prime Minister's Awards for excellence in public service. Civil servants rededicate themselves to the cause of citizens and renew their commitment to public service and work excellence.

q: In July 2020, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the new Supreme Court Building of _____ which was completed with Indian assistance
qs.e: In July 2020, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the new Supreme Court Building of Mauritius, completed with Indian assistance. This building symbolizes the strong ties between India and Mauritius. Mauritius is an island nation located in the Indian Ocean, with its capital at Port Louis. q: Who designed the 'Statue of Unity', which was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 31st October 2018?
qs.e: The Statue of Unity was designed by Ram Vanji Sutar. This statue is dedicated to India's first Deputy Prime Minister, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who is known as the Iron Man of India. q: What is the ancient name of Iran?
qs.e: The ancient name of Iran was Persia. This name is derived from the Persian language, and the region was historically called Pars or Persia. In 1935, the Iranian government officially changed the country's name to Iran on the international stage. 'Iran' means 'land of the Aryans'. The ancient Persian Empire was one of the most powerful empires in the world, with famous rulers like Cyrus the Great and Darius I. Persian culture, art, and architecture influenced the entire world.

q: When was the First World War started?
qs.e: The First World War began on July 28, 1914, when Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. It lasted until November 11, 1918. The war involved the Allied Powers (including Britain, France, Russia) and the Central Powers (including Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire). q: When was the arrangement of Municipal Corporations in Bombay and Calcutta?
qs.e: The Municipal Corporations in Bombay and Calcutta were established in 1726 by the British East India Company. These corporations were early attempts at urban administration and laid the foundation for the development of the municipal system in India. Later, the Charter Act of 1793 granted more powers to these corporations. The year 1726 is considered the beginning of modern urban governance in India.

q: Which country is called "indestructible union of indestructible states"?
qs.e: The United States is called the 'indestructible union of indestructible states', reflecting its federal structure and the indivisibility of states. This phrase is rooted in the U.S. Constitution and national unity. The U.S. is a federal republic of 50 states where states have no right to secede. This concept was strengthened after the Civil War (1861-1865), which established the union's permanence. India is also a union but termed as 'Union of States', not 'indestructible union'. Switzerland and the United Kingdom have different structures.

q: Which of the following states became the 17th state of the Indian Union?
qs.e: The 17th state of the Indian Union, Haryana, was formed on 1 November 1966. It came into existence after the partition of Punjab on linguistic lines, separating Punjabi-speaking and Hindi-speaking regions. At the time of its formation, Haryana had 7 districts: Hisar, Mahendragarh, Gurgaon, Rohtak, Kurukshetra, Karnal, and Ambala. Its area is approximately 44,212 sq km and it is located in northern India. The state capital is Chandigarh, which also serves as the capital of Punjab. Haryana is significant in both agriculture and industry, and its literacy rate is about 75%.

q: In 1200 BC Where was the 'Veersh Shive Movement' Started?
qs.e: The Veerashaiva movement started in the 12th century AD in Karnataka. Its founder was Basaveshwara, who served as a minister under the Kalachuri king Bijjala. This movement opposed caste discrimination, ritualism, and Brahmanical dominance, advocating for equality, devotion, and dignity of labor. The followers of Veerashaivism are known as Lingayats.

q: Cantonment Act in India was passed in _____ year.
qs.e: The Cantonment Act in India was passed in the year 1924. This act deals with the administration, management, and control of military cantonments in India. It provides for local self-government in cantonments and ensures their separate administration from civilian areas. Enacted during the British period, this act was retained after independence with amendments. Currently, the Cantonment Act 2006 (Act No. 41 of 2006) is in force, which replaced the 1924 act. India has a total of 62 cantonments, which fall under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Defence.

q: By 1989, an adult Indian was meant to be a citizen of over ________ years.
qs.e: The age of adulthood in India was 21 years until 1989. This was determined under the provisions of the Indian Constitution related to voting rights and citizenship. Originally, Article 326 of the Constitution set the voting age at 21 years. In 1989, the 61st Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18. This amendment was passed in 1989 and came into effect on 28 March 1992. Prior to this, only citizens aged 21 and above were eligible to vote. Therefore, until 1989, an adult Indian citizen was defined as a person over 21 years of age.
qs.kf:
☛ Which amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 in India? → 61st Amendment
☛ When did the 61st Amendment come into effect? → 28 March 1992
☛ Which article defines the voting age in India? → Article 326
☛ What was the voting age in India before 1989? → 21 years
☛ In which year was the 61st Amendment passed? → 1989

q: Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education is completely funded by the following?
qs.e: Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Sports, Government of India. It is completely funded by the central government. Established in 1957 in Gwalior, it was declared an institute of national importance in 1995. LNIPE offers courses in physical education and sports science. The State Government of Assam, NGOs, or private organizations are not involved in its funding. LNIPE relies entirely on the central government budget.

q: Which is the only state in India has implemented a 69% reservation policy?
qs.e: Tamil Nadu is the only state in India that has implemented a 69% reservation policy. This policy provides reservations in government jobs and educational institutions for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and other categories. The basis for this high reservation percentage is the Tamil Nadu Backward Classes Act, 1993. This policy has been upheld by the Supreme Court, although its extent has been reviewed. Tamil Nadu's model is distinct from other states because it exceeds the usual 50% ceiling. The reservation system in Tamil Nadu aims to address historical social and educational disadvantages.

☛ What did the Supreme Court rule on this policy? → It upheld the policy
☛ In which year was this policy implemented? → 1990

q: What type of federal practice is used in India, Belgium and Spain?
qs.e: India, Belgium, and Spain follow the Federally Administered Method. This is a type of federal system where the central government grants administrative autonomy to states or regions, but retains control in certain matters. India has a federal system of governance with states having some powers. Belgium has regional and community governments, while Spain has autonomous communities. This system differs from a unitary state where all power is centralized. The Indian Constitution features single citizenship and a strong center, distinguishing it from other federal states.
qs.kf:
☛ What type of federal system does India have? → Semi-federal or Federally Administered
☛ What type of federal system does Belgium have? → Based on regional and community governments
☛ What type of federal system does Spain have? → Based on autonomous communities
☛ Whose role is prominent in the Federally Administered Method? → Central government
☛ What is a characteristic of federal states? → Division of powers and dual governance

q: Which state does the Member of Parliament Kamakhya Prasad Tasa belong to?
qs.e: Member of Parliament Kamakhya Prasad Tasa belongs to the state of Assam. He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party and represents the Guwahati parliamentary constituency in the Lok Sabha. Kamakhya Prasad Tasa was elected in the 2019 general elections. He is a resident of Nagaon district in Assam. Prior to becoming an MP, he served as a member of the Assam Legislative Assembly. q: Who was the first Sikh President of India?
qs.e: The first Sikh President of India was Giani Zail Singh, who served from 1982 to 1987. He was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and also served as the Chief Minister of Punjab. Giani Zail Singh played a crucial role in maintaining the unity and integrity of the country. His tenure is known for events like Operation Blue Star and the assassination of Indira Gandhi. q: When was the Supreme Court of India established?
qs.e: The Supreme Court of India was established under the Constitution of India. The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, and on the same day, the Supreme Court was formally inaugurated. Before this, the Federal Court of India (established in 1937) was functioning, which was replaced by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court is the highest judicial body in the country, and its decisions are binding on all courts.

q: Which year was Bangladesh released from Pakistan?
qs.e: Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan in 1971. East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) fought a liberation war against West Pakistan's rule. On 16 December 1971, the Pakistani army surrendered, and Bangladesh emerged as a sovereign nation. India provided military and diplomatic support during the war. Earlier, after the partition of India in 1947, East Pakistan was created. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman became the first President of Bangladesh. This event is a significant milestone in South Asian history.

q: The Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) began in the year _______.
qs.e: The Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) was enacted in India in the year 1986. This act aims to protect consumers from unfair trade practices, defective goods, and deficient services. It provides consumers the right to file complaints and seek compensation. The act established a three-tier consumer dispute redressal mechanism: District Forum, State Commission, and National Commission. It is a landmark legislation that safeguards consumer rights in India.

q: What is the full name of COPRA, a law made in 1986?
qs.e: The full name of COPRA is the Consumer Protection Act, enacted by the Indian Parliament in the year 1986. This law was established to protect consumers from unfair trade practices, defective goods, and deficient services. It ensures consumer rights such as safety, information, choice, and redressal. Under this act, consumer forums were set up at the district, state, and national levels to address consumer grievances. Although the 1986 Act was later replaced by a new Consumer Protection Act in 2019, COPRA 1986 remains the foundational legislation for consumer rights in India.

q: The constitutional assembly was established in year.
qs.e: The Indian Constituent Assembly was established in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. The plan was brought to India in May 1946, and the assembly was formed through elections to the provincial legislatures. Its first meeting was held on December 9, 1946, chaired by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha. Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent chairman. The assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to draft the constitution, which was adopted on November 26, 1949 and came into effect on January 26, 1950.

q: What is the capital of Gujarat?
qs.e: The capital of Gujarat is Gandhinagar. It was made the capital after the formation of Gujarat in 1960. It is named after Mahatma Gandhi. It is located about 23 km north of Ahmedabad. Gandhinagar is one of India's planned cities, designed by town planner H.K. Mewada. It houses the Gujarat Legislative Assembly and Secretariat. Gandhinagar is also known as the Green City.

q: Which structure was constructed to commemorate the visit of King George to India in 1911 ?
qs.e: The Gateway of India was built to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary to India in 1911. It is located at Apollo Bunder, Mumbai. The monument was designed by architect George Wittet and its foundation was laid in 1911, but it was completed and inaugurated in 1924. The structure is built in the Indo-Saracenic style, blending Hindu and Islamic architectural elements. The Gateway of India was historically used as the ceremonial entrance to British India. In 1948, the last British troops departed from India through this monument. It stands as a symbol of Mumbai's colonial history.

q: When did the Universal Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act come into force?
qs.e: The Universal Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act came into force in 1999. This act provides for the registration and protection of Geographical Indications (GI) in India. It aims to identify goods originating from a specific geographical region and protect them from unauthorized use, such as Darjeeling tea or Alleppey handloom. The act aligns with the WTO's TRIPS Agreement, which requires member countries to protect geographical indications. The GI Registry in India is located in Chennai.

q: How many new criminal laws has the Indian Government implemented from July 1, 2024?
qs.e: The Indian Government implemented three new criminal laws from July 1, 2024. These laws replace the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC), Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), and Indian Evidence Act. The new laws are called: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam. They were passed by Parliament in December 2023. The laws aim to modernize the criminal justice system and ensure speedy justice. Key provisions include acceptance of digital evidence, zero FIR, and trial via video conferencing.

q: On which day did Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurate the 'Run for Unity' event in New Delhi as part of National Unity Day?
qs.e: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the 'Run for Unity' event in New Delhi on 29 October 2024 as part of National Unity Day. The run was held ahead of the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on 31 October. National Unity Day is celebrated annually on 31 October to commemorate Patel's birth and his contributions to India's unity. q: General Service Enlistment Act was passed in __________________.
qs.e: The General Service Enlistment Act was passed in 1856 AD. This Act was enacted by the British East India Company, which mandated that all Indian soldiers (sepoys) must be willing to serve overseas. It required newly enlisted soldiers to agree to serve abroad, including crossing the sea, which was against the religious beliefs of many high-caste Hindus. This Act is considered one of the major causes of the Revolt of 1857, as it directly interfered with the religious sentiments of the sepoys. The Act marked a significant change in the service conditions of Indian soldiers under British rule.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the General Service Enlistment Act passed? → 1856 AD
☛ What was the purpose of this Act? → To compel soldiers to serve overseas

☛ Which revolt is related to this Act? → Revolt of 1857
☛ What was against the religious beliefs of soldiers? → Crossing the sea

q: On which date was Narendra Modi sworn-in as India’s Prime Minister for the third time, following 2024 Parliamentary elections?
qs.e: Following the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Narendra Modi was sworn in as the Prime Minister of India for the third time on 9 June 2024. The oath of office was administered by President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held at Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi. Modi became the second Indian leader after Jawaharlal Nehru to serve as Prime Minister for three consecutive terms. The Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured 293 seats out of 543 in the elections, enabling them to form the government. The swearing-in event was attended by various dignitaries and marked the beginning of Modi's third term.

☛ President who administered oath → Droupadi Murmu

☛ Modi-led coalition → National Democratic Alliance (NDA)
☛ NDA seats in 2024 Lok Sabha → 293

q: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) operates under which Act?
qs.e: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) was established under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986. This act was enacted to protect the interests of consumers and provide a mechanism for the speedy redressal of consumer disputes. NCDRC is the apex judicial body under this act, and its decisions can be appealed to the Supreme Court. Although the act was later replaced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, NCDRC continues to exercise its jurisdiction under the old act. The commission plays a vital role in delivering justice to consumers across India.

q: In September 2024, President Droupadi Murmu approved the establishment of which of the following commissions for the 2024-2027 term?
qs.e: In September 2024, President Droupadi Murmu approved the formation of the 23rd Law Commission for the 2024-2027 term. The Law Commission is a non-constitutional body established by the central government to review and reform existing laws. Its recommendations are advisory in nature and aim to improve the legal system. The commission consists of a chairperson and members appointed by the government. q: In November 2024, the Diplomatic Conference on Design Law took place in.
qs.e: In November 2024, the Diplomatic Conference on Design Law was held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Organized by WIPO, the conference aimed to establish an international legal framework for design protection. It focused on the Design Law Treaty (DLT), which will simplify the registration process for industrial designs. By hosting this conference, Saudi Arabia strengthened its global role in intellectual property. The conference was a key step toward making design protection more accessible for designers and businesses worldwide.

q: When was the Basel Convention adopted on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal?
qs.e: The Basel Convention was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992. It was designed to reduce the transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and ensure their environmentally sound disposal. The convention aims to prevent developed countries from dumping hazardous waste in developing countries. It was drafted under the auspices of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). Parties to the convention are required to minimize waste generation within their borders and ensure environmentally sound management.

q: What was the life expectancy in India in 1947?
qs.e: In 1947, at the time of India's independence, life expectancy was approximately 31 years. This was very low mainly due to high infant mortality, infectious diseases, malnutrition, and lack of medical facilities. After independence, the government focused on healthcare, sanitation, and immunization, leading to rapid improvement in life expectancy. India's life expectancy has risen to about 70 years by 2023.

qs.e: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan, rich in natural resources like natural gas, coal, gold, and copper. Rebel groups seek more control over resources and independence from Pakistan. q: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, allows juveniles aged 16-18 to be tried as adults in cases of:
qs.e: Under Sections 15 and 18 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, juveniles aged 16-18 can be tried as adults for heinous offences. Heinous offences are those punishable with minimum imprisonment of seven years. The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) assesses whether the juvenile understood the nature and consequences of the offence. If so, the case may be transferred to a children's court or regular court. Theft, drug abuse, and cybercrime are not automatically heinous unless they carry a minimum seven-year sentence. This provision balances rehabilitation with accountability for serious crimes, ensuring that young offenders are not automatically treated as adults but can be when the crime is grave. The Act aims to reform juveniles while delivering justice in severe cases.
qs.kf:

☛ Minimum sentence for heinous offence? → 7 years imprisonment
☛ Who assesses the juvenile's mental capacity? → Juvenile Justice Board (JJB)
☛ Which sections of JJA 2015? → Sections 15 and 18
☛ Who transfers the case to adult court? → JJB

q: The government tracks the performance of eight core industries to monitor industrial activity. What is the approximate weight of the core industries in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
qs.e: The eight core industries include coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, and electricity. Core sector data is released monthly and is used to forecast GDP growth. The highest weight among core industries is of refinery products (about 28%), while fertilizers have the lowest weight (about 2.6%).

q: When was the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) established to investigate cases of human rights violations in India?
qs.e: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It has the authority to probe deaths in police custody, crimes against Dalits and women, and other human rights abuses.

q: On which day in 2025 did India and Pakistan agree to a US-brokered ceasefire with immediate effect?

q: When was the Mines Act enacted in India?
qs.e: The Mines Act, 1952 was enacted by the Parliament of India to regulate the safety, health, and welfare of workers in mines. ☛ MIL was formed → in 2021 after the dissolution of the Ordnance Factory Board
☛ Ministry granting Miniratna Category-I status → Ministry of Defence
☛ Major products of MIL → Ammunition, explosives, and missile warheads
☛ Year MIL received Miniratna status → 2025

q: In which of the following years was the town of Madrasapatnam, which later expanded and developed into modern-day Chennai, purchased by the East India Company (EIC) from local kings?
qs.e: The town of Madrasapatnam was purchased by the East India Company (EIC) in 1639 from local Nayak rulers. Francis Day obtained a grant of land from King Venkatapati Ray of Chandragiri on 22 August 1639, on which Fort St. George was built. This fort became the nucleus for the development of the city of Madras. The 1639 treaty is considered the foundation of British colonization in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of purchase of Madrasapatnam → 1639
☛ EIC official who negotiated → Francis Day
☛ Ruler who granted the land → Venkatapati Ray
☛ First fort built → Fort St. George
☛ Old name of Chennai → Madrasapatnam

q: On May 20, 2025, the Supreme Court reinstated which requirement for candidates aspiring to become civil judges (junior division)?
o: Three years of legal practice experience
Passing a national-level judicial service exam
qs.e: On May 20, 2025, the Supreme Court reinstated the requirement of three years of legal practice for candidates aspiring to become civil judges (junior division). This decision came in response to a petition related to the Madhya Pradesh Judicial Service Rules, 2021, which had challenged certain eligibility criteria including minimum age and practice experience. The Court emphasized that legal practice experience is essential to ensure the quality and competence of judges, as it provides them with practical knowledge and judicial temperament. The ruling was seen as crucial for maintaining judicial independence and the integrity of the appointment process. This requirement aims to ensure that judges have sufficient experience to handle complex legal matters effectively.
qs.kf:
☛ Minimum practice experience for civil judge (junior division) → 3 years
☛ Rules related to the 2025 Supreme Court decision → Madhya Pradesh Judicial Service Rules, 2021
☛ Purpose of experience in judicial appointments → Ensure quality and competence of judges
☛ State concerned with this requirement → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Reason for reinstatement → Judicial independence and integrity of appointment process

q: Where is India’s first Quantum Computing Village proposed to be established, as per a meeting by that state's government in April 2025, under the Real-Time Governance Society (RTGS)?
qs.e: In April 2025, the Andhra Pradesh government proposed to establish India's first Quantum Computing Village in Amaravati under the Real-Time Governance Society (RTGS). This initiative aims to strengthen the state's digital infrastructure and promote research in quantum computing. Quantum computing is capable of performing calculations much faster than traditional computing. The Andhra Pradesh government has formed a special team through RTGS to develop this village. The project aims to provide a platform for startups, academics, and industries.
qs.kf:
☛ Where is India's first Quantum Computing Village proposed? → Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh
☛ What is the full form of RTGS? → Real-Time Governance Society
☛ Which state's initiative is RTGS? → Andhra Pradesh
☛ On which principle does quantum computing work? → Quantum mechanics
☛ What is the basic unit of quantum computing? → Qubit

q: Which political party formed the government in the state of Andhra Pradesh in 2025?
qs.e: In the 2024 Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly elections, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) defeated the YSR Congress Party to form the government. TDP chief N. Chandrababu Naidu took oath as Chief Minister. TDP won 135 out of 175 seats. Jana Sena Party and Bharatiya Janata Party were also part of the alliance. This victory marked TDP's comeback after its defeat in 2019.
qs.kf:
☛ Party that won 2024 Andhra elections → Telugu Desam Party (TDP)
☛ Current president of TDP → N. Chandrababu Naidu
☛ Capital of Andhra Pradesh → Amaravati
☛ Year of TDP founding → 1982
☛ Founder of YSR Congress Party → Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy

q: The Idukki Disaster Resilience and Information System (IDRIS), India’s first integrated early warning and planning platform using AI and real-time data, was launched in which Indian state?
qs.e: The Idukki Disaster Resilience and Information System (IDRIS) is India's first integrated early warning and planning platform that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and real-time data. It was launched in the state of Kerala, specifically in the Idukki district. This system promotes the use of AI in disaster management and provides timely warnings for disasters like floods and landslides. The Kerala government and the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) have developed it. The platform integrates data from various sources to ensure accurate forecasting and quick response. This will help reduce damage and improve rescue operations.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state was IDRIS launched? → Kerala
☛ What is the full form of IDRIS? → Idukki Disaster Resilience and Information System
☛ What technologies does IDRIS use? → AI and real-time data
☛ Which district is IDRIS focused on? → Idukki district
☛ Which authority is responsible for disaster management in Kerala? → KSDMA

q: To align with modern industrial practices, which new order did the Central Government introduce in 2025 to replace the Sugar (Control) Order, 1966?
qs.e: The Central Government introduced the Sugar (Control) Order, 2025 in 2025, replacing the Sugar (Control) Order, 1966, to align with modern industrial practices. This new order aims to simplify and bring transparency to the regulation of the sugar industry. Under this order, sugar mills are required to upload their production and sales data on an online portal, making monitoring easier. Additionally, rules related to sugar quality, storage, and marketing have been updated. This step is taken to reform the sugar industry and protect the interests of farmers. The order is notified by the Ministry of Food and Consumer Affairs.
qs.kf:
☛ Which new order replaced the Sugar (Control) Order, 1966? → The Sugar (Control) Order, 2025
☛ What is mandatory for sugar mills under the new order? → Uploading production and sales data online
☛ When was the new order implemented? → In 2025
☛ What is the main objective of the new order? → Modernizing the sugar industry and protecting farmer interests
☛ Which ministry issued the new order? → Ministry of Food and Consumer Affairs

q: ________ replaced Steve Ballmer as CEO of Microsoft.
A. J. W. Thompson
B. Satya Nadella
C. Amy Hood
D. Bill Gates
qs.e: Satya Nadella succeeded Steve Ballmer as the third CEO of Microsoft on February 4, 2014. Prior to this, he was Executive Vice President of Microsoft's Cloud and Enterprise Group. Under Nadella's leadership, Microsoft shifted focus to cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and open-source technologies. He oversaw major initiatives such as Windows 10, Microsoft Edge, and the acquisition of LinkedIn. Nadella is the third CEO in Microsoft's history after Bill Gates and Steve Ballmer.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the founder of Microsoft? → Bill Gates and Paul Allen
☛ Who was the first CEO of Microsoft? → Bill Gates
☛ Who was the second CEO of Microsoft? → Steve Ballmer
☛ Who is the third CEO of Microsoft? → Satya Nadella
☛ In which year did Satya Nadella become CEO? → 2014

q: When was Gandhi Smriti and Darshan Samiti (GSDS) formed?
qs.e: The Gandhi Smriti and Darshan Samiti (GSDS) was formed in September 1984 by the Government of India. Its objective is to propagate the ideas and philosophy of Mahatma Gandhi. The Samiti manages the Gandhi Smriti Museum and the Gandhi Darshan Museum. Gandhi Smriti is the place where Mahatma Gandhi spent the last 144 days of his life and was assassinated on 30 January 1948. The Samiti organizes programs, seminars, and exhibitions to promote Gandhian thoughts at national and international levels. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi.
qs.kf:
☛ When was GSDS formed? → September 1984
☛ What is the objective of GSDS? → Propagation of Gandhi's ideas
☛ Where is the headquarters of GSDS? → New Delhi
☛ What is Gandhi Smriti? → The place where Gandhi spent his last days
☛ When was Gandhi assassinated? → 30 January 1948

q: 'Bhotiya' is a caste of scheduled tribes of which of the following states in India?
qs.e: The Bhotiya tribe primarily inhabits the higher Himalayan regions of Uttarakhand. They belong to the Tibeto-Burmese language family and are recognized as a Scheduled Tribe. They are mainly found in the valleys of Johar, Niti, Mana, and Niti. Their primary occupations are animal husbandry and trade. The Bhotiya community has several sub-tribes like Tolcha, Marcha, and Jad. Historically, they have been active in India-Tibet trade for centuries. Currently, they reside in border areas, and their culture is influenced by Buddhism.
qs.kf:
☛ In which state is the Bhotiya tribe found? → Uttarakhand
☛ What are the main sub-tribes of the Bhotiya? → Tolcha, Marcha, Jad
☛ What is the main occupation of the Bhotiya tribe? → Animal husbandry and trade
☛ Which language family does the Bhotiya tribe belong to? → Tibeto-Burmese
☛ Which religion influences the Bhotiya tribe? → Buddhism

q: The Government of India Constituted Narcotics Control Bureau in ________.
qs.e: The Government of India constituted the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) on March 17, 1986. It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Its headquarters is located in New Delhi. The primary objective of NCB is to prevent the illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. It operates under the NDPS Act, 1985. The first Director-General of NCB was R. N. Srivastava. This agency also collaborates internationally. Currently, NCB conducts campaigns against drug trafficking across the country.
qs.kf:
☛ When was NCB formed? → 1986
☛ Which ministry does NCB come under? → Ministry of Home Affairs
☛ Where is the headquarters of NCB? → New Delhi
☛ Under which act does NCB function? → NDPS Act, 1985
☛ What is the main function of NCB? → To prevent drug trafficking

q: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission launched in India?
qs.e: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It is a statutory body that works to protect and promote human rights. Its formation aligns with the Paris Principles. The headquarters of NHRC is in New Delhi. Justice Ranganath Mishra was the first chairman. The commission is headed by a former Chief Justice of India or a judge of the Supreme Court.
qs.kf:
☛ Under which act was NHRC formed? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ Who was the first chairman of NHRC? → Justice Ranganath Mishra
☛ Where is the headquarters of NHRC? → New Delhi
☛ NHRC is a ________ body. → Statutory
☛ Who appoints the members of NHRC? → President

q: Recently, Indian Defence Minister attended the Victory Day Parade in Moscow, Russia on the occasion of the 75th anniversary of the Soviet victory over ____.
qs.e: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh attended the Victory Day Parade in Moscow in June 2020. This parade was held to commemorate the 75th anniversary of the Soviet Union's victory over Nazi Germany in World War II. The Soviet Union achieved victory after Germany's surrender on May 9, 1945. This day is celebrated as a national holiday in Russia. The Defence Minister's visit was significant in strengthening the strategic partnership between India and Russia.
qs.kf:
☛ Victory Day (Russia) → Celebrated on May 9
☛ Soviet victory in WWII → Over Nazi Germany
☛ End of war in Europe 1945 → May 8 (West), May 9 (East)
☛ Indian Defence Minister 2020 → Rajnath Singh
☛ Indian participation in Moscow Victory Parade → 75th anniversary

q: After how many years (approximately) of debate, the Constitution of India was signed?
qs.e: The Constitution of India was drafted after approximately 3 years of extensive debate and discussion. The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946 and adopted the final draft on 26 November 1949. During this period, there were 11 sessions and 165 days of deliberations. Members thoroughly debated each article. The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, prepared the final text. The Constitution came into full effect on 26 January 1950.
qs.kf:
☛ First meeting of Constituent Assembly → 9 December 1946
☛ Constitution adopted → 26 November 1949
☛ Constitution enforced → 26 January 1950
☛ Chairman of Drafting Committee → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Total days of debate → 165 days

q: Which of the following Nations was the member of "Allied Powers" group in World War II?
qs.e: World War II (1939-1945) had two major alliances: the Allied Powers and the Axis Powers. The main Allied Powers included the USA, UK, Soviet Union, China, and France. The Axis Powers consisted of Germany, Italy, and Japan. The USA entered the war in 1941 after the attack on Pearl Harbor and became a key member of the Allies. Italy, Germany, and Japan were all Axis Powers, so they are not the correct answer.
qs.kf:
☛ Key Allied leaders → Franklin D. Roosevelt (USA), Winston Churchill (UK), Joseph Stalin (Soviet Union)
☛ Key Axis leaders → Adolf Hitler (Germany), Benito Mussolini (Italy), Hideki Tojo (Japan)
☛ US entry into war → December 8, 1941, after Pearl Harbor attack
☛ Largest Allied army → Soviet Red Army
☛ End of war → September 2, 1945, with Japan's surrender

q: The subject 'Marriage' belongs to the:
qs.e: The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution includes subjects on which both the central and state governments can legislate. It includes Marriage, education, forests, labor welfare, etc. In case of a conflict between central and state laws, the central law prevails. The Concurrent List originally had 47 subjects, now increased to 52. Marriage falls under family law, which is part of this list. In contrast, the Union List contains subjects of national importance like defense and atomic energy, while the State List includes local matters like agriculture and police. Residuary subjects are those not mentioned in any list, e.g., computer software, and they fall under the central government's jurisdiction.
qs.kf:
☛ Which list does Marriage belong to? → Concurrent List
☛ How many subjects are in the Concurrent List? → 52
☛ What happens if central and state laws conflict? → Central law prevails
☛ Other subjects in the Concurrent List? → Education, forests, labor welfare
☛ Who has jurisdiction over residuary subjects? → Central government

q: When did India adopt its Biological Diversity Act?
qs.e: India adopted its Biological Diversity Act in 2002. This Act reflects India's commitment to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), which India signed in 1992. The Act aims at the conservation of biological resources, sustainable use of its components, and fair equitable sharing of benefits arising from the use of these resources. Under this Act, the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) was established to oversee matters related to access to biological resources and benefit sharing. The Act was passed in 2002 and came into force in 2003. It plays a crucial role in regulating the use of India's rich biodiversity and ensuring that local communities benefit from the commercial use of biological resources.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Biological Diversity Act passed? → 2002
☛ Which authority was established under this Act? → National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)
☛ When did India sign the CBD? → 1992
☛ When did this Act come into force? → 2003
☛ Which international agreement is related to biodiversity? → Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)

q: ________ was the first metro railway in India, inaugurated by former Prime Minister of India, Indira Gandhi.
qs.e: The Kolkata Metro is the first metro railway in India, inaugurated on October 24, 1984, by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It is also the first metro system in South-East Asia. The initial stretch ran from Dum Dum to Tollygunge (3.4 km). The Kolkata Metro is operated under the Indian Railways. After this, the Delhi Metro started in 2002, followed by Mumbai Metro in 2014 and Jaipur Metro in 2015. The Kolkata Metro is often called the 'Lifeline of Kolkata'.
qs.kf:
☛ First metro railway in India → Kolkata Metro (1984)
☛ Inauguration of Kolkata Metro → Indira Gandhi (24 October 1984)
☛ Second metro in India → Delhi Metro (2002)
☛ First suburban railway in India → Kolkata Suburban Railway (1874)
☛ First line of Kolkata Metro → Dum Dum to Tollygunge (3.4 km)

q: The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the council of ministers in a state CANNOT exceed ______ of the total number of members of the legislative assembly of that State.
qs.e: According to Article 164(1A) of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the council of ministers of a state cannot exceed 15% of the total number of members of the legislative assembly of that state. This provision was added by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. The objective was to limit the size of the council of ministers to improve government efficiency and prevent misuse of resources. However, the minimum number of ministers in any state is 12. This rule does not apply to states under President's rule.
qs.kf:
☛ Which constitutional amendment fixed the size of the council of ministers? → 91st Amendment, 2003
☛ Under which article is the size of the council of ministers mentioned? → Article 164(1A)
☛ What is the minimum number of ministers in a state? → 12
☛ On which states does the 15% limit not apply? → States under President's rule
☛ Was there any limit on the size of the council of ministers before 2003? → No

q: Who initiated the Young Bengal Movement?
qs.e: The Young Bengal Movement was initiated by Henry Vivian Derozio in the early 19th century. He was a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta and inspired his students to embrace reason, rationalism, and social reform. The movement criticized superstitions, orthodoxy, and social evils, promoting Western education and science. Derozio's followers were called Derozians and they opposed practices like Sati, child marriage, and caste discrimination. This movement was a key part of the Indian Renaissance.
qs.kf:
☛ Founder of Young Bengal Movement → Henry Vivian Derozio
☛ Derozio taught at which college → Hindu College, Calcutta
☛ Derozio's followers were called → Derozians
☛ Young Bengal Movement opposed → Sati, child marriage, caste discrimination
☛ Impact of Young Bengal Movement → Promoted Indian Renaissance and social reforms

q: Dr Bindeshwar Pathak is associated with the:
qs.e: Dr. Bindeshwar Pathak was a renowned social reformer and human rights activist. He founded the Sulabh Toilet Movement, which is famous for promoting sanitation and developing public toilets in India. He was born on 2 April 1943 in Bihar and was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2017. The Sulabh Movement provided clean toilets for the poor and women and fought against social evils. Dr. Pathak also contributed to the Swachh Bharat Mission.
qs.kf:
☛ Birthplace of Dr. Bindeshwar Pathak → Bihar
☛ Establishment year of Sulabh Toilet Movement → 1970
☛ Major award received by Dr. Pathak → Padma Bhushan (2017)
☛ Headquarters of Sulabh International → New Delhi
☛ Death year of Dr. Pathak → 2023

q: In which year was the Trade Union Act passed in India?
qs.e: The Trade Union Act in India was passed in the year 1926. This Act provides legal recognition to trade unions and regulates their registration, rights, and responsibilities. Under this Act, trade unions are granted immunity from civil and criminal liability and are empowered to engage in collective bargaining. The Act came into effect on June 1, 1927. Its objective is to protect the interests of workers and settle disputes with employers. The Act applies to all unions of workers and employers, ensuring a framework for their functioning.
qs.kf:
☛ Year of Trade Union Act passage → 1926
☛ Date of enforcement of Trade Union Act → June 1, 1927
☛ Main objective of Trade Union Act → Legal recognition of worker organizations
☛ First trade union in India → Madras Labour Union (1918)
☛ First national trade union organization in India → All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC, 1920)

q: Which of the following IITs has been declared one among the seven Eat Right Campus by FSSAI?
qs.e: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has selected seven institutions under its 'Eat Right Campus' initiative, which includes IIT Gandhinagar. This initiative aims to promote healthy and safe food. The selected campuses ensure high standards of hygiene, nutrition, and food safety. Other institutions in this list include Jamia Millia Islamia, AIIMS New Delhi, and some other universities. IIT Gandhinagar has been recognized for this achievement, providing a safe food environment for students and staff.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full form of FSSAI? → Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
☛ When was the Eat Right Campus initiative launched? → 2019
☛ How many institutions are included in the Eat Right Campus list? →7
☛ Where is the headquarters of FSSAI located? → New Delhi
☛ What is the objective of Eat Right Campus? → To promote healthy and safe food

q: Government of India decided to Celebrate the birthday of _____as "Parakram Diwas" every year.
qs.e: The Government of India decided to celebrate the birthday of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose as 'Parakram Diwas' on 23rd January every year. This day is observed to honor his courage, patriotism, and contribution to India's freedom struggle. Netaji formed the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) and gave the slogan 'Delhi Chalo'. He was born on 23rd January 1897 in Cuttack, Odisha. The declaration of Parakram Diwas was made in 2021.
qs.kf:
☛ Birthday of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose → 23rd January
☛ Establishment of Azad Hind Fauj → 1942
☛ Title given to Subhash Chandra Bose → 'Netaji'
☛ Slogan of Subhash Chandra Bose → 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom'
☛ Announcement of Parakram Diwas → 2021

q: As of December 2020, who is the Prime Minister of Australia?
qs.e: As of December 2020, the Prime Minister of Australia was Scott Morrison, who assumed office in August 2018. He is the leader of the Liberal Party and was re-elected in the 2019 federal election. Among the options, Jon Sandberg and Peter Herald are not known Prime Ministers, while Bill Shorten was the opposition leader at that time. During Morrison's tenure, Australia faced the bushfire crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. His leadership focused on strong economic management and international relations.
qs.kf:
☛ Who is the current Prime Minister of Australia? → Scott Morrison (Liberal Party)
☛ When did Scott Morrison become Prime Minister? → August 2018
☛ What is the role of the Prime Minister in Australia's parliamentary system? → Head of government and accountable to Parliament
☛ Who won the 2019 Australian federal election? → Liberal-National coalition led by Scott Morrison
☛ Who was Australia's Prime Minister before Scott Morrison? → Malcolm Turnbull

q: The movement of modern architecture started in the year of-
qs.e: The modern architecture movement began in the 1920s. It broke away from traditional styles and emphasized new construction principles. Key pioneers include Le Corbusier, Walter Gropius, and Frank Lloyd Wright. The Bauhaus School (founded in 1919) also promoted modernist ideas. The 1920s saw the rise of the International Style, which focused on simplicity, functionality, and the rejection of ornamentation. This movement influenced architecture worldwide, leading to minimalist designs and the use of modern materials like steel, glass, and concrete.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the modern architecture movement start? → 1920
☛ When was the Bauhaus School founded? → 1919
☛ Le Corbusier was an architect of which country? → France (born in Switzerland)
☛ What is a feature of International Style? → Simplicity and functionality
☛ Which famous building is by Frank Lloyd Wright? → Fallingwater

q: What is the minimum voting age for women in India?
qs.e: In India, the minimum voting age for both women and men is 18 years. This is provided under Article 326 of the Indian Constitution. The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment in 1988, which expanded political participation among youth. This age applies to elections for the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. The Election Commission of India prepares electoral rolls based on this rule. There is no separate voting age for women; the same rule applies equally to all citizens. The amendment was a significant step toward empowering young voters and ensuring inclusive democracy.
qs.kf:
☛ Which Article prescribes the voting age? → Article 326
☛ Which amendment reduced voting age from 21 to 18? → 61st Amendment, 1988
☛ Minimum age to vote in Lok Sabha elections? → 18 years
☛ Minimum age to become a Rajya Sabha member? → 30 years
☛ Voting age for women in India? → 18 years (same as men)

q: In which of the following years did the Britishers establish their first factory in Bengal?
qs.e: The British East India Company established its first factory in Bengal in 1651 on the banks of the Hooghly River. This factory enabled the Company to trade in Bengal's silk and other products. It marked the beginning of British expansion in India. Later, in 1690, the Company established its presence in Calcutta. The year 1651 is considered significant for British commercial activities in Bengal.
qs.kf:
☛ Where was the first factory of the British East India Company in Bengal established? → Hooghly
☛ Where did the British East India Company establish its first factory in India? → Surat (1613)
☛ Which Mughal emperor granted the British East India Company permission to trade in India? → Jahangir
☛ Who was the Mughal emperor at the time of the establishment of the British factory in Bengal? → Shah Jahan
☛ When did the British East India Company establish its factory in Calcutta? → 1690

q: In which of the following years was Rajiv-Longowal Peace accord signed by Indian Prime Minster Rajeev Gandhi and Akali leader Harchand Singh Longowal?
qs.e: The Rajiv-Longowal Peace Accord was signed on July 24, 1985 between Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and Akali Dal leader Harchand Singh Longowal. The accord aimed to end rising terrorism and separatist activities in Punjab. Key provisions included the transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab, crop insurance for farmers, and release of Akali prisoners. However, the accord was not fully implemented, and Longowal was assassinated shortly after. This agreement remains a significant milestone in the Punjab peace process.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Rajiv-Longowal Accord signed? → July 24, 1985
☛ Main provisions of the accord? → Transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab, crop insurance, release of prisoners
☛ Who were the signatories? → Rajiv Gandhi and Harchand Singh Longowal
☛ What happened after the accord? → Longowal's assassination, incomplete implementation
☛ Purpose of the accord? → To bring peace and end terrorism in Punjab

q: In which of the following years was the first session of the All India Kisan Sabha held?
qs.e: The first session of the All India Kisan Sabha was held in 1936 at Lucknow. It was founded to address the rights and issues of farmers. The session was chaired by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, a prominent peasant leader. The Kisan Sabha played a crucial role in organizing peasants and leading movements against the zamindari system. It was formed with the support of the Indian National Congress and later became a major platform for peasant movements in India.
qs.kf:
☛ Formation year of Kisan Sabha → 1936
☛ Venue of first session → Lucknow
☛ First president → Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
☛ Key demand → Abolition of zamindari
☛ Supported by → Indian National Congress

q: The third battle of Panipat was fought between the Maratha Empire and (the) _____.
qs.e: The third battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire and the Durrani Empire led by Ahmad Shah Durrani. This battle was fought for supremacy in North India after the decline of the Mughal Empire. The Marathas were led by Sadashivrao Bhau, while the Durrani army included allies like the Rohillas and Nawab Shuja-ud-Daulah. The Maratha defeat halted their expansion into the north and paved the way for British rule. It was one of the largest battles of the 18th century, with heavy casualties on both sides.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the third battle of Panipat fought? → 14 January 1761
☛ Who led the Marathas? → Sadashivrao Bhau
☛ Who led the Durrani forces? → Ahmad Shah Durrani
☛ Which Muslim rulers were allied with Durrani? → Rohillas and Shuja-ud-Daulah
☛ Between whom was the first battle of Panipat fought? → Babur and Ibrahim Lodi

q: The people of ___________ were famously involved in execution of the Chipko movement.
qs.e: The Chipko movement started in 1973 in the Garhwal Himalayas region at Reni village (present-day Uttarakhand). It was a forest conservation movement where villagers, especially women, hugged trees to prevent deforestation. Key leaders were Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi. This movement is a historic example of environmental activism and later inspired similar efforts across India.
qs.kf:
☛ Where did the Chipko movement start? → Garhwal Himalayas (Reni village)
☛ Who were the key leaders of the Chipko movement? → Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi
☛ What was the movement against? → Deforestation
☛ What does 'Chipko' literally mean? → To embrace/cling
☛ In which year did the movement begin? → 1973

q: Which of the following is NOT a source of collection of municipal solid waste?
qs.e: Municipal solid waste includes waste from households, shops, offices, schools, and hospitals (non-hazardous). Radioactive waste originates from nuclear power plants, research laboratories, and medical facilities and falls under the category of hazardous waste. It requires special disposal procedures and is not part of municipal solid waste management systems.

☛ Swachh Bharat Mission launched → 2014

qs.e: In the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly elections, there are a total of 81 constituencies. The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) won 34 seats, emerging as the largest party. q: Regarding the 2024 Maharashtra Assembly elections, which of the following statements are correct?
1. The BJP won more than 100 seats.
2. The Congress improved its seat tally compared to 2019.
3. The Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) secured more seats than the Uddhav faction.
4. The Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) alliance was successful in forming the government.
qs.e: In the 2024 Maharashtra Assembly elections, the BJP won 132 seats, which is more than 100, making statement 1 correct. The Congress had won 44 seats in 2019 but only 16 seats in 2024, so statement 2 is incorrect. The Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) secured 57 seats, while the Uddhav faction got 20 seats, hence statement 3 is correct. The Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) alliance won a total of 46 seats and failed to form the government, so statement 4 is incorrect. Thus, the correct statements are 1 and 3.
qs.kf:
☛ BJP seats in 2024 Maharashtra Assembly → 132
☛ Shiv Sena Shinde faction seats → 57
☛ Uddhav faction seats → 20
☛ Congress seats in 2024 → 16
☛ MVA alliance total seats → 46

q: When was the World Bank founded?
qs.e: The World Bank was founded in July 1944 during the Bretton Woods Conference, which took place during the Second World War. Its primary purpose was to assist in the reconstruction and development of war-torn countries. The World Bank is headquartered in Washington D.C. and its current president is Ajay Banga.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the World Bank founded? → 1944
☛ Where is the World Bank headquartered? → Washington D.C.
☛ Who is the current president of the World Bank? → Ajay Banga
☛ When was the Bretton Woods Conference held? → 1944
☛ What was the initial purpose of the World Bank? → Reconstruction of war-torn countries

q: When was the 78th anniversary of the Quit India Movement celebrated?
qs.e: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942. Its 78th anniversary was celebrated on 8 August 2020. The movement was initiated by Mahatma Gandhi at the All India Congress Committee session in Mumbai with the slogan 'Do or Die'. During the movement, Gandhi, Nehru and other leaders were arrested. It was one of the largest mass movements against British rule in India.
qs.kf:
☛ When did the Quit India Movement start? → 8 August 1942
☛ What was the slogan of Quit India Movement? → Do or Die
☛ Where was the Quit India resolution passed? → Mumbai session of AICC
☛ Which leaders were arrested during the movement? → Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, etc.
☛ In which year did the Quit India Movement end? → 1945

q: When did the British enact the Inland Emigration Act?
qs.e: The British government enacted the Inland Emigration Act in 1859 to regulate the movement of laborers in India. This act aimed to control the recruitment and transportation of workers for plantations and mines. Under this act, laborers were required to work under contracts, and their movement was restricted. It primarily applied to workers in tea, coffee, and indigo plantations. The act facilitated the exploitation of laborers by binding them to specific employers and locations. It was a key piece of legislation during the British colonial period to manage labor supply for commercial agriculture.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Inland Emigration Act enacted? → 1859
☛ What was the purpose of the act? → To control labor movement
☛ Who were affected by this act? → Plantation workers
☛ What were laborers required to do under this act? → Work under contract
☛ During which period was this act introduced? → British colonial period

q: The parliament of Norway is called:
qs.e: The parliament of Norway is called the Stortinget, which means "the Great Assembly". It is the supreme legislative body of Norway and was established in 1814. Stortinget is a unicameral parliament with 169 members elected for four-year terms. In contrast, the National Diet is the parliament of Japan, the Folketing is the parliament of Denmark, and Parliament is a general term used for legislative bodies in many countries. Hence, the correct answer is Stortinget.
qs.kf:
☛ Parliament of Norway is called → Stortinget
☛ Parliament of Japan is called → National Diet
☛ Parliament of Denmark is called → Folketing
☛ Number of members in Stortinget → 169
☛ Year of establishment of Stortinget → 1814

q: Which treaty was imposed by the five nuclear Weapon powers and five permanent members of the UN Security Council on the rest of the World in 1968?
qs.e: In 1968, the five permanent members of the UN Security Council (USA, Russia, UK, France, China) and other nuclear weapon powers imposed the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) on the rest of the world. It entered into force in 1970. The treaty aims to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons, promote disarmament, and ensure peaceful use of nuclear energy. The NPT is based on three pillars: non-proliferation, disarmament, and peaceful nuclear technology. Over 190 countries have joined the treaty, but India, Israel, Pakistan, and South Sudan are not signatories. The treaty is reviewed every five years.
qs.kf:
☛ What is the full name of NPT? → Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
☛ When did NPT come into force? → March 5, 1970
☛ What are the three pillars of NPT? → Non-proliferation, Disarmament, Peaceful nuclear energy
☛ How often is NPT reviewed? → Every 5 years
☛ Which country threatened to withdraw from NPT? → North Korea (withdrew in 2003)

q: Bangladesh celebrates its Independence Day on:
qs.e: Bangladesh celebrates its Independence Day on 26 March. This day marks the beginning of the liberation war against the Pakistani army in 1971. On the night of 25 March, the Pakistani army launched a genocide in Dhaka known as 'Operation Searchlight'. The next day, 26 March, the founding father of Bangladesh, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, declared Bangladesh's independence. The war lasted nine months and ended on 16 December 1971 with the surrender of Pakistan. Every year on 26 March, the day is commemorated with national parades, cultural events, and tributes to the martyrs.
qs.kf:
☛ Bangladesh Independence Day → 26 March
☛ Slogan of Bangladesh Liberation → 'Joy Bangla'
☛ Founder of Bangladesh → Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
☛ End of Bangladesh War → 16 December 1971
☛ Date of Operation Searchlight → 25 March 1971

q: Indigenous sports 'Kalaripayattu' originally belongs to which state?
qs.e: Kalaripayattu is an ancient Indian martial art that originated in the state of Kerala. It is considered one of the oldest fighting systems in the world. The term 'Kalaripayattu' means 'practice in the field of battle'. This art is particularly prevalent in the Malabar region of Kerala. It involves the use of weapons and physical movements. Kalaripayattu is also linked to yoga and Ayurveda. It is regarded as an integral part of Kerala's cultural identity.
qs.kf:
☛ Origin state of Kalaripayattu → Kerala
☛ Meaning of Kalaripayattu → Practice in the field of battle
☛ Associated arts with Kalaripayattu → Yoga and Ayurveda
☛ Famous region for Kalaripayattu → Malabar
☛ Key feature of Kalaripayattu → Use of weapons and physical movements

q: Who is known as the modern manu?
qs.e: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar is known as the 'Modern Manu' because he drafted the Indian Constitution as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. In ancient India, Manu was the lawgiver who authored Manusmriti. In the modern context, Ambedkar created a constitution based on social justice, equality, and fundamental rights. He was a Dalit leader who fought against untouchability. He was born on 14 April 1891 and was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990.
qs.kf:
☛ Who drafted the Indian Constitution? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Who wrote Manusmriti? → Manu
☛ Which highest civilian award did Ambedkar receive? → Bharat Ratna
☛ When was Ambedkar born? → 14 April 1891
☛ Which committee did Ambedkar chair? → Constitution Drafting Committee

q: When was the Protection of Human Rights Act passed in India?
qs.e: The Protection of Human Rights Act was passed in India in 1993. This Act provides for the establishment of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs). The NHRC was formed on 12 October 1993. Its objectives are to protect and promote human rights and investigate violations. The Act defines human rights in line with the United Nations Declaration. The Commission consists of a Chairperson and four members. It exercises powers of a civil court to enforce its recommendations.
qs.kf:
☛ When was the Protection of Human Rights Act passed? → 1993
☛ When was NHRC established? → 12 October 1993
☛ Who appoints the Chairperson of NHRC? → President
☛ How many members does NHRC have? → Four
☛ Definition of human rights is derived from? → United Nations Declaration

qs.tag: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3
q: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs), the Government of India's education initiatives for tribal communities, were introduced in which year?
qs.e: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) were introduced by the Government of India to provide quality education to Scheduled Tribe students. These schools were launched in 1997-98 with the aim of offering residential educational facilities to tribal children. The scheme envisages establishing at least one EMRS in each block with a high tribal population. This initiative plays a crucial role in bridging the educational gap for tribal communities, ensuring they have access to opportunities similar to other sections of society.

q: Which among the following significant changes was introduced in the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025?
o: Exemption of Waqf properties from legal scrutiny
Mandating representation of at least two Muslim women on Waqf Boards
Abolition of the Central Waqf Council
qs.e: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 introduced a key change to ensure gender inclusion in Waqf Boards by mandating at least two Muslim women as members. This amendment aims to enhance women's participation in the management of waqf properties. The Act also includes provisions for improving transparency and accountability in waqf administration. The Central Waqf Council was not abolished; its functions were revised. Waqf properties were not exempted from legal scrutiny; instead, audit and monitoring mechanisms were strengthened. Privatisation of waqf properties was not part of the amendment. The focus remains on better governance and representation.
